# Spin-offs and demergers — NiftyTotalMarket

*Run 2026-11-08 · filings window 2025-10-14 → 2026-11-07 · 4454 restructuring filings across 561 companies · 28 confirmed demergers, 117 probable, 28 indicated, 498 rights / preferential offerings, 790 other restructurings · judge: claude-opus-5 read the schemes, three years of calls and the segment pages.*

**The method, in one paragraph.** Spin-offs are where the notes say the bargains hide: the new stock is sold by holders who never chose it for about a year, the parent is often the better buy before the split, insiders tell you what they think through the stock and options they take in the new entity, and a pro-forma statement plus the peer P/E prices what the market is ignoring. This report puts the CONFIRMED demergers first — a demerger scheme on the exchange record — each with when the new entity lists, why management is doing it (three years of calls, with the transcript each point came from), the parent's last three years with charts, P/E and cash flows, and the separated business's own numbers from the annual reports and presentations, page-cited. Probable and indicated cases follow, then every other restructuring on file.

# Confirmed demergers — in full

## UPL — UPL Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 7.1/10 · spin-off · 9 filing(s) from CALLS, NSE · first 2026-01-19, latest 2026-08-01

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'exchange_noc' stage; UPL Global Sustainable Agri Solutions Limited will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; indicated timeline: Press release February 20, 2026: "The transaction is expected to be completed within 12 –15 months"; NSE letter July 29, 2026: listing steps and trading "within sixty days of receipt of the order of the Hon'ble High Court/NCLT"; November 2, 2026 results still say Scheme awaits shareholder, regulator and NCLT approvals.

**The stages, as filed:** exchange_noc (2026-07-29)

**Stated in the filings:** resulting company **UPL Global Sustainable Agri Solutions Limited**; entitlement **1 for every 1**.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** India plus international crop protection business, consolidated into a listed pure-play crop protection platform — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* UPL 2 Promoters indicatively 71.56% post-Scheme, voluntarily locked 18 months from Listing Date; Upswing Trust 16.78% public with one board nominee; Mike Frank CEO of UPL Global.
- *What it reveals:* Separates the group's largest earner: UPL Cayman FY25 turnover USD 4,187 Mn, net worth USD 1,599 Mn, 140+ countries, 16% innovation rate; parent left as diversified agro/specialty holdco. Group net debt USD 1.6bn; split not stated.
- *Selling pressure:* likely — Every UPL 1 holder gets 1 UPL 2 share in a newly listed entity; promoters locked 18 months, so only public can sell.
- *Parent or spin:* spin · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* UPL 2 Information Memorandum / abridged prospectus: assets and liabilities, debt and lender conditions transferred to the resulting company.
- *In their words:* ““Bringing our crop protection businesses under one platform creates the world's second largest listed pure-play crop protection platform.””

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Management framed the separation as the final step of a structure-simplification project begun in 2022, when the India crop protection business was carved into UPL Sustainable Agri Solutions (UPL SAS) while the international crop protection business sat under UPL Crop Protection Holdings (UPL Cayman, 77.78% UPL-owned). The Feb 20, 2026 Composite Scheme does three things in order: merges UPL SAS into UPL Limited (1,000 UPL shares for every 48 UPL SAS shares), demerges the India Crop Protection business into UPL Global Sustainable Agri Solutions (UPL 2) on a 1:1 entitlement, and merges UPL Cayman into UPL 2 (1,000 UPL 2 shares for every 213 UPL Cayman shares) — leaving UPL Limited as a diversified agro/specialty-chemicals platform (SUPERFORM, Advanta, new verticals) and UPL 2 as what Mike Frank called the world's second largest listed pure-play crop protection platform, present in 140+ countries. The stated problems it solves: a conglomerate discount (Bikash Prasad: the market applies 'a single conglomerate multiple' and sum-of-parts is unclear), value trapped at platform level (Toshan Tamhane said the KKR and Alpha Wave private valuations were not flowing through to UPL Limited), a complex holding structure, and the fact that crop protection and seeds have fundamentally different cash-flow and capital-allocation needs — explicitly citing Corteva's announced crop-protection/seeds split as precedent. Separation is meant to give each entity its own capital structure, governance and board focus so each can raise capital independently and attract a different investor, lender and strategic-partner set; Jai Shroff said these businesses 'need an independent life' and claimed they can grow 3x-4x faster than peers. Management said the precondition was deleveraging, which it declared done at the May 2026 CMD: gross debt down from $3.8bn (FY24) to $2.3bn (-40%), net debt $3.1bn to $1.6bn (-48%), gearing 4.6x to below 1.6x, after repaying $400m perpetuals and $500m of loans and extending another $400m to March 2029 — Shroff said leverage 'was an issue which kept the multiple of the company. That is I'm sure gone away now.' The push came from several directions: analysts and rating agencies (five explicit feedback items Prasad catalogued, including the ~INR5,000 crore of below-EBITDA line items and short-term liquidity), platform investors KKR and Alpha Wave seeking value realisation (Advanta's Jan 19, 2026 DRHP is an offer-for-sale with KKR selling 2.2% and UPL Limited 7.8%, proceeds 'largely for deleveraging of the group balance sheet'), and the Upswing Trust, an existing 5% UPL SAS investor that swapped 22.21% of UPL Corp Cayman into UPL Cayman (completed July 31, 2026) and ends with 16.78% of UPL 2 plus one board nomination right. Notably, at least one large holder pushed back: Old Bridge's Tarang Agarwal called the announced structure 'fairly detrimental to the current shareholders' and likely to trigger 'a significant HoldCo discount,' and Prasad said the feedback tracker would go 'unfiltered to the board' within a month or two, while noting at least 10 structures had already been evaluated.

**How it evolved:** On the Aug 1, 2025 Q1 FY26 call the idea surfaced only as a line in Jai Shroff's press release: Bikash Prasad said advisors were just being engaged 'to explore unlocking value across all platforms,' with no structure chosen and deleveraging framed as the near-term priority; by the Nov 6, 2025 Q2 call it had hardened into 'restructuring or strategic fundraising, potential liquidity events like IPO' across platforms, alongside the DECCO-into-Advanta integration, and was explicitly linked to funding the FY27 $900m maturities. On the Feb 2, 2026 Q3 call the first concrete step landed — Advanta's DRHP filed Jan 19, 2026 — with management guiding to 'IPO and restructuring within a period of 1 to 3 years' and Toshan Tamhane giving the industrial logic (crop protection vs seeds cash flows, the Corteva split, Advanta's 'destiny of its own'), while Tarang Agarwal already questioned whether UPL shareholders gained anything. The Scheme itself was approved by the board on Feb 20, 2026 and by the May 11, 2026 Capital Markets Day the debate had shifted from whether to separate to how: Agarwal attacked the chosen structure as HoldCo-discount-creating and asked for alternatives, Shroff and Prasad defended it while promising to take investor feedback to the board, and the process then moved through CCI approval (June 2-3, 2026), BSE/NSE observation letters (July 29, 2026) and completion of the Cayman swap and ESOP swap (July 31, 2026), with Nov 2, 2026 results confirming no accounting effect yet pending NCLT and shareholder approvals.

**What management expects from it:** UPL Limited: a diversified agro and specialty-chemicals platform (SUPERFORM, Advanta, new verticals), lower debt, better ROE. UPL 2: a pure-play crop protection platform with its own capital structure, governance and board focus, manufacturing/R&D/market-access synergies, independent fundraising, a wider investor and lender base, and growth management claims at 3x-4x peers. For holders: clearer sum-of-parts, removing the conglomerate discount.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Aug 2025](https://www.upl-ltd.com/financial_result_and_report_pdfs/r3nhTBqvvaJwil4Yfw2svFbm3ssp7pXGaXZJVwLM/UPL---Q1FY26---Earnings-call-transcript.pdf)* — First acknowledgement: advisors only just being engaged, no structure decided, timeline unknown; purpose stated as unlocking value across platforms, tied to deleveraging the balance sheet over one to two years. “The idea behind engaging advisors is to explore unlocking value across all platforms.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.upl-ltd.com/financial_result_and_report_pdfs/r3nhTBqvvaJwil4Yfw2svFbm3ssp7pXGaXZJVwLM/UPL---Q1FY26---Earnings-call-transcript.pdf)* — Prasad linked the strategic options directly to balance-sheet repair rather than to growth at that stage. “However, as we continue to evaluate various strategic options to unlock value across the platform, our focus will be to significantly deleverage our balance sheet over the next year or two.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.upl-ltd.com/financial_result_and_report_pdfs/UPL-Q2FY26-Earnings-call-transcript.pdf)* — The option set was named for the first time — restructuring, strategic fundraising, IPO — across all platforms, after DECCO was folded into Advanta in September 2025. “UPL continues to evaluate various strategic opportunities to unlock shareholders' value across platforms, including restructuring or strategic fundraising, potential liquidity events like IPO.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.upl-ltd.com/financial_result_and_report_pdfs/UPL-Q2FY26-Earnings-call-transcript.pdf)* — Asked how the ~$900m of FY27 maturities would be met, Prasad made the value-unlock actions part of the funding answer. “We had indicated during Q1 earnings call and press release that we are looking at various options to unlock shareholders' value. And if some of those we decide to take, that would also help in terms of deleveraging the balance sheet.”
- *Feb 2026* — Advanta DRHP filed 19 Jan 2026 as the first concrete corporate action, with a stated 1-3 year window for IPOs and restructuring across all platforms. “As we have communicated earlier, we remain focused in evaluating various corporate actions for all our platforms, including IPO and restructuring within a period of 1 to 3 years.”
- *Feb 2026* — The Advanta IPO is an offer for sale, not primary: KKR selling 2.2% and UPL Limited 7.8%, with proceeds going to the group, chiefly to cut debt. “But it will come to the group largely for deleveraging of the group balance sheet.”
- *Feb 2026* — Tamhane gave the industrial rationale — crop protection and seeds need different capital and cash-flow profiles — and cited Corteva's split as the global precedent, calling Advanta the eighth largest seeds player. “we believe that the needs of crop protection in terms of the cash flows, capital allocation are very different from that of the seeds business.”
- *Feb 2026* — Management conceded that the private-round valuations of platform stakes (KKR, Alpha Wave) were not being reflected in UPL Limited's own price — the trapped-value argument. “Because , if you look at the valuation that KKR and subsequently Alpha Wave came in at , at least we feel that the full value of that is no t flowing through to UPL Limited.”
- *Scheme* — The 20 Feb 2026 Composite Scheme consolidates UPL SAS (India crop protection) and UPL Cayman (global crop protection) into UPL 2 to create a pure-play crop protection platform with its own management. “The Scheme proposes to consolidate  the India Crop Protection Business held in UPL SAS and Global Crop Protection Business held in UPL Cayman, under a single entity, creating a focused, pure -play crop protection platform.”
- *Scheme* — Independent capital raising and capital-structure optimisation for each of the two listed entities is given as a core benefit, alongside a wider investor, lender and partner base and sharper board focus. “The Scheme will allow UPL 1 and UPL 2 to raise capital independently, allowing each entity to optimize its capital structure and pursue business opportunities more efficiently and effectively.”
- *Scheme* — Mechanics and ratios: UPL SAS merges into UPL at 1,000:48, India crop protection demerges into UPL 2 at 1:1, UPL Cayman merges into UPL 2 at 1,000:213; no cash consideration; UPL 2 ends 71.56% promoter / 28.44% public with Upswing Trust at 16.78%, and promoters locked in for 18 months. “1 (One)  equity share of UPL 2 of INR 2 each fully paid -up for every 1 (One)  equity share of UPL 1 of INR 2 each fully paid -up.”
- *Scheme* — Scale claim and leadership: Mike Frank, CEO of UPL Corp, becomes CEO of UPL Global, which management says will be the second largest listed pure-play crop protection company, in 140+ countries with 9 R&D centres and 25 formulation sites. “Bringing our crop protection businesses under one platform creates the world's second largest  listed pure- play crop protection platform.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No quantified synergies, no debt/cost split between the two entities, no SUPERFORM-to-UPL 2 supply pricing, no resolution of the HoldCo-discount objection, no Advanta IPO interaction.

*Calls read (36 months):* Feb 2026

**CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 6.4/10 · spin-off · 15 filing(s) from CALLS, NSE, NSE-BM, NSE-deep · first 2026-02-27, latest 2026-10-29

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'meetings' stage; Astra Space Technologies Private Limited will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; indicated timeline: Press release 27 February 2026: "The Company aims to complete the demerger and list ASTPL by Q1 of FY28, subject to the timely receipt of all approvals." NSE letter 29 October 2026 requires steps for listing completed and trading commenced within sixty days of receipt of the NCLT order

**The stages, as filed:** announced (2026-05-26) → exchange_noc (2026-10-29) → meetings (2026-08-22)

**Stated in the filings:** resulting company **Astra Space Technologies Private Limited**; demerged undertaking: ) is proposed to be demerged into; size hint: 10.6% of ebitda.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Space, Meteorology and Hydrology business of Astra Microwave, demerged into Astra Space Technologies Private Limited — class `regulatory_strategic`.

- *Insiders:* Promoters hold 100% of ASTPL pre-scheme, 6.45% post-scheme (mirror of AMPL). MD S. Gurunatha Reddy resigned from AMPL w.e.f. 30 September 2026 to oversee the demerger and join ASTPL as a Director; CFO Rahul Rungta moved to ASTPL as CFO; MD/WTD bonus criteria include 10% weightage for "Other intiatives of corporate restructuring like merger/demerger"
- *What it reveals:* Separation reveals a scaled-up, profitable, high-growth space/weather business: INR 157 crores FY26 turnover (13.58% of total), ~16% of FY26 revenue, cumulative INR 750 crore ISRO orders plus INR 250 crore to FY28, meteorology INR 330 crore executed with INR 285 crore order book to FY28; margins described as better than defence
- *Selling pressure:* likely — Small relative to parent (13.58% of turnover, stated 10.6% of EBITDA), mirror-shareholding spin of a distinct sector with no index membership
- *Parent or spin:* both · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* The Scheme of Arrangement and valuation/share entitlement report, plus ASTPL's abridged-prospectus financials in the shareholder notice
- *In their words:* “The Space, Meteorology and Hydrology business operates in a sector with distinct industry characteristics, competitive dynamics, regulatory environment, and risk profile, necessitating a differentiated growth strategy aligned with its specific market opportunities.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Management frames the separation as a strategic re-alignment of a company that had grown into two very different businesses: Radar Electronics, Electronic Warfare and Telemetry on one side, and Space, Meteorology and Hydrology on the other, the latter being carved into Astra Space Technologies Private Limited (ASTPL), a wholly owned subsidiary that will be listed separately while AMPL continues as a pure-play Defence and Aerospace company retaining its JVs (Astra Rafael Comsys) and other wholly owned subsidiaries. The stated objective is sharper strategic and operational focus, with dedicated management teams free to pursue sector-specific growth, plus enhanced governance and accountability, a simpler corporate structure, clearer investment propositions and a broader investor base. The Scheme filing is explicit that Space/Met/Hydrology 'operates in a sector with distinct industry characteristics, competitive dynamics, regulatory environment, and risk profile', so it needs a differentiated growth strategy and its own capital allocation, and that a standalone entity is better placed to attract investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders with sector-specific interests. The press release adds the capital angle bluntly: Space and Weather is a scaled-up, profitable, high-growth opportunity in satellite design/assembly and satellite data, but it is capital-intensive and execution-dependent, and the demerger 'creates the structural clarity to attract capital and talent at scale'. The numbers cited are modest but real: the demerged undertaking did roughly INR157 crores of FY26 turnover, 13.58% of AMPL's total (space plus meteorology was ~16% of FY26 revenue); cumulative ISRO orders of over INR750 crores across two decades with INR250 crores still to execute by FY28, and over INR330 crores of met/hydrology contracts with a INR285 crores book to FY28; at December 2025 the standalone order book of INR2,226 crores already contained INR249 crores of space and INR369 crores of metrology/hydrology. Consideration is a 1:1 share entitlement (one INR2 ASTPL share for every INR2 AMPL share), no cash, so ASTPL's shareholding mirrors AMPL's (promoters indicatively 6.45%, public 93.55%), with listing sought on BSE and NSE and completion targeted by Q1 FY28. Leadership was split to match: Managing Director S. Gurunatha Reddy stepped down on 30 September 2026 to oversee the demerger and join ASTPL as a Director, Dr M. V. Reddy became MD of AMPL from 1 October 2026, and CFO Rahul Rungta had already moved to ASTPL in February 2026. The texts name no investor, lender or partner as having demanded the split; it is presented throughout as board-initiated, with the benefit framed as 'unlocking the value of the Demerged Undertaking for the shareholders of the Demerged Company'.

**How it evolved:** The idea surfaces obliquely as a valuation argument: on 14 Aug 2025 Atim Kabra says the separately incorporated space subsidiary is 'very, very valuable' given how thinly-revenued space peers are priced, and on 13 Nov 2025 he extrapolates space alone to near AMPL's whole market capitalisation while flagging heavy space investment and Astra SAT-1; on 13 Feb 2026 he turns to financing, saying the balance sheet must be 'creative' so blue-sky projects are not starved, and teases 'a few very interesting options'. Structurally it moves fast after that: CFO Rahul Rungta is shifted to ASTPL on 11-12 Feb 2026, the Board grants in-principle approval on 27 Feb 2026 with a same-day press release (revised the same day), and SGR announces it on the 27 May 2026 call. The Board approved the full Scheme of Arrangement on 10 June 2026 with the 1:1 ratio and the INR157 crores / 13.58% disclosure, SGR's exit as MD was confirmed on 10 Aug 2026 effective 30 Sep 2026, and BSE/NSE observation letters with no adverse observations/no objection arrived on 29 Oct 2026.

**What management expects from it:** AMPL: a pure-play defence/aerospace company keeping JVs and subsidiaries, with simpler structure, focused management and better capital allocation. ASTPL: an independently listed, profitable, high-growth space-and-weather platform spanning upstream hardware, integration and data, able to attract sector-specific investors, partners, lenders and talent. Both: sharper focus, improved operational efficiency, clearer investment propositions and unlocked shareholder value over the medium to long term.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *CALL Aug 2025* — A year before the demerger was announced, management had already carved space into a separate wholly owned subsidiary (Astra Space Technologies Private Limited) with its own hiring and Bangalore clean rooms, and Atim Kabra pitched it as undervalued inside AMPL on a space order book of about INR230-239 crores. “And given where companies with very limited indigenous capabilities are valued, you might find that our space business is actually very, very valuable.”
- *CALL Nov 2025* — Kabra sharpened the hidden-value argument, saying space peers with almost no revenue were being valued at $750-800 million and that extrapolating Astra's space business alone approached AMPL's entire market capitalisation. “Companies are raising money at like $750 million, $800 million valuation with hardly any revenue numbers to their credit.”
- *CALL Feb 2026* — Two weeks before the Board's in-principle approval, Kabra devoted his remarks to the criticality of adequate financing for development and 'blue sky' projects and hinted at structural options to come, while the standalone order book of INR2,226 crores contained INR249 crores of space and INR369 crores of metrology and hydrology. “So watch the space. There are a few very interesting options as they crystallize, we'll be letting you know.”
- *CALL Jun 2026* — S. G. Reddy announced the Board's in-principle approval of the demerger of the space, meteorology and hydrology business and listed the objectives: dedicated management teams, better governance, a simpler structure and clearer investment propositions, with the formal scheme to follow within weeks; space and meteorology were ~16% of FY26 revenue of INR1,157 crores. “The objective of this move is to create sharper strategic and operational focus for business segments.”
- *CALL Jun 2026* — Management tied the restructuring to global as well as Indian opportunity and to capital allocation and efficiency over the medium to long term, alongside FY27 guidance of 15-20% growth and FY26 operating cash flow of INR370 crores versus minus INR99 crores. “Furthermore, this restructuring will position us to capitalize on emerging opportunities both in India and globally.”
- *Scheme* — The 27 Feb 2026 press release states the purpose as unlocking shareholder value and creating two focused listed platforms - AMPL for Defence and Aerospace, ASTPL for Space, Meteorology and Hydrology - and lists broader investor base, better oversight and less structural complexity as benefits. “The proposed demerger is aimed at unlocking shareholder value and enhancing strategic focus across business verticals.”
- *Scheme* — The same release argues the space and weather business is profitable and high-growth but capital-hungry and execution-dependent, and that the separation is what makes it possible to raise capital and hire for it at scale, on a 20-year base of over INR750 crores of cumulative ISRO orders and over INR330 crores of met/hydrology contracts. “The Indian and global markets are opening simultaneously, India's geopolitical positioning is aligned with this opportunity, and the demerger of ASTPL creates the structural clarity required to attract capital and talent at scale.”
- *Scheme* — The 10 June 2026 Scheme of Arrangement filing gives the formal rationale, including that the segment faces a different regulatory and risk environment and needs its own strategy, and that a standalone entity is better placed to attract investors, strategic partners and lenders. “The Space, Meteorology and Hydrology business operates in a sector with distinct industry characteristics, competitive dynamics, regulatory environment, and risk profile, necessitating a differentiated growth strategy aligned with its specific market opportunities.”
- *Scheme* — The filing sizes the demerged undertaking and sets the terms: no cash consideration, a 1:1 share entitlement ratio so ASTPL's shareholding mirrors AMPL's (promoters 6.45%, public 93.55% indicatively), transfer on a going-concern basis, and listing on BSE and NSE targeted by Q1 FY28. “The turnover of the Demerged Undertaking of the Company for the financial year ended 31st March 2026 was approximately INR. 157 Crores, representing 13.58% of the total turnover of the Demerged Company for the said year.”
- *Scheme* — Management was reorganised around the split: CFO Rahul Rungta moved to ASTPL in February 2026, MD S. Gurunatha Reddy resigned effective 30 September 2026 to oversee the demerger and join ASTPL's board, and Dr M. V. Reddy was elevated to MD of AMPL from 1 October 2026; BSE and NSE issued no-adverse-observation/no-objection letters on 29 October 2026. “In continuation to my earlier letter dated 03/04/2026 informing my resignation from the post of Managing Director wish to inform you that I am resigning from the position Directorship also with effect from the close of business hours on 30th September, 2026, to oversee the ongoing demerger of the Space and Meteorology business pursuant to the Scheme of Arrangement.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No valuation basis, standalone ASTPL financials, margins, capex, debt or working-capital split, transaction costs, or who initiated it; calls never field demerger questions.

## LEMONTREE — Lemon Tree Hotels Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 6.4/10 · spin-off · 29 filing(s) from CALLS, NSE · first 2026-01-10, latest 2026-09-22

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'nclt_sanction' stage; Fleur Hotels Limited will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; indicated timeline: Press release of 9 January 2026: "The entire process to listing of Fleur is expected to be completed within 12 to 15 months"; on the 29 May 2026 call Keswani said 12 months from then if NCLT is quick, otherwise 18 months; NSE observation letter of 22 September 2026 requires trading to commence within sixty days of the NCLT order

**The stages, as filed:** exchange_noc (2026-09-22) → nclt_sanction (2026-01-10)

**Stated in the filings:** resulting company **Fleur Hotels Limited**; demerged undertaking: ), w ill be demerged into Fleur Hotels; appointed date 2026-04-01; pro-forma statements referenced.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Asset-heavy hotel ownership and development undertaking: 12 hotels (11 operating, 1 under construction) plus development capabilities, demerged into Fleur Hotels — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* Promoters Patanjali Govind Keswani and Spank Management hold 22.28% of LTH, 7.34% directly in Fleur post-scheme; Keswani non-retiring Executive Chairman of Fleur, turns non-executive at Lemon Tree March 2027
- *What it reveals:* Fleur becomes India's largest hotel owner by rooms (5,556 rooms, 39 hotels; FY25 revenue Rs 1,189 cr, net EBITDA Rs 509 cr), carries all group debt, and gets Warburg's Rs 960 crore; Lemon Tree is left debt-free, 80% EBITDA-margin fee business
- *Selling pressure:* likely — Odd-lot entitlement (20 Fleur shares per 311 LTH shares) in a newly listed asset-heavy company whose investor base differs from asset-light Lemon Tree
- *Parent or spin:* both · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Fleur's pro-forma financials in the Q4 FY26 presentation (FY27 net EBITDA ~Rs 850 crore) and Fleur's Information Memorandum
- *In their words:* “This structure ensures that the shareholders of the Company directly participate in the economic value of the hotel-ownership and development undertaking through listed shares of the Transferee Company.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Management framed the demerger as splitting one company that had been doing two businesses with two different investor bases: an asset-heavy business that designs, develops, finances and owns hotels (pension funds, insurance companies betting on inflation, repricing and annuity yield) and an asset-light business that monetises brand, management, loyalty, distribution and technology with almost no capital intensity. Keswani said Lemon Tree had only built hotels in 2004-2007 because owners would not hand their hotels to an unknown brand, and that with the brand now widely recognised (MakeMyTrip's CEO told him 20-25% of occupancy comes from them the moment a Lemon Tree opens) there was no reason to keep owning assets rather than monetise the brand — explicitly the Marriott/Host Hotels and Hilton/Park Hotels playbook. Mechanically (Composite Scheme approved 9 Jan 2026, appointed date 1 April 2026): Carnation Hotels and Hamstede Living merge into LTH; Oriole Dr. Fresh, Canary, Sukhsagar and Manakin merge into Fleur against shares to LTH; and the Demerged Undertaking — 11 operating hotels plus Aurika Shimla under construction, the investment in Arum (Aurika Shillong, 165 rooms) and the entire development capability/team with exclusivity on all future ownership, leasing and development — demerges into Fleur, with 20 Fleur shares for every 311 LTH shares (demerged division turnover Rs 23,037.34 lakh, 59.90% of LTH standalone turnover; 1,563 operating rooms across 15 hotels per the presentation, 1,820 keys/17 hotels per the press release). A second stated problem was conflict of interest: development capability was moved to Fleur with 'Chinese firewalls' so Fleur shareholders could never feel Lemon Tree was cherry-picking the best assets for itself, and Lemon Tree must refer new acquisition/development opportunities to Fleur. All group debt (about Rs 1,300 crore at demerger, Rs 1,500 crore total borrowings at FY26-end, cost of debt 7.42%) goes to Fleur, leaving Lemon Tree debt-free with only technology and marketing spend, forcing the Board to frame a dividend/shareholder-reward policy. Warburg Pincus (Coastal Cedar Investments B.V.) bought APG's entire 41.09% of Fleur and committed up to Rs 960 crore of primary equity, giving Fleur roughly Rs 3,000 crore of deployable capital at 1:1 debt-equity against 2,500+ rooms under active discussion and Aurika Nehru Place (572 rooms, ~Rs 700 crore); post-scheme LTH shareholders own ~74% of Fleur (32.96% direct plus ~41% through LTH) versus the 59% LTH owns today, and Fleur lists separately for 'transparent price discovery and market-driven valuation of the asset-heavy business'.

**How it evolved:** The idea was first visible as a Fleur listing aspiration in the Nov 2024 call, where Keswani said debt-freedom would come sooner 'if we list Fleur before that' and put an IPO 'within the next 2-3 years at most'; in the Aug 2025 call he disclosed that committees of directors had been set up in both Lemon Tree and Fleur to evaluate transferring LTH's assets into Fleur via a demerger and listing it, alongside splitting the management teams (Neelendra Singh for LTH from 1 October, Saurabh Shatdal for Fleur), with listing hoped for end-CY2026. In the Nov 2025 call it was 'in process' with a Board subcommittee and a promise of 'some other even more exciting stuff' within three months; the scheme, the Warburg/APG transactions and the 74%/26% shareholding math were announced in the Jan 2026 (15 January) dedicated call with a 12-15 month path to listing. By the Feb 2026 call Keswani confirmed the scheme was effective from 1 April and, responding to Ashish Kumar's request, promised pro forma financials for both entities; those pro formas appeared with the Jun 2026 (29 May) results, where CCI approval (April 2026), Warburg's completed purchase of APG's stake and a longer 12-18 month NCLT-dependent timeline were given, followed by NSE/BSE observation letters on 22 September 2026.

**What management expects from it:** Lemon Tree: debt-free, fee/brand/tech-only, EBITDA margin from ~60% pro forma to 70-80% steady state, ~60% PAT margin, high ROCE, free cash funding dividends. Fleur: India's largest owner (5,600 rooms, 39 hotels), net EBITDA Rs 850 crore FY27 and Rs 1,000+ crore FY28, ~48%+ post-fee margins, Warburg-backed capital for 2,500+ rooms, capital growth not dividends, and separately listed for market valuation.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Jan 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=098527b9-fd65-4aa9-9c6d-1ac184b2eda0.pdf)* — Asked directly by Kunal Lakhan (CLSA) what was wrong with the old structure, Keswani said the hotel business has two subsets with two different investor types — developers/owners wanting chunky yield and inflation-linked annuity returns versus asset-light investors betting on brand and management — and Lemon Tree was a combination of both. “We have actually separated 2 types of businesses. One is asset heavy, long -term appreciating asset, capital intensive. It has a different kind of investor, and this business has a very different kind of investor, and we wanted to actually attract both types of investors.”
- *[Jan 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=098527b9-fd65-4aa9-9c6d-1ac184b2eda0.pdf)* — He explained the historical accident being corrected: hotels were built only to establish the brand, and with the brand now established the company should monetise it instead of owning assets. “We were forced to build hotels to build our brand. But once we build our brand, technically, we do not need hotels because now it is time for Lemon Tree to monetize its brand, which is enormous recall.”
- *[Jan 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=098527b9-fd65-4aa9-9c6d-1ac184b2eda0.pdf)* — The transfer of the development capability and exclusive development mandate to Fleur was driven by a conflict-of-interest problem — Fleur minorities fearing Lemon Tree would keep the best projects for itself — and was solved with firewalls. “Development capability was an issue which was raised in order to maximize Fleur's growth, we did not want shareholders of Fleur to ever feel that Lemon Tree when it recommends any assets was cherry -picking, which means Lemon Tree would say, I have got this very nice asset in Delhi, why should I offer it to Fleur.”
- *[Jan 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=098527b9-fd65-4aa9-9c6d-1ac184b2eda0.pdf)* — All of Lemon Tree's debt moves to Fleur: Fleur carries roughly Rs 1,300 crore of debt against a ~Rs 900 crore net EBITDA and can borrow another ~Rs 1,300 crore, while Lemon Tree goes to zero debt. “Firstly, when this demerger happens, all the debt, including the Lemon Tree's debt, after adjustment is being transferred to Fleur. Fleur will have 100% of our debt and Lemon Tree will have zero debt.”
- *[Jan 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=098527b9-fd65-4aa9-9c6d-1ac184b2eda0.pdf)* — Keswani justified keeping a ~41% indirect stake in Fleur (challenged by Jinesh Joshi on hold-co discount) as Lemon Tree retaining 'skin in the game' as Fleur's manager, with natural dilution as Fleur raises capital; he quantified that Rs 1,000 crore deployed by Fleur generates ~Rs 350 crore of turnover, Rs 170-180 crore EBITDA and ~Rs 30 crore of fees for Lemon Tree. “We felt it was prudent to have significant skin in the game at this stage, which means that going forward, it is very possible that Lemon Tree may dilute or even increase its stake over time; this will obviously be a Board decision .”
- *[Jan 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=098527b9-fd65-4aa9-9c6d-1ac184b2eda0.pdf)* — Warburg's Rs 960 crore primary commitment plus Fleur's own cash and 1:1 debt gives roughly Rs 3,000 crore to deploy pre-listing against 2,500 rooms in active discussion; Keswani guided Fleur to over Rs 1,000 crore net EBITDA by FY28 and Lemon Tree to 80% EBITDA margin / 60% PAT margin. “We have potentially about Rs 3,000 crores available to deploy in this growth before we list.”
- *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=a03e8364-4037-407c-8929-d956c0976b96.pdf)* — Opening the call with pro forma financials for both entities, Keswani described the transaction as simple — Warburg has bought APG's Fleur stake, Lemon Tree transfers 17 hotels and development capabilities in exchange for Fleur shares to LTH shareholders, and Fleur lists. “This scheme will result in 2 distinct financially sound businesses.”
- *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=a03e8364-4037-407c-8929-d956c0976b96.pdf)* — He restated the economic outcome for each entity: Lemon Tree debt-free, high-margin, high-ROCE and fee/brand-driven; Fleur the consolidated owner of a fully renovated portfolio, post-scheme India's largest hotel platform by inventory at 5,600 rooms and 39 operational hotels. “Post the reorganization , Lemon Tree will emerge as a debt -free, high-margin, high ROCE company generating strong free cash flows from fees and brand -related income.”
- *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=a03e8364-4037-407c-8929-d956c0976b96.pdf)* — Shareholder arithmetic: LTH shareholders end up with close to 74% of Fleur (33% direct, ~41% through Lemon Tree) versus the 59% Lemon Tree directly owns in Fleur today, before Warburg's primary infusion; Keswani also said he will cease to be executive at Lemon Tree from March 2027 and focus on Fleur as Executive Chair. “Post reorganization , Lemon Tree shareholders will effectively own close to 74% of Fleur Hotels, 33% directly and about 41% indirectly through Lemon Tree.”
- *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=a03e8364-4037-407c-8929-d956c0976b96.pdf)* — Answering Achal Kumar, Keswani confirmed Fleur will be brand-agnostic post-demerger and may hand assets to other operators — Lemon Tree has no automatic right to Fleur's hotels and must earn them on results. “Yes. But Lemon Tree must be able to deliver best results to get it . Just because Lemon Tree has skin in the game with Fleur does not mean that it has an automatic right to any asset that Fleur develops.”
- *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=a03e8364-4037-407c-8929-d956c0976b96.pdf)* — On capital allocation after the split, Lemon Tree is expected to need almost no capital and move to distributing profits, while Fleur will retain capital for growth rather than pay dividends. “Lemon Tree will not need any significant capital other than potentially investments in technology or in marketing and so on. It will be essentially a zero -debt cash accretive company.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=b0215f7f-3372-4231-8b2f-7f433eb77faf.pdf)* — Keswani confirmed the scheme is effective from 1 April and that Lemon Tree becomes debt-free from next year, with all assets and debt going to Fleur and fee income becoming free cash; the Board must decide a dividend policy within six months. “What will happen is in the scheme of demerger, all the assets of Lemon Tree, including its debt will be transferred to Fleur. Lemon Tree will immediately effectively be a debt -free company from next year.”

*Not explained on the calls:* Absolute valuation of the demerged undertaking and Warburg's price for APG's stake, Fleur's issue price, hold-co discount size, post-demerger ROE, and fate of the two retained leases.

## NATCOPHARM — NATCO Pharma Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 6.4/10 · spin-off · 20 filing(s) from CALLS, NSE, NSE-BM, NSE-deep · first 2025-11-14, latest 2026-09-09

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'exchange_noc' stage; Natco Crop Health Sciences Limited will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**The stages, as filed:** announced (2026-03-24) → exchange_noc (2026-09-09)

**Stated in the filings:** resulting company **Natco Crop Health Sciences Limited**.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Agrochemicals (Crop Health Sciences) division — pesticides, insecticides, herbicides, biostimulants — demerged into Natco Crop Health Sciences Limited — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* Promoter and Promoter Group hold 8,84,65,126 of 17,91,09,870 shares (~49%); 1:1 entitlement carries that stake into the Resulting Company. Demerged Company retains 20% post-listing; director P.S.R.K. Prasad sits on Natco Crop Health Sciences' board.
- *What it reveals:* Demerged turnover was only ₹60.62 crore, 1.48% of total; FY25 agro segment result was a ₹1,458 million loss. Management says it reached ~₹140 crore sales and roughly EBITDA breakeven. Separation removes a loss-maker from pharma and exposes an early-growth agro business.
- *Selling pressure:* likely — Tiny (1.48% of turnover), loss-making, different industry; 4,22,879 pharma shareholders receive 1:1 agrochemical shares, with parent holding 20%.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* The revised Scheme to be filed with Stock Exchanges post Rights Issue — check the share swap ratio and agro segment numbers.
- *In their words:* “The segregation is also expected to unlock the value of the business verticals of the Demerged Company.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

NATCO is demerging its Crop Health Sciences (Agrochemicals) division into Natco Crop Health Sciences Limited, leaving the listed parent as a pure pharmaceutical company (FDFs, APIs, oncology-led branded/complex generics). Management's stated reason is that the two verticals carry different risk-reward profiles and serve entirely different customers — Rajesh Chebiyam said the demerger "gives a more focused approach because the business, ultimately, the customers are quite different" — so a dedicated management, channel and product strategy (differentiated, patent-controlled, limited-competition molecules like the fungicide GLANZ and CTPR combinations) can be run without competing for attention inside a much larger pharma P&L. The second reason is valuation and capital: agro turnover was only INR 60.62 crore in FY25, i.e. 1.48% of total turnover, against FY25 group revenue of INR 4,784 crore and PAT of INR 1,883.4 crore, and Rajeev Nannapaneni said shareholders "will get another business which is not being valued in our system because it is of a very tiny business and a very large business in pharma"; separately listed, "it can raise its own capital and grow by itself." The timing was deliberately set after the division approached breakeven — segment loss of about INR 150 crore in FY25 (including a INR 50 crore non-cash PP&E impairment taken in Q4 FY25), narrowing to a INR 3.2 crore loss in Q1 FY26 on INR 34.7 crore of sales, EBITDA-positive at INR 52.4 crore of sales in Q2 FY26, and roughly INR 140 crore of FY26 sales versus INR 60 crore the prior year, against the INR 150–170 crore management had said was needed for EBITDA breakeven. The Scheme adds the corporate-finance logic: focused growth, operational rationalisation, optimum use of resources, and the ability for each business to "address independent business opportunities, pursue efficient capital allocation and attract different sets of investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders," plus unlocking the value of the verticals. Shareholders get 1 share of the resulting company for every 1 NATCO share, with NATCO retaining 20% of the post-listing equity to keep supporting a business "still at its early growth stages" — so holders retain 100% of the ultimate economic interest (80% direct, 20% through NATCO). The push came from public-market shareholders, not lenders or partners: an investor on the Nov 14, 2025 call asked directly about "value unlocking for the shareholders," and management separately cited shareholder feedback that NATCO's profit base was too concentrated. Agro is almost entirely domestic ("predominantly domestic" sales, with 25–30% input cost inflation flagged in 2026), which management contrasts with the export-weighted pharma business.

**How it evolved:** On the Feb 13, 2025 and May 29, 2025 calls there was no demerger talk — only agro losses, the INR 50 crore impairment and a INR 120–170 crore breakeven target; the Aug 13, 2025 call reported the loss down to INR 3.2 crore with still no mention. The board gave in-principle approval to evaluate the demerger on Sep 25, 2025, and Rajeev first discussed it publicly on the Nov 14, 2025 call ("demerge this business from the main company and list it separately... targeting that for the year 2026"), framing it as value unlocking plus the ability to raise its own capital; the board approved incorporating the wholly-owned resulting company on Nov 14, 2025. On Feb 12, 2026 the timeline was guided to "October, November" 2026 (8–9 months), and the Scheme itself was approved on Mar 24, 2026 with a 1:1 share entitlement, appointed date Oct 1, 2026 and 20% retained by NATCO; the May 29, 2026 call reiterated focus and different customers as the primary reason. By Sep 9, 2026 the Scheme had stock-exchange observation letters but had not been filed with the NCLT, because the INR 1,279.36 crore rights issue at INR 750/share (allotted Oct 23, 2026) changes the capital structure — the board decided to re-cut and re-file the Scheme after the rights issue while keeping the same swap ratio.

**What management expects from it:** Agro: dedicated management focus, its own capital raising, differentiated limited-competition products, growth past breakeven from roughly INR 140 crore sales. Pharma: a cleaner, focused oncology/complex-generics entity. For shareholders: value unlocked in a business "not being valued in our system," a complete see-through into both, operational efficiency, efficient capital allocation, and distinct investor/lender bases.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ac8f848f-8703-4403-9ae3-cb2d420d47da.pdf)* — First public confirmation of the plan: demerge Crop Health Sciences out of the parent and list it separately, targeted for 2026, disclosed alongside the division reaching roughly EBITDA breakeven at INR 52.4 crore of quarterly sales. “I think we have announced earlier that we will demerge this business from the main company and list it separately and we are targeting that for the year 2026.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ac8f848f-8703-4403-9ae3-cb2d420d47da.pdf)* — Rajeev defines the value-unlock logic in response to an investor question: separate listing gives the business special focus and the ability to raise its own capital and grow independently, now that it is breaking even. “Value unlocking means I think what we see is this business now is about breaking even now. So, we will list it separately and then we will have special focus on this and it can raise its own capital and grow by itself.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ac8f848f-8703-4403-9ae3-cb2d420d47da.pdf)* — The core valuation argument: the agro business is too small to be valued inside a pharma company of NATCO's size, and shareholders will get a complete see-through into both businesses. “I think you will get another business which is not being valued in our system because it is of a very tiny business and a very large business in pharma.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=7ea4dc21-a77e-4e6d-967e-2da2d51bc890.pdf)* — Timeline guidance: the process has started, with an internal goal of completing in the next 8–9 months (around October–November 2026), but no firm date committed. “I think we have started the process. So , I think roughly, we're thinking by October, November, but I don't want to say any definite time lines, but this is our, what should I say, goal to do.”
- *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=230327e4-9a77-4095-b46d-b9c836cc9b96.pdf)* — Management's clearest operating rationale, from the head of Crop Health Sciences: a focused approach is needed because the agro customer base is entirely different from pharma, with FY26 agro sales of about INR 140 crore versus INR 60 crore the year before. “So, as you're aware, so we're in the process of demerging the business. And one of the primary reasons we felt also it gives a more focused approach because the business, ultimately, the customers are quite different.”
- *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=230327e4-9a77-4095-b46d-b9c836cc9b96.pdf)* — Growth plans — new differentiated, patent-controlled, limited-competition products, more channel partners and more people — are tied directly back to the demerger as the reason for sharper focus. “So I think we're fairly confident going forward. And that's also one of the main reasons for demerging and having more focus on the business.”
- *Scheme* — The Mar 24, 2026 Scheme of Arrangement grounds the demerger in differing risk-reward profiles of the pharmaceutical and agrochemicals verticals; agro turnover was INR 60.62 crore in FY25, 1.48% of total company turnover. “The Board of Directors of the Demerged Company believe that the risk and reward associated with each of the aforesaid business verticals are different.”
- *Scheme* — The Scheme's capital-markets rationale: each business can chase its own opportunities, allocate capital efficiently and attract its own investor and lender base, alongside focused growth, operational rationalisation and value unlocking. “Each business would be able to address independent business opportunities, pursue efficient capital allocation and attract different sets of investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders.”
- *Scheme* — NATCO keeps 20% of the post-listing equity of the resulting company so it can keep funding and strategically supporting an early-stage business; shareholders get 1 new share for every 1 NATCO share, retaining 100% of the ultimate economic interest (80% direct plus 20% indirect). “Further, the Demerged Company intends to retain the current shareholding in the Resulting Company (20% of post listing shareholding) in order to continue to offer support to the Agrochemicals Business which is still at its early growth stages and help in monitoring the progress and providing strategic support.”
- *Scheme* — The Nov 14, 2025 board filing states the purpose as unlocking value in the core pharmaceutical business while giving each entity operational flexibility, dedicated management and separate brand positioning. “To demerge the Agro business of the Company into a separate entity, the move shall enable value unlocking of the core business (pharmaceuticals) and enhance long -term growth.”
- *[Jun 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=d43e2593-6819-4d99-b9a6-c3019c901490.pdf)* — Pre-demerger baseline for why the division was a drag: a INR 50 crore non-cash impairment on agro property, plant and machinery in Q4 FY25, FY25 agro revenue of about INR 60 crore, and INR 160–170 crore needed just to be EBITDA positive. “So, I think this year, we feel we are going to hit that critical mass where we'll start breaking even. We are doing about INR60 crores net revenue last year. So, I think we need to hit about INR160 crores to INR170 crores at least to have that EBITDA positive.”
- *Scheme* — The Sep 9, 2026 board update: the Scheme had received observation letters from both exchanges but was not filed with the NCLT because the INR 1,300 crore rights issue changes the capital structure, so the Scheme will be amended and re-filed post-issue with the swap ratio unchanged. “The fund raising by way of a Rights Issue proposed at the meeting of the board of directors held on September 09, 2026 is expected to result in change to the Company's capital structure and shareholding pattern and consequently would require necessary changes to the Scheme.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No standalone agro financials, debt/asset split, valuation or swap-ratio basis; no post-demerger profitability, capital needs, board/management, listing date, or revised Scheme terms.

## VEDL — Vedanta Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **LISTED <1Y — selling-pressure window; the bargain forms here** · score 6.4/10 · spin-off · 43 filing(s) from CALLS, NSE, NSE-register · first 2025-12-03, latest 2026-10-03

> **Listing:** LISTED — Talwandi Sabo Power Limited trades since about 2026-04-20

**The stages, as filed:** announced (2026-07-30) → nclt_sanction (2025-12-03) → record_date (2026-04-20)

**Stated in the filings:** resulting company **Talwandi Sabo Power Limited**; pro-forma statements referenced; size hint: 11% of ebitda.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Merchant Power Undertaking — Vedanta's merchant thermal power generation business (Athena, Meenakshi), demerged into Talwandi Sabo Power Limited — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* Each Resulting Company issued 1 share for every 1 Vedanta share, so promoter group (Vedanta Resources, 54.72% of VEDL as on June 30, 2026) carried over pro rata; promoters excluded from VEDL ESOS/ESPP 2026
- *What it reveals:* Separation reveals leverage: Vedanta Power's net debt/EBITDA 4.7x, highest of the five, though debt is mostly structural long-term PFC/REC with 7-10 year maturities; residual Vedanta sits at 0.30x with AA+/stable
- *Selling pressure:* likely — 1:1 shares pushed to every Vedanta holder; thermal power unrelated to parent's metals/mining mandate; most levered of the five entities
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Vedanta Power Limited's own post-listing results and production release, plus Athena Unit 1 restart update and its PFC/REC debt maturity schedule
- *In their words:* “The de-merger has been architected with precision on capital structure, aligning debt with earning strength and growth stage of each resulting company.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Management framed the separation as the core of "Vedanta 2.0": breaking one monolithic diversified natural-resources company into five independent, sector-specific pure-play listed companies — Vedanta Limited (residual: Zinc India/HZL, Zinc International, Copper, Ferrochrome/FACOR, Nickel), Vedanta Aluminium Metal Ltd, Vedanta Power/Talwandi Sabo Power (merchant power), Vedanta Oil & Gas/Malco Energy (Cairn), and Vedanta Iron & Steel — so that each could "chart out their own growth trajectory and attract respective thematic investors" rather than being valued as a conglomerate (Apr 2026, Apr 2025: "pure-play entities that will enhance strategic focus and operational flexibility"). The stated problem was that a single balance sheet and single capital-allocation process blurred very different businesses: Zinc India at 56% EBITDA margin and $959/t COP, aluminium at 38% margin, versus a Copper trading business running ~1% margin, and a power business that wants to add 10–12 GW. The fix was a capital structure "architected with precision… aligning debt with earning strength and growth stage of each resulting company": of $5.5bn net debt (group leverage 0.95x), $3.5bn goes to Aluminium (1.3x), Power sits at 4.7x on long-dated PFC/REC paper, Vedanta Limited keeps ~$1bn (0.4x), while Oil & Gas is nil-debt and Iron & Steel carries no more than $0.2bn. Specific frictions the split removes: the Copper brand fee drops from 3% to 0.75% on ~$3.1–3.2bn of revenue (~$65m, +2.25% to EBITDA), taking Copper margin from ~1% toward at least 5% in FY27; the dividend policy moves from "prescriptive" to "descriptive", from rule-based (minimum 30% of profit) to principle-based, and the mandate to upstream Hindustan Zinc dividends within six months falls away; Ajay Goel also called it "an opportunity… from taxation viewpoint" via recast balance sheets, accumulated losses and unabsorbed depreciation. Third parties shaped the terms: lenders demanded debt allocation be "broadly aligned with the bankers as a precondition for granting NOC"; the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas objected at NCLT over ~$512–520m of disputed dues and was satisfied only by a Vedanta corporate guarantee covering the full alleged claims, with any arbitration outcome ring-fenced to Oil & Gas; creditor SEPCO was settled in full for ₹660 crore "as part of demerger proceedings… paving the way for a proposed demerger process", and a ₹1,248 crore cash-backed bank guarantee was lodged with NCLAT over the TSPL power demerger. Management also pointed to equity-side demand — "many anchor investors domestically and globally are very keen to come in the cap table" of the de-merged entities as a fresh deleveraging avenue for VRL's remaining $4.7bn. Three months after listing, the Board extended the same logic to a second, vertical separation: ~2,264 acres and ~53,185 sq ft of surplus real estate (22 assets, only ₹1.26 crore of FY26 turnover, 0.001% of standalone revenue) into Vedanta Property Platforms Ltd at 1 share for every 20, because the portfolio was "historically subject to limited focused utilisation, resulting in sub-optimal visibility… and value realization."

**How it evolved:** The demerger was already a live execution item by the Feb 2025 call (Jan 31, 2025), where Ajay Goel flagged the Feb 18 shareholder/creditor meetings as "the important stage of execution"; on the Apr 2025 call (Apr 30, 2025) Deshnee Naidoo recast it as creating "pure-play entities" under Vedanta 2.0 with completion guided for September 2025. It then slipped repeatedly on legal and stakeholder hurdles — Aug 2025 (Jul 31, 2025) disclosed the NCLT second-motion part-hearing of July 2 with the next date Aug 20, an NCLAT interim stay on the TSPL power order, and the MoPNG objection; Nov 2025 (Oct 31, 2025) resolved SEPCO for ₹660 crore and MoPNG via a Vedanta corporate guarantee, guiding to a final Nov 12 hearing and five listings by FY26-end. Jan 2026 (Jan 29, 2026) reported NCLT approval on Dec 16, 2025 (power on Jan 9, 2026) and shifted the detail toward mechanics — bank NOCs conditioned on debt allocation, recast balance sheets, tax structuring — targeting Apr 1 effectiveness; Apr 2026 (Apr 29, 2026) set the record date at May 1 with mid-June listing, 4 extra shares per share, and added two new rationales not previously spelled out: the Copper brand-fee cut to 0.75% and five independent dividend policies. By the Jul 30, 2026 filings the plan had extended beyond the original five, with a sixth vertical split of surplus real estate into Vedanta Property Platforms Ltd at 1:20.

**What management expects from it:** Five pure-plays each chasing its own growth and thematic investors; debt matched to earnings — Oil & Gas nil, Iron & Steel <$0.2bn, Aluminium 1.3x, Power 4.7x, Vedanta Ltd 0.4x; Copper brand fee 3%→0.75% lifting margin ~1%→5%+; independent dividend policies with HZL upstream mandate dropped; tax efficiency from recast balance sheets; anchor investors entering entity cap tables to deleverage VRL; real estate platform targeting ₹30,000 crore+.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Feb 2025](https://www.vedantalimited.com/uploads/investor-overview/financial-results/VedantaEarnings-transcript-Jan31-2025.pdf)* — The demerger was already at the shareholder/creditor-vote stage, pitched purely as investor value unlock, with no operational rationale given on this call. “On the demerger front, we are in the important stage of execution , the shareholders and the creditors meeting scheduled on Feb 18th. This transformative step is poised to unlock significant value for our investors.”
- *[Apr 2025](https://www.vedantalimited.com/uploads/investor-overview/financial-results/Vedanta-CallTranscript-Apr30-2025_v2.pdf)* — First explicit statement of the design goal — pure-play entities for strategic focus and operational flexibility — inside the Vedanta 2.0 ambition of a $100bn critical minerals, energy and technology powerhouse; completion then guided for September 2025. “We are making good progress with our demerger plan, aiming to create pure-play entities that will enhance strategic focus and operational flexibility.”
- *[Apr 2025](https://www.vedantalimited.com/uploads/investor-overview/financial-results/Vedanta-CallTranscript-Apr30-2025_v2.pdf)* — A shareholder (Ashish Kejriwal, Nuvama) pressed that mining leases — Sijimali bauxite and the coal blocks held under Vedanta Limited — must first be transferred to Vedanta Aluminium before the split can complete; management confirmed a parallel approvals plan. “Ashish, you are right. This is part of the overall approvals that we have in our sight.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.vedantalimited.com/uploads/investor-overview/financial-results/2026/Vedanta_Transcript_Jul31_2025.pdf)* — Execution stalled in two forums at once: the NCLT second-motion petition was part-heard on July 2 with the next date Aug 20, and NCLAT granted an interim stay on the TSPL power demerger order, backed by a ₹1,248 crore fully cash-backed bank guarantee over the SEPCO creditor matter. “Separately, the NCL AT has granted an interim stay on TSPL, our power demerger order by NCLT, with the next hearing scheduled on 4th August.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.vedantalimited.com/uploads/investor-overview/financial-results/2026/Vedanta_Transcript_Jul31_2025.pdf)* — The Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas objected at NCLT, questioning whether the demerged, standalone Cairn oil & gas P&L could absorb disputed dues if arbitration went against Vedanta — i.e. a regulator worrying that separation strips a weaker entity of parent support. “In the last NCLT hearing, they did express concern about the payments of any of the disputed dues that may become payable by Cairn in case the ongoing arbitration ruling, as we have all learned now, comes in their favor.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.vedantalimited.com/uploads/investor-overview/financial-results/2026/VEDL_Q2FY26_Transcript.pdf)* — A long-standing SEPCO creditor dispute was settled in full for ₹660 crore (part of ₹1,547 crore of net exceptional items that quarter) explicitly to clear the path for the scheme. “As part of demerger proceedings, a full and final settlement of Rs. 660 Cr has been done with SEPCO , thereby resolving a long -standing dispute, paving the way for a proposed demerger process.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.vedantalimited.com/uploads/investor-overview/financial-results/2026/VEDL_Q2FY26_Transcript.pdf)* — MoPNG's objection — over roughly $512–520m of alleged claims — was resolved not by cash but by a Vedanta corporate guarantee covering the full extent of the claims, so the demerged oil & gas entity would not carry the obligation. “Their concern has been taken care of by us providing a corporate guarantee from Vedanta.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.vedantalimited.com/uploads/investor-overview/financial-results/2026/VEDL_Q2FY26_Transcript.pdf)* — Five simultaneous listings by FY26-end were framed as the vehicle for sharper strategic focus, with Goel adding that it unlocks "focused value across our five verticals". “This will set the stage for the listing of all five demerge d entities by the end of FY '26, enabling greater strategic focus and enhanced value creation for all stakeholders.”
- *[Jan 2026](https://www.vedantalimited.com/uploads/investor-overview/financial-results/2026/Transcript_29Jan2026.pdf)* — After NCLT approval on Dec 16, 2025 (power order Jan 9, 2026), the rationale was stated as three things at once — sharper strategy, stronger standalone balance sheets, faster growth — with Q3 results already reported under Ind AS 105 demerger accounting. “This marks a defining moment in our journey, one that empowers our businesses to sharpen the strategies, strengthen the balance sheets and accelerate growth with the aim of unlocking shareholder value.”
- *[Jan 2026](https://www.vedantalimited.com/uploads/investor-overview/financial-results/2026/Transcript_29Jan2026.pdf)* — Lenders drove the capital-structure design: debt allocation across the five entities had to be agreed with banks before they would issue no-objection certificates, with $6.7bn of Vedanta India consol net debt split by asset ratio and each entity's own cash-generation and debt-servicing capability. “When we went to the banker seeking NOC, in that case, debt allocation was broadly aligned with the bankers as a precondition for granting NOC for demerger approval.”
- *[Jan 2026](https://www.vedantalimited.com/uploads/investor-overview/financial-results/2026/Transcript_29Jan2026.pdf)* — Goel named taxation and deleveraging as further gains — recast balance sheets, accumulated losses and unabsorbed depreciation per entity — alongside the intent to make oil & gas and iron & steel debt-free, funded partly by the ₹3,000 crore HZL OFS. “One thing I can confirm to the entire audience and to the stakeholders at large, that demerger in fact, becomes an opportunity across the areas.”
- *[Apr 2026](https://www.vedantalimited.com/uploads/investor-overview/financial-results/2026/Vedanta-Transcript-Apr29-2026.pdf)* — Final articulation: five sector-specific pure-play companies whose purpose is independent growth paths and dedicated thematic investor bases; record date May 1, 2026, one Vedanta share yielding four additional shares, listing targeted by Q1 FY27 (mid-June). “This will entail creation of five independent sector -specific pure -play companies, allowing each company to chart out their own growth trajectory and attract respective thematic investors.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No per-entity EBITDA/valuation targets, no quantified stranded corporate or listing costs, no reason the other four brand fees stay at 3%, no real-estate monetisation timeline or revenue model.

### The business being separated — its own numbers

**Power (Merchant Power Undertaking — reported as the 'Power' business segment under discontinued operations from FY2026)** · unit ₹ crore · Operating profit = segment results (EBITDA), a non-GAAP measure as reported by the CODM; revenue is external revenue (excludes inter-segment: nil in FY2024/FY2025, ₹170 crore in FY2026 for discontinued Power, and excludes other operating income). FY2026 and FY2025 figures are the 'Power' segment under DISCONTINUED operations (the demerged merchant/thermal power business, excluding captive power); the separate continuing-operations Power segment (Mettur + wind) is excluded — FY2026: external revenue 135, EBITDA 89; FY2025: external revenue 137, EBITDA 87 (Annual Report 2026 — pages 260, 261). FY2024 is the undivided consolidated Power segment (no continuing/discontinued split was presented), so it includes the retained wind/Mettur power. Consolidated-level segment reporting only; the full-year FY2025 Power segment as originally reported in AR2025 was external revenue 6,159 and EBITDA 737 (Annual Report 2025 — page 252).
