## ASTRAL — Astral Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 5.8/10 · spin-off · 8 filing(s) from NSE, NSE-deep · first 2026-03-23, latest 2026-07-29

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; indicated timeline: June 25, 2026: "Upon the effectiveness of the Scheme and subject to receipt of regulatory approvals, the New Shares will be listed on the Stock Exchanges" — no date given; Scheme withdrawn July 29, 2026, so no listing

**Stated in the filings:** entitlement **1 for every 1**; size hint: 21% of turnover.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Chemicals Business Undertaking — adhesives, sealants, construction chemicals — into Astral Chemie, merging with its paints/coatings business — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* Promoters and Promoter Group hold 100% of Resulting Company pre-Scheme, 54.22% post-Scheme (mirror of parent); MD Sandeep Engineer's son Saumya runs adhesives and paints.
- *What it reveals:* Chemicals turnover ₹12,663 million, 21% of Astral's ₹59,076 million; adhesive India EBITDA 15.1%, UK turned 6.5% positive, paints still loss-making (₹6 crore in Q4) — yet consultant said scale insufficient to stand alone.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — Board withdrew the Scheme on July 29, 2026; no shares of the Resulting Company will be issued or listed.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Independent Consultant's scale findings on the Chemical Business; next quarterly segment numbers for adhesives and paints.
- *In their words:* “Accordingly, the Board has decided to withdraw the Composite Scheme of Arrangement now, and no further steps will be undertaken in relation to the proposed the Composite Scheme of Arrangement.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Astral's board approved a Composite Scheme on 25 June 2026 that would (i) demerge the Chemicals Business Undertaking — adhesives, sealants, polyvinyl acetate, cyanoacrylates, solvent cements, silicone sealants, epoxy resins, construction chemicals, putties and specialty chemicals added 'through recent strategic acquisitions of DSS' — out of Astral Limited into its wholly-owned subsidiary Astral Chemie Limited (formerly Astral Coatings Pvt Ltd), which already holds the Paints & Coatings (Gem/Astral Paints) business, and (ii) amalgamate another wholly-owned subsidiary, Al-Aziz Plastics Pvt Ltd (electrofusion/compression fittings, saddles; FY26 turnover ₹373 mn, net worth ₹215 mn), back into Astral alongside Plumbing. The chemicals undertaking was ₹12,663 mn of FY26 turnover, 21% of Astral's ₹59,076 mn standalone revenue (net worth ₹41,058 mn); in the 20 May 2026 analyst meet management described the same mix as 'piping 72%, paint and adhesive 28%' of consolidated sales. The stated reasons: the two verticals have different products, customers, operating models, capital requirements, risk profiles, regulatory frameworks and growth opportunities, so each needs a dedicated leadership team and a specialised board instead of 'overlapping boardroom priorities'; combining all chemical verticals (adhesive, paint, specialty chemicals) under one umbrella was said to yield 'huge cost saving in Plants, Warehousing, Marketing and R&D' from shared labs, machinery and technical staff; capital deployment discipline — eliminating 'internal capital allocation conflicts', letting each vertical set its own capex, working capital and funding, and explicitly helping 'Bathware business in capital allocation discipline' while 'liberating the existing management to focus exclusively on the core plumbing business'; and value unlocking — the Scheme 'eliminates any conglomerate discount', lets global investors, institutions and shareholders back either vertical, and gives 'credit rating agencies, lenders, and research analysts … a clean, unbundled view of each Business vertical's financial and operating metrics'. The Al-Aziz merger was justified on the opposite logic: its fittings and Astral's pipes are interdependent ('their standalone utility is limited'), so merging internalises the supply chain, adds PAN-India plants/depots/field staff, centralises overlapping HDPE, specialty polymer and metallic insert buying for bulk discounts, and removes a separate legal entity's compliance and duplicate roles. Consideration was non-cash: 1 Astral Chemie share of ₹1 for every 1 Astral share held (1:1), Astral Chemie's pre-scheme capital cancelled, so its shareholding mirrored Astral's (promoters 54.22%, public 45.78%) with NSE/BSE listing to be sought; Al-Aziz shares simply extinguished with no new issue. No lender, partner or named investor is recorded as having asked for the split — the only requesters cited are 'various stakeholders, including shareholders, investors and other market participants', and their post-announcement feedback is what stopped it: on 5 July 2026 the board ordered a comprehensive independent review by 'any one of the big four or equivalent firm' (report within 30 days), and on 29 July 2026 that Independent Consultant 'recommended not to proceed … in the present form in light of the current scale of the Chemical Business'. The board withdrew the Scheme entirely, saying it 'may not be in the best interests of the Company and its shareholders' at this stage and that the chemicals demerger 'may be considered once it achieves scale and has financial strength to fund its organic and inorganic growth' — consistent with the chemicals segment's own May 2026 commentary that it was only now ready to scale (adhesives India targeting ₹2,000 cr and paints ₹1,000 cr in 3-4 years, paints still EBITDA-negative with a ₹6 cr Q4 loss).

**How it evolved:** The separation does not appear in any earnings call in the record: the 12 Aug 2025 (Q1 FY26), 6 Nov 2025 (Q2 FY26) and 20 May 2026 analyst-meet transcripts discuss only CPVC backward integration, the Al-Aziz and Nexelon acquisitions, UK/paint turnarounds and ROE pressure, and the 5 Feb 2026 'call' is only an exchange letter with an audio link, no transcript. What the calls do show is mounting investor pressure on the diversification (Sujit Jain on falling ROE and 2x capex overruns in Aug 2025; Sudeep Jain asking for per-acquisition sales/margin/cash-conversion/ROCE disclosure; questions in May 2025 on whether Astral would exit the UK), against management saying the opposite — 'we are not looking to exit any business' (Aug 2025) and 'we also are not looking at any other segments now than whatever the four segments we are in' (20 May 2026). The idea surfaces fully formed in the 25 June 2026 board filing and press release, is put under big-four independent review on 5 July 2026 after 'feedback from various stakeholders post the announcement', and is withdrawn on 29 July 2026 on the consultant's advice, with the demerger deferred until the chemicals business has scale.

**What management expects from it:** Chemicals (adhesives, sealants, construction chemicals plus Gem/Astral paints) gains dedicated leadership, shared R&D/plant/warehouse/marketing cost savings, its own capex and funding decisions, and separately listed equity; Astral keeps plumbing and absorbs Al-Aziz fittings for procurement scale and fewer compliances. Both get ring-fenced capital allocation, unbundled metrics for lenders and analysts, no conglomerate discount, specialised boards.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The 25 June 2026 board approved a composite two-part restructuring: demerge the Chemicals Business (adhesives, sealants, construction chemicals, specialty chemicals from the DSS acquisitions) into wholly-owned Astral Chemie (which holds paints and coatings), and merge Al-Aziz Plastics back into Astral with Plumbing. “Each business has evolved into a distinct business vertical with different products, customer segments, operating models, capital requirements, risk profiles and growth opportunities, demanding focused operational, financial and administrative expertise.”
- *Scheme* — The demerged chemicals undertaking was sized at ₹12,663 million of FY26 turnover, 21% of Astral's ₹59,076 million standalone revenue; Al-Aziz was tiny at ₹373 million turnover and ₹215 million net worth. “The turnover of the Demerged Undertaking for the year ended March 31, 2026 stood at ₹ 12,663 million.”
- *Scheme* — Capital-allocation conflict between verticals was an explicit problem the split was meant to solve, including freeing the Bathware business and letting plumbing management stop splitting attention. “At the same time it will help Bathware business in capital allocation discipline, seamlessly enabling the new management to focus exclusively on driving growth across the core chemical, Adhesive & Sealant, paint, and specialty chemical portfolios, while concurrently liberating the existing management to focus exclusively on the core plumbing business, thereby ensuring that both independent verticals benefit from concentrated domain expertise, optimized operations, and enhanced long-term stakeholder value.”
- *Scheme* — Valuation was named directly: separate listings were to remove the holding-company/conglomerate discount and give lenders, rating agencies and analysts unbundled metrics for each vertical. “The Scheme eliminates any conglomerate discount and allows the capital markets to distinctively value each independent vertical.”
- *Scheme* — Sandeep Engineer framed it as the businesses having outgrown shared management, with shareholders getting 1 Astral Chemie share for each Astral share (1:1) and continuing to own both. “We believe these businesses have now reached a stage where dedicated leadership, greater accountability, sharper strategic focus and independent capital allocation can meaningfully accelerate their next phase of growth.”
- *Scheme* — The Al-Aziz leg used the reverse argument — integration rather than separation — because its fittings need Astral's pipes to be sellable, plus HDPE/polymer procurement scale, PAN-India depots and fewer duplicate compliances. “Given that the Transferee Company's fittings cannot function independently and inherently require specific piping systems manufactured by the Transferor Company, their standalone utility is limited.”
- *Scheme* — Ten days after announcing it, the board put the whole Scheme under a big-four independent review because of shareholder/investor/market feedback, with recommendations due in 30 days. “the management has received feedback from various stakeholders post the announcement of the Scheme. In view of the feedback received, the Board has decided to undertake a comprehensive independent review of the Scheme.”
- *Scheme* — On 29 July 2026 the Scheme was withdrawn outright: the independent consultant judged the chemicals business too small to stand alone in that form. “The Independent Consultant has recommended not to proceed with the Composite Scheme of Arrangement in the present form in light of the current scale of the Chemical Business.”
- *Scheme* — The demerger was deferred rather than abandoned in principle, conditional on the chemicals business reaching scale and being able to self-fund growth and acquisitions. “the demerger of the Chemical Business may be considered once it achieves scale and has financial strength to fund its organic and inorganic growth.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.astralltd.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/Analysts-Meet-2026-Transcript.pdf)* — Six weeks before the announcement, management still presented the chemicals division as an in-house platform just reaching its scaling phase, with adhesives India targeting ₹2,000 crore and paints ₹1,000 crore in 3-4 years and paints not yet EBITDA-positive (₹6 crore Q4 loss) — the very scale shortfall later cited for withdrawal. “The vision is to touch 2000 as fast as we can and we are sure that in next 3 to four years we'll be touching 2000 plus in Indian revenue not UK will be separate.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.astralltd.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/Analysts-Meet-2026-Transcript.pdf)* — Hiranand Savlani framed the company's history as plumbing then chemical diversification, with the chemical platform 'ready' to scale under Astral — no hint of hiving it off. “1996 to 2014 was the plumbing era where the focus was on the plumbing side of the business.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.astralltd.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/Analysts-Meet-2026-Transcript.pdf)* — The segment mix disclosed on the call (72% piping / 28% paint+adhesive consolidated) is the economic basis of the later split, though the Scheme's 21% is on standalone turnover, which excludes the UK adhesive business. “This is basically piping is contributing 72% and paint and adhesive is contributing 28%.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No margin, cost-saving or valuation numbers quantified; DSS acquisition unexplained; Astral Chemie standalone financials, advisor identity, and which stakeholders objected never disclosed; calls never mentioned the demerger.

## APOLLOHOSP — Apollo Hospitals Enterprise Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 5.7/10 · spin-off · 25 filing(s) from CALLS, NSE · first 2025-12-24, latest 2026-06-26

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'nclt_sanction' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; indicated timeline: On May 21, 2026 management said the NCLT-convened shareholder meeting was called for June 24 and they were "hopeful the demerger process is completed by Q4 FY27 as planned earlier," with "end of December or early Q4 FY27" when Apollo Healthtech should get demerged and listed; NSE's December 23, 2025 observation letter requires trading to commence within sixty days of receipt of the NCLT order

**The stages, as filed:** exchange_noc (2025-12-24) → meetings (2026-05-21) → nclt_sanction (2026-04-03)

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Apollo's omnichannel pharmacy and digital health business, demerged into a separately listed company — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* Promoter group held 4,02,87,130 shares (voted 100% for). Shobana Kamineni to be Executive Chairperson of Resultant Company; Rasmeli-funded upside share agreement (max 9% of upside at 4x MOIC) to her and identified employees; new ESOP to be established
- *What it reveals:* A pharmacy/digital platform at ~INR 25,000 crore run-rate revenue with 6.5-7% targeted EBITDA margin, digital losses near breakeven, Keimed distribution consolidated; promoter and investor incentives concentrated in the spin, not the hospital parent
- *Selling pressure:* likely — Shares distributed to all 1.75 lakh AHEL holders in a different industry (pharmacy distribution/digital health) than the hospital parent they own
- *Parent or spin:* spin · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* The Scheme's Demerger Share Entitlement Ratio and the Part E abridged-prospectus disclosures for Apollo Healthtech
- *In their words:* “During the year, we also announced a strategic restructuring of the omnichannel pharmacy and digital health business, an important step towards sharpening focus on unlocking long-term value across our integrated health care platform.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The business being separated is AHEL's omnichannel pharmacy and digital health vertical — Apollo HealthCo, comprising the ~7,500-store Apollo Pharmacy retail/front-end network and the Apollo 24/7 digital platform (46mn users, INR 528 cr quarterly platform GMV) — which is being demerged into Apollo Healthtech Ltd, with Apollo Healthco Ltd and the promoter-linked distributor Keimed Private Limited (which supplies ~60,000 pharmacy stores) amalgamated into the same vehicle, which is then renamed Apollo Healthco Limited and listed; hospital-based pharmacies stay inside Healthcare Services, since as A. Krishnan put it in Aug 2025, 'what we are spinning out is only the retail pharmacies and the online.' The Scheme's own rationale states the problem plainly: the Identified Business Undertaking is 'distinct from other businesses undertaken by the Demerged Company' and 'necessitates a differentiated strategy aligned to its industry specific risks, market dynamics, and growth trajectory', so separation lets hospitals and retail/digital each focus on 'their respective businesses, efficient management, and control', consolidates HealthCo's and Keimed's distribution 'in an independent company focusing exclusively on digital health and pharmacy distribution', and lets the new entity 'build a wider capital and financial base, by attracting a different set of investors, strategic partners, lenders and stakeholders' — plus supply-chain integration, wider assortment, 'improved transparency in the supply chain preventing the entry of counterfeit or substandard medicines', administrative efficiency, board/managerial rationalisation and economies of scale. The financial case management repeated for six straight quarters is scale plus margin convergence: pro-forma combined revenue of INR 4,430 cr in Q1 FY26 (~INR 17,000 cr run-rate, INR 19,000 cr for FY26) becoming a INR 25,000 cr run-rate at 7% EBITDA by Q4 FY27; Sanjiv Gupta's arithmetic was that a 3.2% blended FY25 margin is already 6.4% once Apollo 24/7's losses and the accelerated ESOP charge are stripped out, with offline pharmacy going 7.4%→8-9% on private label (15.5% of pharmacy sales) and Keimed 3.1%→3.5%. The loss drag has in fact collapsed — digital cash losses fell from INR 111 cr (Q4 FY24) and INR 101 cr (Q2 FY25) to INR 29 cr in Q3 FY26 and INR 16 cr in Q4 FY26, with breakeven ex-ESOP guided to Q1 FY27 and including ESOP (~INR 50 cr FY27) by Q3 FY27 — and Apollo HealthCo crossed INR 10,000 cr of annual revenue in FY26, making it listable on its own. Keimed's merger was justified on concrete synergies: shared technology, data, people and product categories, cheaper dark stores (22 today) to push beyond the top six metros to the next ten cities, and private-label penetration across Keimed's franchise base. The push is not purely internal: Rasmeli Limited, the investor holding Class A/B compulsorily convertible preference shares in Apollo Healthco, receives a nominee director in the Resultant Company and signed a June 30, 2025 Upside Agreement sharing up to 9% of its own upside (only above 4x MOIC) with Ms. Shobana Kamineni — proposed Executive Chairperson — and identified employees; after shareholder and proxy-adviser pushback the Company issued clarifications on June 15 and June 19, 2026 adding 10% fall-away thresholds on nomination rights, tiered caps on promoter nominees, an individual 5% waiver, six independent directors and a Lead Independent Director. A second, separate separation was announced in May 2026: AHLL's Apollo Cradle and fertility verticals (INR 450 cr FY26 revenue, INR 45 cr IGAAP EBITDA) were combined with Cloudnine at INR 1,550 cr — 35x EBITDA — for cash plus a 9.9% stake, with the INR 750 cr of cash redeployed into primary care and diagnostics, which management called the funnel into Apollo.

**How it evolved:** The idea surfaced before this window as the 'strategic intent' for Apollo HealthCo (Aug 14, 2024 call) and was tracked through Feb 11, 2025 and the May 31, 2025 (Jun 2025) call purely as the Keimed merger 'progressing well', with a ~15-month timeline and Sanjiv Gupta's 3.2%→7% FY27 margin bridge; the composite Scheme itself was board-approved and filed on June 30, 2025. On the Aug 13, 2025 call management first spelled out the full shape — Apollo HealthCo as it stands gets demerged and separately listed by Q4 FY27, all steps within 18-21 months, only retail plus online moving out, Keimed folded in for technology/data/people/product synergies. Nov 7, 2025 and Feb 11, 2026 were process updates (statutory steps on track; CCI and SEBI approvals obtained, NSE no-objection Dec 23, 2025, NCLT filed and hearings begun, Keimed's subsidiaries consolidated to 100%), and the May 21, 2026 call set the NCLT-convened shareholder meeting for June 24, 2026 with completion still Q4 FY27. In the final stretch the plan changed on governance rather than structure: clarifications dated June 15 and June 19, 2026 added nomination-right fall-away thresholds in response to shareholder feedback, and on June 24, 2026 the Scheme passed with 90.44% of all votes and 85.71% of public votes in favour, but 14.31% of institutional votes against.

**What management expects from it:** Apollo Healthtech becomes a pure-play pharmacy and digital health company: INR 25,000 cr run-rate revenue at 6.5-7% EBITDA by Q4 FY27 (FY26 exit 4.3%), digital at breakeven, Keimed 3.1%-to-3.5%, offline pharmacy 8-9% on private label, its own investors, lenders and board. AHEL keeps hospitals and AHLL at 25.4% ROCE, redeploying cash into beds, primary care and diagnostics.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Aug 2024](https://www.apollohospitals.com/apollo_pdf/Transcript-of-Apollo-Hospitals-Q1-FY25.pdf)* — Earliest reference in the window: integration of the acquired distribution business plus offline pharmacy growth is framed as the path to HealthCo's 'strategic intent' over three years, before any demerger language appears. “Transaction integration and healthy growth in offline pharmacy distribution revenues will drive Apollo HealthCo towards its stated strategic intent in the next 3 years.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://cdn.apollohospitals.com/apollohospitals/apollo_pdf/Transcript-of-Apollo-Hospitals-Q3-FY25.pdf)* — The restructuring is still presented as a merger-plus-breakeven story, with Sanjiv Gupta quantifying the FY27 target for the combined entity at INR 25,000 crore of revenue and 6-7% EBITDA, against a then run-rate of ~INR 17,000 crore at 6.5% excluding digital losses. “So, we are looking at about INR 25,000 crore of revenue and about 6% to 7% of EBITDA in FY 27.”
- *[Jun 2025](https://www.apollohospitals.com/sites/default/files/2025-06/transcript-of-apollo-hospitals---q4-fy25-earnings-call---1-.pdf)* — Suneeta Reddy's closing remarks on the Q4 FY25 call tie the Keimed merger explicitly to scale and margin durability in pharmacy, not to a listing. “The Keimed merger process is also progressing well, which will further enhance scale and margin resilience in our Pharmacy business.”
- *[Jun 2025](https://www.apollohospitals.com/sites/default/files/2025-06/transcript-of-apollo-hospitals---q4-fy25-earnings-call---1-.pdf)* — Sanjiv Gupta gave the margin bridge that underpins the 7% target: removing Apollo 24/7's operating losses and the ESOP charge (INR 100 cr in FY26, falling to a third thereafter) lifts the blended 3.2% to 6.4% even on then-current numbers. “If I remove these two things, if I assume these two things even today and remove these losses and the ESOP cost, the new number that comes for the EBITDA percentage is 6.4%.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.apollohospitals.com/sites/default/files/2025-08/transcript-of-apollo-hospitals---q1-fy26-earnings-call---13-august-2025.pdf)* — First explicit statement on a call of the demerger and separate listing, with the 18-21 month timetable and the INR 25,000 crore / 7% EBITDA end-state for the scheme concluding by FY27. “The strategic reorganization of our omni -channel pharmacy and digital health business is proceeding as planned , and we expect to complete all steps within 18 to 21 months, a timeline that we had earlier announced.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.apollohospitals.com/sites/default/files/2025-08/transcript-of-apollo-hospitals---q1-fy26-earnings-call---13-august-2025.pdf)* — A. Krishnan confirmed the mechanics in answer to an investor: HealthCo in its current form is the entity being demerged and listed by Q4 FY27, by which time Keimed's NCLT merger will also have happened. “What will happen is Apollo HealthCo., as you are seeing in the current form, is what is going to be demerged and will be listed separately by Q4 of FY27.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.apollohospitals.com/sites/default/files/2025-08/transcript-of-apollo-hospitals---q1-fy26-earnings-call---13-august-2025.pdf)* — Scope limit made explicit — hospital-based pharmacies stay with Healthcare Services; only the ~6,500-store retail chain and the online business leave, alongside Keimed, which supplies about 60,000 third-party pharmacy stores. “The hospital -based pharmacies continues as part of hospitals, which I am sure you know, but it is something that , remember, what we are spinning out is only the retail pharmacies and the online out of that.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.apollohospitals.com/sites/default/files/2025-08/transcript-of-apollo-hospitals---q1-fy26-earnings-call---13-august-2025.pdf)* — Madhivanan Balakrishnan listed the Keimed synergies: shared technology, data and people, cheaper dark stores (22 at the time) enabling expansion from the top 6 cities to the next 10 and beyond, and private label (then 14.6% of sales) pushed across Keimed's franchises. “So , technology, data, people, and product categories , all the four synergies should start playing out as this merger comes in place.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://drupal-cdn-hfaeddcdbng5hfbg.a01.azurefd.net/sites/default/files/2025-11/transcript-of-apollo-hospitals---q2-fy26-earnings-call---7-november-2025....pdf)* — Process update framing the combination as the way to capture scale benefits inside HealthCo; separately Madhivanan said merging Keimed, Apollo Pharmacy and the digital business would release further cost synergies from the next financial year. “The statutory processes for the restructuring within Apollo HealthCo and the Keimed merger continue to proceed as per plan, and we remain well positioned to capture the full benefit of scale within Apollo HealthCo.”

## HINDUNILVR — Hindustan Unilever Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **LISTED <1Y — selling-pressure window; the bargain forms here** · score 5.7/10 · spin-off · 17 filing(s) from CALLS, NSE, NSE-register · first 2025-11-11, latest 2026-02-13

> **Listing:** LISTED — the resulting company trades since about 2025-12-05 (record date 2025-12-05)

**The stages, as filed:** exchange_noc (2025-11-23) → nclt_sanction (2025-11-11) → effective (2025-11-18) → record_date (2025-11-18) → listed (2026-02-13)

**Stated in the filings:** entitlement **1 for every 1**; record date 2025-12-05; appointed date 2025-12-01.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** HUL's Ice Cream business undertaking, demerged into Kwality Wall's (India) Limited on a going-concern basis — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* Promoter stake in KWIL not stated; HUL's own shareholding in KWIL was reduced and cancelled and KWIL ceased to be a subsidiary. KWIL has a dedicated management team (Chitrank Goel, Deputy MD; Prashant Premrajka, CFO) drawn from HUL.
- *What it reveals:* Cost apportionment puts KWIL at only 1.91% of HUL's value versus 98.09%, set on net assets as at 30 November 2025 — a small, separately listed ice-cream pure-play, 2,34,95,91,262 shares of Re 1, with Kwality Wall's, Cornetto and Magnum.
- *Selling pressure:* likely — Very small relative size (1.91% of pre-demerger cost basis) distributed 1:1 to every HUL holder; a separate ice-cream company versus a large FMCG parent.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* KWIL's first standalone results and balance sheet — the net assets behind the 1.91% cost apportionment.
- *In their words:* “The Scheme has come into effect on 1st December , 2025, being the Effective Date (as defined under the Scheme ).”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The business being separated is HUL's Ice Cream business — the Kwality Wall's, Cornetto and Magnum brands — demerged into a new listed entity, Kwality Wall's (India) Limited (KWIL), under a Scheme of Arrangement sanctioned by NCLT Mumbai (orders dated 30 October 2025 and 6 November 2025), effective 1 December 2025, with KWIL listing on 16 February 2026. The Scheme's stated benefit is the 'creation of a leading listed ice cream company in India with focused management having greater flexibility to deploy strategies suited to the Ice Cream business's distinctive operating model and market dynamics, to realise its full potential' — i.e. the structural argument is that ice cream does not fit HUL's FMCG operating model. The financial case management gave on the calls is size and dilution: Ice Cream is 'roughly 3-odd percentage of our business' and 'makes low single-digit margin', below the HUL average, so CFO Ritesh Tiwari guided that removing it adds 50–60bps to reported EBITDA margin on top of the 22–23% guidance (later restated by Niranjan Gupta as a 50bps benefit, giving an implied 22.5–23.5% band). FY26 also showed the category's volatility — Ice Cream 'declined year on year, impacted by extended monsoon in addition to GST transition' in the September quarter — reinforcing the seasonality/operating-model argument. Mechanically it was a two-step process: demerger completed in the December quarter with Ice Cream reported as a discontinued business, then listing in Q4 FY26; shareholders received 1 KWIL share of Re.1 for every 1 HUL share (2,34,95,91,262 shares allotted on 1:1), with cost of acquisition apportioned 98.09% HUL / 1.91% KWIL. The December quarter reported PAT of Rs. 6,603 crores (up 121%) included a 'one-time non-cash gain arising from Ice Cream demerger', and HUL flagged it would lose PLI benefits that had flowed through the P&L via Ice Cream. By May 2026 Priya Nair framed it as portfolio rotation — 'strategic actions such as the demerger of Ice Cream, along with the investments at OZiva and Minimalist, are already enhancing the growth mix of the portfolio' — while explicitly keeping Foods (Tea, Coffee, Horlicks/Boost, Kissan) 'outside the perimeter of the Unilever transaction that we have done'.

**How it evolved:** In the Apr 2025 call (24 April 2025, FY25 results) it was already an in-flight action — 'progressing on track with regulatory requirements', completion expected by end of FY26 — the original announcement rationale sitting in earlier calls not included here. By the Oct 2025 call (23 October 2025) the plan was firmed and quantified: demerger in the December quarter with Ice Cream shown as a discontinued business, listing in Q4 FY26, ~3% of business at low single-digit margin, 50–60bps reported-margin accretion, plus the admission that Ice Cream had declined on extended monsoon and GST transition. In the Feb 2026 call (12 February 2026) it was done — demerger completed in December, KWIL listing announced for 16 February 2026, a one-time non-cash demerger gain in reported PAT, and the guided EBITDA band reset to an implied 22.5–23.5%. By the May 2026 call (30 April 2026) it was cited retrospectively as one of the portfolio actions improving HUL's growth mix, alongside Minimalist and OZiva.

**What management expects from it:** For HUL: ~50–60bps uplift to reported EBITDA margin (22–23% guidance becoming an implied 22.5–23.5%), since Ice Cream, ~3% of turnover, earned low single-digit margins; a better growth mix; a one-time non-cash gain; loss of PLI income. For KWIL: dedicated management, singular focus and flexibility to capture India's growing ice cream opportunity.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The Scheme's stated rationale is a focused, separately listed ice cream company with management flexibility suited to the business's own operating model and market dynamics. “Creation of a leading listed ice cream company in India with focused management having greater flexibility to deploy strategies suited to the Ice Cream businesses' distinctive operating model and market dynamics, to realise its full potential”
- *Scheme* — Mechanics: 1:1 entitlement of Re.1 KWIL shares to HUL shareholders on the 5 December 2025 record date; 2,34,95,91,262 shares were allotted and cost of acquisition was apportioned 98.09% HUL / 1.91% KWIL. “for every 1 (one) equity share of face value of Re. 1/- fully paid up held in HUL, 1 (one) equity share of face value of Re. 1/- credited as fully paid up in KWIL”
- *CALL Apr 2025* — At FY25 results the demerger was already in motion, with regulatory work on track and completion targeted by end of FY26 — no fresh rationale was restated. “The demerger of Ice cream business is progressing on track with regulatory requirements, and we expect it to be completed by the end of financial year 2026.”
- *CALL Oct 2025* — Ritesh Tiwari quantified the dilution being removed: Ice Cream is about 3% of HUL's business at low single-digit margin, running even below that in FY26 because of monsoon and investment. “Ice Cream, as we had called out even earlier, it's roughly 3-odd percentage of our business. and the business makes low single-digit margin.”
- *CALL Oct 2025* — The margin benefit was sized at 50–60bps on reported EBITDA, explicitly because Ice Cream earns below the HUL average — on top of the unchanged 22–23% guidance. “Coming to EBITDA margin, Ice Cream demerger is expected to result in an improvement of 50-60 bps to the reported margin as Ice Cream business operates at a margin lower than HUL average.”
- *CALL Oct 2025* — The category's volatility was on display in the quarter being separated, and the process was described as two-step: demerger/discontinued-business reporting in Q3, listing in Q4 FY26. “Ice Cream business declined year on year, impacted by extended monsoon in addition to GST transition. As you are aware, the Ice Cream demerger process is currently underway.”
- *CALL Feb 2026* — On completion, Priya Nair justified it by dedicated leadership and undivided focus letting KWIL chase India's growing ice cream opportunity; listing was set for 16 February 2026. “With a dedicated management team and singular focus, we are confident that KWIL is well positioned to capitalise on the growing market opportunity in India and deliver sustained performance.”
- *CALL Feb 2026* — Niranjan Gupta confirmed the guidance arithmetic — the old 22–23% band plus a 50bps demerger benefit, i.e. an implied 22.5–23.5% — and reported a one-time non-cash demerger gain inside the Rs. 6,603 crores reported PAT. “So, our guided range has been that 22% to 23%. We also outlined that the range, therefore, you will see a benefit of the ice cream demerger to the extent of 50 basis points.”
- *CALL May 2026* — A year on, the demerger is presented as one of several portfolio-rotation moves lifting the quality and growth profile of what remains. “Strategic actions such as the demerger of Ice Cream, along with the investments at OZiva and Minimalist, are already enhancing the growth mix of the portfolio.”
- *CALL May 2026* — Asked whether Unilever's global retreat from foods implies more separations, Priya Nair drew the boundary: HUL's Foods (Tea, Coffee, Horlicks/Boost, Kissan) is deliberately outside the transaction perimeter and remains a strategic priority. “So therefore that, combined with the opportunities that exist in India in Foods, is the reason why Foods is outside the perimeter of the Unilever transaction that we have done, and Foods continues to be a very important area and focus of strategy for HUL.”

*Not explained on the calls:* Never explained: original announcement rationale (older transcripts omitted/scanned), KWIL standalone financials and capital structure, Unilever's global ice-cream separation, and whether any investor, lender or partner requested it.

### The business being separated — its own numbers

**Ice Cream Business (reported as 'Discontinued Operations' in the FY2025-26 segment note; Demerged Undertaking demerged into Kwality Wall's (India) Limited, KWIL)** · unit ₹ crore · Revenue = 'Segment Revenue from Discontinued Operations' (segment revenue; note states there are no intersegment transactions, so effectively external). Operating profit = 'Segment Results from Discontinued Operations', i.e. segment result = profit before other income, finance costs, exceptional items and tax (EBIT-type, not EBITDA). PAT = 'Profit/(Loss) for the year from Discontinued Operations'. FY2026 figures cover only part of the year (Kwality Wall's ceased to be a subsidiary / demerger effective 30th November, 2025), and FY2026 PAT of 4,407 is dominated by the one-off positive impact of the Ice Cream demerger accounted per the approved scheme, not by trading profit; FY2026 PBT before exceptional items from discontinued operations was (135). ## SKFINDIA — SKF India Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **LISTED 1–2Y — the second-year window** · score 5.7/10 · spin-off · 9 filing(s) from CALLS, NSE, NSE-register · first 2025-10-15, latest 2026-08-20

> **Listing:** LISTED — the resulting company trades since about 2025-10-15 (record date 2025-10-15)

**The stages, as filed:** exchange_noc (2025-11-28) → nclt_sanction (2025-11-15) → record_date (2025-10-15)

**Stated in the filings:** record date 2025-10-15; size hint: 15% of ebitda.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** The Industrial business (Demerged Undertaking) — bearings for infrastructure, manufacturing, railways, energy — into SKF India (Industrial) Limited — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* Mirror-image demerger: 1 SKF Industrial share per SKF India share; Resulting Company's shareholding pattern mirrors the parent on the record date, so no valuation was carried out. Management incentives in the new entity not stated
- *What it reveals:* Industrial carries 53.12% of the cost base versus 46.88% automotive, so the spun half is larger. Retained automotive guides only 11-12% PBT, 15.3% EBITDA, below Schaeffler/Timken ~20%; management says industrial is a little higher margin business than automotive
- *Selling pressure:* likely — New separate listing of the larger half; every automotive-focused shareholder automatically received industrial shares in a different end-market
- *Parent or spin:* spin · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* SKF India (Industrial) Limited's Information Memorandum and its own results — industrial margins and the inter-company trading/rent arrangement
- *In their words:* “The demerger gives us the strategic clarity to sharpen our priorities, accelerate growth, and unlock greater value for all stakeholders.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

SKF India separated its Industrial bearings business out of the listed company into SKF India (Industrial) Limited, leaving SKF India Ltd as a pure-play Automotive bearings company (management called it a "reverse carve-out" mirroring SKF AB's global split of Automotive, ~30% of group revenue versus 34-35% in India). Management's stated logic rested on three pillars: fundamentally different macro drivers (Automotive: EV/CAFE and BS-VII emission norms, 30% EV penetration target by 2030, premiumization/SUVs, last-mile commercial vehicles; Industrial: infrastructure spend, Make in India/NIP/PLI, China-Plus-One, railways/metro/Vande Bharat, wind and renewables doubling by 2030); different customer needs (a few large auto OEMs needing application-specific, longer-cycle engineered products — 60-65% engineered order in Auto versus ~25-30% in Industrial — against hundreds of industrial verticals wanting uptime, condition monitoring and remanufacturing); and a different manufacturing philosophy (Auto = large batch, small/medium bearings, automation and cycle-time efficiency; Industrial = wide assortment, small/large sizes, flexible lines with fast changeover plus a large traded component). The problems they said this solves: management attention split across two unlike businesses, capital allocation that could not be tailored (Auto was short of capacity, Industrial needed a brand-new Pune plant and localization from ~30-35% toward 70%), slow decision-making and launches, mismatched innovation cycles, and poor financial visibility for investors in a combined P&L. Operationally the split was defined down to the line: Bangalore 10 lines (7 Auto, 3 Industrial, with those 3 moving to Pune so Bangalore becomes 100% Auto), Pune 22 lines (12 Auto, 10 Industrial), Haridwar 4 lines all Auto; land 85:15 in Bangalore, 52:48 in Pune, 100% Auto in Haridwar; manpower 55-60% Auto versus 40-45% Industrial; cash allocated on the two businesses' last three years of profits. Shareholders received one SKF Industrial share of Rs 10 for every SKF India share held (PwC Business Consulting share entitlement report dated 24 December 2024; Saffron Capital fairness opinion 25 December 2024), with pre-demerger cost of acquisition apportioned 46.88% to SKF India and 53.12% to SKF Industrial. Pro forma FY24 economics shown to investors were Auto ~18% EBITDA and Industrial ~17%, both ~16% PBT, off a combined FY24 revenue of INR 45.7 billion; FY25 combined revenue was INR 4,919.9 crore (+7.65%) with PBT INR 763.1 crore (+3.71%). Nobody external demanded the separation — it was a group-level decision, with investors on the calls supportive (one explicitly "wholeheartedly supported" it) while pressing for structural clarity given SKF would still have three Indian entities including the unlisted SKF Engineering & Lubrication (Ahmedabad plant, global technical centre, lubrication and sealing factories); no lender or partner requirement was ever cited.

**How it evolved:** The demerger was announced in Q4 CY2024 and first explained in detail on a dedicated update call on 9 April 2025, which laid out the three macro/customer/manufacturing drivers, the six enablers (management focus, manufacturing efficiency, tailored capital, agility, innovation, investor visibility), pro forma FY24 carve-out financials and a 12-15 month timeline, plus an aspiration of "2 to 3 more points" of EBITDA. By the 19 May 2025 Q4 call the plant allocation had firmed up (Haridwar 100% Auto, Bangalore ~80-85% Auto, a new Industrial factory beside the Pune plant), and the 30 June 2025 investor meet added line-by-line, land and manpower splits, segment revenue mixes from FY22-FY25, three-year guidance (Auto 10-12%, Industrial 8-10% to FY28, margins held at 17-19%) and a step-up in capex from ~INR 150 crore to roughly INR 350-400 crore a year (INR 450-500 crore Pune industrial plant by 2028, INR 500-600 crore Auto capex to 2030); the NCLT-convened shareholder meeting on 14 July 2025 approved the 1:1 scheme, and the 6-7 August 2025 AGM and Q1 FY26 call quantified the cost for the first time (INR 184 million in Q1, mostly SAP/IT separation and consultants, 1.5-2% margin drag running into H1 FY27, plus stamp duty on asset transfer) while conceding the businesses were "so deeply integrated" that separation was complex. After NCLT sanction on 26 September 2025, effectiveness on 1 October 2025 and a 15 October 2025 record date, the story changed tone: the 21 May 2026 call presented SKF India as a standalone automotive company guiding to only 11-12% PBT margin (FY26 EBITDA 15.3%) with investors complaining that disclosure had "dropped substantially" post-demerger and that margins were far below what was promised in the run-up to the demerger vote, management answering that royalty was unchanged and this was a transition.

**What management expects from it:** Two fit-for-purpose entities growing faster and more profitably: automotive 10-12% and industrial 8-10% growth to FY28, both holding 17-19% EBITDA with 2-3 points of upside later; sharper management focus, tailored capital deployment and manufacturing efficiency, plus separate financial visibility attracting more aligned investors.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Apr 2025* — The stated purpose: two independent, fit-for-purpose companies that each accelerate growth and profitability, driven by three differences — industry dynamics, customer needs and manufacturing philosophy. “The intention of this demerger is to create 2 fit-for-purposes independent companies, which will accelerate both growth and profitability of both companies.”
- *Apr 2025* — Management summarised the rationale as three separate axes of difference, with manufacturing efficiency and customer service as the payoff. “So to summarize, macro drivers are different. Customer drivers and innovation is different; and third, the manufacturing itself, the process of manufacturing itself is very different, what will make us most efficient and help us serve the customer needs.”
- *Apr 2025* — Manufacturing philosophy was the concrete operating problem: Auto runs large batches of small/medium bearings for few OEMs with automation and economies of scale, while Industrial needs flexible lines, customised solutions and a large traded/regional component. “Automotive has a large batch sizes with small and medium-sized bearings.”
- *Apr 2025* — Margin ambition attached to the separation: 2-3 percentage points of EBITDA upside in both businesses, from more efficient manufacturing, procurement and value-based pricing of premium products such as ceramic and energy-efficient bearings. “So I would say while the margins are typically relatively thin, we would hope that we can get at least 2 to 3 more points on our EBITDA going forward.”
- *Apr 2025* — Shareholders were told the split was economically neutral — a mirror shareholding with a 1:1 share issue and listing of SKF Industrial on both exchanges. “The new company will mirror the shareholding of the existing listed company with each shareholder of SKF India receiving one share of SKF Industrial as a consideration of the demerger.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=78b3fd3b-6609-4f9b-ac56-5ec9fc26a320.pdf)* — Investor visibility into the two businesses' separate performance was explicitly listed as one of the demerger benefits, alongside tailored capital deployment and two different manufacturing philosophies. “and finally, just more visibility for the -- our investors, all of you, to be able to see the performance of the 2 entities independently.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=78b3fd3b-6609-4f9b-ac56-5ec9fc26a320.pdf)* — Pro forma FY24 carve-out economics given to investors: Automotive ~18% EBITDA, Industrial ~17%, both around 16% PBT, with capex set to double from INR 130-150 crore as a new Industrial plant is built next to the existing Pune site. “So if you look at FY '24, our EBITDA margins for automotive was around 18%. And industrial was around 17%.”
- *[Jul 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=3d94636c-b87c-4f11-91b6-556b4efcce20.pdf)* — The asset split was disclosed line by line — Bangalore 10 lines 70:30 with three lines moving to Pune so Bangalore becomes 100% Automotive, Pune 52:48 land, Haridwar 100% Automotive, manpower roughly 55:45. “There are three main plants, as we said, Bangalore, Pune and Haridwar. Bangalore, today there are 10 lines that will be split in the ratio of 70 to 30.”
- *[Jul 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=3d94636c-b87c-4f11-91b6-556b4efcce20.pdf)* — Three-year guidance for the two entities: Automotive 10-12% growth, Industrial 8-10% (held back until the new Pune plant and localization land in FY27-28), with margins maintained at 17-19% and upside beyond FY28. “Next 3 years till '28, we expect growth in automotive to be in the 10 % to 12% range, industrial to be a little lower, 8% to 10% range.”
- *[Jul 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=3d94636c-b87c-4f11-91b6-556b4efcce20.pdf)* — Capital allocation was the hard constraint being fixed: a brand-new Industrial-only Pune plant (DGBB, TRB, unitised bearings) costing INR 450-500 crore by 2028 plus INR 350-450 crore of additional lines, on top of INR 500-600 crore of Automotive capex to 2030. “Pune, we will be setting up a new plant, fully industrial, for industrial, making primarily DGBBs, which are deep groove ball bearings, tapered roller bearings, and unitized bearings, which are UCs.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=6801dc1e-769f-42ac-9ea4-5ada85787e74.pdf)* — At the NCLT-convened shareholder meeting, management conceded the separation was complex precisely because the two businesses were deeply intertwined, and said the total demerger cost was still being accumulated. “As you know, it's a complex project primarily because the businesses both automotive and industrial, they are so deeply integrated that having two independent businesses is a complex process.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=6801dc1e-769f-42ac-9ea4-5ada85787e74.pdf)* — An existing institutional shareholder (Ravi Purohit) publicly backed the demerger while asking why India would still be left with three SKF entities when the group was simplifying structures; management said no merger of entities was contemplated until the demerger completed. “And first of all, we'd like to congratulate and have wholeheartedly supported this demerger initiative that SKF Group is undertaking.”

*Not explained on the calls:* Never quantified: total demerger cost, dis-synergies, inter-entity trading/rent/service charges, or why post-demerger margins (11-12% PBT) fall far below the 16-19% promised pre-demerger.

*Calls read (36 months):* Apr 2025, [Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=6801dc1e-769f-42ac-9ea4-5ada85787e74.pdf), [Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=458af4e6-8be5-4ce2-b4f1-119e53cd4c5a.pdf), [Jul 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=3d94636c-b87c-4f11-91b6-556b4efcce20.pdf), [May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=78b3fd3b-6609-4f9b-ac56-5ec9fc26a320.pdf)

## TMPV — Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **LISTED 1–2Y — the second-year window** · score 5.7/10 · spin-off · 21 filing(s) from NSE, NSE-register · first 2025-10-14, latest 2026-11-01

> **Listing:** LISTED — the resulting company trades since about 2025-10-14

**The stages, as filed:** meetings (2025-11-28) → record_date (2025-10-14)

**Stated in the filings:** demerged undertaking: , undertaking.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** The Commercial Vehicles business, demerged from Tata Motors Limited into TML Commercial Vehicles Limited, now renamed Tata Motors Limited — class `regulatory_strategic`.

- *Insiders:* Tata Sons Private Limited is Promoter; promoter group held 1,565,402,703 of 3,682,582,902 shares (~42.5%), mirrored 1:1 in the resulting company. P B Balaji (4,93,186 shares) is a director of the CV entity.
- *What it reveals:* Separation leaves the parent as cars/SUVs plus JLR: India PV net cash ~Rs.7,000 Cr with 15% FY26 volume growth, over 40% EV share, while JLR carries Rs.33,000 Cr net debt and 0.7% EBIT; CV took 31.15% of cost base.
- *Selling pressure:* likely — Every PV holder received 1:1 shares in a smaller, different-industry commercial-vehicle entity (31.15% of apportioned cost); index effects not stated.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Clause 9 of the Composite Scheme (NCLT orders August 25 / September 10, 2025) on share-based incentives, plus TMCV's own standalone results
- *In their words:* “In this regard, we wish to inform that TMCV has intimated the Company today that it has received approval from BSE Limited and National Stock Exchange of India Limited for listing and trading of its equity shares, effective November 12, 2025.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The separation at issue is the demerger of the Commercial Vehicles business out of the old Tata Motors Limited into TML Commercial Vehicles Limited, executed together with the amalgamation of the PV subsidiary back into the listed parent, under one Composite Scheme of Arrangement sanctioned by NCLT Mumbai (orders of August 25, 2025 and a rectification order of September 10, 2025), with an appointed date of July 1, 2025 and effective date of October 1, 2025. The Scheme states only two objectives in these texts: to transfer the Commercial Vehicles undertaking to the Resulting Company 'on a going concern basis' in compliance with Section 2(19AA) of the Income-tax Act, and to amalgamate Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited into TML 'with an objective of consolidating the Passenger Vehicles Business with TML', after which TML was renamed Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited and TMLCVL renamed Tata Motors Limited (w.e.f. October 13, 2025). The result is that, as the postal ballot puts it, 'the Commercial Vehicle and Passenger Vehicle businesses of the Company are housed in two separate entities', each with its own reconstituted board and KMP (Shailesh Chandra as MD & CEO of TMPV from October 1, 2025; P B Balaji moved from Group CFO to CEO of Jaguar Land Rover from November 17, 2025), and TMPV left reporting one automotive segment of JLR plus Tata Passenger Vehicles, 'other than CV segment moving out'. Shareholders were handed direct ownership of both: 1 TMLCVL share for every 1 TML share held on the October 14, 2025 record date, with historical cost apportioned 31.15% to the CV entity and 68.85% to TMPV, and the new CV shares listed from November 12, 2025. Management's only economic framing on the calls is accounting and capital: a notional demerger gain of ~Rs. 83,000 Cr (CV business valued at ~Rs. 94,000 Cr by third-party agencies against ~Rs. 11,000 Cr book value of net assets transferred), fully offset by a contra deemed-dividend entry so there is 'absolutely no impact on either distributable reserves or on our net worth'; an India PV business that is net cash (~Rs. 5,000 Cr at Q3 FY26, ~Rs. 7,000 Cr at FY26-end) which 'gives a lot of flex to fund the rich product investment cycle'; and the two entities now declaring dividends separately (Rs. 3 at TMPV plus Rs. 4 at TMLCV, 'a total dividend of Rs. 7 in the year when the demerger was undertaken' versus Rs. 6 before). Costs disclosed are stamp duty: a Rs. 400 Cr provision in Q3 FY26, included within about Rs. 4,100 Cr of FY26 exceptionals. No investor, lender or partner is named anywhere in these texts as having asked for the separation; the only stakeholder input recorded is the shareholder vote, which management described as 'overwhelming votes in our favor', and the nine AGM resolutions passed in July 2026.

**How it evolved:** On the Feb 2025 call (Q3 FY25, January 29, 2025) the demerger was already a filed corporate action awaiting exchange/SEBI NOC, with appointed date July 1 and effective date around October 1, 2025; by the Jun 2025 call (Q4 FY25, May 13, 2025) the shareholder vote had passed overwhelmingly and both dates were reconfirmed, and on the Aug 2025 call (Q1 FY26, August 8, 2025) the NCLT final hearing had concluded that same day with judgment reserved and the October 1 effective date 'on plan'. The Nov 2025 call (Q2 FY26, November 14, 2025) was the first set of results reported post-separation, where management walked through the demerger accounting entries, the Rs. 83,000 Cr notional gain and contra deemed dividend, and the new segment structure. Thereafter the subject narrows to residuals and costs: the Feb 2026 call (February 5, 2026) notes CV is out of the segments and books a Rs. 400 Cr stamp duty provision, and the Jun 2026 call (May 14, 2026) folds stamp duty into FY26 exceptionals and frames the two separate dividends as Rs. 7 combined; the strategic 'why' is never revisited on any of these six calls.

**What management expects from it:** Stated only indirectly: CV and PV housed in two separate listed entities, each with its own board, leadership and dividend (Rs. 3 + Rs. 4 vs Rs. 6 before); TMPV consolidating PV, EV and JLR under one automotive segment, with a net-cash India business (Rs. 7,000 Cr) giving flexibility to fund its product investment cycle while JLR carries Rs. 33,000 Cr net debt.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The Scheme bundles two steps: hiving off the Commercial Vehicles undertaking into TMLCVL on a going concern basis (structured to qualify under Section 2(19AA) of the Income-tax Act), and amalgamating the PV subsidiary into the listed parent — the only explicit objective language in any document supplied. “Amalgamation of TMLPV with TML with an objective of consolidating the Passenger Vehicles Business with TML and consequent dissolution of TMLPV without being wound up.”
- *Scheme* — The November 2025 postal ballot explains the consequence the separation was meant to produce — two self-standing entities — and uses it as the reason to rebuild both boards, appointing Shailesh Chandra MD & CEO of TMPV from October 1, 2025 and P B Balaji as a non-executive director while he became CEO of Jaguar Land Rover from November 17, 2025. “In view of the above, it was proposed to reconstitute the Board of Directors of both  the entities .”
- *Scheme* — Shareholders were given direct ownership of both businesses rather than cash, at a strict 1:1 entitlement on the October 14, 2025 record date, with historical cost of acquisition apportioned 31.15% to the CV entity and 68.85% to TMPV; the CV shares were approved for listing and trading from November 12, 2025. “1 (one) share of the Resulting Company (face value of INR 2/- each fully paid up), for every 1 (one) share of the Demerged Company (face value of INR 2/- each fully paid up) of the same class of shares outstanding and as held by such shareholder in the Demerged Company, without any further application, act or deed (‘Share Entitlement Ratio’).”
- *Scheme* — At the 81st AGM (July 8, 2026) the Chairman and the MD & CEO presented the demerger as completed and as the platform for TMPV's own roadmap, pairing it with JLR's new Panapakkam, Tamil Nadu production and with long-term growth aspirations to FY31 on a consolidated basis. “He highlighted the demerger of Commercial Vehicles business into a separate legal entity and commencement of commercial production by JLR at Panapakkam, Tamil Nadu reflecting the synergy between the Company and JLR.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=28345af3-7271-4146-8cf3-8da0f9c73222.pdf)* — The demerger was presented purely as a corporate action on track — filings with the exchanges and SEBI complete, operational carve-out work advanced, appointed date July 1 and effective date around October 1, 2025 — alongside the parallel Tata Motors Finance merger into Tata Capital. “Operational activities are in an advanced stage and progressing as per plan.”
- *[Jun 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=80350d5e-9578-469f-bf9f-31610098f897.pdf)* — Management reported that shareholders had backed the Scheme decisively and that both the appointed and effective dates were intact; asked about asset allocation, Balaji confirmed the Tata Capital stake would sit with the CV business after separation. “we had overwhelming votes in our favor and therefore we are on track for an appointed date of July 1st”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=2a91a004-4cbd-440e-93d3-2ca8967ff37b.pdf)* — The NCLT final hearing concluded on the day of the call with judgment reserved, which management said would let them complete the demerger within the quarter for an October 1 effective date; the same slide carried the CV side's Iveco acquisition, i.e. each business already pursuing its own agenda. “Hot of the press is the demerger.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=e6684a03-5a4d-4c7a-8da0-d5b2c52ec7d1.pdf)* — First results after separation: the demerger produced a ~Rs. 83,000 Cr book gain on disposal of the CV undertaking (CV valued at ~Rs. 94,000 Cr by third-party agencies versus ~Rs. 11,000 Cr book value of net assets transferred), but it is entirely notional with no effect on net worth or distributable reserves. “But this is only a notional gain as there is a contra entry of ~Rs. 83,000 Cr as a deemed dividend.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=e6684a03-5a4d-4c7a-8da0-d5b2c52ec7d1.pdf)* — Reporting was simplified to one automotive segment comprising JLR and Tata Passenger Vehicles plus 'others' (mainly Tata Technologies and Tata Motors Holdings Pte Singapore); prior-period income statements were restated to TMPV only, while prior balance sheets still include CV and are not comparable. “The automotive segment will now comprise of JLR and Tata Passenger Vehicles business.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=e6684a03-5a4d-4c7a-8da0-d5b2c52ec7d1.pdf)* — Capital framing of the standalone PV entity: the India business is net cash, which management said gives flexibility to fund its heavy product investment cycle; one residual link to CV remains — the Rs. 6,500 Cr PLI cap still applies to PV and CV together because the original 2021 application was made as a Group. “We had applied originally in 2021 as a Group.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=7907e958-7953-4b49-b831-aab03d6e2746.pdf)* — CV is confirmed out of the reporting perimeter with nothing else changed, and the first demerger cost is booked — a Rs. 400 Cr stamp duty provision within Rs. 1,600 Cr of quarterly exceptionals alongside JLR cyber and India wage-bill charges. “Commercial vehicle business is out I think last quarter post the demerger , everything else is the same.”
- *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=b4d386d7-de53-4409-8e90-187e08cb4a91.pdf)* — FY26 exceptionals of about Rs. 4,100 Cr include demerger stamp duty; separately, the two entities now set dividends independently — Rs. 3 per share at TMPV (about Rs. 1,100 Cr outflow) plus Rs. 4 at TMLCV — which management framed as more total distribution than the pre-demerger company paid. “So this actually represents a total dividend of Rs. 7 in the year when the demerger was undertaken and an increase over the Rs. 6 that we have paid for the last two years.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No value-unlock, focus, valuation or synergy argument; no demerger costs/benefits beyond stamp duty; no dis-synergies, debt-allocation logic, or any investor, lender or partner request.

## ANANTRAJ — Anant Raj Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 5.0/10 · spin-off · 6 filing(s) from NSE, NSE-deep · first 2026-05-11, latest 2026-07-21

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**The stages, as filed:** announced (2026-07-21)

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** The Data Centre and Cloud Services business of ARL and ARCPL, vested in Ashok Cloud Private Limited — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* ARL promoters hold 57.42% of ARL; post-scheme ACPL is 28.14% promoters directly plus 51% held by ARL (79.14% total), public 20.86%. Promoter-group Anish Sarin oversees data-centre rollout.
- *What it reveals:* Demerged Undertaking turnover Rs 145.90 cr is only 8.96% of Rs 1,627.72 cr; management cites ~75% data-centre EBITDA margin, 357 MW planned capacity, Rs 20,000 cr capex, net-cash parent with Rs 4,471.64 cr net worth.
- *Selling pressure:* likely — Small (8.96% of turnover), only 20.86% public float in ACPL, and a digital-infrastructure business alien to real-estate holders.
- *Parent or spin:* both · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* The full Composite Scheme: asset/liability split and valuation of the Demerged Undertaking versus ACPL's Rs 74.86 cr rights issue.
- *In their words:* “The Data Centre Business has evolved significantly over the years and is well poised to chart its own growth path and operate as a separate listed entity focused on the rapidly growing Data Centre Business whilst continuing to leverage ARL's institutional strengths, strong brand equity and goodwill.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Management says Anant Raj Ltd today runs two unlike businesses under one roof — the legacy real estate/infrastructure business (residential townships, luxury housing, commercial leasing, hospitality) and a data centre & cloud services business — and that the Data Centre Business is itself split across two entities, Anant Raj Limited and its wholly owned Anant Raj Cloud Private Limited (ARCPL), with assets, employees, investments and operations housed in both. The Composite Scheme therefore first amalgamates ARCPL into ARL and then demerges the whole Data Centre Business out of ARL into Ashok Cloud Private Limited (ACPL), so all of it sits in one dedicated, separately listed company. The stated problems it solves: the two verticals differ 'significantly in their nature, risk profile, competitive dynamics, and capital requirements', and the Board recorded on May 11, 2026 that keeping both in one company 'does not adequately reflect the true potential and intrinsic value of each business segment, thereby impacting stakeholder returns'; the split is meant to give independent market-driven valuation of a pure-play digital infrastructure asset, dedicated management focus, a simpler ownership structure with intra-group arrangements cancelled/rationalised, and the ability to attract sector-specific capital, strategic investors and partnerships. The numbers cited: the Demerged Undertaking did ₹145.90 cr turnover in FY26 versus ₹1,627.72 cr aggregated (8.96%); ARCPL turnover ₹136.20 cr and net worth ₹49.45 cr versus ARL's ₹1,491.52 cr turnover and ₹4,471.64 cr net worth; ACPL had nil turnover and ₹0.04 cr net worth and was capitalised days earlier via a ₹74.86 cr rights issue (37,43,22,553 shares at ₹2). Scale is the driver: the Board noted an MOU with the Govt. of Andhra Pradesh for 50 MW IT load taking total planned capacity to 357 MW IT load, requiring about ₹20,000 cr of investment — against a real estate business management repeatedly said should carry as little debt as possible. Mechanically, ARL shareholders get 1 ACPL share of ₹2 for every 1 ARL share of ₹2, giving them 49% of ACPL directly (promoters 28.14%, public 20.86%) while ARL retains 51%, so ACPL stays a subsidiary and ARL holders keep 100% of the ultimate economic interest; ACPL will be listed on BSE and NSE under the Rule 19(7) exemption. The ask came from the equity market side — an investor asked about a demerger as early as the Apr 2024 call, and analysts kept pressing for separate real estate vs data centre reporting — not from lenders or partners, who are never cited as requesting it.

**How it evolved:** On the Apr 25, 2024 call Arpit Shah of Stallion Asset asked outright whether there were plans to demerge the business and Amit Sarin refused — 'too soon', focus on execution — while describing the cloud venture as a half-megawatt pilot with TCIL. By the Oct 30, 2024 call (Q2 FY25) management was framing the group as 'two full-fledged divisions' (real estate plus a technology division) with a ₹2,100 cr fundraise earmarked purely for data centre/cloud, and Raj Sarraf pushed for separate data centre revenue disclosure; on the Nov 12, 2025 call (Q2/H1 FY26) the CFO called the company 'at an important inflection point' with a 'legacy real estate business' alongside the data centre/cloud 'future ready platform', the ₹1,100 cr QIP was done, and analysts again asked for a separate segment/EBITDA breakup, which management declined on the 10%-of-revenue threshold. The demerger itself was never discussed on any of the three calls: it surfaced in the May 11, 2026 board note (which recorded the need for merger/demerger and set up a committee of Amit Sarin, Ashim Sarin, Manoj Goyal and Pankaj Gupta to frame a scheme), then was executed as the ACPL rights-issue funding on July 20, 2026 and the Composite Scheme approved on July 21, 2026.

**What management expects from it:** Ashok Cloud: pure-play digital-infrastructure valuation and independent market recognition, sector-specific growth capital, partnerships and acquisitions, dedicated leadership, consolidated ownership (75% EBITDA-margin colocation/cloud, 357 MW plan, ~₹20,000 cr capex). Anant Raj: sharper focus on real estate, infrastructure and hospitality, low debt, continued execution. Both: operational efficiency, agility, faster decision-making, transparency, unlocked shareholder value, with holders participating directly in each.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Apr 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=03aa7997-f0a0-4f9b-8373-f4a4684da92d.pdf)* — An investor (Arpit Shah, Stallion Asset) directly asked about demerging the data centre business; management declined to engage, calling the business too young and prioritising execution toward the 300 MW mark in four years. “We are too soon to say anything on that. Let's focus on execution, Arpit.”
- *[Apr 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=03aa7997-f0a0-4f9b-8373-f4a4684da92d.pdf)* — Management set out the different capital philosophies that later justify separation: real estate was to be net debt-free by December 2024 and the only debt acceptable would be lease rental discounting, including against long 10-15 year data centre leases. “And the only debt which Anant Raj is open to taking is LRD and this is one of the best items for LRD because you have long-term leases and good clients.”
- *[Nov 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=27b8b856-615a-44a5-8be4-157fd1831d5c.pdf)* — Management began describing the group as two separate divisions — the historic real estate 'bread and butter' and a new technology division of colocation and cloud — the same two-vertical framing the Scheme later uses. “So Anant Raj Limited will now have two full-fledged divisions. Real estate division which is the historical, the division of the company, the bread and butter of the company as of now and plus the technology division, in which we will be data center, co-location infrastructure and cloud.”
- *[Nov 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=27b8b856-615a-44a5-8be4-157fd1831d5c.pdf)* — The ₹2,100 cr fundraise (₹100 cr promoters, ₹2,000 cr market) was ring-fenced entirely for the data centre/cloud build-out, with real estate funded from internal accruals — distinct funding requirements per vertical, with cloud capex cited at ~₹100 cr per MW on top of ₹26 cr colocation capex. “This is purely data center, sir. This fund is going to be purely for data centers. For our real estate, we are completely funded with our internal sources.”
- *[Nov 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=27b8b856-615a-44a5-8be4-157fd1831d5c.pdf)* — An analyst (Raj Sarraf of Finvestors) asked for data centre revenue to be reported separately from real estate because it would become the major contributor; management conceded the point. “Sir, both the revenues are going to be substantial and we will be breaking them up, sir . We will do that definitely.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=3ac557ff-2c8f-4014-b2d4-e7e582aa0e59.pdf)* — The CFO positioned the company at an 'inflection point' with a legacy real estate business and a separate future-ready data centre/cloud platform — H1 FY26 revenue ₹1,223.2 cr of which data centre only ₹58.42 cr, ₹1,100 cr QIP completed, net cash positive, ~₹700 cr capital employed in data centres at 75% EBITDA margin. “Our legacy real estate business continues to deliver a consistent growth and strengthen our leadership in high demanding markets. At the same time, our Data Center and Cloud initiatives are shaping up the future ready platform that positions us as a diversified resilient enterprise s.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=3ac557ff-2c8f-4014-b2d4-e7e582aa0e59.pdf)* — Investors (Sri Gopal of StockHifi, Ashwani Sharma of Emkay) again pressed for separate real estate vs data centre revenue and EBITDA reporting; management said formal segment disclosure was not yet triggered because data centre revenue was under 10% of the total. “In this, you have to give segmental breakup once you do 10%.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=3ac557ff-2c8f-4014-b2d4-e7e582aa0e59.pdf)* — Asked whether the company should lever up to scale data centres faster, management refused on the grounds that real estate is the backbone and must stay low-debt — a tension a separately funded data centre entity resolves. Capacity plans were 63 MW by Dec 2026, 117 MW by FY28 and 307 MW by FY31-32. “And as it is, we feel that our backbone is still real estate, which will always be. And we feel that real estate should be as low on debt as possible.”
- *Scheme* — The May 11, 2026 board note first records the need for a merger/demerger, citing differing nature, risk profile, competitive dynamics and capital requirements, plus the 357 MW IT load plan (after the 50 MW Andhra Pradesh MOU) needing about ₹20,000 cr; a committee of Amit Sarin, Ashim Sarin, Manoj Goyal and Pankaj Gupta was formed to design it. “The Board of Directors have considered that the Company is presently engaged in two distinct business undertakings, namely Real Estate Development and Data Center Services, which differ significantly in their nature, risk profile, competitive dynamics, and capital requirements and continuing both businesses under a single corporate does not adequately reflect the true potential and intrinsic value of each business segment, thereby impacting stakeholder returns.”
- *Scheme* — The July 21, 2026 Scheme explains the data centre business is split across ARL and ARCPL, so ARCPL is first merged into ARL and the combined Data Centre Business then demerged into Ashok Cloud — consolidating it in one entity and creating two focused listed companies. “The Data Centre Business is presently conducted through ARL and ARCPL, with various assets, employees, investments and business operations pertaining to the Data Centre Business being housed across both entities.”
- *Scheme* — Stated benefit one: independent market recognition and valuation of the data centre business given its distinct operating profile, growth trajectory, risk-return characteristics and funding needs; demerged undertaking turnover was ₹145.90 cr, 8.96% of ₹1,627.72 cr for FY26. “the segregation of the Data Centre Business into a separately listed company would facilitate independent market recognition and valuation of the Data Centre Business, having regard to its distinct operating profile, growth trajectory, risk-return characteristics and funding requirements;”
- *Scheme* — Stated benefit two: a distinct legal entity lets Ashok Cloud attract sector-specific capital, investors, acquisitions and partnerships, with simpler ownership and intra-group arrangements cancelled or rationalised. “the separation of the Data Centre Business into a distinct legal entity will enable Ashok Cloud to effectively attract sector specific resources for its growth requirements and pursue strategic investments, partnerships, thereby unlocking greater value for its shareholders;”

*Not explained on the calls:* Calls never mention the demerger; no appointed date, debt/cash/asset split, valuation or swap basis, why ARL keeps 51%, how ₹20,000 cr capex gets funded, or listing timeline.
