Appointed Date 1 October 2026

**The stages, as filed:** announced (2026-09-18)

**Stated in the filings:** demerged undertaking: ) from DBRL to HSCL as a going concern, on an as is where is basis,; size hint: 3.39% of turnover.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Dalmia Bharat Refractories' Tyre Business — designing, manufacturing and development of all types of tyre and tyre products — class `regulatory_strategic`.

- *Insiders:* HSCL Promoter & Promoter Group 26,48,59,302 shares, 52.49% pre-Scheme to 52.47% post; DBRL promoters stay 74.99%, unchanged. HSCL has 53,896 outstanding exercisable employee stock options
- *What it reveals:* A ₹149.31 crore-turnover tyre business (3.39% of HSCL turnover) moves in for only 1,76,462 new shares — promoter stake dilutes just 0.02pp. Management targets ₹3,000 crore Birla Tyres top line in 4-5 years; EBITDA breakeven not yet reached
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — Only 1,76,462 new shares on 50.45 crore base; 1-for-260 entitlement leaves most DBRL holders fractions pooled with a trustee
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* The Scheme on www.himadri.com — Demerged Undertaking's assets, liabilities and Birla Tyres' standalone profitability
- *In their words:* “The Demerger will enable the Resulting Company to integrate the Tyre Business with its existing carbon black and advanced carbon materials business, thereby strengthening its presence across the tyre value chain.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Read against the documents, HSCL is not separating a business of its own — it is the receiving side of a separation: the 21 September 2026 Scheme demerges the Tyre Business (Birla Tyres, Balasore) out of Dalmia Bharat Refractories Limited (DBRL, the Demerged Company) and vests it in HSCL (the Resulting Company) as a going concern on an as-is-where-is basis with appointed date 1 October 2026, with no cash consideration — only 1 new HSCL share of Re 1 for every 260 DBRL shares of Rs 10, which adds just 1,76,462 shares and moves promoter holding from 52.49% to 52.47% (50,45,74,175 to 50,47,50,637 shares). The Board's stated reasons are: strategic forward integration of tyres with HSCL's existing carbon black and advanced carbon materials business; leveraging HSCL's material expertise, R&D, manufacturing and customer relationships for tyre product customisation; synergies across raw material sourcing, product development, manufacturing, logistics, distribution, market development, shared services and customer engagement; direct ownership and control to coordinate capacity utilisation, modernisation and product expansion; and greater strategic and financial flexibility to align investment, funding and capacity expansion — plus 'more focused ownership and a robust operating structure' so each company can direct management attention and capital to its own strengths. The business being moved is small and loss-making for now: turnover of the Demerged Undertaking was INR 149.31 crores at 31 March 2026, just 3.39% of HSCL's turnover (management separately cited Birla Tyres FY26 topline of INR 187 crores, INR 60+ crores in Q3FY26, INR 26 crores in Q2FY26, INR 5 crores in Q1FY26 and INR 127 crores in Q1FY27), with commercial operations only from 29 May 2025, EBITDA breakeven/cash-positive guided 'in this financial year' (FY27), and a target of INR 3,000 crores topline in 4-5 years. The problem it solves, as the calls make plain, is the awkward interim structure: tyres were manufactured on DBRL's balance sheet and merely bought and resold by wholly-owned Himadri Clean Energy, so HSCL booked tyre revenue but no tyre profit — 'we don't have any positive or negative impact as such as of now' (Jan 2026), 'we have not consolidated' (Apr 2026), and 'once it becomes part of Himadri, then the numbers will come' (Jul 2026). Direct ownership also lines up with the heavy spend already running through tyres — roughly INR 250-300 crores of additional capex in FY26 continuing for three years, and INR 500 crores of the ~INR 2,000 crores FY27-28 capex earmarked for Birla Tyres to convert Truck & Bus Bias capacity to OTR/OHT and commission a PCR line by FY28 for EV/SUV tyres. Notably, nobody on these calls says investors, lenders or partners demanded the step: analysts repeatedly pushed for tyre consolidation and segment numbers (Sanjesh Jain, Jul 2025; Dhruvin Kadakia, Apr 2026; Bhavin Chheda, Jul 2026) and Bharat Shah of ASK questioned whether a B2C tyre business was a distraction from speciality chemicals, but the Scheme is presented purely as a Board decision backed by a valuation report and a fairness opinion, with no lender or JV-partner request disclosed.

**How it evolved:** Through FY26 management framed Birla Tyres as deliberately arm's-length: on the Jul 18, 2025 call it was 'a standalone business' with its own P&L, HSCL explicitly selling it no carbon black, and when asked when the manufacturing entity would come inside HSCL the answer was flat — 'there is no intention as such now as of date.' The Oct 24, 2025 and Jan 21, 2026 calls kept the trading structure (Himadri Clean Energy buying from DBRL and reselling, so tyre margin landed nowhere in HSCL), while distributors grew 20 → 29 → 36; by Apr 27, 2026 the line was 'we have not consolidated — once we consolidate, then we can discuss this,' and on Jul 16, 2026 the CMD said tyres still sit on Dalmia Refractory's balance sheet and 'once it becomes part of Himadri, then the numbers will come,' alongside a INR 500 crore tyre capex plan. The Board then gave notice on 18 September 2026 and approved the demerger Scheme on 21 September 2026 (valuation and fairness opinion both dated 20 September 2026), with 1 October 2026 as the appointed date.

**What management expects from it:** For HSCL: forward integration across the tyre value chain, synergies in sourcing, product development, logistics, distribution and shared services, direct control over capacity utilisation, modernisation, OTR/PCR expansion, and flexibility to fund it — tyres reaching EBITDA breakeven in FY27 and INR 3,000 crores topline in 4-5 years. For DBRL: focused ownership, with management attention and capital redirected to its own strategic businesses.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=0c1a9508-b961-438a-8682-231850034afe.pdf)* — At the outset the tyre entry was positioned as deliberately non-integrated: Himadri would not supply carbon black to Birla Tyres because it could sell the same black at a premium elsewhere, and each business kept its own P&L. “However, it is important to note that Himadri will not be selling any carbon black to Birla Tyres.”
- *[Jul 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=0fd7bd5d-bcd3-4fba-90f2-35cf68ef18a1.pdf)* — Asked directly when the tyre manufacturing entity would be brought inside Himadri, management ruled it out at the time, calling Birla Tyres a standalone business acquired for about INR 300 crores against assets worth INR 3,400 crores. “No, there is no intention as such now as of date of its coming into Himadri.”
- *[Jul 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=0fd7bd5d-bcd3-4fba-90f2-35cf68ef18a1.pdf)* — Bharat Shah of ASK Investment Managers challenged the fit of a B2C tyre business inside a B2B speciality chemicals company; the CMD defended it as the ready-made launching pad into B2C with a 40-year brand, run by a separate vertical head. “See, today or tomorrow I have to go into B2C.”

To be very frank, we are not considering this as any revenue.”
- *[Jan 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=1448ca83-4f42-4c4c-92fc-6ecb61d0192b.pdf)* — The interim structure was spelled out: tyres were made under the Dalmia Bharat Refractories partnership and merely bought and resold by Himadri Clean Energy, so no tyre profit or loss reached HSCL on INR 60+ crores of quarterly tyre revenue. “So in Himadri, in Himadri Clean Energy, we are buying from Dalmia Refractory and selling the Birla Tyres. So we don't have any positive or negative impact as such as of now.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=4d692690-5309-49f1-9328-33ae32723066.pdf)* — Asked for tyre volumes and realisation, management refused on the ground that tyres were not consolidated — only clubbed into an 'others' segment with mining — while disclosing FY26 tyre topline of INR 187 crores and a INR 3,000 crore ambition in four years. “Tyre still now, we have not consolidated. Once we consolidate, then we can discuss this.”
- *[Jul 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=aba2c1e9-bf26-4569-afee-2e8b196215cb.pdf)* — On Bhavin Chheda's question whether the INR 127 crore quarterly tyre revenue was EBITDA positive, the CMD said not yet and tied the missing profit disclosure explicitly to the business sitting on DBRL's balance sheet pending transfer into Himadri. “So now Birla Tyres is reflected on Dalmia Refractory balance sheet. So once it becomes part of Himadri, then the numbers will come.”
- *[Jul 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=aba2c1e9-bf26-4569-afee-2e8b196215cb.pdf)* — The capital case for direct ownership: INR 500 crores of the ~INR 2,000 crore FY27-FY28 capex is for Birla Tyres, funding phased TBB-to-OTR conversion, modernisation/automation, 400+ new SKUs and a PCR line by FY28, with breakeven guided for FY27. “We reach EBITDA breakeven in this financial year only. We will be cash positive.”
- *Scheme* — The Board's first stated benefit is forward integration — folding the tyre business into HSCL's carbon black and advanced carbon materials platform to own more of the tyre value chain, reversing the earlier 'separate P&Ls, no internal carbon black sales' stance. “The Demerger will enable the Resulting Company to integrate the Tyre Business with its existing carbon black and advanced carbon materials business, thereby strengthening its presence across the tyre value chain.”
- *Scheme* — Control and funding flexibility are cited as the operating rationale: direct ownership lets HSCL coordinate capacity utilisation, modernisation, product expansion and distribution, and align tyre investment and funding with group strategy. “Direct ownership will enable the Resulting Company to align investment, funding, capacity expansion and growth priorities of the Tyre Business with its broader business strategy.”
- *Scheme* — Scale of what moves: the Demerged Undertaking (all assets, liabilities, contracts, employees, brands, trademarks, licences of DBRL's tyre business) had turnover of INR 149.31 crores at 31 March 2026, only 3.39% of HSCL's turnover. “Turnover of the Demerged Undertaking as on 31 March 2026, was INR 149.31 crores, which constitutes 3.39% of total turnover of Resulting Company in the immediately preceding financial year / based on financials of last financial year (i.e. for year ended 31 March 2026).”
- *Scheme* — Consideration is non-cash and barely dilutive: 1 HSCL share per 260 DBRL shares, based on a 20 September 2026 valuation by SSPA & Co and CA Manish Gadia with a fairness opinion from Jajodia Equity Advisors; promoter holding moves 52.49% to 52.47%. “1 (One) fully paid-up equity shares of face value of INR 1 (one) each of the Resulting Company shall be issued and allotted for every 260 (Two Hundred Sixty) fully paid-up equity shares of face value of INR 10 (ten) each held in the Demerged Company”

*Not explained on the calls:* No reason given for DBRL exiting or for reversing the Jul 2025 'no intention' stance; no tyre EBITDA, debt, or treatment of HSCL's INR 300 crore stake, NCDs or HBTMPL 49%.

## MOTHERSON — Samvardhana Motherson International Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 5.0/10 · spin-off · 2 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-10-16, latest 2026-10-26

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**Stated in the filings:** demerged undertaking: of Samvardhana.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Automotive Manufacturing and Services Business (Demerged Undertaking) of Samvardhana Motherson Innovative Solutions Limited, transferred into listed parent SAMIL — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* Not stated. Demerged Company is a 100% subsidiary of the Resulting Company, so no shares are issued; documents give no promoter or management stake or incentive details
- *What it reveals:* Internal pull-up, not a separation: an automotive manufacturing and services business already owned 100% moves into the listed entity, with SMISL's Remaining Business retained. Pre- and post-arrangement net worth of both companies is positive; amalgamating SMAS has negative net worth
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — No shares issued, no new listed entity, no index change; wholly owned subsidiaries within the same group
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Scheme of Arrangement, Annexure F (pages 555-625), Clause 5 of Part B: assets/liabilities of the Demerged Undertaking
- *In their words:* “Since the Demerged Company is 100% (one hundred percent) subsidiary of the Resulting Company, no shares will be issued by the Resulting Company.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Two distinct things are going on, and only one of them is explained in detail. The hard, documented action is a composite scheme of arrangement approved by SAMIL's board on 07.02.2025 and sanctioned by NCLT Mumbai on 26.10.2026, with an Appointed Date of 01.04.2024: the 'Automotive Manufacturing and Services Business' (the Demerged Undertaking) is carved out of wholly owned subsidiary Samvardhana Motherson Innovative Solutions Limited (SMISL) and vested in listed parent Samvardhana Motherson International Limited (SAMIL), while SMISL's 'Remaining Business' stays behind; alongside it, Samvardhana Motherson Auto System Private Limited (SMAS) amalgamates into SAMIL and Motherson Machinery and Automations Limited (MMAL) amalgamates into SMISL, both amalgamating companies dissolving without winding up and their share capital simply cancelled. Management's stated reasons for the demerger are focused management attention and leadership, independence and flexibility over each business's cash flows so projects can be run 'more consistently and advantageously', a leaner and more focused organisation, a reduction in layers of investments producing a simpler structure, more transparent shareholding with better visibility and accountability, and enhanced shareholder value. The merger legs are justified separately as eliminating multiple group entities, pooling financial, human, technological and managerial resources, cutting duplicated administrative expenses and overheads and compliances, better day-to-day coordination, and unlocking synergies across products, customers, technology and manufacturing. No valuation, ratio or cash changes hands: because SMISL is a 100% subsidiary, 'no shares will be issued by the Resulting Company', and SMAS/MMAL shareholders likewise get nothing — the scheme is pure structural plumbing within wholly owned entities. Separately and far more loudly, the Sep 2025 investor meet framed a different kind of separation as a Vision 2030 deliverable: having 'successfully took out MSWIL', management said many businesses are 'ripe to now leave the SAMIL fold and be independently listed on their own', explicitly flagging aerospace (grown 550x in five years, ~USD 250mn revenue, >USD 1bn order book then, USD 1.6bn by May 2026) as 'probably ripe for the independence'. Nobody outside management — no investor, lender, customer or JV partner — is cited as asking for either; the RD, ROC and Official Liquidator raised only process points (SMAS's negative net worth, protection of creditors, BEN-2 filings, Income Tax scrutiny), and the Petitioners answered that nothing in the Companies Act bars merging a negative-net-worth company and that both demerged and resulting net worth are positive.

**How it evolved:** The idea first appears as corporate action on 07.02.2025 (board approval, intimated to exchanges 28.02.2025), then NCLT first motion on 30.05.2025 and further service affidavits through 18.09.2025; the earnings calls never mention it. The only management articulation comes at the Sep 2025 investor meet, where Vaaman Sehgal makes 'independent companies from SAMIL' a Vision 2030 target, citing the MSWIL precedent and naming aerospace as the likeliest candidate. The Aug 2025, Nov 2025, Feb 2026 and May 2026 calls say nothing about any separation — they stay on European restructuring, consumer electronics GF1/GF2/GF3, aerospace order book and acquisitions (Atsumitec, Yutaka Giken, Nexans Autoelectric). Final NCLT sanction landed 26.10.2026, binding from the 01.04.2024 Appointed Date, with SMAS and MMAL dissolved.

**What management expects from it:** Per the Scheme: focused management attention, independent control of each business's cash flows, a leaner organisation with higher operational efficiency, fewer investment layers and a simpler, more transparent structure with better accountability, lower duplicated overheads and compliance cost, pooled resources, product/customer/technology synergies, and enhanced shareholder value. Per Sep 2025: independently listed companies unlocking shareholder value, aerospace first.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Sep 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=52763e10-5ff5-49dd-bb00-3f519df3db3c.pdf)* — Vaaman Sehgal makes separation an explicit Vision 2030 deliverable, citing the already-completed MSWIL (Motherson Sumi Wiring India) carve-out as the template for more businesses leaving the SAMIL fold as separately listed companies. “We successfully took out MSWIL, which has been extremely successful for us. And we believe that many companies are ripe to now leave the SAMIL fold and be independently listed on their own.”
- *[Sep 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=52763e10-5ff5-49dd-bb00-3f519df3db3c.pdf)* — He frames the purpose as value unlocking for shareholders from businesses incubated inside SAMIL that can now stand alone, and says it will go beyond divisions to multiple independent companies. “We're going to create a lot more independent companies from SAMIL, which they have been incubated and stand on their own feet and unlock a tremendous amount of value for all our shareholders.”
- *[Sep 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=52763e10-5ff5-49dd-bb00-3f519df3db3c.pdf)* — Aerospace is singled out as the most likely candidate for independence, right after Kunal Bajaj's segment reporting 550x growth in five years, ~USD 250mn revenue and over USD 1bn order book from a standing start. “Ladies and gentlemen, one of the most exciting verticals, probably ripe for the independence that I spoke about, and a lot of things are going to happen in this vertical.”
- *Scheme* — Clause 3.1(i): the core stated reason for hiving the Automotive Manufacturing and Services Business out of SMISL and into SAMIL is focused management attention and leadership. “To ensure focused management attention and leadership it is proposed to segregate the Demerged Undertaking from the Demerged Company into the Resulting Company.”
- *Scheme* — Clause 3.1(ii): the separation is justified as giving each business independent control over its own cash flows and project funding decisions. “The structure post Demerger will provide independence and flexibility to the management in decisions regarding the use of their respective cash flow under various projects.”
- *Scheme* — Clause 3.1(iii)–(iv): efficiency and shareholder-value arguments — a leaner, focused organisation and a focused operating strategy in the interest of shareholders, employees and other stakeholders. “Overall, Demerger would enhance operational efficiency and effectiveness by creating leaner and focused organisation.”
- *Scheme* — Clause 3.1(v)–(vi): the structural problems being solved are stacked investment layers and opaque shareholding inside the group holding chain. “The Demerger will facilitate a reduction of layers of investments, leading to a simpler structure.”
- *Scheme* — Clause 3.2: the two amalgamation legs (SMAS into SAMIL, MMAL into SMISL) are justified on entity-count reduction, resource pooling and removal of duplicated administrative expenses, overheads and compliances. “Simplification of the corporate structure by elimination of multiple entities in the group.”
- *Scheme* — Clause 3.2(v): the mergers are also expected to unlock cross-business synergies, the same language used across Motherson's acquisition rationales. “Unlocking potential synergies across  products, customers, technology and manufacturing excellence.”
- *Scheme* — Clauses 14.1, 25.1–25.2 and 37.1: no consideration, no share issuance and no ratio — all participating entities are wholly owned, so SMAS's and MMAL's capital is simply cancelled on the Effective Date and both dissolve without winding up. “Since the Demerged Company is 100% (one hundred percent) subsidiary of the Resulting Company, no shares will be issued by the Resulting Company.”
- *Scheme* — The Registrar of Companies flagged that SMAS carried a negative net worth as at 31.03.2025; the Petitioners answered that nothing in the Companies Act bars merging such a company and that both Demerged and Resulting Company net worth is positive post-arrangement. “From the Financials of the Amalgamating  Company 1 i.e. Samvardhana Motherson  Auto System P rivate Limited  as at  31.03.2025, it is observed that the  company is having negative net worth.”
- *Scheme* — The scheme is backdated: the Appointed Date is 01.04.2024, with the First Motion application filed 06.03.2025 to stay inside the one-year window under section 232(6), and NCLT sanction only arriving 26.10.2026. “The Appointed Date  fixed under the proposed Scheme of A rrangement  is 01.04.2024.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No revenue, EBITDA, assets or employee numbers for the Demerged Undertaking; no margin, capital-allocation or valuation math; no listing timetable; no named candidate entities; no mention on any earnings call.

## PRICOLLTD — Pricol Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 5.0/10 · spin-off · 6 filing(s) from NSE, NSE-deep · first 2026-06-27, latest 2026-11-04

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; Pricol Autotech Limited will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; indicated timeline: No date stated; 27 June 2026 filing: "Yes. The equity shares of the Resulting Company shall be listed and admitted to trading on the Stock Exchanges pursuant to the Scheme subject to receipt of requisite approvals from statutory and regulatory authorities" — proposed on NSE and BSE, shown as the last of six milestones after NCLT approval

**Stated in the filings:** resulting company **Pricol Autotech Limited**; entitlement **1 for every 1**; appointed date 2026-06-27; size hint: 4.5% of revenue.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Driver Information & Connected Vehicle Solutions (DICVS) business — instrument clusters, infotainment, e-cockpit, telematics, battery management, some sensors — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* Promoters 100% of Resulting Company pre-Scheme (via Pricol), cancelled; post-Scheme promoters 38.51%, public 61.49% — mirroring Pricol. Vikram Mohan Chairman & MD; "dedicated leadership, specialised talent and incentive structures"
- *What it reveals:* The separated DICVS business is the larger half — INR 2,424.63 crores, 61.17% of FY26 consolidated turnover — a high-growth electronics/technology platform; separation seeks "appropriate valuation benchmarks for each business, free from conglomerate discount"
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — Not a small stub: 61.17% of consolidated turnover, same automotive sector, 1:1 mirror shareholding; documents state no index or size effects
- *Parent or spin:* spin · *option pricing date:* Share Entitlement Ratio Report dated 27th June 2026 by SSPA & Co, with Fairness Opinion from Saffron Capital Advisors
- *Read next:* The Scheme of Arrangement on pricol.com/investors — DICVS carve-out assets, debt and EBITDA assigned to Pricol Autotech
- *In their words:* “The turnover of the DICVS Business for the financial year ending March 31, 2026, stood at INR 2,424.63 crores.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Pricol's board, on 27 June 2026, approved demerging the Driver Information & Connected Vehicle Solutions (DICVS) undertaking — connected/electronic/mechanical/electro-mechanical instrument clusters, infotainment, e-cockpit, telematics, battery management systems and some sensors — into a newly incorporated wholly-owned company, Pricol Autotech Limited, leaving Pricol Limited with Actuation, Control & Fluid Management Systems (ACFMS) and the Precision Products polymer business (P3L, acquired from Sundaram Auto Components on 1 February 2025). DICVS was not a small tail: its FY26 turnover was INR 2,424.63 crores, 61.17% of the INR 3,963.85 crore consolidated revenue, and on the 15 May 2026 call management put the mix at roughly 60% DICVS, 20% ACFMS, 20% P3L. The stated problem is that the two halves had drifted apart on "differing customer needs, competitive dynamics, capital allocation and risk profiles" while both had reached "sufficient scale and maturity to function more effectively as focused standalone businesses" — an innovation-led electronics platform (software, display/chip partnerships like the exclusive BOE MOU, 4.5% of revenue on R&D, semiconductor and technology-disruption risk) versus a scale-led manufacturing platform (capacity, automation, tooling, commodity cost and cyclicality risk). The calls show the underlying economics the split addresses: DICVS at INR 2,100–2,200 crores with 12.5–13% EBITDA, ACFMS at ~INR 600 crores targeting 30–35% growth, and polymer at INR 850–900 crores at ~9.5%, a business management said "will never have a 13 to 15% EBITDA because it is a component company" — plus competing claims on one balance sheet, with INR 680–700 crores of capex planned for FY27 alone. The filing says the separation will give each entity financial flexibility for its own investment decisions, reduce operational complexity and speed decision-making, provide "independent and dedicated management teams," let each tailor processes, systems and governance, and deliver "clear market recognition and appropriate valuation benchmarks for each business, free from conglomerate discount," improving the ability to attract strategic and financial investors. Shareholders get 1 new Pricol Autotech share per Pricol share (1:1, INR 1 face value), so the 38.51% promoter / 61.49% public pattern is mirrored, with no cash consideration and listing sought on NSE and BSE. Notably, no investor, lender, customer or partner is named anywhere as having asked for the separation: it is presented as a board-initiated strategic decision, supported by Veda Corporate Advisors, Khaitan & Co, Ramani & Shankar, PwC, SSPA & Co (share entitlement ratio) and Saffron Capital (fairness opinion).

**How it evolved:** Across all eleven calls from 9 November 2023 to 15 May 2026 the separation is never mentioned — what evolves is the three-vertical structure that makes it possible: DICVS/ACFMS running at ~69:31 in May 2024, the TVS-group plastics acquisition announced on the 30 January 2025 call and closed 1 February 2025, and by 7 November 2025 three verticals with explicitly divergent profiles (DICVS INR 2,100–2,200 cr at 12.5–13%, ACFMS ~INR 600 cr growing 30–35%, polymer INR 850–900 cr at 9.5%). The only visible pre-announcement trace is the 30 January 2026 call, where a question about a newly incorporated subsidiary was answered as flexibility for technology partnerships and the BOE MOU, not as a carve-out vehicle; the 15 May 2026 call likewise discussed only capex, headwinds and polymer value-addition. The plan surfaces fully formed in the 27 June 2026 board filing, media note and presentation, and is then carried as a one-line note in the 30 July 2026 and 4 November 2026 results, with Pricol Autotech Limited, Coimbatore appearing in the consolidated subsidiary list and approvals from the exchanges, NCLT, shareholders and creditors still pending.

**What management expects from it:** Pricol Autotech: an innovation-led electronics platform funded for talent, software, global R&D and overseas M&A, with higher content per vehicle. Pricol Limited: scale-led ACFMS plus polymer, funded for capacity, automation and domestic M&A, riding exports and disc-brake/ABS mandates. For both: separate valuation benchmarks free of conglomerate discount, tailored capital allocation, dedicated leadership, faster decisions, and easier access to strategic and financial investors.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The core stated problem: the DICVS undertaking and the remaining ACFMS/P3L business had come to differ on customers, competition, capital allocation and risk, and each had grown big enough to stand alone. “The Demerged Undertaking and the Remaining Business of the Demerged Company currently operates with differing customer needs, competitive dynamics, capital allocation and risk profiles.”
- *Scheme* — Scale of what is leaving: DICVS turnover of INR 2,424.63 crores in FY26, i.e. 61.17% of consolidated turnover — the majority of the company, not a tail business. “The turnover of the DICVS Business for the financial year ending March 31, 2026, stood at INR 2,424.63 crores. This represents 61.17% of the total consolidated turnover of the Company for the financial year ending March 31, 2026.”
- *Scheme* — Valuation is an explicit objective — the presentation names the conglomerate discount as the thing being removed by giving each business its own benchmark. “Clear market recognition and appropriate valuation benchmarks for each business, free from conglomerate discount”
- *Scheme* — Capital allocation is framed as structurally incompatible: Autotech's money goes to talent, software, global R&D centres and overseas acquisitions, while Pricol Ltd's goes to plants, automation and domestic acquisitions. “Talent, product development, software, global R&D centres, tech investments & overseas acquisitions”
- *Scheme* — The two entities are also said to carry different risk books — technology/semiconductor risk on one side, cyclicality and commodity/execution risk on the other. “Technology disruption, product innovation cycles & semiconductor ecosystem risks”
- *Scheme* — Operational benefits claimed: dedicated management teams, faster decisions, and the ability to tailor processes, policies, systems and governance per business. “This demerger will provide each of the businesses with independent and dedicated management teams enabling clear market access and a clean operating model, allowing them to better leverage growth opportunities in the domestic and international markets”
- *Scheme* — Consideration and ownership: no cash, a 1:1 share entitlement so Pricol Autotech mirrors the 38.51% promoter / 61.49% public pattern, with listing to be sought on NSE and BSE. “Shareholders of Pricol Limited will receive one fully paid-up equity share of Pricol Autotech Limited for every one fully paid-up equity share held in Pricol Limited (1:1 share entitlement ratio), resulting in the shareholding of Pricol Autotech Limited mirroring the shareholding of Pricol Limited, subject to the Scheme becoming effective.”
- *Scheme* — Vikram Mohan's framing of timing — the businesses have become differentiated enough that independence, not scale, is now the constraint. “We believe this is the right time for each business to operate independently with dedicated leadership, sharper strategic focus and greater operational agility.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=26bade69-10e6-4c8a-81c7-8d7391d0be51.pdf)* — The only pre-announcement trace on any call: a newly incorporated subsidiary (Pricol Autotech was later the resulting company) was explained purely as flexibility for technology partnerships such as the BOE MOU, with no mention of a carve-out. “Considering all these aspects, we wanted to have the flexibility and have a company in place.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ceafd440-d32e-4124-b0d8-0986c8098710.pdf)* — One month before the board approval, management sized the three verticals that the scheme then split 60:40 — DICVS against ACFMS plus P3L. “On the DICVS our revenue is about 60% of our total revenue, and ACFMS is about 20% and P3L would be about 20%.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=aca6af66-645a-45a7-a8e0-c1e158f53fe5.pdf)* — The divergent financial profiles the split formalises were laid out on this call: DICVS at INR 2,100–2,200 crores and 12.5–13% margin, ACFMS at ~INR 600 crores targeting 30–35% growth, polymer at INR 850–900 crores at ~9.5%. “And the DICVS vertical will be at around INR 2,100 crores to INR 2,200 crores, and the margin is likely to be at around 12.5% to 13%.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=464bedf8-3c0b-4544-9b8e-ff2c0a9706a4.pdf)* — Management stated the structural margin ceiling difference between the electronics business and the newly acquired polymer component business — the economic gap that later justifies separate valuation frameworks. “Pricol Precision Products will never have a 13 to 15% EBITDA because it is a component company.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No explanation of who asked, debt/asset split, Autotech's standalone P&L or margin targets, dis-synergies and duplicated costs, listing timeline, or named management teams; no earnings call ever discussed it.

- *In their words:* “The Company has received a letter dated August 6, 2026, from the RBI, conveying that the application has been examined and that the request has not been acceded to.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Religare is demerging its entire financial services business — SME/MSME lending (Religare Finvest), retail broking plus e-governance (Religare Broking and its subsidiary Religare Digital Solutions), affordable housing finance (Religare Housing Development Finance, already an RFL subsidiary), and the related investment and ancillary/support activities — out of the listed holdco REL into RFL, which will itself be listed, leaving REL as a pure-play holder of its 63.2% stake in Care Health Insurance; REL shareholders get 1 RFL share for every REL share, and RFL's pre-scheme capital held by REL is cancelled so RFL's shareholding mirrors REL's. Management framed it as three converging conditions rather than a reaction to distress: the Burman Group's completed takeover as promoters (open offer concluded Feb 2025, board reconstituted July 2025, promoters at 29.75% fully diluted in Feb 2026 and ~30.3% by May 2026 after ~4% of open-market buying, heading to ~34% on warrant conversion), the INR1,500 crore preferential warrant raise subscribed 50:50 by the Burmans and marquee investors (earmarked INR600 crore to Care, INR250 crore to housing finance, INR200 crore to broking, INR75 crore to repay REL's own debt and INR375 crore general corporate purpose), and the fact that the businesses had reached an inflection point where "each business also operates with different capital requirements, risk frameworks, manpower talent and growth trajectories." The stated problems it solves are a conglomerate structure in which insurance (FY26 GWP INR11,417 crore, PBT INR539 crore on 'n' basis, 19.7% retail SAHI share) drowns out a tiny financial services segment (FY25 demerged-undertaking turnover of only INR457.29 crore, 6.2% of consolidated revenue), investors who cannot value the two halves, and management bandwidth: the scheme's four pillars are streamlined focus/simplified structure, value unlocking plus targeted capital raising through a separate RFL listing, dedicated leadership with sector-specific talent and performance-linked rewards, and risk/compliance frameworks tailored to each segment. The financial services side is being restarted from a cleaned-up base — RFL is debt-free with all legacy promoter-era diversion issues provided or written off (including the full INR750 crore Lakshmi Vilas Bank FD), RBI's Corrective Action Plan lifted in July 2025 and bank fraud tags removed, leaving ~INR591 crore cash, ~INR900 crore net worth, 261% CRAR, NOF of INR821 crore and only a ~INR60 crore core SME book — so Arjun Lamba tied the demerger directly to scaling: "Our intent is to scale all of these business to make them meaningful and sizable and part of this demerger is on account of this." Who asked for it: shareholders and analysts had been pressing since the first call back in Nov 2025 (Vikas Shrivastav on demerging Care and removing the holdco discount, Dixit Doshi on IPO vs demerger of Care), and after the announcement nearly every questioner — Umang Shah, Adarsh, Hitaindra Pradhan, Ravi Purohit, Niharika Karnani, Sarvesh Gupta — argued the value sits in Care and demanded a reverse merger giving direct Care shares, citing the Max Financial precedent. Management conceded the point but said IRDAI's 25–26% promoter requirement cannot be met while the Burmans' look-through stake in Care is only ~18–19%, so this was "the first step in that direction," done after evaluating structural alternatives with leading advisors; Lamba refused to amend the scheme and would not commit to a timeline for a second one. Execution has since run into the regulator: exchanges gave no-objection/no-adverse-observation letters on 7 July 2026, but on 6–7 August 2026 RBI informed REL and RFL that their application for no-objection/prior approval "has not been acceded to," and the companies said they would engage further with the regulator.

**How it evolved:** On the Nov 2025 call (Q2/H1 FY26, the first investor call after the Burman takeover) there was no plan — Vikas Shrivastav asked directly what the structure would look like in two years and whether Care would be demerged from the holdco, and CFO Pratul Gupta would only say the board was evaluating options and wanted to make the businesses "larger, better, stronger" before any capital-market action, while Dixit Doshi asked whether Care would be IPO'd or demerged. A Moneycontrol report on 3 Feb 2026 that REL would demerge and list Care drew an exchange query, which REL denied as a disclosable event; eleven days later, on 14 Feb 2026, the REL and RFL boards approved the scheme — and the Feb 2026 call (16 Feb) was where Gupta laid out the full rationale, the four pillars, the 1:1 ratio, the 15–18 month timetable and a Q1 FY28 RFL listing, while every analyst pushed back that Care, not financial services, should have been separated. By the May 2026 call (13 May, Q4/FY26) the framing had shifted from Gupta's structural logic to Executive Director Arjun Lamba's: separating FS from insurance was "number one," the promoters had bought ~4% more stock toward the IRDAI threshold, and he declined to amend the scheme while leaving a later reverse merger of Care open "at an appropriate stage." The 7 July 2026 exchange observation letters cleared the way, but the 7 Aug 2026 filings disclosed RBI had refused to accede to the application, leaving the scheme stalled pending further engagement.

**What management expects from it:** REL becomes a pure-play health insurance holdco around Care (GWP INR11,417 crore, PBT INR539 crore 'n' basis, combined ratio heading from 101.4% to ~100% in two years on operating leverage, 18–24% growth). RFL becomes an integrated, separately listed financial services platform — debt-free, ~INR900 crore net worth, ~INR591 crore cash, 261% CRAR — able to leverage to industry norms, raise targeted capital, hire sector-specific leadership on performance-linked rewards, run tailored risk frameworks, and unlock value via mirror 1:1 listing.

The investment in CARE shall continue to be retained in REL.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=b273d588-fe12-446c-bee6-b5d6269b6a44.pdf)* — A separate RFL listing is meant to unlock value, widen investor participation and let that business raise its own capital — the second of four stated pillars. “The independent listing of RFL is expected to unlock shareholder value and enhance investor participation.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=b273d588-fe12-446c-bee6-b5d6269b6a44.pdf)* — Analysts attacked the design immediately: Umang Shah argued demerging Care directly would have removed the holdco discount on the asset that carries most of the value. “I'm a bit puzzled why we chose to demerge financial services and not CARE directly?”

- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=b273d588-fe12-446c-bee6-b5d6269b6a44.pdf)* — The binding constraint on a Care reverse merger is the IRDAI promoter-shareholding rule against a Burman look-through stake in Care of only ~18–19%, which Gupta confirmed when Vikas Srivastava spelled out the law. “So you are right in terms of the fact that the look - through shareholding of the promoter group today in CARE is at around 18% to 19%.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=b273d588-fe12-446c-bee6-b5d6269b6a44.pdf)* — Management said the structure was chosen after a full review of alternatives with external advisors, and promised no operational, customer or employee disruption during implementation. “This has resulted after comprehensive evalu ation of various structural alternatives which were discussed with leading advisors.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=87938b4d-578d-40b0-89a8-7803462a6057.pdf)* — Arjun Lamba restated the core purpose as separating financial services from insurance to give shareholders a clean, understandable structure and management a single focus, while acknowledging the holdco-discount complaint. “And for us, number one has been to separate the FS business from the insurance business and to provide a clean structure so that the shareholders can understand, th e management can be very focused in doing what they have to do.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=87938b4d-578d-40b0-89a8-7803462a6057.pdf)* — Lamba linked the demerger to the capital allocation plan — INR600 crore to Care, INR250 crore to housing finance, INR200 crore to broking, ~INR375 crore general corporate purpose, with RFL needing none given ~INR900–1,000 crore net worth and ~INR600 crore cash. “Our intent is to scale all of these business to make them meaningful and sizable and part of this demerger is on account of this.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No cost-benefit or synergy quantification, no RFL valuation or AUM/ROE targets, no holdco-discount fix or Care reverse-merger timeline, no stated path to IRDAI's 26%, and no RBI-rejection reasoning.

- *Selling pressure:* unclear — Documents state only the 1:1 allotment to every parent shareholder and the December 5, 2025 listing; no index, size or shareholder-flow detail given

- *In their words:* “The results come against the backdrop of SKF's demerger into two sector-focused, strategically independent organizations, enabling sharper market orientation, faster decision-making, and enhanced long-term value creation for shareholders, marking a pivotal step in SKF's 102-year India journey.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The separation is the demerger of the Industrial undertaking of SKF India Limited (automotive remaining with SKF India Ltd.) into SKF India (Industrial) Limited, a company incorporated 17 December 2024 purely to receive it, sanctioned by NCLT Mumbai on 26 September 2025 with appointed/effective date 1 October 2025, a 1:1 share exchange (49,437,963 shares to SKF India holders on the 15 October 2025 record date) and listing on BSE/NSE from 5 December 2025. Management's stated reason is sector focus: the Q3 FY25-26 release frames it as 'SKF's demerger into two sector-focused, strategically independent organizations, enabling sharper market orientation, faster decision-making, and enhanced long-term value creation for shareholders,' a 'pivotal step in SKF's 102-year India journey,' with the industrial entity 'more agile and focused,' able to 'respond faster to market needs' and 'tailor it's manufacturing capabilities' for manufacturing, railways, renewables, cement and heavy engineering. On the 13 May 2026 call the operating logic is spelled out as the ACES strategy to 2028 (accelerate localization, commercial excellence, disciplined execution, one SKF) plus the point that industrial economics differ structurally from automotive — 'industrial business is all about flexibility in the channels... because the lot size, unlike automotive, is smaller' — and that localization lets it re-enter segments it had exited (wind, freight railways, agricultural tractors). Dedicated capacity is the second half of the logic: the Board approved a new Pune factory on 3 February 2026, part of INR 800 crore+ capex to FY29-30 (including INR 350-400 crore of DGBB/TRB channel additions), commissioning end-CY2028, because the business is 'running out of capacity' and currently relies on SKF India job work. The cost of separating was explicit: INR 1,800.8 million of exceptional demerger charges in Q3 FY26 (IT, professional fees, large stamp duty/transfer premium on the land transferred from SKF India), INR 1,961 million for nine months, and a further INR 183 million of demerger IT cost in Q4, which turned reported Q3 PBT to negative INR 671.4 million against INR 1,129.4 million before exceptionals. Management's payoff case is margin recovery to ~13% once demerger costs lapse by end-CY2026, ~15% by FY29-30 and an aspiration of 16-18%, on 8%+ growth; interim performance cited was Q4 FY26 sales INR 9,457.2 million (+9.8% QoQ, +31% YoY), PBT 9.5% reported and 11.5% ex-one-offs, net working capital down 2.8% to 18.7% of sales, then Q1 FY27 revenue INR 9,707.7 million (+18.3% YoY) at 9.0% PBT.

**How it evolved:** These texts contain no pre-demerger call, so the origin of the idea is not on record here; the earliest document is the Scheme itself (NCLT order 26 September 2025, effective 1 October 2025, listing 5 December 2025). The 4 February 2026 press release, reporting the first post-demerger quarter, carries the only explicit rationale statement (two sector-focused independent organizations, sharper orientation, faster decisions, shareholder value) alongside INR 1,800.8 million of separation costs, and the same Board meeting on 3 February 2026 approved the new Pune factory — converting the rationale into standalone capacity. By the 13 May 2026 Q4/FY26 call the framing had shifted from justification to execution: the ACES strategy 'as we are now a separate listed entity,' INR 800 crore+ capex, re-entry into previously exited wind/railway/tractor business, and a margin path of 13% near term to 15% by FY29-30. The 12 August 2026 Q1 FY27 release continues the 'focused, independent business' framing with 18.3% YoY growth at 9% PBT.

**What management expects from it:** For SKF India (Industrial): sharper market orientation, faster decisions, agility and manufacturing tailored to industrial lot sizes; ~8% growth with PBT recovering to ~13% by end-CY2026, ~15% by FY29-30 (16-18% aspiration); net working capital 19-20% of sales; INR 800 crore+ own capex and a new Pune plant replacing SKF India job work; shareholder value via two independent listed entities.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The Scheme of Arrangement between SKF India Limited (Demerged Company) and SKF India (Industrial) Limited (Resulting Company) transferred the Industrial Undertaking on a going-concern basis at carrying values, with the difference credited to Capital Reserve; NCLT order dated 26 September 2025, appointed and effective date 1 October 2025. “The Scheme, among other provisions, entails the demerger of the Demerged Undertaking from the Demerged Company into the Resulting Company on a going concern basis.”
- *Scheme* — The only explicit statement of purpose in the filings: two sector-focused, independent organizations for sharper market orientation, faster decision-making and shareholder value, after 102 years of SKF in India. “The results come against the backdrop of SKF's demerger into two sector-focused, strategically independent organizations, enabling sharper market orientation, faster decision-making, and enhanced long-term value creation for shareholders, marking a pivotal step in SKF's 102-year India journey.”
- *Scheme* — MD Mukund Vasudevan's rationale in the 4 February 2026 Q3 FY25-26 release: agility, speed of response and manufacturing tailored to industrial customers, serving manufacturing, railways, renewables, cement and heavy engineering. “As a more agile and focused industrial entity, SKF India (Industrial) is well-positioned to respond faster to market needs, tailor it's manufacturing capabilities, and support India's accelerating infrastructure and manufacturing build-out.”
- *Scheme* — Separation cost quantified as exceptional items: INR 1,800.8 million in Q3 FY26 and INR 1,961 million for nine months for IT cost, professional services and stamp duty including transfer premium on land acquired under the Scheme — which pushed reported Q3 PBT to negative INR 671.4 million versus INR 1,129.4 million before exceptionals. “During the quarter and nine months ended 31 December 2025, the Company accounted certain demerger expenses for IT Cost, professional services and stamp duty, including estimated transfer premium payable to statutory authorities to effect transfer of registration of land acquired under the Scheme, aggregating to Rs. 1,800.8 million and Rs. 1,961 million, respectively, which have been included under "Exceptional items".”
- *Scheme* — The Board meeting of 3 February 2026 — the same meeting that approved the first post-demerger results — approved a new standalone factory at Pune, the capacity leg of the separation. “We wish to inform you that the Board of Directors of the Company at its meeting held today, i.e. on February 03, 2026, has approved the setting up of a new factory /plant at Pune, Maharashtra.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=1289a753-236a-4201-9367-4432f4270674.pdf)* — Management re-stated the ACES strategy (accelerate localization, commercial excellence, disciplined execution, one SKF, defined through 2028) explicitly because the company is now separately listed and needs its own growth and profitability narrative. “I thought it's important to reiterate our strategy as we are now a separate listed entity as SKF India (Industrial) and I think it helps to kind of say what are we trying to do and how are we trying to grow and make our business more profitable.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=1289a753-236a-4201-9367-4432f4270674.pdf)* — The structural case for separate industrial management: industrial runs on small lot sizes and channel flexibility unlike automotive — the Pune TRB example raised capacity from 600,000 to 886,000 pieces, cut cost ~18% and improved changeover/flexibility 20% and new-product lead time 35%. “Flexibility, which is key, which is industrial business is all about flexibility in the channels, which means we can switch between one product and another because the lot size, unlike automotive, is smaller.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=1289a753-236a-4201-9367-4432f4270674.pdf)* — A concrete problem the focused, localized entity solves: segments previously abandoned on cost/margin grounds — wind, freight railways, agricultural tractors — are being re-entered via localization, including a 32.5 crore tractor OEM win and ZF/Suzlon wind orders that drove 91% QoQ wind growth. “The reason you are right, we did exit wind business . Because of localization we are now getting back into it.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=1289a753-236a-4201-9367-4432f4270674.pdf)* — Residual entanglement with the automotive entity persists: SKF India (Industrial) manufactures for SKF India Automotive (~4% of FY26 sales), pays royalty/trademark (up ~INR 60 million QoQ) and a transfer-pricing margin on services, and SKF India job-works for it until the new plant starts. “We are , till that new plant comes up , comes about, we are continuing to do some our SKF India entity is continuing to manufacture some for us on a job work basis.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=1289a753-236a-4201-9367-4432f4270674.pdf)* — The one-off separation charges continued into Q4 FY26 at INR 183 million, so reported PBT of 9.5% was 11.5% adjusted (versus 13.1% adjusted in Q3), with the remaining gap blamed on OEM mix (OEM up from 46% to 50%) and full bonus accrual. “In this quarter, we again had demerger -related IT costs, primarily that, totalling up to INR 183 million.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=1289a753-236a-4201-9367-4432f4270674.pdf)* — Margin roadmap post-separation: back to ~13% once demerger costs end around end-CY2026, ~15% by FY29-30 through localization, operational efficiency and S&A leverage, with 16-18% only an aspiration held back by OEM mix, competition and depreciation from the new plant. “So given the recent demerger expenses, right, by we would say towards the end of this calendar year, we see that mostly normalizing. We should get back to a little more around 13%.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=1289a753-236a-4201-9367-4432f4270674.pdf)* — Standalone capital plan: INR 800 crore+ capex FY26-27 to FY29-30, a large part for the new Pune plant plus DGBB and TRB channel additions (the INR 350-400 crore earlier flagged), operational mid-2028 and fully ramped by end-CY2028, with growth of ~8% in the interim. “So, on capex, the overall plan for the between FY 26, FY27 to FY 29, FY30, we are looking at doing a capex spend of around INR 800 crores plus, which includes a significant chunk of investment on the new Pune plant which we are in the process of setting up.”

## TMCV — Tata Motors Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (this company IS the resulting company of a demerger, listed on 2025-11-12 — the spun entity in its first year) · **LISTED <1Y — selling-pressure window; the bargain forms here** · score 5.0/10 · spin-off · 29 filing(s) from NSE, NSE-deep · first 2025-12-01, latest 2026-11-07

> **Listing:** THIS COMPANY IS THE SPIN-OFF — the resulting company of the parent's demerger, listed on 2025-11-12 (361 days ago)

**The stages, as filed:** listed (2025-11-12)

**Stated in the filings:** demerged undertaking: ) to the Company on a going; appointed date 2025-07-01.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Tata Motors' commercial vehicle business (trucks, buses, pick-ups, vans), demerged into TML Commercial Vehicles Limited, now renamed Tata Motors Limited — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* Promoter stake not stated. Under the Tata Motors Limited Share-based Long Term Incentive Scheme (Board-approved March 11, 2026), participants' outstanding Demerged Company PSUs convert into up to 23,07,647 new-company PSUs at Rs. 2, 0.062% dilution.
- *What it reveals:* A high-quality pure-play CV business: FY26 revenue ~Rs. 77,000 crores, EBITDA margin 13.2% (vs 7.8% in FY23), first double-digit EBIT at 11%, FCF Rs. 9,200 crores (12% of revenue), Auto ROCE 72%, net cash Rs. 7,500 crores standalone.
- *Selling pressure:* unclear — Documents state only that shares listed on BSE and NSE effective 12 November 2025; no index, float or shareholder-disposition detail given.
- *Parent or spin:* spin · *option pricing date:* March 11, 2026 (Board approved TML SLTI Scheme; Exercise Price Rs. 2 per PSU, face value)
- *Read next:* Q1 FY27 results: commodity pass-through after the April 2% price increase, and the Iveco bridge-loan refinancing equity/debt mix.
- *In their words:* “Demerger being effective from 1st of October 2025, Tata Motors is now a pure play commercial vehicle company, and this is a defining shift that changes how we think is most appropriate to present our financials.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Management presents the separation as a Composite Scheme of Arrangement under Sections 230–232, sanctioned by the NCLT Mumbai Bench amongst Tata Motors Limited (the demerged company, now Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited), TML Commercial Vehicles Limited (the resulting company) and Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited (amalgamated into the demerged entity), effective 1 October 2025; the resulting company was renamed Tata Motors Limited on 29 October 2025 and its shares listed on BSE/NSE (ticker TMCV) on 12 November 2025, with outstanding PSUs replaced one-for-one under a new scheme covering up to 23,07,647 shares (0.062% dilution). The stated problem the split solves is a reporting and identity one: 'Historically, we reported a CV segment. It was an internal construct that carved out CV operations from within the erstwhile combined entity. That was a practical necessity then' — from Q4 FY26 the company reports standalone financials including the Tata Cummins joint operation as its primary lens, giving 'a cleaner, more complete, and more directly comparable picture'. The separation cost ₹960 crore of one-time demerger expense booked in Q3 FY26 (part of ₹1,500 crore standalone / ₹1,600 crore consolidated exceptionals, alongside ₹603 crore of new labour code and ₹82 crore of Iveco acquisition cost). The pure-play case is argued with numbers: FY26 revenue ₹77,000 crore (vs ₹66,000 crore FY23), EBITDA margin up from 7.8% (FY23) to 13.2% (FY26) — ~550bps of 'structural improvement' — EBITDA doubled from ₹5,100 crore to ₹10,200 crore, PBT before exceptionals ₹8,700 crore, first-ever double-digit EBIT at 11% (the CV segment first crossed it at 10.6% in Q3 FY26), FCF ₹9,200 crore or 12% of revenue, Auto ROCE 72%, cash conversion cycle of negative 31 days, net cash ₹7,500 crore standalone and ₹13,700 crore consolidated, and a maiden final dividend of ₹4/share (~₹1,500 crore outflow). Cyclicality is the second problem: non-cyclical revenue (parts & service, Fleet Edge digital subscriptions, Smart City e-bus operations) is compounding at 2.7x the cyclical CAGR, 'deliberately building this mix', and Q4 working-capital sinks historically concentrated in Q4 have been spread through the year. Third, the standalone CV entity became the acquisition vehicle: its own balance sheet and a committed EUR 3.825 billion bridge from Morgan Stanley and MUFG funded an all-cash voluntary totalitarian tender offer for Iveco Group N.V. at EUR 14.10 (raised to EUR 14.40), valuing Iveco at ~EUR 3.82 billion, creating ~EUR 21 billion (INR 2,28,000 crore+) of combined revenue and ~590k units with Europe ~46%/India ~32%/South America ~8%/RoW ~14% and 'substantially no overlap' — expected to 'drive better operating leverage by spreading its capital investments over larger volumes, generating operating efficiencies and reducing the cash flow volatility inherent in the commercial vehicles sector', plus enhancing Iveco's FPT powertrain business. Structural simplification continues inside the CV entity: TMF Holdings Limited and TMF Business Services Limited (wholly owned subsidiaries) are being amalgamated into it, and Tata Motor Finance had already been folded into Tata Capital (whose October 2025 IPO priced 20–25% below the merger valuation, forcing a ₹2,000 crore mark-to-market loss in Q2 FY26 and a ₹295 crore write-back in Q3).

**How it evolved:** In the Nov 2025 call (Q2 FY26, 13 November 2025) management reported the split as done rather than argued for it — demerger effective 1 October, CV listing completed as TMCV 'as committed previously', Iveco approvals underway and the bridge loan secured. In the Feb 2026 call (Q3 FY26, 29 January 2026) the cost showed up as a ₹960 crore one-time demerger exceptional while the CV segment hit a double-digit EBIT margin (10.6%) for the first time and Iveco approvals were guided to end-March. In the May 2026 call (Q4 FY26, 13 May 2026) the framing shifted decisively: 'Tata Motors is now a pure play commercial vehicle company... a defining shift', the old carved-out CV segment was retired in favour of standalone reporting, three-year pure-play metrics were laid out, and Iveco closure slipped to Q2 FY27 pending French and Spanish financial-regulator approvals. Filings then show execution: offer launched 4 September 2026, 89.42% tendered by 27 October 2026, 96.29% after the reopening on 6 November 2026, triggering the Dutch legal squeeze-out, alongside the TMF Holdings/TMF Business Services amalgamation notices.

**What management expects from it:** Pure-play CV: cleaner, comparable standalone reporting including Tata Cummins joint operations; teens (not mid-teens) EBITDA guidance, double-digit EBIT, capex 2–4% of revenue, FCF ~12% of revenue, 72% ROCE, net cash ₹7,500cr standalone/₹13,700cr consolidated funding a ₹4 dividend and the Iveco bid; with Iveco, ~EUR21bn revenue, operating leverage over larger volumes, less cash-flow volatility. No PV-entity commentary.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *CALL Nov 2025* — First call of the separated entity: management confirmed the demerger took effect 1 October 2025 and that the CV business was listed as Tata Motors Limited under ticker TMCV on both exchanges, describing it as a commitment delivered. “We successfully completed the demerger with Effective date of 1st October.”
- *CALL Nov 2025* — Comparatives had to be derived because the resulting company only came into existence in June 2024 — a direct consequence of the scheme structure. “the prior period financials in this presentation, they reflect the impact of the demerger as it has just been effective since the Company’s incorporation that happened in June 2024.”
- *CALL Nov 2025* — The newly separated CV entity immediately tied up its own acquisition financing for Iveco through a bridge loan, with refinancing options (equity or debt) left open. “On the Iveco acquisition, the regulatory approvals are underway and the initial funding through bridge loan has been secured.”
- *CALL Feb 2026* — The separation carried an explicit one-time cost of ₹960 crore, booked as an exceptional item in Q3 FY26 within ₹1,500 crore of standalone exceptionals (with ₹603 crore labour code and ₹82 crore Iveco acquisition cost). “Demerger cost has been around ₹960 crore.”
- *CALL Feb 2026* — Management flagged the demerger and labour-code charges as non-recurring, separating transaction cost from underlying performance. “And both these are going to be one-time for us. We don't expect this on a recurring basis.”
- *CALL Feb 2026* — The CV business crossed a double-digit EBIT margin for the first time as a standalone reporting unit — the profitability milestone used to validate the standalone case. “The CV segment also achieved the milestone of a double-digit EBIT margin for the first time, which now stands at 10.6%.”
- *CALL May 2026* — The clearest statement of what the separation achieved: a pure-play commercial vehicle company, which management calls a defining shift that changes how the business should be presented. “Demerger being effective from 1st of October 2025, Tata Motors is now a pure play commercial vehicle company, and this is a defining shift that changes how we think is most appropriate to present our financials.”
- *CALL May 2026* — The problem the split solves, as stated: the CV business was previously visible only as an internal carve-out construct inside the combined entity. “Historically, we reported a CV segment. It was an internal construct that carved out CV operations from within the erstwhile combined entity. That was a practical necessity then.”
- *CALL May 2026* — Post-demerger reporting switched to standalone financials including the Tata Cummins joint operation as the primary lens, for transparency and comparability. “This gives you a cleaner, more complete, and more directly comparable picture of the business going forward.”
- *CALL May 2026* — The margin record cited as structural rather than cyclical: 7.8% to 13.2% EBITDA over three years, with EBITDA doubling from ₹5,100 crore to ₹10,200 crore and FY26 EBIT at 11%. “EBITDA margins have expanded from 7.8% in FY23 to 13.2% in FY26. That's nearly 550 bps of structural improvement over three years.”
- *CALL May 2026* — Capital-efficiency case for the standalone entity: ₹9,200 crore FCF (12% of revenue), ₹2,800 crore reinvested, Auto ROCE of 72%, negative 31-day cash conversion cycle, net cash ₹7,500 crore standalone and ₹13,700 crore consolidated. “Finally, the Auto ROCE stands at 72% is an industry-leading number, when EBIT doubles, capital discipline holds, returns follow.”
- *CALL May 2026* — Deliberate de-cyclicalisation of the standalone business via parts & service, Fleet Edge digital and Smart City e-buses, growing far faster than the cyclical truck business. “Over the period, non-cyclical CAGR is running at 2.7x the cyclical CAGR. We've been deliberately building this mix, and this is now showing up meaningfully in the numbers.”

*Not explained on the calls:* Why separate at all — no pre-demerger call is in the record: no stated valuation-unlock, synergy or capital-allocation rationale, no investor, lender or partner named as requesting it, no entitlement ratio.

## INDIAGLYCO — India Glycols Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **LISTED <1Y — selling-pressure window; the bargain forms here** · score 4.3/10 · spin-off · 42 filing(s) from BSE-screener, CALLS, NSE, NSE-register · first 2025-11-14, latest 2026-11-02

> **Listing:** LISTED — Ennature Bio Pharma Limited trades since about 2026-08-20 (record date 2026-08-20)

**The stages, as filed:** exchange_noc (2025-11-20) → meetings (2026-03-24) → nclt_sanction (2026-01-16) → effective (2026-10-06) → record_date (2026-08-21) → listed (2026-11-02)

**Stated in the filings:** resulting company **Ennature Bio Pharma Limited**; demerged undertaking: s from the Demerged; entitlement **1 for every 3**; record date 2026-08-20; appointed date 2026-04-01.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** The Bio Pharma (Biopharma) Undertaking — bio-pharma and bio-polymers businesses, plant-based APIs, nutraceuticals and nicotine derivatives — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* Promoter family controls it: Pragya Bhartia Barwale Managing Director 5 years (ran the division to Rs 200 crore revenue); father U.S. Bhartia and sister Pooja Jhaver non-executive directors; promoters held 3,99,67,854 of 6,70,26,765 IGL shares, voted 100% in favour.
- *What it reveals:* Tax cost apportionment assigns Ennature 20.61% of value on only ~2% of group revenue (FY26 segment revenue Rs 207.77 crore, EBIT Rs 7.23 crore, 3.5%, down from 20.76 crore EBIT in FY25), with segment assets Rs 426.42 crore versus liabilities Rs 92.49 crore — a depressed-margin, asset-heavy business management says is being rebuilt into branded nutraceuticals.
- *Selling pressure:* likely — Smallest of three entities, only 2,23,42,255 shares on a 1-for-3 ratio creating odd lots; pharma/nutraceuticals unrelated to chemicals or spirits holders bought.
- *Parent or spin:* spin · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Ennature Bio Pharma's Information Memorandum (board-approved 8 September 2026) — standalone balance sheet, debt allocation and segment margin trend.
- *In their words:* “Ennature Bio Pharma Limited will house the bio-pharma and bio-polymers businesses.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Management presented the separation as a focus-and-investor-base argument, not a rescue: India Glycols was running four structurally different businesses under one listing — Bio-based Specialties & Performance Chemicals (BSPC, including the 49% Clariant IGL Specialty Chemicals JV into which IGL sells ethylene oxide), Potable Spirits (country liquor/IMIL plus IMFL, with the Amrut and Bacardi tie-ups), Bio-Fuel/ethanol-ENA sold at government-administered prices to OMCs, and Ennature Biopharma (thiocolchicoside, nicotine, nutraceuticals) with biopolymers. On 4 February 2025 the board approved splitting these into India Glycols (chemicals, glycols, bio-glycols, new specialties, industrial gases, plus the Clariant JV), IGL Spirits (spirits + bio-fuel/ENA) and Ennature Bio Pharma (biopharma + biopolymers), all three to be listed via the NCLT route. CEO Rupark Sarswat said the purpose was to run the companies differently with much more focus and to allow potential investments in different businesses because different investors have different appetites; CFO Anand Singhal listed the benefits as independent growth for each business, reducing the risk of one business affecting the others, unlocking value by drawing focused investors, and clearer focus leading to improved management and resource allocation — while insisting the structure would not unduly increase the cost base. Scale was quantified with 9MFY25 numbers: chemicals Rs 1,079 cr at 13.6% EBITDA margin, IGL Spirits Rs 1,628 cr net at 14.4%, Ennature Bio Pharma Rs 178 cr at 14.9% (against FY24 BSPC Rs 1,626 cr, Bio-Fuel Rs 512 cr, Potable Spirits Rs 5,575 cr gross). Capital allocation was the hard constraint: big capex was frozen until after the demerger, long-term debt was pre-allocated with the SBI-led consortium (about Rs 500 cr chemicals / Rs 700 cr liquor out of Rs 1,200 cr in May 2025, restated to Rs 600 cr / Rs 800 cr out of about Rs 1,400 cr in November 2025), the Rs 467 cr preferential allotment at Rs 915/share in November 2025 went entirely into prepaying debt, and the credit rating was parked on watch-list with no upgrade possible until the demerger completed. Management simultaneously defended keeping bio-fuel with spirits rather than with chemicals, arguing captive multi-feedstock ethanol/ENA gives backward integration, quality control, scale and resilience even if it dilutes percentage margin, and that plant proximity and the EO-to-JV link preserve synergies. By FY26 the residual chemicals business was pitched as under-earning for want of focus and in-house cost streamlining, with the contracted sale of a further 24% of the Clariant JV in FY29 expected to make the chemicals entity debt-free. The scheme was sanctioned by NCLT Allahabad on 17 July 2026, became effective 1 September 2026 (appointed date 1 April 2026), with IGL Spirits and Ennature Bio Pharma listing and trading from 2–4 November 2026.

**How it evolved:** First disclosed on the 6 February 2025 call as a composite scheme that also folded promoter holding company Kashipur Holdings into IGL so promoters would hold IGL directly; by the 21 May 2025 call it was accompanied by a Rs 500 cr/Rs 700 cr debt split, and the board on 16 May 2025 dropped the KHL amalgamation to pursue the demerger alone. The 11 August 2025 and 18 November 2025 calls hardened the mechanics — three named entities, capex deferred to the post-demerger companies, debt restated to Rs 600 cr/Rs 800 cr, and a Rs 467 cr promoter-and-associates preferential issue to cut debt — while an investor on the August call openly questioned demerging a unit in degrowth. The 12 February 2026 call added that the credit rating would stay on watch-list and no sizeable capex would be sanctioned until completion, and the 18 May 2026 call was spent waiting on the NCLT hearing of 21 May. Shareholders (4,42,48,625 of 4,42,48,626 votes) and unsecured creditors (100% by value) approved on 24 March 2026; NCLT sanctioned on 17 July 2026, effective 1 September 2026, record date 2 September 2026, with trading in both new entities from 4 November 2026.

**What management expects from it:** Chemicals: cost streamlining, higher-value performance chemicals, improving EBIT (11.7% FY26), JV stake sale funding a debt-free unit by FY29. IGL Spirits: premiumisation toward ~22% EBIT margins on captive ENA, geographic and CSD expansion. Ennature: branded nutraceuticals margin recovery. All three: dedicated focus, own capital allocation, focused investors, value unlock.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *CALL Feb 2025* — Rupark Sarswat first unveiled the three-way restructuring, initially to sit inside the IGL group before listing. “So, essentially what we are trying to do is to restructure these businesses into three separate companies, for the time being within the IGL group.”
- *CALL Feb 2025* — The core stated reason: different businesses need different strategies and attract different pools of capital. “And also, to allow potential investments in different businesses because different investors tend to have a different focus for investments.”
- *CALL Feb 2025* — CFO Anand Singhal framed one benefit as ring-fencing contagion between segments (relevant given Ennature's margin collapse and the chemicals/EO price squeeze). “Separating the business will reduce the risk of one business affecting the others.”
- *CALL Feb 2025* — Anand gave the pro-forma 9MFY25 size and margins of each proposed entity — chemicals Rs 1,079 cr at 13.6%, spirits+biofuel Rs 1,628 cr at 14.4%, Ennature Rs 178 cr at 14.9%. “IGL Spirits, which is proposed to be the other Company which will be having the Liquor business and the Bio-Fuel business, is having 9MFY25 turnover of Rs. 1,628, this is on net basis with 14.4% EBITDA margin.”
- *CALL Feb 2025* — Anand confirmed the NCLT route, a 12-15 month timetable, 1 April 2026 appointed date and listing of all three entities. “So, this demerger will be effective from 1st April, 26 and all the three companies will be listed on the stock exchange.”
- *CALL Feb 2025* — Investors pushed on listing of the biggest piece, noting over 75% of the business would sit in IGL Spirits. “Sir, my first question regarding post restructuring, more than 75% of business comes from IGL Spirits. Is there any plan to list that entity?”
- *CALL Feb 2025* — Lender involvement: working capital and term loan allocation across the three companies had to be negotiated with the SBI-led consortium and was not yet confirmed. “Rohit, regarding the working capital allocation to each Company and the term loan allocation, we are talking to the term lender, mainly the State Bank of India, who is the leader in our consortium banking.”
- *CALL Feb 2025* — Rupark stressed the split must not create duplicate overheads; corporate resources would stay shared with an allocation mechanism. “The principle of demerger to start with is to continue to run the businesses under one umbrella, but differently as in separately from a strategic perspective, but not unduly increasing the cost base.”
- *CALL Feb 2025* — Asked by Saket Kapoor whether clubbing government-priced bio-fuel with liquor would dilute the IMFL valuation, Rupark defended it as backward integration, quality control and scale. “Well, percentage margin is one factor, but the overall profitability and resilience of the business also improves.”
- *CALL May 2025* — First debt allocation disclosed: Rs 1,200 cr long-term debt split roughly Rs 500 cr to chemicals and Rs 700 cr to liquor, with annual repayments of Rs 150-160 cr (spirits) and Rs 90 cr (chemicals). “Just to brief you as of now position, we are having about INR 1,200 crores long-term debt in the books of the company, out of which about INR 500 crores will go to the Chemical division and INR 700 crores will go to the liquor division.”
- *CALL Aug 2025* — Rupark restated the rationale and the exact clustering — spirits with ethanol/bio-fuel into IGL Spirits, chemicals with the Clariant JV, Ennature with biopolymers. “The idea is that different investors have different appetites for different kind of businesses.”
- *CALL Aug 2025* — Growth capex was explicitly deferred to the post-demerger entities; FY26 limited to rollover and Rs 40-50 cr maintenance capex. “And after the demerger, the separate companies will think over the CapEx.”

*Not explained on the calls:* Never quantified: value unlock, standalone corporate costs, inter-company ENA/EO transfer pricing, shared Kashipur utilities, debt-covenant consents; no investor, lender or partner was named as having requested it.
