## INOXGREEN — Inox Green Energy Services Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **LISTED <1Y — selling-pressure window; the bargain forms here** · score 4.3/10 · spin-off · 21 filing(s) from CALLS, NSE, NSE-register · first 2026-03-14, latest 2026-08-24

> **Listing:** LISTED — Inox Renewable Solutions Limited trades since about 2026-08-01 (record date 2026-08-01)

**The stages, as filed:** nclt_sanction (2026-03-14) → effective (2026-05-04) → record_date (2026-07-22)

**Stated in the filings:** resulting company **Inox Renewable Solutions Limited**; demerged undertaking: ) of Inox Green Energy Services; entitlement **122 for every 2,000**; record date 2026-08-01.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Power Evacuation Business (substation/evacuation infrastructure) demerged from Inox Green into Inox Renewable Solutions Limited — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* Inox Wind Limited, promoter/holding company, directly holds 51.13% of Inox Green and receives mirror IRSL shares; directors/KMP hold only token stakes (Bindu Saxena 12,640; Sanjeev Jain 3,362). No separate incentive disclosed.
- *What it reveals:* Demerger strips ~Rs 1,000 crore gross block and Rs 50-55 crore annual depreciation from Inox Green, lifting profit, ROE/ROCE; parent keeps ~50%-margin O&M with Rs 700 crore tax shield. IRSL carries listed NCDs, secured/unsecured debt and a Rs 96.80 crore tax demand.
- *Selling pressure:* likely — Only 122 IRSL shares per 1,000 held: tiny 4,89,82,030-share float, newly listed EPC/evacuation business in a different line from O&M
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* IRSL listing/trading approval and its balance sheet: Rs 96.80 crore AY2023-24 tax demand, secured/unsecured debt, accumulated losses
- *In their words:* “122 equity shares of IRSL (face value Rs. 10/- each) shall be issued for every 1,000 equity shares (face value Rs. 10/- each) held in Inox Green Energy Services Limited.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The business being separated is Inox Green's Power Evacuation / substation business — the commissioned substations, 33kV and EHV transmission lines and common evacuation infrastructure sitting on IGESL's balance sheet — which is being demerged out of Inox Green Energy Services Ltd (the wind/solar O&M arm) and merged into Inox Renewable Solutions Ltd (IRSL, formerly Resco Global Wind Services, the group's EPC arm and a subsidiary of parent Inox Wind), with Appointed Date 1 October 2024. Management's core argument is that these assets are not needed to run O&M at all — they exist to deliver turnkey/EPC solutions — so they only inflate IGESL's balance sheet and depress its returns: Inox Green was described as merely the 'trustee' of substations customers had already paid for, and the asset block was explained as a legacy of IGESL having once housed both the EPC and O&M businesses, where the pre-IPO slump sale of EPC to Resco could not carry over already-commissioned infra because that would have required consent from over 200 customers who would have reopened O&M contracts — hence the NCLT scheme route. The quantified benefit moved from a net block of ~INR750 crore (Aug 2024) to a gross block of ~INR1,000 crore leaving the books, with annual depreciation of ~INR50–55 crore eliminated (quarterly depreciation had been running INR13–17 crore, i.e. ~INR12 crore added to quarterly PAT), against only a token revenue loss — first put at INR4–5 crore a year, then INR3–4 crore a quarter, and finally ~INR10 crore. With no depreciation, virtually nil finance cost and ~INR700 crore of carried-forward tax losses that stay at company level (losses attach to the company, not the asset), management says EBITDA converts to PBT, PAT and cash profit, so the ~INR600 crore FY27 EBITDA guidance is effectively all operating cash, and ROE/ROCE improve 'significantly'. The scheme's own rationale adds that O&M and Power Evacuation have separate and distinct risk, reward, financial profile, competition and opportunity sets, that evacuation infra can attract a different investor/partner/lender base, that consolidating the same line of business into IRSL unlocks value and focus, and that the outcome is two listed entities — a pure-play O&M company and an EPC/evacuation company — each free to pursue its own strategy. Consideration is paid in IRSL shares to IGESL shareholders (122 IRSL shares per 1,000 IGESL shares; management earlier framed it as IGESL shareholders owning ~20% of Resco, 10% minority and 10% promoters), with IRSL automatically listing — which management (Devansh Jain, Sanjeev Agarwal) says 'unlocks substantial value' for both Inox Wind and Inox Green and gives a shareholder the choice of holding the O&M business, the infrastructure business, or the whole value chain via Inox Wind. No lender or counterparty demand was cited; secured creditors, unsecured creditors, warrant and debenture holders and shareholders all approved the scheme unanimously or with requisite majority, and analysts/retail holders (Hansal Thakkar on rationalising subsidiaries, Pradyumna Choudhary and Pradeep Motwani on timelines and value unlocking for minority shareholders) pushed management on it rather than originating it.

**How it evolved:** The idea first surfaced as a board action on the 9 Aug 2024 call (Q1 FY25), where consultants and registered valuers had been appointed to evaluate demerging the power evacuation business for a 'cleaner and asset light balance sheet', and Devansh Jain explained on that same call why the infra could not be moved at the pre-IPO EPC slump sale (200+ customer consents); by the 25 Oct 2024 call (tagged Nov 2024) valuation was underway with a quantified ~INR12 crore quarterly PAT uplift and IGESL shareholders to receive Resco shares, and the board approved the scheme on 13 Nov 2024 with Appointed Date 1 Oct 2024. On 31 Jan 2025 (Feb 2025 tag) Akhil Jindal promised an 'asset-light balance sheet' with no depreciation 'next year', ~20% of Resco to IGESL shareholders and confirmation that the ~INR700 crore tax losses stay with IGESL; by 1 Sep 2025 exchange no-objections were in and the scheme was filed at NCLT Ahmedabad with the figure firmed up at ~INR1,000 crore gross block and INR50–55 crore depreciation plus ROE/ROCE gains, and on 14 Nov 2025 shareholder and creditor approvals were announced. The 13 Feb 2026 call put it in 'final stages of hearing' with only ~INR10 crore of revenue leaving, and the 29 May 2026 call confirmed NCLT approval (order 13 Mar 2026); filings then show the scheme effective 4 May 2026, record date 1 Aug 2026 and 4,89,82,030 IRSL shares allotted on 24 Aug 2026 — with the only real change in plan being management's Sep 2025 rejection of any further demerger of IGESL/IRSL out of Inox Wind itself.

**What management expects from it:** Inox Green: pure-play, asset-light, zero-capex O&M annuity — ~INR1,000 crore gross block and INR50–55 crore depreciation gone, only ~INR10 crore revenue lost, ~50% EBITDA margins converting to PBT/PAT/cash via a INR700 crore tax shield, FY27 EBITDA upwards of INR600 crore nearly all cash, materially better ROE/ROCE. IRSL: consolidated EPC/evacuation platform, separately listed, its own investors and lenders, value unlocked for Inox Wind and Inox Green holders.

- *[Aug 2024](https://inoxgreen.com/PDF/MOSL-InoxGreenEnergy-Aug09-2024_IGESL.pdf)* — The board formally started the process by appointing consultants and registered valuers, with the stated purpose of a cleaner, asset-light balance sheet and depreciation elimination. “Demerger of power infrastructure facilities currently on the balance sheet of Inox Green will result in a cleaner and asset light balance sheet.”
- *[Aug 2024](https://inoxgreen.com/PDF/MOSL-InoxGreenEnergy-Aug09-2024_IGESL.pdf)* — Devansh Jain gave the historical reason the assets were stranded at IGESL: moving commissioned substations at the pre-IPO EPC slump sale would have needed consent from over 200 customers who would have renegotiated O&M contracts. “We could not shunt it out from this balance sheet into Resco because that would have entailed taking approval from over 200 customers and then arm twisting us in terms of renegotiating contracts and screwing the entire O&M business.”
- *[Aug 2024](https://inoxgreen.com/PDF/MOSL-InoxGreenEnergy-Aug09-2024_IGESL.pdf)* — He characterised IGESL as only the trustee of substations customers had already paid for, so the balance sheet was inflated for no economic reason; net block then put at ~INR750 crore and the model described as zero-capex annuity. “Inox Green's balance sheet is unnecessarily inflated thanks to these historical substations which are lying on its balance sheet of which we are actually the trustee.”
- *[Nov 2024](https://www.inoxgreen.com/PDF/MOSL-InoxGreenEnergy-Oct25-2024.pdf)* — First quantification of the trade-off: only ~INR3–4 crore of quarterly revenue exits while the entire depreciation goes, adding ~INR12 crore to quarterly PAT; consideration to IGESL holders is Resco shares. “Excluding the substation business , the revenue would be down by around Rs. 3 crores or Rs. 4 crores on a quarterly basis , and the whole depreciation will go away. So, broadly that will add around Rs. 12-odd crore in the bottom line on a quarterly basis.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=a6149a06-42db-4b82-ae77-0dc15e5abe49.pdf)* — Akhil Jindal set the end-state: an asset-light balance sheet with no depreciation as a continuing item, so EBITDA becomes the benchmark for PAT; Mathusudhana added IGESL shareholders would own ~20% of Resco (10% minority, 10% promoters). “So when you're looking into the next year's balance sheet of Inox Green, it would be an asset - light balance sheet. And it would also have no depreciation charges as a continued item.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=a6149a06-42db-4b82-ae77-0dc15e5abe49.pdf)* — Confirmed the ~INR700 crore of accumulated tax losses are not stripped out with the assets, because losses sit at company level — key to EBITDA converting to cash PAT. “So the tax losses would be on a company level, not on an asset level. So the tax losses will remain in this company.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=a6149a06-42db-4b82-ae77-0dc15e5abe49.pdf)* — Answering whether depreciation simply becomes opex, management argued the evacuation and common infrastructure is irrelevant to O&M delivery and belongs with the turnkey/EPC business. “So as far as the power evacuation and the common infrastructure, we have developed is not required for O&M services per se. That is required for further providing a turnkey solution to the customers.”
- *[Sep 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ac349021-05a3-4a4e-84a8-edb5f23d90bd.pdf)* — With exchange no-objections received and the scheme filed at NCLT Ahmedabad, the benefit was firmed up at ~INR1,000 crore gross block off the books, INR50–55 crore of annual depreciation eliminated and higher ROE/ROCE. “Once the scheme is approved by the NCLT, the gross block of around INR1,000 crore will be off our balance sheet and subsequently the depreciation of approximately INR50 crores to INR55 crores annually will be eliminated , thereby increasing the PBT by that amount.”
- *[Sep 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ac349021-05a3-4a4e-84a8-edb5f23d90bd.pdf)* — Asked by a shareholder whether IGESL and IRSL would be demerged out of Inox Wind to IWL holders, management refused — the only separation intended was the infra assets into Resco, which then lists, giving holders a choice of exposure. “And I think from a shareholder's perspective, a shareholder has got now a choice to hold any part of the business. He can hold the O&M business, he can hold the infrastructure business, he can hold the entire value chain together under Inox Wind.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=12a9f200-8091-44c1-a30e-eb06b0e51134.pdf)* — Shareholder and creditor approvals obtained; the benefit framed as two-sided — IRSL listing as Inox Wind's EPC arm, and depreciation elimination at Inox Green. “This will add value for both Inox Wind, with subsequent listing of Inox Renewable solution as an EPC arm of Inox Wind, and Inox Green with elimination of depreciation on demergers of the asset blocks”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=12a9f200-8091-44c1-a30e-eb06b0e51134.pdf)* — Devansh Jain put the value-unlocking claim explicitly on the demerger plus subsequent listing of IRSL. “I believe that the de -merger and subsequent listing of Inox Renewable Solutions will unlock substantial value for both Inox Wind and Inox Green.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No IRSL pro-forma revenue/EBITDA (declined), no economics of the transferred block, how evacuation charges re-route, stamp-duty/tax cost, IRSL listing date, dividend policy; revenue-loss figures drifted inconsistently.

## PICCADIL — Piccadily Agro Industries Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 4.3/10 · spin-off · 6 filing(s) from CALLS, NSE · first 2026-04-28, latest 2026-08-17

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'exchange_noc' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; indicated timeline: Press release and earnings call (28–29 April 2026): demerger scheme filed with SEBI, "expects completion by the end of FY27"; NSE observation letter (14 August 2026): listing/trading must commence "within sixty days of receipt of the order of the Hon'ble High Court/NCLT"; shares frozen in depositories till trading permission.

**The stages, as filed:** exchange_noc (2026-08-17)

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** The Sugar Business — white crystal sugar, allied and food products — demerged into wholly owned Piccadily Food & Essentials Limited — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* Not stated as a percentage; shareholding proportionate — no change in PAIL's pattern; PFEL's pre-scheme capital cancelled, no consideration. Promoter converted 6,36,942 warrants into PAIL shares, listed November 2025.
- *What it reveals:* Parent becomes pure-play alco-bev: FY26 distillery segment result Rs 23,658.72 lakhs vs sugar's Rs 494.79 lakhs on 20.53% of turnover; sugar segment liabilities Rs 22,166.79 lakhs exceed its assets Rs 10,553.97 lakhs, so leverage leaves with the stub.
- *Selling pressure:* likely — Entitlement is only 1 PFEL share per 9 PAIL shares; sugar is a different, seasonal industry premium-spirits holders did not buy.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Scheme explanatory statement: value of assets and liabilities transferred to PFEL, plus PFEL's abridged prospectus/Information Memorandum.
- *In their words:* “The effectiveness of the Scheme would result in the creation of two listed companies with proportionate shareholding with the Resulting Company housing the Sugar Business and the Company housing the Distillery Business.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Management is demerging the Sugar Business of Piccadily Agro Industries Ltd. (PAIL) into Piccadily Food & Essentials Limited (PFEL), a wholly owned subsidiary, so that PAIL becomes a pure-play premium alco-bev company; CFO Natwar Aggarwal framed it on the April 29, 2026 call as "we want to be a global alco-bev company and in that pursuit we want to focus on our core brand portfolio," with the scheme Board-approved April 28, 2026, filed with SEBI, KPMG as adviser, and completion envisaged in FY27. The stated intent is to pool human and capital resources behind the Alco-Bev portfolio (Indri single malt, Camikara rum, Cashmir vodka, Whistler blended whisky) and to list sugar — described as a "traditional heritage business" — as a separate entity rather than sell it. The economics behind it are visible in the numbers management cited: Alco-Bev revenue grew 42% to INR 908 crore (from INR 639 crore) with 31.5% EBITDA margins and 45–50% IMFL margins, while sugar was only INR 233.05 crore of turnover (20.53% of the listed entity) and dragged Q4 standalone EBITDA margin down ~300 bps as sugar's quarterly EBITDA margin collapsed from 11% to 2%; the segment tables show the sugar segment result at a loss of INR 904.62 lakh in FY26 versus a loss of INR 327.13 lakh in FY25, with sugar segment assets of INR 10,553.97 lakh against segment liabilities of INR 22,166.79 lakh. Management also repeatedly blamed sugar seasonality for making quarter-to-quarter margins hard to read. The scheme's own rationale (Annexure B) lists focused attention for each core business and the ability to attract required investment, greater business focus and enhanced shareholder value, more efficient use of financial resources, managerial talent, technical skills and marketing resources, value unlock "through price-discovery of the individual entities," the "right operating architecture" with sharper individual strategies and "clear capital allocation," and separately listed companies attracting a specific set of investors with financial flexibility and "stronger capital market outcomes." Mechanically it is a mirror listing: no cash consideration, 1 PFEL share of INR 10 for every 9 PAIL shares (ratio fixed on sugar's turnover and assets), PFEL's pre-scheme capital cancelled, no change in PAIL's shareholding pattern, producing "two listed companies with proportionate shareholding." No investor, lender or business partner is identified anywhere as having demanded the separation — it is presented as a management/Board decision, recommended by the Audit Committee and Independent Directors, alongside the unrelated FY27 agenda of INR 250–300 crore incremental Indri revenue, INR 300–400 crore from the 200 KLPD Chhattisgarh plant, 60–70% growth and brand-side inorganic options.

**How it evolved:** Only one earnings call falls in the window, the FY26 call of April 29, 2026, and the demerger appears there already as a done decision rather than an idea being floated — announced in the CFO's opening remarks the day after the April 28, 2026 Board meeting approved the scheme and filed it with the exchanges/SEBI, with KPMG as partner and FY27 as the completion target. It resurfaced later in the same call only when Himanshu Shah of Dolat Capital pressed on intent (sell or separately list), drawing the explicit answer that sugar would be listed separately, not sold. The filings then track execution rather than rationale: the April 28, 2026 Regulation 30 outcome with the full Annexure B rationale, share entitlement ratio and sugar turnover of INR 233.05 crore (20.53%), the April 28, 2026 press release restating the pure-play framing, and the August 17, 2026 intimation of BSE/NSE no-adverse-observation letters dated August 14, 2026 (SEBI comments dated August 13, 2026) clearing the way for the NCLT petition. Earlier filings in the window (November–December 2025) concern only CCD and warrant conversions and never mention a separation.

**What management expects from it:** Alco-Bev PAIL becomes a pure-play premium spirits company: sharper focus, pooled human and capital resources, better capital allocation, and 31.5% alco-bev / 45–50% IMFL margins no longer diluted by seasonal sugar; 60–70% FY27 growth and 3–4x revenue in 3–4 years. Sugar, housed in PFEL, gets focused attention, its own investor set, price discovery, financial flexibility and ability to attract investment.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[May 2026](https://www.piccadily.com/themes/piccadily/pdfs/piccadily_transcript_earnings_call_dated_29_4_26.pdf)* — Timeline and process: scheme filed with SEBI, NCLT filing after SEBI go-ahead, completion envisaged within FY27. “Once we get go-ahead from SEBI, we will follow the due process of filing it to NCLT and we envisage to complete this process by FY '27 this year.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.piccadily.com/themes/piccadily/pdfs/piccadily_transcript_earnings_call_dated_29_4_26.pdf)* — Management restated the demerger purely as a focus measure alongside guidance of 60–70% FY27 growth and 3x–4x revenue in three to four years. “As mentioned earlier, we also in a process of demerger just to focus on the main Alco-Bev business.”

We want to pool our human and capital resources just for the Alco-Bev business.”

- *[May 2026](https://www.piccadily.com/themes/piccadily/pdfs/piccadily_transcript_earnings_call_dated_29_4_26.pdf)* — Management contrasted sugar's drag with Alco-Bev EBITDA margins of about 31.5% (and IMFL margins of 45–50%), which it expects to maintain or improve with premiumisation. “I would like to highlight one more point here that if you look at our Alco-Bev business EBITDA margins, which is in the range of, let's say, current year about 31.5%, which is one of the highest margin in any Alco-Bev competition.”

## THOMASCOOK — Thomas Cook (India) Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 4.3/10 · spin-off · 15 filing(s) from CALLS, NSE, NSE-BM · first 2026-03-20, latest 2026-11-05

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'nclt_sanction' stage; Sterling Holiday Resorts Limited will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; indicated timeline: On March 20, 2026 filings: "Shares of SHRL will be listed on BSE and NSE" and listing "is proposed" subject to approvals; NSE letter dated September 1, 2026 requires SHRL to complete listing and commence trading "within sixty days of receipt of the order of the NCLT"; on the May 13, 2026 call Debasis Nandy said it will take "12 to 15 months" and "We expect this process to get completed by Q1 of FY '28"

**The stages, as filed:** announced (2026-03-20) → exchange_noc (2026-09-01) → nclt_sanction (2026-11-05)

**Stated in the filings:** resulting company **Sterling Holiday Resorts Limited**; demerged undertaking: Resort Business of TCIL (Demerged Company) are transferred to Sterling Holiday Resorts.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** TCIL's resorts and resort management business (Nature Trails brand) demerged into Sterling Holiday Resorts Limited — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* Promoter Fairbridge Capital (Mauritius)/Fairfax holds 63.83% of TCIL; SHRL post-scheme promoters 65.55% (incl. 7% held by TCIL), ESOP Trust 2.16%, public 32.30%; 65,70,000 ESOP 2024 options accelerated
- *What it reveals:* Resort undertaking demerged is tiny — INR 70 crore turnover, ~0.4% of TCIL standalone revenue — but recipient SHRL is a 78-resort, ~3,800-room, debt-free hospitality platform with INR 5,487mn FY26 revenue, 31% EBITDA margin, INR 3,400mn cash, 25 straight profitable quarters
- *Selling pressure:* unclear — Documents state no change in TCIL shareholding pattern and similar promoter/public patterns post-demerger; no index or size discussion stated
- *Parent or spin:* spin · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Scheme explanatory statement: SHRL post-demerger balance sheet, valuation report and share entitlement basis
- *In their words:* “Accordingly, the Board of TCIL is of the view that for better focus and maximum result, it is better to divest the Resorts and Resort Management Business into SHRL and subsequently list SHRL.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Management presented this as a two-part move announced on 20 March 2026: TCIL demerges its own Resorts and Resort Management undertaking — the six resorts it owns/operates directly under the Nature Trails brand (adventure holidays, educational trips, corporate getaways), with turnover of only INR 70 crore for the year ended 31 December 2025, about 0.4% of TCIL's standalone turnover — into Sterling Holiday Resorts Limited (SHRL), its wholly owned hospitality subsidiary, which is then listed on BSE and NSE. The boards' first reason is capability fit: the resort business 'would reap more benefit from being owned and operated by SHRL in light of their vast expertise in the hospitality industry' (SHRL had 72+ resorts across 62 locations at announcement, 78 resorts/~3,800 rooms/65 destinations by FY26). The second is that SHRL has 'matured' and is 'well poised to chart its own growth path' as a separate listed entity — FY26 revenue INR 5,487mn, EBITDA INR 1,701mn (31% margin), PBT INR 1,142mn (21%), 25 consecutive profitable quarters, ~INR 3,400mn cash at a 55% multi-year CAGR, debt-free, targeting 95 resorts and 4,500 rooms in 2027. The third is investor-facing: unlock value, 'attract differentiated investor cohorts for each business segment', and let two listed entities pursue growth aligned to their own industry dynamics with improved operational efficiency and profitability, while TCIL concentrates on core Travel and Financial Services (FY26 group income INR 83,982mn, EBT INR 3,268mn, down 14% on the Pahalgam/Operation Sindoor and US-Israel-Iran disruptions). Riding along are three capital-structure fixes: consolidation of four Re.1 shares into one Rs.4 share to improve key financial ratios and better reflect intrinsic value; a reduction of face value from Rs.4 to Rs.3 with no payout to 'right size the balance sheet' and improve EPS; and absorption of three dormant subsidiaries (TC Visa Services, Jardin Travel Solutions, Borderless Travel Services) that incur 'unnecessary compliance and administrative costs'. Consideration is non-cash: 81 SHRL shares of Rs.10 for every 100 TCIL shares of Re.1; TCIL keeps its existing SHRL shares (~7%); SHRL's post-scheme pattern mirrors TCIL's (promoters 65.55%, public 32.30%, ESOP trust 2.16%). The documented originators are internal — the Audit Committee and the Independent Directors Committee recommended it to the Board; no investor, lender, franchise or JV partner is cited anywhere as having asked for it, and the capital-deployment questions analysts did press (Mukul Varma, Anil Shah, Meet Shah on the ~INR 780-800 crore net cash and dividends) were answered with 'no conversations' as late as February 2026.

**How it evolved:** Nothing in the Q4 FY25 call (14 May 2025) or Q1 FY26 call (1 August 2025) hints at a separation, though both lay the groundwork: TCIL had just absorbed the Nature Trails resorts business by slump sale in March 2025 for INR 522.5mn, and Vikram Lalvani declared Sterling's 'transformation is complete' and in a growth phase, debt-free with rising cash. The Q2 FY26 (14 November 2025) and Q3 FY26 (6 February 2026) calls still carry no mention — on 6 February 2026 Mahesh Iyer explicitly said there were no conversations on returning cash or acquisitions, six weeks before the Board acted. The Board gave in-principle approval on 20 March 2026 (Scheme, press release, and separate demerger/merger/consolidation/capital-reduction filings), and the first and only call discussion came on 13 May 2026, where Iyer called it a 'strategic divestment… significant strategic move', Lalvani confirmed 'the demerger process from Thomas Cook has also been initiated', and Debasis Nandy reaffirmed the original 12-15 month timeline with completion expected in Q1 FY28. Execution then ran ahead of the calls: BSE no-adverse-observation (31 August 2026), NSE no-objection (1 September 2026), and an NCLT Mumbai procedural order of 4 November 2026 admitting the application and directing meetings of TCIL's equity shareholders and unsecured creditors.

**What management expects from it:** TCIL: streamlined capital structure, resources concentrated on core Travel and Financial Services, improved EPS from the 4:1 consolidation, face-value reduction and dormant-subsidiary merger. Sterling: a separately listed hospitality pure-play charting its own growth path, holding 31-35% EBITDA margins, debt-free, scaling toward 95 resorts and 4,500 rooms. Both: differentiated investor cohorts, sharper focus, better operational efficiency and profitability.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The Board acted on 20 March 2026 on recommendations from the Audit Committee and the Independent Directors Committee, approving demerger of the Resorts and Resort Management business into SHRL plus a capital restructuring of TCIL. “Based on a recommendation by the audit committee and independent committee, the Board of Thomas Cook (India) Limited (TCIL) today gave an in-principle approval to a proposal for the demerger of the company's Resorts and Resort Management business into Sterling Holiday Resorts Limited (SHRL) and a subsequent capital restructuring of TCIL.”
- *Scheme* — Stated objective one: unlock value for TCIL shareholders and let each business segment be owned by the investor base that suits it, with a future SHRL listing on BSE and NSE. “Unlock value for the shareholders of TCIL by demerging the Resorts and Resort Management business into SHRL and to attract differentiated investor cohorts for each business segment”
- *Scheme* — Capability argument: the six Nature Trails resorts TCIL runs directly belong with Sterling, whose hospitality expertise and scale (72+ resorts, 62 locations) make it the better operator. “TCIL and SHRL's Management believes that the Resort Business of TCIL would reap more benefit from being owned and operated by SHRL in light of their vast expertise in the hospitality industry.”
- *Scheme* — Maturity argument: Sterling is ready to be its own listed company in a fast-growing sector rather than a subsidiary line item. “Further, SHRL's Management is of the view that SHRL has matured over the years and is well poised to chart its own growth path and operate as a separate listed entity in the fast-growing hospitality industry.”
- *Scheme* — Focus argument: segregate verticals so two listed entities can each chase growth on their own industry dynamics, improving operating efficiency and profitability. “The main objective of the proposed restructuring, by way of a composite scheme, is to re-organize and segregate the different business verticals and focus on core businesses, in compliance with relevant regulations.”
- *Scheme* — Scale of what leaves TCIL is tiny — the demerged undertaking is roughly 0.4% of standalone turnover, so this is a listing/value-unlock move, not a disposal of earnings. “The turnover of the Demerged Undertaking for the year ended 31st December 2025 was INR 70 Crores representing ~0.4% of the total standalone turnover of the Company for the year ended 31st December 2025.”
- *Scheme* — Consideration is all-paper: 81 SHRL shares of Rs.10 for every 100 TCIL shares of Re.1, no cash, with TCIL retaining its existing SHRL stake (~7%) and shareholding patterns mirrored. “for every 100 (One Hundred only) equity shares of Thomas Cook (India) Limited of face value of INR 1/- each credited as fully paid up, the issue and allotment by Sterling Holiday Resorts Limited of 81 (Eighty One only) equity shares of Sterling Holiday Resorts Limited of face value of INR 10/-each credited as fully paid up”
- *Scheme* — The share-capital reduction (Rs.4 to Rs.3 face value, no payment to shareholders) is justified purely as balance-sheet right-sizing and EPS improvement; the 4:1 consolidation is justified as improving key ratios and reflecting intrinsic value. “The Management of TCIL believes that the proposed reduction of share capital is required to right size the balance sheet and capital structure of TCIL such that TCIL has a more efficient capital structure and the shareholders also benefit in terms of improved earnings per share.”
- *Scheme* — Three dormant subsidiaries (TCVSL, JTSL, BTSL — FY25 turnover INR 1.2cr, nil, nil) are folded back into TCIL purely to kill compliance and administrative overhead; their shares stand cancelled with no issuance. “TCVSL, JTSL and BTSL are dormant and non-operative companies, incurring unnecessary compliance and administrative costs.”
- *CALL May 2026* — Iyer's first call commentary on it: value unlock for shareholders, a streamlined TCIL capital structure, and resources refocused on Travel and Financial Services, with the face-value consolidation and dormant-subsidiary merger improving EPS. “For Thomas Cook (India) Limited, this restructuring allows us to streamline our capital structure and concentrate our resources on our core Travel and Financial Services business.”
- *CALL May 2026* — Nandy, answering Ananya Khanna on timing, reaffirmed the 12-15 month Board timeline, NSE/BSE applications filed and queries being answered, with completion expected in Q1 FY28. “We expect this process to get completed by Q1 of FY '28, which was the original timeline that we had intimated.”
- *CALL May 2026* — Lalvani tied Sterling's own readiness to the split: transformation behind it, record FY26 (revenue INR 5,487mn, 31% EBITDA margin, 21% PBT margin, 25 profitable quarters, ~INR 3,400mn cash, debt-free) and a brand re-architecture underway alongside the demerger. “In parallel, as you are aware, the demerger process from Thomas Cook has also been initiated.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No basis given for the 81:100 ratio or valuation, why face value drops to Rs.3, Sterling's standalone capital needs, tax effects, dis-synergies, or who initiated it.

## DBREALTY — VALOR ESTATE Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **SPINNING — record date set; the new entity lists soon** · score 4.2/10 · spin-off · 5 filing(s) from NSE · first 2025-11-12, latest 2026-01-30

> **Listing:** RECORD DATE set; Horizontal Ventures Private Limited not yet listed — resulting companies have typically listed 4–10 weeks after the record date; filings/calls say: Press release dated November 12, 2025: "today announced the proposed listing of its equity shares on the National Stock Exchange of India Ltd. (NSE) and BSE Ltd on November 13, 2025"

**The stages, as filed:** nclt_sanction (2025-11-15) → effective (2025-11-14)

**Stated in the filings:** resulting company **Horizontal Ventures Private Limited**; demerged undertaking: / Discontinued Operations are given as under:; entitlement **1 for every 10**; appointed date 2025-04-01.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** The hospitality (hotel ownership) business of Valor Estate, demerged into Advent Hotels International Limited — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* Mr. Arshad Balwa is Promoter Director of AHIL; Rahul Pandit is MD & CEO; AHIL governed by own Board post-demerger. Shareholders received 1 AHIL share per 10 Valor shares; promoters held 47.43% of Valor. AHIL promoter stake not stated.
- *What it reveals:* Spin holds 313-key Grand Hyatt Goa and 171-key Hilton Mumbai, five projects under development, EBITDA under Rs.200 crore targeted above Rs.1,200 crore by FY32 (3,100+ keys). Parent left as pure real estate; consolidated borrowings fell sharply post-demerger.
- *Selling pressure:* likely — Only 1 AHIL share per 10 held, so tiny odd-lot positions; hospitality is a different industry from the parent's real estate.
- *Parent or spin:* both · *option pricing date:* 14th August 2025 (Nomination and Remuneration Committee approved grant of 10,00,000 options under ESOP 2024); earlier ESOP 2022 options exercised at Rs. 41.45 per share during quarter ended 30th June 2025
- *Read next:* AHIL's own balance sheet: the Rs. 2,01,956.25 lakhs other non-current financial liabilities transferred with the demerged undertaking
- *In their words:* “A Composite Scheme of Amalgamation and Arrangement was entered into between the Company ("Amalgamated Company" and "Demerged Company") and Esteem Properties Private Limited ("Amalgamating Company"/"EPPL") and Advent Hotels International Limited (formerly known as Shiva Realtors Suburban Private Limited) ("Resulting Company"/"AHIL) ("Scheme") mainly with aim to demerge hospitality business of the Company into Resulting Company and thus unlock overall value for the shareholders.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

No earnings-call transcripts are on file, so the reasoning below is reconstructed only from the filings. The separation is the demerger of Valor Estate Ltd's (formerly D B Realty Ltd) hospitality business into Advent Hotels International Limited (formerly Shiva Realtors Suburban Private Limited) under a Composite Scheme of Amalgamation and Arrangement that also amalgamated Esteem Properties Private Limited into Valor; the Explanatory Statement to the 12th December 2025 EGM says the Scheme was entered into 'mainly with aim to demerge hospitality business of the Company into Resulting Company and thus unlock overall value for the shareholders.' NCLT Mumbai sanctioned it on 12 June 2025, it became effective 1 July 2025 (demerger appointed date 1 April 2025; Esteem amalgamation appointed date 1 April 2024), and shareholders on the 18 July 2025 record date received 1 AHIL share of Rs. 10 for every 10 Valor shares. The carve-out moved consolidated net assets of Rs. 1,02,194.65 lakhs (standalone Rs. 1,01,512.91 lakhs) out of Valor — Rs. 1,49,386.00 lakhs of property, plant and equipment, Rs. 54,858.00 lakhs of goodwill, Rs. 29,117.12 lakhs of intangibles, against Rs. 46,196.17 lakhs non-current and Rs. 16,028.03 lakhs current borrowings, Rs. 2,01,956.25 lakhs of other non-current financial liabilities and Rs. 28,951.71 lakhs of deferred tax liability — and took out a business that had FY25 revenue of Rs. 36,650.21 lakhs and PAT of Rs. 4,468.06 lakhs, now shown as discontinued operations. Management's stated problems solved are focus and structure: Valor 'is now engaged solely in the real estate business, which constitutes its only reportable segment,' so segment reporting ceased, while Advent gets 'its own Board and Management team,' NSE/BSE listing on 13 November 2025 for 'enhanced market visibility, liquidity for existing shareholders, and a strengthened capital structure,' and an asset-heavy growth path (five projects, 3,100 keys, EBITDA from under Rs. 200 crore to over Rs. 1,200 crore by FY32, targeted mid-teens compounded ROE) that a combined entity would have had to fund alongside real estate. The second, smaller separation/consolidation strand is non-core cleanup: Sahyadri Agro and Dairy Private Limited (dairy farming, milk procurement and trading), taken to 76.63% via enforcement of security and then to 100% 'as the transaction relates to the liquidation of non-core assets,' sold its entire dairy business under a Business Transfer Agreement at a gain of Rs. 6,901.20 lakhs with Rs. 1,697.63 lakhs of non-compete fees booked as an exceptional item, is now 'evaluating opportunities to engage in the business of real estate development,' and was amalgamated into Horizontal Ventures Private Limited for structural simplification, synergies, avoidance of duplication and lower compliance and overhead costs. Running alongside is balance-sheet repair the filings tie to the same strategy: consolidated secured debt down to Rs. 730 crore, full redemption of Rs. 235 crore of NCDs out of the Rs. 262 crore Dahisar/Aradhya Park development-rights conveyance, and the Scheme-driven reduction and consolidation of the 8% RPS (Clause 32: Rs. 10 face value cut to Rs. 9, then 10 consolidated into 9) plus Clause 20's 1:10 allotment of AHIL preference shares, followed by the November 2025 proposal to convert KRPL's 6,45,75,000 RPS into 0.0001% CCPS converting into 32,02,330 equity shares at Rs. 201.65 'with a view to conserve the financial resources of the Company.' No filing names any investor, lender or partner as having demanded the separation; the only named partner is Prestige Group, which sits on Advent's side as a 50:50 JV partner in the Sahar project and co-developer at Aerocity.

**How it evolved:** There are no transcripts on file, so the idea cannot be traced call by call; the paper trail runs through filings and the Scheme itself. The Composite Scheme was sanctioned by NCLT Mumbai on 12 June 2025, became effective 1 July 2025 with demerger appointed date 1 April 2025, and the 1:10 entitlement was fixed on the 18 July 2025 record date; the SADPL-into-HVPL amalgamation was approved by both boards on 18 August 2025 with appointed date 1 April 2025. The plan then became visible in public filings in quick succession: Advent's listing press release (12 November 2025), Valor's Q2FY26 results and press release (14-15 November 2025) which first framed the demerger as completed and as the basis for debt reduction, the EGM notice and corrigendum (20 November and 8 December 2025) which disclosed the Scheme's preference-share reduction, consolidation and 1:10 AHIL allotment and layered the RPS-to-CCPS conversion on top, and finally the NCLT order of 29 January 2026 and effective date of 12 March 2026 completing the SADPL consolidation. The shape of the plan therefore widened over time from a single hospitality demerger into a package: demerger plus listing, plus non-core dairy liquidation and merger, plus capital-structure conversion.

**What management expects from it:** Valor: pure-play real estate, single reportable segment, leaner and more efficient capital structure, lower debt (secured debt ₹730 crore), greater financial flexibility, unlocked value. Advent: independent board and management, focused hospitality platform, better visibility, shareholder liquidity, stronger capital structure, 3,100 keys and EBITDA above ₹1,200 crore by FY32, mid-teens compounded ROE.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The Composite Scheme's stated purpose, as put to shareholders in the EGM explanatory statement, was to demerge the hospitality business into Advent Hotels International Limited and unlock shareholder value; it simultaneously amalgamated Esteem Properties Private Limited into Valor. “mainly with aim to demerge hospitality business of the Company into Resulting Company and thus unlock overall value for the shareholders”
- *Scheme* — Post-demerger Valor is a pure-play real estate company with a single reportable segment, and prior-period hospitality results are reclassified as discontinued operations under Ind AS 105. “Consequent to the demerger, the Company is now engaged solely in the real estate business, which constitutes its only reportable segment.”
- *Scheme* — Management framed the separation as letting each business pursue its own growth path: Chairman Vinod Goenka tied Q2FY26 progress to completing the demerger and listing of hospitality. “We successfully completed the demerger and listing of our Hospitality business, an important milestone that enables each platform to pursue its independent growth path.”
- *Scheme* — The Q2FY26 press release states the problems the split solves on Valor's side: targeted independent strategies for each business, sharper operational focus, and unlocked long-term value. “This development enables each business to pursue a targeted, independent growth strategy, strengthens operational focus, and positions the Group to unlock enhanced long-term value for shareholders.”
- *Scheme* — Advent's 13 November 2025 NSE/BSE listing was justified on visibility, shareholder liquidity and capital structure, with Advent carved out of Valor and run by its own board and management. “The listing will mark a significant milestone in Advent's journey as a dedicated hospitality platform, enabling enhanced market visibility, liquidity for existing shareholders, and a strengthened capital structure to support future growth.”
- *Scheme* — Advent now has independent governance: two operating hotels (313-key Grand Hyatt Bambolim Goa plus 113 keys under development, and a 171-key Hilton in Andheri East, Mumbai). “The Company is governed by its own Board and Management team following the demerger.”
- *Scheme* — Advent quantified the growth the standalone platform is meant to fund: five projects under development including St. Regis and Marriott Marquis at Aerocity Delhi with Prestige Group (FY27), Waldorf Astoria and Hilton at Worli, and a 1,175-key BKC hotel. “With five projects under development, the company is on track to expand to 3,100 keys. EBITDA, currently under ₹200 crore, is projected to surpass ₹1,200 crore as these projects mature by FY32, reflecting the company's robust growth and institutional approach.”
- *Scheme* — Advent's MD & CEO Rahul Pandit cast the separation and listing as a governance and financing fix for an asset-heavy hospitality business; Promoter Director Arshad Balwa targeted mid-teens compounded ROE over the next decade. “This listing enhances our financial flexibility, strengthens governance, and enables sustainable value generation for all stakeholders.”
- *Scheme* — Vice Chairman & MD Shahid Balwa linked the demerger and non-core divestments to deleveraging — consolidated secured debt of ₹730 crore, full redemption of ₹235 crore of NCDs from the ₹262 crore Dahisar/Aradhya Park development-rights conveyance. “The rationalisation of our project portfolio, combined with selective monetisation initiatives, including the divestment of non-core assets, has enabled us to reduce debt levels, bringing us closer to our medium-term objective of a leaner and more efficient capital structure.”
- *Scheme* — Sahyadri Agro and Dairy was treated explicitly as a non-core asset being liquidated: the Group went to 76.63% through enforcement of security, then to 100%, and SADPL sold its dairy assets under a Business Transfer Agreement at a gain of Rs. 6,901.20 lakhs with Rs. 1,697.63 lakhs of non-compete fees as an exceptional item. “As the transaction relates to the liquidation of non-core assets, SADPL has not been consolidated.”
- *Scheme* — The NCLT order of 29 January 2026 records the benefits claimed for folding dairy-turned-real-estate SADPL into Horizontal Ventures Private Limited, a wholly-owned-subsidiary merger inside the group with appointed date 1 April 2025, effective 12 March 2026. “Simplification  and rationalisation  of corporate  struct ure through consolidation;”
- *Scheme* — The same order lists compliance and overhead reduction as the operating rationale for the SADPL-HVPL consolidation, with the petitioners undertaking not to claim Section 72A tax-loss benefits after the Income-tax Officer objected. “Reduction in multiplicity of legal and regulatory compliances,  reduction in overheads, including administrative, managerial and other administrative costs.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No call transcripts supplied; filings never name investors, lenders or partners who asked for it, nor give swap-ratio valuation basis, cost savings, or Advent fundraising plans.

**CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **LISTED <1Y — selling-pressure window; the bargain forms here** · score 4.2/10 · spin-off · 48 filing(s) from BSE-screener, NSE, NSE-register · first 2026-01-09, latest 2026-11-04

**The stages, as filed:** announced (2026-10-15) → meetings (2026-04-02) → nclt_sanction (2026-05-05) → effective (2026-08-24) → record_date (2026-07-29)

**Stated in the filings:** resulting company **HEG Graphite Limited**; demerged undertaking: — i.e., the Company's graphite business — is to be demerged from HEG Limited into HEG Graphite; entitlement **1 for every 1**; record date 2026-09-07; appointed date 2024-04-01; size hint: 0% of ebitda.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** The Graphite Undertaking — graphite electrodes business plus overseas investment and TAWA power plant assets/liabilities — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* Ravi Jhunjhunwala is Chairman, MD & CEO of HEG Limited (Resulting Company); son Riju Jhunjhunwala chairs HEGAM. Promoter stake in new entity not stated.
- *What it reveals:* Graphite carried Rs 4,601.53 cr assets vs Rs 1,357.07 cr liabilities (June 30, 2026) and earned Rs 319.71 cr H1 FY27 PAT; parent keeps debt-free hydro with over Rs 300 cr annual cash flows and Rs 1,322.84 cr cash.
- *Selling pressure:* likely — 1 share issued to every HEGAM holder; shares still unlisted pending trading approval; graphite is a different industry from parent's advanced materials/power.
- *Parent or spin:* spin · *option pricing date:* not stated (ESOP 2026 approved by Board November 3, 2026; pricing formula 'As per Scheme (as determined by Nomination and Remuneration Committee)')
- *Read next:* HEG Limited's listing/trading approval intimation, and its standalone balance sheet borrowings of Rs 708.97 cr.
- *In their words:* “Under the Scheme, the graphite electrodes business was transferred to HEG Limited (earlier known as HEG Graphite Limited), and Bhilwara Energy Limited was amalgamated into the Company.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

HEGAM's separation is the "Composite Scheme of Arrangement" among HEG Advanced Materials Limited (formerly HEG Limited, the Demerged Company), HEG Limited (formerly HEG Graphite Limited, the Resulting Company) and Bhilwara Energy Limited (the Transferor Company): the legacy Graphite Undertaking — the graphite electrodes business, plus the overseas investment and the assets and liabilities of the TAWA power plant — was demerged into the Resulting Company on a going-concern basis with mirror shares issued to HEGAM shareholders, while Bhilwara Energy Limited was simultaneously amalgamated into HEGAM. As the filings present it, the purpose is to put the mature, cyclical electrodes business (FY26 revenue ₹2,568.50 crore, H1 FY27 ₹1,207.36 crore and PAT ₹192.33 crore, carrying ₹4,419.21 crore of segment assets and ₹1,245.85 crore of liabilities) in one listed vehicle, and leave HEGAM as a "technology-led, globally competitive advanced materials platform" spanning anode materials (TACC), graphene (HEG Graphene Materials), battery energy storage (Replus Engitech, 74% held) and green power. The amalgamation of Bhilwara Energy brings 278 MW of debt-free hydro (86 MW MPCL + 192 MW AD Hydro) plus 14 MW of wind into HEGAM, which the CFO says "provides a sound financial foundation for the Group" with "stable cash flows of over ₹300 crore" annually — i.e. the hydro cash flow and the ₹1,322.84 crore cash pile now sit against the heavy new-materials capex rather than against electrodes. The problem it solves is capital allocation and identity: HEGAM's board on 3 November 2026 approved a revised Phase-1 anode cost of ~₹2,350 crore (20,000 MT, COD June 2027, 61% built), a ₹1,606 crore Phase-2 to 44,000 MT by March 2029, a ₹475 crore crucible plant for "backward integration" and cost optimisation, and a ₹500 crore 500 MTPA graphene plant — none of which belong on an electrode balance sheet. The company also altered its main object clause to insert "Anode, Graphene, crucible, advanced carbon materials and other allied material" (CIN changed from L23109MP1972PLC008290 to L35100MP1972PLC008290) and implemented an ESOP of up to 98,93,970 options, so each entity can be objected, incentivised and financed on its own. Leadership was split along the same line: Ravi Jhunjhunwala moved to Chairman, MD & CEO of the demerged HEG Limited (graphite), while Riju Jhunjhunwala leads HEGAM and has now taken the chair of MPCL and AD Hydro. A lender appears in the record on the power side: CYHPL bought Statkraft's 49% of MPCL on 17 November 2025 and intends to merge MPCL and ADHPL into itself "for consolidating the hydro power asstes of the group in the CYHPL in line with undertaking given by CYHPL to ICICI Bank."

**How it evolved:** No earnings-call transcripts were supplied, so the sequence can only be traced through filings: by 19 January 2026 the Scheme was already public enough to warrant an investor "Webinar on Update on Composite Scheme of Arrangement," and the 49% MPCL buy-out from Statkraft (SPA 9 September 2025, closed 17 November 2025) had pre-positioned the hydro assets. Shareholders approved it at the NCLT-convened meeting on 5 May 2026 with requisite majority; the NCLT Indore Bench sanctioned it on 13 August 2026; the board fixed 1 September 2026 as Effective Date (Appointed Date backdated to 1 April 2024) and allotted the new shares on 7 September 2026, lifting paid-up capital from ₹38.60 crore to ₹65.96 crore. Only after effectiveness did the plan visibly widen from "separate graphite" to "build out advanced materials": the 3 November 2026 board added Phase-2 anode (44,000 MT), crucibles, graphene, an ESOP and the new object clause, while on 29–30 October 2026 the object-clause CIN change was registered and HEGAM had to publish the unlisted Resulting Company's results on its behalf pending listing.

**What management expects from it:** Graphite stands alone as HEG Limited (FY26 revenue ₹2,568.50 crore), pending listing. HEGAM becomes a focused advanced-materials platform — anode 20,000→44,000 MT, crucibles, 500 MTPA graphene, Replus BESS (1→6 GWh), 278 MW debt-free hydro giving ₹300 crore-plus annual cash flow and ₹1,322.84 crore cash to fund capex — with diversified revenues, ESOP-aligned talent and "multiple avenues for value creation."

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The Scheme's core mechanic: the Graphite Undertaking — including the overseas investment and the TAWA power plant assets and liabilities — goes out to the Resulting Company, and Bhilwara Energy comes in. “the demerger of the Graphite Undertaking including overseas investment and assets and liabilities pertaining to TAWA power plant of the Company into the Resulting Company and amalgamation of the Transferor Company with the Company”
- *Scheme* — The press release states plainly what moved where on the 1 September 2026 effective date, and that the two sides are now reported separately as continuing and discontinued operations. “Under the Scheme, the graphite electrodes business was transferred to HEG Limited (earlier known as HEG Graphite Limited), and Bhilwara Energy Limited was amalgamated into the Company.”
- *Scheme* — Riju Jhunjhunwala frames the remaining entity's purpose as a technology-led advanced materials platform across anode, graphene, BESS and green power, with "research to revenue" as the motto. “Q2 FY27 reflects our continued progress towards building HEG Advanced Materials into a technology -led, globally competitive advanced materials platform.”
- *Scheme* — CFO Neha Rajvanshi explains the financial logic of pulling hydro in: the debt-free green power business funds and underwrites the developmental verticals. “Our Green Power Business, with its differentiated model, profitable operations, debt -free position and stable cash flows, provides a sound financial foundation for the Group.”
- *Scheme* — The scale of that foundation: 278 MW of hydro in Himachal (86 MW MPCL + 192 MW AD Hydro) plus 14 MW wind, all debt-free, against H1 FY27 cash of ₹1,322.84 crore. “Both operating hydro projects and the wind project are debt -free, and the existing hydro assets generate annually stable cash flows of over ₹300 crore.”
- *Scheme* — Immediately post-demerger the board sanctioned the capex the new entity exists to carry: Phase-1 20,000 MT anode revised to ~₹2,350 crore (COD June 2027), Phase-2 24,000 MT for ~₹1,606 crore to reach 44,000 MT by March 2029. “Proposal for expansion plan by increasing the capacity from 20,000 MT to 44,000 MT.  The estimated cost is ~ Rs. 1606 crore with target COD by March 2029.”
- *Scheme* — The ₹475 crore, 80,000-unit crucible plant is justified as backward integration into the anode line rather than as a new market. “The project is expected to strengthen backward integration, optimize procurement costs, and improve operational  efficiencies,  thereby supporting the long-term growth and competitiveness of the subsidiary.”
- *Scheme* — The ₹500 crore, 500 MTPA graphene plant in HEG Graphene Materials Limited is positioned as a new growth avenue built through a subsidiary. “The proposed project is expected to create a new avenue for business growth through the subsidiary, strengthen the Company's long-term business prospects, and contribute to sustainable  value  creation  for stakeholders”
- *Scheme* — The legal identity was re-pointed at the new businesses: the object clause was amended to insert anode, graphene, crucible and advanced carbon materials, which changed the CIN from L23109MP1972PLC008290 to L35100MP1972PLC008290. “Alteration of the main object clause of Memorandum of Association (MOA) of the company by inserting the objects relating to Anode, Graphene, crucible, advanced carbon materials and other allied material, subject to the approval of shareholders.”
- *Scheme* — A lender's requirement drives the parallel power-side restructuring: CYHPL, having bought Statkraft's 49% of MPCL on 17 November 2025, plans to acquire the remaining 51% and merge MPCL and ADHPL into itself. “Theproposed acquisition andmerger isbeing done forconsolidating thehydro power asstes of the group in the CYHPL in line with undertaking given by CYHPL to ICICI Bank.”
- *Scheme* — Shareholders, not just the board, carried the Scheme — approved at the NCLT-convened meeting of 5 May 2026, sanctioned by NCLT Indore on 13 August 2026, effective 1 September 2026 with 1 April 2024 as appointed date. “The equity shareholders at the NCLT -convened meeting held on May 05, 2026  have passed the resolution with requisite majority approv ing the Scheme .”
- *Scheme* — Management had been briefing investors on the Scheme well before effectiveness, via a dedicated webinar in January 2026. “Please find below the link for Video Recording of Webinar on Update on Composite Scheme of Arrangement held on 19th January, 2026 at 1600 hrs IST.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No earnings-call transcripts were provided, so no Q&A, no Scheme rationale clause, no share-exchange ratio, valuation, debt allocation, target multiples, or named investor/partner demands.

## MAHSEAMLES — Maharashtra Seamless Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 4.2/10 · spin-off · 4 filing(s) from BSE-screener, NSE · first 2026-05-22, latest 2026-10-07

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; MSL Seamless Tubes Limited will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; indicated timeline: On 07 October 2026 (and earlier 22 May 2026): "Yes. The equity shares of MSTL and USL shall be listed and admitted to trading on BSE and NSE pursuant to the Scheme subject to receipt of requisite approvals from statutory and regulatory authorities." No expected listing date stated; Appointed Date 01st October 2026, NCLT approval pending.

**The stages, as filed:** announced (2026-10-07)

**Stated in the filings:** resulting company **MSL Seamless Tubes Limited**; demerged undertaking: 1 into MSL Seamless Tubes Limited; entitlement **1 for every 5**; appointed date 2026-10-01.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Two seamless pipe plants: Mangaon (125,000 MTPA) with Beed solar; Narketpally Telangana (200,000 MTPA) with Rajasthan solar and rig — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* Promoter & Promoter Group get 70.3008% of each resulting company (1,88,40,507 of 2,67,99,850 shares), mirroring their MSL stake; no cash consideration; no other incentive disclosed.
- *What it reveals:* Separate reporting prices each plant's economics: UD1 Rs 793 crore turnover (16.98%), UD2 Rs 693 crore (14.84%), remaining Rs 3,185 crore (68.18%). Parent retains Nagothane plus Rs 3,115 crore treasury management said to back ~50% of market cap.
- *Selling pressure:* likely — Each spin tiny: ~15-17% of turnover, only 2,67,99,850 shares, 1 share per 5 held; rig/solar assets differ from pipes.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* The full Scheme filed with NCLT: which specified assets, liabilities and the Rs 3,115 crore treasury stay with MSL.
- *In their words:* “The above share exchange ratios shall ensure same proportionate shareholding structure of Resulting Company 1 and Resulting Company 2 with Demerged Company and hence Scheme shall be value neutral to the Demerged Company's shareholders.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

This is not a sale but a three-way split by demerger: a Scheme of Arrangement approved by MSL's board (first on 22 May 2026, then re-approved 7 October 2026 with an Appointed Date of 1 October 2026) carves two 'Demerged Undertakings' out of Maharashtra Seamless into two wholly owned subsidiaries that will themselves be listed on BSE and NSE. Demerged Undertaking 1 — the Mangaon, Maharashtra seamless pipe plant (125,000 MTPA) plus the 10 MW captive solar plant at Beed — goes to MSL Seamless Tubes Limited (MSTL); Demerged Undertaking 2 — the Narketpally, Telangana seamless mill (200,000 MTPA), the Khetusar (20 MW) and Pokhran (5 MW) solar plants in Rajasthan, and the rig Jindal Explorer — goes to United Seamless Limited (USL), i.e. the asset base MSL bought out of IBC as United Seamless Tubulaar for INR477 crores plus INR73 crores of reactivation capex. On FY2025-26 operational turnover the split is Undertaking 1 INR793 crores (16.98%), Undertaking 2 INR693 crores (14.84%) and the residual company (Nagothane pipes, ERW, treasury) INR3,185 crores (68.18%) of INR4,671 crores. The board's stated reasons are that the undertakings have 'distinct geographies, product profiles, technologies used, operational requirements, customer profile and base, market focus, logistics consideration' — specifically three different mill technologies, CPE at Nagothane, MPM at Mangaon and FQM at Telangana, each needing its own modernization and technical expertise — so each should run as a focused, independently reported vertical. It also says manufacturing, drilling and renewable energy have 'different capital intensity and funding requirements', so splitting them allows better assessment of capital needs and more flexibility for expansion; the renewable plants are attached to the mills they can power; and the rig business, long described on calls as outside the core, is segregated because it has 'distinct operational and commercial characteristics as compared to the pipe manufacturing business'. No cash changes hands: shareholders get 1 share of INR5 in each resulting company for every 5 MSL shares, producing the same proportionate holding (promoter ~70.30%, public ~29.70%, 2,67,99,850 shares in each), which the filing calls 'value neutral'; creditor liabilities are neither reduced nor extinguished and travel with each undertaking. Notably, the nine earnings calls supplied — including Feb 2026, three months before the first board approval — contain no mention of a demerger at all; the only antecedents are repeated investor pressure to exit the rig and one shareholder's demand to split the company, and management's standing answer that it would continue 'in the steel pipe segment only' and that exit was 'for the Board to decide'.

**How it evolved:** The idea surfaced only as a rig exit: on the Feb 2024 call (30 Jan 2024) Chairman D.P. Jindal said of staying in rigs 'we have to take the appropriate decision at the right time', and on the Nov 2024 call (29 Oct 2024) an investor asked directly about demerging or selling the rig, to which management said it was something 'we want to do, but it is subject to Board approval'. Pressure widened over the next year: on the Feb 2025 call (28 Jan 2025) management personally agreed the rig-to-Jindal-Drilling structure 'doesn't look in line' with its governance clean-up, on the Jun 2025 call (27 May 2025) it confirmed 'there was a view of getting out of the rig business' with no board update, and on the Aug 2025 call (31 July 2025) a shareholder explicitly asked management to 'divide the company in two parts' — a holding company and a seamless company — and got only 'I don't have anything to add'. By the Nov 2025 call (5 Nov 2025) there was still 'no update on the proposal', and the Feb 2026 call (29 Jan 2026) discussed only cash conservation, treasury and a hunt for distressed acquisitions. The actual plan then appeared without any call commentary: board approval 22 May 2026, a 15 June 2026 notice that the Scheme was 'under further review', and a revised, re-approved Scheme on 7 October 2026 that widened it from a rig/holding split into a full three-way break-up of the three mills by technology, with 'related assets and liabilities' tightened to 'specified assets and liabilities' and 'mirror shareholding' restated as 'same proportionate shareholding'.

**What management expects from it:** Per the Scheme only: each mill run as a focused vertical with dedicated management and technology-specific modernization; sharper assessment and deployment of capital across pipes, drilling and renewables, with more flexibility for expansion; solar assets aligned to the mills they serve; the rig managed on its own terms; independent reporting improving transparency and performance evaluation; identical proportionate shareholding, so value-neutral. No margin, cost, ROCE or valuation figures were given.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — Two undertakings are carved out into two wholly owned subsidiaries, MSL Seamless Tubes Limited and United Seamless Limited, both to be listed, with an Appointed Date of 1 October 2026; the Mangaon 125,000 MTPA mill and the 10 MW Beed captive solar plant form Undertaking 1. “Demerged Undertaking 1: Seamless pipe manufacturing business of the Demerged Company located at Mangaon, Maharashtra (125,000 MTPA), captive solar power plant at Beed, Maharashtra (10 MW), along with the specified assets and liabilities of Demerged Undertaking 1.”
- *Scheme* — Undertaking 2 bundles the Telangana (Narketpally) 200,000 MTPA mill with the Rajasthan solar plants and the rig Jindal Explorer into United Seamless Limited — effectively re-separating the ex-United Seamless Tubulaar asset base and the rig in one entity. “Demerged Undertaking 2: Seamless pipe manufacturing facility of the Demerged Company located at Narketpally, Telangana (200,000 MTPA), solar power plants at Khetusar (20 MW) & Pokhran (5MW) in Rajasthan, rig Jindal Explorer along with the specified assets and liabilities of Demerged Undertaking 2.”
- *Scheme* — The headline justification is that one company holds businesses with nothing in common operationally — different geographies, products, technologies, customers and logistics — so each should be managed separately. “The said undertakings having distinct geographies, product profiles, technologies used, operational requirements, customer profile and base, market focus, logistics consideration, commercial considerations and growth opportunities.”
- *Scheme* — The most concrete operating reason given is that the three mills run on three different pipe-making technologies, each needing its own specialised management and modernization programme — which maps exactly onto the three-way split. “The manufacturing facilities operate on different technological platforms, including CPE technology at Nagothane, MPM technology at Mangaon and FQM technology at Telangana, each requiring specialized operational management, modernization initiatives and technical expertise.”
- *Scheme* — Capital allocation is cited: pipes, drilling and renewables have different capital intensity, so separation is meant to let each assess and fund its own needs — relevant given the stalled INR852 crore capex plan and the INR350 crore Nagothane hot-mill upgrade never started. “Efficient Capital Allocation: The manufacturing, drilling and renewable energy businesses have different capital intensity and funding requirements.”
- *Scheme* — The rig is singled out for segregation on the grounds that it is commercially unlike pipe manufacturing — the same objection investors had raised on calls for two years. “Focused Development of Rig Operations: The rig business has distinct operational and commercial characteristics as compared to the pipe manufacturing business.”
- *Scheme* — The renewable plants are deliberately attached to the mills they sit beside rather than kept central, framed as energy-management efficiency and sustainability support for each business. “The renewable power assets proposed to be transferred along with the respective undertakings are expected to provide better operational alignment, energy management efficiencies and support sustainability initiatives of the corresponding businesses.”
- *Scheme* — Separate financial and operational reporting per entity is itself presented as a benefit — transparency and performance evaluation — which speaks to the calls where management refused to give product-wise or mill-wise margins. “Improved Transparency and Value Creation: The proposed demerger would result in creation of focused business entities with independent financial and operational reporting, thereby enhancing transparency, improving performance evaluation and facilitating long-term value creation for stakeholders.”
- *Scheme* — No cash is paid; shareholders receive 1 INR5 share in each resulting company per 5 MSL shares, giving identical proportionate ownership (promoter 70.3008%, public 29.6992%, 2,67,99,850 shares each) and, the board says, value neutrality. “The above share exchange ratios shall ensure same proportionate shareholding structure of Resulting Company 1 and Resulting Company 2 with Demerged Company and hence Scheme shall be value neutral to the Demerged Company's shareholders.”
- *Scheme* — Lenders are explicitly left untouched: no arrangement or compromise with creditors, liabilities travelling with each undertaking — i.e. the split is not presented as lender-driven or a debt restructuring. “The liabilities towards the creditors of the Demerged Company and/or the Resulting Companies under the Scheme are neither being reduced nor being extinguished and the liabilities pertaining to the respective undertakings shall be assumed and discharged by the respective Resulting Companies in the ordinary course of business.”
- *Scheme* — The plan was not stable: approved 22 May 2026, pulled back for review on 15 June 2026, and re-approved only on 7 October 2026 with tightened wording ('specified' rather than 'related' assets, 'same proportionate' rather than 'mirror' shareholding) and slightly revised indicative share counts (promoter 70.2784% to 70.3008%). “This is further to the intimation dated 22nd May, 2026, about the approval of the Scheme of Arrangement by the Board of Directors of the Company, we have to inform you that the said Scheme is under further review and would be placed before any subsequent Board Meeting for its approval and would be submitted to Stock Exchanges thereafter.”
- *[Feb 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=b72c7b85-4c69-46c2-a090-5ef0d9c829bd.pdf)* — The first hint of any separation was about the rig: asked whether MSL would keep two verticals, the Chairman declined to commit, while noting day rates had risen (~$40,000/day, expecting a new contract above $80,000). “Well, we have to take the appropriate decision at the right time.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No call ever mentioned it. Silent on where the ~INR3,500 crore treasury, debt, ERW and premium-connections subsidiary sit, on margins, valuation, lost shared overheads, and NCLT timing.

*Calls read (36 months):* [Nov 2023](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=132dfb4c-b880-4f4e-8e84-430872794cb3.pdf), [Nov 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=527a8802-c766-46b3-bf40-c501d9bde473.pdf)
