## ABLBL — Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (this company IS the resulting company of Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limited's demerger, listed on 2025-06-23 — the spun entity in its second year) · **LISTED 1–2Y — the second-year window** · score 3.6/10 · spin-off · 6 filing(s) from CALLS, NSE · first 2026-02-02, latest 2026-03-31

> **Listing:** THIS COMPANY IS THE SPIN-OFF — the resulting company of Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limited's demerger, listed on 2025-06-23 (503 days ago)

**The stages, as filed:** listed (2025-06-23)

**Stated in the filings:** entitlement **1 for every 1**.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Madura Fashion and Lifestyle ('MFL') Business — branded apparels (garments and accessories) — transferred from ABFRL to ABLBL — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* Promoter stake not stated; all shareholders hold identical shareholdings in both companies. ESOP Scheme 2026 covers 1,83,07,800 shares (1.5%), max 0.50% per employee; promoters/promoter group excluded.
- *What it reveals:* FY26 revenue ₹8,396 cr, EBITDA ₹1,429 cr (17%, +90bps), reported PAT ₹171 cr but pre-IndAS PAT before exceptional ₹313 cr; net debt down to ₹726 cr; Emerging Business turning from breakeven to ~4% EBITDA.
- *Selling pressure:* unclear — Documents state only 1:1 allotment of 1,22,02,94,773 shares to all ABFRL holders; no mention of index exclusion or flowback.
- *Parent or spin:* spin · *option pricing date:* not stated — Option Exercise Price is the closing price one day prior to the NRC's grant date; scheme approved by Board on August 1, 2026
- *Read next:* Postal ballot result on ESOP Scheme 2026, due on or before November 4, 2026, then the actual grant price
- *In their words:* “One of the primary reasons for demerger was to create an entity which can reinvest back more aggressively into growth.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The separation at issue is the demerger of the Madura Fashion & Lifestyle (MFL) business — the four Lifestyle/Power brands (Louis Philippe, Van Heusen, Allen Solly, Peter England) plus the emerging portfolio of Reebok, American Eagle and Van Heusen Innerwear, and a contract-manufacturing/institutional arm — out of Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Ltd (ABFRL, the Demerged Company) into Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands Ltd (ABLBL, the Resulting Company), on a going-concern basis with 1:1 shares so holders own identical stakes in both; the Board approved it on April 19, 2024, NCLT sanctioned it on March 27, 2025, it became effective May 1, 2025, 1,22,02,94,773 shares were allotted May 26, 2025 (record date May 22, 2025) and ABLBL listed June 23, 2025. The reason management gave is capital allocation, stated most bluntly by Ashish Dikshit on the Feb 3, 2026 call: 'One of the primary reasons for demerger was to create an entity which can reinvest back more aggressively into growth' — because inside ABFRL the cash this branded business threw off 'was used to actually kick start or acquire multiple new businesses' (Aug 14, 2025), starving the mature brands of reinvestment. The quantification: the business generates roughly INR 900 crores of EBITDA cash, part to working capital and part to capex, where historical capex was 'close to 150 to 200 in the best years, maybe INR225 odd crores'; post-demerger FY26 capex went 'north of INR300 crores, perhaps INR320 crores, INR330 crores', funding 300+ gross store additions to 3,348 stores / 4.9 million sq ft across ~800 towns, 65 renovations in one quarter, and a new Pulivendula factory. Debt came across by formula — 'at the time of demerger, the company got the borrowings transferred based on the allocation formula' — about INR 800 crores at March 2025, peaking near INR 1,000 crores in September 2025 on festive inventory, INR 800 crores in December 2025 and INR 726 crores at March 2026 versus INR 781 crores a year earlier; INR 500 crores of NCDs repaid in January 2026 were refinanced with 'no fresh borrowing', and management guided to INR 200–300 crores of annual reduction and near-zero net debt in about three years, with capex ranked ahead of deleveraging ('Only the subsequent part will go towards debt reduction'). Management also kept repeating the structural promise that neither entity would raise equity except ABFRL's retained 'tomorrow' businesses, and demonstrated the self-funding claim with a maiden 50 paise dividend in year one and a stated 15–25%-of-PAT payout range. Growth is to be split by entity economics: Lifestyle Brands in early double digits on 6–7% (later '7%') steady-state LTL plus ~200 store adds a year, and the emerging brands at 18–20%+ (Dikshit: 'in excess of 20%'), rising to one-fourth of ABLBL in four to five years, with Reebok already doubled in sales and network tripled since acquisition and Van Heusen Innerwear losses halving on the way to break-even. Notably, no call or filing attributes the demerger request to any investor, lender or brand partner — it is presented purely as a board/strategy decision about where cash gets reinvested.

**How it evolved:** The Scheme itself dates to the April 19, 2024 board approval, with NCLT sanction on March 27, 2025 and effect from May 1, 2025, and the Aug 14, 2025 (Q1 FY26) call was the first as an independent listee — there Dikshit gave the rationale in answer to Niharika Karnani, that cash which had been used to kick-start or acquire new businesses inside ABFRL would now fund this business's own growth (capex first, debt reduction later, debt-free in 2.5–3 years, newer brands 18–20% vs Lifestyle early double digits). The Nov 5, 2025 (Q2 FY26) call barely revisited the rationale and instead exposed a transition cost: comparable prior-year segment numbers were missing because the business 'was part of the consolidated ABFRL', while net debt had risen ~INR 200 crores on festive and Bangladesh-related inventory build. On Feb 3, 2026 (Q3 FY26) the logic was restated most explicitly and tested — Ambit's Videesha Sheth challenged the INR 500 crore NCD board approval against the no-fundraise promise, management explained the demerger-allocated borrowings and pure refinancing, and Dikshit tied slower deleveraging directly to the demerger's purpose (capex INR 320–330 crores vs INR 150–225 crores historically), while guiding emerging brands to one-fourth of the company in 4–5 years. By May 8, 2026 (Q4 FY26) the narrative shifted from rationale to proof: 'a strong start to being an independent entity', 300+ stores added, net debt down to INR 726 crores, and the first dividend (50 paise) with a 15–25% payout framework, debt-free in three years but explicitly 'not something that we are chasing'.

**What management expects from it:** ABLBL: its own ~INR 900cr EBITDA cash reinvested in growth — FY26 capex INR 320–330cr, 300+ new stores, Lifestyle early-double-digit growth with gradual margin expansion, emerging brands 18–20%+ reaching one-fourth of revenue in 4–5 years; net debt INR 726cr falling INR 200–300cr yearly toward zero in three years; dividends 15–25% of PAT. Only ABFRL's retained 'tomorrow' businesses raise capital.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *CALL Feb 2026* — Dikshit states the core demerger rationale outright — creating an entity that can reinvest its own cash flow aggressively into growth — and cites ~INR 900 crores of EBITDA cash split between working capital and capex. “One of the primary reasons for demerger was to create an entity which can reinvest back more aggressively into growth.”
- *CALL Aug 2025* — Answering Niharika Karnani on use of cash, Dikshit says the branded business's cash was previously consumed by ABFRL's new-business acquisitions, and the demerger's purpose was to keep that cash for this business's growth. “The cash generated by this business in the past has -- was used to actually kick start or acquire multiple new businesses. And the whole purpose of demerger was actually to need the cash for this business to grow faster.”
- *CALL Aug 2025* — Capital allocation priority post-demerger is explicitly growth capex (especially retail) ahead of deleveraging, with INR 200–300 crores of annual debt reduction and debt-free status in 2.5–3 years. “Only the subsequent part will go towards debt reduction.”
- *CALL Feb 2026* — The demerger's reinvestment logic is quantified: capex rose from a historical INR 150–225 crores to INR 320–330 crores in FY26, which management says is exactly why net debt fell little that year. “This year, our capex will be north of INR300 crores , perhaps INR320 crores , INR330 crores . And that's really why the debt reduction is not very large this year.”
- *CALL Feb 2026* — Debt was allocated to ABLBL at demerger by formula; the INR 500 crores of NCDs approved by the board in Feb 2026 were only to refinance debentures repaid in January, not new money — answering Ambit's challenge to the no-fundraise promise made for both entities except the 'tomorrow' business. “at the time of demerger, the company got the borrowings transferred based on the allocation formula. The INR500 crores debentures which we repaid recently in the month of January, we intend to raise it and to refinance the existing, the debentures repaid. There is no fresh borrowin g.”
- *CALL May 2026* — Management frames the standalone cash flow case as proven: a maiden 50 paise dividend in the first year post-demerger, a 15–25% of net profit payout range, and debt-free capability in about three years though not chased. “As you know, we had announced at the time of formation of company that looking at the predictable, consistent, historical cash flows of the company, we are very confident that this company over a period of time will become a debt-free company and equally will be able to pay dividends as it goes forward.”
- *CALL May 2026* — First full year as a separate company is presented as validation: 300+ store additions to 3,348 stores / 4.9 million sq ft across ~800 towns, revenue INR 8,396 crores (+7%), EBITDA INR 1,429 crores (17%, +90bps), net debt INR 726 crores vs INR 781 crores. “The year marked a strong start to being an independent entity supported by encouraging business momentum and several positive operating milestones across brands and channels.”
- *CALL Feb 2026* — The separated portfolio's growth is to be re-weighted toward the emerging brands (Reebok, Van Heusen Innerwear, American Eagle), targeted at a quarter of the company within four to five years, versus early-double-digit Lifestyle Brands. “This portfolio is expected to be one-fourth of overall ABLBL business in next 4 -5 years.”
- *CALL Aug 2025* — Differential growth rates by entity sub-portfolio were set at the post-demerger analyst meet: newer businesses 18–20% (elsewhere 'in excess of 20%') against Lifestyle Brands in early double digits, with capex ~80%+ going to Lifestyle expansion and renovation. “We expect the newer business to grow anything between 18 % to 20 %, while Lifestyle Brands business will grow in early double digits.”
- *CALL Nov 2025* — A cost of the split surfaced: analysts could not get comparable prior-year segment data because the business had been reported inside consolidated ABFRL, and reporting definitions had changed. “Yes, Yes, Devanshu, you know, it was part of the consolidated ABFRL, so we are splitting up, but, you know, we'll provide you separately.”
- *Scheme* — The Scheme of Arrangement demerged the Madura Fashion and Lifestyle business from ABFRL into ABLBL on a going-concern basis for shares, so shareholders hold identical stakes in both entities; effective May 1, 2025, 1,22,02,94,773 shares allotted May 26, 2025, listed June 23, 2025. “The Scheme provided for demerger, transfer, and vesting of the MFL Business from the Demerged Company to the Resulting Company on a going concern basis, with the Resulting Company issuing equity shares to the equity shareholders of the Demerged Company as a consideration.”
- *Scheme* — Legacy liabilities of the demerged business still follow ABLBL: multiple GST orders issued in the name of ABFRL in March 2026 (including a INR 310.13 crore demand) relate to the business demerged effective May 1, 2025 and are being appealed. “Order is in the name of Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limited (ABFRL). However, it relates to the business of the Company, which got demerged from ABFRL, pursuant to a Scheme of Arrangement effective from May 1, 2025.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No one is named as asking for it — no investor, lender or brand partner; no debt-allocation formula, no ABFRL-side rationale, no valuation re-rating or dis-synergy/separation-cost estimate.

## CELLO — Cello World Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 3.6/10 · spin-off · 10 filing(s) from BSE-screener, CALLS, NSE, NSE-BM · first 2025-12-09, latest 2026-09-17

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'meetings' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**The stages, as filed:** announced (2026-02-14) → meetings (2025-12-09)

**Stated in the filings:** appointed date 2025-04-01; size hint: 5.1% of ebitda.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Wim Plast's manufacturing business (moulded furniture, allied products) demerged into Cello Consumer Products, a wholly owned CWL subsidiary — class `regulatory_strategic`.

- *Insiders:* Promoter and Promoter Group held 165,662,977 of 220,885,034 shares (~75%), voting 100% in favour; demerged undertaking sits in CCPPL, wholly owned by CWL, so no separate promoter stake; promoter entity CPIW holds the Cello brand
- *What it reveals:* No new listing — furniture manufacturing folds into a wholly owned subsidiary. It isolates the weaker piece (Moulded Furniture FY26 revenue Rs 349 crore, -5%, gross margin 39.5% vs 47.8% elsewhere) inside a near debt-free parent (debt-equity 0.01) holding roughly Rs 724 crore cash and investments
- *Selling pressure:* likely — Only 46,53,239 CWL shares (~2% of equity) issued to ex-WPL holders; WPL dissolved without winding up; different segment
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* June 09, 2026 (Record Date fixed for determining WPL shareholders to whom CWL shares are allotted)
- *Read next:* The Composite Scheme itself with KPMG's share entitlement ratio report, and WPL's assets/liabilities transferred to CCPPL
- *In their words:* “The Composite Scheme of Arrangement amongst Wim Plast Limited ("WPL"), Cello Consumer Products Private Limited ("CCPPL") and the Company has been sanctioned by the Hon'ble NCLT, Ahmedabad Bench vide order dated May 14, 2026.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Strictly read, Cello World is not spinning a business out to create value — it is collapsing a second listing, and the only 'separation' is a carve-out inside the group. The Composite Scheme of Arrangement (board-approved 12 Nov 2024) among Wim Plast Limited (WPL, the 55%-owned separately listed moulded-furniture/plastics maker — plastic moulded furniture, extrusion sheets, air coolers, dustbins, industrial pallets, industrial and engineering moulds, plus an investment book), Cello Consumer Products Private Limited (CCPPL, a wholly owned CWL subsidiary) and Cello World Limited does two things: WPL's Manufacturing Business (the 'Demerged Undertaking') is demerged and vested in CCPPL on a going-concern basis, and WPL's Remaining Business is amalgamated into CWL, after which WPL 'stands dissolved without winding up.' Management's stated reasons were blunt and structural, not margin-driven: Gaurav Rathod said on 13 Nov 2024 there were 'two rationales' — 'we do not see any point in running 2 separate listed entities as the business is not very different,' and WPL 'has a lot of manufacturing facilities… in different parts of the country wherein we can share manufacturing facilities with our other plastic product lines' — adding that it 'reduces our compliance while having it under Cello World,' and that since CWL already owned about 55% of WPL, 'it's only about 45% that is being acquired.' The scheme petition filed at NCLT lists three benefits: synergy of operations and economies of scale with 'the legal and regulatory compliances of both the listed entities… unified and streamlined'; 'consolidation of ownership interests in one listed company instead of two listed entities'; and a 'unified approach on customer engagement, distribution and supply chain management.' The numbers cited: a 0.86 aggregate swap (55 CWL shares of ₹5 per 100 WPL shares of ₹10 for the demerger plus 31 per 100 for the amalgamation), 46,53,239 new CWL shares (29,75,909 + 16,77,330), authorised capital reclassified to ₹140 crore / 28 crore shares, appointed date 1 April 2025, FY26 moulded furniture revenue ₹349 crore (−5% YoY; Q4 FY26 ₹91.5 crore, −13.5%) on ~39.5–40.9% gross margin with '62% of the cost of moulded furniture is actually polymer,' and the ₹100 crore WimPlast-to-CWL loan already repaid out of the ₹738 crore QIP. Pressure came from investors, not lenders or partners: Jay Doshi (14 Aug 2024) flagged merger enablement as a QIP objective, Aniket Kulkarni noted 'in the last couple of calls, I think we had spoken about the possibility of merging WimPlast,' Deepesh Sancheti asked the rationale twice, and Ashok Shah (13 Aug 2025) challenged whether the ratio was fair to WimPlast's 40–45% minority (CFO Atul Parolia: 'it will be beneficial to all'); the gating parties were SEBI/BSE/NSE (NOCs 2–3 July 2025), the shareholders and creditors (approved 6 Dec 2025, 201,355,406 shares for vs 17 against), and NCLT Ahmedabad (sanctioned 14 May 2026). Notably, management explicitly refused the opposite idea — when asked on 13 Nov 2024 whether the three verticals should be listed separately to enhance shareholder value, Rathod said no, 'otherwise, we would have not merged this back into Cello World,' because 'our furniture is very, very similar to our other plastic manufactured products.'

**How it evolved:** It surfaced first as an unresolved management wish on the 14 Aug 2024 call, framed as a QIP enabler and contingent on 'both the boards' — and the ₹100 crore WimPlast loan to CWL was repaid from QIP proceeds to clear the way. On the 13 Nov 2024 call the board had just approved the draft scheme and Rathod articulated the full two-part rationale (no point in two listed entities; shared plastic manufacturing capacity; lower compliance; only ~45% actually being acquired), while simultaneously rejecting an investor's suggestion to demerge the three verticals into separate listings. It then went quiet through the Feb 2025, May 2025 and Nov 2025 calls, resurfacing on 13 Aug 2025 when Parolia disclosed the 0.86 swap ratio already filed with the exchanges and Rathod said the needed SEBI permissions had come and 'now we are in the phase of merging'; on 16 Feb 2026 Parolia put the NCLT final hearing in the last week of February and completion within '2, 3 months' off the 1 April 2025 appointed date. By the 29 May 2026 call it was done — effective 27 May 2026, comparatives restated, and the forward-looking claim narrowed to 'the synergies between consumerware and moulded furniture can be explored further.'

**What management expects from it:** For Cello World: one listed entity, unified and streamlined compliance for both, consolidated ownership, economies of scale, shared multi-location plastic manufacturing, a unified customer/distribution/supply-chain approach, and newly explorable consumerware–moulded-furniture synergies. For the furniture business inside CCPPL: no revenue re-rating — low single-digit growth, EBIT lifted only by premiumisation and outdoor furniture. No margin, capital-release or valuation target was quantified.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Aug 2024* — Asked by Jay Doshi whether the QIP was partly to enable a WimPlast consolidation, Rathod confirmed management wanted the merger but had not yet obtained board decisions — it was still an intention, not a plan. “In terms of WimPlast ideally, of course, from a management perspective we would like both of them to be merged and once it is decided by both the boards, I think we'll be able to go ahead on that as well.”
- *[Nov 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=c77bdd03-cfc6-4d5e-b8b4-dceed9acc301.pdf)* — With the board having just approved the draft scheme, Rathod gave the two core reasons: a second listed entity made no sense given overlapping businesses, and WimPlast's multi-location plants could be shared with Cello's other plastic lines. “So, I think, we previously mentioned this as well, there are 2 rationales, one is that there is - we do not see any point in running 2 separate listed entities as the business is not very different.”
- *[Nov 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=c77bdd03-cfc6-4d5e-b8b4-dceed9acc301.pdf)* — Re-asked by Aniket Kulkarni, Rathod added compliance reduction and sized the transaction: CWL already held ~55% of WimPlast, so only the ~45% minority was being acquired, and WimPlast's spare manufacturing locations could serve other plastic product lines. “Already because Cello World owns about 55% of the company in any case. So it's only about 45% that is being acquired.”
- *[Nov 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=c77bdd03-cfc6-4d5e-b8b4-dceed9acc301.pdf)* — Deepesh Sancheti proposed the reverse — demerging plastics, pens and glassware/consumerware into three separate listings — and Rathod rejected it outright as inconsistent with the WimPlast merger, citing manufacturing synergy between furniture and other moulded plastics. “No, I think - I don't think we are looking at that because otherwise, we would have not merged this back into Cello World.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=a18f5f35-d53b-419d-8f9c-1c166ffda34d.pdf)* — Pressed by Ashok Shah on whether the ratio disadvantaged WimPlast's minority holders versus Cello World's financials, Parolia disclosed the already-filed swap ratio of 0.86 and asserted the deal was beneficial to all; Rathod said the required SEBI permissions had come through. “It's there already in the exchange. It's 0.86.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=a18f5f35-d53b-419d-8f9c-1c166ffda34d.pdf)* — Rathod characterised the transaction as procedurally simple rather than structurally complex, with the only real hurdle being regulatory clearance, which had been received. “It's not a complicated merger. It is just -- we needed some permissions from SEBI. And I think that's already come and now we are in the phase of merging.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ed77a542-fbbd-418e-8d9f-d5f3c07eedeb.pdf)* — Parolia gave the completion timeline — NCLT final hearing in the last week of February, roughly two to three months to close, with effect from the 1 April 2025 appointed date; Rathod confirmed Q1 FY27 completion. “See, in the month of Feb only final hearing is there -- is around last week of Feb. And thereafter, once we get the approval, then everything is set, then we will be in the process of merging the thing.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ed77a542-fbbd-418e-8d9f-d5f3c07eedeb.pdf)* — Asked by Aniruddha whether all subsidiaries should likewise be merged for seamless capital flow and single billing, Rathod declined — the multi-subsidiary structure is deliberately kept to preserve unit-level P&L discipline, so the WimPlast merger was about removing a listing, not collapsing legal entities. “So overall, while things can get easier, it also kind of dilutes the P&L of each and every unit and focus on unit economics kind of goes away.”
- *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=42de0942-a266-4ad3-80e5-708476185d0f.pdf)* — Rathod confirmed completion and stated the only forward-looking benefit in explicit terms — exploring synergies between consumerware and moulded furniture — in the same quarter moulded furniture revenue fell 13.5% YoY to ₹91.5 crore. “We have completed the merger of Wimplast Limited with Cello World. With this integration, the synergies between consumerware and moulded furniture can be explored further.”
- *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=42de0942-a266-4ad3-80e5-708476185d0f.pdf)* — Parolia closed the loop on accounting: the scheme became effective 27 May 2026 with a 1 April 2025 appointed date, forcing restatement of comparatives and a consequential EPS impact for shares pending issuance. “Lastly, I would like to inform that composite scheme of arrangement among Wimplast, Cello Consumer Products Limited and the company has become effective from 27th May 2026, with an appointed date of 1st April 2025 as defined under the scheme.”
- *Scheme* — The scheme's two legs: WimPlast's Manufacturing Business (the Demerged Undertaking) is demerged into CCPPL, a wholly owned CWL subsidiary, on a going-concern basis, with CWL — not CCPPL — issuing the consideration shares to WimPlast's non-CWL shareholders. “the demerger, transfer and vesting of the Demerged Undertaking (as defined in the scheme) from WPL into CCPL on a going concern basis, and issue of equity shares by CWL to the shareholders of WPL (other than the shares held by CWL), in consideration there of”
- *Scheme* — The NCLT petition states three benefits — scale/synergy with unified compliance across the two listed entities, consolidation of ownership into one listed company, and a single approach to customers, distribution and supply chain. “Bring about synergy of operations and economies of scale and additionally the legal and regulatory compliances of both the listed entities will be unified and streamlined;”

*Not explained on the calls:* No quantified synergies, cost savings or EPS accretion; no reason manufacturing went to CCPPL rather than CWL; no valuation basis for 55:31; no tax or minority-exit detail.

## STAR — Strides Pharma Science Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **SPINNING — record date set; the new entity lists soon** · score 3.6/10 · spin-off · 4 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-05-20, latest 2026-06-27

> **Listing:** RECORD DATE set; the resulting company not yet listed — resulting companies have typically listed 4–10 weeks after the record date

**The stages, as filed:** nclt_sanction (2026-05-20) → effective (2026-06-01)

**Stated in the filings:** demerged undertaking: of Arco Lab Private Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary of Strides Pharma Science Limited.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Arco Lab's Life Sciences business and Digital Innovation business — its tech-enabled life sciences services platform — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* Promoter stake in Pivot Path not stated. Post-transaction capital structure: Strides 19.95%, Investors 65.05%, ESOP Pool 15%; Pivot Path reclassified as an Associate Company.
- *What it reveals:* A profitable platform buried in the GCC: FY26 revenue Rs. 1,447 million (3% of Strides turnover) and EBITDA Rs. 169 million, yet valued ~Rs. 2,300 million post-money; Strides realises ~Rs. 1,000 million plus a retained ~20% stake.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — Pivot Path shares were allotted to Strides, not to Strides' shareholders, then majority sold to a private equity consortium; no listing mentioned.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Q1 FY27 results: gain on the Rs. 1,000 million stake sale and Pivot Path's associate accounting
- *In their words:* “The Scheme provides for the demerger of Arco Lab's Life Sciences business and Digital Innovation business (the "Demerged Undertaking") into Pivot Path, pursuant to Sections 230–232 of the Companies Act, 2013 and other applicable provisions of the Act and the Rules framed thereunder ("Scheme").”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The business being separated is not a pharma business at all: it is the Life Sciences business and the Digital Innovation business of Arco Lab Private Limited, Strides' wholly owned Global Capability Centre (GCC), carved out into a new wholly owned subsidiary, Pivot Path Private Limited, under a Sections 230–232 Scheme of Arrangement, and then majority-sold. Management's stated reason is that this unit — built inside Arco Lab across life sciences consulting, digital transformation, quality and compliance, and technology-enabled operational services — outgrew its captive role: 'As demand from external pharmaceutical and life sciences companies grew, the business evolved into an independent platform serving industry-leading customers.' The filings name four problems the separation solves: supporting its next phase of growth, serving global customers effectively, building agentic-AI platforms, and enabling access to external capital — none of which a cost-centre inside a pharma manufacturer can fund or staff. The numbers cited are modest and explain why it is not core to Strides: FY26 revenue of ₹1,447 million (including revenues for services rendered to Strides) — just 3% of Strides' turnover — with EBITDA of ₹169 million, net worth of ₹100 million standalone (0.3% of Strides' net worth) and ₹360 million consolidated (1%). Ascent Capital (through Ascent Growth Trust) with co-investor Vintage Classic Limited values Pivot Path at ~₹2,300 million post-money; Strides realises ~₹1,000 million (₹750 million at closing, ₹250 million on the first anniversary), keeps 19.95%, and Ascent injects ₹500 million of primary capital, leaving Investors 65.05% and a 15% ESOP pool, with Pivot Path reclassified as an Associate. Badree Komandur frames it as Strides' repeatable playbook — 'Strides' proven capability to identify, incubate and scale high-potential businesses' — that 'unlocks value for Strides, provides Pivot Path with the resources to scale independently, and allows Strides to retain meaningful participation in its future success,' while also 'strengthens the Company's balance sheet.' No investor, lender or partner is named as having demanded the separation; the pull came from external life-sciences customers and from the incoming financial investor, whose rationale (per Raja Kumar) is to pair 400+ subject matter experts with technology and agentic AI in 'core, non-discretionary segments of the pharmaceutical industry.' Pricing rests on an independent valuation by a SEBI-registered merchant banker, and the deal is declared not a related party transaction and outside Regulation 37A.

**How it evolved:** The idea does not appear in a single one of the thirteen earnings calls; it exists only in the filings, which reference an intimation of May 15, 2025 for the Arco Lab–Pivot Path scheme, with an Appointed Date of April 10, 2025 — i.e. the carve-out was in motion for more than a year unmentioned. NCLT Bengaluru pronounced approval on May 18, 2026 (the same day as the Q4 FY26 board meeting whose call, on May 18, 2026, discussed only US/ex-US growth, margins and deleveraging), the order hit the NCLT portal May 20, 2026, the certified copy arrived May 25, 2026, and the Scheme became effective June 1, 2026. Only on June 27, 2026 did the plan's second leg surface: the board approved selling a majority stake to the Ascent Capital consortium, converting what the Scheme had set up as a wholly owned subsidiary into a ~20%-held Associate. The nearest the calls come is context on the earlier OneSource/softgel playbook — Arco Lab named as the wholly owned subsidiary parking the OneSource stake (May 22, 2025 call) and the ₹78.8 billion returned to shareholders via that demerger and listing (July 29, 2025 call).

**What management expects from it:** For Pivot Path: ₹500m primary capital, resources to scale independently, serve global customers, build agentic-AI platforms, access external capital and Ascent's expertise, plus a 15% ESOP pool. For Strides: ~₹1,000m realised (₹750m at closing, ₹250m at one year), a strengthened balance sheet, and a ~20% associate stake retaining upside. No margin, focus or re-rating claims are made.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The separated business is Arco Lab's Life Sciences business plus its Digital Innovation business, demerged into Pivot Path under Sections 230–232, with Appointed Date April 10, 2025 and NCLT approval pronounced May 18, 2026. “The Scheme provides for the demerger of Arco Lab’s Life Sciences business and Digital Innovation business (the “Demerged Undertaking”) into Pivot Path, pursuant to Sections 230–232 of the Companies Act, 2013 and other applicable provisions of the Act and the Rules framed thereunder (“Scheme”).”
- *Scheme* — The stated purpose of the carve-out is growth capacity, global customer service, agentic-AI platform building and access to outside capital — things it could not do as a captive GCC unit. “To support its next phase of growth, serve global customers effectively, build agentic-AI platforms, and enable access to external capital, the business was carved out into Pivot Path pursuant to a Scheme of Arrangement approved by the Hon'ble National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) in May 2026.”
- *Scheme* — The trigger was external demand: a unit originally serving Strides internally began winning third-party pharma and life-sciences customers and became a standalone platform. “As demand from external pharmaceutical and life sciences companies grew, the business evolved into an independent platform serving industry-leading customers.”
- *Scheme* — Strides positions it as a repeatable incubate-and-unlock model rather than a disposal of a problem asset, keeping economic participation. “The transaction reflects Strides' strategy of creating, scaling and unlocking value from high-potential businesses while retaining participation in their future growth.”
- *Scheme* — Scale cited: FY26 revenue ₹1,447 million (3% of Strides' turnover) and EBITDA ₹169 million; net worth ₹100 million standalone (0.3%) and ₹360 million consolidated (1%) — small enough that it is clearly non-core. “For FY26, the carved-out business reported revenue of ₹1,447 million (including revenues for services rendered to Strides) and EBITDA of ₹169 million, demonstrating its operating scale and growth trajectory.”
- *Scheme* — Economics: ~₹2,300m post-money valuation, ~₹1,000m realised by Strides (₹750m at closing, ₹250m after one year), ₹500m primary infusion by Ascent, Strides left at 19.95% with Investors 65.05% and a 15% ESOP pool. “The transaction values Pivot Path at ~₹2,300m on a post-money basis, enables Strides to realise ~₹1,000m while retaining a ~20% stake, and includes a primary capital infusion of ₹500 million to accelerate Pivot Path's next phase of growth.”
- *Scheme* — Badree Komandur's framing of the three-way benefit — cash and balance-sheet strength for Strides, independent scaling resources for Pivot Path, retained upside. “This transaction unlocks value for Strides, provides Pivot Path with the resources to scale independently, and allows Strides to retain meaningful participation in its future success.”
- *Scheme* — Accounting consequence: Pivot Path drops out of consolidation and becomes an Associate; the deal is declared non-related-party, priced off an independent SEBI-registered merchant banker valuation. “Upon completion of the transaction, Pivot Path shall be reclassified as an Associate Company.”
- *Scheme* — The incoming investor's rationale: 400+ subject matter experts applying technology and agentic AI to compliance, digital transformation and drug safety in non-discretionary pharma spend. “Pivot Path brings deep domain expertise across the core, non-discretionary segments of the pharmaceutical industry, capabilities that have been rigorously honed within the Strides stable.”
- *CALL May 2026* — The Q4 FY26 call, held May 18, 2026 — the very day NCLT pronounced the Pivot Path order — never mentions Pivot Path, Arco Lab or any carve-out; the three-year strategy is described purely in pharma terms. “Over the last 3 years, we have been very clear on our priorities, geographical diversification, profitability and balance sheet strength.”
- *CALL Aug 2025* — The only call-level support for the value-unlocking logic is the OneSource precedent, cited as the company's demonstrated way of returning value to shareholders. “And the recent one being we distributed INR 78.8 billion back to shareholders in the form of demerger and listing.”
- *CALL May 2025* — Arco Lab — the entity Pivot Path was later carved out of — is discussed on the calls only as the wholly owned subsidiary holding the residual 1.6% OneSource stake, with no hint of a services business inside it. “So we retained this in Arco Lab, which is a wholly owned subsidiary of Strides.”

*Not explained on the calls:* Calls never mention Pivot Path or Arco Lab's demerger. No use of proceeds, no reason for selling majority rather than listing, no customer, employee or related-party-pricing detail.

## TRIVENI — Triveni Engineering & Industries Ltd.

**CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **LISTED <1Y — selling-pressure window; the bargain forms here** · score 3.6/10 · spin-off · 38 filing(s) from BSE-screener, CALLS, NSE, NSE-register · first 2025-12-07, latest 2026-10-09

> **Listing:** LISTED — Triveni Power Transmission Limited trades since about 2026-10-09

**The stages, as filed:** announced (2026-09-16) → exchange_noc (2026-06-04) → meetings (2025-12-07) → nclt_sanction (2026-05-19) → effective (2026-05-07) → record_date (2026-01-30) → listed (2026-10-09)

**Stated in the filings:** resulting company **Triveni Power Transmission Limited**; entitlement **100 for every 137**; appointed date 2026-04-01.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** The Power Transmission Business: high-speed and niche low-speed gearboxes, defence products, aftermarket and retro-fitment services — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* Tarun Sawhney (promoter) appointed TPTL Vice Chairman & Managing Director for five years; Dhruv M. Sawhney non-executive Chairman; Nikhil Sawhney director. 3.13 crore shares locked in to Oct 2027/2029; stake % not stated.
- *What it reveals:* A ~35-36% PBIT-margin global gearbox and defence business buried inside a sugar company: only 4.45% of turnover yet 13.40% of cost-of-acquisition allocation, order book just under ₹500 crore (up 25%), ₹340 crore capex enabling about ₹700 crore output.
- *Selling pressure:* likely — Small spin (13.4% of cost allocation), 1-for-3 entitlement, engineering/defence shares handed to sugar-commodity holders; 7.35 crore of 10.48 crore shares free.
- *Parent or spin:* spin · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* TPTL's first standalone quarterly results and order book after the ₹340 crore capex completes in September 2026.
- *In their words:* “As power transmission migrates into Triveni Power Transmission Limited, the company is armed with sufficient cash flows and a balance sheet to be able to incur all of this CapEx and OpEx and more.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Triveni Engineering & Industries (TEIL) is carving out its Power Transmission Business (PTB) — the Mysuru high-speed/turbo gearbox and incubating defence-products business — into Triveni Power Transmission Ltd (TPTL), a then-wholly-owned subsidiary, via a composite scheme that also amalgamates the 61.77%-owned listed subsidiary Sir Shadi Lal Enterprises (SSEL) into TEIL; management's stated purpose, repeated almost verbatim across calls, is 'value unlocking' and later 'to unlock value and to drive operational efficiencies'. The implicit problem is the conglomerate mix: PTB is the one segment with predictable, high-quality economics (FY25 turnover +27%, PBIT ₹126.8 crore, +18.4%, PBIT margin >34%; H1 FY26 PBIT ~36%, one quarter at 41%; Suresh Taneja in Jun 2026: 'we have been maintaining about 35% PBIT'), while sugar and distillery are price- and policy-regulated commodity businesses whose margins collapsed in FY25 on a 69 bps gross-recovery fall, red rot/pest damage, ₹300/MT UP cane-price increases and frozen ethanol prices — exactly the asymmetry investor Bharat Shah (ASK) pressed management on in Feb 2025. Separation also funds and showcases PTB's own growth programme: board-approved capex in three tranches totalling ₹340 crore (₹231 crore spent to 31 Mar 2026, of which ₹78 crore on the defence facility), lifting gears capacity from ~₹400 crore to ~₹700 crore of output by September 2026, against a global high-speed/turbo gear market management sized at '$650-$700-odd million', a Swiss subsidiary (Triveni Power Transmission GmbH, bought by TPTL in FY26), AVL qualifications with global OEMs, and exports targeted at 'more than half' of original-equipment sales; Tarun Sawhney said TPTL is 'armed with sufficient cash flows and a balance sheet to be able to incur all of this CapEx and OpEx and more'. Crucially, TEIL deliberately retains ~30% of TPTL rather than a clean split — investor Resham Jain (DSP) challenged this as re-importing a holdco discount — because, per Sawhney, the defence business is being incubated and 'in establishing pre-qualifications (PQs) and the ability to be able to quote, there are balance sheet considerations that even from a Group perspective that are very, very important', plus the view that the earlier Triveni Turbine separation 'was actually quite a positive one'. Preparation was operational as well as legal: systems, CRM, SAP HANA/ERP migration, digital-twin and smart-factory work so TPTL could 'hit the ground sprinting' as a standalone, with separate board meetings and separate earnings calls promised for TEIL and TPTL from Q1 FY27. The scheme was approved by shareholders/creditors in December 2025, sanctioned by NCLT Allahabad (orders 7 and 18 May 2026), effective 19 May 2026, with scheme appointed date 1 April 2025 and demerger appointed date 1 April 2026; shareholders receive 1 TPTL share of ₹2 for every 3 TEIL shares of ₹1, and ICRA reaffirmed TEIL at AA+ Stable, 'lifting it from its previous under watch status'. Water/wastewater, sugar, distillery and IMIL/IMFL stay with TEIL, which keeps the residual cash flows the board said it would run workshops on to evaluate deployment options.

**How it evolved:** The composite scheme was approved by TEIL's board on 10 December 2024 and first discussed on the Feb 5, 2025 call, where Sawhney framed it purely as 'value unlocking', defended the ~30% retained stake on defence pre-qualification/balance-sheet grounds against Resham Jain's holdco-discount objection, and guided to NCLT approval 'by the end of this calendar year'. Through May 28, 2025 and Jul 30, 2025 the plan was unchanged but stuck at SEBI ('following up continuously with SEBI', possibly '+30-odd days'), with separation still expected in Q4 FY26/early CY2026, while Resham Jain asked for granular PTB disclosure 'given that this is going to get separately listed' and the board began workshops on what residual TEIL would do with its cash. By Nov 7, 2025 the stock exchanges had issued observation letters (BSE 7 Aug, NSE 11 Aug 2025), NCLT-convened stakeholder meetings were set for late November/early December, and TPTL had acquired the Swiss entity; on Feb 2, 2026 management added the second rationale — 'to unlock value and to drive operational efficiencies' — reported December 2025 shareholder/creditor approval, a February NCLT hearing, and said 'the next time we speak in all probability, this will be two separate companies'. On Jun 4, 2026 Sawhney confirmed NCLT approval (19 May 2026 effective date), the two record dates, restored AA+ rating and guided to TPTL listing 'by the end of August' with separate calls for both entities; in fact the demerger record date was 22 July 2026 and TPTL's 10,47,54,338 shares only began trading on BSE/NSE on 12 October 2026, with cost of acquisition split 86.60% TEIL / 13.40% TPTL.

**What management expects from it:** TPTL: independently listed, ~35% PBIT margins sustained, own cash flows funding the ₹340 crore capex to ~₹700 crore gears output plus the defence facility, exports above 50% of original equipment, global AVL access; TEIL's retained ~30% preserves defence pre-qualification credibility. TEIL: sugar, distillery, water retained, AA+ Stable restored, investable cash flows, separate results and calls for both.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=32ebf539-4c61-4455-9d21-3cc24a97dd7a.pdf)* — First call after the 10 December 2024 announcement; the scheme is presented as two linked steps — amalgamating the 61.77%-held listed subsidiary SSEL into TEIL and vesting the Power Transmission Business undertaking into wholly-owned Triveni Power Transmission Ltd — with value unlocking as the stated board motive. “I also wanted to provide an update on the Scheme, as you're all aware, this is in conjunction with value unlocking that the Board of Directors has felt very important.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=32ebf539-4c61-4455-9d21-3cc24a97dd7a.pdf)* — Resham Jain (DSP) objected that TEIL retaining ~30% of TPTL recreates the Triveni Turbines-style holdco discount and is not a clean value unlock — the clearest instance of an investor shaping the debate on structure. “It seems that Triveni Engineering will still be holding 30% stake even after demerger. So why such structure, if the value unlocking has to happen, it should have been a clean structure where Triveni would not be holding anything otherwise, the same Holdco discount will be applicable to the Power Transmission business once it gets demerged.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=32ebf539-4c61-4455-9d21-3cc24a97dd7a.pdf)* — Sawhney justified the retained stake on two grounds: the Triveni Turbines precedent was positive, and the co-located defence business needs group balance-sheet backing to win pre-qualifications and bid — i.e. a clean split would handicap defence. “The second and very, very important is because we are incubating a Defence business, which we have large aspirations for. In establishing pre-qualifications (PQs) and the ability to be able to quote, there are balance sheet considerations that even from a Group perspective that are very, very important to allow us to be in contention.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=32ebf539-4c61-4455-9d21-3cc24a97dd7a.pdf)* — Bharat Shah (ASK Investment Managers) framed the underlying investor problem the separation addresses: PTB is the one predictable, compounding business while the rest of the portfolio produces erratic outcomes, making long-term valuation of the whole impossible. “If you look at the composition of various businesses that we are in, barring the Power Transmission business, which is relatively more robust, predictable economics and predictable outcomes over a period of time, brick-by-brick being built.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=32ebf539-4c61-4455-9d21-3cc24a97dd7a.pdf)* — The same board meeting approved an incremental ₹60 crore capex to lift gears capacity from ~₹400 crore to ₹700 crore by September 2026, sized against a global high-speed/turbo gear market of roughly $650-700 million — the growth case the separate listing is meant to fund and surface. “The Board has confidence that we need ₹700 crore worth of capacity as we start off 2026-27.”
- *[Jun 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=24085d8d-b7bb-42bb-bd4f-8cb00e75ea19.pdf)* — PTB's FY25 numbers were the evidence for separate valuation: turnover +27%, PBIT ₹126.8 crore (+18.4%), PBIT margin above 34%, order booking over ₹475 crore and record Q4 revenue of almost ₹140 crore — growth without margin dilution. “And the PBIT grew by 18.4% to ₹126.8 crore with PBIT margins in excess of 34%, which is a very much in line with our long-term average.”
- *[Jun 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=24085d8d-b7bb-42bb-bd4f-8cb00e75ea19.pdf)* — Resham Jain asked for far more granular PTB disclosure — customers, industry mix — explicitly because it will be separately listed; management accepted, showing investor demand driving pre-separation transparency. “So I would request maybe if you can start giving more colour on the Power Transmission business from like what kind of customers you are targeting ?”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=a50ea3c4-1d70-4e28-a663-9393cce6158b.pdf)* — The plan was unchanged in substance but stalled at SEBI, with timing guided to Q1 of the next calendar year / Q4 FY26 and possible slippage of about 30 days; separately the board said it would run workshops on how residual TEIL would deploy its cash flows post-demerger. “We are still awaiting regulatory approvals. We're following up continuously with SEBI.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ec578aab-464f-47c2-8bc5-cb3982d61b3e.pdf)* — Stock-exchange approvals were in hand and the NCLT process had begun with stakeholder meetings scheduled for late November/early December 2025; in parallel TPTL acquired 100% of Triveni Power Transmission GmbH (Switzerland), building the export engine inside the entity being demerged. “The proposed scheme has been approved by the stock exchanges, and the process is obtaining approval of NCLT.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=2bc4c751-c2b8-4a3a-a75a-a00326d1ee32.pdf)* — Management for the first time stated both objectives together — unlocking value and driving operational efficiencies — and confirmed December 2025 shareholder/creditor approval with a further NCLT hearing in February 2026. “Lastly, with respect to the proposed scheme of amalgamation of SSEL and the demerger of the Power Transmission business to unlock value and to drive operational efficiencies, the scheme has been approved by shareholders of creditors, this was in December of 2025.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=2bc4c751-c2b8-4a3a-a75a-a00326d1ee32.pdf)* — Standalone readiness was being built deliberately — skills, systems, CRM, smart factory and SAP HANA migration — so TPTL could run as an independent company with TEIL-level efficiency from day one. “A lot of systems work is being done as we speak to let them hit the ground sprinting, frankly speaking, and have the same kind of efficiencies that we've had at Triveni Engineering and any of the other businesses that the company has run.”

# Probable spin-offs and listings

## POLYMED — Poly Medicure Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a scheme of arrangement whose nature the documents on file do not settle) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 6.7/10 · scheme (nature unclear) · 1 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-11-05, latest 2026-11-05

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**Stated in the filings:** size hint: 10% of revenue.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** not stated — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* not stated
- *What it reveals:* not stated
- *Selling pressure:* unclear — No demerger, resulting company, share-entitlement ratio or index change is described in the documents provided.
- *Parent or spin:* unclear · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Board outcome filing of November 05, 2026 meeting, and the updated Policy on Material Subsidiary on company website.
- *In their words:* “The Board of Directors of Poly Medicure Limited ("Company") in compliance with the provisions of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 ("SEBI Listing Regulations"), updated the policy for determining 'material' subsidiaries ("Policy") vide its Board meeting held on November 05, 2026.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

On the evidence supplied, Poly Medicure is not separating a business — nothing in the seven earnings/acquisition call transcripts or the one filing announces or discusses a demerger, spin-off, slump sale, hive-off or carve-out of any division, and no scheme of arrangement is on record. The structural direction management describes is the exact opposite: inbound acquisition and consolidation into one entity. In FY26 the company bought PendraCare (Netherlands, interventional cardiology guiding/diagnostic catheters; CY24 revenue €9.9m, EBITDA €1.4m, 74% gross margin; 90% stake for €11m equity plus €3.2m intra-group loans, ~1.8x EV/revenue and 13x EV/EBITDA, remaining 10% to be bought in 2030 off CY29 EBITDA), Citieffe (Bologna, Italy, trauma and extremities orthopaedics; CY24 revenue €17.3m, EBITDA €3.1m, ~90% gross margin; €18.8m equity plus €4.2m shareholder loan plus €8m debt = ~€31m EV, ~10x EBITDA) and Medyneo in Brazil (a shell with ANVISA and import licences, ~$40,000, bought to save 18–24 months of registration time). Himanshu Baid's framing on 25 May 2026 was explicitly integrative — 'in 1 or 2 years, we'll make these 3 businesses into a single global platform' — with cross-selling both ways, Indian R&D supporting Europe, some manufacturing eventually shifted to India, and subsidiary EBITDA guided from 12–14% to 18–20% over 2–3 years. The core Infusion Therapy business is being de-weighted in mix (65% historically, 57% of Q4 FY25, 50% of Q4 FY26, with Renal ~11%) but is expressly retained and used to fund the new verticals: 'this doesn't mean that we are not focusing on our core infusion business, which is generating significant profits, enabling us to invest into these new high-growth areas.' The only deliberate exit described is channel-level, not structural — shrinking government/tender business from ~10–12% of domestic revenue to a target 6–7% because of L1 pricing and state payment delays — and the only facility decision reversed was dropping the planned Jaipur plant in favour of land at YEIDA. The single filing (5 Nov 2026) is a routine board-approved refresh of five governance policies; 'demerger' appears in it only as a generic Schedule III disclosure category, not as a transaction. Financial context given: FY26 standalone revenue ₹1,662 crore (+4%), consolidated ₹1,875 crore (+12.3%), standalone EBITDA ₹446 crore at 26.8%, consolidated cash ₹842 crore, FY26 capex ₹296 crore, FY27 guidance ₹1,900–1,950 crore standalone and ₹2,300–2,400 crore consolidated; no part of that guidance is attributed to any separation.

**How it evolved:** Across the window the corporate-structure thread runs only one way — toward acquiring and absorbing. On 7 May 2025 management said only that it was on a 'constant lookout' for technology M&A and refused to name a vertical; on 8 Aug 2025 it added a wholly owned Brazil subsidiary and two CDMO contracts; the dedicated calls of 4 Sep 2025 (PendraCare) and 25 Sep 2025 (Citieffe) set out the two acquisitions, closed 23 Sep and 6 Nov 2025 respectively and reported in the 10 Nov 2025 call as adding ~₹280 crore of annualised revenue. By 6 Feb 2026 the language was integration and 'a fundamental upgrade of our business model' (not a split), and by 25 May 2026 it was explicit consolidation of three businesses into one platform plus the Medyneo bolt-on. At no point — including the 5 Nov 2026 filing — does any separation, demerger or divestment of a Polymed business appear.

**What management expects from it:** Nothing — no separation was proposed. The only structural expectations stated are for acquisitions: PendraCare and Citieffe moving from 12–14% to 18–20% EBITDA over 2–3 years, €3–4 million of group synergy EBITDA, Citieffe revenue doubling in five years, standalone EBITDA 25–27% versus consolidated 23–25%, and three businesses run as one global platform.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *CALL May 2026* — Management's stated structural intent is to merge, not separate: Polymed standalone plus PendraCare plus Citieffe are to be run as one global platform, with cross-selling, shared R&D and procurement synergies. “I think in 1 or 2 years, we'll make these 3 businesses into a single global platform for growth.”
- *CALL May 2026* — Despite Infusion Therapy falling from 57% of Q4 FY25 revenue to 50% in Q4 FY26, Baid insists it stays in-house at ~50% of mix, citing ~11% global IV-catheter share — i.e. no carve-out of the legacy business. “Again, that is our core, core, core business.”
- *CALL May 2026* — The acquired entities are to be margin-upgraded inside the group (12–14% EBITDA now, 18–20% in 2–3 years) through Indian engineering, global supply chain and partial manufacturing transfer — the opposite of separating them out. “All that will help us in the long run will help us to -- see, currently, these companies will operate, let's say, around 12% to 14% margin.”
- *CALL Mar 2026* — The 'transition' repeatedly described is a product/technology mix shift from low-tech to cardiology, critical care and orthopaedics — explicitly funded by the retained infusion business, not a legal separation of either part. “Having said that, this doesn't mean that we are not focusing on our core infusion business, which is generating significant profits, enabling us to invest into these new high-growth areas.”
- *CALL Mar 2026* — The only business management says it is deliberately exiting is the government/tender channel (~10–12% of domestic revenue, degrowth of 18% in Q3 FY26, target 6–7%) on price and receivables grounds — a channel de-emphasis, not a separation. “And deliberately, we are reducing our government business exposure as the prices are lower in government business.”
- *CALL Nov 2025* — The two European deals were presented as additive to the existing business, adding roughly ₹280 crore of annualised revenue, with integration already begun — no mention of any offsetting disposal. “With these two acquisitions, we will add around close to Rs. 280 crores of revenue to our existing business on an annual basis.”
- *CALL Oct 2025* — On the Citieffe call, the stated M&A doctrine is to stay inside medical devices and its adjacencies and to pause and absorb — Citieffe adds orthopaedics on top of cardiology, critical care and renal, with no suggestion of separating any vertical. “I think on the M&A strategy, which we have said in the past that we want to obviously stick to the medical devices and we'll stick to the adjacencies of the medical devices.”
- *CALL Oct 2025* — Even manufacturing is kept where it is: Rahul Gautam rejects moving Citieffe's Bologna production to India because customers value Made-in-Europe, limiting change to outsourcing parts of processes. “We have currently no such plans.”
- *CALL Sep 2025* — PendraCare was framed as a bolt-on platform to globalise Polymed's own cardiology products (DES clinical registry of 2,000 patients, EU/FDA approvals), targeting €3–4m of incremental group EBITDA synergies and ~€25m revenue by 2030. “This is very much part of our core strategy to grow into cardiology, something which we have been doing over the last 12 to 18 months.”
- *CALL May 2025* — At the start of the window the only structural plan disclosed was inorganic expansion funded by the Aug-2024 QIP cash (~₹1,100 crore liquidity, ~₹500 crore earmarked for organic capex); no divestment or demerger was contemplated. “Of course, we are looking at some new opportunities in M&A side and as soon as we finalize something, we will definitely get back to you with proper details.”
- *Scheme* — There is no scheme of arrangement in the record. The sole filing (5 Nov 2026) is a board-approved refresh of five governance policies; 'demerger' appears in it only inside the boilerplate Schedule III list of disclosable event categories. “Acquisition(s) (including agreement to acquire), Scheme of Arrangement (amalgamation/ merger/ demerger/restructuring), sale or disposal of any unit(s), division(s), whole or substantially the whole of the undertaking(s) or subsidiary of the listed entity, sale of stake in the associate company of the listed entity or any other restructuring.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No call or filing mentions a demerger, spin-off, slump sale or carve-out, so no rationale, perimeter, swap ratio, or investor/lender/partner demand for one is explained.

## INOXWIND — Inox Wind Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a filing's text names a demerger; no scheme filing names it yet) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 6.4/10 · spin-off · 12 filing(s) from CALLS, NSE · first 2025-11-14, latest 2026-02-13

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; indicated timeline: Nov 14, 2025: scheme "receives approval from shareholders and creditors", application filed with NCLT. Feb 13, 2026: "in the final stages of hearing at Hon'ble NCLT Ahmedabad; post receipt of approval from NCLT and merger of the assets, IRSL will be automatically listed on the stock exchanges"; on the Feb 13, 2026 call: "NCLT approval should come in a month or so" and "within 3-odd months, 2-3 months, it should get on the process". NCLT sanctioned March 12, 2026 (order dated 13 March 2026 per Aug 2026 notes); scheme effective May 04, 2026; May 29, 2026 call: "broadly in the next 1-2 months, it will get completed". No listing date confirmed in the filings through Aug 7, 2026

**Stated in the filings:** size hint: 20% of profit.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Power Evacuation / substation (evacuation infrastructure) business of subsidiary Inox Green Energy Services Limited, demerged into Inox Renewable Solutions — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* Inox Wind's IRSL holding 88.41%, "expected to reduced from 88.41% to 79.75%" post-scheme; it holds ~54.78% of Inox Green; promoter is Inox Leasing and Finance Limited; recent IRSL stake sales went to non-promoter third parties
- *What it reveals:* IRSL: revenue Rs 564.05 crore (12.83% of consolidated) and net worth Rs 897.77 crore (14.07%) in FY2025-26; ~0.86% stake sold for ~Rs 50 crore implies a value far above book; demerger removes Rs 1,000 crore gross block and Rs 50-55 crore depreciation from Inox Green
- *Selling pressure:* likely — Tiny entitlement — 122 IRSL shares per 1,000 Inox Green shares; automatic listing with no issue; EPC/evacuation infrastructure differs from O&M
- *Parent or spin:* both · *option pricing date:* 13th November, 2025 (ESOP grant at 50% discount to NSE close of Rs 148.56) and 12th February, 2026 (50% discount to Rs 109.32)
- *Read next:* IRSL standalone financials and the NCLT-sanctioned scheme; then the record date notice for the 122-per-1,000 share issue
- *In their words:* “Pursuant to the Scheme, 122 equity share in the Resulting company for every 1000 share held in the demerged company to be issued to the shareholders as on the record date.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The separation is the demerger of the power-evacuation / substation (common infrastructure) business out of Inox Wind's listed O&M subsidiary Inox Green Energy Services Ltd (IGESL, ~56% held by IWL, later diluted to 54.78%) and its merger into Inox Renewable Solutions Ltd (IRSL, formerly Resco Global Wind Services, ~88.84% held by IWL), IWL's EPC arm, after which IRSL is automatically listed and Inox Green's shareholders receive 122 IRSL shares for every 1,000 Inox Green shares. The problem management says it fixes: Inox Green's balance sheet carried roughly Rs 1,000 crore of gross block of substations/evacuation assets (84 substations pan-India) that produced only about Rs 10 crore of revenue but around Rs 50-55 crore of annual depreciation, depressing PBT, ROE and ROCE and burying the asset-light ~50%-EBITDA-margin O&M business. Post-demerger Inox Green has virtually no depreciation and negligible finance cost, so PBT equals EBITDA equals cash profit — FY27 EBITDA guided above Rs 600 crore, 'broadly everything' converting to operating cash profit, helped by a ~Rs 700 crore accumulated-loss tax shield. The infrastructure instead lands in IRSL, where the group's EPC capability, in-housed cranes, transformer manufacturing and multi-gigawatt project/land pipeline already sit, and whose value rose after the Sept-2025 CERC amendment allowing hybridisation of existing wind evacuation with solar above 50 MW — giving access to what Devansh Jain called almost 10 GW of plug-and-play infrastructure. Akhil Jindal framed the intent as shareholder choice: investors can hold the O&M business, the infrastructure business, or the whole value chain through Inox Wind, and he said no further corporate action is therefore needed (explicitly refusing to demerge Green or IRSL out of IWL). Value-unlocking is the other stated driver: IRSL raised Rs 175 crore in Sept 2025 at a valuation of ~Rs 7,400 crore, and IWL has since sold small IRSL stakes to group parties (91.90%→88.84% for Rs 173.5 crore; then →87.98% for ~Rs 50 crore). Investors and analysts (Vishal Singh, Pradyumna Choudhary, Hansal Thakker, Prit Nagersheth, Pradeep Motwani) repeatedly pressed on timing and on whether minority shareholders would see value unlocked; the scheme also required and received approval from equity shareholders, warrant holders and secured and unsecured creditors (1 Nov 2025) — no lender or partner demand was cited as the trigger.

**How it evolved:** IGESL's board approved the scheme on 13 Nov 2024; the earliest discussion in these transcripts is the Feb 2025 call (31 Jan 2025), where Manish Garg confirmed board approval and filing with NSE/BSE after an investor asked when 'the demerger of that EPC subsidiary' would happen. By the Sep 2025 call (1 Sep 2025) exchange no-objections were in, the scheme was filed at NCLT Ahmedabad with approval guided in 2-3 quarters, IRSL had raised Rs 175 crore at ~Rs 7,400 crore, and Akhil Jindal reframed the logic as giving shareholders a choice of which business to own while ruling out any further demerger out of IWL. On the Nov 2025 call (14 Nov 2025) shareholder and creditor approvals were announced and Devansh Jain said the demerger and IRSL listing would 'unlock substantial value'; on the Feb 2026 call (13 Feb 2026) it was in final NCLT hearings with the impact quantified (only ~Rs 10 crore revenue out, ~Rs 50 crore depreciation out, 84 substations to be merged). NCLT sanctioned it on 12 March 2026, effective 4 May 2026, and on the Jun 2026 call (29 May 2026) management confirmed the Rs 1,000 crore gross block and Rs 50-55 crore depreciation were eliminated, with listing 1-2 months away, while declining to give IRSL's financials until it is demerged.

**What management expects from it:** Inox Green: ~Rs 1,000 cr gross block and ~Rs 50-55 cr annual depreciation gone, higher PBT, sharply better ROE/ROCE, a pure-play ~50%-margin asset-light O&M business whose FY27 EBITDA (>Rs 600 cr) converts almost fully to cash. IRSL: a separately listed EPC/infrastructure arm of Inox Wind holding evacuation infra, cranes, transformers and hybridisation-ready plug-and-play sites. Both: substantial value unlocking.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=f109d78c-28df-4776-a2e4-c431980e8e1d.pdf)* — First disclosure in these calls: the IGESL board had approved demerging the substation business and the scheme was filed with NSE/BSE, to be followed by an NCLT filing; an investor had asked when the 'EPC subsidiary' demerger would happen. “So the Board approval for a demerger of the substation business from Inox Green has already been taken in the last Board meeting, the scheme has been filed with NSE and BSE, and we are waiting for their approval.”
- *[Sep 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=57f70e92-334e-4b9f-9c4d-c279fe985831.pdf)* — Akhil Jindal explained the mechanics — infrastructure and connectivity assets move out of Inox Green into Resco/IRSL, which then lists automatically, with Inox Green shareholders receiving IRSL shares. “Under that, there would have been an automatic listing of Resco. And to that extent, the shareholders of INOX Green would be getting the shares of INOX Resco also.”
- *[Sep 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=57f70e92-334e-4b9f-9c4d-c279fe985831.pdf)* — Asked whether IGESL and IRSL would later be demerged to IWL shareholders, Jindal said the point of separating these businesses was to let shareholders pick which business to own, so no further corporate action is needed. “As management, we have provided enough window for a shareholder to be present where he wants to be. And I think that was the intention of separating these businesses.”
- *[Sep 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=57f70e92-334e-4b9f-9c4d-c279fe985831.pdf)* — The balance-sheet rationale quantified: ~Rs 1,000 crore gross block leaves Inox Green and ~Rs 50-55 crore of annual depreciation is eliminated, lifting PBT and improving ROE/ROCE. “Once the scheme is approved by the NCLT, the gross block of around INR1,000 crores will be off our balance sheet and subsequently the depreciation of approximately INR50 crores to INR55 crores annually will be eliminated, thereby increasing the PBT by that amount.”
- *[Sep 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=57f70e92-334e-4b9f-9c4d-c279fe985831.pdf)* — IRSL was independently valued shortly before the demerger, and the CERC hybridisation amendment (allowing existing wind evacuation infra to be shared with solar above 50 MW) multiplied the value of the infrastructure being moved into it. “We have recently raised INR175 crores at Inox Renewable Solutions at a valuation of approximately INR7,400 crores.”
- *[Sep 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=57f70e92-334e-4b9f-9c4d-c279fe985831.pdf)* — Devansh Jain sized the infrastructure asset that IRSL will house post-hybridisation as near-unique in India. “I think it gives us access to almost 10 gigawatts of plug and play infrastructure across wind and solar , which is huge.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=4bbce864-7e06-41a8-86d0-000fe5504407.pdf)* — On receiving shareholder and creditor approvals, Sanjeev Agarwal set out the two-sided benefit: IRSL lists as Inox Wind's EPC arm, Inox Green sheds the depreciation on the demerged asset blocks. “This will add value for both Inox Wind, with subsequent listing of Inox Renewable solution as an EPC arm of Inox Wind, and Inox Green with elimination of depreciation on demergers of the asset blocks”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=4bbce864-7e06-41a8-86d0-000fe5504407.pdf)* — Devansh Jain stated the headline objective as value unlocking for both listed entities. “I believe that the de-merger and subsequent listing of Inox Renewable Solutions will unlock substantial value for both Inox Wind and Inox Green.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=86e8969e-f7a8-4e84-93bc-7fe21c4eba9c.pdf)* — Management quantified the asymmetry that makes the separation accretive for Inox Green: barely any revenue leaves, but the depreciation does. “So post the demerger, as we have clarified on the multiple cores, there would be a very limited amount of revenue in the range of INR 10 odd crore will get out of the balance sheet. And around INR 50 odd crores of depreciation will go out from the balance sheet.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=86e8969e-f7a8-4e84-93bc-7fe21c4eba9c.pdf)* — Mathusudhana described the scale of the infrastructure being consolidated — 84 substations pan-India — and claimed further unquantified synergy value plus a connectivity advantage no competitor has. “And like merging 84 substations across India, it will be a huge exercise. - *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=848794f9-ab25-4f1b-a5d9-6942bd67b0ff.pdf)* — Post-NCLT confirmation that the benefit has crystallised in Inox Green's accounts, with the residual step being administrative before IRSL's automatic listing (guided at 1-2 months). “With this gross block of approximately INR1,000 crores has been eliminated from Inox Green's balance sheet. - *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=848794f9-ab25-4f1b-a5d9-6942bd67b0ff.pdf)* — Devansh Jain placed the IRSL demerger in a sequence of value-creating separations, after the Inox Green spin-off, while shrugging off the share-price criticism from minority holders. “We've spun off Inox Green, which has created tremendous value.
