**The stages, as filed:** meetings (2026-08-25)

**Stated in the filings:** size hint: 12.6% of income.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Loads Business Undertaking transferred as going concern to wholly owned subsidiary BlackBuck Transport Services Private Limited on slump sale basis — class `regulatory_strategic`.

- *Insiders:* Buyer is a wholly owned subsidiary; "Buyer does not belong to the promoter/ promoter group"; no change in Company's shareholding pattern. Promoters Yabaji, Hridaya, Balasubramaniam sold 36,00,000 shares on 18.11.2025.
- *What it reveals:* Loads undertaking is only 12.6% of standalone total income and 0.07% of net worth (INR 9.88 million), moved at NAV/book value; calls show loads (superloads) still loss-making, investment-mode, while core payments/telematics fund it.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — No shares issued to shareholders; "There will be no change in the shareholding pattern of the Company pursuant to the slump sale".
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* The business transfer agreement (BTA) and the NAV-based lump sum cash consideration on the Closing Date.
- *In their words:* “There will be no change in the shareholding pattern of the Company pursuant to the slump sale of relevant business undertaking of the Company to its wholly owned subsidiary i.e., BTSPL.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The separation on record is the transfer of BlackBuck Ltd.'s Loads Business Undertaking — the freight-matching business comprising the classifieds load board and the full-stack 'Superloads' brokerage — as a going concern, on a slump-sale basis, to BlackBuck Transport Services Private Limited (BTSPL), a wholly owned subsidiary 'engaged in business of Transportation and Storage', approved by the Board on the Audit Committee's recommendation on October 12, 2026. The only rationale management put in writing is operational: 'Restructuring to organize its businesses under dedicated wholly owned subsidiary and improve operational efficiency.' The scale given is small and asset-light: FY26 revenue of the transferred undertaking was INR 887.43 million, 12.6% of the Company's standalone total income, while its net worth at March 31, 2026 was INR 9.88 million, just 0.07% of standalone net worth — so the lump-sum cash consideration, set at the Net Asset Value / book value on the closing date, is immaterial and the deal is a related-party transaction with its own subsidiary rather than a sale of value. It is deliberately structured outside a scheme of arrangement, via a Business Transfer Agreement, so Regulation 37A does not apply, there is no NCLT process, no share-exchange ratio, and 'no change in the shareholding pattern of the Company' — i.e. a ring-fencing of the business inside the group, not a demerger to shareholders. The earnings calls never mention the transfer, but they supply the operating logic the filing compresses: loads is the one vertical booked at gross value, forcing management to invent a 'net revenues' metric in Aug 2025; by Feb 2026 Rajesh Yabaji described core and growth as having 'literally no connection' with 'pretty independent' costs and called Superloads 'essentially a independent business which has basically its losses'; and it was the loss-making, 250-person, hub-by-hub expansion (Bangalore/Hyderabad to 9–14 cities, then 10 more) that was diluting consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin from ~36% to ~31%. It also follows the company's established pattern of parking distinct or regulated businesses in dedicated wholly owned subsidiaries — Blackbuck Finserve (NBFC; INR 140 crore of IPO proceeds plus a INR 100 crore rights issue in Dec 2025) and TZF Logistics (PPI licence from RBI, INR 21.99 crore rights issue in Sept 2026 partly to meet 'regulatory requirements applicable to PPI issuers') — with the dormant ZZ Logistics struck off in May 2026. Nothing in these texts shows any investor, lender or partner asking for the separation; investors asked only for segment-level disclosure, which management repeatedly deferred as 'too early'.

**How it evolved:** The loads business was described on May 27, 2025 as the pivot of classifieds into brokerage (five hubs, playbook-building, 6–8% take rate), and on Aug 5, 2025 it was first reported as a separate 'growth business' line whose gross-level accounting forced the new 'net revenues' metric. On Nov 5, 2025 management went 'aggressive' — four hubs to 14, team from ~50 to ~250 people — and on Feb 5, 2026 Yabaji explicitly framed core and growth as independent businesses with independent costs and independent investment decisions; on May 19, 2026 he conceded Superloads' pace 'could have been much stronger' and declined to split profitability, saying it was 'still too early'. The legal separation then appears with no prior signalling: the Board approved the slump sale of the Loads Business Undertaking to BTSPL on October 12, 2026, with the BTA still to be executed and closing subject to conditions precedent. No earnings call in the 36-month window discusses, previews or explains it.

**What management expects from it:** Only what the filing states: the loads business run inside a dedicated wholly owned subsidiary (BTSPL, Transportation and Storage), with businesses better organised and operational efficiency improved. Consideration is book-value cash, shareholding unchanged. No stated expectation for margins, capital, valuation, re-rating, fundraising or focus at either BlackBuck Ltd. or BTSPL level.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — Board, on Audit Committee recommendation, approved transferring the Loads Business Undertaking as a going concern to wholly owned subsidiary BlackBuck Transport Services Private Limited (BTSPL) on a slump-sale basis on October 12, 2026; the BTA is yet to be executed and closing is subject to conditions precedent. “the Board of Directors of BlackBuck Limited (Formerly known as Zinka Logistics Solutions Limited) ("Company"), at its meeting held today i.e. Monday, October 12, 2026, inter-alia, on recommendation of the Audit Committee, have considered and approved the transfer of Loads Business Undertaking ("Transferred Business Undertaking") as a going concern to BlackBuck Transport Services Private Limited, Wholly Owned Subsidiary ("BTSPL") on a slump sale basis.”
- *Scheme* — The entire stated rationale is one line: housing businesses in a dedicated wholly owned subsidiary and operational efficiency. No mention of margins, capital allocation, valuation, funding or partner/lender demands. “Restructuring to organize its businesses under dedicated wholly owned subsidiary and improve operational efficiency.”
- *Scheme* — Size of the carved-out business: FY26 revenue INR 887.43 million, 12.6% of standalone total income, but net worth of only INR 9.88 million, 0.07% of standalone net worth — a revenue-heavy, capital-light, gross-booked undertaking. “Revenue of the Transferred Business Undertaking for FY 2025-2026 is INR 887.43 Million, representing 12.6% of the Total Income of the Company on a standalone basis.”
- *Scheme* — Consideration is lump-sum cash at Net Asset Value / book value on the closing date — i.e. no value is being crystallised or marked up; it is an intra-group related-party transfer to a 100% subsidiary, not a sale to a third party. “The Company will receive a lump sum cash consideration for the Proposed Transfer, which shall be based on the Net Asset Value (NAV) of the Transferred Business determined as on the Closing Date of the Proposed Transfer.”
- *Scheme* — Deliberately structured as a BTA outside any scheme of arrangement, so Regulation 37A / NCLT process does not apply, and shareholders get nothing directly — the shareholding pattern is unchanged. “There will be no change in the shareholding pattern of the Company pursuant to the slump sale of relevant business undertaking of the Company to its wholly owned subsidiary i.e., BTSPL.”
- *Scheme* — Pattern of the same playbook elsewhere: the payments entity TZF Logistics got a INR 21.99 crore rights-issue infusion on September 28, 2026, expressly tied to growth and to PPI regulatory capital under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act; the NBFC Blackbuck Finserve took INR 140 crore of IPO proceeds plus INR 100 crore of rights issue on December 15, 2025. “Further the investment will also support the subsidiary in meeting the regulatory requirements applicable to PPI issuers under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007 and the RBI regulations.”
- *CALL Aug 2025* — Loads/Superloads is the only vertical booked at gross value, which distorted the consolidated P&L and forced management to introduce a 'net revenues' metric (gross margin of Superloads added to other operating revenue) — an accounting mismatch a separate entity cleanly isolates. “Important point to note is that Super Loads business in an accounting terms happens to be at a gross level, right?”
- *CALL Feb 2026* — Management already treated loads as a standalone, loss-making business with no cost or P&L connection to core payments/telematics, requiring HO-cost allocation to be understood at all. “We need to basically split this after allocating the HO cost into what is the core business EBITDA margin and what is the new business EBITDA margin because at the business line vertical level there is literally no connection in terms of both these businesses.”
- *CALL Feb 2026* — Superloads' losses and its independent investment decisions were explicitly described as driving the blended margin, with further 'depression' in EBITDA promised if they chose to out-invest. “And this is essentially a independent business which has basically its losses.”
- *CALL May 2026* — Investors (Ankush Agarwal, Surge Capital) pressed for separate core vs growth profitability disclosure because the blended number made modelling impossible; management agreed but deferred it as too early — the closest thing on record to an outside party asking for separation, and it was about disclosure, not legal structure. “Fully agree with you but we believe it's still too early we will evaluate this down the line when can we improve the visibility and I definitely understand your pain because modelling is tough for you.”
- *CALL May 2026* — Context for 'organizing businesses': management was already re-sorting verticals between 'core' and 'growth' buckets as they matured, saying vehicle finance would exit investment mode and migrate to core — a narrative reclassification that the Oct 2026 slump sale makes a legal one for loads. “Vehicle finance business probably by the end of this financial year would no longer be in the investment mode and would start probably churning cash flows which will also enable us to move that into a core business kind of a trajectory from a narrative perspective.”
- *CALL Nov 2025* — The scale-up that preceded the carve-out: from four hubs to 14-15 within six months, with the Superloads team going from under 50 to about 250 people, and management admitting they could not yet model the resulting contribution or losses. “we plan to open 10 new hubs and take this number in the range of 14-15 hubs over the course of next six months.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No call ever mentions the transfer; no stated benefit to margins, capital, valuation, tax, or future external funding of BTSPL; no consideration amount, closing date, employee/licence transfer detail, or requester named.

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

These documents do not describe any separation, demerger, spin-off, hive-off or scheme of arrangement at Aditya Infotech Ltd. (CPPLUS), so no rationale for one can be reconstructed from them; the only occurrences of the words 'demerger' and 'spin-off' are inside boilerplate corporate-action adjustment clauses of the Aditya Infotech Employee Stock Option Plan 2024 resolutions in the February 26, 2026 postal ballot notice, which list them generically alongside rights issue, bonus, merger, amalgamation, sale of division and split as events that would trigger fair adjustment of option counts and exercise prices. Every structural move management actually discusses runs the other way — toward consolidation and vertical integration, not separation. The company bought Dixon Technologies' 50% stake in the manufacturing JV in September 2024 (a share swap valuing the deal at about Rs. 4,000 crores, leaving Dixon with roughly 6.6% of the parent and a board seat), made AIL Dixon a wholly owned subsidiary, and management repeatedly cites 'consolidation of the subsidiary AIL Dixon' as an FY26 margin driver; the Feb 26, 2026 postal ballot even adds Article 102A preserving Dixon's right to nominate one director while it holds at least 4%. New entities being created are additive, not carve-outs: Aditya Infotech Taiwan Company Limited (wholly owned R&D subsidiary) and a 50:50 JV with Orient Cables for coaxial/network/CCTV cable manufacturing in a ~1 lakh sq ft Rajasthan plant (commercial ops Q2–Q3 FY27), both framed as backward integration for 'quality consistency, supply consistency, contribution to the EBITDA basis points.' The one business genuinely shrinking is the legacy Dahua third-party distribution line, but management describes it as a natural STQC-driven runoff (down 25–30% in FY26, under Rs. 100–150 crores in FY27, 'INR10-15 crores a month', at roughly one-third the margin of own-brand CP PLUS, which is 86–87% of revenue), not as an entity being separated; no board approval, no scheme, no record date and no appointed date appear anywhere. The capital actions on record are the opposite of a separation: Rs. 375 crores of IPO proceeds used to cut gross debt 89% to Rs. 48 crores, and an August 19, 2026 board approval to raise up to Rs. 1,500 crores via public issue and/or QIP, with shareholder approval by postal ballot. No investor, lender or partner on any of these four calls asks for a separation; questions concern margins, memory/SoC shortages, price hikes, market share (20.8% FY25 to ~45.4% in Q3 FY26), capex and exports. Any answer naming a separated business, its numbers or its rationale would have to be invented, which these texts do not support.

**How it evolved:** The idea never surfaces. Across Aug 20, 2025 (Q1 FY26, maiden call), Nov 13, 2025 (Q2 FY26), Feb 13, 2026 (Q3 FY26) and May 28, 2026 (Q4/FY26) the structural narrative moves only toward integration — AIL Dixon fully consolidated, a Taiwan R&D subsidiary, an Orient Cables 50:50 JV, Qualcomm and L&T Semiconductor collaborations, and multi-brand launches (Nexivue, Eyra) inside the same listed entity. The filings follow the same direction: the Feb 26, 2026 postal ballot entrenches Dixon's nominee-director right and ratifies the ESOP, and the Aug 19, 2026 board meeting approves a Rs. 1,500 crore equity raise. The only textual trace of 'demerger'/'spin-off' is undated boilerplate in the ESOP adjustment clauses, which signals nothing about intent.

**What management expects from it:** Nothing, because no separation is proposed. The benefits management actually claims come from the opposite: consolidating AIL Dixon, backward integration (housing, cables, lenses) and brand mix lifting FY26 EBITDA margin 540 bps to 13.7% with FY27 guidance of 14-15% EBITDA and 8.5-9.5% PAT, plus IPO debt repayment cutting finance cost 27.8%.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The sole appearance of 'demerger' and 'spin-off' in all supplied material is a generic ESOP corporate-action adjustment clause in the February 26, 2026 postal ballot notice (Items 1 and 2), not a proposal to separate anything. “RESOLVED FURTHER THAT in case of any corporate action(s) such as rights issue, bonus issue, merger demerger, spin-off, consolidation, amalgamation and sale of division, split, change in capital structure of the Company and other restructuring of the Company, requisite adjustments (which may include adjustments to the number of options and exercise price) shall be appropriately made by the Board (including Committee thereof), in a fair and reasonable manner in accordance with the AIL ESOP Plan 2024.”
- *Scheme* — The same postal ballot moves toward binding Dixon in, inserting Article 102A to preserve Dixon Technologies' right to nominate one director while it holds at least 4% of share capital — a consolidation of the relationship, not a separation. “102A. "Till such time as Dixon Technologies (India) Limited, and/or its successors and permitted assigns (hereinafter referred to as “DTIL”) holds at least 4% (four percent) of the Share Capital, DTIL shall have the right to nominate 1 (one) Director (“DTIL Nominee Director”) on the Board.”
- *Scheme* — The only capital-structure event in the filings is the August 19, 2026 board approval of a fund raise of up to Rs. 1,500 crores by public issue and/or QIP, subject to shareholder approval by postal ballot — no scheme of arrangement, appointed date or record date is disclosed. “Issuance of securities up to an aggregate amount not exceeding ₹ 1,500 crores (Rupees One Thousand Five Hundred Crores) or an equivalent amount thereof (inclusive of such premium as may be fixed, if any), at such price or prices as may be permissible under applicable law, in one or more tranches and / or by way of one or more issuances.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=049b1218-7309-450a-8095-d9d690a06306.pdf)* — The maiden call describes the manufacturing JV being absorbed, not separated: Dixon's 50% stake in AIL Dixon Technologies Private Limited was acquired in September 2024 at a deal valuation of about Rs. 4,000 crores via share swap, leaving Dixon with ~6.6% of the parent. “Last year in September 2024, we then acquired Dixon's 50% stake in the JV, making AIL Dixon a wholly owned subsidiary . And Dixon in turn retained 6. 6% stake in Aditya Infotech , underscoring their long -term confidence in our growth journey.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=bfc3ed01-7ea5-476c-8246-c0a4ca2c9571.pdf)* — Management cites the consolidation of AIL Dixon as a margin and efficiency driver in H1 FY26, alongside IPO debt repayment — the structural change on record is integration of the manufacturing entity into the listed company. “Also, our consolidation of the subsidiary AIL Dixon is showing gains in H1 FY26.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=c5a40d0f-53d8-4774-a42a-07d57187b0c8.pdf)* — New legal entities discussed are additive backward-integration vehicles, not carve-outs: a 50:50 MoU/JV with Orient Cables for coaxial and network cables primarily for CP PLUS captive consumption, and a wholly owned Taiwan R&D subsidiary. “We have also advanced our backward integration agenda by signing an M oU with Orient Cables for the manufacturing of coaxial and network cables, primarily for CP PLUS captive consumption.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=c5a40d0f-53d8-4774-a42a-07d57187b0c8.pdf)* — The one business being wound down is the legacy Dahua third-party distribution line, but purely as an STQC-driven revenue runoff (under Rs. 100-150 crores in FY27, Rs. 10-15 crores a month in FY26) at roughly one-third the own-brand margin — not an entity being separated. “So, I think Dahua, first I’ll take the second part of the question . Dahua Next year would be not even INR100 - 150 crores of our revenue.”

*Not explained on the calls:* Everything about a separation: no business identified, no board approval, scheme, swap ratio, appointed or record date, entity financials, lender or partner consent, or management commentary exists in these texts.

- *Insiders:* Post-demerger STPL was not under the Company's control and was managed by a separate promoter entity not related to the Company, viz. Rattan India Power Limited and Rattan India Enterprises Limited (the New Promoters).

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Across the three transcripts tagged here (the Q3/9M FY26 call of February 10, 2026, which appears twice, and the Q4/FY26 call of May 21, 2026) and all 27 filings, Embassy Developments Limited (EMBDL/EDL) never announces, proposes or explains a separation, demerger, spin-off or carve-out of any of its own businesses — the stated direction of travel is the opposite, consolidation: FY26 was 'the first full year of the merged platform following the integration of NAM Estates and the erstwhile Indiabulls Real Estate Limited under the unified Embassy Developments brand', accounted for as a reverse merger under Ind AS 103 with NAM as accounting acquirer and EDL as accounting acquiree. The only separation management actually explains is historical and belongs to the predecessor group: a court-approved demerger in FY2010-11 that separated the power business, Sinnar Thermal Power Limited (STPL), from the erstwhile Indiabulls Group / real estate business, after which STPL was controlled by the unrelated Rattan India Group (Rattan India Power Limited and Rattan India Enterprises Limited) and 'was not under the control of the Company'. Management raised that 15-year-old separation only because a lender used its surviving guarantee framework against EDL: Canara Bank (successor to Syndicate Bank, which had sanctioned facilities aggregating Rs 1,444.00 million to STPL) claimed Rs 372 crore under a 2010/2011 corporate guarantee tied to an equity-infusion undertaking and filed a Section 7 IBC application; NCLT admitted CIRP on December 9, 2025, NCLAT stayed it on December 11, 2025, and on May 4, 2026 NCLAT quashed it, holding 'that no deed of guarantee existed and that the application was barred under Section 10A of the IBC', after which EDL exited the NSE ASM framework on May 6, 2026. EDL's defence rested on the separation itself: the obligation was an equity infusion and not 'debt', it was limited, contingent and secondary to the Rattan India Group post-demerger, and against a required infusion of Rs 2,454 crore the Rattan India Group had already infused Rs 3,026 crore, so no obligation survived. The forward-looking corporate actions in the window are consolidations and disposals rather than business separations: the Spero Properties and Services amalgamation into Equinox India Infraestate (appointed date April 1, 2025), and repeated voluntary strike-offs of non-operational subsidiaries (Ariston Investments, Lenus Constructions, Sentia Constructions, Equinox India Multiplex Services, Mariana Constructions, Apesh Real Estate, Varali Real Estate, Devona Infrastructure, Dev Property Development) undertaken 'to simplify its corporate structure and reduce administrative and compliance costs'. The closest thing to separating a business is asset-level monetisation: the April 11, 2026 share purchase agreement to sell 100% of Sepset Real Estate Limited — owner of the 'Mega Mall' commercial project in Jodhpur, which contributed Rs 18.55 crore of income (0.85%) and negative net worth of Rs 114.07 crore — to Pen India Limited for Rs 100 crore cash, plus the flagged disposal of non-core, non-contiguous Panvel parcels, possible disposal of the 500+ acre Sohna land where only ~75 acres is developable, and the Nashik 'debonding' exercise to strip SEZ status from ~1,500 acres so it can be sold as industrial plots. One potential separation was explicitly considered and dropped: management 'had a thought about forward purchasing' Embassy East Business Park (Phase 1, 2.7 msf, GDV ~Rs 3,100 crore) with Embassy REIT and chose instead to build it out and defer any exit-versus-hold decision by three to four years, while targeting an 80:20 residential:commercial mix moving toward 70:30. No investor, lender, banker or partner in these texts asks for a separation; the asks are presales and collections delivery, a lower cost of debt (14.8% down toward 10%), lower leverage (0.3x net debt/equity), reduction of the promoter pledge (68% back toward 47-48%), and clarity on when the reported P&L turns positive.

**How it evolved:** February 10, 2026 (Q3/9M FY26, the first earnings call as the merged entity): the only separation discussed is the FY2010-11 court-approved demerger of the power business (STPL) from the erstwhile Indiabulls Group, surfaced purely as context for Canara Bank's Rs 372 crore Section 7 claim and the NCLAT stay, while a possible REIT carve-out of Embassy East Business Park is disclosed as considered and dropped in favour of building it out. Between calls the separation-adjacent activity is disposal, not demerger: the April 11-12, 2026 sale of Sepset Real Estate (Mega Mall, Jodhpur) to Pen India for Rs 100 crore, continuing subsidiary strike-offs (March 10/16, April 6/21, June 10, 2026), and the May 4, 2026 NCLAT order quashing CIRP on the merits of the old demerger-era guarantee. May 21, 2026 (Q4/FY26): the legacy separation is closed out as a won litigation, and management reframes portfolio pruning — monetising scattered/unmutated erstwhile-Indiabulls land, entertaining offers on Sohna, and 'debonding' the ~1,500-acre Nashik SEZ — as non-core exits rather than any business separation. Nothing in the August-October 2026 filings (Rs 1,020 crore and Rs 105 crore NCDs, the Rs 362.62 crore promoter warrant issue fully converted by October 30, 2026) introduces a separation; they raise and recapitalise within one entity.

**What management expects from it:** No separation benefits are claimed, because none is planned. For the disposals they do describe: unlocked value, a stronger balance sheet and capital redeployed into core markets; non-core land exits and Nashik debonding to raise realisable value; lower cost of debt (14.8% toward 10%) and net debt/equity near 0.3x; ~47-50% net cash surplus margins; simpler structure cutting compliance cost.

## GMRAIRPORT — GMR Airports Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a scheme of arrangement whose nature the documents on file do not settle) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 5.0/10 · scheme (nature unclear) · 2 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-09-29, latest 2026-10-29

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** not stated; documents describe a composite amalgamation/arrangement scheme and OCRPS conversion, no business separation — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* GMR Group promoter; Groupe ADP co-promoter since 2020, its subsidiary GISPL holds OCRPS; promoters' FCCB call option advanced to March 2027; directors hold 5,45,160 and 17,000 shares
- *What it reveals:* Conversion ratio 1:40 means large latent dilution from 2,60,44,40,880 OCRPS; against that, FY26 PAT positive first time in over a decade, net debt INR340bn at 5.5x EBITDA, guided below 4x in 18-24 months
- *Selling pressure:* unclear — Only 102mn shares issued, 0.96% of post-allotment capital; ADP said no further stake sale contemplated near future; no lock-in stated
- *Parent or spin:* unclear · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Composite Scheme / OCRPS terms per July 25, 2024 intimation: dilution from the 2,60,18,90,880 OCRPS still unconverted
- *In their words:* “This is in context of the Composite Scheme of Amalgamation & Arrangement amongst erstwhile GMR Airports Ltd, erstwhile GMR Infra Developers Limited and the Company, which became effective from July 25, 2024.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Across all twelve tagged calls and the three filings, management never explains a separation, spin-off or demerger of any business — the only corporate scheme in these texts runs the opposite way. It is the Composite Scheme of Amalgamation & Arrangement amongst erstwhile GMR Airports Ltd, erstwhile GMR Infra Developers Ltd and the listed company (then GMR Airports Infrastructure Ltd), effective 25 July 2024, under which the listed entity issued 2,79,40,26,763 equity shares to Aeroports de Paris S.A. and 25,75,82,066 to GMR Infra Services Pvt Ltd, plus 2,60,44,40,880 OCRPS of Rs 40 each convertible 1:40 (25,50,000 of which converted into 10,20,00,000 shares, 0.96% of post-allotment capital, on 29 Sep 2026). The reasons management gave for that merger were a streamlined corporate structure, airport assets moved closer to the erstwhile GIL shareholders, enhanced governance with an expanded board, a future-ready balance sheet, GMR promoters retaining management control, and tax-efficient upstreaming of airport dividends to the Listco — with Groupe ADP moving from a 49% holder of the unlisted GMR Airports to roughly 33% of the listed entity while keeping the same five board seats as the GMR family. Every other structural move described is also consolidation, not separation: buying Fraport's 10% of Delhi Airport to take GAL to 74% 'at a deep discount to what the analysts have been valuing Delhi airport', acquiring the residual 70% of ESR GMR Logistics Park for Rs 413 mn at high-teens IRRs against single-digit debt cost, and pulling duty-free, cargo, car park, F&B and retail out of JVs and airport SPVs into GAL as a 'second platform' (Delhi duty-free FY25 revenue Rs 2,200 cr and PAT ~Rs 210 cr; Delhi cargo FY25 revenue Rs 780 cr and PAT Rs 120 cr; GAL standalone FY25 revenue ~Rs 1,200 cr and EBITDA ~Rs 600 cr, guided to operating income above Rs 2,200 cr in FY26; duty-free EBITDA margin guided 15–17%; non-aero growth target 15%+ with 'least capital employed'; by Jun 2026 'non-aero platform numbers are now higher than Hyderabad airport numbers'), with real estate self-development named the 'third platform'. The only divestment is equity in Cebu airport (Rs 4.1 bn exceptional gain in Q3FY25, GMR staying on as technical services provider to December 2026) and the sale of Groupe ADP's own 7.3% stake in GAL to GMR promoters — a shareholder transaction, not a business separation. The word 'de-merger' appears exactly once, in Feb 2026, purely as a profitability benchmark ('the first positive and highest profit seen since de-merger'), referring to an earlier, already-completed split that these texts never describe or justify. Pressure in these texts came from Groupe ADP's new leadership wanting dividends from international assets, from lenders and rating agencies (Crisil A+ on GAL targeting AA-/AAA, DIAL and GHIAL upgrades, GHIAL reaching international investment grade), and from analysts asking when dividends start — and management's answer to all of them was consolidation and deleveraging, not a carve-out. Any separation thesis therefore cannot be sourced to this record; the texts affirmatively describe a group collapsing structures into the listed company.

**How it evolved:** The only restructuring story starts in the Feb 2025-tagged call (transcript 14 Aug 2024), the first call of the merged entity, where management reports the GMR Airports / GMR Airports Infrastructure merger as complete and frames it as a streamlined structure, assets closer to GIL shareholders and tax-efficient dividend flow. Through Jan 2025, May 2025 and Jul 2025 the direction is consolidation — Cebu equity exit, ADIA-backed promoter pledge reduction from 53.9% to 34.8%, Fraport's 10% of DIAL bought to reach 74%, ESR GMR Logistics Park taken to 100%, and duty-free/cargo moved into the listed GAL from 27–28 July 2025 and 10 Sep 2025. By Nov 2025 and Feb 2026 the 'GAL platform' is presented as the non-aero second platform inside the listed entity, with the single word 'de-merger' used only as the profit benchmark in Feb 2026; Jun 2026 adds real estate as a 'third platform' and reports ADP's 7.3% stake sale to the promoters with no further sales contemplated. At no point across these calls does the plan change toward separating a business — the idea of a separation never surfaces.

**What management expects from it:** No separation is discussed, so no per-entity expectations exist. For the consolidation they did describe: streamlined structure, tax-efficient dividend upstreaming to the Listco, GAL as a non-aero/real-estate consumer platform at 15%+ growth on minimal capital, duty-free margins 15-17%, net debt/EBITDA below 4x and ratings toward AAA, dividends once leverage reaches 3-3.5x.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Feb 2025](https://investor.gmraero.com/pdf/GMR%20Airports%20Infra-Q1FY25%20Concall%20Transcript.pdf)* — First call of the merged entity: management presents the amalgamation of GMR Airports into the listed GMR Airports Infrastructure Ltd as complete, justified by a streamlined structure, assets closer to shareholders, better governance and a stronger balance sheet. “Corporate structure of GMR Airports Infrastructure Limited is now streamlined, and airport assets have moved closer to the GIL shareholders.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://investor.gmraero.com/pdf/GMR%20Airports%20Infra-Q1FY25%20Concall%20Transcript.pdf)* — Asked what changes operationally, management says nothing changes for ADP — it simply moves from 49% of the unlisted subsidiary to ~33% of the Listco with the same five board seats; the benefit is tax-efficient dividend flow to the listed company. “Obviously, the benefits are more from efficiency of movement of earnings once the entity starts -- the airport entities start to declare dividend.”
- *[Jan 2025](https://investor.gmraero.com/pdf/GMR%20Airports%20-Q3FY25%20Concall%20Transcript.pdf)* — Cebu is the one asset actually exited — equity divested for a Rs 4.1 billion exceptional gain, with GMR retaining only a technical services role to December 2026. “PAT from continuing operations was INR2 billion and included an exceptional gain of INR4.1 billion, arising due to the completion of divestment in Cebu Airport.”
- *[Jan 2025](https://investor.gmraero.com/pdf/GMR%20Airports%20-Q3FY25%20Concall%20Transcript.pdf)* — Promoter-level deleveraging via the ADIA transaction (concluded 7 Jan 2025) cut the pledge on GMR promoter holding in GAL and removed refinancing and settlement risk — a shareholder fix, not a business separation. “This has resulted in significant reduction in the pledge of GMR Promoter group shareholding in GAL to 34.8% from 53.9% along with mitigating both refinancing and settlement risk.”
- *[May 2025](https://investor.gmraero.com/pdf/GMR%20Airports%20-Q4FY25%20Concall%20Transcript.pdf)* — The stated strategic project is building the listed entity into a consumer business on top of the regulated airport utility, by absorbing adjacency businesses rather than separating anything. “We are steadfast in long term strategy of converting GAL into a consumer business with the underpinnings of a utility company.”
- *[Jul 2025](https://investor.gmraero.com/pdf/GMR%20Airports%20-Q1FY26%20Concall%20Transcript.pdf)* — Delhi duty-free is brought fully in-house after the JV concession ended on 27 July, won back through competitive bidding, so the 33% that previously went to the JV partner now accrues to GAL; management cites procurement and marketing efficiencies from a single platform. “That concession came to an end on 27th of July. That's where GMR Airports got this concession through a competitive bidding and have started operating it as a wholly owned business of GMR Airports.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://investor.gmraero.com/pdf/GMR%20Airports%20-Q2FY26%20Concall%20Transcript.pdf)* — Management confirms the non-aero platform was deliberately built at the listed entity level — five business platforms (Delhi and Hyderabad duty-free, Delhi cargo, car park, F&B/retail) now sit inside GAL. “We have always advised that we have created this GAL platform at the listed entity to get into non -aero business.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://investor.gmraero.com/pdf/GMR%20Airports%20-Q3FY26%20Concall%20Transcript.pdf)* — The only use of the word de-merger in the entire record is as a profit milestone, with no explanation of what was separated, from whom, or why. “This was the first positive and highest profit seen since de-merger.”
- *[Jun 2026](https://investor.gmraero.com/pdf/GMR%20Airports%20-Q4FY26%20Concall%20Transcript.pdf)* — Strategy is described as stacking platforms inside one listed company — aero utility, then non-aero, then real estate — and the non-aero platform's numbers now exceed Hyderabad airport's on minimal capital. “like we have built our second platform of business which is the non -aero business, we are very much focused on building our third platform which is the real estate development business.”
- *[Jun 2026](https://investor.gmraero.com/pdf/GMR%20Airports%20-Q4FY26%20Concall%20Transcript.pdf)* — The only stake reduction discussed is Groupe ADP selling about 7.3% of GAL to the GMR promoters, with no further sales contemplated and FCCB conversion still scheduled for March 2028. “They have indicated that post this current stub of sale of about 7.3% stake in GAL, they do not contemplate any further stake sale in the near future.”
- *Scheme* — The 29 Sep 2026 filing documents the actual scheme in force — a Composite Scheme of Amalgamation & Arrangement effective 25 July 2024 that issued equity and OCRPS to Aeroports de Paris and its subsidiary; it is an amalgamation, with no separation, split or spin-off recited anywhere. “This is in context of the Composite Scheme of Amalgamation & Arrangement amongst erstwhile GMR Airports Ltd, erstwhile GMR Infra Developers Limited and the Company, which became effective from July 25, 2024.”

*Not explained on the calls:* Everything: the texts describe no separation, name no separated business, and give no rationale, timeline, structure, valuation or ratio-swap; the single de-merger mention is unexplained.

## HDFCBANK — HDFC Bank Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a subsidiary's listing is in motion (DRHP / board approval)) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 5.0/10 · partial spin-off / listing · 2 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-01-17, latest 2026-01-17

> **Listing:** IPO / listing of the subsidiary in motion since 2026-01-17; date not fixed

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** HDB Financial Services Limited, the Bank's non-deposit taking NBFC subsidiary, listed via IPO with Bank offer-for-sale — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* Bank divested 13,51,35,135 shares at Rs 740 for Rs 10,000 crore and still holds 74.1% of HDBFSL; HDB Employee Welfare Trust consolidated as subsidiary
- *What it reveals:* Offer for sale produced a net gain of Rs 9,179.40 crore standalone and Rs 7,000.27 crore consolidated, showing carrying value far below the Rs 740 sale price; HDBFSL Q3 PAT grew 36.3% on a Rs 1,146 billion loan book
- *Selling pressure:* unclear — not stated
- *Parent or spin:* unclear · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* HDBFSL standalone financials and the carrying value of the Bank's residual 74.1% stake
- *In their words:* “HDB Financial Services Ltd (HDBFSL), is a non-deposit taking NBFC in which the Bank holds a 74.1% stake.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

On these texts alone there is no business separation, demerger, spin-off or Scheme of Arrangement at HDFC Bank — the only 'separation' management actually described is the partial carve-out of its NBFC subsidiary HDB Financial Services Limited (HDBFS) via an IPO, and even that was a stake dilution rather than a separation of a business from the Bank. Sashidhar Jagdishan disclosed it only in passing in the Jul 2025 (Q1 FY26) call: the Bank 'carried out the HDB Financial Services listing process, wherein the bank also diluted some stake,' with listing on 2 July 2025. The filings give the mechanics: the IPO launched 25 June 2025 comprised a fresh issue of Rs 2,500 crore plus an offer for sale by the Bank of Rs 10,000 crore, under which the Bank divested 13,51,35,135 equity shares of Rs 10 each at Rs 740 per share, booking a net gain of Rs 9,179.40 crore standalone (before tax, net of IPO expenses) and Rs 7,000.27 crore consolidated; the Bank retains 74.1% of HDBFS, whose loan book was Rs 1,146 billion with Stage 3 at 2.81% and total CAR 21.8% (Tier 1 17.3%) at 31 December 2025. Management never framed this as solving a strategic problem; the only problem it addressed in their words was customer overlap, raised by an analyst, not by management: asked by Pranav Gundlapalle (Bernstein) whether the Bank and HDBFS would conflict over the same customers, Jagdishan said HDBFS serves a segment 'a notch or two below' the Bank at higher rack rates, so de-duplication overlap would be 'extremely minimal' and segmentation would stay distinct 'for a long period of time.' The financial consequence management did discuss was the gain's effect on the base — in Jul 2026 the CFO stripped out 'HDB gains' as a one-timer, restating 5% reported PAT growth to 9.8% adjusted. Separately, the direction of group travel in these texts is consolidation, not separation: the July 2023 merger of HDFC Limited into the Bank (described repeatedly as the largest merger in recent Indian corporate history, with cross-sell and liability synergies cited — e-HDFC home-loan liability penetration up from 36% to ~50%, CASA balances from Rs 50,000 crore to Rs 86,000 crore), and an April 2026 Board approval to invest up to Rs 1,000 crore in a preferential issue by subsidiary HDFC Life. The only adjacent capital theme is surplus capital: with CAR at 19.9%-19.7% and capital generation matching consumption, Jagdishan said the Bank would 'keep on exploring' options 'to delight shareholders,' which in FY26 took the form of a 1:1 bonus issue and an interim dividend of Rs 5 per share rather than any separation.

**How it evolved:** Apr 2025 (Q4 FY25 call): no mention of any separation; discussion is CD-ratio glide path, reorganisation of the asset side under the Deputy MD, and surplus capital. Jul 2025 (Q1 FY26 call, 19 July 2025): the HDBFS listing is disclosed as completed with partial stake dilution, and the only 'why' offered comes in answer to Bernstein's conflict question — distinct customer segments, minimal overlap. Oct 2025 (Q2 FY26 call): capital surplus is probed; management says it will 'keep on exploring' shareholder-friendly options, but names none, while Jan 2026 and Jul 2026 treat the HDB gain purely as a base-effect one-timer; Apr 2026 moves the other way with up to Rs 1,000 crore into HDFC Life. Across Mar 2026 (governance call), Apr 2026 (Q4 FY26) and Jul 2026 (Q1 FY27) the plan never evolves into a separation — it is never raised again.

**What management expects from it:** Nothing was stated, because no separation was announced. For the HDBFS partial listing management claimed only distinct customer segments (HDBFS a notch or two below the Bank, minimal overlap), a one-time pre-tax gain of Rs 9,179.40 crore standalone / Rs 7,000.27 crore consolidated, and continued 74.1% ownership. No margin, capital-release, valuation-unlock or focus benefit was quantified for either entity.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Jul 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=d1268138-e288-4335-9764-7a944dfa3570.pdf)* — The only separation event disclosed anywhere in these texts: the Bank processed the HDB Financial Services listing and itself diluted stake, with the stock listing on 2 July 2025. No strategic rationale was volunteered in the opening remarks. “During the quarter, we carried out the HDB Financial Services listing process, wherein the bank also diluted some stake, and which eventually culminated in the stocks being listed on 2nd of July.”
- *[Jul 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=d1268138-e288-4335-9764-7a944dfa3570.pdf)* — The rationale question came from an investor, not management: Pranav Gundlapalle (Bernstein) asked what share of the Bank's 100 million customers are loan customers, noting HDB claims almost 20 million customers and growth ambition, and whether the two entities would collide. “And was wondering if there's a chance of a future conflict where both entities target the same customer.”
- *[Jul 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=d1268138-e288-4335-9764-7a944dfa3570.pdf)* — Jagdishan's answer is the closest thing to a stated problem solved: HDBFS serves a segment a notch or two below the Bank at higher rack rates, so overlap on de-duplication would be minimal and segmentation stays distinct for a long period. “Obviously, it has to be a notch below and that is not a segment that we are catering to at this juncture.”
- *Scheme* — Jan 2026 results filing (note to Q3 FY26 accounts) gives the only hard numbers: IPO of 25 June 2025 with Rs 2,500 crore fresh issue plus Rs 10,000 crore offer for sale by the Bank; 13,51,35,135 shares of Rs 10 each at Rs 740; standalone net gain Rs 9,179.40 crore, consolidated Rs 7,000.27 crore; Bank retains 74.1%. “On June 25, 2025, the Bank's subsidiary company, HDB Financial Services Limited ("HDBFS") launched its initial public offering ("IPO"), comprised of a fresh issuance of equity shares aggregating to 2,500.00 crore and an offer for sale ("OFS") of equity shares by the Bank, aggregating to 10,000.00 crore.”
- *Oct 2025* — Asked by Chintan (Autonomous) what the Bank will do with excess capital at ~19.9% CAR, Jagdishan kept shareholder-return options open but named none; the FY26 outcome was a 1:1 bonus issue and Rs 5 interim dividend, not a separation. “Having said that, if there are any opportunities that may arise in terms of other options that are available to sort of delight shareholders, we would be more than happy to do so.”
- *[Jul 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=509cc499-6cb1-4d9f-8de9-9c7de6c70eef.pdf)* — The HDBFS stake sale is treated only as a base-effect item: the CFO strips 'HDB gains', the floating/counter-cyclical provision and contingent provisions out of the prior-year base to restate 5% reported PAT growth as 9.8%. “But last year included certain one-timers like HDB gains and then we had a floating provision counter-cyclical buffer that we added and some contingent provision and so on.”
- *[Apr 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=a77abbbb-954a-4221-8240-67bf0da6ba1c.pdf)* — Group direction in these texts is the opposite of separation: Kaizad Bharucha details merger synergies from absorbing HDFC Limited — e-HDFC home-loan liability penetration up from 36% to ~50%, CASA from Rs 50,000 crore to Rs 86,000 crore, 98% of new home-loan customers opening an account, 23% holding active cards. “Net of attritions, net of acquisitions over this journey, this 36% has come as high as 50% within the last 2.5 years.”

*Not explained on the calls:* Everything: no demerger rationale, scheme, record date, entity perimeter, lender or regulator demand, or valuation/capital logic appears. The HDBFS IPO's purpose is never explained.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Linjemontage (LMG), KPIL's Swedish pure-play power-infrastructure EPC step-down subsidiary, partly sold and listed via IPO on Nasdaq Stockholm — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* KPTS (KPIL wholly owned subsidiary) retains 66.45% / 34,042,919 shares, down from 96.12%; 360-day lock-up for Kalpataru Sweden, board and group management; employee/director shareholders sold 991,950 shares mainly to repay acquisition financing
- *What it reveals:* A high-return asset-light business priced publicly: FY25/26 net sales SEK 3,225m, adjusted EBITA SEK 245m (7.6%), R.O.C.E. 48.1%, net cash SEK 172.1m, order book SEK 4,349m, valued at SEK 2,356,557,000 — yet only ~11.14% of KPIL revenue and ~4.5% of its net worth

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The business being separated is Linjemontage i Grästorp AB (LMG), KPIL's Swedish power-grid EPC subsidiary held through Kalpataru Power Transmission Sweden AB (KPTS) — separated not by demerger but by an offer-for-sale IPO on Nasdaq Stockholm (listed 25 September 2026), in which KPTS sold down from 96.12% to 66.45% rather than giving LMG new capital. The trigger management cited on the calls was value crystallisation and cash: LMG had compounded from ~INR1,000 crores revenue in FY24 to INR1,800+ crores in FY25 (PBT INR21 crores to INR70+ crores) to ~INR3,000 crores in FY26 with EBITDA ~INR200 crores and PBT ~INR170 crores (both up over 100%), i.e. SEK1.3bn to SEK3.2bn net sales at a 56.6% CAGR with adjusted EBITA margin rising from 4.4% to 7.6%, net cash of SEK172.1m, ROCE of 48.1% and an order book of SEK4,349m — yet it was only ~11.14% of KPIL's consolidated revenue and ~4.5% of consolidated net worth. Mohnot repeatedly placed the Sweden 'fundraise' inside the same bucket as the noncore exits (Vindhyachal road asset sold January 2026 for ~INR799 crores EV / INR600+ crores net, Indore real estate, Shree Shubham Logistics), i.e. as a source of 'further cash flows' to cut leverage and fund the INR800-900 crores/year capex programme and lift ROCE; the IPO delivered KPTS gross proceeds of ~SEK711.45m at SEK46/share, valuing LMG at SEK2,356.6m (~INR2,324 crores). The second problem it solves is that LMG's economics are structurally different from KPIL's: management argued a 6%-7% PBT in a 'mature market' is fine there because 'the ROCE numbers are very, very high and they are cash positive always' — a profile the consolidated KPIL multiple was not reflecting. LMG's own filings justify the separation on strategic grounds: visibility, credibility and brand recognition with customers, partners and employees, transparency, a platform for long-term value creation, a broadened shareholder base, and support for its ambition to lead Nordic power-infrastructure EPC in a Swedish serviceable market growing from ~SEK19bn (2025) to ~SEK31bn (2030) at 11% CAGR (transmission 17%), with ~80% of Sweden's transmission grid over 40 years old and Statnett planning NOK150-200bn of 2025-2034 investment. Pressure came from investors and analysts, not lenders: Carnelian and DAM Capital pushed management on why a T&D business sitting inside a T&D company needed its own listing, while cornerstone demand from Tredje AP-fonden and Unionen (SEK290m) anchored the book; LMG's management/employee shareholders (991,950 shares) sold mainly to repay the financing they had used to buy their shares. KPIL stressed continuity, not exit: KPTS 'indicated an intention to remain a long-term major shareholder', is locked up for 360 days, and LMG remains a step-down subsidiary.

**How it evolved:** The idea surfaced on the 19 May 2025 Q4 FY25 call, where Mohnot disclosed that the Board had approved appointing bankers and intermediaries to examine 'fundraising options' at Linjemontage — framed alongside the noncore clean-up (VEPL, Indore, Shubham); the 14 Feb 2025 call had contained no such plan, only LMG's record order book of INR3,143 crores. By 8 August 2025 (Q1 FY26) it had hardened into a disclosed 'strategic overview… including options related to IPO, subject to market conditions', and management refused to explain the logic when Carnelian asked why a T&D business inside a T&D company needed a separate listing, even withdrawing LMG margin guidance because the process had started. On 31 October 2025 Mohnot said the path was still undecided but expected 'some light' on valuation in FY26-27, and on 5 February 2026 he said the Sweden mandate was 'progressing well' and should throw off cash in FY26-27; by 15 May 2026 he described it only as 'some strategic investment coming into our Swedish subsidiary in whatever form it comes'. The form was fixed in the filings: KPTS board approval on 9 September 2026, prospectus and SEK46 price on 16 September, listing and ~32.1% offer on 25 September, and partial greenshoe exercise on 23-24 October 2026 leaving KPIL at 66.45%.

**What management expects from it:** For LMG: standalone visibility, credibility and brand with customers and employees; transparency; a growth platform and broadened shareholder base; revenue above SEK5bn, adjusted EBITA margin above 8%, net debt/EBITDA under 1.0x, 25% payout. For KPIL: ~SEK711m cash to cut debt and fund capex, value crystallised at SEK2.36bn, retained 66.45% control, higher ROCE and a cleaner noncore-free core EPC portfolio.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Feb 2025](https://kalpataruprojects.com/api/view-file/KPIL_Q3_FY25_Transcript.pdf)* — Baseline: no separation plan existed; LMG was simply presented as a record performer, with revenue doubling and an all-time-high order book of INR3,143 crores. “LMG's order book is at a all time high of INR3,143 crores.”
- *[May 2025](https://kalpataruprojects.com/api/view-file/KPIL_Q4_FY25_Transcript.pdf)* — First disclosure of the separation idea — the Board approved bankers and intermediaries to study fundraising options at Linjemontage, mentioned in the same breath as LMG's PBT rising from ~INR21 crores to ~INR70+ crores. “the Board has also approved appointment of bankers as well as intermediaries to look at fund options, fundraising options in Sweden Linjemontage in the last Board meeting, which we have declared to everyone.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://kalpataruprojects.com/api/view-file/KPIL_Q1FY26_transcript.pdf)* — Formalised as a disclosed 'strategic overview' with an IPO explicitly named as one of the options, and merchant bankers and advisers appointed; LMG had already begun preparatory steps. “We have initiated a strategic overview on LMG where various options are being evaluated, including options related to IPO, subject to market conditions.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://kalpataruprojects.com/api/view-file/KPIL_Q1FY26_transcript.pdf)* — An investor (Mihir Manohar, Carnelian Capital) pressed on exactly the question management never answered — why carve out a T&D business that already sits inside a T&D company; Mohnot declined to comment. “I just wanted to understand the thought process because I mean, it is also T&D business similarly sitting in KPIL.”
- *[Oct 2025](https://kalpataruprojects.com/api/view-file/KPIL_Q2_FY26_Transcript.pdf)* — Management explained LMG's different economic profile — lower PBT than KPIL's core but very high ROCE and permanently cash positive — the implicit valuation argument for separating it, with bankers still mandated and the path undecided. “As far as margins are concerned, I think that those are mature markets where a PBT of 6% to 7% is very reasonably good because the ROCE numbers are very, very high and they are cash positive always.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://kalpataruprojects.com/api/view-file/KPIL_Q3_FY26_Earnings_Call_Transcript-5th_feb_2026.pdf)* — The Sweden transaction was placed squarely in the monetisation/debt-reduction bucket alongside transmission assets, the last road asset and Shree Shubham Logistics, with cash expected in FY26-27. “We do not know which options and what timing it exactly is, but we have appointed bankers to look at exploring fund option raising at Sweden also, which I'm expecting in FY26-27 should give us further cash flows.”
- *[May 2026](https://kalpataruprojects.com/api/view-file/KPILQ4_FY26_Earnings_Call_Transcript_final.pdf)* — Final pre-IPO framing: a 'strategic investment' into the Swedish subsidiary grouped with remaining divestments as free-cash-flow events to strengthen the balance sheet, set against INR800+ crores of annual capex and net debt already down 50% to INR915 crores. “We also have some events of free cash flows coming in next year, whether it is through a few more divestments which are left, which might happen either next year or a year after that or whether it is through some strategic investment coming into our Swedish subsidiary in whatever form it comes.”
- *Scheme* — The 9 September 2026 filing/press release gives the official rationale — standalone visibility, credibility, brand and Nordic leadership ambition — and discloses LMG's scale: SEK3,225m FY26 revenue (~11.14% of KPIL consolidated revenue) but only SEK334m net worth (~4.5% of KPIL's). “The Listing is expected to enhance the Company's visibility, credibility and brand recognition among customers, partners and employees, and to support Linjemontage's long-term ambition to strengthen its position in the Nordics as one of the leading EPC providers within power infrastructure.”
- *Scheme* — Transparency, long-term value creation and a diversified shareholder base are the stated second leg, with KPTS committing to stay a long-term major shareholder (360-day lock-up) and LMG remaining a step-down subsidiary. “Becoming a publicly listed company will also provide greater transparency and a platform for long-term value creation, while diversifying the shareholder base.”
- *Scheme* — Structurally this is a pure sell-down, not a capital raise for LMG: 14,311,620 base shares plus a 2,146,743-share greenshoe at SEK46, ~32.1% of LMG, giving KPTS gross proceeds of ~SEK711.45m at a SEK2,356.6m (~INR2,324 crores) valuation and taking KPTS from 96.12% to 66.45% after the partial greenshoe exercise of 1,877,911 shares. “The Offering consists only of existing shares and the Company will therefore not receive any proceeds from the Offering.”
- *Scheme* — Demand was investor-led: Tredje AP-fonden and Unionen cornerstoned SEK290m, while LMG's own management/director/employee holders sold 991,950 shares chiefly to repay the borrowings used to buy them. “All individual Selling Shareholders other than Kalpataru Sweden are selling shares in the Offering primarily to repay financing arrangements relating to their respective acquisitions of shares in the Company.”
- *Scheme* — LMG's standalone financial targets quantify what separation is meant to unlock — revenue above SEK5bn, adjusted EBITA margin above 8% (from 7.6%), net debt/adj EBITDA below 1.0x and a 25% dividend payout — in a market growing 11% CAGR to SEK31bn by 2030. “Profitability : Linjemontage aims to reach an adjusted EBITA margin exceeding 8 per cent in the medium term.”

*Not explained on the calls:* Calls never explained why a listing over a trade sale, the valuation sought, use of proceeds, dilution to consolidated EPS, or minority/governance terms; management explicitly refused to give the rationale.

*Calls read (36 months):* [Aug 2025](https://kalpataruprojects.com/api/view-file/KPIL_Q1FY26_transcript.pdf)

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

On the documents supplied, Lloyds Engineering Works Ltd. (LEWL) is NOT separating a business — it is doing the opposite: a Scheme of Merger by Absorption approved by all four boards on 29 December 2025 that folds three group entities INTO the listed company, with Appointed Date 1 April 2025. The transferors are Lloyds Infrastructure & Construction Ltd. (LICL, an unlisted associate in which LEWL holds ~24.20%, EPC/roads, bridges, railways, industrial civil, slurry pipelines, BOOT/BOO/BOLT/PPP), Metalfab Hightech Pvt. Ltd. (MHPL, 76% subsidiary, heavy fabrication for steel, railways and infrastructure) and Techno Industries Pvt. Ltd. (TIPL, wholly owned, elevators, escalators, motors and pumps); LEWL itself makes process plant equipment for hydrocarbon, steel, captive power, marine, ports and nuclear heat exchangers. The headline number management cites repeatedly is LICL's 'robust order book of over ₹4,500 crores', which combined with LEWL's manufacturing and execution capability is said to create one 'unified engineering and infrastructure company' able to bid for larger, multidisciplinary contracts; the merging businesses are described as having 'complementary capabilities, overlapping customer base and shared execution requirements'. The stated problems it solves are structural and financial: duplicated/redundant functions, fragmented management, scattered technical and financial resources, a complex multi-entity shareholding that burdens the 'ever-evolving regulatory compliance framework' and governance/transparency, and a smaller balance sheet with costlier borrowing — hence 'improved borrowing capabilities and reduced borrowing costs' and 'unfettered access to cash flow generated by the combined businesses'. Scale being consolidated: LICL FY26 revenue ₹1,902.25 cr / PAT ₹173.81 cr / EBITDA ₹280.01 cr (vs ₹1,060.98 cr / ₹66.66 cr in FY25 and ₹395.14 cr / ₹22.10 cr in FY24), MHPL ₹173.36 cr / ₹33.47 cr, TIPL ₹185.74 cr / ₹5.20 cr, against LEWL's own ₹1,052.22 cr / ₹118.27 cr / ₹188.12 cr; assets/liabilities transferred are LICL ₹1,315.93 cr/₹1,012.61 cr, MHPL ₹321.60 cr/₹269.67 cr, TIPL ₹240.83 cr/₹158.55 cr. Consideration is 1,798 LEWL shares per 1,500 LICL shares (Streamland Estate LLP gets 36,19,97,330 shares, Pravriddhi Trust 59,93,333, all classified Public) and 94 LEWL shares per 5 MHPL shares (Manan Agrawal 1,29,72,000); nothing is paid for TIPL as a wholly owned subsidiary. Who asked: no investor, lender or partner demand is recorded anywhere — it is board-driven, with lenders merely consenting (NOC from lending scheduled commercial banks/financial institutions obtained, 'no conditions imposed by the lenders'), CCI clearing it on 12 May 2026, NSE/BSE observation letters on 18/19 May 2026, NCLT ordering meetings on 19 August 2026, and on 16 October 2026 equity shareholders and unsecured creditors (758,413,241 votes, 72.54% of outstanding, 100% in favour) approving it.

**How it evolved:** No earnings-call transcripts were provided ('no transcripts on file'), so the idea cannot be traced call by call; the only record is filings. It surfaces fully formed on 29 December 2025 (simultaneous board approvals, valuation by Bansi S. Mehta Valuers LLP and fairness opinion from Mark Corporate Advisors, both dated that day), is prepared through 2026 by moving MHPL's registered office to Mumbai (20 December 2025) and TIPL's from Ahmedabad to Mumbai (Regional Director order, 27 February 2026), clears CCI (12 May 2026), the exchanges (18–19 May 2026) and NCLT (19 August 2026), and is approved by shareholders and unsecured creditors on 16 October 2026 with results filed 17 October 2026. In parallel the group consolidates further rather than separating: a 17 August 2026 preferential allotment of 7,00,42,458 shares at ₹71.25 swaps in 1,66,35,087 shares of Steel Infra Solutions Company Ltd. (SISCOL), plus 7,00,000 shares for cash; and on 6 August 2026 the board re-cut the April 2025 rights-issue objects (₹987.25 cr gross, ₹660.52 cr spent, ₹326.73 cr unutilised at 30 June 2026), cutting the Bhilai Engineering Corporation asset purchase from ₹130.25 cr to ₹71.25 cr and adding ₹86.59 cr to working capital — passed by postal ballot on 25 September 2026 (99.9948% in favour).

**What management expects from it:** No separated entities exist — only one survivor. For LEWL: ~₹4,500 cr added order book, FY26 combined revenue of roughly ₹3,314 cr versus ₹1,052 cr standalone, larger net worth and asset base, cost synergies from removing duplicated functions and compliance costs, unfettered access to combined cash flows, improved borrowing capacity at lower cost, simplified shareholding, better governance, and value unlocked via a larger, more diversified entity.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The scheme is a merger by absorption of LICL, MHPL and TIPL into listed LEWL, with the transferors dissolved without winding up — a consolidation, not a separation or demerger. “Merger of LICL, MHPL and TIPL with LEWL and dissolution of LICL, MHPL and TIPL without winding up.”
- *Scheme* — The core stated purpose is to end the split between the listed equipment-manufacturing business and the group's EPC/construction business by putting them in one company. “The amalgamation will create a unified engineering and infrastructure company.”
- *Scheme* — The one hard number management leans on is LICL's order book, repeated in the synopsis, the explanatory statement and the revenue-capacity section. “The amalgamation of LICL with LEWL will enable the combined entity to leverage LICL’s robust order book of over Rs. 4500 crores and proven project execution capabilities, thereby expanding operational scale in India, and enhancing competitiveness in bidding for and executing larger, multidisciplinary contracts.”
- *Scheme* — The businesses are presented as overlapping rather than distinct, which is the stated reason to combine instead of keep apart. “Considering the complementary capabilities, overlapping customer base and shared execution requirements of the manufacturing/engineering business and the infrastructure/construction business, the proposed restructuring would enable the combined entity to leverage LICL's robust order book of over ₹4,500 crores together with LEWL's proven manufacturing and project execution capabilities, thereby expanding operational scale, achieving focused management, consolidating technical and financial resources, and enhancing competitiveness in bidding for and executing larger, multidisciplinary contracts across the sector.”
- *Scheme* — Problem named: a complicated multi-entity group structure creating compliance burden and weaker governance/transparency. “The amalgamation will result in a simplified shareholding and group structure, thereby streamlining the ever-evolving regulatory compliance framework.”
- *Scheme* — Problem named: cash and capital trapped in separate entities, a smaller balance sheet and higher cost of borrowing. “The combined entity will have enhanced financial strengths with large net worth, strong asset base and balance sheet, greater efficiency in cash management, unfettered access to cash flow generated by the combined businesses, efficient capital allocation and better capital utilization.”
- *Scheme* — Problem named: duplicated functions and dispersed management across the four companies; cost synergies and compliance-cost reduction are the claimed fix. “The combined entity will have greater operational efficiency through elimination of duplication/redundant functions, centralized and focused management, consolidating and optimizing resources under a unified leadership;”
- *Scheme* — The explicit valuation claim made to shareholders. “The Scheme is expected to unlock value for shareholders by creating a larger and more diversified entity with a stronger combined asset base, enhanced technical and financial capabilities, and improved market positioning across the hydrocarbon, steel, power, marine, nuclear and infrastructure sectors.”
- *Scheme* — Consideration for LICL: 1,798 LEWL shares per 1,500 LICL shares, giving Streamland Estate LLP 36,19,97,330 LEWL shares and Pravriddhi Trust 59,93,333, both classified as Public; nothing is issued for wholly owned TIPL. ““1,798 (One Thousand Seven Hundred Ninety-Eight) equity shares having face value of INR1/- each of the Transferee Company for every 1,500 (One Thousand Five Hundred) equity shares having face value of INR 1/- each held in the Transferor Company 1 (“Share Exchange Ratio”)””
- *Scheme* — Lenders were asked only for consent, not drivers of the deal: NOCs obtained from the listed company's banks and no conditions attached. “There are no conditions imposed by the lenders in relation to the proposed Scheme.”
- *Scheme* — Creditors of LEWL (₹104.55 cr across 1,012 unsecured creditors) backed it unanimously on 16 October 2026 — 758,413,241 votes polled, 72.54% of outstanding, 100% in favour, zero against. “The resolution set out in the Hon'ble NCLT Convened Meeting Notice has been duly passed, through e-voting, with the requisite majority by the Unsecured Creditors of the Company.”
- *Scheme* — A related-party overlap is disclosed: LEWL non-executive director Balasubramanian Prabhakaran is promoter of Thriveni Earthmovers (8.64% public shareholder of LEWL) and a partner in LICL's promoter. “Further Mr. Balasubramanian Prabhakaran is also a partner in Streamland Estate LLP who is a promoter of LICL, an entity forming part of the Scheme, First Applicant Company.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No earnings calls supplied; no separation/demerger exists in these texts. Filings never quantify synergies, cost savings, margin or borrowing-cost impact, dilution, or investor/lender demand.
