## MANKIND — Mankind Pharma Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a scheme of arrangement whose nature the documents on file do not settle) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 5.0/10 · scheme (nature unclear) · 9 filing(s) from NSE, NSE-deep · first 2026-04-13, latest 2026-10-26

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Broadway Hospitality Services, a wholly owned hospitality subsidiary, sold outright for cash; no demerger or scheme — class `unrelated`.

- *Insiders:* Buyers "do not belong to the Promoter or Promoter Group of the Company"; transaction "would not fall within related party transactions". No promoter stake in buyer stated.
- *What it reveals:* Broadway contributed 0.07% of turnover (₹9.63 crores) and 0.24% of net worth (₹38.99 crores); sold for ₹49.00 crores, above its carrying net worth. Immaterial to Mankind's value.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — Cash sale to a third party; no shares distributed to shareholders, so no new listed stock to be sold.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* The Share Purchase Agreement and closing intimation, for final consideration after closing adjustments.
- *In their words:* “As part of the Company’s strategy to divest it’s non-core assets, the Board of Directors of the Company at its meeting held today i.e. July 11, 2026, has approved the divestment of 100% stake in Broadway, to AKRK Projects LLP and Partners and authorised for execution of Share Purchase Agreement.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Nothing in these texts describes a demerger, spin-off or NCLT scheme; what management actually explains are three narrower separations plus a new offshore holding vehicle. (1) The Consumer Healthcare/OTC business was carved out into a wholly-owned subsidiary of Mankind Pharma (announced on the Q2 FY25 call, first quarter of reporting as a separate segment in Q3 FY25) because OTC is a 'push' business whose channel economics and culture differ from prescription — Rajeev Juneja identified 'a mixed kind of a culture where one guy, one leader is taking care of OTC and pharma both' as the thing being fixed, alongside cutting stockist numbers from a few thousand, stopping cash-and-carry trade that was causing rate-cutting in the market, and pushing modern trade/e-commerce (9% of OTC sales in FY25 to 13% in FY26, growing 40–57%). (2) The numbers cited for OTC: INR232 cr (+20%) in Q2 FY25, INR193 cr (+30%) in Q3 FY25, INR809 cr (+15%) FY25, INR879 cr (+9%) FY26 with Q4 FY26 at INR213 cr (+20%); roughly 7% of company revenue at 18–20% EBITDA versus company guidance of 25–26%, which Abhishek Agarwal said is 'not going to contribute or significantly, you can say, dilute the overall margins.' (3) Separately, BSV's inherited TTK branded-generic prescription portfolio was separated out of BSV and slump-sold into Mankind (slump-sale notification flagged in Q1 FY26, transition effective 1 November 2025) on the logic that BSV should hold only super-specialty, high-entry-barrier biologics (Anti-D, Foligraf, HMG, ASVS, recombinants, immunoglobulins) while branded generics belong on Mankind's 'Delhi Mankind' platform, which 'understands the Rx business better.' (4) The TTK fix was quantified: three divisions collapsed into one, 600-plus field staff reduced to 440 by March 2025 and then ~325, MR productivity up from ~INR2 lakh PCPM to ~INR2.9 lakh, BSV blended PCPM 6.5 lakh versus above INR8 lakh excluding TTK, against TTK turnover that had collapsed from INR197 cr to INR104 cr (FY24 to FY25) after inventory corrections; total BSV synergies were guided at INR50–100 cr over 12–24 months, with margins 26–28% rising 50–100 bps a year toward 30% by FY30. Stamp duty on that intra-group slump sale was booked as an exceptional item in Q3 FY26, part of why reported EBITDA margin was 22.9% against adjusted 25.9%. (5) The third strand is non-core divestment to delever after the INR10,000 cr BSV debt raise: Mahananda Spa & Resorts sold for INR562 cr on 11 February 2025 (against a INR600–650 cr target for the two hospitality units), Broadway Hospitality Services approved for 100% sale to AKRK Projects LLP for INR49 cr on 11 July 2026 (FY26 revenue INR9.63 cr, 0.07% of company; net worth INR38.99 cr), BSV's surplus Hyderabad land being returned to the authorities with a INR13 cr impairment, and the dormant Sri Lanka subsidiary wound up on 13 April 2026. (6) No investor, lender or partner is recorded as asking for any of this: the demand side is management's own 'prudent financial strategy' and promoter long-termism, with shareholder-approved INR3,000 cr QIP proceeds, net debt down to INR3,932 cr and 1.1x adjusted EBITDA at Q4 FY26, and full acquisition-debt retirement targeted by FY28. (7) Forward-looking, the 11 July 2026 board also approved a Netherlands wholly-owned SPV (up to EUR 5 million) to hold R&D assets and do niche-therapy business development through JVs or strategic interests — i.e. ring-fencing innovation risk outside the operating company, alongside the Vadodara biotech plant funded via up to INR500 cr into Mankind Medicare, the manufacturing arm.

**How it evolved:** The idea surfaced on the Nov 2024 (Q2 FY25) call, where OTC was said to have been carved into a wholly-owned subsidiary for its 'next phase of growth' and, in the same breath, TTK was described as 'not a core BSV kind of a business' that 'will be separated out'; Ashutosh Dhawan simultaneously named Mahananda and Broadway as hospitality units being liquidated to retire debt. Jan 2025 reported the first post-carve-out OTC quarter (+30%) and explained the TTK shift as Mankind 'understanding the Rx business better'; May 2025 confirmed Mahananda's INR562 cr sale and framed the move as 'integration of BSV's prescription business into Mankind's platform'; Aug 2025 disclosed the formal slump-sale notification. Nov 2025 gave the field-force and PCPM metrics, Feb 2026 confirmed the 1 November 2025 transition, the stamp-duty exceptional and the Hyderabad land impairment, and May 2026 moved on to the Vadodara biotech build via Mankind Medicare. The filings then extend the same non-core logic: Sri Lanka WOS wound up 13 April 2026, and on 11 July 2026 Broadway sold for INR49 cr while a Netherlands R&D SPV was approved — so the plan migrated from fixing acquired businesses to housing new R&D risk offshore.

**What management expects from it:** OTC subsidiary: own leadership and culture, cleaner channel (stockists cut, cash-and-carry stopped, e-com/MT 9%→13%), double-digit growth, 18–20% EBITDA scaling to company average. BSV: retains only super-specialty high-entry-barrier biologics, 26–28% margins rising 50–100 bps yearly toward 30%. Mankind: TTK branded generics on its Rx platform, PCPM INR2→2.9 lakh, INR50–100 cr synergies. Divestments fund deleveraging to 1.1x, debt-free by FY28.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *CALL Nov 2024* — First announcement of the OTC/Consumer Healthcare carve-out into a wholly-owned subsidiary, justified purely on the business's untapped potential; OTC revenue that quarter was INR232 cr, up 20% YoY. “We believe this business has a huge potential, and hence, we have carved out our OTC business to a wholly owned subsidiary of Mankind Pharma, which sets this business for next phase of growth.”
- *CALL Nov 2024* — On the same call Rajeev Juneja said BSV's inherited TTK prescription business was not core to BSV and would be separated out, and that Mankind's arrival would accelerate everything else at BSV. “TTK business will come, which is not a core BSV kind of a business, will be separated out - I mean, the right things will happen.”
- *CALL Nov 2024* — The non-core divestment track was set out at the same time: two hospitality units (Mahananda and Broadway) were already in liquidation, targeted at INR600–650 cr of proceeds explicitly earmarked for repaying the INR10,000 cr BSV acquisition debt. “So these are the two hospitality units, one is the name of Mahananda, separate entity and one is broadway which are in the process of being liquidated.”
- *CALL Nov 2024* — Management mapped the overlap it expected between BSV and Mankind at only 5–10%, with TTK the single place needing restructuring because its 3–4 divisions sold branded prescription products that belong on Mankind's Delhi platform. “We see 5 - 10% overlapping that's all, nothing more.”
- *CALL Jan 2025* — First quarter of OTC operating as a separate subsidiary, framed as unlocking its 'true potential'; revenue rose 30% YoY to INR193 cr in Q3 FY25 and 15% to INR631 cr for 9M FY25. “This has been the first quarter of the OTC business post carving out the same into wholly-owned subsidiary of Mankind to maximize its true potential.”
- *CALL Jan 2025* — Rajeev Juneja gave the clearest statement of the problem the OTC separation solves — one leader running both OTC and pharma produced a mixed culture, alongside too many distributors; growth followed the split. “I mean, it was number of distributors, whether hiving off, bringing different talent, making sure that it's not a mixed kind of a culture where one guy, one leader is taking care of OTC and pharma both.”
- *CALL Jan 2025* — Prakash Agarwal explained the TTK/Rx shift as a capability argument plus field-force and portfolio rationalisation: a very small division carrying more than 600 people, with hygiene of the business as the stated goal. “So there is a significant restructuring going in the Rx business, that is the TTK business of the BSV. Because we understand Rx business better, that is getting shifted to Mankind.”
- *CALL May 2025* — The structural logic was spelled out: TTK's branded prescription brands sit naturally in Delhi Mankind, while BSV retains only super-specialty, high-entry-barrier products; by March 2025 TTK's three divisions were one and headcount had gone from 600+ to 440. “When we acquired BSV, it came to us with TTK products - prescription brands, which we have integrated in Mankind because for that, Delhi Mankind is an appropriate company.”
- *CALL May 2025* — Completion of the first non-core separation was confirmed, with proceeds recycled into deleveraging and the accounts split into continuing and discontinued operations. “Also, as committed, we have monetized our noncore asset that is Mahananda Spa and Resorts Private Limited for a cash consideration of INR562 crores on 11th of February 2025.”
- *CALL Aug 2025* — The TTK transfer was formalised as a slump sale, with Mankind's office to run it entirely because it is a branded-generic business; Rajeev Juneja listed it among promises delivered, alongside the QIP, the Mahananda sale and the new biologics plant. “Actually, some growth is there. We are not calling out the number, but there is some growth, especially in the international business and also in the specialty.”
- *CALL Aug 2025* — Rajeev Juneja presented the TTK shift to Mankind as one of a checklist of structural commitments already executed — QIP, hotel sale, TTK transfer, second biologics plant, R&D expansion. “We said that TTK prescription business will be shifted to Mankind. It has been done.”
- *CALL Nov 2025* — Quantified the synergy from separating TTK onto Mankind's operating model: field force normalised from 550-plus MRs to about 325 with productivity up roughly 45%, described as the one big synergy already played out, plus vendor/raw-material renegotiation. “So from 550-plus MRs that has been normalized to about 325 plus. Sales have started improving. We are seeing MR productivity increase from around INR2 lakh PCPM to now about INR2.9 lakh PCPM and we expect this number to grow much more in the upcoming quarters and years.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No demerger scheme, listing, shareholder entitlement or valuation-unlock case; no separate OTC subsidiary financials; no slump-sale consideration, tax or stamp-duty quantum; no investor, lender or partner demand named.

## NMDC — NMDC Ltd.

> **Listing:** RECORD DATE set; the resulting company not yet listed — resulting companies have typically listed 4–10 weeks after the record date

**The stages, as filed:** effective (2026-08-14)

**Stated in the filings:** demerged undertaking: stood transferred and vested into NMDC.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** NMDC Iron & Steel Plant (NISP), the steel-making undertaking, demerged from NMDC into NMDC Steel Limited — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* not stated; NMDC is "A GOVT. OF INDIA ENTERPRISE" and the call says NSL "was, as you know, is under the same management", with marketing then done by SAIL
- *What it reveals:* Parent is a high-margin iron ore pure-play — iron ore segment EBITDA still 42% versus 33% blended once steel trading entered — but it bankrolls the spin: INR 1,601.39 crores demerger dues plus INR 4,846.56 crores trade and other receivables from NSL
- *Selling pressure:* unclear — Documents disclose no share allotment, index treatment or shareholder detail; scheme was already effective October 13, 2022
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* NMDC Steel Limited's own results and the repayment schedule it gave this quarter for the INR 1,601.39 crores demerger receivable
- *In their words:* “Pursuant to the Scheme, the Demerged Undertaking stood transferred and vested into NMDC Steel Limited.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The business being separated is NMDC's steel-making arm — the 3 MTPA NMDC Iron & Steel Plant (NISP) at Nagarnar, Chhattisgarh — which was demerged out of NMDC Limited into a separate listed company, NMDC Steel Limited (NSL), under a Scheme of Arrangement sanctioned by the MCA on 6 October 2022 (effective 13 October 2022, appointed date 1 April 2021), leaving NMDC as a pure mining company and NSL as the vehicle the Government of India intends to privatise, with NMDC retaining a 10% stake. Management never presented a board-level strategic case on these calls; the reasons they did give are (a) the demerger is a government/DIPAM-driven disinvestment, run by GCOM/'Deepam' and not by NMDC — the draft SPA was shown to NMDC, which 'gave the go ahead' — and management repeatedly said it has 'no visibility' on it, (b) a deliberate corporate policy that NMDC will not build any more steel plants after Nagarnar (the reason the 2,857-acre Karnataka/KVSL land bought for a 3 MTPA plant was left stranded with ₹639.61 crores paid to KIADB and still unresolved as of Jun 2026), and (c) identity as a merchant miner rather than an end-consumer of its own ore, which management said in Aug 2024 put NMDC 'in a more comfortable, more reassuring space' than peers when the Supreme Court retrospective-royalty judgment landed. The numbers they cited for the drag steel puts on the miner are blunt: consolidated EBITDA margin fell from 42% to 33% purely because of the steel business, while standalone iron ore stayed at 42% (Jun 2026); ₹2,502.64 crores of pre-demerger expenses were incurred by NMDC on NSL's behalf (₹901.25 crores repaid, ₹1,601.39 crores still outstanding); NSL and RINL were the only two credit accounts behind receivables of about ₹7,800 crores at FY25 (NSL trade receivables ₹4,499.20 crores plus ₹167.53 crores employee costs and ₹179.83 crores HR-coil advance at Jun 2026); and these advances earn NMDC no interest at all ('No we cannot. This is not a deposit'). Post-demerger NMDC supplies NSL at arm's length — about 5 million tonnes of ore at NSL's 3 MTPA peak, roughly 10% of NMDC sales rising to ~13% of Bailadila — and management insisted the ore relationship survives any change of ownership because Bailadila, 131 km away, stays the nearest source. Separation also lets each side run its own plan: NMDC's ₹50,000–70,000 crores capex to 100 million tonnes by FY30, coal (Tokisud, Rohne), rare earths/critical minerals and overseas acquisitions; NSL as a lean, low-manpower, energy-efficient single-blast-furnace producer targeting ~25% EBITDA at ~90% utilisation.

**How it evolved:** The demerger was already done before this window (MCA sanction Oct 2022), so the calls track the privatisation and the unwinding of entanglement rather than the decision: in Nov 2023 management said multiple offers had come, the draft SPA had been discussed and cleared from NMDC's side, but progress stalled around the Chhattisgarh election and questions should go to 'Deepam'; in Feb 2024 it said the sale was 'being driven by GCOM and not by us' with 'huge amount of interest' and no visibility, and investors flagged that halted privatisation news had dented confidence. By Jun 2024 management stated the deliberate policy of no more steel plants after Nagarnar (stranding the Karnataka land) and spoke of 'a blueprint' for taking NMDC and NSL separately to the next level, while Aug 2024 and Feb 2025 handled the sale as a given — ore sourcing unaffected by ownership, the retained 10% stake monetisable only 'as and when it is proposed to the disinvestment', a 'hypothetical question'. From Jun 2025 to Jun 2026 the privatisation dropped out of the discussion entirely and the talk became operational cleanup: NSL under 'the same management', marketing routed ~60% through SAIL, HR-coil trading by NMDC as a one-off cash-flow bridge, pre-demerger dues down from ₹2,500 crores to ₹1,800 crores at ~₹100 crores a month, and the steel business shown as the sole cause of EBITDA falling from 42% to 33%.

**What management expects from it:** NMDC: a pure-play miner at 42-43% EBITDA (vs 33% blended), undiluted by steel, funding ₹50,000-70,000 crores capex to 100 mt by FY30 plus coal, rare earths and overseas assets from internal accruals; receivables and ₹1,601 crores demerger dues liquidated in 1.5-2 years. NSL: a lean, energy-efficient 3 MTPA plant reaching ~25% EBITDA at ~90% utilisation, privatised by the government, with NMDC's 10% stake monetised then.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The separation is a formal demerger of the Nagarnar steel plant (NISP) out of NMDC into NMDC Steel Limited, sanctioned by the MCA with an appointed date of 1 April 2021, under which NMDC held the undertaking in trust for NSL between appointed and effective dates. “The Scheme of Arrangement for the demerger of NMDC Iron & Steel Plant (NISP) from NMDC Limited (NMDC) into NMDC Steel Limited (NSL), along with their respective shareholders and creditors, was sanctioned by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) on October 6, 2022.”
- *Scheme* — The trust arrangement left NMDC funding NSL: ₹2,502.64 crores of pre-demerger expenses with no repayment schedule in the Scheme, of which ₹1,601.39 crores was still outstanding at 30 June 2026, on top of ₹4,499.20 crores of iron-ore trade receivables, ₹167.53 crores of employee costs and a ₹179.83 crores HR-product advance. “As per the terms, NMDC shall act in trust for NSL and accordingly, an amount of ₹ 2,502.64 crores was incurred by NMDC on behalf of NSL with no specific repayment schedule defined in the scheme.”
- *[Nov 2023](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=23b38a68-2cf4-46ae-b390-053574a8f788.pdf)* — Asked about the divestment, management said the process belongs to the government's disinvestment department, not NMDC — it had cleared the draft SPA from its side, several offers had come, and progress stalled around the Chhattisgarh election. “As of now we do not have a clear visibility on that issue so in fact we should be referring that to Deepam.”
- *[Feb 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=dfea6f9a-6c27-4c49-b82b-42e73bd676c3.pdf)* — Management reiterated it is a government-run sale handled by GCOM, with strong bidder interest in what it called a state-of-the-art plant, while NMDC concentrated only on ramping production. “Of course when it was being driven, it is being driven by GCOM and not by us we were aware that there is a huge amount of interest in that very special interest and rightly so it is the state of the art plant.”
- *[Jun 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=5e9aaa09-2c0a-4d36-a166-16fda2d13b82.pdf)* — The underlying corporate rationale management did state: NMDC will not build any more steel plants after Nagarnar — which is why the 2,857-acre Karnataka (KVSL) land bought for a 3 MTPA plant, with ₹639.61 crores paid to KIADB, was left without a use and handed to consultants. “So that -- now we are left with finding out alternatives.”
- *[Jun 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=5e9aaa09-2c0a-4d36-a166-16fda2d13b82.pdf)* — Management framed NMDC and NSL as two separately steered companies with their own growth blueprints rather than one integrated group. “We plan to take both the companies NMDC and NSL to the next level, and we are -- it's not an ad hoc plan.”
- *[Jun 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=5e9aaa09-2c0a-4d36-a166-16fda2d13b82.pdf)* — The inter-company funding is uncompensated — the ₹2,500-2,600 crores of pre-demerger expenses plus ~₹1,300 crores of ore credit carry no interest because they are not deposits under Section 186, so the drag sat entirely on NMDC's balance sheet. “No we cannot. This is not a deposit.”
- *[Aug 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=8f0c6243-39ec-440d-9769-a91a846cceae.pdf)* — Post-demerger, ore to the steel plant is an arm's-length sale, not an internal transfer, sized at about 5 million tonnes at NSL's 3 MTPA peak — roughly 10% of NMDC's total sales and ~13% of Bailadila. “No. It's not an internal, it's an arm length sale.”
- *[Aug 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=8f0c6243-39ec-440d-9769-a91a846cceae.pdf)* — Asked directly whether selling NSL to a private buyer would hurt NMDC, management said ore sourcing is unaffected by ownership because Bailadila, 131 km away, remains the nearest source versus Odisha. “So I don't think -- the sourcing of material irrespective of the ownership, whether it's stays with us or it doesn't stay with us irrespective of the ownership Bailadila will remain.”
- *[Aug 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=8f0c6243-39ec-440d-9769-a91a846cceae.pdf)* — On the Supreme Court retrospective mining-levy judgment (~₹2,500-2,600 crores Karnataka, ₹144 crores Chhattisgarh, ₹21 crores Panna), management argued a pure merchant miner is structurally better placed than an integrated miner-consumer because levies pass through to customers. “As I have -- hopefully I've been able to clarify that as merchant miners we are in a more comfortable, more reassuring space than maybe those -- our counterparts who are also the end consumer of what they mine.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=f42a4267-f360-4c1f-8185-e7cd6977d8c1.pdf)* — On monetising the residual 10% NMDC holds in NSL and recovering receivables, management treated the timing as entirely the government's call and the question as hypothetical; recovery was tied only to NSL reaching breakeven at 2-2.5 rakes a day. “The 10% equity stake is as and when it is proposed to the disinvestment on which I don't have much of idea as of now.”
- *[Jun 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=02a75b47-ed37-46b9-8ef9-aaee3eb65d39.pdf)* — FY25 receivables ballooned to about ₹7,800 crores driven by just two state-owned counterparties, NSL and RINL, with ~₹50 crores of expected-credit-loss provisioning taken; NSL had begun repaying ~₹200 crores a month. “There are only two accounts. One is RINL, the other is NSL. We don't sell on credit to any other people.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No board/government rationale, no valuation-unlock or synergy-loss math, no disinvestment timeline or price, no explanation why NMDC kept funding NSL interest-free post-demerger.

## POWERINDIA — Hitachi Energy India Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a filing's text names a demerger; no scheme filing names it yet) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 5.0/10 · spin-off · 1 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-07-31, latest 2026-07-31

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'meetings' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**The stages, as filed:** meetings (2026-07-31)

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** not stated — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* Haka's shareholding in Company NIL; directors/KMP interested only via shareholdings in Hitachi Japan; RSU replaces cash LTIP, 3-year vesting, grants Hitachi Japan shares, not Company shares.
- *What it reveals:* Documents show a strong, cash-rich entity: paid-up capital Rs 8.91 Crores against free reserves Rs 5,168.42 Crores, Rs 8/share (400%) dividend, record backlog Rs 29,555.3 Crores, FY26 PAT Rs 987.8 Crores, negligible finance cost.
- *Selling pressure:* unclear — Demerger appears only as a past scheme; no size, index-exclusion or shareholder-distribution detail is given.
- *Parent or spin:* spin · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* The Scheme of Arrangement (Demerger) itself, plus FY26 audited financial statements behind the Rs 5,168.42 Crores free reserves.
- *In their words:* “Pursuant to the Scheme of Arrangement (Demerger), 1,07,421 equity shares were allotted directly to the IEPF account.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Nothing in these texts announces or explains POWERINDIA separating, demerging, spinning off or divesting a business — the premise is not supported by the seven supplied transcripts or the one AGM filing, and I am not importing anything from memory. The only 'separation' management actually describes is internal and organisational: the carve-out of Service into a standalone fifth business unit effective 1 April 2025, sitting alongside the four existing BUs (Transformers, High Voltage Products, Grid Integration, Grid Automation), mirroring a 'separate global BU Service' at Hitachi Energy — no new legal entity, no share issuance, no record date, no NCLT scheme, no listed-entity restructuring. The reasons given for that carve-out were an aging installed base (Venu cited 'Rs.60,000 crores worth of installed base in India since last 75 years' in the May 2025 call; the Feb 2025 slide said 'approximately Rs. (+80,000) crores'), the urgency of the energy transition, an 'ever evolving workforce' and the organisational shift to digitalization. The prize was sized at roughly Rs. 2,000 crores of service orders per year against a then run-rate of Rs. 500–600 crores, described as a 3-to-5-year journey; service was 7.4% of FY25 orders, 11–12% in individual quarters, and 'high single digit' thereafter, with service orders up ~60% YoY in FY25 and ~90% YoY in Q1 FY26. The problems it was said to solve were fragmented lifecycle engagement and an inconsistent customer experience ('develop service and digital proficiency and unify the customer service experience'), plus new-age customers such as data centres wanting a 'life cycle partner' rather than only equipment supply. It was also explicitly a margin lever, named by Venu alongside volume/fixed-cost leverage, exports and pricing excellence in the road map to and beyond double-digit EBITDA. Nobody asked for a separation: no investor, lender, analyst or partner in any call requests one — analysts instead pressed on margins versus peers, the ~4% royalty, admin and other expenses (Dhavan Shah even suggested cutting royalty and raising dividend instead), and management defended the royalty and promised operating leverage rather than any structural split. The single occurrence of the word 'demerger' anywhere in the record is a backward-looking administrative reference in the 31 July 2026 AGM notice to the Scheme of Arrangement that created the company, cited only to explain 1,07,421 shares allotted to the IEPF account, with no rationale attached.

**How it evolved:** The idea first surfaced on the Jan 30, 2025 call (tagged Feb 2025), where Venu said the company 'will work towards a new service business unit' as a fifth BU from 1 April 2025 and framed it against the aging installed base and digitalization. It was confirmed as launched on the May 15, 2025 call (installed base Rs. 60,000 crores, potential Rs. 2,000 crores of orders per year versus Rs. 500–600 crores today), described as 'carved out' on the Jul 30, 2025 call, and reframed on the Nov 7, 2025 call as a top-line and bottom-line margin lever. By Feb 5, 2026 it was a 'separate global BU Service including in India' with the stated aim of 'shifting center of gravity' toward export, service and digital; by May 26, 2026 service was merely a 'key pillar' and the only structural news ran the other way — Rs. 2,000 crores of additional capex (Rs. 4,000 crores cumulative) and a greenfield Karjan transformer plant, i.e. consolidation and expansion inside one entity, not separation.

**What management expects from it:** Only for the internal Service BU: convert a Rs. 60,000–80,000 crore installed base into roughly Rs. 2,000 crores of orders a year, lift both top line and bottom line, help sustain double-digit and then ~15% EBITDA, shift mix toward service, export and digital, and lock in life-cycle partnerships with data-centre and industrial customers. No entity-level margin, capital or valuation claims are made.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=52cee7d2-456e-4877-8323-d66fcab09759.pdf)* — First mention of any carve-out: a new Service business unit, the fifth BU, to start 1 April 2025, justified by an aging installed base of 'approximately Rs. (+80,000) crores', the energy-transition urgency, an evolving workforce and the shift to digitalization; explicitly 'the first step to develop service and digital proficiency and unify the customer service experience'. No legal separation of any business is mentioned. “In our ambition to enhance customer experience with a strengthened and future-focused service system globally, we will work towards a new service business unit from the coming financial year of 2025-2026.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=8e6cad37-2825-4ec7-973d-e1b216797368.pdf)* — Launch confirmed as an internal business unit covering the whole asset life cycle; Venu sized the India installed base at Rs. 60,000 crores over 75 years, the annual order potential at Rs. 2,000 crores versus a current Rs. 500–600 crores, and called it a 3-to-5-year journey. Service was 7.4% of FY25 orders (up ~60% YoY). No entity separation discussed. “Furthermore, foreseeing immense potential in service and maintenance, the company has introduced its service business unit that is the 5th business unit, from April 1st, 2025.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=3919f070-bf69-4d8a-b65a-3df11a834ca3.pdf)* — The word 'carved out' is used for the first and only time, and it refers to this internal service BU, not to any business being separated from the listed company; its purpose is stated as intensifying life-cycle engagement with utilities, industries and new-age customers, with all other BUs working alongside it. Service orders grew 90% YoY. “This is also our first quarter after we carved out our new service business, effective from 1st of April, 2025, and contributed a high single digit to the overall order book.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=965bc83d-b034-4d8f-ad5b-a40a5c537d41.pdf)* — The service BU is recast as one of the explicit margin levers — listed with growth/fixed-cost leverage, export gross margin and pricing excellence — in the stated long-term plan to reach and sustain double-digit EBITDA margins. “We have created a dedicated service business unit, because we have a huge amount of install base, and we would like to leverage and then improve on both top line and bottom line.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ade5f144-1c9b-4780-82e1-f063be4c5701.pdf)* — The unit is described as a separate global BU Service replicated in India, tied to the ambition of 'shifting center of gravity' toward export, service and digital and to data-centre customers who want a life-cycle partner, not just equipment. Still no mention of separating, demerging or divesting any business. “so we created the separate global BU Service including in India and we hope that the efforts of this particular team would start fetching the results over a period of time.”
- *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=eaaedf53-be58-4291-950d-719797c5f5b1.pdf)* — The most recent call contains no separation, demerger or divestment of any kind; the structural news is the opposite — Rs. 2,000 crores of fresh board-approved capex (Rs. 4,000 crores cumulative) including a greenfield large power transformer and HVDC converter transformer plant at Karjan, Vadodara, due in Q4 CY2028, plus two added power-quality lines in Bangalore, all inside the one entity. “During our Q4FY26 Board Meeting, the Board approved an additional investment of Rs. 2,000 Crores.”
- *Scheme* — The only use of 'Demerger' in the entire record is an administrative, backward-looking reference in the 31 July 2026 AGM notice, explaining shares allotted to the IEPF account under the historical Scheme of Arrangement that formed the company (incorporated 19 February 2019). No rationale, scope, business, counterparty or financial effect is described, and the notice's five agenda items are accounts, dividend, Haka's re-appointment, cost-auditor fees and the Hitachi ESPP/RSU — none of them a separation. “Pursuant to the Scheme of Arrangement (Demerger), 1,07,421 equity shares were allotted directly to the IEPF account.”

*Not explained on the calls:* Everything about an actual separation: whether one was considered, its scope, scheme terms, standalone financials, capital allocation, valuation or re-rating case, and who wanted it.

## QUESS — Quess Corp Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a filing's text names a demerger; no scheme filing names it yet) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 5.0/10 · spin-off · 4 filing(s) from CALLS, NSE · first 2026-09-01, latest 2026-10-05

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; indicated timeline: At the AGM on August 25, 2026: "In FY25, we completed a three-way demerger. Where there was one company, there are now three separately listed companies: Quess Corp, Bluspring Enterprises and Digitide Solutions"; the Q3 FY26 call (January 29, 2026) dates the demerger "since 1st April 2024"

**Stated in the filings:** entitlement **1,889 for every 10,000**; size hint: 2% of revenue.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Technology and industrial services businesses separated from Quess's workforce/staffing core in a completed FY25 three-way demerger — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* Promoters/promoter group excluded from QSOP 2026 (52,50,000 RSUs, 3.52% of capital); CEO Lohit Bhatia holds 0.08%, gets 4,00,000 TSR-linked RSUs, CFO 1,00,000. Stake in demerged entities not stated.
- *What it reveals:* Parent is zero gross debt with ₹271 crore net cash, 20% ROE, 80% EBITDA-to-OCF; Professional Staffing (12%+ margin) and Overseas, ~14% of revenue, now give 50% of operating profit, hidden inside a 2% blended margin.
- *Selling pressure:* likely — "the stock saw some weakness immediately following the demerger"; demerged entities are technology and industrial services platforms, different industries from staffing
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Note 37.3/38.3 on disallowed 80JJAA deductions behind the modified audit opinion, plus ₹296 crore direct-tax and ₹372 crore GST contingent liabilities
- *In their words:* “While the stock saw some weakness immediately following the demerger, it has since recovered strongly and delivered a return of around 25% over the past year, although the broader Indian equity market has remained largely flat.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Management presented the separation as a three-way demerger of the old conglomerate Quess Corp — effective 1 April 2024 and legally completed during FY25 "well ahead of stated timeline" — into three separately listed companies: Quess Corp (pure-play workforce/staffing: General Staffing, Professional Staffing/IT staffing, Overseas staffing, digital platforms Hamara Jobs/Taskmo), Digitide Solutions (Global Technology Solutions — BPM, customer lifecycle management, platform/payroll/InsurTech, plus foundit and the Brainhunter US/Canada business), and Bluspring Enterprises (Operating Asset Maintenance — IFM, food & beverage incl. the acquired Archer business, security, and Vedang telecom infra, plus the Golden Star facility-management contracts). The stated reasons were a sharper strategic identity and unlocking shareholder value: four unlike platforms sitting in one listed entity were split so each would have "its own focus and its own management", be "agile, strategically focused" with their own boards and leadership teams (Quess's board was strengthened post-demerger; key leadership hires completed; Lohit Bhatia later made CEO from 1 Jan 2026 and ED/Group CEO from 1 June 2026, Neeraj Jain CFO from 3 Dec 2025). The demerger was explicitly used as the trigger for a portfolio clean-up: a "comprehensive review" led the Board and management to discontinue non-core, long-gestation, outcome-based projects in skilling and utilities (meter reading/bill distribution), producing a Q4 FY25 exceptional charge of INR 158 crore — INR 119 crore of accelerated expected credit loss on discontinued projects, INR 26 crore goodwill impairment (INR 7 crore Stellarslog, INR 19 crore Quess International Services, the repurposed Golden Star) and INR 13 crore of demerger costs (mainly stamp duty) — forfeiting roughly INR 300 crore of revenue at ~20% EBITDA margin from skilling, with Digitide likewise "rationalizing low-margin low-efficiency contracts" ahead of separation. Balance-sheet repair was part of the thesis: gross debt was cut (INR 224 crore at Dec 2024) to INR 12 crore by 31 March 2025 and zero later, leaving net cash of INR 255 crore (INR 271/273 crore subsequently), a new dividend policy of up to 75% of free cash flow over a rolling three-year block, and an adjusted ROE target crossing 20%. Management repeatedly conceded the cost: standalone EBITDA margin optically reset from the 2.4–2.5% the workforce division earned pre-demerger to 1.8%, because standalone corporate overheads now sit in Quess and because the high-margin skilling and Brainhunter businesses left, making history "noncomparable"; demerger expenses hit reported PAT by INR 22 crore in Q3 FY25, INR 13 crore in Q4 FY25 and INR 2 crore in Q1 FY26, and the stock "saw some weakness immediately following the demerger". Nothing in these texts says any investor, lender or partner asked for the separation — it is presented throughout as a management-and-Board decision, with shareholders and creditors merely approving it on 9 December 2024 and the NCLT sanctioning it; the only external parties named are the demerger-linked cross-sell partners (Quess selling Origint GCC-as-a-Service using Bluspring and Digitide capabilities).

**How it evolved:** On the 30 Jan 2025 call (Q3 FY25) the demerger was already in flight — first NCLT approval obtained, shareholder and creditor approvals secured on 9 December, INR 22 crore of demerger costs booked, leadership/controls being built per entity, and Digitide pre-emptively rationalizing low-margin contracts — with listing guided for Q1 FY26. By the 20 May 2025 call it was done "well ahead of stated timeline" and Quess held its "first earnings call as an independent entity", pairing the split with the INR 158 crore exceptional clean-up of skilling/utilities projects, zero-ish gross debt, net cash of INR 255 crore, the new 75%-of-FCF dividend policy, and a frank reset of margin guidance from 2.4–2.5% to 1.8% rising to 2%. Through 29 Jul 2025 ("pure-play staffing leader", residual INR 2 crore of demerger fees) and 29 Jan 2026 (the demerger invoked to explain why 4–4.5% historic margins are "noncomparable", and the Q4 FY25 ECL recalled as "the discontinued businesses as part of the demerger"), the story shifted from execution to justification; on 5 May 2026 management closed the loop by exiting the last non-conforming business — a 7,000-headcount milestone-based project worth ~INR 200 crore (1.3% of revenue) — citing the commitment made "closer to our demerger timeline". At the 25 Aug 2026 AGM the Chairman recast it retrospectively as value creation: three listed companies, ~INR 500 crore combined EBITDA, 600,000+ people, Quess debt-free, and a forward plan ("Quess 2.0") to lift dollar-linked revenue from 7% to 20% and Professional Staffing plus Overseas profit share from 50% to 65%.

**What management expects from it:** Quess: pure-play, single-mandate staffing with sharper focus on high-margin Professional Staffing and Overseas (now 50% of profit, targeted 65%), margin from 1.8% to 2.0–2.4%, 20% ROE, zero debt, net cash, up to 75% of free cash flow returned. Digitide and Bluspring: independent technology and industrial-services platforms with their own management; three entities together about INR 500 crore EBITDA.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ab1e6459-1459-49fc-9855-02180f47ca7d.pdf)* — With first NCLT approval in hand and shareholder/creditor approvals obtained on 9 December 2024, management framed the split as unlocking shareholder value and building separate leadership teams, internal controls and processes for each demerged entity. “Our aim is to create independent entities that are agile, strategically focused and well positioned to unlock value for all stakeholders in the long term.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ab1e6459-1459-49fc-9855-02180f47ca7d.pdf)* — Ahead of separation, the soon-to-be Digitide entity was already pruning its own book, with the stated purpose of lifting the separated company's long-term operating margin. “As a run-up to demerger, with a new entity, Digitide, we are examining our existing service lines and rationalizing low-margin low-efficiency contracts, which would give a sustainable upside to our long-term operating margins.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ab1e6459-1459-49fc-9855-02180f47ca7d.pdf)* — The demerger carried visible cash and margin costs during execution: INR 22 crore of demerger expenses in Q3 FY25 drove a 9% sequential PAT decline, and platform margins compressed on sales/leadership investment made in the run-up. “Demerger -related expenses of INR 22 crores were recognized during the quarter, which resulted in a PAT decline of 9% on a sequential basis.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=a0bbc19f-4b12-4e2e-94c9-02c1ae6af031.pdf)* — First call as a standalone company: the 3-way demerger was completed ahead of the stated timeline and sold as sharper focus plus value unlocking, alongside a seamless leadership transition (Kamal Pal Hoda moving to Bluspring as CEO, Sushanth Pai joining Quess as CFO). “This important milestone leads to a sharper focus and unlocking value, strategic transformation, and delivering sustained growth.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=a0bbc19f-4b12-4e2e-94c9-02c1ae6af031.pdf)* — The demerger was the explicit trigger for exiting non-core projects in skilling and utilities (meter reading/bill distribution), long-gestation outcome-based work the Board decided not to carry into the new structure. “As part of the demerger transformation, we have revisited some of our businesses through a comprehensive review, and we will be exiting certain non -core projects, in line with the position taken by the management and the Board to discontinue such projects pursuant to the scheme of demerger.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=a0bbc19f-4b12-4e2e-94c9-02c1ae6af031.pdf)* — That clean-up cost INR 158 crore of exceptional items in Q4 FY25 — INR 119 crore accelerated ECL on discontinued projects, INR 26 crore goodwill impairment (INR 7 crore Stellarslog, INR 19 crore Quess International Services) and INR 13 crore of demerger expenses, mainly stamp duty — with no cash outflow, and forfeited roughly INR 300 crore of ~20%-margin skilling revenue. “This has impacted reported PAT by INR 158 crores in the quarter.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=a0bbc19f-4b12-4e2e-94c9-02c1ae6af031.pdf)* — Management conceded the standalone margin optics: the workforce division earned 2.4–2.5% inside the old group, but standalone corporate overheads reset Quess to 1.8%, with a staged recovery to about 2% by the exit of FY26 (delivered: FY26 at 2.0%, Q4 FY26 at 2.2%). “I mean, if you look at the overall margin was hovering between 2.4% to 2.5% prior to demerger, specifically for the workforce as a division.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=a0bbc19f-4b12-4e2e-94c9-02c1ae6af031.pdf)* — Capital allocation was redefined around the separated entity: gross debt cut to INR 12 crore and net cash of INR 255 crore at 31 March 2025, a new policy to return up to 75% of free cash flow over a rolling three-year block, DSO improved 7 days to 37, and adjusted ROE guided above 20%. Asked about new geographies, management said focus came first. “See, as part of this demerger, Siddharth, our focus is going to be on the core businesses and how much more we can do and bring in more efficiency and stay profitable.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=6ead2617-fae8-46a9-ba34-f49155443329.pdf)* — Quess positioned itself as a pure-play staffing company, while still monetising the separation by partnering its demerged siblings: the new Origint GCC-as-a-Service line is delivered by bringing Bluspring and Digitide capabilities together on a cost-plus, asset-light basis. “So, as we strengthen our position as a pure -play staffing leader, we remain deeply committed to operational excellence, innovation and continuously evolving our offerings to meet the dynamic needs of our clients.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=30ebba67-5636-4798-a64b-0da5f7c4fda1.pdf)* — Asked why margins are ~2% versus 4–5% historically, management used the demerger to explain the break in the series — Bluspring and Digitide are out, skilling was discontinued, and Brainhunter (US/Canada) moved to Digitide. “With all of those business with high EBITDA margins, we were averaging around 4%, 4.5%, but that businesses have been discontinued and Brain hunter as part of demerger has moved into Digitide.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=30ebba67-5636-4798-a64b-0da5f7c4fda1.pdf)* — The INR 120 crore Q4 FY25 ECL was re-confirmed as demerger-driven, relating to the discontinued government skilling project, with collections still being pursued (delayed from Q3 to Q4 FY26 by a new RBI escrow process) and any recovery to be reported as upside. “If you recollect, in Q4, these were the discontinued businesses as part of the demerger that we had announced to the Street, and we had taken an exceptional credit loss on that.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=57792063-4601-4365-9e78-0dfb4c9a7d79.pdf)* — The portfolio-discipline promise made at the time of the demerger was carried through: a 7,000-headcount milestone-based project worth about INR 200 crore (1.3% of revenue) was fully exited in FY26, with no further such events known. “So, as you would remember, closer to our demerger timeline, we had said any business which does not meet the financi al metrics of the company and does not yield us the cash realization , we will exit and discontinue such businesses.”

## RELIANCE — Reliance Industries Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a filing's text names a demerger; no scheme filing names it yet) · **SPINNING — record date set; the new entity lists soon** · score 5.0/10 · spin-off · 13 filing(s) from CALLS, NSE · first 2025-12-01, latest 2026-10-24

> **Listing:** RECORD DATE set; the resulting company not yet listed — resulting companies have typically listed 4–10 weeks after the record date

**The stages, as filed:** exchange_noc (2026-08-28) → nclt_sanction (2026-01-29) → effective (2025-12-01)

**Stated in the filings:** size hint: 16.4% of ebitda.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** The Consumer Brands (FMCG) Business Undertaking, demerged from Reliance Retail Ventures Limited into Tira Beauty Limited, renamed Reliance Consumer Products Limited — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* New RCPL became an 83.56% direct subsidiary of the Company; RRVL shareholders received 1 New RCPL share for every 2 RRVL shares. Promoter/management stake and incentives in the new entity: not stated.
- *What it reveals:* A fast-scaling FMCG arm: FY26 revenue Rs.22,000 crore and Q1 FY27 Rs.8,600 crore, both roughly 2x year-ago, Campa Rs.4,700 crore, yet only "breakeven on EBITDA terms" with a Rs.1 lakh crore FY2030 target; retail's reported growth and 8% margin had carried it.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — Not listed; shares allotted to unlisted RRVL's shareholders, with RIL holding 83.56% directly, so no public float or index exclusion.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* RCPL's standalone EBITDA, which Reliance Retail's CFO said would only be disclosed "next quarter" (Jan 2026 call).
- *In their words:* “With a broad and diverse product basket ranging from classic Indian brands to new age labels, the consumer products vertical is progressing on its accelerated growth trajectory with a focused organizational structure.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The business being separated is Reliance's FMCG/consumer-brands arm. Under a composite scheme of arrangement among Reliance Retail Limited, Reliance Retail Ventures Limited (RRVL), the old Reliance Consumer Products Limited (RCPL) and Tira Beauty Limited (renamed Reliance Consumer Products Limited, 'New RCPL'), the 'Consumer Brands Business Undertaking' was demerged out of RRVL effective 1 December 2025; the old RCPL stood dissolved, RRVL shareholders received 1 New RCPL share of Rs.10 for every 2 RRVL shares of Rs.10, New RCPL's pre-scheme capital held by RRVL was cancelled without consideration, and RCPL became an 83.56% DIRECT subsidiary of RIL instead of sitting under retail — confirmed on the Jan 2026 call ('RCPL became the direct subsidiary of RIL from 1st December 2025'). The only explicit rationale management gave is organisational focus and growth speed: the 16 January 2026 media release said the consumer products vertical, 'ranging from classic Indian brands to new age labels,' is 'progressing on its accelerated growth trajectory with a focused organizational structure.' Everything else they offered was scale and investment facts that imply the logic: FMCG revenue of Rs.5,000 cr in Q3 FY26 (+60% Y-o-Y), Rs.15,000 cr for 9M FY26, Rs.22,000 cr for FY26 and Rs.7,350 cr in Q4 FY26 (both ~2x), Campa at Rs.4,700 cr (4th largest CSD brand), Independence at Rs.2,600 cr, #3 water player, Rs.8,600 cr in Q1 FY27 (2x, beverages Rs.2,900 cr, daily essentials Rs.3,200 cr, #3 NARTD), 5,000+ distributors, 3 million outlets, >80% of sales through external channels, 40 export markets, 12 plants plus integrated food parks and an acquisition run (Udhaiyam, Manna, Goodness Group, Sosyo majority, Brylcreem, Toni & Guy, Badedas, Matey) — i.e. a heavy-capex, acquisitive, breakeven-EBITDA business ('yes, we are breakeven on EBITDA terms') chasing Rs.1 lakh crore by FY2030, run through third-party general trade, which fits poorly inside a ~7.9-8.0% margin omni-channel retailer. The visible consequence management kept quantifying was the drag it removes from retail's reported growth: Q4 FY26 retail growth of 11% was 'almost 14%' adjusted for the demerger, and Q1 FY27 was 7.4% reported versus 11.6% underlying. No investor, lender or partner was named as having asked for it — the scheme was presented as done, and analysts (Harit Kapoor, Vikash Jain, Percy Panthaki) only pressed afterwards for the like-for-like revenue and EBITDA impact, which Dinesh Taluja deferred ('It is a number which is going out. It is a number as well... We will have to wait for the next quarter'). Two parallel separation tracks run alongside it: the Jio Platforms IPO (fresh issue of up to 27 crore shares, DRHP 19 June 2026, SEBI observation letter 28 August 2026, RHP 14 October 2026, priced at Rs.1,119 on 24 October 2026, with Rs.2,500 cr reserved for individual/HUF RIL shareholders and Rs.500 cr for employees), and the ring-fencing of AI/data-centre capex into RIL/'Reliance Intelligence' with JPL kept asset-light ('the AI data centers are not being done in Jio Platforms Limited').

**How it evolved:** On the Oct 2024 call the consumer-brands business was still reported inside Reliance Retail as a line item ('general trade revenues are growing at 250% plus'), with no hint of a separation. By the Jan 2026 call (16 Jan 2026) it was presented as a completed fact — 'the demerger happened on 1st December' — RCPL had become a direct RIL subsidiary, got its own presenter (Ketan Mody) and its own revenue disclosure, and the same-day media release supplied the only stated reason: 'a focused organizational structure' and an 'accelerated growth trajectory.' On the Apr 2026 and Jul 2026 calls the demerger appeared only as a base adjustment to retail growth (11% reported vs ~14% adjusted; 7.4% vs 11.6%), while RCPL's own disclosure escalated to Rs.22,000 cr FY26 revenue, EBITDA breakeven and a Rs.1 lakh crore FY2030 target. In parallel, the Jio Platforms listing moved from 'imminent' and 'awaiting the new notification from the government' (Jan/Apr 2026) to DRHP on 19 June 2026 and pricing at Rs.1,119 on 24 October 2026.

**What management expects from it:** For RCPL: a focused structure and accelerated growth — 2x revenue run-rate toward Rs.1 lakh crore by FY2030, margin improving from EBITDA breakeven as food parks, beverage lines and distribution (5,000 distributors, 3m outlets) scale. For retail: cleaner reported growth (11.6% vs 7.4%) and undiluted focus on omni-channel/hyperlocal. For JPL: public market pricing (Rs.1,119) with RIL shareholders and employees given reserved allotments, and an asset-light P&L.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The 1 Dec 2025 filing sets out the mechanics: the Consumer Brands Business Undertaking is demerged from RRVL into Tira Beauty Limited (renamed RCPL), with a 1-for-2 share entitlement to RRVL shareholders. “Further, in terms of the Scheme, as consideration for the demerger of the Consumer Brands Business Undertaking from RRVL to New RCPL, New RCPL will allot 1 (one) fully paid-up equity share of Rs. 10 (Rupees ten only) each for every 2 (two) fully paid-up equity shares of Rs. 10 (Rupees ten only) each of RRVL, to the shareholders of RRVL.”
- *Scheme* — The same filing confirms the old RCPL was dissolved and that the effect of the scheme is to move FMCG out from under retail and make it a direct RIL subsidiary at 83.56%. “Accordingly, New RCPL will become 83.56% direct subsidiary of the Company.”
- *Scheme* — The 16 January 2026 media release carries the only stated strategic reason: a focused organisational structure to accelerate the consumer products vertical's growth (Mukesh Ambani's commentary on the quarter). “With a broad and diverse product basket ranging from classic Indian brands to new age labels, the consumer products vertical is progressing on its accelerated growth trajectory with a focused organizational structure.”
- *[Jan 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=26290395-526a-441f-a347-c8ac12e4adf3.pdf)* — Srikanth confirmed the demerger date and the scale of the separated business — over Rs.5,000 crore of quarterly turnover, up 60% Y-o-Y — in the same breath as announcing it. “On the FMCG side, the demerger happened on 1st December.”
- *[Jan 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=26290395-526a-441f-a347-c8ac12e4adf3.pdf)* — Ketan Mody opened the FMCG section by restating the new ownership position: RCPL now reports directly to RIL, not to Reliance Retail, with 9M FY26 revenue of Rs.15,000 crore. “So RCPL became the direct subsidiary of RIL from 1st December 2025.”
- *[Jan 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=26290395-526a-441f-a347-c8ac12e4adf3.pdf)* — Asked by Vikash Jain and Harit Kapoor to size the revenue and EBITDA that leaves retail, Dinesh Taluja conceded there is an EBITDA number going out but refused to quantify it. “No, it is a number which is going out. It is a number as well.”
- *[Apr 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=971d8c86-397a-4780-b843-5a84d3006d0b.pdf)* — The demerger is now used mainly to explain away retail's reported growth: Q4 FY26 retail growth of 11% becomes almost 14% once RCPL's exit is adjusted for. “Now, if you recollect, RCPL business was demerged out in the last quarter adjusted for that, the growth is almost 14%, for the full year the growth is 12% and if you exclude RCPL demerger the growth would be even higher.”
- *[Apr 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=971d8c86-397a-4780-b843-5a84d3006d0b.pdf)* — Ashutosh Goyal gave the first full-year standalone FMCG numbers post-demerger — Rs.22,000 crore FY26 revenue (2x), Campa at Rs.4,700 crore, Independence at Rs.2,600 crore, presence in 40 countries. “In terms of Camp a brand , we delivered a revenue of Rs.4700 Crores making it fourth largest carbonated soft drink brands in the country in a very short span of time.”
- *[Jul 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=c9d3d96a-8b04-4b41-b454-3f98d1f90702.pdf)* — A full quarter after the carve-out, retail's reported 7.4% growth versus 11.6% underlying shows the mechanical hit to the retail entity's optics from the separation. “Adjusted for that, the underlying revenue growth is 11.6%. On a reported basis, the growth is 7.4%.”
- *[Jul 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=c9d3d96a-8b04-4b41-b454-3f98d1f90702.pdf)* — Asked by Vikash Jain for FMCG profitability, Ketan Mody confirmed the separated entity is only at EBITDA breakeven and is deliberately prioritising share and supply chain over margin, against a Rs.1 lakh crore FY2030 target. “EBI TDA, I would put it across since the concentration there, yes, we are breakeven on EBITDA terms, but EBITDA will improve as a scale and all the supply chain is kind of put it across but yes, right now the concentration more on the market share and on the daily essentials part, we have Independence , we have equally Good Life also, so it is all put together.”
- *[Oct 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=0e6309fa-450f-4db6-88b2-d76d9a3ff756.pdf)* — Baseline before the separation: consumer brands were a sub-line of Reliance Retail's results, with no separation discussion at all. “Consumer brands business continues to scale up very nicely.”
- *Scheme* — A parallel separation track: JPL's board approved the DRHP on 19 June 2026 for a fresh issue of up to 27 crore shares, with the RHP later reserving up to Rs.2,500 crore for individual RIL shareholders and Rs.500 crore for employees. “The Board of Directors of Jio Platforms Limited (JPL), a material subsidiary of the Company, has today , i.e., June 19 , 2026, approved the Draft Red Herring Prospectus ("DRHP") to be filed with the Securities and Exchange Board of India, BSE Limited and National Stock Exchange of India Limited in connection with its proposed Initial Public Offer by way of a fresh issue of up to 27,00,00,000 (twenty seven crore) equity shares of face value of Rs. 10 each”

*Not explained on the calls:* No valuation, no RCPL standalone P&L or EBITDA drag quantified, no explanation of the 1:2 ratio, 83.56% stake, Tira vehicle, listing plans, or who requested it.

## SCI — Shipping Corporation of India Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a filing's text names a demerger; no scheme filing names it yet) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 5.0/10 · spin-off · 3 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-02-06, latest 2026-02-06

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** 192 non-core assets (land/property) transferred to a separate asset company, 185 leased back to SCI — class `regulatory_strategic`.

- *Insiders:* Not stated for stakes; management says "SCILAL is a separate legal entity, and this is a matter where Government, our Ministry will take decision if at all anything is there."
- *What it reveals:* Separates 192 non-core land assets from the shipping fleet ahead of Government strategic disinvestment; SCI retains use via leaseback of 185 assets treated as short-term lease pending a final agreement; consolidated NAV ~Rs 300/share.
- *Selling pressure:* unclear — Documents give no SCILAL listing, size, shareholding or index treatment; only that it is a separate legal entity.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Note 8 / final lease agreement and DIPAM disinvestment status; any Ministry decision on SCILAL reverse merger.
- *In their words:* “Pursuant to approval of demerger scheme by MCA vide its order dated 22.02.2023, 192 non-core assets were transferred from the Company (Demerged Company) to Shipping Corporation of India Land and Assets Limited (Resulting Company) (hereinafter referred to as SCILAL) w.e.f. 01 April 2021 and 185 non-core assets are leased back to the demerged company, has been treated as short term lease, pending execution of final agreement and disinvestment process as detailed in note no. 7.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The business being separated is not a shipping line but SCI's non-core land and property portfolio, carved out into a separate listed-to-be entity, Shipping Corporation of India Land and Assets Limited (SCILAL), with SCI as the 'Demerged Company' and SCILAL as the 'Resulting Company'. The filings state the mechanics precisely: MCA approved the demerger scheme by order dated 22.02.2023, 192 non-core assets were transferred from SCI to SCILAL with effect from 01 April 2021, and 185 of those assets are leased back to SCI so that the shipping operations can keep using the premises they occupy. The stated reason the separation exists is the Government of India's strategic disinvestment of SCI: note 7 says the process is being run by the Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM) with a Transaction Advisor, that the Preliminary Information Memorandum inviting expressions of interest was released on 22.12.2020, and that the Virtual Data Room is open and being managed by the Transaction Advisor for due diligence by Qualified Interested Parties — i.e. the buyer is being sold the shipping company, and the real estate is being kept out of the sale. So the asker is the owner-seller (the Government, via DIPAM and its Transaction Advisor) and the audience is prospective strategic bidders, not lenders or JV partners; no investor on either call asked for it. The problem it solves, as the documents frame it, is that the land and buildings are 'non-core' to a shipping business and would otherwise sit inside the entity being privatised; the leaseback keeps SCI operationally whole after they leave its balance sheet. The separation is still unfinished: the leaseback is accounted for as a short-term lease only because the final lease agreement has not been executed, pending the disinvestment process, and the joint statutory auditors (D. R. Mohnot & Co and PSD & Associates) flag both note 7 and note 8 as emphasis-of-matter items in the 31.12.2025 limited review. Management itself volunteered none of this on the calls — the only live discussion was a question about a possible reverse merger of SCILAL back into SCI, which the CMD declined to answer on the ground that SCILAL is a separate legal entity and the decision rests with the Government and the Ministry.

**How it evolved:** On the Q2 FY26 call of 10 November 2025 the demerger, SCILAL and the disinvestment were not raised at all — management's entire strategic narrative was additive (the 59-vessel oil-PSU JV, the 2047 business plan, VLGC inductions), not separative. It surfaced only on the Q4 FY26 call of 11 May 2026, and then from an investor: Amitabh Vatsya of Sadhan Ventures asked about 'rumours or some news about reverse merger of SILAL with SCI', citing a signed NBCC MOU, and Capt. Tyagi answered that the NBCC MOU concerns upgrading SCI's Powai training institute and that SCILAL is a separate legal entity on which only the Government/Ministry can decide, adding 'We have no information regarding this at this stage.' Across the three filings of 06.02.2026 the language is unchanged and boilerplate — same note 7, same note 8, same auditor emphasis — so the only movement in the period is directional ambiguity (an investor floating reversal of the demerger) rather than any new company disclosure.

**What management expects from it:** Nothing was stated on either call — no margin, capital, valuation or focus claim for SCI or SCILAL. Only the filings imply the intent: 192 non-core land assets sit in SCILAL while SCI operates on 185 leased back, keeping property out of the shipping entity DIPAM is selling. The sole forward statement was upgrading the Powai training institute via the NBCC/Synergy MOUs.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — Note 8 of the 31.12.2025 standalone and consolidated results sets out the carve-out: MCA order dated 22.02.2023, 192 non-core assets moved from SCI to SCILAL effective 01 April 2021, and 185 of them leased back to SCI, with the leaseback treated as a short-term lease only because the final agreement is unexecuted pending disinvestment. “Pursuant to approval of demerger scheme by MCA vide its order dated 22.02.2023, 192 non-core assets were transferred from the Company (Demerged Company) to Shipping Corporation of India Land and Assets Limited (Resulting Company) (hereinafter referred to as SCILAL) w.e.f. 01 April 2021 and 185 non-core assets are leased back to the demerged company, has been treated as short term lease, pending execution of final agreement and disinvestment process as detailed in note no. 7.”
- *Scheme* — Note 7 names who is driving the separation and why it is still open — DIPAM with a Transaction Advisor, a PIM issued 22.12.2020, and a Virtual Data Room currently open for due diligence by Qualified Interested Parties, i.e. prospective strategic buyers of the shipping business. “The proposed strategic disinvestment of SCI is being handled by Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM) with the engagement of Transaction Advisor. In this regard, Preliminary Information Memorandum (PIM) for inviting expression of interest was released on 22.12.2020. The Virtual Data Room is open and is being managed by the Transaction Advisor for the process of due diligence by the Qualified Interested Parties.”
- *Scheme* — The joint statutory auditors draw attention to the demerger and leaseback as an emphasis-of-matter in their limited review report dated 06.02.2026, expressly tying management's short-term-lease judgement to the unexecuted formal lease agreement and the disinvestment process. “Note no. 8 regarding MCA’a approval in FY 22-23 for demerger between The Shipping Corporation of India Limited (“Demerged Company”) and The Shipping corporation of India Limited Land and Assets Limited (“Resulting Company”) and consequently, transfer of non-core assets to SCI LAL and leaseback of the same to SCI and management’s assessment of treating the same as short term lease pending execution of formal lease agreement and disinvestment process.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.shipindia.com/upload/investorsubpage/transcript.pdf)* — An investor (Amitabh Vatsya, Sadhan Ventures) raised press reports of a reverse merger of SCILAL back into SCI, linking it to a newly signed NBCC MOU — the only time the separation was discussed live on either call. “So, is there are some rumours or some news about reverse merger of SILAL with SCI?”
- *[May 2026](https://www.shipindia.com/upload/investorsubpage/transcript.pdf)* — Capt. B.K. Tyagi declined to give any rationale or status, treating SCILAL as outside SCI's control and the decision as the Government's/Ministry's alone, and disclaiming any information. “As far as this SCILAL and SCI reversal is concerned, SCILAL is a separate legal entity, and this is a matter where Government, our Ministry will take decision if at all anything is there.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.shipindia.com/upload/investorsubpage/transcript.pdf)* — He redirected the question to the NBCC MOU's actual purpose — upgrading and better utilising SCI's large maritime training institute at Powai, alongside an MOU with international ship manager Synergy — not to any land-entity restructuring. “See, number one, this NBCC MOU was signed few days back. And idea is we have got a one big training institute in Powai.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.shipindia.com/upload/investorsubpage/Transcript_Antique-ShippingCorp-Nov10-2025.pdf)* — The November 2025 call contains no reference to the demerger, SCILAL, non-core assets or disinvestment; management's strategic framing was entirely about adding entities (a 50%-owned oil-PSU JV for 59 vessels, later Bharat Container Shipping Line) rather than separating existing ones. “It will be a separate entity and where SCI will hold a shareholding up to 50%.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No rationale, valuation, rent quantum, lease term, timetable, SCILAL listing/shareholding plan, or buyer status; management would not address the reverse-merger reports or confirm anything about SCILAL.

## SIEMENS — Siemens Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a filing's text names a demerger; no scheme filing names it yet) · **SPINNING — record date set; the new entity lists soon** · score 5.0/10 · spin-off · 6 filing(s) from BSE-screener, CALLS, NSE · first 2025-11-14, latest 2026-11-06

> **Listing:** RECORD DATE set; the resulting company not yet listed — resulting companies have typically listed 4–10 weeks after the record date

**The stages, as filed:** nclt_sanction (2025-11-14) → effective (2026-08-11)

**Stated in the filings:** appointed date 2025-03-01; size hint: 10.5% of revenue.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** The Energy business of Siemens Limited, transferred to Siemens Energy India Limited under a Scheme of Arrangement — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* not stated — no promoter or management shareholding, stake, or incentive in Siemens Energy India Limited is disclosed anywhere in these documents
- *What it reveals:* Energy left with net assets of Rs 37,846 million including Rs 25,478 million cash; it earned Rs 9,418 million PBT on Rs 61,580 million revenue in FY2024. Parent remains cash-rich (Rs 77,905 million cash and bank, 30 Sep 2026) with a Rs 47,034 crore backlog.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — Energy was large, not a stub (FY2024 revenue Rs 61,580 million); management said combined share prices rose ~40%
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Siemens Energy India Limited's own results and the Scheme, for the Rs 37,846 million net assets and Rs 25,478 million cash transferred
- *In their words:* “Pursuant to receipt of necessary statutory approvals and in accordance with the Scheme, the Company has demerged the Energy business effective 25 March 2025, with appointed date being 1 March 2025, as per the Scheme.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Siemens Ltd. has separated two businesses, and the one management explained in the most detail is the Low Voltage Motors (LVM, plus geared motors and related customer service) business, sold as a going concern on a slump-sale basis to Innomotics India Private Limited for an enterprise value of INR 22 billion (INR 2,200 crore), cash-free/debt-free. The trigger was not Indian: on 1 October 2024 Siemens AG sold the global Innomotics business — and all of its intellectual property — to KPS Capital Partners, leaving the Indian unit as, in Sunil Mathur's words, a licensed sales organisation with no IP, no manufacturing (contract-manufactured to Innomotics design, ~97% of the Business's revenue) and survival dependent on an Agency & Distributorship Agreement and a Technical Cooperation & License Agreement with an entity now controlled by a private-equity owner. So the counterparty, not investors or lenders, effectively forced the decision: the Board stated the Business could not be sold to anyone else because Innomotics owns the IP, making the only alternatives selling to Innomotics India or restructuring the Business and bearing those costs. The numbers management cited were small and deteriorating: for the 12 months to 30 September 2025, revenue from operations of INR 9.67 billion (INR 967 crore) and profit from operations of INR 0.35 billion (INR 35 crore) — 6% of the company's revenue and ~2.2% of its profit from operations ex-Energy — with net capital employed of negative INR 1.38 billion, orders down 6.9% y/y in Q2 FY25, H1 EBITDA of 7.8% (down 130bps on lower price realisation and higher royalties paid to Innomotics), volumes that 'have not increased', cyclicality tied to private-sector capex and copper, and only 89 sales employees; the filing also recorded negative net worth of INR 1,175.66 million and 4.53% of revenue in FY24. Management said synergies with the rest of Siemens Ltd. were 'very limited' and framed the exit as portfolio optimisation that creates value and cash while giving customers and employees continuity. Price was set after negotiation using two independent valuations (Grant Thornton Bharat LLP and KPMG Valuation Services LLP) as at 30 September 2025, and Mathur stressed INR 22 billion was 'the same price that had been offered earlier on by the parent company' despite volumes having since declined. The earlier, larger separation was the Energy demerger into Siemens Energy India Limited (appointed date 1 March 2025, effective 25 March 2025), justified as creating two independent pure-play companies focused on their relevant markets, each with a large backlog; it transferred net assets of INR 37,846 million including INR 25,478 million of cash, cost INR 1.0 billion of demerger expenses in FY25 versus INR 0.1 billion in FY24, and under the November 2023 disclosure the promoters agreed procedures to let Siemens Energy AG acquire a majority in the new listed entity.

**How it evolved:** Dec 2024 call (20 Dec 2024): only the Energy demerger is discussed as a separation — 'on track', creating two independent companies, with LVM not yet flagged as a portfolio issue. May 2025 call (20 May 2025): after the Siemens AG–KPS Innomotics deal of October 2024 and visible margin pressure from royalties paid to Innomotics, management formally said it would 'explore options for the future' of LVM. Dec 2025 (board 8 Dec 2025; analyst meet 12 Dec 2025): the option became a signed slump-sale agreement with Innomotics India at INR 22 billion, justified by lost IP, no local manufacturing, declining volumes (6% of revenue, 2% of profit) and shareholder interest, with closing guided to mid-2026. Jun 2026 call (28 May 2026) reconfirmed completion 'on track for June 2026'; the sale closed 1 June 2026 with a provisional gain of INR 20,990 million, while in the opposite direction the Board approved amalgamating subsidiary Siemens Rail Automation into the parent (26 May 2026) and took C&S Electric to 100% via capital reduction (NCLT order 24 September 2026).

**What management expects from it:** For Siemens Ltd.: a cleaner three-business technology portfolio (DI, SI, Mobility), removal of a sub-scale, negative-capital-employed, royalty-burdened unit worth 6% of revenue but only 2% of profit, INR 22 billion of cash plus an INR 2,099 crore gain, and portfolio optimisation 'creating value and cash'. For Innomotics India: ownership aligned with the IP it already holds, continuity for LVM customers and the 89 sales staff. For Energy: an independent pure-play.

- *[Dec 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=82783258-f887-444b-a6f1-cbeaf34f0b62.pdf)* — The prior, bigger separation is presented as completed and successful — Energy is now a separately listed pure-play, leaving Siemens Ltd. with DI, SI and Mobility. “A major development during this period has been the demerger of Siemens Energy India Limited, which is now a separately listed pure play energy company.”
- *[Dec 2024](https://assets.new.siemens.com/siemens/assets/api/uuid:dc7b02ca-736c-4db6-8118-da2b47754aa6/Analyst-Call-Transcript-website.pdf)* — Rationale originally given for the Energy demerger: two focused, independently capitalised companies each with large backlogs. “Both companies are very well prepared for the future growth, focusing on their relevant markets.”

- *Scheme* — Filing of 8 Dec 2025 states the hard constraint: without Innomotics/KPS support Siemens Ltd. cannot run the business, which is why the only buyer was the counterparty itself. “The Company itself does not have the requisite intellectual property or other capabilities to service the Business without support from Innomotics GmbH which is now owned by KPS.”
- *Scheme* — Strategic-fit argument plus the stated financial benefit of exiting — portfolio optimisation generating value and cash. “Synergies between the Business and the rest of the Company’s businesses are very limited.”
