## UNITDSPR — United Spirits Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a scheme of arrangement whose nature the documents on file do not settle) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 5.0/10 · scheme (nature unclear) · 3 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-03-24, latest 2026-03-24

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**Stated in the filings:** size hint: 1.9% of net worth.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Royal Challengers Sports Private Limited, owner-operator of the RCB IPL and WPL cricket franchises, sold 100% for cash — class `unrelated`.

- *Insiders:* Not stated. Buyers "do not belong to any promoter/promoter group/group companies" of USL; on completion USL ceases to hold any shareholding in RCSPL. No management stake or incentive disclosed.
- *What it reveals:* RCSPL was only 1.9% of USL standalone revenue (Rs 504 cr) and 4.1% of net worth (Rs 321 cr) yet fetched INR 166.6 bn all cash — a non-core asset carried far below realisable value, now converted to cash.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — All-cash private sale to a consortium; no shares distributed to USL holders, so no new listed entity for anyone to dump.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Q4 FY26 earnings call / results for use of the INR 166.6 bn proceeds — dividend, buyback or reinvestment.
- *In their words:* “This transaction marks an important milestone for USL as we sharpen focus on our core beverage alcohol business to unlock its true potential with sustained growth, and to continue delivering on long-term value creation for our stakeholders.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The business being separated is not a spirits brand but USL's wholly owned cricket subsidiary, Royal Challengers Sports Private Limited (RCSPL), which owns and operates the Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) franchises in the IPL and the Women's Premier League; USL agreed on March 24, 2026 to sell 100% of RCSPL (14,690 equity shares) to a consortium of Aditya Birla Group (Aelius Investments Pte Ltd), The Times of India Group (Times Internet Limited and Metropolitan Media Company Limited), Bolt Ventures (Bolt IPL Holdings LLC) and Blackstone's perpetual private equity strategy BXPE (Asia Investment Topco II Pte. Ltd.) for INR 166.6 bn in an all-cash transaction. The only rationale management actually gave, in MD & CEO Praveen Someshwar's press-release comment, is focus: the deal lets USL 'sharpen focus on our core beverage alcohol business to unlock its true potential with sustained growth' and continue 'long-term value creation for our stakeholders.' The second stated reason is that the asset has outgrown its owner's purpose — RCB is 'the most prominent and commercially successful franchise in the IPL and WPL' with a globally recognised brand, and 'As Sports enters a new phase of growth in India & globally, we believe this is in the best interest of the franchise and our stakeholders,' i.e. the franchise needs an owner whose business is sport. The size disclosure makes the focus argument concrete and also shows the valuation gap: RCSPL contributed revenue from operations of only INR 504 crore in FY24-25 (1.9% of USL standalone revenue) and net worth of INR 321 crore as at March 31, 2025 (4.1% of USL standalone net worth), and USL expressly notes RCSPL 'is not a material subsidiary of USL' — yet it fetched INR 166.6 bn, roughly 50x its book net worth, in cash. No operational problem, loss, capital drain, covenant, partner demand or investor campaign is cited anywhere in the supplied texts as the trigger; the stated problems solved are strategic focus and stewardship of the franchise, not fixing a weak business. Structurally the separation is a clean cash share sale rather than a demerger or scheme of arrangement (the filing marks 'Whether the sale... is outside Scheme of Arrangement' as not applicable), with USL ceasing to hold any shareholding and RCSPL ceasing to be a subsidiary on completion. Residual ties are limited and transitional: USL and its affiliates will provide certain support services to RCSPL on a transitory basis, and a co-existence arrangement will govern usage of certain brand names between USL and RCSPL, both effective only from completion. Conditions are customary plus approvals from the Board of Control for Cricket in India and the Competition Commission of India, with completion expected within six months of March 24, 2026; Citigroup India advised USL and AZB Partners was counsel.

**How it evolved:** In the only readable call, May 23, 2025, there is no separation idea at all — RCB is presented as a core strength, a 'differentiated asset' with exceptional brand equity ranking among the top five global sports teams on engagement behind only Real Madrid and FC Barcelona (the sole divestment-adjacent remark is analyst Harit Kapoor's aside that one Lower Prestige brand 'could be on the block,' which management did not address). The idea surfaces formally on November 5, 2025, the date the March 2026 filings repeatedly cite as when USL announced and 'initiated' a strategic review of RCSPL. It concludes at the board meeting of March 24, 2026 (18:09–19:00 IST), where the SPA was approved and the press release states the announcement 'concludes the strategic review of RCSPL that was initiated by USL, as announced on November 05, 2025' — i.e. the review ended in a full exit rather than a partial stake sale or demerger. The Nov 2025, Jan 2026 and May 2026 call transcripts supplied here have no extractable text, so management's call-by-call commentary between review and signing cannot be reconstructed from these documents.

**What management expects from it:** For USL: sharper focus on the core beverage-alcohol business to 'unlock its true potential with sustained growth' and long-term stakeholder value creation, plus INR 166.6 bn of all-cash proceeds against RCSPL's INR 321 crore net worth. For RCB: growth under owners with sport, media, technology and brand-building strengths as sport enters a new global phase. No margin, capital-allocation or valuation numbers for the remaining business were given.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[May 2025](https://www.diageoindia.com/%7E/media/Files/D/Diageo-V2/Diageo-India/investors/financials/results-reports-and-presentations/earnings-call-transcript-q4-fy25.pdf)* — RCB is framed as a core competitive asset, not a candidate for separation — management highlights its brand equity and global engagement ranking, with no mention of a review or sale. “RCB, our differentiated asset continues to build on its strength.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.diageoindia.com/%7E/media/Files/D/Diageo-V2/Diageo-India/investors/financials/results-reports-and-presentations/earnings-call-transcript-q4-fy25.pdf)* — The only divestment hint on a readable call is an analyst's passing reference to a Lower Prestige brand being up for sale; management's reply discussed Andhra Pradesh-driven growth and did not confirm or address any sale. “I understand in the Lower Prestige, there's also one of the brands, which could be on the block.”
- *Scheme* — USL's board approved the sale of all 14,690 equity shares of RCSPL — a 100% exit from the IPL/WPL franchise owner — for INR 166.6 bn in cash, under an SPA dated March 24, 2026. “has inter alia approved the sale of 14,690 equity shares of Ro yal Challengers Sports Private Limited (“ RCSPL ”), a wholly owned subsidiary of USL for an aggregate consideration of INR 166.6 bn”
- *Scheme* — Management's stated rationale is focus on the core alcobev business and value creation, not repair of a problem business. ““This transaction marks an important milestone for USL as we sharpen focus on our core beverage alcohol business to unlock its true pot ential with sustained growth, and to continue delivering on long-term value creation for our  stakeholders.”
- *Scheme* — The second rationale is stewardship: sport is entering a new growth phase, so new owners are better placed to take RCB forward. “As Sports enters a new phase of growth in India & globally,  we believe this is in the best interest of the franchise and our stakeholders.”
- *Scheme* — RCSPL was financially small relative to USL — FY24-25 revenue INR 504 crore (1.9% of USL standalone revenue) and net worth INR 321 crore (4.1%) — and is explicitly not a material subsidiary, underlining the valuation unlock versus book value. “Further, it is noted that RCSPL is not a material subsidiary of USL.”
- *Scheme* — The deal closes a process begun months earlier: the strategic review announced on November 5, 2025 ends in a full divestiture. “This announcement concludes the strategic review of RCSPL that was initiated by USL, as announced on November 05, 2025.”
- *Scheme* — Buyers are a four-party consortium with sport, media, brand and capital credentials — ABG, Times of India Group, Bolt Ventures and Blackstone's BXPE — none of them related to USL's promoter group, and the transaction is not a related-party transaction. “The Acquiring Consortium  brings together three partners with complementary strengths across sport, media, technology, and brand-building”
- *Scheme* — Post-completion ties are deliberately limited: transitional support services from USL and a brand-name co-existence arrangement, both effective only on completion. “Further, the SPA contemplates, upon and on from completion of the Proposed Transaction, the provision of certain support services by USL and its relevant affiliated entities to RCSPL on a transitory basis, and a co-existence arrangement governing the usage of certain brand names as between USL and RCSPL, each of which will be entered into only upon completion of the Proposed Transaction and effective therefrom.”
- *Scheme* — Closing needs BCCI and CCI clearance and is expected within six months of signing; USL will hold no shares in RCSPL thereafter. “USL wi ll cease to hold any s hareholding in RCSPL and consequently RCSPL will cease to be a subsidiary of USL.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No use of proceeds, no EPS/margin/ROCE impact, no capital-return plan, no mention of who pushed for it, and no readable call Q&A on the review or sale.

## PREMIERENE — Premier Energies Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a subsidiary's listing is in motion (DRHP / board approval)) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 4.4/10 · partial spin-off / listing · 2 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-08-06, latest 2026-08-06

> **Listing:** IPO / listing of the subsidiary in motion since 2026-08-06; date not fixed

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** not stated - documents describe acquisitions, not any separation or demerger of a business — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* Chiranjeev Singh Saluja holds 25,96,12,382 shares (57.31%) of Premier Energies; Sudhir Moola 2.98%; Surenderpal Singh Saluja 1,500 shares (0.00%); nothing stated on any new entity
- *What it reveals:* Documents reveal a newly consolidated Transcon Ind Limited subsidiary (51%, goodwill Rs 2,422.14 million) reported as a separate 'Power Transmission & Distribution Equipment' segment, Q1 FY27 revenue Rs 1,064.68 million, result Rs 240.79 million
- *Selling pressure:* unclear — No separation, demerger or new listing is disclosed in the documents, so no basis is stated
- *Parent or spin:* neither · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Annual Report FY2025-26 and Transcon segment disclosure for standalone transformer-business economics
- *In their words:* “Consequently, Transcon Ind Limited has become a subsidiary of the Company with effect from April 3, 2026.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Nothing in these three years of earnings calls or in the filings provided describes Premier Energies separating, demerging, spinning off or hiving off any business, and there is no scheme of arrangement in the record — so the premise of the question cannot be supported from these texts. The direction management describes is the opposite: consolidation and diversification into one group. Across the Nov 2025, Jan 2026 and May 2026 calls the company adds businesses rather than sheds them — a 51% stake in transformer maker Transcon Ind Limited for up to ₹5,003.00 million (₹2,500.02 million for 34.21% in Dec 2025, the balance ₹2,502.98 million in April 2026, taking Transcon and its subsidiary Neotrafo to subsidiary/step-down status), a 51% inverter JV with Syrma SGS around KSolare (FY25 revenue cited at ₹143 crores), a 6 GWh-per-phase cell-to-pack BESS line at ₹280 crores, aluminium frames at ₹260 crores, a 10 GW ingot-wafer project at about ₹5,900 crores, and a 51% stake in HeliosAnthos Energies for ₹10.45 lakh. Management's stated rationale for keeping these together is synergy, not separation: Vinay Rustagi argued 10 GVA of transformer demand per GW of renewable capacity added, with roughly 80% of installs now renewable, so transformers, inverters and BESS go to 'the same clients who we are selling our modules', 'reducing the cost of customer acquisition', and the new businesses together with BESS are expected to contribute 'approximately 30% of our revenue over time'. The only two events in the record that even resemble a separation are (a) the voluntary winding-up by strike-off of IBD Solar Powertech (Pvt.) Ltd, a Bangladesh step-down wholly owned subsidiary with nil revenue, nil turnover contribution and negative net worth of ₹2.09 lakh, where the Reg. 30 annexure marks every sale/disposal/scheme field 'Not Applicable'; and (b) the abandonment of the KSolare acquisition in Q1 FY27 — a reversal of an inbound deal, not a carve-out, with 'no financial implications arising from the same'. There is also an accounting-only split — Power Transmission & Distribution Equipment became a separate reportable segment under Ind AS 108 from the Transcon acquisition date — but that is segment disclosure, not a legal or structural separation. On these texts alone, there is no separation to explain, and no investor, lender or partner is recorded as asking for one.

**How it evolved:** The idea never surfaces: in Feb 2025 and May 2025 management frames 'Mission 2028' as a single integrated 10 GW ingot-wafer-cell-module platform plus BESS and inverters, with ₹125,000 million of capex inside one group. Jul 2025 and Nov 2025 add, not subtract — the 4.8 GW cell line is scaled to 7 GW, and the KSolare (inverter) and Transcon (transformer) acquisitions are announced as 'highly complementary and value accretive'. Jan 2026 reports the Transcon acquisition completed in Dec 2025 and KSolare closing 'in the next one month'; by May 2026 the KSolare deal is dropped for lack of agreement on final documentation while Transcon's 51% is completed, and the Aug 2026 and Sep 2026 filings record only a new reportable segment and the strike-off of the dormant Bangladesh shell. At no point in May 2025, Jul 2025, Nov 2025, Jan 2026 or May 2026 does any analyst or executive mention a demerger, spin-off, slump sale or scheme.

**What management expects from it:** Not applicable — no separation is described. Management's stated expectations are for the combined group: ~30% of revenue from inverters, BESS and transformers over time; Transcon margins rising toward 20-25% EBITDA as mix shifts to MV/HV/EHV with 7x-10x fixed-asset turns; cross-sell synergies lowering customer-acquisition cost; and debt/equity held near 1.0 and debt/EBITDA near 1.5 through the capex cycle.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The only disposal-type disclosure in the filings is the strike-off of a dormant, non-operating Bangladesh step-down subsidiary — not a business separation; the Reg. 30 annexure marks turnover contribution nil, net worth negative ₹2.09 lakh, and every sale/disposal/scheme-of-arrangement field 'Not Applicable'. “IBD, had no revenue or commercial operations and had filed an application for voluntary winding-up by way of strike off of name on 10th October, 2023 with the Office of the Registrar of Joint Stock Companies and Firms, Bangladesh.”
- *Scheme* — The filings explicitly confirm no scheme of arrangement or undertaking disposal is involved in that winding-up. “Whether the sale, lease or disposal of the undertaking is outside Scheme of Arrangement? If yes, details of the same including compliance with regulation 37A of LODR Regulations.  Not Applicable”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=98bf38bd-e1c7-48ad-ad7f-0962d6093683.pdf)* — Management's stated logic is combination, not separation: the inverter and transformer acquisitions are kept inside the group precisely because they are complementary and are expected to supply about 30% of revenue over time. “Both these acquisitions are highly complementary and value accretive.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=98bf38bd-e1c7-48ad-ad7f-0962d6093683.pdf)* — Rustagi quantified the cross-sell synergy that argues against separating the equipment businesses — roughly 10 GVA of transformer demand per GW of capacity added, sold to the same module customers. “there is a, you know, 10x the 10 GVA is the demand for transformers.”
- *[Jan 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=3c75cc20-8dd8-416e-91f4-688f59134d09.pdf)* — Transcon is described as a future growth engine being scaled sevenfold inside the group (2.5 GVA to 16.75 GVA by July 2026) and moved up into MV/HV/EHV, with a ₹1,000 crore-plus top line targeted by FY28 — the opposite of a carve-out. “This business is expected to become a key growth contributor for us.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=15e4b0a9-dfac-4928-83dc-c6744dc37699.pdf)* — The one deal that was unwound was an inbound acquisition (KSolare), dropped over documentation terms, with the inverter ambition retained in-house via the SMA/Syrma SGS JV route — again no separation of an existing Premier business. “I think that is the reason why the transaction could not be completed.”
- *Scheme* — The only 'split' in the record is an accounting one: a new reportable segment created by the Transcon acquisition under Ind AS 108, effective from the April 3, 2026 acquisition date. “Consequently, the Company has identified Power Transmission & Distribution Equipment as a separate reportable segment in accordance with the requirements of Ind AS 108 - Operating Segments.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=15e4b0a9-dfac-4928-83dc-c6744dc37699.pdf)* — Forward capital plans are framed as one diversified platform funded centrally (FY27 capex ₹5,100 crores across cells, ingot-wafers, batteries and inverters; ₹5,000 crores enabling fundraise resolution), with no mention of releasing capital by separating an entity. “FY27 is a year of large capex for us at INR5,100 crores to be deployed across cells, ingot wafers, batteries and inverters.”

*Not explained on the calls:* The calls and filings never mention any demerger, spin-off, slump sale or scheme of arrangement, so no rationale, no requesting party, and no expected benefits are explained anywhere.

## SAATVIKGL — Saatvik Green Energy Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a subsidiary's listing is in motion (DRHP / board approval)) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 4.4/10 · partial spin-off / listing · 3 filing(s) from CALLS, NSE · first 2026-02-04, latest 2026-02-04

> **Listing:** IPO / listing of the subsidiary in motion since 2026-02-04; date not fixed

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Not stated — documents show only further investment in wholly owned subsidiary Saatvik Solar Industries; no separation or demerger announced — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* SSIPL remains 100% held by Saatvik Green Energy; no change in shareholding. Under SGEL ESOS 2024, promoters and independent directors are not entitled to any stock options
- *What it reveals:* SSIPL turnover grew 35.95 million (FY24) to 11,852.52 million (FY25) and carries a 15% preferred income tax rate versus 25% at the parent; cell manufacturing is said to add 3-4% EBITDA on cell volumes
- *Selling pressure:* unclear — No demerger, distribution or separate listing of the subsidiary is stated, so no share-overhang mechanism is described
- *Parent or spin:* unclear · *option pricing date:* not stated (exercise price is set at the closing market price on the date of the NRC meeting approving the grant; 3,69,000 options granted, 2,85,000 active as of the postal ballot notice)
- *Read next:* Prospectus dated September 23, 2025 — IPO objects and SSIPL standalone financials for the Odisha 4 GW project
- *In their words:* “It will continue to remain a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Across all four transcripts (Oct 2025, Nov 2025, Feb 2026, May 2026) and both filings, Saatvik Green Energy announces NO separation, demerger, spin-off or scheme of arrangement of any business, so no management rationale for one exists in these texts; the stated strategy is the opposite — consolidating a single integrated platform. Management repeatedly describes building "entire integrated forward, backward and sideways energy company" spanning ingot/wafer, cell (scaled from 4.8 GW to 6 GW), module (8.8 GW), encapsulant (2 GW commissioned in Ambala, roadmap raised to 5 GW), inverters (UDAY series), solar pumps, EPC, BESS, transformers and components — with backward integration justified as cost competitiveness, margin sustainability and supply-chain security, worth an additional 3-5% EBITDA on self-produced cell volume. The only 'separation' language is about creating standalone business units/entities INSIDE the group, not divesting: solar pumps (INR ~2 crore FY25 revenue, targeted INR 50-80 crore in FY26, 4,000-5,000 pumps, 15,000 next year) described as "a division which has a potential of becoming a separate business unit"; encapsulant built "not only for our supply chain resilience, but also as a separate business unit" because third-party module makers "are ready to pay a premium on encapsulant" (5-10% internal saving, 7-10% of module cost); plus Saatvik Power Storage Solutions Limited launched for BESS and an 80% stake bought in Melcon Transformers and Electricals. Capacity is also being housed in separate legal vehicles — subsidiary Saatvik Solar Industries Private Limited (FY25 turnover INR 11,852.52 million) holds the new-technology capacity and carries a 15% concessional tax rate versus 25% at the parent, pulling the blended rate to 18-20% — which is corporate structuring, not a separation. Management cites capital needs that argue against breaking anything off: INR 1,850 crore Odisha capex (INR 1,300-1,350 crore cell, INR 550 crore module), INR 1,700 crore FY27 capex, INR 1,800-2,500 crore for the 6 GW ingot project in FY28, funded 70:30 debt:equity at 8.9-9%, with debt-equity to be held between 1.0x and 1.5x (0.65x in FY26 versus 1.34x in FY25). No investor, lender or partner in any of these calls asks for a separation, and no analyst question on the topic appears.

**How it evolved:** The idea never surfaces as a corporate separation in any call. Oct 10, 2025 (Q1FY26) is the first time 'separate business unit' appears, as an internal ambition for solar pumps; Nov 10, 2025 (Q2FY26) adds the subsidiary tax-rate point and Saatvik Solar Industries as the order-taking entity; Feb 5, 2026 (Q3FY26) hardens solar pumps into a targeted "standalone business unit" (then only 0.35% of revenue); May 21, 2026 (Q4FY26) extends the pattern to encapsulant as a merchant business unit, a new BESS company (Saatvik Power Storage Solutions Limited) and the Melcon transformer acquisition — all additions to the group, never a carve-out.

**What management expects from it:** Nothing is claimed for a separation, because none is announced. For the internal business units they expect: encapsulant to add merchant sales plus 5-10% input savings; cell integration to add 3-5% EBITDA on captive volume, DCR pricing and "value unlocking"; solar pumps to scale to INR 50-80 crore then 15,000 pumps; subsidiary structure to cut blended tax to 18-20%.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Oct 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=833e2278-a14f-45b0-b3cc-4865519aeb08.pdf)* — Solar pumps, scaling from under INR 2 crore to about INR 50 crore of revenue, is first flagged as a candidate to become its own business unit inside the group. “So, the kind of growth which will be seen from less than INR2 crores revenue last year to about INR50 crores revenue this year and that is also a division which has a potential of becoming a separate business unit.”
- *[Oct 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=833e2278-a14f-45b0-b3cc-4865519aeb08.pdf)* — The strategic direction stated by the CEO is full integration across the value chain plus adjacencies, not separation of any business. “So, all in all we are building -- we are also doing BESS projects and ultimately the target is to get into battery storage products also. So, all in all we are building entire integrated forward, backward and sideways energy company, renewable energy company especially.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=b2ee3ca6-6aa7-49a8-a80c-5c5ce156da7f.pdf)* — Management explicitly says module capacity will be capped around 9-10 GW and growth will come from backward integration into cell and ingot-wafer, i.e. consolidation rather than divestment. “So, our focus is not to grow our module capacities beyond 9, 10 gigawatts because that is a respectable where you can get economies of scale and we will focus on building our backward integration towards cell, towards ingot wafer and also bring in more products, you know, which are supportive to our solar module business in this industry.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=b2ee3ca6-6aa7-49a8-a80c-5c5ce156da7f.pdf)* — The only entity-level rationale given is tax: new capacity sits in subsidiary Saatvik Solar at a 15% rate versus 25% at the parent, lowering the blended rate to 18-20%. “So, in Saatvik Green Energy, we have normal tax rate, while in comparison , Saatvik Solar has a preferred rate at the rate of 15%. So, more revenue from Saatvik Solar Industries, the lower tax rate overall.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=96e61630-6cb7-4fcd-b518-35c31125a0aa.pdf)* — Solar pumps, at 0.35% of revenue, are being formalised as a standalone business unit within the company during FY26. “This year we target to make it a business unit, a standalone business unit.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=3312a28f-060f-4f9f-a630-cebe13ee1bc4.pdf)* — The 2 GW (now 5 GW roadmap) EPE encapsulant plant is being run as its own business unit selling to third-party module makers at a premium, on top of 5-10% internal cost savings on 7-10% of module cost. “So initially we started this 2 gigawatt for our internal usage, but what we have found is that there are, you know, manufacturers who are not good at planning and they are not importing, they are not able to secure. So they are ready to pay a premium on encapsulant.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=3312a28f-060f-4f9f-a630-cebe13ee1bc4.pdf)* — New activities are being placed in new legal vehicles and acquisitions rather than separated out of the company: a BESS company was launched and 80% of a transformer maker was bought. “In parallel, we launched Saatvik Power Storage Solutions Limited, focused on battery energy storage systems.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=3312a28f-060f-4f9f-a630-cebe13ee1bc4.pdf)* — Capital plans point to heavier consolidation, not separation: INR 1,700 crore FY27 capex and about INR 2,500 crore for the 6 GW ingot project, with gearing held at 1.0-1.5x. “So, for FY27, our capex requirement for this expansion is about 1,700 crores.”
- *Scheme* — No scheme of arrangement, demerger or spin-off is present in the filings; the only structural filing is a INR 251.60 crore rights-issue infusion into wholly owned subsidiary SSIPL for the Odisha 4 GW module plant, with no change in shareholding, alongside a postal ballot on an independent director and ESOP ratification. “There will be no change in the percentage of shareholding of the Company in SSIPL . It will continue to remain a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company.”

*Not explained on the calls:* Everything about a separation: no demerger, scheme, record date, entity perimeters, debt or capex allocation, valuation, listing plan, or any investor, lender or partner request for one.

> **Listing:** IPO / listing of the subsidiary in motion since 2026-08-13; date not fixed

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** not stated — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* not stated
- *What it reveals:* not stated
- *Selling pressure:* unclear — Documents describe no separation, demerger or new listing, so no size or index effect is stated.
- *Parent or spin:* neither · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Outcome of the open Delhi T3 tender; its licence expires 30 September 2026 and the 60% SPV's fate is undecided.
- *In their words:* “Travel Food Services (Delhi Terminal 3) Private Limited ("Delhi T3" or "the Subsidiary"), a material subsidiary of the Company in which the Company holds a 60% equity interest, was awarded a licence agreement for a period of ten years with effect from 6 February 2010.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

No separation, demerger, spin-off, slump sale, scheme of arrangement or carve-out of any business is mentioned anywhere in the four earnings calls (Aug 2025, Nov 2025, Feb 2026, Jun 2026) or in the single filing provided (the 13 August 2026 Outcome of Board Meeting with Q1 FY27 standalone and consolidated results and limited review reports). On the contrary, management describes Travel Food Services as one integrated platform and the auditor-reviewed results state that travel QSR, lounges and related services 'comprise of only one operating segment' reviewed by the Board as the Chief Operating Decision Maker, which is the opposite of a separation narrative. The only structural changes discussed are: (1) the deconsolidation of JV entity Semolina Kitchens effective 14 October 2024, which management repeatedly frames purely as an accounting/comparability matter done 'as planned' (FY25 base restated to exclude Semolina; Q1 FY25 Semolina losses added back), not as a separation of a business with a strategic rationale; (2) the scheduled expiry on 30 September 2026 of the Delhi Terminal 3 licence held by 60:40 SPV Travel Food Services (Delhi Terminal 3) Private Limited (TFS 60%, DIAL 40%) — Varun Kapur said the SPV 'had a life tied into that concession' and that TFS would re-bid for Delhi T3 through its existing JV GMR Hospitality (GHL), with the filing noting a material uncertainty at the subsidiary level that 'does not give rise to a material uncertainty at the Group level'; and (3) new legal entities created to house growth, not to exit anything — wholly owned subsidiary Elite Assist Technology and Services (EATS) for the lounge-access tech platform, Travel Food Services Worldwide FZCO in Dubai (w.e.f. 10 July 2025) and PT Travel Food Services Indonesia (w.e.f. 23 September 2025) for international lounges. Management's stated direction across all four calls is expansion and consolidation of the same platform: 20 airports, 550+ travel QSR outlets and lounges, 145+ brands, FY26 system-wide sales of INR32.1 billion (+25.4%) and adjusted PAT of INR4.5 billion (+21.4%), zero debt with INR8.4 billion of cash, and new verticals (international lounges in Malaysia/Hong Kong/Middle East, wayside amenities on access-controlled expressways) all pursued inside the group. No investor, lender, airport partner or brand partner is recorded as asking for a separation; the only partner-related questions were about Adani/DreamFolks risk and SSP support, which Varun answered by pointing to deeper JV integration, not separation.

**How it evolved:** The idea never surfaces: across Aug 2025, Nov 2025, Feb 2026 and Jun 2026 no analyst asks about a demerger and management never raises one. The closest recurring thread is the Semolina Kitchens deconsolidation of 14 October 2024, repeated in identical accounting-comparability language in Aug 2025, Nov 2025, Feb 2026 and Jun 2026. The second thread is Delhi T3, which moves from 'contract comes up for renewal this financial year' (Nov 2025) to a six-month extension to 30 September 2026 with re-bidding intended through GHL (Feb 2026 and Jun 2026), confirmed in the 13 August 2026 filing as a licence expiry and subsidiary-level going-concern note. Entity creation runs the other way over time — EATS (Aug/Nov 2025), Dubai FZCO (July 2025) and Indonesia (September 2025) are added to pursue new business, not to separate existing business.

**What management expects from it:** Nothing, because no separation was announced. For the group as a whole they guided to 80-83% gross margin, PAT margin of 20-22% pre-JV and 25-28% including JV share, FY27 capex of INR50-60 crore, receivables normalising to 40-45 days by H1 FY27, ~45% ROCE, zero debt, and growth from LFL plus net contract gains.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — No scheme of arrangement, demerger or separation document exists in the material supplied; the only filing is the 13 August 2026 board outcome approving Q1 FY27 results, and its segment note affirms the group is run as a single business. “The Group derives revenue exclusively from Travel QSR outlets, Lounge and related services. In the context of Indian Accounting Standard (Ind AS) 108 - Operating Segments, these products and service lines comprise of only one operating segment, whose operating results are regularly reviewed by the entity's Board of Directors ('Chief Operating Decision Maker') to make decisions about resources to be allocated and assess its performance.”
- *Scheme* — The only entity whose life is ending is the Delhi T3 SPV, and only because its ten-year licence (with extensions) runs out on 30 September 2026 — an expiry, not a separation; the filing says the resulting uncertainty is confined to the subsidiary. “After considering all extensions granted from time to time, the said licence agreement is scheduled to expire on 30 September 2026.”
- *Scheme* — The filing explicitly ring-fences the Delhi T3 issue at subsidiary level, citing group cash flows and liquidity, and gives no separation rationale. “Accordingly, while the above matter represents a material uncertainty at the Subsidiary level, it does not give rise to a material uncertainty at the Group level, and these Consolidated Financial Results have been prepared on a going concern basis.”
- *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=1ef0c8a2-3651-42f2-a0da-eb97edb2e273.pdf)* — The Semolina Kitchens deconsolidation is explained solely as an accounting restatement to permit like-for-like comparison of FY25 and FY26 — no strategic separation reason, no valuation or margin argument, no counterparty request. “This entity was consolidated in our financials until October 14, 2024, and was subsequently deconsolidated.”
- *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=1ef0c8a2-3651-42f2-a0da-eb97edb2e273.pdf)* — Varun Kapur describes the Delhi T3 vehicle as a special purpose vehicle whose life was tied to the concession, and says TFS will simply re-bid through its existing JV, GHL — a contract-structure consequence rather than a business separation. “It was operating through a special purpose vehicle, which had a life tied into that concession.”
- *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=1ef0c8a2-3651-42f2-a0da-eb97edb2e273.pdf)* — Asked about capital allocation with INR8 billion-plus of cash and zero debt, management pointed only to reinvestment in international lounges and expressway wayside amenities at ~45% ROCE — never to unlocking value via a separation. “And as you can see, our ROCE have been at north of 40%, about 45% ROCEs.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=a34eae52-037f-4a76-aa35-15db70915fed.pdf)* — Vikas Kapoor sets out the Delhi T3 SPV shareholding (TFS 60%, DIAL 40%) and says the renewal will go to open tender, with the winner consolidating the operations — the outcome depends on bidding, not on any planned separation. “So our Delhi T3 is an existing joint venture as part of the SPV , when we had won that contract , wherein we hold 60% and DIAL holds 40%.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=a34eae52-037f-4a76-aa35-15db70915fed.pdf)* — The Semolina adjustment is again framed as a planned deconsolidation for comparability only, with details in the presentation. “Semolina Kitchens, was part of our consolidated financials for the first half and part of Q3 of FY '25 and was subsequently deconsolidated , as planned effective October 14, 2024.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=b1ea6a41-2b55-4a4a-9da8-019051bf68c5.pdf)* — The lounge-access technology business was placed in a wholly owned subsidiary, Elite Assist Technology and Services (EATS), to build a new capability inside the group — presented as integration with banks and card networks, removing aggregators, not as a carve-out. “Additionally, at our lounges, we enable the technology platform to provide direct integration to banks and card networks for a smooth lounge access for their customers through our wholly owned subsidiary, Elite Assist Technology and Services.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=b1ea6a41-2b55-4a4a-9da8-019051bf68c5.pdf)* — Asked directly about partner concentration risk with Adani-operated airports (roughly 120 of the then 500+ units) and the DreamFolks precedent, Varun Kapur's answer was deeper joint-venture alignment with the airport operator — the opposite of separating the business. “We already are in a joint venture with Adani Airports.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=082359c9-2f99-4f8d-9bb0-173e76b3da4d.pdf)* — In the first post-listing call, management laid out the two commercial models (consolidated long-term contracts vs equity-accounted JVs/associates) and the reason for reporting system-wide sales; this is the structure of the business as designed, with no mention of separating any part of it. “Long-term contracts are fully consolidated into our P&L and strategic partnerships are accounted as JVs or Associates under the equity pickup model.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=082359c9-2f99-4f8d-9bb0-173e76b3da4d.pdf)* — The Semolina treatment is introduced as an added-back comparability adjustment for FY25 losses and FY25 profits, confirming the accounting-only character of the only 'deconsolidation' in the record. “Accordingly, Semolina's Q1 losses for FY'25 have been added back to the results.”

*Not explained on the calls:* Everything about a separation: no business named, no rationale, numbers, timeline, entity structure, share ratio, requesting party, approvals, or expected benefits appears in any call or the filing.

## AMBER — Amber Enterprises India Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a subsidiary's listing is in motion (DRHP / board approval)) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 4.3/10 · partial spin-off / listing · 4 filing(s) from BSE-screener, NSE · first 2026-04-30, latest 2026-11-07

> **Listing:** IPO / listing of the subsidiary in motion since 2026-04-30; date not fixed

**The stages, as filed:** announced (2026-04-30) → exchange_noc (2026-10-01) → nclt_sanction (2026-06-08)

**Stated in the filings:** appointed date 2025-04-01.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** IL JIN Electronics, Amber's material subsidiary in electronics manufacturing services (EMS), being separately listed via proposed IPO — class `regulatory_strategic`.

- *Insiders:* Amber holds 60,98,240 IL JIN shares, 89.72% post rights issue (Rs 296.02 crore subscribed); promoters Jasbir Singh and Daljit Singh are directors on IL JIN's board; CCPS holders' maximum dilution ~30%
- *What it reveals:* Electronics division FY26 revenue Rs 3,268 crore (+49%), operating EBITDA Rs 287 crore (+89%), guided ~40% FY27 growth at 9.5-10% margins; IL JIN raised Rs 1,750 crore from marquee investors; bought 2018 as a Rs 300-crore, 3%-EBITDA company
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — IPO, not a share distribution to Amber holders; Amber keeps 89.72%; offer size and index effects not stated
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* The DRHP dated 6th November 2026: IL JIN standalone financials, fresh-issue versus offer-for-sale split, and CCPS conversion terms
- *In their words:* “The IPO will be subject to receipt of the required regulatory approvals.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The business being separated is Amber's Electronics / EMS arm, housed in IL JIN Electronics (India) Ltd — PCB assembly (~INR2,281cr of FY26 revenue), bare PCB through Ascent Circuits (98.5% owned), Shogini Technoarts (80%) and the Ascent-K/Korea Circuit HDI JV (~INR600cr), plus Power-One Microsystems (60%, power electronics, ~15% EBITDA) and 50.4% of Israel-listed Unitronics (industrial automation, 24-25% EBITDA) — leaving Amber with the RAC/consumer-durables division (INR8,383cr FY26) and Sidwal railway/defence (INR535cr). The stated driver is funding: essentially all of the group's capex sits in electronics, with more than INR4,500cr of ECMS investment approvals (Ascent multilayer INR991cr, Ascent-K HDI INR3,200cr, Shogini INR500cr), asset turns of only 0.75-1.1x, and the 48% MeitY plus 42% UP incentives arriving 5-6 years after the spend, so FY27 capex of INR1,800-2,000cr (INR1,100-1,200cr cash) and ~INR1,400-1,500cr in FY28 must be pre-funded against a board policy never to exceed 2x debt/EBITDA and Jasbir Singh's pledge to be net-debt-free. Management said investors asked for it: private equity funds were 'chasing to invest in the electronic division', and instead of loading Amber's balance sheet they raised INR1,750cr inside ILJIN (mostly CCPS, including ChrysCapital's INR1,100cr) while Amber separately did a INR1,000cr QIP. Separation also gives electronics its own margin and valuation identity — 2.8% EBITDA when ILJIN was bought in 2018 on INR300cr revenue, 6.9% FY25, 8.8% FY26, 10.8% in Q4 FY26, 26% ROCE, guidance of 40% FY27 growth at 9.5-10% and a $1bn revenue target at 11.5-12% EBITDA — against a weather-driven RAC business that saw quarters of -30% to -35% and nine bad seasons in 25 years. The outside CCPS holders also need a price: conversion happens 'based on the future multiple and valuation' (auditors provisioned up to ~30% dilution in NCI), which a listing supplies; and their presence already constrains group structuring, since management could not say whether the new Oppo mobile-phone business would sit in ILJIN 'because we have other shareholders also in the IL JIN cap table'. It is being done as a listing of the subsidiary, not a demerger: in April 2026 Amber put another INR296.02cr into an INR328.12cr ILJIN rights issue (89.58% to 89.72%); in July 2026 ILJIN split shares from Rs10 to Rs5, raised authorised capital to Rs250cr, issued a 25:1 bonus, converted from private to public limited, shifted its registered office from Pune to Greater Noida and resolved to explore fund-raising 'including... public issue'; the DRHP was filed on 7 November 2026. In parallel Amber is cleaning up the rest of the portfolio — merging wholly-owned AmberPR Technoplast into itself for compliance/cost reduction and peer benchmarking, and selling Sidwal's entire 49% Shivaliks (Titagarh Firema) JV for a nominal Rs1,09,798.85 after INR112cr of FY26 impairment/JV losses, 'to curtail future losses'.

**How it evolved:** The capex trigger appears first on the Jan 2025 call (Korea Circuit JV awaiting the ECMS scheme, Rs1,000cr+ threshold) and on 19 May 2025, when the funding answer is still vague — 'in touch with various institutions' — alongside an INR3,000cr application plan. By 30 July 2025 it has split into two named routes, an INR2,500cr QIP enabling resolution at Amber and 'private equity funds who are chasing to invest in the electronic division', with the $1bn/11.5-12% electronics ambition and a net-debt-free pledge framing why outside money must sit at ILJIN; on 7 Nov 2025 the INR1,750cr ILJIN raise (CCPS, ChrysCapital INR1,100cr pending CCI) and Amber's INR1,000cr QIP are both announced, and 10 Feb 2026 confirms the full INR1,750cr received with Amber still at 90% until CCPS convert. From there it becomes an exit path for those investors: 18 May 2026 ties conversion to 'future multiple and valuation' (~30% assumed dilution), 20 June 2026 shows the ILJIN cap table already constraining where new businesses can be placed, and the filings then execute mechanically — Mar/Apr 2026 rights issue, 11 July 2026 split, 25:1 bonus, public-limited conversion, registered office to Greater Noida and a 'public issue' resolution, and the DRHP on 7 Nov 2026 — none of it ever discussed on an earnings call.

**What management expects from it:** Electronics: self-funded ECMS PCB capex, $1bn revenue in ~3 years, margins from 2.8% (2018) toward 11.5-12%, double digits from FY27, ~26% ROCE, stickier high-entry-barrier industrial/defence mix. Amber: retains ~89.7%, frees cash for consumer durables and railway (30-35% growth, 16-17% margins), stays under 2x debt/EBITDA near net-debt-free; CCPS dilution finally priced off a market valuation.

**Point by point, with the source:**

FY27 capex is guided at INR1,800-2,000cr (INR1,100-1,200cr cash), net debt INR511cr rising to INR700-800cr. “It will happen in future based on the future multiple and valuation.”
- *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=e758d7f3-9942-4baf-b20b-0e80b2d6971a.pdf)* — The ILJIN cap table already limits group structuring — management cannot say whether the new Oppo mobile-phone business (8m units year one, 13-15m year two, sub-INR50cr capex, 1.5-2% industry EBITDA) will sit inside ILJIN or directly under Amber. “But we will not be able to define it right now because we have other shareholders also in the IL JIN cap table .”
- *Scheme* — April 2026: Amber pre-funds ILJIN again, subscribing INR296.02cr of a INR328.12cr rights issue (12,46,430 shares), taking its holding from 89.58% to 89.72% — capital in before the listing, not a stake sale. “Further, pursuant to the allotment of equity shares under the rights issue by IL JIN on 21st April 2026, which has resulted in an investment of Rs. 296.02 Crore, Amber Enterprises India Limited (“Amber” or “the Company”) has subscribed to and been allotted 12,46,430 equity shares.”
- *Scheme* — July 2026: ILJIN is mechanically prepared for listing — Rs10 to Rs5 share split, authorised capital to Rs250cr, 25:1 bonus, conversion from private to public limited, registered office moved Pune to Greater Noida, and a board resolution to explore fund-raising modes including a public issue. “Evaluation and exploration of various fund-raising options to support its future growth initiatives.”

## EMMVEE — Emmvee Photovoltaic Power Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a subsidiary's listing is in motion (DRHP / board approval)) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 4.3/10 · partial spin-off / listing · 1 filing(s) from NSE · first 2025-12-02, latest 2025-12-02

> **Listing:** IPO / listing of the subsidiary in motion since 2025-12-02; date not fixed — No demerged entity stated; the Company itself: "The equity shares of the Company were listed on the National Stock Exchange of India Limited (NSE) and BSE Limited (BSE) on November 18, 2025" (said December 2, 2025)

**The stages, as filed:** meetings (2025-12-02)

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Nothing; documents disclose no demerger or spin-off, only ESOS 2025 ratification by postal ballot — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* Promoters and promoter group employees, and directors holding over 10% of equity, are excluded from ESOS 2025; no director/KMP interest beyond shareholding or options grantable.
- *What it reveals:* not stated
- *Selling pressure:* unclear — No separation disclosed; only potential dilution of 35,00,000 equity shares of Rs.2 face value under ESOS 2025.
- *Parent or spin:* neither · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* ESOS 2025 scheme document and postal ballot results due on or before Monday, January 05, 2026
- *In their words:* “The equity shares of the Company were listed on the National Stock Exchange of India Limited (NSE) and BSE Limited (BSE) on November 18, 2025.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The documents supplied contain no separation, demerger, spin-off, slump sale, hive-off or scheme of arrangement for Emmvee Photovoltaic Power Ltd., and management never explains one — so no rationale can be reconstructed from these texts. Across all four calls (Dec 2025, Jan 2026, Apr/May 2026, Jul 2026) the strategic direction stated is the opposite of separation: deeper vertical integration inside one group. Management's stated plan is to add a 6 GW integrated TOPCon cell+module facility at Devanahalli/ITIR Phase 2 (total cost ~INR 5,500 crores, hard costs ~INR 4,600 crores, IREDA term loan sanctioned at INR 3,306 crores at 7.95%/sub-8%), taking capacity to ~16.3 GW modules and 8.9 GW cells by end-FY27, then backward integrate into 9 GW of ingot and wafer in two phases (5 GW in FY29, 4 GW in FY30, ~INR 600-700 crores per GW, largely from internal accruals) 'primarily to protect margins, reduce exposure to upstream supply chain volatility, and strengthen the economics of our domestic cell and module manufacturing operations.' Suhas Manjunatha explicitly argued that standalone module capacity in India 'starts to become irrelevant' and that the future belongs to integrated cell+module and then wafer/ingot players — an argument for combining businesses, not splitting them. The only structural fact disclosed is that the group already operates through two manufacturing entities — the parent Emmvee Photovoltaic Power Ltd. and subsidiary Emmvee Energy — with inter-company order execution and eliminations, but this is described purely as an accounting/execution matter 'all within the group,' with no plan to separate them. The only filing provided is a December 2, 2025 postal ballot notice seeking ratification of ESOS-2025 (35,00,000 options) and extension of ESOS benefits to subsidiary employees; its sole references to demerger are standard ESOP boilerplate on corporate-action adjustments and option treatment, not an announced transaction. No investor, lender, partner or analyst on any call asked for a separation.

**How it evolved:** The idea never surfaces. Dec 2, 2025 (Q2 FY26 call) sets the four-pillar integrated strategy and flags intended backward integration into wafers and ingots timed to ALMM List 3 (June 2028); Jan 16, 2026 (Q3 FY26) repeats that wafer/ingot is 'the next transition' but declines to commit a timeline pending ALMM clarity; Apr 29, 2026 (Q4/FY26) quantifies it at 9 GW in two phases (FY29/FY30) and says 'we will deepen integration'; Jul 16, 2026 (Q1 FY27) restates the same 9 GW plan with commissioning around mid-CY2028 and reiterates margin protection as the purpose. At no point in this 36-month sequence does management, an analyst or a filing raise separating, demerging or divesting any business.

**What management expects from it:** Nothing is said about a separation. What management does quantify is from integration: EBITDA margin up to 35% in Q1 FY27 on higher internal cell use, EBITDA per watt of ~INR 2-2.5 (non-DCR module), ~INR 6-6.5 (cell), ~INR 8.5-9 (DCR module), ~INR 2,400 crores EBITDA targeted for FY27, net debt/equity of -0.06x, ROCE 38%, ROE 51%, and ICRA upgrades to A.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=a073e549-706d-4091-bf9d-f6cdbdcff699.pdf)* — Management's stated structural direction for FY27 is deeper integration across the value chain, not separation of any business. “For Emmvee, the direction is clear: we will deepen integration, scale with discipline, improve technology and efficiency, pro tect balance sheet strength and build resilience across the supply chain.”
- *Dec 2025* — Suhas Manjunatha argued the industry is moving toward integrated cell+module (and later wafer/ingot) players, with standalone module manufacturing becoming irrelevant — a case for combining, not separating, businesses. “So when look at standalone module manufacturers, I think the roadmap of the industry is quite clear that in the next couple of years the standalone module capacity in India starts to become irrelevant and the focus is going to be completely on integrated module manufacturers.”
- *[Jul 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=e6f11bde-6a33-4790-bc65-52bad1cf8680.pdf)* — The stated purpose of the only structural initiative disclosed — 9 GW of ingot and wafer backward integration in two phases (5 GW FY29, 4 GW FY30) funded largely from internal accruals — is margin protection and supply-chain control, not separation. “This backward integration is intended primarily to protect margins, reduce exposure to upstream supply chain volatility, and strengthen the economics of our domestic cell and module manufacturing operations.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=a073e549-706d-4091-bf9d-f6cdbdcff699.pdf)* — The only group-structure disclosure is that two entities — parent Emmvee Photovoltaic Power Ltd. and subsidiary Emmvee Energy — both manufacture, with cross-entity order execution producing inter-company eliminations, explicitly described as internal to the group. “Yeah, yeah, you’re right. I mean, basically, it’s like, you know, we have two , companies basically, one, is the parent and other is a subsidiary where both have manufacturing capacities and one has cell manufacturing capacity.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=a073e549-706d-4091-bf9d-f6cdbdcff699.pdf)* — Capital allocation for the 6 GW integrated Devanahalli facility is being kept inside the existing company, with land paid for and taken into the company's possession and an IREDA term loan of INR 3,306 crores sanctioned — no separate vehicle or carve-out is mentioned. “IREDA has sanctioned our term loan for INR3,306 crores for this facility. We have also completed payment for land allotment at Devanahalli, Bengaluru and the land is now in the company’s possession.”
- *Scheme* — The December 2, 2025 postal ballot's only references to demerger/reorganisation are generic ESOS-2025 provisions for adjusting options on corporate actions — boilerplate, not an announced separation. “RESOLVED FURTHER THAT  in case of any corporate action(s) such as rights issues, bonus issues, merger and sale of division or other re -organization, split  or any other change in the capital structure of the Company, as applicable from time to time, requisite adjustments (which may include adjustments to the number of options in ESOS 2025 ) shall be appropriately made, in a fair and reasonable manner in accordance with ESOS 2025 .”
- *Scheme* — The same notice contemplates employees being transferred under a scheme of arrangement only as a contingency for option treatment, with no transaction identified, no businesses named and no rationale given. “In the event that an employee who has been granted benefits under the Scheme is transferred pursuant to a scheme of arrangement, amalgamation, merger or demerger, or continued in the existing company prior to the vesting or exercise, the treatment of options in such case shall be as specified in such scheme of arrangement, amalgamation, merger or demerger, provided that such treatment shall not be prejudicial to the interest of the employee.”

*Not explained on the calls:* Everything: the calls and the single filing never mention a separation, so no businesses, numbers, problems solved, requesting parties, timeline or plan changes are explained anywhere.

## FIRSTCRY — Brainbees Solutions Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a subsidiary's listing is in motion (DRHP / board approval)) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 4.3/10 · partial spin-off / listing · 11 filing(s) from NSE · first 2025-12-26, latest 2026-10-07

> **Listing:** IPO / listing of the subsidiary in motion since 2025-12-26; date not fixed

**The stages, as filed:** meetings (2026-08-29)

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Swara Baby, the group's hygiene contract-manufacturing business (baby/adult diapers, sanitary napkins), via a separate IPO — class `unrelated`.

- *Insiders:* Brainbees holds 76.59% and remains Promoter of Swara Baby; it will sell up to Rs 3,000 million in the Rs 5,000 million OFS. Operations led by Mr. Alok Birla and Mr. Udit Birla; Supam Maheshwari and Gautam Sharma are non-executive directors.
- *What it reveals:* Swara Baby is "the largest contract manufacturer by value in Fiscal 2025" in Indian hygiene manufacturing, with FY26 revenue of Rs 11,639 million and EBITDA of Rs 1,927.70 million buried inside Brainbees' India multi-channel segment, while consolidated Brainbees posted an FY26 loss of Rs 2,036.58 million.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — No shares distributed to Brainbees holders; Swara Baby lists via fresh issue plus OFS, and Brainbees stays majority owner.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Swara Baby DRHP dated July 2, 2026 - Risk Factor No. 2, pages 23-24, on revenue dependence on Brainbees
- *In their words:* “With this expansive and global vision in contract manufacturing of disposable hygiene products with different capex and working capital needs, we decided to initiate the process of separately listing this business so that they can follow their independent journey.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The business being separated is Swara Baby Products Limited, Brainbees' diaper/hygiene manufacturing subsidiary, which filed a DRHP on July 02, 2026 for an IPO of up to Rs 10,000 million (Rs 5,000 million fresh issue plus Rs 5,000 million offer for sale), with Brainbees itself selling up to Rs 3,000 million in the OFS (board approval July 01, 2026). Management's stated reason is drift in purpose: Brainbees invested Rs 906.17 million in 2020 for 53.45% (fully diluted) purely as backward integration — "to scale up our home brands within diaper category" with "more control on quality at scale, production timelines and continued innovation in diaper manufacturing" — but Swara then became the largest contract manufacturer by value in Fiscal 2025 in Indian hygiene manufacturing, adding adult diapers and sanitary napkins (similar absorbent raw materials and processes), third-party and multinational customers, and exports via a US subsidiary (Swara Corp, incorporated 08 December 2025). Brainbees' share of Swara's revenue fell from 27.03% in FY24 to 22.64% in FY26, so management says Swara "has charted a very different long term vision as compared to the original alignment with Brainbees," with "different capex and working capital needs" it should "bridge their own capital requirement" rather than draw on Brainbees' cash. On selling into the OFS despite holding cash, management argued "holding cash and holding an investment are two different capital allocation decisions" and that partial monetisation lets it "crystallize value, improve return on investment and maintain flexibility for future strategic opportunities." Control and commercials are explicitly unchanged: Brainbees stays Promoter at 76.59% (raised from 75.92% in a December 2025 swap that moved Solis Hygiene under Swara to put the hygiene vertical "under a single roof"), Swara remains a subsidiary, Brainbees' management has no involvement in running it (Alok Birla and Udit Birla lead; Supam Maheshwari and Gautam Sharma sit as non-executive directors), and "terms of trade" stay at arm's length with "no impact either on supply chain or pricing." Swara contributed Rs 11,639 million revenue in FY26 (Rs 9,004.39 million after eliminating Rs 2,634.61 million of inter-company sales) and Rs 1,445.7 million of adjusted EBITDA into the India multi-channel segment. No lender, partner or investor is named as having demanded it; analysts had only pushed on a separate asset, GlobalBees, where Supam said in August 2025 that "the most probable outcome for Globalbees... will be listing" given its separate board, management and investors (Premji, Lightspeed, Chiratae).

**How it evolved:** The idea first surfaced as an analyst question about a different unit: on the Aug 2025 call (Aug 13, 2025) Sachin Dixit asked whether FirstCry investors could expect liquidity from GlobalBees "getting demerged, having its own IPO," and Supam said listing was the most probable outcome over a few years; on the Feb 2026 call (Feb 13, 2026) Ajay Agarwal asked for GlobalBees listing timelines and got no answer. Meanwhile the hygiene business was quietly being tidied for separation — a December 26, 2025 intra-group restructuring put Solis Hygiene under Swara Baby to bring the whole hygiene vertical under one roof, lifting Brainbees' Swara stake to 76.59%. Neither the Feb 2026 nor the Jun 2026 call (May 26, 2026) mentioned Swara or any separation at all; on Jun 2026 Supam even said buybacks and similar capital actions had not been discussed internally or at board level. The plan then appeared fully formed in filings only — board approval of OFS participation on July 01, 2026, DRHP plus a management Q&A on July 02, 2026 — followed by a related narrowing at GlobalBees, whose non-core brand rationalisation culminated in the October 07, 2026 sale of its entire 51.54% in Mush Textile.

**What management expects from it:** Swara funds its own capex/working capital from the Rs 5,000 million fresh issue and pursues an independent global contract-manufacturing path; Brainbees crystallizes value, improves ROI and gains flexibility via up to Rs 3,000 million OFS cash, while keeping 76.59% control, Promoter status, consolidation of Swara's Rs 9,004 million revenue and Rs 1,445.7 million adjusted EBITDA, and unchanged arm's-length supply and pricing.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=4e061dce-c165-4749-9bdb-c4d6dae5f4c6.pdf)* — Asked by JM Financial's Sachin Dixit whether FirstCry shareholders could get liquidity from GlobalBees being demerged or separately IPO'd, Supam framed listing as the likely eventual route and Brainbees' monetisation path over a few years. “Having said this, the most probable outcome for Globalbees as an outcome will be listing, which company and its shareholders will decide over a period of time, is when Brainbees also will find a monetization opportunity over a period of a few years.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=4e061dce-c165-4749-9bdb-c4d6dae5f4c6.pdf)* — The structural argument for separability given for GlobalBees was that it already runs independently of Brainbees, with its own CEO, board and outside shareholders including Premji, Lightspeed and Chiratae. “The company has a separate management team, which is run separately and also it has its separate board, and also it has a separate set of investors as well, apart from Brainbees as well, which includes Premji, Lightspeed, and Chiratae, and so on and so forth.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=b7f23ae4-cfbb-47ce-b8a9-a579caae0f24.pdf)* — Garima Mishra pressed on the CCPS infusion into GlobalBees; Gautam said it funded working capital, and that all three investor-directors who had stepped off the GlobalBees board participated in that round — the capital-need theme that later justifies Swara funding itself. “This is largely for taking care of their working capital requirement, Garima”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=c27dd63f-321b-4b7b-af06-12c29e11d89d.pdf)* — Ajay Agarwal again asked directly for a GlobalBees listing timeline; the reply covered only Flipkart's revenue-recognition impact and GlobalBees' EBITDA growth (c.150% YoY in Q3, c.50% in 9M), with no timeline given. “And again on Globalbees, any plans on listing of Globalbees? Can you share the tentative timelines or any sense on the same?”
- *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=c3d40b3d-ee57-4607-a1df-fcd732269f6b.pdf)* — Five weeks before the Swara DRHP, asked about the low valuation, takeover risk and buybacks, Supam said no such capital action had been discussed internally or by the board — and said nothing about any separation. “Yes, we have sufficient cash on the company, but we haven't discussed any of these buybacks and stuff like that so far, in our internal discussions or even board discussions.”
- *Scheme* — The July 02, 2026 DRHP filing states the original purpose of the 2020 Rs 906.17 million investment for 53.45%: backward integration to scale FirstCry's own diaper home brands with control over quality, timelines and innovation. “We wanted to scale up our home brands within diaper category and wanted to do backward integration to get more control on quality at scale, production timelines and continued innovation in diaper manufacturing.”
- *Scheme* — Core rationale: Swara outgrew the FirstCry ecosystem — multiple third-party and multinational customers, adult diapers and feminine hygiene, exports and a US subsidiary, with Brainbees' share of its revenue down from 27.03% (FY24) to 22.64% (FY26). “With Swara Baby's diversification across product lines, more channels, expansion into International geographies, the business has charted a very different long term vision as compared to the original alignment with Brainbees.”
- *Scheme* — Why not just fund Swara off Brainbees' balance sheet: its capex and working-capital profile differs, so it should raise its own money while Brainbees keeps supply and arm's-length pricing unchanged. “With this expansive and global vision in contract manufacturing of disposable hygiene products with different capex and working capital needs, we decided to initiate the process of separately listing this business so that they can follow their independent journey and bridge their own capital requirement.”
- *Scheme* — Why Brainbees sells up to Rs 3,000 million into the OFS despite ample cash: capital-allocation discipline and value crystallisation, while Swara stays a 76.59% subsidiary and Brainbees' management stays out of its operations. “Partial monetization of a successful investment allows us to crystallize value, improve return on investment and maintain flexibility for future strategic opportunities.”
- *Scheme* — Preparatory step on December 26, 2025: Swara Baby acquired 100% of Solis Hygiene (FY25 turnover Rs 240.73 crore, 3% of consolidated), with Brainbees swapping its 79.34% Solis stake for 56,26,738 Swara shares, lifting its Swara holding from 75.92% to 76.59%. “In order to bring the complete Hygiene vertical under a single roof, the restructuring is being done.”
- *Scheme* — The parallel pruning at GlobalBees: on October 07, 2026 it signed an MOU to sell its entire 51.54% in Mush Textile (brands Mush and BePlush, Rs 11.34 crore or 0.13% of FY26 turnover) for Rs 5,68,93,940 to Nihar Gosalia and Vaishvik Brahmbhatt. “Upon completion of the aforesaid transaction, Mush will cease to be a Subsidiary of GlobalBees and, accordingly, will also cease to be a Step-down Subsidiary of the Company.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=c27dd63f-321b-4b7b-af06-12c29e11d89d.pdf)* — The GlobalBees brand-rationalisation logic that frames the Mush exit: loss-making, slow-growing non-core brands were being exited, with core categories at 30% growth and 4.9% adjusted EBITDA versus 2% consolidated. “As you're aware, over the last few quarters, we've been speaking about rationalizing certain brands because they were delivering a relatively lower revenue growth as well as incurring losses.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No earnings call ever mentions the Swara IPO, its valuation, or use of OFS proceeds; GlobalBees listing timeline never answered; Mush sale pricing and loss unexplained.
