**The stages, as filed:** nclt_sanction (2026-09-29)

**Stated in the filings:** entitlement **5 for every 41**.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Nothing is spun off — listed subsidiary Shiva Cement is amalgamated into parent JSW Cement — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* JSW Cement holds 66.23% of Shiva's equity and all its OCCRPS; promoter group of JSW Cement goes 72.02% to 71.39% post-merger; no consideration/benefit to promoters stated.
- *What it reveals:* Shiva's 1.32 mtpa Sundargarh clinker unit plus FY26-commissioned 1.0 MTPA Sambalpur grinding unit come in with negative net worth (INR -30.08 crore) and INR 133.92 crore accumulated losses written off against securities premium.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — Only 1.21 crore new shares on 137.55 crore base (~0.9%); same industry, same promoter, larger and more liquid entity.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* The Regulation 37 Scheme filing with the valuation report and fairness opinions behind the 5:41 share exchange ratio.
- *In their words:* “This consolidation creates a single unified cement platform to unlock operational, financial, and management synergies.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The premise needs one correction: across these texts JSW Cement is not separating a business — the only scheme of arrangement on record (Boards of 29 September 2026) is the opposite, an amalgamation of its listed 66.23%-owned subsidiary Shiva Cement Limited into JSW Cement under Sections 230-232 read with Sections 52 and 66, appointed date 1 April 2026, expected to close in 12-14 months. Management's stated reasons are: (i) business synergies from pooling financial, managerial, technical, distribution and marketing resources, giving cost reduction and streamlined day-to-day running of the units; (ii) backward integration into Shiva's 1.32 MTPA clinker plant at Sundargarh, Odisha, so clinker — 'a key raw material in manufacturing of cement' — is available internally instead of bought from third parties with mark-ups; (iii) financial synergies, i.e. raising funds 'within a single entity on more favorable terms' and eliminating inter-company guarantees — relevant because Shiva standalone had negative net worth of INR (30.08) crore at 31 March 2026 on turnover of only INR 435.17 crore, against JSW Cement's INR 7,029.47 crore net worth and INR 5,995.28 crore turnover; (iv) ending the cost of running two listed entities — duplicated administration, multiple record-keeping, double compliance and group-consolidation effort; (v) giving Shiva's 33.50% public float shares in a far more liquid, institutionally-held stock (consideration is 5 JSW Cement shares of FV INR 10 for every 41 Shiva shares of FV INR 2, no cash, taking JSW Cement to 1,37,55,13,537 shares and diluting promoters from 72.02% to 71.39%); and (vi) 'right sizing' both balance sheets — Shiva's accumulated losses set against its securities premium (leaving retained earnings at INR (133.92) crore and SPA nil) and the Amalgamation Adjustment Deficit Account set against JSW Cement's premium, which ends at INR 4,335.67 crore. The genuine separations in these texts are divestments, not demergers: the 17 November 2025 Securities Purchase Agreement selling 100% of Algebra Endeavour Private Limited / Vadraj Energy Gujarat Ltd (a Gujarat power plant) to Nuvoco Vistas for INR 191.63 crore, a unit that contributed nothing to turnover or net worth, and the 13 August 2026 Board approval to sell up to INR 123 crore of JSW One Platforms shares as Promoter Selling Shareholder in JOPL's IPO. Valuation was done by PwC Business Consulting Services and BDO Valuation Advisory, with fairness opinions from SBI Capital Markets (for JSW Cement) and DAM Capital (for Shiva), JM Financial as exclusive financial advisor.

**How it evolved:** The Shiva merger never appears in any earnings call in the window — not Sep 2025 (Q1 FY26), not Feb 2026, not the 21 May 2026 Q4 FY26 call; the Nov 2025 call transcript is an unextractable scanned PDF, so it cannot be checked. What the calls do show is investors pushing on the group's other unconsolidated structure: on 3 September 2025 Kamlesh Bagmar argued holding the Fujairah clinker capacity through a JV 'don't make much sense for the shareholders' and Narinder Singh replied the financial investors would exit and it would become a full subsidiary; on 21 May 2026 Raghav Maheshwari asked directly about merging that JV in and was told 'not as of now', maybe in two to three years once the financial investor is given an exit. The Shiva amalgamation then arrives fully formed in the 29 September 2026 Board outcome, press release and Regulation 30 annexure, and is restated as a 'Key Business Update' in the 27 October 2026 Q2 FY27 press release with the 12-14 month timeline unchanged.

**What management expects from it:** JSW Cement: one unified platform with category leadership, higher share and efficient resource use; cost reduction from pooled resources; in-house clinker from Shiva's 1.32 mtpa Sundargarh kiln avoiding third-party mark-ups; cheaper funding in a single entity, inter-company guarantees gone; right-sized statements (SPA INR 4,335.67 crore). Shiva holders: direct economics plus liquidity in a bigger, institutionally-held stock.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The 29 September 2026 Board approved amalgamating listed subsidiary Shiva Cement into JSW Cement, framed as building one consolidated platform rather than splitting anything off. “This consolidation creates a single unified cement platform to unlock operational, financial, and management synergies.”
- *Scheme* — The core industrial logic is securing clinker internally: Shiva's 1.32 mtpa Sundargarh, Odisha kiln becomes an in-house raw-material source rather than a related-party supplier. “The proposed amalgamation will result in backward integration of clinker manufacturing with the Transferee Company's cement manufacturing business. The internal availability of clinker is expected to reduce dependence on external procurement, improve supply-chain efficiency, and result in cost savings by avoiding third-party purchases and associated mark-ups.”
- *Scheme* — Funding is an explicit driver — one borrower instead of two, and the inter-company guarantees JSW Cement had been giving for Shiva fall away. “The proposed amalgamation will lead to greater ability of the consolidated entity to access and raise funds within a single entity on more favorable terms, leading to elimination of inter company guarantees and facilitate more efficient funding arrangements.”
- *Scheme* — Shiva's 33.50% public float (9,88,24,292 shares) is moved into a much larger, more liquid stock; this is the benefit management offers minorities in place of cash. “The public shareholders of the Transferor Company would become shareholders in the Transferee Company, which has a higher traded equity share base, greater market liquidity, and a diversified institutional investor base, thereby providing shareholders with enhanced liquidity, broader market participation, and improved opportunities for value realization.”
- *Scheme* — Running two listed cement companies in the same group was itself the problem — duplicated administration, double compliance and group consolidation effort. “The proposed amalgamation will result in a simplification of the existing corporate structure and eliminate administrative functions and duplications, reducing regulatory and legal compliances of two listed entities, eliminating multiple record keeping and reducing time and efforts for consolidation of financials at the group level, consequently reducing the administrative costs of maintaining separate companies, while reducing the multiple legal and regulatory compliances.”
- *Scheme* — Shiva was a loss-making, negative-net-worth entity (net worth INR (30.08) crore at 31 March 2026 on INR 435.17 crore FY26 turnover), so the Scheme writes its accumulated losses off against its securities premium, leaving retained earnings at INR (133.92) crore and SPA nil; JSW Cement's premium absorbs the Amalgamation Adjustment Deficit and ends at INR 4,335.67 crore. “The reorganization of reserves shall result in the right sizing of the financial statement of the Transferor Company which will reflect its true and fair financial position.”
- *Scheme* — Consideration is all-paper at 5-for-41 with no cash, taking JSW Cement from 1,36,33,64,936 to 1,37,55,13,537 shares and promoters from 72.02% to 71.39%; JSW Cement's own 66.23% stake and Shiva's entire INR 100 crore of 1% OCCRPS held by JSW Cement are cancelled. “The Transferee Company shall, without any further application, act or deed, issue and allot to the equity shareholder(s) of the Transferor Company (except the Transferee Company) whose names are recorded in the register of members as a member of the Transferor Company on the Record Date 5 (Five) Equity Shares of the face value of INR 10 (Indian Rupees Ten only) each fully paid-up, for every 41 (Forty One) equity shares of the face value of INR 2 (Indian Rupees Two only) each fully paid-up held by such member in the Transferor Company.”
- *Scheme* — CEO Nilesh Narwekar's own framing on 29 September 2026 puts integration, synergies, structural simplicity and minority liquidity in one sentence. “The proposed merger is a strategic step towards creating a more integrated and efficient business. It will unlock operational and financial synergies, strengthen backward integration, and simplify our corporate structure. Importantly, it will enable Shiva Cement's public shareholders to participate directly in the growth of a larger and more liquid listed entity.”
- *Scheme* — Strategic ambition beyond cost: a single platform is presented as the vehicle for scale and share, with closing dependent on exchanges, SEBI, NCLT Mumbai, Odisha IDCO, shareholders and creditors over 12-14 months. “Unified Cement Platform: Creating a consolidated cement platform supports Transferee Company's strategy, enabling category leadership, increased competitiveness, enhanced market share and efficient resource utilization.”
- *CALL May 2026* — On 21 May 2026 an investor (Raghav Maheshwari, Equirus) asked whether the unconsolidated UAE Fujairah clinker JV would be folded in; management deferred, citing the need to exit a financial investor first — the only consolidation question asked on any call in the window, and it was about the JV, not Shiva. “Not as of now. Probably going forward in next 2-3 years, we will have a look because there is a financial investor sitting there, we'll have to provide exit to him.”
- *CALL Sep 2025* — The structural-simplification pressure came from investors as early as 3 September 2025, when Kamlesh Bagmar (Lotus Asset Managers) argued that holding Fujairah clinker through a JV 'don't make much sense for the shareholders'. “So, Kamlesh, as I mentioned earlier, the other stakeholders in the Fujairah entity are financial investors. So, over a period of time, definitely they will be taking the exit, and this becomes a full subsidiary.”
- *CALL Feb 2026* — The genuine disposals are non-core asset sales, not demergers: the Q3 FY26 deck disclosed the sale of the Gujarat power-plant entity to Nuvoco (the 17 November 2025 SPA covers 100% of Algebra Endeavour Private Limited, a unit the filing says contributes nothing to turnover or net worth). “Entered into a Share Purchase Agreement with Nuvoco Vistas Corp. Ltd. for the transfer of Vadraj Energy Gujarat Ltd. (owning a power plant in Gujarat), for a consideration of Rs. 191.63 crore”

*Not explained on the calls:* No quantified synergy, clinker-saving or cost figure; no call commentary, Q&A or analyst pushback on the merger; Nov 2025 transcript unreadable; Fujairah JV consolidation still unresolved.

## NTPC — NTPC Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a scheme of arrangement whose nature the documents on file do not settle) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 4.3/10 · scheme (nature unclear) · 1 filing(s) from NSE · first 2025-11-28, latest 2025-11-28

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'nclt_sanction' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**The stages, as filed:** nclt_sanction (2025-11-28)

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Coal mining business — captive coal mines plus Ranchi Coal Mining Head Quarter — hived off to NTPC Mining Limited — class `regulatory_strategic`.

- *Insiders:* NML is a wholly owned subsidiary of NTPC; no promoter (Government of India) or management stake, shareholding change or incentive in NML is stated in the documents.
- *What it reveals:* Transfer executed under BTA at estimated value Rs 10,503 crore; cumulative coal-mining capex Rs 14,136 crore as on 31 Dec 2025 under cost-plus framework giving stable ROE; nine coal blocks, 92 MMTPA peak, 48.66 MT produced FY26, captive share 18% rising to 25% by FY30.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — No shares distributed to shareholders; NML is an unlisted wholly owned subsidiary, so no index exclusion or forced selling arises.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Business Transfer Agreement dated 17 September 2025 and the Rs 10,503 crore transfer value versus NML regulated equity
- *In their words:* “With this, the hiving-off of the Coal Mining Business has been completed in all respects, and all coal mining units stand transferred to NTPC Mining Limited.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The business being separated is NTPC's captive coal mining business — nine coal blocks with 92 MMTPA peak rated capacity — hived off out of NTPC standalone into NTPC Mining Limited (NML), a wholly owned subsidiary, under a Business Transfer Agreement "at an estimated value of 10,503 crore" (amended BTA dated 17 September 2025), executed in tranches (Chatti Bariatu and Badam first, per the 28 Aug / 1 Oct / 1 Dec 2025 and 1 Feb 2026 disclosures) and completed with the final tranche — Pakri Barwadih mine plus the Coal Mining Head Quarter at Ranchi — effective 1 April 2026, on which date Pakri Barwadih North West was also declared commercial. Management's stated case rests first on scale and fuel security: captive production rose from 35.64 MT (FY24) to 45.82 MT in FY25 (+29%) to 47.88–48.66 MT in FY26 (+8.5%), cumulative mining capex climbed INR12,380 crore (FY25) → INR13,300 crore (Sep-25) → INR14,136 crore (Dec-25), captive coal now meets 18% of requirement and is targeted at 25% by FY30 (CMD: 25% "in next 3 to 4 years"), and in FY26 no coal was imported at all. Second, economics: Director (Finance) repeatedly framed mining capex as "long-term equity deployment under the cost-plus framework and supporting a stable return on equity," and standalone regulated equity is reported as a single pool "for conventional power and mining business" (INR94,631 crore at 31 March 2026), while Aug 2025 he said the "more preponderant thing is fuel security," not cheaper coal than Coal India. Third — and this is the only explicit reason given for needing a separate company — CMD stressed the entity's name: "it is not Coal Mining Limited, it is a Mining Limited," because "we are trying to have some other mines also into that," and NML is the vehicle to pursue "all kind of possibilities within or outside," naming the Government's ~INR37,000 crore coal-gasification programme (coal-to-SNG, pilot 0.4 MTPA at Talaipalli with EIL, potentially feeding NTPC's idle gas plants at peak) and, under the SHANTI Act, fuel processing in the nuclear chain. Structurally it repeats the pattern of NGEL (renewables plus green chemicals; listed 27 November 2024), NPUNL (advanced nuclear, incorporated Jan 2025) and the ASHVINI JV with NPCIL — each business in a dedicated entity carrying its own capex inside a programme of INR17 lakh crore to FY37 and 41% of future capacity sitting in JVs/subsidiaries, with Government of India having raised the investment-approval limit for renewable subsidiaries to INR20,000 crore. Critically, no lender, partner or investor was named as having asked for the mining hive-off, and management never attached a tax, tariff, valuation or monetisation rationale to it; the only "unlocking value" language in three years of calls came in response to an investor question (Apoorva Bahadur, 23 May 2026) about press reports of listing THDC, NEEPCO and Hindustan Urvarak, where DF said there are "no definitive plans," it is "one of the options," and as a JV with the UP government it must be "dealt at the fairly senior policy level."

**How it evolved:** Through the 25 Jan 2025, 24 May 2025 and 18 Aug 2025 meetings there is no mention of NML at all — the separation story is NGEL's 27 Nov 2024 listing, NPUNL's incorporation, and mining described only as capex "contributing to Regulated Equity growth" and a fuel-security play. The hive-off surfaces in the 30 Oct 2025 (Q2 FY26) call as a done deal already signed: BTA for INR10,503 crore, Chatti Bariatu and Badam transferred, "we expect to complete transfer of all the remaining mines to NML in the current fiscal." The 30 Jan 2026 call reports only progress metrics (INR14,136 crore mining capex, Pakri Barwadih NW dispatch, Badam mine-opening clearance), the 23 May 2026 call announces completion on 1 April 2026, and only at the 27 July 2026 annual meet did management explain the logic — DF: "we have now carved it out as a separate company"; CMD: the name is Mining, not Coal Mining, so other mines can come in, with coal gasification and nuclear-fuel processing flagged as the adjacent prizes.

**What management expects from it:** For NML: fuel security — captive coal from 18% of requirement to 25% by FY30, nine mines/92 MMTPA, mining capex (INR14,136 crore) as cost-plus regulated equity earning stable ROE, plus a platform for non-coal minerals, coal gasification and fuel processing. For NTPC: an unchanged cost-plus core. No margin, valuation or listing target was given.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Jan 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=5470e555-5c40-4a84-bfbf-52804e035934.pdf)* — The template for carve-outs is set: NGEL, the renewables vehicle, was listed on 27 November 2024 and presented as the way to position the clean-energy business separately. “The successful listing of NTPC Green Energy Limited (NGEL) during the quarter marks a significant milestone in NTPC's journey towards sustainable energy leadership.”
- *[May 2025](https://ntpc.co.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/REVTranscriptConcall24052025.pdf)* — Before any hive-off is mentioned, mining is justified inside NTPC purely as regulated-equity-accretive capex — INR12,380 crore invested on a standalone basis — plus captive production up 29% to 45.82 MT. “We have invested 12,380 crore in developing our coal mines on standalone basis, contributing to Regulated Equity growth and resulting in additional revenue stream for the Company.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=293230fa-9f9f-49b0-b470-98641c90f216.pdf)* — Asked by Ramesh Bhojwani whether captive coal is cheaper than Coal India's, DF declined the cost argument and named fuel security as the dominant purpose of owning mines, noting new mines carry higher stripping ratios and capital cost. “See, the primary idea of NTPC getting into its own captive mines is, the more preponderant thing is fuel security.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=293230fa-9f9f-49b0-b470-98641c90f216.pdf)* — On an investor question about where new businesses will sit, CMD confirmed the group's entity-per-business design — green chemicals and hydrogen derivatives go into NTPC Green, not the parent. “You have already said, the green chemicals will be part of the NTPC Green.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=73638cb2-aa32-49e8-91ce-6f452625f693.pdf)* — First disclosure of the separation in a call: the Business Transfer Agreement for hiving off coal mining to NTPC Mining Limited was signed at an estimated value of INR10,503 crore, with Chatti Bariatu and Badam already transferred. “We expect to complete transfer of all the remaining mines to NML in the current fiscal.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=a34b65bf-06e8-4d67-b630-5dd881ccf2a0.pdf)* — Mid-transfer, the economics are restated as cost-plus: cumulative mining capex of INR14,136 crore at 31 December 2025 is presented as equity earning a regulated, stable return — the same framework that will travel with the business into NML. “The cumulative capital expenditure in coal mining stood at INR14,136 crores as on 31st December 2025, providing a long-term equity deployment under the cost-plus framework and supporting a stable return on equity.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=d2a690dd-c88b-4131-ae93-58eace85d36c.pdf)* — Completion announced: with Pakri Barwadih moving on 1 April 2026 the whole mining business now sits in a wholly owned subsidiary; captive coal (18% of requirement, 47.88 MT, +8.5%) is cited as why fuel security is "more assured than ever before." “With the transfer of Pakri Barwadih coal mines on 1st of April 2026, the transfer of NTPC's mining business to NTPC Mining Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary, has been fully completed under the business transfer agreement.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=d2a690dd-c88b-4131-ae93-58eace85d36c.pdf)* — The only investor-initiated separation question in three years: Apoorva Bahadur (IIFL) raised press reports of listing THDC, NEEPCO and Hindustan Urvarak; DF said there are no definitive plans, that THDC is a JV with the UP government needing a senior policy mandate. “As a group, we keep exploring all these avenues as a part of our financial strategies and unlocking value.”
- *[Aug 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=e33897c7-dc88-4321-8509-24d5a43a21d1.pdf)* — DF formally characterises the step as a carve-out of the mining business — nine mines, 92 MMTPA peak capacity, FY26 production 48.66 MT — with all existing NTPC mining assets transferred. “And we have now carved it out as a separate company, as you all know, this is the NTPC Mining Limited.”
- *[Aug 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=e33897c7-dc88-4321-8509-24d5a43a21d1.pdf)* — CMD gives the clearest reason for a separate vehicle: the subsidiary was deliberately named "Mining," not "Coal Mining," so that non-coal mines can be brought into it. “And take a note that it is not Coal Mining Limited, it is a Mining Limited.”
- *[Aug 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=e33897c7-dc88-4321-8509-24d5a43a21d1.pdf)* — NML is positioned as the platform for adjacent fuel businesses — the Government's ~INR37,000 crore coal gasification programme (coal-to-SNG, a serious contender) and, under the SHANTI Act, nuclear fuel processing. “But as I was mentioning that this is the NTPC Mining Limited, so we are exploring all kind of possibilities within or outside, whatever it is.”
- *[Aug 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=e33897c7-dc88-4321-8509-24d5a43a21d1.pdf)* — The quantified payoff management attaches to the mining business: captive share of coal requirement rising from 18% to 25% by FY30 (CMD: within 3-4 years), with no coal imported at all in FY26. “Presently, 18% of our coal requirement is met through our captive coal mines, which would go up to 25% fulfilment through captive mining by FY30, thus enhancing the fuel security and supply reliability.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No stated tax, tariff or regulated-equity consequence; no NML standalone financials, funding or listing plan; no named initiator; no employee-transfer or consideration mechanics beyond the INR10,503 crore valuation.

### The business being separated — its own numbers

**Coal Mining Business of NTPC Limited (hived off to wholly owned subsidiary NTPC Mining Limited, NML)** · unit ₹ crore · No standalone revenue or profit line exists for the coal mining business anywhere in the tagged pages. Ind AS 108 segment reporting (Annual Reports 2024, 2025, 2026 — standalone and consolidated) has only two reportable segments, 'Generation of energy' and 'Others'; coal mining is bundled inside 'Others' together with consultancy, project management & supervision, energy trading and oil & gas exploration, so the 'Others' figures cannot be used as the mining business's own financials. The only mining-specific financial line on these pages is the profit after tax of the recipient subsidiary NTPC Mining Ltd in the 'Profit of Subsidiaries' tables of the quarterly presentations; this is PAT (bottom line) of NML, not segment result/EBIT/EBITDA, and no revenue or operating profit is given for it. FY2026 NML PAT is only partial-period/partial-business: five of the six coal mining businesses were transferred to NML on various dates during FY2026 and the sixth only with effect from 1 April 2026 (Annual Report 2026 — page 240); Presentation Aug 2026 — page 13 confirms 'Transfer of Coal Mining Business to NTPC Mining Ltd completed on 01st April 2026'.

## ORKLAINDIA — Orkla India Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a subsidiary's listing is in motion (DRHP / board approval)) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 4.3/10 · partial spin-off / listing · 1 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-07-25, latest 2026-07-25

> **Listing:** IPO / listing of the subsidiary in motion since 2026-07-25; date not fixed — Already listed: "Orkla India got listed on BSE and NSE on 6th of November" (Q2 FY26 call, November 13, 2025); ESOP/MSOP resolutions refer to listing "consequent to the Initial Public Offer"

**The stages, as filed:** meetings (2026-07-25)

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Nothing demerged; Orkla ASA's Indian food business (MTR, Eastern spices and convenience foods) separately listed via IPO — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* Holding company Orkla ASA; promoter stake not stated. ESOP 2025 up to 27,39,784 options (2% of capital), MSOP 2025 4,70,000 (0.34%), extended to holding/subsidiary employees; management incentive "aligned to shareholder value creation"
- *What it reveals:* A cash-generative branded food business: FY26 revenue INR 2,493 crores (+5.7%), EBITDA INR 424 crores at 16.9% margin, ROCE 27.7%, INR 600 crores cash surplus, no debt mentioned; margins below MDH/Everest peers per analyst question
- *Selling pressure:* unclear — Documents describe an IPO listing on BSE/NSE, not a share distribution; no float, shareholding pattern or index details stated
- *Parent or spin:* spin · *option pricing date:* not stated; exercise price is specified in each Award Letter and shall not be less than face value (plans approved by Board May 12, 2025 and shareholders May 16, 2025, ratification sought at AGM August 19, 2026)
- *Read next:* FY2025-26 Annual Report shareholding pattern — Orkla ASA's post-IPO promoter stake and public float
- *In their words:* “As you all know, Orkla India got listed on BSE and NSE on 6th of November.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

These texts do not describe Orkla India separating, demerging or spinning off any business — on the evidence here the company is moving the other way, having merged Eastern with MTR Foods into a single listed entity (Feb 2026: 'Post-the merger of Eastern with MTR Foods and the creation of Orkla India'), merged the two export books into one international business of ~21% of sales across 45 countries, and named M&A a 'major priority' for acquiring, not divesting. The only 'separation' management discusses is operational and internal: a re-architecting of brand Eastern's legacy direct-to-retail distribution system in Kerala, which Orkla left untouched from the 2021 acquisition until FY26. Management says Eastern runs on 'one system for all' with a 200-SKU range, and that this legacy route-to-market has 'sub-optimal market coverage, lack of customer focus in tune with the trade evolution', and 'ineffective focus on convenience food'. The fix is to split the channel into separate units — one dedicated to spices, one to convenience foods — plus a dedicated standalone modern-trade structure, further digitisation of the retailing framework and better trade-marketing effectiveness. The stated problems it solves: Eastern is 'very heavily indexed on spices and more so pure spices' and carries lower EBITDA margin than MTR, so convenience food needs its own feet-on-street; and numeric reach in Kerala is only 70% despite being 2x the nearest competitor, so coverage can still be extended. The cited cost is real: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 6.2% versus 7.8% excluding Kerala, domestic growth 6.5% versus 8.9% ex-Kerala, spices 6.1% versus 11.1% ex-Kerala (6.5% volume), and Kerala category share fell 50bps MAT March '26 (Kerala also hit by a HoReCa LPG crisis). No investor, lender or partner is said to have asked for it; the nearest external push is Ravi Purohit (May 2026) pressing on why Orkla earns ~16% EBITDA versus MDH/Everest at 20-25%, to which management tied Eastern's margin catch-up to this restructuring and the convenience-food shift.

**How it evolved:** Nov 13, 2025 (first post-listing call): disclosed as a modest efficiency project — Eastern's direct-to-retail Kerala model untouched since acquisition, now to be improved via three changes, the first being splitting the 200-SKU channel into separate spices and convenience-food units. Feb 11, 2026: the project is not mentioned at all; the call instead covers deflation, GST 2.0, MTR Prakriti and M&A ambitions. May 19, 2026: it reappears much larger and renamed an 'internal sales restructuring project'/'re-architecting' of the distribution model, kicked off early in Q4 FY26, now with three phases (one done, second by end-May, third over two more quarters), a dedicated modern-trade structure added, and quantified Kerala damage plus completion by Jan 1, 2027. The July 25, 2026 filing is only the AGM notice (ESOP/MSOP ratification) and contains no scheme of arrangement.

**What management expects from it:** No separate entities are created, so no per-entity economics are given. For the restructured Kerala/Eastern business: segmented, agile, scalable distribution; wider numeric reach beyond today's 70%; faster convenience-food, modern-trade and open-format-outlet growth; Eastern's EBITDA margin converging toward MTR's as the mix de-indexes from pure spices; positive momentum across all lines once complete by January 1, 2027; disruption for roughly two more quarters.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=51cf5b1c-5dfa-4c26-9c1d-c2b23586d5a6.pdf)* — First disclosure: Eastern's Kerala distribution is a non-standard direct-to-retail system that Orkla deliberately left unchanged since the 2021 acquisition, and is only now being made more efficient. “Post acquisition of Eastern, we have not made any changes to this distribution model.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=51cf5b1c-5dfa-4c26-9c1d-c2b23586d5a6.pdf)* — The only literal 'separation' in these texts — the Eastern sales channel is split into two dedicated units because one force cannot carry a 200-product range across both spices and convenience foods. “We have a very large range of 200 products. So, we have split the channel into two separate units. One that will focus only on spices and one that will focus on the convenience foods range.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=d26ca37b-9484-4e24-948d-b08ad840c0de.pdf)* — Direction of travel is consolidation, not separation: the two companies and two cultures have been merged into one entity, Orkla India, with a single integrated international business. “Post-the merger of Eastern with MTR Foods and the creation of Orkla India, this was the first engagement survey that we conducted.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=d26ca37b-9484-4e24-948d-b08ad840c0de.pdf)* — Asked about portfolio moves, management flags buying businesses in new states, not separating any — and the Kerala restructuring is never mentioned on this call. “Yes, so as far as M&A is concerned, I think it's an important strategy for our growth to go beyond our local agenda.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=de69651c-eea6-4489-8b7d-7383e580eafb.pdf)* — Re-framed as a structural re-architecting; the diagnosis is that a single undifferentiated distribution system caps what the company can capture by category and channel. “Today, our distributions for Eastern operates on a "one system for all" approach, which limits our ability to fully capture the potential across categories and channels.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=de69651c-eea6-4489-8b7d-7383e580eafb.pdf)* — A third dedicated structure is added for standalone modern trade, alongside deeper spices coverage and a sharper convenience-food engine. “Third, we are creating a dedicated structure for standalone modern trade, enabling us to capture growth more effectively and strengthen our market shares.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=de69651c-eea6-4489-8b7d-7383e580eafb.pdf)* — The quantified cost: Kerala dragged Q4 growth to 6.2% (7.8% ex-Kerala), spices to 6.1% (11.1% ex-Kerala, 6.5% volume), domestic to 6.5% (8.9% ex-Kerala), with Kerala share down 50bps; execution is district-by-district in three phases, complete by Jan 1, 2027, with impact for about two more quarters. “While this transition has led to some near-term disruption in Kerala market, these steps are structural in nature and are aimed at building a stronger, more scalable distribution engine.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=de69651c-eea6-4489-8b7d-7383e580eafb.pdf)* — Answering an investor comparison with MDH/Everest at 20-25% margins versus Orkla's ~16%, the CFO ties the restructuring to lifting Eastern's margin by de-indexing it from pure spices toward convenience foods. “Eastern today is very heavily indexed on spices and more so pure spices, and by shifting and accelerating the growth of convenience foods, we expect that margins in Eastern will also improve.”
- *Scheme* — No scheme of arrangement, demerger, slump sale or spin-off document exists in these texts; the single filing supplied is the 30th AGM notice (Aug 19, 2026), whose only special business is ratification of ESOP 2025 (27,39,784 options, 2% of capital) and MSOP 2025 (4,70,000 options, 0.34%) and their extension to subsidiary and holding-company employees. “To receive, consider and adopt the Audited Financial Statements (both Standalone and Consolidated Financial Statements) of the Company for the Financial Year ended March 31, 2026, together with the reports of the Board of Directors and Auditors thereon.”

*Not explained on the calls:* Everything about an actual separation: no demerger, entity, scheme, record date, capital structure, valuation, lender or partner consent, or margin/capital split is discussed anywhere in these texts.

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The premise cannot be supported from these texts: across the three transcripts supplied (Investor & Analyst Day of 25 March 2026, Q4/FY26 call of 12 May 2026, Q1 FY27 call of 21 July 2026) and the two filings supplied (the 29 May 2026 postal ballot notice and the 28 January 2026 Q3 FY26 press release), Sagility Ltd. never announces, proposes, or discusses separating, demerging, spinning off, hiving off, or divesting any business, and there is no scheme of arrangement, NCLT filing, record date, share-entitlement ratio, or appointed-date language anywhere in the material. The strategic direction management actually articulates is the opposite of separation: consolidation and bolt-on acquisition. They bought BroadPath (closed January 2025, bringing roughly 30 mostly mid-market payer clients and onshore, open-enrolment-heavy delivery) and CareSeed (closed 11 June 2026, Kansas City, founded 2012, CY2025 revenue 5.1 million dollars, 95 percent recurring, 31.4 percent EBITDA margin, 30 clients of which 26 new, 14 staff, platforms Forecast and Harvest), and Ramesh Gopalan says BroadPath is now fully integrated to the point that revenue cannot be split out, with Srinivas Mattapalli giving only an approximate 13.5 to 13.6 million dollars for BroadPath clients in Q1 FY27. The two reporting segments an investor might expect to be split, Payer (89.6 percent of Q1 FY27 revenue) and Provider (10.4 percent), are both explicitly described as businesses the company intends to keep and grow, including doubling down on provider-side RCM with an agentic AI layer. Capital allocation is framed as full debt repayment during FY27 (net debt 1,110 million rupees, 0.06x adjusted EBITDA), cash of 9,674 million rupees retained for M&A and AI investment, and a small final dividend of 0.10 rupees per share, with no mention of unlocking value through a separation. The only separation-like event referenced anywhere is historical and appears solely in a press-release footnote: the earlier carve-out of the healthcare business from HGS, cited as the origin of intangible amortisation now adjusted out of Adjusted PAT. The only corporate action actually put to shareholders in the filings is the Sagility Limited Employee Stock Options and Performance Stock Units Scheme 2026 (up to 3,09,10,845 options and 12,36,43,222 PSUs, exercisable into up to 15,45,54,067 shares, run through the Sagility ESOP Trust with an interest-free loan capped at 5 percent of paid-up capital and free reserves).

**How it evolved:** The idea does not surface at all. At the Investor & Analyst Day on 25 March 2026 the plan presented is capability expansion (managed services, Synchrony, MLR-reduction, clinical) plus capability-led M&A, and Ramesh Gopalan rules out even moving outside healthcare. On the 12 May 2026 Q4/FY26 call the forward agenda is FY27 debt extinguishment, retained cash for acquisitions in both payer and provider, and a possible dividend review. By the 21 July 2026 Q1 FY27 call the company has added CareSeed and is scouting further clinical, provider and healthcare-technology targets, so the trajectory over the three calls is consolidation, not separation.

**What management expects from it:** Not stated, because no separation is proposed. What they do quantify is the opposite path: FY27 organic growth in low double digits in constant currency, adjusted EBITDA margin of 24 to 25 percent absorbing 120 basis points of Karnataka and Telangana minimum-wage impact, full debt repayment in FY27, adjusted ROCE above 50 percent, and cash retained for further acquisitions and AI investment.

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

These texts do not describe Indus Towers separating, demerging, spinning off or hiving down any business, so no separation rationale can be reconstructed from them — the premise is not supported by the supplied material. Across all seven transcripts (Nov 2023 through May 2026) and the one filing (Q1 FY27 results, July 27, 2026), management discusses the opposite direction: consolidation and bolt-on expansion of a single tower business. The only structural actions named are (a) the acquisition of about 12,600 towers (including lean) from Bharti Airtel, completed in the last week of March 2025 for roughly INR 18-20 billion of consideration (Rs. 1,800 crore line item in cash flow; Rs. 18 billion booked to common control reserves; Rs. 1.7 billion of restated opex/depreciation from 19 Nov 2024), and (b) the creation of a new Africa holding structure — wholly owned subsidiaries in UAE plus Zambia, Uganda and Nigeria entities, and Indus Towers Global Ventures IFSC Limited (incorporated 28 April 2026) — which management repeatedly frames as greenfield organic growth of the same core tower business, not a carve-out of an existing one. The only 'separation' language anywhere is operational, not corporate: the EV-charging pilot was to be run by a 'separate business unit, separate team' (Jan 2025), and by May 2025 that pilot was still being evaluated and might be held back so 'focus will remain on the towers.' The filing's single reference to a 'scheme of arrangement' is a legacy depreciation-to-general-reserve adjustment (Rs. 185 million in Q1 FY27, Rs. 795 million in FY26), not a new separation, and both standalone and consolidated results state the company 'has a single reportable segment.' Capital-structure debate in these calls is about dividends versus leverage (INR 14 per share final dividend for FY26, about INR 37-38 billion, roughly 100% of FY26 free cash flow of INR 37.6 billion) — not about separating anything. No investor, lender or partner on any of these calls asks for a separation.

**How it evolved:** The idea never surfaces. Nov 2023 through May 2025 the structural theme is consolidation (Airtel's 12,600 towers, 'aggressively pursuing market share through both organic and inorganic routes'); Jan 2025 adds an EV-charging pilot as a 'separate business unit,' which by May 2025 is merely 'evaluating that pilot' and may be dropped in favour of towers. Oct 2025 announces Africa (Nigeria, Uganda, Zambia) explicitly as the same tower business, not diversification; Feb 2026 adds the UAE/local-country holding structure and possible GIFT City debt funding, and the July 2026 filing lists ten subsidiaries plus Indus Towers Global Ventures IFSC Limited (28 April 2026). May 2026 closes on Zambia licence in hand, Uganda/Nigeria approvals pending, and a resumed dividend — with no separation mentioned on any call.

**What management expects from it:** No separation is announced, so no per-entity expectation is stated. For the Africa subsidiaries management expects differentiation on cost per tower, SLA, uptime and energy efficiency, debt-funded, 'value accretive over the long term,' with return profile, MSA structure and hurdle rate explicitly still undecided. India expectations stay 55%-plus EBITDA margin, growth capex and progressive FCF distribution.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Oct 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=bf1b0d5a-4a8e-4de6-ba37-09ab3d822d8f.pdf)* — Africa is framed as an extension of the existing tower business rather than a separate or separable venture — management explicitly rejects the diversification framing. “So I think the overall Africa strategy is not diversification business. It's our tower business. That's our core strength.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ba2c5d56-b570-4102-a410-170606a93a06.pdf)* — The only new corporate structure described is an Africa holding chain of wholly owned subsidiaries (UAE plus each local market) created for execution and funding, not to separate an existing business out of Indus. “We have set up a holding structure through the incorporation of wholly owned subsidiaries in UAE and at the local country level in each of our markets, establishing a clear country-level execution framework.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ba2c5d56-b570-4102-a410-170606a93a06.pdf)* — Funding for the Africa entities was still undecided between UAE-level and GIFT City-level debt, with 'nothing major' required — the scale discussed is a start-up, not a carve-out. “It could be -- one of the possibilities, it could be at the UAE level. It could also be at the GIFT City level and so on. So we are yet to work on those details.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.industowers.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/Earnings-Call-Transcript_Q4-FY25.pdf)* — Strategy articulated to the Board was consolidation and market-share capture — the opposite of separating a business — evidenced by acquiring about 12,600 Airtel towers. “The strategy includes aggressively pursuing market share through both organic and inorganic routes as demonstrated by our acquisition of Bharti Airtel's towers.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.industowers.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/Earnings-Call-Transcript_Q4-FY25.pdf)* — The acquired Airtel portfolio was booked as a common control transaction with Rs. 18 billion to common control reserves and Rs. 1.7 billion of restated opex/depreciation — an in-bound consolidation, with no counterpart separation. “Accordingly, the difference of Rs. 18 billion between purchase consideration and carrying value is recognized as common control reserves.”
- *[Jan 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=3252c003-d947-487f-bc82-8004f0bd0606.pdf)* — The only 'separate' entity language in three years is operational ring-fencing of an EV-charging pilot inside the company, deliberately kept apart so the tower business does not suffer. “I think it is something that will be new to the industry as well so we will be very cautious on that one but it is a separate business, yes.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.industowers.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/Earnings-Call-Transcript_Q4-FY25.pdf)* — By the next call that EV pilot was still unproven and might be abandoned rather than scaled or separated, with focus returning to towers. “And if not, I think our focus will remain on the towers.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.industowers.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/Earnings-Call-Transcript_Q4-FY25.pdf)* — Management explicitly denied even considering a data-centre business, attributing the idea to media speculation — no adjacent business exists that could be separated. “So I don't think we have discussed that as an option currently because our focus remains on the tower growth primarily.”
- *Scheme* — The Q1 FY27 filing (July 27, 2026) uses 'scheme of arrangement' only for a legacy depreciation-to-general-reserve adjustment (Rs. 185 million in the quarter, Rs. 795 million in FY26) and reports Indus as one business with one segment — no demerger, hive-off or separation is disclosed. “Accordingly, the Company has a single reportable segment.”

- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=55d79cdd-7dbd-4f98-83b5-13500c817fe9.pdf)* — The latest call's capital-allocation discussion is about distributing FY26 free cash flow (INR 37.6 billion; INR 14 per share final dividend) and preserving leverage headroom for growth — not about separating or releasing a business. “See, the Board evaluated the FCF situation and the debt levels that we want to maintain and decided accordingly to distribute the FCF of FY26.”
- *[Nov 2023](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=8b6c9809-e795-4c47-af11-adced84bd53a.pdf)* — The earliest call in the set also describes only organic expansion of one passive-infrastructure business (record 5,928 macro towers, 5,583 co-locations in Q2 FY24), with no structural review of any kind. “Driven by continued strong demand from one of our customers, we added 5,928 macro towers and 5,583 corresponding co-locations.”

- *In their words:* “RESOLVED FURTHER THAT in case the equity shares of the Company are either sub-divided or consolidated, then the number of equity shares to be issued and allotted on exercise of Options granted under the ESOP Plan and the exercise price of Options granted under the ESOP Plan shall automatically stand increased or reduced, as the case may be, in the same proportion as the present face value of Rs.10 (Rupee Ten Only) per equity share bears to their revised face value of the equity shares of the Company after such sub-division or consolidation, without affecting any other rights or obligations of the Employees who have been granted Options under the ESOP Plan.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

These texts contain no separation, demerger, spin-off, slump sale out, hive-off or scheme of arrangement by KRN — there is no Scheme document among the ten filings, no shareholder resolution for one (the 15 April 2026 EGM covers only promoter re-appointments, an ESOP plan of 6,00,000 options and a ₹500 crore QIP), and no call question or management answer about separating any business. The only going-concern business transfer in the record runs inward, not outward: on 6 October 2025 wholly-owned subsidiary KRN HVAC Products Pvt Ltd signed a Business Transfer Agreement with Sphere Refrigeration Systems Pvt Ltd to acquire its bus air-conditioning division, which management framed as buying technology, know-how, the three ex-Subros/'Sparrows Motherson' professionals, their 12–13 years of experience, employees, assets and store, with the price 'not much' and never disclosed — Sphere Refrigeration's own top line was only ₹2–3 crore, while the related Sphere Thermal did ₹40–50 crore and had been sold six months earlier to a third party wanting railway HVAC entry. The separation visible in that deal is the counterparty's: Sphere's founders sold Sphere Thermal and 'bought back' the bus AC business into Sphere Refrigeration, which KRN then acquired. KRN's own structure is deliberately multi-entity rather than separating: the new 600,000 sq ft Neemrana plant sits in KRN HVAC because it carries the 15% concessional tax rate, the ₹141.72 crore white-goods PLI sanctioned by IFCI (5%, then 4%, over three years) and Rajasthan RIPS at ~1.56% of top line for 10 years, while the listed parent runs at the old tax rate and full capacity; Thermotech Research Laboratory Pvt Ltd was incorporated as a 100% subsidiary with a separate plot, separate building, separate investment and a name 'not linked to KRN' precisely so it can act as an independent AHRI-accredited third-party lab. Two filings point the other way from separation: on 12 January 2026 the parent amended its 15 April 2023 loan agreement (₹100 crore limit, ₹99.94 crore outstanding) to make the loan convertible into KRN HVAC equity at the lender's discretion, and granted Thermotech a ₹10 crore unsecured loan at 12% — deeper consolidation of ownership, not a split. Nobody asked for a separation: no investor on any of the seven calls raised it, lenders appear only via the CRISIL A-/Stable rating and the ₹350 crore QIP allotted 1 June 2026 at ₹1,060 (to ValueQuest, Ashoka WhiteOak, ADIA, Bank of India funds, Subhkam and others), and partners/customers appear only as OEM approvals. The 9 June 2026 promoter sale of 10,00,000 shares (1.52%, Santosh Kumar Yadav and Anju Devi 5,00,000 each, taking the group from 67.22% to 65.69%) is an open-market OFS of shares, not a separation of any business.

**How it evolved:** No separation idea surfaces in any call. The nearest structural events are: 15 May 2025 and 1 August 2025, when Thermotech Research Laboratory is described as deliberately kept 'separate' in identity, plot, building and name so it can serve as an AHRI third-party lab; 6 November 2025, when the inbound Sphere bus-AC Business Transfer Agreement is announced alongside the CRISIL A-/Stable rating and management says both 'have not contributed to the H1 FY26 performance' but 'set the stage for the next leg of growth'; 9 February 2026, when the acquisition cost is refused ('cost of course we cannot disclose… it's not much'), gross margin is said to beat existing products and the ₹1,000 crore-plus Indian bus AC market growing 20–25% is targeted at 15% share; and 15 May 2026, when bus AC has delivered ~₹10 crore in FY26 against a ₹150 crore presentation figure, with 12 January 2026 and 1 June 2026 filings adding loan-to-equity convertibility in KRN HVAC and the ₹350 crore QIP.

**What management expects from it:** No separation is discussed, so no expectations are stated for one. For the acquired bus AC business they expect gross margin above 20% and better than existing products, 15% of a ₹1,000 crore-plus market, and ₹150–160 crore revenue. For KRN HVAC they expect 15% tax, ₹141.72 crore PLI, RIPS 1.56% for 10 years, solar savings and 1–2% PAT improvement. Thermotech's separateness is expected to deliver credible AHRI third-party certification.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *CALL Nov 2025* — The only going-concern business transfer disclosed is an acquisition into the subsidiary, not a separation out of KRN: KRN HVAC signing a BTA for Sphere Refrigeration's bus AC division, presented as expanding into automotive HVAC. “Our subsidiary, KRN HVAC Products Private Limited has signed a business transfer agreement to acquire the best air-conditioning division of spare refrigeration systems Private Limited.”
- *Scheme* — There is no scheme of arrangement in the filings; the 6 February 2026 results note records the same transaction as an inbound going-concern transfer dated 6 October 2025. “During the quarter, the Company's wholly owned subsidiary (KRN HVAC) entered Into a Business Transfer Agreement on 6th October, 2025 with a private company (Sphere Refrigeration Systems Private Limited) for transfer of certain identified business/assets on a going-concern basis.”
- *CALL Nov 2025* — The separation described is the seller's, not KRN's: Sphere's three founders sold Sphere Thermal to a buyer seeking railway HVAC credentials, then moved the bus AC business back into Sphere Refrigeration, which KRN bought. “And then they promoted three, they buy back bus air conditioning from their old company to this spare refrigeration.”
- *CALL Feb 2026* — Management sized the two Sphere entities — the bigger one (₹40–50 crore) already sold away six months earlier, the acquired one only ₹2–3 crore of top line — in a ₹1,000 crore-plus market growing 20–25%. “So main business they do in Sphere Thermal but they already like had some agreement with some other guy and they already sold that company before six months with like aligned with us.”
- *CALL Nov 2025* — The acquisition rationale was technology, know-how, people and Pan-India service capability without large investment — backward integration already in-house — not divestment or focus-sharpening. “So, we have new facility, but we don't have technology that time and know-how. So, that's why we acquired this company.”
- *CALL May 2025* — The one business KRN deliberately held apart is the testing lab, kept as a separate entity, plot, building and brand so its certificates carry third-party (AHRI) credibility with OEM customers. “So, there is a separate plot number, separate building and we invest in separately and even name is also not linked to KRN.”
- *CALL Aug 2025* — The parent/subsidiary split exists to park new capacity where the fiscal benefits sit — 15% tax in KRN HVAC, the ₹141.72 crore PLI and RIPS — while the listed entity stays at the old rate and full utilisation. “So, HVAC have new tax rate and Heat has old tax rate. So, now whatever growth will come is from new facility only.”
- *Scheme* — The 12 January 2026 filing moves toward tighter consolidation, not separation: the ₹100 crore parent loan to KRN HVAC (₹99.94 crore outstanding) became convertible into the subsidiary's equity at the parent's discretion. “The Lender shall have the right, but not the obligation, at its sole discretion, to convert the whole or any part of the outstanding unsecured loan(s), together with accrued interest thereon, into fully paid- up equity shares of the Borrower.”
- *Scheme* — The only ownership 'separation' in the record is a promoter share sale on 9 June 2026, cutting the promoter group from 67.22% to 65.69% — shares, not a business. “in respect of transfer of 10,00,000 equity shares, representing 1.52% of the paid-up equity share capital of the Company, pursuant to an sale transaction undertaken on June 9, 2026.”
- *CALL May 2026* — By FY26 close the acquired bus AC business was being scaled inside the group — ~₹10 crore achieved, 15% market share targeted, full in-house backward integration — with no mention of separating it or anything else. “Last year, we achieved around Rs.10 crores from bus AC only. And this year, whatever is the market size, so we are expecting at least 15% market share.”

*Not explained on the calls:* Everything: no separation, demerger or scheme is mentioned, so no rationale, structure, record date, entity split, valuation or requester exists in these texts. Sphere acquisition price also undisclosed.

## M&M — Mahindra & Mahindra Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a scheme of arrangement whose nature the documents on file do not settle) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 4.2/10 · scheme (nature unclear) · 4 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-02-10, latest 2026-07-29

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** 'Alembic Undertaking', a Bengaluru residential real estate project of Mahindra Lifespace, slump-sold into subsidiary MBLDL for a Mitsui joint venture — class `regulatory_strategic`.

- *Insiders:* MBLDL is a subsidiary of MLDL and an indirect subsidiary of Mahindra & Mahindra, holding and promoter company; promoter group has no interest except that indirect shareholding. MLDL keeps 51% and up to three directors.
- *What it reveals:* Project contributed no turnover, revenue, income or net worth last year, yet transfers at net consideration up to Rs. 100 crores and MBLDL raises a Rs. 230.30 crore rights issue — Mitsui Fudosan funds 49% at par.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — No shares distributed to shareholders; MBLDL is unlisted, 49% sold to Mitsui Fudosan; MLDL's shareholding pattern unchanged.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* MLDL shareholders' approval under Section 180(1)(a)/Regulation 37A and the independent valuation report for the Alembic Undertaking
- *In their words:* “The transfer of Alembic Undertaking (including all the relevant assets and liabilities), a residential real estate development project in Bengaluru will provide operational flexibility, efficient management, sharp execution focus and better monitoring of the project.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The business being separated is M&M's Mahindra Truck & Bus Division (MTBD), which the board on 29 July 2026 approved selling as a going concern on a slump-sale basis to SML Mahindra Limited (formerly SML Isuzu), M&M's own listed subsidiary, for Rs 525 crore subject to working-capital adjustment, priced off a valuation report from GT Valuation Advisors Private Limited. Management's stated reason is structural, not financial distress: M&M had two separate truck-and-bus businesses after buying 58.97% of SML from Sumitomo Corporation and Isuzu Motors on 1 August 2025 plus the mandatory open offer, and the filings call the MTBD transfer 'a natural next step in creating a simplified operating model with sharper market focus, enhanced scale and improved competitiveness.' The problem it solves is fragmentation and subscale presence — MTBD covers light, intermediate and heavy trucks and buses, SML is a market leader in ILCV buses, and combining them is meant to produce one entity across the whole >3.5T CV segment with 'enhanced scale, broader market coverage, a strengthened product portfolio and improved operational efficiencies.' The sizing shows how small the business is inside M&M: MTBD generated total income of Rs 2,989 crore in FY2025-26, about 2.02% of M&M's total income from operations, and M&M's investment in it was ~Rs 481 crore, about 0.65% of net worth — small enough that M&M states it does not even qualify as an 'undertaking' under Section 180(1)(a), so no shareholder vote and no Regulation 37A process. SML's own scale was Rs 2,837.92 crore revenue in FY2025-26 (Rs 2,398.99 crore FY2024-25, Rs 2,195.93 crore FY2023-24) on a net worth of only Rs 519.34 crore, which is why the combined entity needs funding: SML's board approved a rights issue of up to Rs 1,450 crore on 6 November 2026, with M&M committing ~Rs 855 crore for its entitlement plus up to ~Rs 595 crore for any unsubscribed portion — i.e. M&M is prepared to fund the entire raise. Operational continuity is preserved because M&M will keep making Mahindra-branded trucks and buses for SML under a contract manufacturing arrangement, and both brands' heritage and positioning are to be retained. No investor, lender or partner is named as having asked for the separation; it is presented as a group-level capital-allocation and structure decision, consistent with the parallel exits (Erkunt Foundry, Blue Planet) and the Mauritius holding-company merger aimed at a streamlined group structure.

**How it evolved:** There are no earnings-call transcripts on file, so the idea can only be traced through filings: the enabling step was M&M's purchase of 58.97% of SML Isuzu from Sumitomo and Isuzu on 1 August 2025 followed by the open offer, which left the group with two overlapping truck-and-bus businesses. On 29 July 2026 the M&M board approved the MTBD slump sale to SML for Rs 525 crore, with the BTA to be executed by 7 August 2026 and closing on or before 31 January 2027 (FY2027), plus a contract-manufacturing arrangement so M&M keeps building Mahindra-branded trucks and buses. One day later, on 30 July 2026, the board approved absorbing Mahindra Investment Company (Mauritius) Limited to rationalise overseas entities, part of the same simplification push that also included the 10 April 2026 exit from Erkunt Foundry 'in line with capital allocation framework' and the 2 March 2026 exit from Blue Planet. The plan's funding leg appeared last: on 6 November 2026 SML approved a rights issue of up to Rs 1,450 crore and M&M committed ~Rs 855 crore of entitlement plus up to ~Rs 595 crore of any unsubscribed shares, with no change of control envisaged.

**What management expects from it:** For SML: enhanced scale, broader market coverage, a strengthened product portfolio, improved operational efficiencies and competitiveness in a consolidating CV market, funded by up to Rs 1,450 crore of rights equity M&M will largely supply. For M&M: a simplified CV structure, sharper market focus, retained factory utilisation via contract manufacturing, Rs 525 crore of proceeds, and capital freed per its allocation framework. No margin, synergy or valuation targets were quantified.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — Board approval of the slump sale of the Truck & Bus Division — employees, assets, IP, licences, contracts and liabilities — to listed subsidiary SML Mahindra for Rs 525 crore under a Business Transfer Agreement. “We hereby inform you that the Board of Directors of the Company, at its meeting held today, i.e. 29th July 2026, accorded its approval for the sale, transfer, and disposal of the Company's Truck & Bus Division together with its employees, assets, intellectual property, licenses, permits, insurance policies, contracts, interests, rights, and liabilities ("MTBD Business Undertaking"), as a going concern on a slump sale basis, as per Section 2(103) and other applicable provisions of the Income-tax Act, 2025, to SML Mahindra Limited, a listed subsidiary of the Company, under a Business Transfer Agreement ("BTA"), for a consideration of Rs. 525 crore, subject to working capital adjustments as set out in BTA.”
- *Scheme* — The stated rationale: one unified Mahindra Group truck-and-bus business spanning light, intermediate and heavy CVs plus buses. “The combination of MTBD Business Undertaking and SML is a strategic step towards creating a unified Truck & Bus business in Mahindra Group with a comprehensive presence across light, intermediate and heavy commercial vehicles, as well as buses.”
- *Scheme* — Expected benefits are scale, coverage, portfolio and efficiency, producing a 'future-ready' organisation. “The combined business is expected to benefit from enhanced scale, broader market coverage, a strengthened product portfolio and improved operational efficiencies.”
- *Scheme* — The move is framed as the sequel to M&M's August 2025 acquisition of control of SML Isuzu from Sumitomo and Isuzu. “Following M&M's acquisition of a 58.97% stake in SML Mahindra Limited (formerly SML Isuzu Limited) from Sumitomo Corporation and Isuzu Motors Limited on August 1, 2025, and the subsequent mandatory open offer, the proposed transfer of MTBD to SML is a natural next step in creating a simplified operating model with sharper market focus, enhanced scale and improved competitiveness.”
- *Scheme* — Group CEO Anish Shah frames it as simplifying the group's CV structure into a single focused entity aimed at CV leadership. “The transaction simplifies Mahindra Group's commercial vehicle business structure by consolidating truck and bus operations under SML Mahindra, creating a single focused entity dedicated to growth and leadership in the commercial vehicle sector.”
- *Scheme* — Auto & Farm CEO Rajesh Jejurikar points to synergies across operations, technology and customer-facing domains while keeping both brands distinct. “By combining strengths of SML and Mahindra Truck & Bus, we can drive meaningful synergies across operations, technology and customer-facing domains while preserving the unique heritage and market positioning of both brands.”
- *Scheme* — SML Executive Chairman Vinod Sahay positions it as a single unified CV platform with greater scale and 'significant commercial and operational synergies'. “By bringing together SML and Mahindra Truck & Business under one unified commercial vehicle platform, we are creating a stronger business with greater scale, broader market coverage and a more comprehensive product portfolio.”
- *Scheme* — MTBD's smallness inside M&M is quantified — Rs 2,989 crore total income, ~2.02% of income; investment of ~Rs 481 crore, ~0.65% of net worth. “The MTBD Business Undertaking generated a total income of Rs. 2,989 crore during the financial year ended 31st March 2026, representing approximately 2.02% of the Company's total income from operations for the said year.”
- *Scheme* — Because MTBD is not an 'undertaking' under Section 180(1)(a), the sale avoids Regulation 37A and the shareholder-approval route, though it is a related-party transaction done at arm's length and priced on an external valuation. “The provisions of Regulation 37A of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 are not applicable to this transaction, as MTBD Business Undertaking which is being transferred by the Company through a slump sale does not qualify as an "undertaking" within the meaning of Section 180(1)(a) of the Companies Act, 2013.”
- *Scheme* — M&M retains the factories: it will keep manufacturing Mahindra-branded trucks and buses for SML under contract. “Manufacturing of Mahindra branded trucks and buses will continue to be undertaken by M&M under a contract manufacturing arrangement, ensuring continuity of supply and operational stability.”
- *Scheme* — Timing and shareholding: closing on or before 31 January 2027 (during FY2027), with no change to M&M's shareholding pattern. “Slump Sale of MTBD Business Undertaking is proposed to be consummated on or before 31st January 2027, or such later date as may be mutually agreed upon by the parties, subject to satisfactory fulfilment of the conditions precedent, including obtaining all requisite approvals and completion of such procedures as may be required, in accordance with the terms of the BTA.”
- *Scheme* — Funding leg (6 November 2026): M&M backstops SML's Rs 1,450 crore rights issue in full — ~Rs 855 crore entitlement plus up to ~Rs 595 crore of any unsubscribed shares — with no change of control. “Subscription to additional equity shares and/or any portion of the rights issue that remains unsubscribed, if any, beyond the Company's entitlement, aggregating ~Rs. 595 crore.”
