## NAM-INDIA — Nippon Life India Asset Management Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a scheme of arrangement whose nature the documents on file do not settle) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 4.2/10 · scheme (nature unclear) · 3 filing(s) from NSE, NSE-deep · first 2026-03-14, latest 2026-03-14

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Nippon Life India AIF Management Limited — the AIF/alternatives arm; 40% minority stake issued to DWS, not a demerger — class `regulatory_strategic`.

- *Insiders:* Company retains 60% of NAIF; NAIF remains a subsidiary. Promoter Nippon Life Insurance holds 5.00% stake in DWS. Company accepts transfer, lock-in and non-compete restrictions; DWS gets put-option and exit rights.
- *What it reveals:* Issue price Rs 21,569/share values NAIF at ~Rs 1,833 crore post-money, for a unit contributing only INR 101.96 crore turnover (4.6%) and INR 102.18 crore net worth (3.1%) — alternatives arm priced far above book.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — No shares distributed to shareholders; NAIF stays an unlisted subsidiary contributing 4.6% of turnover, 3.1% of net worth.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated (SHA contains a "put-option, exit rights granted to DWS" but no pricing date is disclosed)
- *Read next:* NAIF standalone financials on the company website (Parag: "our financial are put on the website"); next call for DWS unit economics
- *In their words:* “After the said issuance of equity shares , NAIF will cease to be a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company and it would continue to remain as a subsidiary.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

What is being 'separated' is not a demerger or spin-off: it is a 40% minority dilution of Nippon Life India AIF Management Limited (NAIF), NAM India's wholly owned alternatives (AIF) subsidiary, to DWS Group GmbH & Co. KGaA via a fresh issue of 3,40,000 equity shares (face value INR 10) at INR 21,569 per share for INR 733,34,60,000 (~INR 733.35 crore), after which NAIF 'will cease to be a wholly owned subsidiary' but 'continue to remain as a subsidiary' — so NAM India keeps control and consolidation, and the filing states 'No impact' on management or control of the listed entity. The stated purpose in the Scheme documents is 'to jointly develop and build a leading alternative investment funds franchise in India along with DWS'; management's own explanation on the calls is purely about distribution reach, not about fixing a problem inside the business. Sikka's logic, repeated across three calls, is that NAM India is strong domestically and has 'very strong Japanese access' through parent Nippon Life Insurance, but 'Europe access was lower', and DWS — described by him as 'the largest asset manager of Europe' (EUR 1,085 bn AUM at Dec 31, 2025, ~5,000 employees per the filing) — is the channel to bring European money into India, 'especially the alternate and the infrastructure side.' The collaboration is explicitly wider than the JV: the Nov 13, 2025 board authorisation says NAM India and DWS 'will also work closely in other areas including passive investment products and global distribution,' and Sikka added it will help the mutual fund business on 'capability of international funds, ETFs, and also offshore money.' Scale context given: NAIF's cumulative AIF commitments were INR 95.8 bn (Q1 FY27, +18% YoY), up from INR 74.1 bn at Q4 FY25; NAIF contributed INR 101.96 crore of turnover (4.6%) and INR 102.18 crore of net worth (3.1%) in the last financial year; non-MF products are ~8% of gross revenue and MF was 91% of FY26 revenue; and Parag confirmed the AIF entity is already 'a profitable company. It's a profitable franchise.' The background pressure visible in the calls is the persistent failure of the offshore/international engine to scale — offshore AUM went from INR 172 bn (Sep-2024) to INR 161 bn (Sep-2025) to INR 139 bn (Mar-2026), and Sikka conceded 'we would have expected offshore contribution to be higher… it is a little binary' — so the DWS tie-up reads as the fix for foreign-inflow access rather than for anything in the domestic MF franchise. Nobody — no investor, lender or regulator — is said to have asked for it; the counterparty link is related-party-adjacent only in that promoter Nippon Life Insurance 'presently holds 5.00% stake in DWS,' and DWS had already been listed in Apr 2025 as one of the Nippon Life network entities through which offshore business was being sourced. The deal is conditional on SEBI and CCI approvals plus consent of NAIF's AIF investors, with a 12-month long-stop date, and the SHA gives DWS board and senior-management appointment rights, reserved matters requiring its consent, a put option, exit rights, non-compete, transfer restrictions and lock-in.

**How it evolved:** Through Jul 2024 and Oct 2024 AIF is only flagged as 'an important focus area' with senior hiring and seed capital, and in Apr 2025 DWS appears merely as one of several Nippon Life network entities (with GENKAI, BBLAM, Cathay) through which offshore money already trickles in, while Nov 2025 shows management conceding offshore is 'a small part of our overall business, but the ambition is to grow bigger.' The idea surfaces formally at the Feb 2026 call (Q3 FY26, held Jan 29, 2026), which discloses the Nov 13, 2025 board authorisation of a strategic collaboration with DWS taking 'up to 40%' of NAIF plus cooperation in passives and global distribution — still only a non-binding agreement, with Sikka declining detail beyond 'the idea will be to get more global flow into India.' By the Apr 2026 call it is called a JV and justified as access to overseas money 'especially the alternate and the infrastructure side' plus spillover to the MF business; the Mar 14, 2026 filings then harden it into signed SHA/SSA with a fixed 40%, INR 733.35 crore price and SEBI/CCI conditions. At the Jul 2026 call the stake is confirmed as 40%, approvals are still awaited, the Japan-plus-Europe positioning is sharpened ('one side it will be Europe and one side it will be Japan'), and unit economics are declined as 'too early.'

**What management expects from it:** For NAIF: European capital into Indian alternates and infrastructure, INR 733.35 crore of fresh primary capital inside the subsidiary, DWS board/veto/put rights, and a jointly built 'leading' India AIF franchise that stays a consolidated, already-profitable subsidiary. For NAM India: Europe access added to its Japan access, spillover capability in international funds, ETFs, passives and global distribution. No margin, capital-release or valuation benefit was ever quantified.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Apr 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=151b44bf-70e7-4dd1-b5f0-be68ddc419fc.pdf)* — Pre-history: DWS is already named as one of the Nippon Life group entities through which NAM India's offshore business is sourced, alongside Japan, Thailand and Taiwan affiliates. “Till now, if you see where most of our business that is coming, international business is coming – you can look at slide in the presentation, whether it is coming through DWS, whether it is from the GENKAI which is Japan, BBLAM which is Bangkok Life Asset Management and Cathay, which is Taiwan.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=72929088-2f2c-46b0-91ef-37d89b0a0fbe.pdf)* — Context for the deal: the non-MF businesses (AIF subsidiary, offshore subsidiary) are tiny in the mix but are the stated growth ambition; yields on these products range 60–120 bps versus ~36 bps blended MF yield. “Currently, it's a small part of our overall business, but the ambition is to grow bigger.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=7328832d-1c78-414e-9c71-12f3e0b72b87.pdf)* — First disclosure of the separation: the Nov 13, 2025 board authorisation of DWS acquiring up to 40% of the AIF subsidiary via fresh equity, plus a wider collaboration on passives and global distribution. “Our Board of Directors at their meeting on November 13, 2025, authorised the Company to enter into a strategic collaboration with DWS Group (a leading European Asset Manager), wherein DWS intends to acquire a minority stake of up to 40% in Nippon Life India AIF Management Limited by subscribing to fresh issuance of equity shares.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=7328832d-1c78-414e-9c71-12f3e0b72b87.pdf)* — Management's one-line rationale at first disclosure, delivered in the same breath as the admission that offshore inflows have disappointed and are 'binary'. “As I mentioned in my speech earlier, our AIF is getting into a JV with DWS. Again, the idea will be to get more global flow into India.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=7328832d-1c78-414e-9c71-12f3e0b72b87.pdf)* — The problem the tie-up is meant to address: offshore contribution has undershot management's own expectations for years, partly on USD-INR, and is lumpy institutional-mandate driven rather than predictable like SIPs. “I have mentioned in past also - clearly we would have expected offshore contribution to be higher. It has taken a little more time; it is a little binary.”
- *[Apr 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=0af7699a-8896-47d2-a07c-0ee76a962512.pdf)* — Purpose restated as sourcing overseas capital specifically for alternates and infrastructure, still under a non-binding agreement at that date. “The idea is we clearly see an opportunity to get a lot of overseas money and especially the alternate and the infrastructure side.”
- *[Apr 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=0af7699a-8896-47d2-a07c-0ee76a962512.pdf)* — The JV is explicitly not ring-fenced to AIF — management expects collateral capability transfer into the mutual fund business (international funds, ETFs, offshore money). “Also, as far as the JV is concerned, it will also help in collaboration not only in the AIF where it will be a JV, but also with the mutual fund business, you know, to as in whether from a capability of international funds, ETFs, and also offshore money.”
- *[Apr 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=0af7699a-8896-47d2-a07c-0ee76a962512.pdf)* — The strategic gap being closed is geographic: Japan access was already strong via the parent; Europe was the missing leg. “The idea is to keep getting ready as India keeps, you know, getting stronger. More foreign money will come into India and I think building capabilities access, we were always very strong in Japan. So now this JV gives us an access to Europe.”
- *[Apr 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=0af7699a-8896-47d2-a07c-0ee76a962512.pdf)* — Management also flags DWS's passive/ETF strength as a reason the partnership could extend to product launches in India if investor demand appears. “And to your earlier question, having DWS with us, you know, and DWS is one of the largest international players both in not also in ETF space, but also passives, you know.”
- *Scheme* — The signed deal (Mar 14, 2026): SHA with the Company, NAIF and DWS plus an SSA, with the stated object of jointly building an India alternatives franchise and DWS taking 40%. “To jointly develop and build a leading alternative investment funds franchise in India along with DWS and in pursuance thereof DWS has agreed to acquire a minority stake of 40 percent in NAIF.”
- *Scheme* — Price and mechanics: INR 733.35 crore of primary capital into NAIF for 3,40,000 fresh shares at INR 21,569 each — money goes into the subsidiary, not to the listed parent as sale proceeds. “DWS has agreed to pay a sum of INR 733,34,60,000/- (Indian Rupees Seven Hundred Thirty-Three Crores Thirty-Four Lakhs Sixty Thousand only) as consideration for acquiring 40% equity stake in NAIF by subscribing to 3,40,000 equity shares [having a face value of INR 10/- (Indian Rupees Ten) per share], to be issued by NAIF by way of preferential allotment.”
- *Scheme* — Scale of what is being diluted: NAIF is ~4.6% of turnover and ~3.1% of net worth — i.e. the separation touches a small slice of the group. “During the last financial year, NAIF contributed INR 101.96 crore to the Turnover (4.6%) and INR 102.18 crore to the Net Worth (3.1%) of the Company.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No margin, valuation, capital-use or AUM targets; why 40%; how the INR 733 cr is deployed; NAIF standalone P&L; put/exit pricing; dilution impact on consolidated EPS; no investor or lender demand cited.

## POWERMECH — Power Mech Projects Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a filing's text names a demerger; no scheme filing names it yet) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 4.2/10 · spin-off · 2 filing(s) from NSE · first 2025-11-20, latest 2026-08-26

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'meetings' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**The stages, as filed:** meetings (2025-11-20)

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** not stated — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* No new entity disclosed. PMPL ESOP-2026: up to 10,00,000 options (3.16% of capital, fully diluted); KMP and Senior Management capped at 25% of pool; max 10,000 options per employee per year.
- *What it reveals:* not stated — no separation disclosed. Filings cover only ESOP-2026 (exercise price 10%–25% of market price on grant date) and raising borrowing limits from ₹5,000 crore to ₹7,500 crore.
- *Selling pressure:* unclear — No demerged entity, share-entitlement ratio or index treatment stated anywhere in the documents.
- *Parent or spin:* unclear · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Draft PMPL ESOP-2026 scheme at powermechprojects.com/codes-policies — grant dates and exercise price within the 10%–25% band.
- *In their words:* “The Options will be granted at an Exercise Price ranging from a minimum of 10% to a maximum of 25% of the Market Price of the Shares on the date of grant.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

These texts do not describe Power Mech Projects separating, demerging or spinning off any business — there is no scheme of arrangement, no NCLT filing, no record date, no share-entitlement ratio, and no management discussion of hiving off a division on any of the six calls (May 2025 through May 2026) or in either filing (postal ballot of 10 November 2025 and AGM notice of 8 August 2026). The only occurrences of the words 'merger/demerger, sale of division/undertaking' are inside the standard corporate-action adjustment clause of the proposed 'Power Mech Projects Limited -Employee Stock Option Plan -2026' (10,00,000 options, of which up to 2,00,000 for subsidiary employees, 3.16%–3.19% of capital on a fully diluted basis), which merely says options would be re-priced fairly if such an action ever occurred; it is boilerplate, not a plan. What the texts actually show is the opposite of separation — consolidation and the use of subsidiaries/SPVs inside one listed entity: the Transmission/Electrical division was wound down and its portfolio 'shifted' into the Civil business while a new BOP EPC vertical was added (May 2026); a 100% subsidiary, PM Green, was incorporated for the 250 MW / 1,000 MWh West Bengal BESS BOO project (INR 800 crore capex, INR 103 crore/year over 15 years, INR 1,563 crore, 51% Power Mech-led consortium, 16–18% equity IRR) which was later cancelled by the West Bengal State Electricity department; MDO assets sit in SPVs (Tasra SPV carrying INR 400 crore of coal-handling-plant and railway-siding capex, KBP raising a INR 256 crore term loan, the INR 690–700 crore washery built in Power Mech's own books) and riverbed-mineral/sand mines sit in LLPs taxed at 35% versus 25% at company level, lifting the consolidated effective tax rate to 28–29%. Portfolio pruning that did happen was order-book, not corporate: INR 4,264 crore of non-moving Adani FGD orders (Kawai, Tiroda, Mundra) were removed by mutual agreement, leaving only the INR 936 crore Udupi job, and management said it is 'not showing interest' in new water projects, with the UP Jal Jeevan Mission book run down to about INR 900 crore pending central funding. Management's stated strategic direction is to concentrate the same listed company on power, O&M, BOP EPC and MDO (visibility to FY30, 12.3% FY26 EBITDA rising toward 14% by FY30) — not to separate anything. If a separation exists, it is documented somewhere outside the material supplied here.

**How it evolved:** The idea never surfaces: across CALL Feb 2025, CALL May 2025, CALL Aug 2025, CALL Nov 2025, CALL Feb 2026 and CALL May 2026 no analyst asks about a demerger and no manager raises one; the only corporate-structure questions concern succession (Rohit Sajja's induction to the Board, May 2025) and fund-raising (QIP of INR 240 crore, borrowing limit raised from INR 5,000 crore to INR 7,500 crore in the November 2025 postal ballot). The two filings in the window are an ESOP-2026 postal ballot (10 November 2025, voting 21 November–20 December 2025, with a 1%-of-capital grant resolution) and the 27th AGM notice (8 August 2026, meeting 17 September 2026) re-tabling the same ESOP plus a INR 1.50 dividend, independent-director appointment and director remuneration — none of which mention a separation. The nearest thing to a structural change evolves as consolidation: PM Green is created for BESS (disclosed CALL Feb 2026), the BESS order is then cancelled (CALL May 2026), and the Electrical/Transmission division is declared 'over' and merged into Civil while BOP EPC is created as the new vertical (CALL Nov 2025 signalling, confirmed CALL May 2026).

**What management expects from it:** Nothing is stated, because no separation is proposed. Management's expectations are for the single consolidated entity: FY27 revenue growth of 21% on INR 6,107 crore, EBITDA rising from 12.3% to about 12.5% and toward 14% by FY30 as O&M (15-16%) and MDO (15% to 20-21% at peak rated capacity) outweigh sub-10% construction margins, with operating cash flow of INR 430 crore and debt/equity of 0.32x funding capex internally.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *CALL May 2026* — The closest actual restructuring is internal consolidation, not separation: the Transmission/Electrical segment was discontinued and absorbed into the Civil division, with BOP EPC created as the replacement reporting vertical. “No, it is a different business because, actually, earlier the Transmission division used to do the transmission erection of the lines and other things. That business is over now.”
- *CALL May 2026* — Management explicitly folded the electrical/T&D portfolio into civil rather than separating it, and added BOP EPC as a new line of activity. “So, now we shifted that entire portfolio to the civil business, and we added a new line of activity of BOP EPC business.”
- *CALL Feb 2026* — New energy-transition activity was housed in a wholly owned subsidiary (PM Green) kept inside the group, described as a cautious experiment, not a business being carved out. “So , we have incorporated a 100% subsidiary as a PM Green for this, and this is a small attempt we to see where the renewable segment fits into the Power Mech's vision of sustained growth and margins.”
- *CALL May 2026* — MDO assets are held in SPVs within the consolidated group, with capex split between the Tasra SPV and Power Mech standalone - a financing structure, not a separation. “And in TASRA SPV, INR 400 crores of Capex Tasra Coal Handling Plant and railway siding is added.”
- *CALL Aug 2025* — Riverbed-mineral/sand-mine operations run through LLP entities taxed at 35% versus 25% at company level, lifting the consolidated tax rate to 28-29% - the only structure-driven economic friction management quantified. “The exceptional revenue generat ed from the Riverbed Minerals business was booked through L LP. Where applicable tax rate is 35%, compared to 25% at the company level .”
- *CALL May 2025* — Portfolio pruning that did occur was contractual, not corporate: INR 4,264 crore of non-moving Adani FGD orders were removed from the order book by mutual agreement, leaving only the INR 936 crore Udupi package. “So, we have taken a djustment of non moving FGD orders – after discussion and negotiations with the client.”
- *CALL May 2026* — Management said it is stepping back from the water/Jal Jeevan Mission business to concentrate on power and O&M - a reallocation of bidding focus, with no entity-level separation proposed. “As of now, we are not showing interest, ma'am, because the power orders, we are getting more power orders.”
- *Scheme* — The only 'demerger / sale of division' language in the filings is the standard option-adjustment clause of the proposed PMPL ESOP-2026 (10,00,000 options, up to 2,00,000 for subsidiary employees), appearing identically in both the 10 November 2025 postal ballot and the 8 August 2026 AGM notice; it is contingent boilerplate, not an announced transaction. “RESOLVED FURTHER THAT in case of any corporate action(s) such as rights issues, bonus issues, stock splits, consolidation of shares, merger/ demerger, sale of division/undertaking etc., if any, Options will be adjusted accordingly to the Options grantees for the purpose of making a fair and reasonable adjustment to the Options granted earlier/to be granted,”

*Not explained on the calls:* Everything about a separation: no rationale, scheme, entity split, ratio, listing plan, lender or investor demand, timeline, or allocation of debt, order book or MDO SPVs appears anywhere.

## TRITURBINE — Triveni Turbine Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a filing's text names a demerger; no scheme filing names it yet) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 4.2/10 · spin-off · 1 filing(s) from NSE · first 2025-11-21, latest 2025-11-21

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Triveni Turbine itself — the industrial steam turbine business demerged from parent Triveni Engineering and Industries Limited in 2010 — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* Not stated for promoters. Documents state TEIL held 21.85% equity capital of TTL since the demerger until 2022, fully divesting on September 21, 2022. Dhruv M. Sawhney is Chairman & MD; son Nikhil Sawhney Vice Chairman & MD.
- *What it reveals:* A high-quality standalone: ranks second globally in steam turbines up to 100 MW, 6000+ installations in 80+ countries, FY26 revenue ₹21.81 billion (+9%), EBITDA 24.2%, closing order book ₹20.54 billion, negligible finance costs (₹19 million 9M).
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — Demerger was 2010; the parent's residual 21.85% overhang was fully divested on September 21, 2022. No current distribution pending.
- *Parent or spin:* spin · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* FY26 annual report subsidiary accounts — US subsidiary ~₹21 crore loss and South African TTAPL/TSE turnover
- *In their words:* “It was demerged from its parent Company, Triveni Engineering and Industries Limited (TEIL) in 2010.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

These texts contain no business separation, demerger, spin-off, slump sale or scheme of arrangement by Triveni Turbine Ltd. — the premise cannot be supported from the material supplied, and the corporate-structure actions disclosed all run in the opposite direction, toward consolidation. The only scheme-type filing is the April 2026 South African merger in which TSE Engineering (Pty) Ltd was merged INTO Triveni Turbines Africa (Pty) Ltd — both step-down wholly owned subsidiaries held via Triveni Turbines DMCC, UAE — approved by the CIPC on April 14, 2026 and effective April 1, 2026, with TSE dissolved; FY25 turnover was ₹119 Cr (ZAR 257 million) for TTAPL and ₹50 Cr (ZAR 109 million) for TSE, with no cash consideration, no share-exchange ratio and no change in TTL's shareholding pattern. The stated rationale is simplification, not separation: to simplify the Group's South African corporate structure, gain operational and administrative efficiencies, and consolidate into a single unified legal entity for improved governance and streamlined reporting. This followed the Q3 FY26 buy-in of the remaining 30% of TSE for ZAR 10.97 million (₹56 million), which management framed on the Nov 2025 call as consolidating ownership, strengthening operational control, simplifying the group structure, improving decision-making and agility and realising operational synergies and cost efficiencies through unified management — and on the Feb 2026 call as 'unifying our operations in the South African market' while widening scope from SADC to Sub-Saharan Africa. The only other structural items are a Ind AS 19/wage-code exceptional charge of ₹157 million (not structural at all) and the NCLT-approved reduction of share capital of wholly owned Triveni Energy Solutions Limited, which produced a ₹360 million standalone exceptional gain in Q3 FY25 — a capital reduction within a wholly owned subsidiary, not a business separation. The sole separation anywhere in the texts is historical and concerns the parent, not TTL's own businesses: the About-the-Company boilerplate in the November 21, 2025 press release notes TTL 'was demerged from its parent Company, Triveni Engineering and Industries Limited (TEIL) in 2010', with TEIL holding 21.85% until it fully divested on September 21, 2022 — no rationale, numbers or requesting party is given for that 2010 demerger. Consistent with this, both standalone and consolidated results state the company operates in a single reportable segment, 'Power Generating Equipment and Solutions', with no reportable segments under Ind AS 108, and Nikhil Sawhney told the May 2026 call the company is 'still pretty much a steam turbine company' — i.e. no separable second business is even presented, and no investor, lender or partner is recorded as asking for one.

**How it evolved:** No separation idea surfaces in any call. Instead: Aug 2025 and May 2025 discuss investing in and absorbing losses at the US and South African subsidiaries; Nov 12, 2025 announces buying TSE's remaining 30% for ZAR 10.97 million to consolidate ownership and simplify group structure; Feb 4, 2026 says 100% control allows 'unifying our operations' and widening scope from SADC to Sub-Saharan Africa; the April 15, 2026 filing completes that by merging TSE into Triveni Turbines Africa effective April 1, 2026. The May 19, 2026 call does not mention the merger or any separation at all.

**What management expects from it:** Nothing is claimed for a separation, because none is proposed. For the South African consolidation management expects a simplified group structure, operational and administrative efficiencies, a single unified legal entity with improved governance and streamlined reporting, stronger operational control, faster decision-making and agility, and operational synergies and cost efficiencies under unified management — plus scope widening from SADC to Sub-Saharan Africa. No margin, capital or valuation targets are quantified.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The April 15, 2026 filing is a merger of TSE Engineering into Triveni Turbines Africa (both step-down wholly owned subsidiaries), effective April 1, 2026 after CIPC approval of April 14, 2026, with TSE dissolved — consolidation, not separation. “With effectiveness of the scheme, TSE stands dissolved and ceased to be the step-down wholly owned subsidiary of the Company.”
- *Scheme* — The filing's stated rationale is structural simplification and efficiency within South Africa, with no divestment, no cash consideration, no share-exchange ratio and no change in TTL's shareholding pattern. “The merger has been undertaken to simplify the Group's corporate structure in South Africa, achieve enhanced operational and administrative efficiencies, and consolidate the operations into a single unified legal entity, thereby enabling improved governance, streamlined reporting.”
- *Scheme* — Sizes given for the two merging entities: TTAPL ₹119 Cr and TSE ₹50 Cr of FY25 turnover; consideration is nil because both are 100% group-owned. “There is no cash consideration and share -exchange ratio, as both entities are 100% owned within the same group.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=e284c057-7b7f-4f4c-9bdb-d88807e00402.pdf)* — Management announced buying the remaining 30% of TSE Engineering for ZAR 10.97 million (₹56 million), explicitly to consolidate ownership and control rather than to separate anything. “This is in line with the company's strategic objective to consolidate its ownership and strengthen operational control over its subsidiaries.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=e284c057-7b7f-4f4c-9bdb-d88807e00402.pdf)* — The benefits management cited are simplification, agility, synergies and cost efficiency under unified management — the standard consolidation case, not a separation case. “The move will enable simplifying the group structure, enhance decision -making and agility, while at the same time, aligning the group's long -term business goals, which would reali se operational synergies and cost efficiencies through a unified management and streamlined process.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=c3ee1092-90cf-4e58-9a26-9edd9f2b48b8.pdf)* — With 100% of TSE in hand, management said it would unify South African operations and widen the addressable scope from SADC to Sub-Saharan Africa for both products and Aftermarket. “And we would look at unifying our operations in the South African market.”
- *Scheme* — The only other structural action disclosed is a capital reduction inside a wholly owned Indian subsidiary, booked as a ₹360 million standalone exceptional gain in Q3 FY25 — not a business separation. “During the quarter ended December 31, 2024, pursuant to the Hon'ble National Company Law Tribunal order on the reduction of share capital of Triveni Energy Solutions Limited, a Wholly Owned Subsidiary of the Company,< 360 million of gain on account of such capital reduction had been presented as an exceptional item”
- *Scheme* — The single separation anywhere in the texts is historical and concerns TTL's own creation out of its parent in 2010, with no rationale, numbers or requesting party disclosed. “It was demerged from its parent Company, Triveni Engineering and Industries Limited (TEIL)  in 2010.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=7eb58552-4e6c-4fe7-a688-a8cfa6177583.pdf)* — Management still describes TTL as effectively one business, which is why no separable second business is presented in any call. “But we're still pretty much a steam turbine company at this point in time.”
- *Scheme* — The financial results confirm a single-business filer, with no segment carved out for separation. “The Company primarily operates in a single reportable segment- Power Generating Equipment and Solutions. Accordingly, there are no reportable segments as per Ind AS 108.”

*Not explained on the calls:* Everything: no separation, rationale, entities, numbers, problems solved, requesting investors, lenders or partners, timeline or plan evolution appears anywhere in these calls or filings.

**Stated in the filings:** resulting company **Special Economic Zone Limited**.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** No demerger; 49% of Adani Vizhinjam Port Private Limited sold to MSC's terminal arm TiL; AHSL amalgamated into APSEZ — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* Buyer Mundi/TiL does not belong to promoter/promoter group; not a related party transaction. APSEZ retains 51% equity, majority of board seats, consolidates AVPPL. Promoter stake not stated
- *What it reveals:* Reveals a great asset: AVPPL income Rs 843.19 crore and networth Rs 2,813.98 crore as on 31.03.26 valued at USD 2.85bn total; 49% fetches USD 1.397bn, of which USD 858mn funds expansion capex
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — No shares distributed or listed; TiL invests cash in two tranches, APSEZ keeps 51% and continues consolidating AVPPL
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* The attached investor presentation's tranche table and Q1 FY27 results for accounting of the USD 539mn stake consideration
- *In their words:* “APSEZ will retain 51% of equity, hold majority of board seats, and will continue to consolidate AVPPL as a subsidiary company”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

On the evidence of these transcripts and filings, APSEZ is not separating or demerging a business, and management never explains one, because no separation exists in the record: the only Scheme of Arrangement here runs the other way, folding a subsidiary in. The Scheme is the amalgamation of Adani Harbour Services Limited (AHSL, the wholly-owned harbour/marine-services arm) INTO APSEZ under Sections 230-232 of the Companies Act, 2013 — intimated by the letter of November 4, 2025, sanctioned by the NCLT Ahmedabad Bench on April 1, 2026, and effective April 21, 2026 when the certified order was filed with the RoC Gujarat; no rationale, synergy, cost saving or valuation argument is given in the filing, and no earnings call mentions it. The only transaction that separates economic interest in a business is the Vizhinjam partial sell-down: a Share Purchase and Subscription Agreement dated June 29, 2026 under which Mundi Limited, a subsidiary of Terminal Investment Limited (TiL, the terminal arm of MSC), takes 49% of Adani Vizhinjam Port Private Limited (AVPPL) at a total deal value of USD 2.85bn, of which TiL's 49% share is USD 1.397bn — USD 539mn for the stake and USD 858mn on completion of the Phase 2 expansion by December 2028 (total expansion capex USD 1.75bn, capacity 1.6m to 5.7m TEUs, 3.5x; quay 800m to 2,000m; STS cranes 8 to 29). This is explicitly not a demerger or slump sale (both marked "Not Applicable" in the Regulation 30 disclosure): APSEZ keeps 51%, a majority of board seats, and continues to consolidate AVPPL as a subsidiary, so it is a partner-led monetisation of a minority stake, not a separation of the asset from the group. The problems it is said to solve are commercial, not structural — enhanced volume visibility and ramp-up ahead of plan, a higher share of Bangladesh cargo today routed through competing Southeast Asian transshipment hubs, a stronger position on East Africa trade routes, more relay cargo — plus funding: "Transaction unlocks USD 1.397bn for APSEZ's future growth trajectory" against AVPPL FY26 income of Rs 843.19 crore, share capital of Rs 897.00 crore and net worth of Rs 2,813.98 crore at 31.03.26. Who asked: the counterparty is MSC/TiL, a third strategic partnership after Mundra CT3 (AICTPL, 50:50, 3.2m TEUs in FY26) and Ennore (AECTPL, 51:49, 701K TEUs in FY26); no investor, lender or rating agency in these texts asks for any business to be separated, and investors instead asked for, and got, separate REPORTING lines (international ports, marine, trucking and international freight network) plus capital-allocation detail. Management's stated strategic direction across every call is the opposite of separation — integration and consolidation into one "integrated transport utility" with scale, and the only business they declined to own, shipbuilding, was declined on competency grounds, not separated.

**How it evolved:** The idea of a separation never surfaces in the calls: Oct 2024, Feb 2025, May 2025 (May 1, 2025), Nov 2025 (Nov 4, 2025) and the Apr 30, 2026 Q4 call discuss volumes, margins, ROCE, capex and leverage, with no demerger, spin-off or listing of a vertical mentioned. What did evolve was disclosure and structure: at the May 2025 call management introduced separate reporting lines for international ports, marine services and trucking/IFN "thanks to your feedback"; on November 4, 2025 — the same date as the Q2 FY26 call, where it was not discussed — APSEZ intimated the inward amalgamation of Adani Harbour Services into the parent, sanctioned April 1, 2026 and effective April 21, 2026. Only after the last call in this set does a partial separation of economic interest appear, in the June 29-30, 2026 Vizhinjam agreement with MSC's TiL for 49% of AVPPL, which was never previewed or justified on any call in this record. Across the whole window the narrative runs toward consolidation — Ambition 2031, capex first, strategic M&A second, buyback "the last option" — not toward breaking anything out.

**What management expects from it:** No separation, so no per-entity expectations are given. For the Vizhinjam 49% sell-down they expect faster ramp-up and volume visibility, more Bangladesh and East Africa relay cargo, and USD 1.397bn unlocked for growth, while APSEZ keeps 51%, board control and consolidation. For the AHSL amalgamation into APSEZ, no margin, capital or valuation benefit is stated anywhere.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The only Scheme of Arrangement in the record is an inward amalgamation, not a separation: wholly-owned Adani Harbour Services Limited was merged into APSEZ under Sections 230-232, sanctioned by the NCLT Ahmedabad Bench on April 1, 2026, with no rationale stated in the filing. “the Scheme of Amalgamation of Adani Harbour Services Limited ("Transferor Company") with Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Limited ("Transferee Company") under Sections 230 to 232 and other applicable all provisions of the Companies Act, 2013, has been sanctioned by the Hon'ble National Company Law Tribunal, Ahmedabad Bench by its order passed on April 1, 2026.”
- *Scheme* — The amalgamation completed on filing the certified NCLT order with the RoC Gujarat; the first intimation was a letter dated November 4, 2025, the same day as the Q2 FY26 call, where it was never mentioned. “Accordingly, the effective date of Scheme is April 21, 2026.”
- *Scheme* — The only separation of economic interest is a 49% stake sale in the Vizhinjam port entity (AVPPL) to Mundi Limited, a subsidiary of MSC's terminal arm TiL, signed June 29, 2026 and subject to customary and regulatory approvals. “the Company has entered into Share Purchase and Subscription Agreement on June 29, 2026 with Mundi Limited ("Mundi"), pursuant to which Mundi will invest for 49% interest in Adani Vizhinjam Port Private Limited ("AVPPL").”
- *Scheme* — Vizhinjam is explicitly NOT being separated from APSEZ: control, board majority and consolidation are retained, and the disclosure marks both "disposal of the undertaking outside Scheme of Arrangement" and "slump sale" as Not Applicable. “APSEZ will retain 51% of equity, hold majority of board seats, and will continue to consolidate AVPPL as a subsidiary company”
- *Scheme* — Pricing and staging: total deal value USD 2.85bn, TiL's 49% share USD 1.397bn — USD 539mn for the stake plus USD 858mn on completion of the Phase 2 expansion by December 2028 (expansion capex USD 1.75bn), against AVPPL FY26 income of Rs 843.19 crore and net worth of Rs 2,813.98 crore. “TiL to invest USD 1.397bn, equivalent to its proportionate 49% share of USD 2.85bn.”
- *Scheme* — The funding rationale is stated as growth capital for the parent rather than any structural or governance problem being solved. “Transaction unlocks USD 1.397bn for APSEZ's future growth trajectory”
- *Scheme* — The commercial case is cargo, not corporate structure: faster ramp-up, Bangladesh volumes currently going to rival Southeast Asian hubs, East Africa routes and relay cargo; it is the third APSEZ-TiL tie-up after Mundra CT3 (50:50, 3.2m TEUs FY26) and Ennore (51:49, 701K TEUs FY26). “Higher share of Bangladesh cargo, largely dependent on competing Southeast Asian transshipment hubs”
- *May 2026* — On the last call before the Vizhinjam agreement, capital allocation was described with no reference to any separation, demerger or value-unlocking structure — organic capex first, strategic M&A second, buyback last. “Our priority number 1 is to invest in the capacity expansion and creating new capacities. Our priority for strategic M&A.”
- *May 2026* — Asked by Pulkit Patni (Goldman Sachs) whether a possible group shipbuilding venture would sit inside Adani Ports or in a separate entity, the CEO refused the business on competency grounds rather than discussing any separate-entity structure. “I don't think that's our competency. Our competency is to build the infrastructure ecosystem and to run it efficiently and effectively that's our competency.”
- *May 2026* — Closing remarks frame integration across ports, logistics and marine as the core competitive advantage — the opposite of a separation thesis. “our strength, which is scale, but and which is integrated, right, makes us different than others.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.adaniports.com/-/media/Project/Ports/Investor/Transcripts/Transcript-InvestecQ2--H1-FY26--Updated.pdf)* — Even in the quarter when the AHSL amalgamation was intimated (letter of November 4, 2025, the call date), the stated direction of travel was one consolidated global platform, with no mention of the scheme on the call. “Looking ahead, we are building a truly global integrated transport platform.”
- *May 2025* — What investors actually asked for and received was segment-level transparency — separate reporting for international ports, marine and trucking/IFN — not legal or structural separation of any business. “As our business evolves, and thanks to your feedback. We are introducing new reporting lines.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No rationale for the AHSL merger; no call discusses either deal. Feb 2026 transcript duplicates the Apr 2026 call; Aug 2025 unreadable — those windows unverifiable.

(NSE) on 01 December 2025" (filing 2 December 2025) and "on 23 June 2026" (filing 23 June 2026). No equity listing timeline stated

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** not stated — no demerger or separation; filings cover only a share buyback and subsidiary debenture listings — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* No new entity. In Bajaj Auto, Promoters and Promoter Group held 15,37,56,828 shares (55.01%) pre-buyback and 55.95% post; they "expressed their intention to not participate in the Buyback"
- *What it reveals:* not stated. Filings do disclose wholly owned Bajaj Auto Credit Limited at ~INR20,000 crore AUM, Q1 FY27 PAT INR227 crore, ROE over 25%, plus listed step-down subsidiary Bajaj Mobility AG — value sitting inside the parent, not separated
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — No demerged shares are distributed; only NCD listings by a subsidiary, so no index exclusion or forced selling arises

- *In their words:* “The said Non-convertible Debentures has been listed on National Stock Exchange of India Ltd. (NSE) on 23 June 2026.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

These texts do not describe Bajaj Auto separating, demerging or spinning off any business, so no rationale for one can be reconstructed from them — the only structural moves management discusses run in the opposite direction, toward consolidation. In the Jul 2026 call the electric two-wheeler business was folded INTO an existing unit: 'to capture some synergies, we have brought our electric two-wheeler business in the umbrella of the two-wheeler business unit.' On KTM, Bajaj moved from a 49.9% associate stake to control (BAIH BV holding 100% of BAIH AG, which holds ~74.9%–75% of Bajaj Mobility AG), completed 18 November 2025 after the European Commission subsidies approval of 10 November 2025, with line-by-line consolidation from Q4 FY26 at a one-quarter lag — an acquisition, not a separation. KTM is described as being 'run as an independent company' with its own Executive Board, but that is operating autonomy inside the group, not a separation of a Bajaj business; the turnaround workstreams there explicitly include 'simplifying the organization and corporate structure' and resetting fixed costs. The capital-structure action in the filings is a buyback of up to 46,94,000 shares at INR 12,000 (INR 5,632.80 crore, 1.68% of capital, 16.93% of standalone capital+free reserves), combined with a INR 150/share final dividend (INR 4,192 crore) for a 100% payout of FY26 PAT of INR 9,825 crore — justified by surplus cash (INR 18,000 crore at FY26 close, over INR 21,000 crore at June 2026), FY26 free cash flow above INR 8,000 crore, and an expected improvement in EPS and ROE, not by any portfolio separation. Subsidiaries that are already separate legal entities — Bajaj Auto Credit Ltd (AUM ~INR 20,000 crore, PAT INR 227 crore in Q1 FY27, ROE over 25%, CP and NCD listed) and the Brazil subsidiary — are presented as scaling contributors to consolidated results, with the last equity infusion into BACL described as the final one, again with no mention of separating them. The buyback explanatory statement is explicit on the point: the Board confirmed 'there is no pendency of any scheme of amalgamation or compromise or arrangement pursuant to the provisions of the Act, as on date.'

**How it evolved:** Aug 2025 and Nov 2025 track the KTM/Pierer transaction toward control (regulatory approvals, call options on Stefan Pierer's and Pierer Industries' 50% stake, Austrian Takeover Commission clearance 23 October 2025), i.e. combination rather than separation. Feb 2026 and May 2026 report change of control effective 18 November 2025, renaming of Pierer Bajaj AG to Bajaj Auto International Holdings AG and Pierer Mobility AG to Bajaj Mobility AG, and a turnaround plan whose only structural element is simplification of KTM's own organization and corporate structure. May 2026 adds the 100% payout plus buyback as the shareholder-return mechanism, and Jul 2026 reports the buyback's completion (46,94,000 shares extinguished 24 July 2026) alongside the internal folding of the electric two-wheeler business into the two-wheeler BU. At no point across these eleven months does any call or filing announce, foreshadow or explain a separation of a Bajaj Auto business.

**What management expects from it:** Nothing, because no separation was announced. Management's stated expectations concern the opposite: synergies from folding Chetak into the two-wheeler BU; KTM's turnaround via fixed-cost reset, portfolio sharpening and India sourcing; capacity going from 7 to 9 million units; and, from the buyback plus 100% payout, improved EPS and return on equity.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Jul 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=8490aae2-16b7-41b1-a0a3-de3e86380cf9.pdf)* — The only portfolio-structure change announced is an internal consolidation — the electric two-wheeler (Chetak) business was moved under the domestic two-wheeler business unit to capture synergies, the opposite of a separation. “Domestic two-wheelers, to capture some synergies, we have brought our electric two-wheeler business in the umbrella of the two-wheeler business unit.”
- *[Jul 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=8490aae2-16b7-41b1-a0a3-de3e86380cf9.pdf)* — Asked about India-KTM integration, Rakesh Sharma framed KTM's autonomy as governance of an acquired subsidiary run by its own management, not as a separation of a Bajaj business; collaboration and Indian manufacturing for KTM are being expanded. “So first of all, I must say that KTM is being run as an independent company.”
- *[Jul 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=8490aae2-16b7-41b1-a0a3-de3e86380cf9.pdf)* — The reason given for KTM operating separately is brand/franchise difference, with KTM to be run by its own management on arm's-length competitive benchmarks — a reason for autonomy, not for carving out any Bajaj unit. “So, they are going to be run separately.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=cbc90a41-3f6e-4dcb-b47c-36dc70b66634.pdf)* — The structural event of the period was Bajaj moving from a minority to a controlling stake in KTM, with BMAG and KTM AG becoming step-down subsidiaries consolidated line-by-line with a one-quarter lag — an acquisition and integration, not a demerger. “With the transaction completed on 18th of November, Bajaj moved from being a minority position to a controlling stake and BMAG and KTM are now step -down subsidiaries of the group.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=8874f8f9-b675-43ce-ad9c-6ed3bfffeb9a.pdf)* — The KTM 360-degree turnaround plan's structural workstream is simplification of KTM's own organization and corporate structure plus cost reset and Bajaj-KTM synergies — internal restructuring inside the group, with no separation of any business. “This broadly will encompass sharpening the product portfolio across the 3 bands of KTM, Husqvarna and GASGAS, reworking the target operating model for go -to-market and looking for synergies between the Bajaj and the KTM system, resetting the fixed cost base across all lines, simplifying the organization and corporate structure.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=6beac10f-a781-42da-b71b-38ad4dd37e78.pdf)* — Pierer Mobility AG was renamed Bajaj Mobility AG and kept listed in Zurich and Vienna with Bajaj appointees replacing Pierer nominees on both boards — a change of control and rebranding of an acquired listed entity, not a separation. “In terms of next steps, an extraordinary general meeting has been called for and will be convened on 19th of November at which the name of the company will be changed, it is proposed to be changed from P ierer Mobility AG to Bajaj Mobility AG.”
- *Scheme* — The buyback explanatory statement contains the Board's express confirmation that no scheme of arrangement — the vehicle a demerger or separation would require — is pending at the company. “there is no pendency of any scheme of amalgamation or compromise or arrangement pursuant to the provisions of the Act, as on date;”
- *Scheme* — The stated purpose of the only corporate action in the filings (the INR 5,632.80 crore tender-offer buyback at INR 12,000 per share, 1.68% of capital) is returning surplus cash and improving EPS and ROE — explicitly a capital-return rationale, with no portfolio or separation rationale offered. “The Buyback reinforces the Company's commitment to its shareholders by returning surplus cash to them in an effective and efficient manner, and is expected to improve its earnings per share and return on equity.”

*Not explained on the calls:* Everything about a separation: no business identified, no scheme, no rationale, no investor, lender or partner demand, no financial or valuation targets, no timeline.

## BANKBARODA — Bank of Baroda

**PROBABLE** (a subsidiary's listing is in motion (DRHP / board approval)) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 3.6/10 · partial spin-off / listing · 1 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-09-08, latest 2026-09-08

> **Listing:** IPO / listing of the subsidiary in motion since 2026-09-08; date not fixed — Filing dated 08.09.2026: equity shares transferred to the "Escrow Account" on 08th September 2026; expected date of completion of sale/disposal "End of September 2026 (As indicated by NSE)"

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Bank's minority shareholding in National Stock Exchange of India Limited, part-monetised via Offer for Sale in NSE's IPO — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* not stated; documents state buyers do not belong to promoter/promoter group/group companies and the transaction is not a related party transaction
- *What it reveals:* An unlisted associate/investment stake whose only disclosed contribution was dividend of ₹76,90,37,500 in FY2025-26; the IPO puts a market price on 76,90,375 shares that are 35% of the Bank's holding.
- *Selling pressure:* likely — Bank tendering upto 76,90,375 shares, 35% of its NSE holding, into the IPO offer for sale; shares already moved to escrow
- *Parent or spin:* unclear · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* NSE IPO prospectus for offer price and the Bank's later Regulation 30 disclosure of consideration received post-OFS
- *In their words:* “Pursuant to Regulation 30 and other applicable provisions of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations 2015, we advise that the Bank of Baroda is proposing to divest upto 76,90,375 equity shares, being equivalent to 35% of the shares held by the Bank in National Stock Exchange of India Limited (NSE), by way of Offer for Sale through Initial Public Offering, subject to all regulatory approvals.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

On the evidence of these four transcripts and four filings, Bank of Baroda is not separating or demerging an existing business, and management never offered a separation rationale — no scheme of arrangement, demerger, carve-out listing or hive-off is discussed anywhere, and the word 'spin-off' never appears. What the texts do show is the opposite direction of travel: building new businesses *outside* the standalone bank as fresh subsidiaries rather than splitting existing ones out. On the May 2026 (8 May) call Dr. Debadatta Chand said the bank 'made one of the subsidiary operating from 1st April' — BOB Securities and Giltedge Limited, a standalone primary dealer company that will also do DCM and act as market maker in debt instruments, with committed capital of ₹2,000 crore of which only ₹500 crore had been availed; the stated logic was that the bank 'having a large investment book internally... as a group we can do well on the debt market segment', i.e. sitting the PD/DCM activity in a separate regulated vehicle alongside BOBCAP (equity), insurance, mutual fund, the card business and Baroda Sun Technology (the tech company formalised the prior year). The second new entity is a pension fund: the bank had only received the sponsor appointment letter, with PFRDA and other approvals pending and a 6–9 month timeline. The only genuine *reductions* in the group perimeter are not management-initiated strategy: the Government of India gazette notification CG-DL-E-07042025-262329 dated 05.04.2025 amalgamated Regional Rural Banks one-per-state from 01.05.2025, under which Baroda Rajasthan Kshetriya Gramin Bank passed to State Bank of India as sponsor (consolidated P&L debited ₹1,307.14 crore on reversal of carrying value versus the ₹108.27 crore capital redemption received, while ₹2,466.38 crore of excess equity over cost went to reserves, and the bank subscribed ₹35.99 crore and ₹341.43 crore for 35% of Gujarat Gramin Bank and Uttar Pradesh Gramin Bank); the Malaysia joint venture India International Bank (Malaysia) Berhad was placed under liquidation on 06.11.2025 with capital repatriated; BOB (UK) Ltd repatriated GBP 75 million by capital reduction on 27.03.2026; and the 08.09.2026 filing discloses an offer-for-sale of up to 76,90,375 NSE shares — 35% of the bank's holding — into the NSE IPO, which is minority stake monetisation, not separation of a business. No investor, lender, rating agency or partner is recorded anywhere as asking for any separation; CARE Ratings' 07.10.2026 rationale is standalone and discusses only GoI ownership, capital, asset quality and the ₹5,680 crore NMC settlement.

**How it evolved:** Oct 2024 (25 Oct) contains nothing on group structure at all. The Feb 2026 call (30 Jan 2026) is silent too, with the RRB sponsorship transfer and the Malaysia JV liquidation appearing only in the notes to the Q3 results filed the same day. The idea surfaces as additive subsidiary-building on the May 2026 call (8 May), where BOB Securities and Giltedge Limited is announced as operational from 1 April 2026 and the pension fund sponsor appointment as announced 'yesterday', with Chand closing the topic — 'my current plan of getting into other businesses outside the standalone Bank, I think we're done with that' — and then the Jul 2026 call (24 Jul) returns to zero mentions, while the 8 September 2026 filing adds the NSE offer-for-sale.

**What management expects from it:** Nothing was said about margins, capital release or re-rating from any separation. For the new subsidiaries management expects only scale-up: the PD/DCM entity to become a debt-market maker leveraging the group's large investment book from ₹500 crore of ₹2,000 crore committed capital, the pension fund to be built after PFRDA approval, and existing subsidiaries to be stabilised and strengthened before anything further.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=9a23d6b8-7d66-4fe7-8c6f-b5ed9ad613bd.pdf)* — The only new business moved outside the standalone bank is the primary dealer/DCM activity, incorporated as BOB Securities and Giltedge Limited and made operational from 1 April 2026. “At the same time, we announced that we have made one of the subsidiary operating from 1st April, that is we created a primary dealer business in terms of creating a BOB's Securities and Giltedge Limited.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=9a23d6b8-7d66-4fe7-8c6f-b5ed9ad613bd.pdf)* — The PD entity is funded with ₹2,000 crore committed capital of which only ₹500 crore had been drawn, and is expected to be a market maker in debt instruments leveraging the bank's own large investment book. “We have committed a capital of Rs. 2,000 crores for this, the PD business. And currently they have only availed Rs. 500 crores.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=9a23d6b8-7d66-4fe7-8c6f-b5ed9ad613bd.pdf)* — Chand framed the subsidiary set as complete and complementary — BOBCAP for equity, the new entity for PD plus DCM, pension fund next, plus insurance, mutual fund, cards and Baroda Sun Technology — with no further structural moves planned. “So, I think with this, my current plan of getting into other businesses outside the standalone Bank, I think we're done with that.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=9a23d6b8-7d66-4fe7-8c6f-b5ed9ad613bd.pdf)* — The pension fund subsidiary was only at appointment-letter stage, with PFRDA and other regulatory approvals pending and a 6-to-9-month setup estimate; the PD company was already live and needed to be scaled from a standing start. “So, as I said, on the pension fund 6 to 9 months, whereas the standalone PD, the PD is already operational from 1st April 2026.”
- *Scheme* — Filing 08.09.2026: the bank will sell 35% of its National Stock Exchange holding — up to 76,90,375 shares — through the offer-for-sale in NSE's IPO; FY2025-26 dividend from NSE was ₹76,90,37,500. This is stake monetisation, with no business or division separated. “we advise that the Bank of Baroda is proposing to divest upto 76,90,375 equity shares, being equivalent to 35% of the shares held by the Bank in National Stock Exchange of India Limited (NSE), by way of Offer for Sale through Initial Public Offering, subject to all regulatory approvals.”
- *Scheme* — Filing 30.01.2026 (Q3 notes): the RRB exit was imposed by government gazette, not chosen — one RRB per state from 01.05.2025, moving Baroda Rajasthan Kshetriya Gramin Bank's sponsorship to State Bank of India while BOB took 35% of the merged Gujarat and Uttar Pradesh entities. “The Government of India, vide gazette notification CG-DL-E-07042025-262329 dated 05.04.2025, has provided for the amalgamation of Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) into a single Regional Rural Bank (RRB) in different states effective from 01.05.2025.”
- *Scheme* — Filing 30.01.2026: the Rajasthan RRB exit cost ₹1,307.14 crore through the consolidated P&L against a ₹108.27 crore capital redemption, with ₹2,466.38 crore of excess equity over cost taken to reserves — the only quantified structural impact in the documents. “In case of Baroda Rajasthan Kshetriya Gramin Bank, the Bank has debited its consolidated profit and loss account by ₹ 130714 lakhs towards reversal of difference between the carrying value of investments and the proceeds received for capital redemption.”
- *Scheme* — Other perimeter reductions are wind-downs and capital repatriation rather than separations: the Malaysia joint venture went into voluntary liquidation on 06.11.2025, and BOB (UK) Ltd returned GBP 75 million by capital reduction on 27.03.2026. “During the quarter, India International Bank (Malaysia) Berhad, a joint venture of Bank of Baroda, was placed under liquidation on November 06, 2025.”
- *[Jul 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=434e8419-d728-4195-8230-c2a00598d808.pdf)* — The most recent call (24 July 2026) discusses no separation at all; its 'closure of a legacy matter' language refers to the USD 600 million NMC Health out-of-court settlement charged to Q1 FY27, not to any structural change. “It allows us to close a legacy matter and focus on our customer, stakeholder and long-term sustainable growth.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No scheme of arrangement, demerger or listing of any business; no entity-level financials, valuation, margin or capital-release targets; no investor, lender or partner demand cited anywhere.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** not stated — no separation, demerger or subsidiary listing is described in these documents — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* Only parent-level stake stated: Vice-Chairman says "as a family, we own around 71%"; promoters earlier willing to dilute ~20% for a funded acquisition. Nothing on a new entity.
- *What it reveals:* Filings/calls disclose subsidiary Caplin Steriles separately: FY26 EBITDA INR 142 crore (30%) vs INR 102 crore (27.9%), Q4 margin 33%, own US label ~INR 100 crore in year one, 60 ANDAs, zero debt, INR 2,726 crore liquid assets.
- *Selling pressure:* unclear — No listing, share entitlement, size or index treatment is stated anywhere in the documents.
- *Parent or spin:* unclear · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* A board resolution or scheme of arrangement on any Caplin Steriles listing — absent here; else Caplin Steriles standalone financials.
- *In their words:* “Caplin Steriles Limited (CSL), a Subsidiary of Caplin Point Laboratories Limited, is a fast growing sterile product manufacturing company that is approved by several regulatory agencies such as US FDA, EU-GMP, ANVISA and INVIMA.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

No separation, demerger, spin-off, slump sale or scheme of arrangement is disclosed anywhere in these three years of calls or in the eight filings provided — so the premise cannot be sourced from these texts, and I will not reconstruct a rationale that management never gave. The eight filings are all ANDA approval press releases from Caplin Steriles Limited (Foscarnet Sodium, Calcium Gluconate, Potassium Phosphates, Desmopressin Acetate, Sodium Phosphates, Methylprednisolone Acetate, Linezolid, Acetaminophen); none is a scheme, record-date, valuation report, NCLT or restructuring intimation. What management actually describes is the opposite direction of travel: tighter integration of an already-subsidiarised group — Caplin Point (LatAm/RoW parent), Caplin Steriles Limited (CSL, US/regulated injectables), Caplin Steriles USA (CSU, own-label front end), Caplin One Labs (COL, oncology), the Vizag API unit and Amaris Clinical — funded entirely from internal accruals, zero debt, INR 1,471 crore cash and INR 2,726 crore liquid assets at FY26, with roughly INR 1,000–1,100 crore of capex of which about INR 510 crore remains. The only de-coupling management explains with numbers is commercial, not corporate: CSL stopped signing exclusive B2B deals with upfront milestones and launched its own US label, because B2B partners squeezed manufacturer prices and took 50% of profit — 'that 50% that we've been sharing over the last few years, it accrues directly back to us now' (Feb 2025) — producing nearly INR 100 crore / ~$11mn of own-label revenue in FY26 with 30 products launched, CSL FY26 EBITDA of INR 142 crore (30%, vs INR 102 crore / 27.9%), and no degrowth in B2B. The only equity-structure questions raised by investors were (a) Sachin Kasera asking in Feb 2025 whether CSL's minority investors would be taken out via a listing or buyback, which the Chairman said had never been discussed, and (b) a top-10 PE fund in Nov 2025 offering ~$300mn to co-fund a ~$200mn US target, which would have diluted the family's ~71% holding — management declined it as 'not a meaningful fit'. Nobody — no investor, lender or partner — asked for a business to be separated in any of these six calls, and no lender pressure exists to create one, the group being virtually debt-free with no finance cost.

**How it evolved:** The idea never surfaces. The nearest equity-structure moment is Feb 05, 2025, when an investor asks about listing or buying out CSL's minority holders and the Chairman says it was never discussed; and Nov 06, 2025, when a PE fund's ~$300mn offer that would have diluted the promoters' ~71% stake is rejected as not complementary. By Feb 05, 2026 and May 14, 2026 the discussion has moved entirely to 17 injectable lines, INR 510 crore residual capex, ANDA buyouts and a possible LatAm distribution acquisition — i.e. consolidation inside one group, with Feb 2026 explicitly describing the aim as 'a vertically integrated company like any other big company'.

**What management expects from it:** Nothing, because no separation was announced. The nearest guidance concerns the own-label pivot: CSU breaking even in its first quarter, capturing the 50% profit share once paid to B2B partners, ~INR 100 crore FY26 own-label revenue targeted to double to ~INR 200 crore, CSL EBITDA INR 142 crore (30%), group PAT held at 26–29% and EBITDA 38–39%.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Feb 2025](https://www.caplinpoint.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Earnings-Call-transcript.pdf)* — The only question about separating out an entity was whether CSL's outside investors would exit via listing or buyback; the Chairman said the subject had never even been raised internally or by them. “Yes. That, of course, we haven't discussed, and they are also happy.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.caplinpoint.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Earnings-Call-transcript.pdf)* — The real de-coupling management explains is from B2B front-end partners, not a corporate separation: CSL stopped exclusive deals and milestone/royalty upfronts so the 50% profit share previously given away accrues to Caplin. “Now, why I say mid - to long term is that over the mid - to long term, that 50% that we've been sharing over the last few years, it accrues directly back to us now.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.caplinpoint.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Q4-FY25-Earnings-Transcript.pdf)* — The stated reason for taking the US front end in-house was partner behaviour — cheaper CMOs undercutting on price and B2B partners protecting their own margins by squeezing manufacturers. “Number 2, with the amount of competition our B2B partners being the size that they are, they are always going to ensure that their margins are not affected.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.caplinpoint.net/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/TranscriptCaplinPoint-Nov06-2025.pdf)* — The only structural equity event discussed was a top-10 PE fund's ~$300mn investment into a ~$200mn US target that would have diluted the family's ~71% stake; it was turned down as not complementary to existing lines of growth. “See, as a family, we own around 71%.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.caplinpoint.net/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Transcript_Q3_FY26.pdf)* — Asked directly for a material update on inorganic plans, management said there was nothing at a late stage — and described the end-state as one vertically integrated company, not separated businesses. “Nothing to report at this point, please.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.caplinpoint.net/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Earnings-Call-Transcript_Q4.pdf)* — The FY26 close is framed as scaling an integrated group — 60 ANDAs, 17 injectable lines planned, INR 510 crore residual capex, INR 1,471 crore cash, zero leverage — with acquisitions sought only if 'meaningful'; no separation is mentioned. “I would say that in summary, our US business is transitioning from a phase of foundation building to one that is scaling and growing in depth.”
- *Scheme* — No scheme of arrangement exists in the material supplied: all eight filings are Caplin Steriles ANDA approval press releases, with no record date, valuation, share-entitlement ratio, NCLT or restructuring intimation. “Sub: Press Release – Receipt  of USFDA approval for Foscarnet Sodium Injection”
