## COALINDIA — Coal India Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a subsidiary's listing is in motion (DRHP / board approval)) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 3.6/10 · partial spin-off / listing · 10 filing(s) from NSE · first 2025-12-23, latest 2026-11-02

> **Listing:** IPO / listing of the subsidiary in motion since 2025-12-23; date not fixed — MoC memorandum dated 16.12.2025 advised listing of MCL and SECL 'in the upcoming financial year'; BCCL 'listed on BSE Limited and National Stock Exchange of India Limited effective January 19, 2026' (filing 19.01.2026); CMPDIL 'listed on BSE Limited and National Stock Exchange of India Limited effective March 30th, 2026' (filing 30.03.2026); MCL DRHP dated 1st September 2026 and SECL DRHP dated 01st November 2026 filed, IPOs 'subject to receipt of applicable approvals, prevailing market conditions'

**The stages, as filed:** announced (2025-12-23)

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Minority stakes in CIL's wholly owned coal subsidiaries, listed via IPO offer for sale by Coal India — class `regulatory_strategic`.

- *Insiders:* Not stated. CIL stays promoter and selling shareholder: holding fell 100%-to-90% in BCCL and 100%-to-85% in CMPDIL; MCL/SECL offers are pure offers for sale by CIL
- *What it reveals:* Listings price previously buried subsidiaries: CMPDIL at Rs 172/share on 714,000,000 shares and BCCL at Rs 23/share on 4,657,000,000 shares; MCL (661,836,300 shares offered) and SECL (668,056,100 shares offered) still unpriced
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — Shares sold by IPO offer for sale to willing buyers, not distributed to CIL shareholders; no index exclusion stated
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* SECL DRHP dated 01.11.2026 and MCL DRHP dated 01.09.2026 for subsidiary financials and implied valuations
- *In their words:* “Ministry of Coal, vide its Office Memorandum I/37811/2025 dated 16.12.2025 had advised CIL to take concrete steps to ensure further listing of subsidiaries namely MCL and SECL in the upcoming financial year.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

On the evidence supplied, the "separation" is not a demerger or business carve-out at all: it is a sequence of minority listings of Coal India's wholly-owned mining and planning subsidiaries, each done purely as an Offer for Sale of CIL-held shares, and management never explained a rationale for it on any of the three calls. The filings show the trigger was the owner, not the market: Ministry of Coal Office Memorandum I/37811/2025 dated 16.12.2025 "advised CIL to take concrete steps to ensure further listing of subsidiaries namely MCL and SECL in the upcoming financial year," after which the CIL Board gave in-principle approval by circular resolution on 23.12.2025 for onward submission to DIPAM — i.e. a government disinvestment instruction routed through the administrative ministry, with no investor, lender or JV-partner request cited anywhere. Executed so far: Bharat Coking Coal (BCCL) sold 465,700,000 shares of ₹10 face value at ₹23, listed 19.01.2026, cutting CIL from 100% to 90% (4,657,000,000 to 4,191,300,000 shares); Central Mine Planning & Design Institute (CMPDIL) sold 107,100,000 shares of ₹2 face value at ₹172, listed 30.03.2026, cutting CIL from 100% to 85% (714,000,000 to 606,900,000 shares). In the pipeline: MCL DRHP dated 01.09.2026 for an OFS of up to 661,836,300 shares (₹2 face value) and SECL DRHP dated 01.11.2026 for up to 668,056,100 shares (₹2 face value), both "held by Coal India Limited" and subject to approvals and market conditions. Each filing states the subsidiary "ceases to be a wholly-owned subsidiary… However, it continues to remain a subsidiary," so control, consolidation and sale proceeds all stay with CIL and no fresh capital reaches the units. The only separation question ever asked on a call — Feb 2024, on housing the renewable/alternative-energy verticals as a demerged entity — was refused by management, who said existing subsidiaries and JVs already covered it and "It is not in our discussion right now." The calls do, however, describe the businesses now being listed: BCCL as an all-coking-coal producer (~41 mt target FY24; ~3.7 mt supplied to steel, 2.4–2.7 mt washed) constrained by washing capacity and monetising assets (2 mt Durga washery won by JSW Steel); SECL as the chronic underperformer (197 mt target vs 162 mt, slipping 8–9 mt on land and heavy rainfall); MCL as the low-cost, low-stripping-ratio, low-manpower unit (89.4 mt with 21,523 employees); and CMPDIL as the in-house planning/design arm building CIL's own e-auction platform.

**How it evolved:** Across all three calls in the window (21 Nov 2023, 19 Feb 2024, 14 May 2025) there is no mention of listing or separating any subsidiary; discussion is confined to volumes, e-auction premiums, FMC/railway evacuation, capex of ~₹80,000 crore over five years, employee cost and diversification into solar, gasification and critical minerals. The idea surfaced only once on a call, on 19 Feb 2024, when an investor asked whether the energy/alternative-energy verticals would be a "separate demerged entity" — and management rejected it outright. The actual separation then appears without any call-side preparation in the filings: Ministry of Coal OM of 16.12.2025, CIL Board in-principle approval for MCL and SECL on 23.12.2025, BCCL RHP 02.01.2026 and listing 19.01.2026, CMPDIL RHP 12.03.2026 and listing 30.03.2026, MCL DRHP 02.09.2026 and SECL DRHP 02.11.2026. The sequencing shifted in practice — the two subsidiaries the ministry named (MCL, SECL) were overtaken by BCCL and CMPDIL, which listed first, while MCL and SECL are still only at DRHP stage a year after the directive.

**What management expects from it:** Nothing stated. Across all three calls management gave no expectation for any separation — no margin, capital-allocation, valuation-unlocking or focus argument, and on 19 Feb 2024 it denied any such plan. The filings are bare Regulation 30 disclosures citing only approvals and market conditions; being pure Offers for Sale, they raise no capital for BCCL, CMPDIL, MCL or SECL, and CIL retains 90% and 85% control respectively.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Feb 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=06da4b0a-5420-4ecc-aa42-737719710147.pdf)* — The only time separation came up on any call: an investor asked whether Coal India's energy/alternative-energy verticals would be hived off as a demerged entity. “Okay. And do you have any plans going forward once we have coal, we have CIL energy and then we have -- we're investing a lot in terms of alternative energy as well. Would you have that as a separate demerged entity or something in the future?”
- *[Feb 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=06da4b0a-5420-4ecc-aa42-737719710147.pdf)* — Management rejected the demerger idea, saying existing subsidiaries and JVs already housed the renewable/diversification verticals and nothing further was being considered. “We are not going to create any new subsidy. It is not in our discussion right now.”
- *Scheme* — The trigger is a government instruction, not a corporate initiative: MoC Office Memorandum I/37811/2025 of 16.12.2025 told CIL to list MCL and SECL, and the CIL Board gave in-principle approval by circular resolution for onward submission to DIPAM (filings dated 23.12.2025). “Ministry of Coal, vide its Office Memorandum I/37811/2025 dated 16.12.2025 had advised CIL to take concrete steps to ensure further listing of subsidiaries namely MCL and SECL in the upcoming financial year.”
- *Scheme* — BCCL, the all-coking-coal subsidiary, listed first on 19.01.2026: 465,700,000 shares of ₹10 face value sold at ₹23 by CIL, taking CIL from 100% to 90% (4,657,000,000 to 4,191,300,000 shares). “Bharat Coking Coal Limited, pursuant to its IPO, has sold 465,700,000 Equity Shares at an issue price of ₹ 23 per share which were offered for sale by the Company.”
- *Scheme* — Every transaction is a pure Offer for Sale of CIL's own shares — no primary issue — so cash accrues to the parent and the units stay subsidiaries under CIL control. “Consequent to the above, Bharat Coking Coal ceases to be a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company. However, it continues to remain a subsidiary of the Company.”
- *Scheme* — CMPDIL, the planning and design arm, listed on 30.03.2026 at ₹172 per ₹2-face-value share for 107,100,000 shares, reducing CIL from 100% to 85% (714,000,000 to 606,900,000 shares). “Central Mine Planning & Design Institute Limited, pursuant to its IPO, has sold 107,100,000 Equity Shares at an offer price of ₹172.00 per share which were offered for sale by the Company.”
- *Scheme* — MCL's DRHP dated 01.09.2026 proposes an OFS of up to 661,836,300 shares of ₹2 face value held by CIL, still conditional on approvals and markets. “The DRHP filing pertains to the proposed Initial Public Offering ("IPO") of MCL, comprising an Offer for Sale of up to 661,836,300 equity shares having a face value of INR 2 each, held by Coal India Limited.”
- *Scheme* — SECL's DRHP dated 01.11.2026 proposes an OFS of up to 668,056,100 shares of ₹2 face value held by CIL — the last of the four and nearly a year after the ministry's directive. “The DRHP filing pertains to the proposed Initial Public Offering ("IPO") of SECL, comprising an Offer for Sale of up to 668,056,100 equity shares having a face value of INR 2 each, held by Coal India Limited.”
- *Scheme* — In parallel, CIL keeps putting non-coal businesses into separate JV vehicles rather than inside CIL: on 27.07.2026 the Board approved subscribing 2,22,000 shares at ₹10 (₹22.20 lakh) in the CIL Rajasthan Akshay Urja rights issue, holding 74% against RVUNL's 26%. “To develop, construct and operate the solar power projects, PSP projects and wind power projects or such other projects as may be mutually agreed between the Parties in writing through a suitable model”
- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=f26c1f2d-5905-47eb-b473-a448cab9c8ee.pdf)* — Context on BCCL, the first unit separated: it is 100% coking coal but cannot use its own output because washing capacity is short — hence three new washeries and monetisation of the 2 mt Durga washery to JSW Steel, with only ~3.7 mt supplied to steel of which 2.4–2.7 mt was washed. “Coking coal capacity is BCCL, the entire production is coking coal only, so we are planning for three coking coal washeries there.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=f26c1f2d-5905-47eb-b473-a448cab9c8ee.pdf)* — Context on SECL, the fourth unit in the queue: it was one of the two subsidiaries whose slippage kept FY25 volumes flat, on rainfall and land acquisition. “At SECL, the main issue was abnormally heavy rainfall, seasonal rainfall and certain issues related to land acquisition there and in CCL also issues related to clearances, EC and FC clearances from the Ministry for certain patches.”
- *Nov 2023* — Context on MCL, structurally the best asset being listed — 89.4 mt from 21,523 employees, with management attributing it to newer opencast mines and a very low stripping ratio versus ~30 underground mines each at SECL and ECL. “So relatively new mines, open cast mines, stripping ratio is very less.”

*Not explained on the calls:* Everything: no call discusses the IPOs, rationale, valuation, proceeds use, or subsidiary autonomy. No call after May 2025 is provided, so the Dec 2025 directive onward is unexplained by management.

## GPIL — Godawari Power & Ispat Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a subsidiary's listing is in motion (DRHP / board approval)) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 3.6/10 · partial spin-off / listing · 4 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-07-24, latest 2026-10-17

> **Listing:** IPO / listing of the subsidiary in motion since 2026-07-24; date not fixed

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** No demerger or subsidiary listing; only a partial divestment of GPIL's stake in associate Jammu Pigments Limited — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* Buyers are Promoters of Jammu Pigments Limited and/or their relatives or affiliates; buyer does not belong to GPIL's promoter/promoter group; no new entity, no insider stake stated
- *What it reveals:* JPL contributed Rs.1536.21 Lakhs profit/income (1.92%) and Rs.27381.90 Lakhs net worth (4.68%) on a consolidated basis in FY ended 31.03.2026; 16,75,000 shares sold at Rs.298.45 fair value aggregating Rs.49.99 Crores
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — Private transfer of 16,75,000 shares to JPL promoters; no shares distributed to GPIL shareholders and no new listing
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* The definitive agreement with the Proposed Buyer and the Independent Valuer's fair value report for JPL
- *In their words:* “The Company shall enter into a definitive agreement with the Proposed Buyer.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

These texts contain no demerger or spin-off of an operating division — there is no scheme of arrangement for a split, no share-entitlement ratio, and the only court scheme in the filings runs the other way (wholly-owned Godawari Energy Limited amalgamated INTO GPIL, NCLT order 10.03.2026, effective 23.03.2026, appointed date 01.04.2025) — so the separation management actually explains is portfolio and group-structure separation in three parts. First, GPIL exited its entire 37.85% associate stake in Ardent Steel, a merchant iron ore pellet plant, for about INR 91 crores, framed in Feb 2026 as 'part of the company's ongoing efforts to simplify and streamline group structure'; the economics management gave for that kind of asset is that merchant pellet players 'solely dependent on market for purchase of iron ore' face 'a squeeze in margins' (May 2026) and that 'buying fines in the market and investing in pellet plant, I don't see a business proposition there' (Feb 2025) — while GPIL's own pellet book is captive-ore backed, 2.7 to 4.7 mt with Ari Dongri going 2.35 to 6 mt. The accounting they walked through: INR 91 crore dividend plus ~INR 73 crore book profit standalone (standalone PAT +19%), but under equity method only INR 17 crore gain consolidated, netted against a ~INR 36-37 crore write-off of erstwhile Godawari Energy's thermal power preoperative cost, 'dropped during the year on account of shifting to Solar power', leaving a net INR 17-18 crore consolidated exceptional loss. Second, the non-ferrous recycling arm Jammu Pigments — acquired in FY25 for INR 255 crore on a ~INR 500 crore post-money valuation for 51%, diluted to 43.96% when promoters converted loans — was first declared operationally stand-alone and self-funded ('Jammu Pigments will run independently... We have no intention of investing any further money', Feb 2026), then partly sold back to JPL's own promoters/affiliates in July 2026: 16,75,000 shares at an independent-valuer price of Rs 298.45, Rs 49.99 crores, cutting GPIL from 85,69,762 (43.96%) to 68,94,762 (35.36%); that filing sizes JPL at only 1.92% of FY26 consolidated profit/income (Rs 1,536.21 lakhs) and 4.68% of net worth (Rs 27,381.90 lakhs). Third, the new low-margin, high-volume businesses are deliberately kept outside the steel entity from inception: the BESS plant (10 GW announced Aug/Nov 2025, scaled to a single-line 20 GW with Rs 1,025 crore capex by Feb 2026) sits in wholly-owned Godawari New Energy Private Limited at AURIC/Bidkin on 112 acres, funded '40% from GPIL and balance... by the debt in the SPV', with GPIL's sanctioned investment raised from Rs 500 crore to Rs 700 crore in May 2026, and the contracting layer put into a second wholly-owned Maharashtra company, Godawari Energy Solutions Private Limited, incorporated 17.10.2026 for BESS/renewables EPC; the residential school likewise sits in 81%-held Godawari Education and Research Foundation, funded by an enabling Rs 150 crore loan at 12% and expected to 'separately go for the loan from the other sources'. The problem this structure solves, on management's own numbers, is margin and capital dilution of the steel franchise: BESS at 7-8% and CRM at 8-10% EBITDA against GPIL's FY26 consolidated 23% EBITDA / 15% PAT, which is why the 2031 vision shows ~Rs 3,000 crore PAT on a much larger top line, and why debt for the new verticals is raised at SPV level with prepayment options rather than loaded on GPIL, management having said explicitly they 'don't want to go back into the same debt cycle, which we had entered last 10 years back'. Nobody is recorded as demanding the separations — not lenders, not partners (EVE, Shanghai Shenyi Roche, FIMER, GAIL contract at the project/subsidiary level) — but analysts repeatedly pressed on exactly this (Vikash Singh on capital allocation and 'Jammu Pigments hasn't done anything yet', Sahil Sanghvi on 'we are getting into low profitable businesses', Divya Agarwal on the 10% PAT margin), and the same pruning instinct earlier killed the 2 mt greenfield steel plant and the OPVC pipe project (Feb 2025).

**How it evolved:** The pruning starts Feb 2025, when the 2 million-ton greenfield steel plant and the OPVC pipe venture are both dropped (capex mis-estimation from ~INR 6,000 crore to INR 8,000 crore-plus, and loss of first-mover advantage) only months after the Dec 2024 call pitched Jammu Pigments as diversification; by Aug 2025 the new verticals are explicitly ring-fenced, BESS placed in 100% subsidiary Godawari New Energy Private Limited with 40% GPIL equity and SPV-level debt, confirmed with land and INR 175 crore equity in Nov 2025. Feb 2026 is the turning point for exits: the Board approves disinvestment of the whole 37.85% Ardent Steel stake for ~INR 91 crores expressly to 'simplify and streamline group structure', and management simultaneously declares Jammu Pigments will run independently with no further GPIL money. May 2026 reports it done — stake de-recognised, INR 91 crore dividend plus ~INR 73 crore standalone gain, INR 17 crore consolidated gain against the INR 36-37 crore Godawari Energy thermal write-off — alongside the GEL merger into GPIL (effective 23.03.2026) and a raise of GNEPL funding to INR 700 crore; then July 2026 extends the sell-down logic to Jammu Pigments (16.75 lakh shares, Rs 298.45, Rs 49.99 crores, 43.96% to 35.36%) and Oct 2026 adds a further carve-out, Godawari Energy Solutions Private Limited, for BESS/renewables EPC.

**What management expects from it:** Core steel/mining keeps its captive-ore premium and 23% EBITDA, free of merchant-pellet margin squeeze, with cash recycled into Ari Dongri 6mt, pellets, CRM and solar. BESS and EPC sit in separate SPVs carrying their own debt and 7-10% margins, so group leverage stays near-zero. Jammu Pigments self-funds; ~INR 141 crore released; group structure simplified.

## GREAVESCOT — Greaves Cotton Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a subsidiary's listing is in motion (DRHP / board approval)) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 3.6/10 · partial spin-off / listing · 1 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-10-29, latest 2026-10-29

> **Listing:** IPO / listing of the subsidiary in motion since 2026-10-29; date not fixed — Final SEBI observations dated May 8, 2025 required the Offer to open within 12 months, i.e., May 7, 2026; SEBI's April 7, 2026 circular extended validity to September 30, 2026; on July 31, 2026 GEML said it 'does not propose to avail the one time relaxation... the validity of the SEBI Final Observations has lapsed. Consequently, the Company will not be proceeding with the Offer.' On August 3, 2026 GEML said it 'remains committed to pursuing a public listing at an appropriate time, subject to market conditions, regulatory approvals and other relevant considerations.'

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Greaves Electric Mobility Limited (GEML), the electric two- and three-wheeler mobility business, via proposed IPO/public listing — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* Greaves Cotton holds 62.48% of GEML, unchanged after the Rs 530 crore rights issue (GCL subscribed Rs 331.12 crore; ALJ Green Mobility Rs 198.87 crore). Post-IPO intent: 'below 51% but... significant large shareholders'
- *What it reveals:* H1 FY27 segment data separates a profitable core (Engines and Engineering Products: Rs 1,478.05 crore revenue, Rs 210.55 crore result) from loss-making Electric Mobility (Rs 679.88 crore revenue, Rs 94.44 crore loss) and Vehicle Finance; parent standalone PAT Rs 91.15 crore vs consolidated loss Rs 23.65 crore
- *Selling pressure:* unclear — Documents describe a primary IPO plus small OFS, not a distribution to Greaves Cotton shareholders; the Offer was withdrawn, and no index or size effects are stated
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated

- *In their words:* “While GEML has presently decided not to avail itself of the SEBI extension for the proposed Offer, it remains committed to pursuing a public listing at an appropriate time, subject to market conditions, regulatory approvals and other relevant considerations.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The business being separated is Greaves Electric Mobility Limited (GEML) — the Ampere/ELE/Greaves 3-Wheelers electric 2W and L5 3W business, with step-downs MLR Auto and Bestway Agencies — which management reclassified under its GREAVES.NEXT strategy (Nov 2025) as an 'investee business' alongside Greaves Finance (ev.fin), as distinct from the 'core' B2B engineering company of Energy, Mobility and Industrial Solutions. Management's stated reasons were: (1) GEML needs growth capital the core cannot and should not fund — the DRHP (filed 23 Dec 2024) sought a ₹1,000 crore primary issue plus a smaller OFS, for technology development, the technology centre, in-house battery assembly, expanding subsidiaries' manufacturing capacity, raising stake in one subsidiary, digitisation/IT, inorganic growth and general corporate purposes, while the core's own ₹500–700 crore capex is funded internally; (2) GEML's losses dilute consolidated profitability — Q2 FY26 EV loss of ~₹50 crore against >₹100 crore EBIT in the other segments, FY26 EV segment result of −₹182.01 crore, GEML consolidated FY26 net loss of ₹204.51 crore, EBITDA improving only from −30% to −20%; (3) capital locked in the investees wrecks returns — of ₹1,619 crore net worth a large part sits in GEML/GFL plus ₹500+ crore cash, roughly ₹900 crore that Manish Poddar took out of the ROCE calculation to leave ~₹700 crore of core capital employed earning 'healthy returns'; (4) the two have different maturity curves, different paths to profitability and different orientation (B2B engineering vs consumer), so they must be managed, measured and valued separately, with GEML's employee cost and investment ahead of revenue not comparable to GCL's; (5) partner Abdul Latif Jameel (then ~36%) did not want to be a promoter after a public listing and so was forced to dilute toward 20%, as set out in the DRHP; and (6) investors repeatedly pressed that the two are worth more apart — Zaki Nasser said Greaves and Greaves EV 'will be worth much more separately' and that against Ola/Bajaj/Ather valuations and a re-rating Kirloskar Oil the combined entity is 'caught somewhere in between', while Krisha Kansara wanted the market 'valuing both our businesses separately'. Post-IPO GCL intended to drop below 51% while remaining the largest shareholder, after which consolidation of EV losses and the parent's financial support would cease — which Parag Satpute confirmed as 'a fair understanding'.

**How it evolved:** The idea surfaced from investors first: on the Nov 2024 call shareholders asked about an IPO or demerger of EV and 'unlocking' value via a separate listing, and Akhila Balachandar would only say the board was 'cognizant'; by the Jan 2025 call the DRHP had been filed (23 Dec 2024) with its use of proceeds, and on the May 2025 call the chairman disclosed SEBI's observations and ALJ's forced dilution from 36% toward 20% because it would not be a promoter post-listing. Through Aug 2025 and Nov 2025 the IPO stayed in 'active conversations' and the separation was formalised conceptually as 'core' versus 'investee' businesses under GREAVES.NEXT, with management saying GCL would fall below 51% but stay the largest shareholder; by Feb 2026 the ₹1,000 crore primary was spelled out, Akhila said there was no plan B, and Saket Kapoor got agreement that the EV drag on parent profits would end. On the May 2026 call the plan had slipped — SEBI extended the observation letter's validity to 30 Sep 2026 and the IPO committee would act only when it could get 'a proper valuation' — and the DRHP gag left management unable to answer breakeven questions at all. The plan then changed materially in the filings: on 9 Jul 2026 the board approved subscribing ₹331.12 crore to a GEML rights issue, on 31 Jul 2026 GEML told SEBI it would not avail the extension so the Offer lapsed, the ₹530 crore rights issue was fully subscribed on 2 Aug 2026 (GCL ₹331.12 crore, ALJ ₹198.87 crore) leaving GCL at an unchanged 62.48%, and the Oct 2026 results wrote off ₹12.66 crore of IPO costs as exceptional — separation deferred to 'an appropriate time'.

**What management expects from it:** GEML: ₹1,000 crore primary for technology, in-house battery assembly, subsidiary capacity, digitisation, inorganic growth, and its own market valuation. GCL core: 16–18% organic growth, 13–15% EBITDA, ₹500–700 crore internally funded capex, no further consolidation drag on profits, improved ROCE once the ~₹900 crore tied up in investees and cash is deployed; GCL below 51% yet largest shareholder.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Nov 2024* — Investors, not management, raised separation first — asking directly whether an IPO or demerger of the EV business would improve focus and growth parameters; management gave no commitment. “Second, are we considering an IPO or a demerger of the EV mobility business?”
- *Nov 2024* — Asked about value unlocking and listing the segments separately within two-three years, the CFO said only that the board was aware of the option. “Any decisions on unlocking of value, capital raise, this is something that the board is cognizant of, and we will come back to you as and when the board gives a different decision.”
- *Jan 2025* — GEML's DRHP was filed with SEBI on 23 December 2024, and the use of proceeds was laid out — technology, battery assembly, subsidiary capacity, stake increase, digitisation and inorganic growth, i.e. capital the core would otherwise have to supply. “We propose to utilize the proceeds for investments in technology development, enhancing capabilities at our technology center, development of in-house battery assembly, funding expansion of manufacturing capacities of our subsidiaries, increasing the stake in one of the subsidiaries, increasing digitization and deployment of information technology infrastructure, funding inorganic growth opportunities and general corporate purposes.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=a3e7827f-efe9-48b7-a618-e571d2804eb6.pdf)* — A partner requirement drove part of the structure: ALJ, then holding 36%, refused promoter status after listing and therefore had to dilute toward 20%, as reflected in the DRHP. “And I think I said in my speech that ALJ did not want to be a promoter post a public listing.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=9cfc7607-ba9b-4dd0-bf51-83f3102efa15.pdf)* — Shareholders framed the separation as a valuation problem — the engineering business had begun a strong growth trajectory and they wanted the market to price the two businesses independently. “I wanted to understand if there is a demand in the market for us to successfully launch this IPO because as investors of Greaves Cotton, it is also very crucial for us that the market starts seeing and valuing both our businesses separately.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=9cfc7607-ba9b-4dd0-bf51-83f3102efa15.pdf)* — Management made the timing conditional from the outset — SEBI's final observations were in hand but the launch depended on markets, readiness and 'strategic considerations'. “The actual IPO launch, however, will be subject to prevailing market conditions, internal preparedness, and other strategic considerations.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=3a868a23-d652-4d95-830d-edcdedbb250f.pdf)* — GREAVES.NEXT formalised the split: GCL core is a B2B engineering company (Energy, Mobility, Industrial Solutions) while Greaves Electric and Greaves Finance are consumer-facing 'investee' businesses to be managed differently, with core growth of 16–20% CAGR and ₹500–700 crore capex ring-fenced to the core. “While our investee companies of Greaves Electric and Greaves Finance will continue to pursue their growth ambitions, the core of Greaves Cotton Limited will remain centered on building a trusted future-ready engineering company.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=3a868a23-d652-4d95-830d-edcdedbb250f.pdf)* — An investor quantified the drag the separation is meant to remove — a ₹50 crore quarterly EV loss against more than ₹100 crore of EBIT in the rest of the group, with consolidated EBIT margin of 17% ex-EV. “This quarter also, EV reported Rs. 50 crore loss, while the other segments reported more than Rs. 100 crore of EBIT?”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=3a868a23-d652-4d95-830d-edcdedbb250f.pdf)* — Management stated the intended end-state ownership: GCL would go below 51% after the IPO (deconsolidating control) but stay a large shareholder. “But yes, that is the strategic thinking that post the IPO, we will be below 51% but we will continue to remain significant large shareholders in the company.”
- *Feb 2026* — The funding purpose was restated with numbers — a ₹1,000 crore primary issue flowing directly into GEML (plus a smaller OFS to GCL and ALJ), which the CFO identified as the very point of the IPO when asked how long the loss-making business could be sustained. “And if you have read through the documents, we will be raising approximately a primary of 1,000 crores, which will be utilized for funding the growth aspirations of Greaves Electric Mobility.”
- *Feb 2026* — Management confirmed an investor's reading that after the raise the parent's financial support to, and consolidation drag from, the mobility business would cease, leaving a clean view of core operations — Parag Satpute replied 'That's a fair understanding.' “So that is the only fair understanding investors can keep in mind that by May, we should expect that this depleting of the profitability for the parent company because of consolidation and its financial support to the mobility franchise will cease and we will have fair understanding of the core operations of the company.”
- *Feb 2026* — Pressed on the nine-month delay since SEBI's May 2025 observations and on alternatives if the IPO did not happen, the CFO said there was no plan B. “The plan A is to go for the IPO and we are working on that.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No GEML breakeven date or volume, no valuation, no post-listing accounting treatment, no reason rights replaced the IPO beyond market conditions, no cap on further GCL funding.

## HFCL — HFCL Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a filing's text names a demerger; no scheme filing names it yet) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 3.6/10 · spin-off · 7 filing(s) from CALLS, NSE · first 2026-01-13, latest 2026-08-19

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Defence and aerospace business consolidated into subsidiary HFCL Advance Systems; no share demerger stated in documents — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* Promoters hold no HASPL stake as of date; post-deal HFCL 51.02%, Mr. Anant Nahata 6.50%, employee ESOP trust 14.99%; HFCL Group nominates 4 of 6 directors
- *What it reveals:* Separation reveals a defence/aerospace platform with ~₹1,890–1,930 crore export order book, HDSPL turnover ₹166.21 crore FY25-26, while TWS revenue was only ₹0.66 crore (0.01% of consolidated revenue) with ₹21.24 crore net worth
- *Selling pressure:* unclear — No shares distributed or listed; HASPL stays a 51.02% subsidiary funded by cash and third-party investors, not shareholders
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* 7,50,00,000 promoter warrants allotted May 25, 2026 at ₹74 exercise price, exercisable within 18 months of allotment
- *Read next:* Restructuring Committee outcome with Ernst & Young's advice on merging/demerging each business, and HASPL share subscription agreement terms
- *In their words:* “The transfer of the TWS Business is part of the Company's strategic initiative to consolidate its defence-related businesses under a dedicated platform, i.e., HASPL.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The separation is of HFCL's defence & aerospace business, which is being consolidated out of the listed parent into subsidiary HFCL Advance Systems Private Limited (HASPL), with a Board Restructuring Committee (formed April 30, 2026, advised by Ernst & Young from the July 2026 call) simultaneously studying whether to go further and demerge HFCL's other verticals — optical fibre/OFC, telecom products, and the EPC/turnkey business. Management's stated problem is that the three businesses need entirely different people and execution capability: 'Defense requires different capability, different set of people. EPC needs a different set of people, and fiber business needs a different set of people.' The binding constraint Nahata named twice on the April 30, 2026 call was partner capital: HFCL had received offers from strategic partners, but 'any strategic partner cannot come into such a mix of products where defense, EPC and cable and telecom all are mixed up,' and when asked how the ~₹230 crore Andhra Pradesh ammunition plant would be funded he said equity partnership 'cannot be done when you are a mix of a telecom, defense and fiber-optic. That's why this restructuring committee.' The second driver was an acquisition HFCL could not do organically: the Defsys aerostructures business carries certifications and a confirmed export-oriented order book of ~₹1,930 crore (₹1,890 crore in the June 3, 2026 filings), and Nahata said building it in-house 'would not have been possible for next five to seven years' because aerostructure component approvals take five to seven years. HASPL became the vehicle: on June 3, 2026 HFCL subscribed ₹89.25 crore of a ₹175 crore round (HFCL left at 51.02%, Anant Nahata 6.50%, the Gupta/DMG group 9.50% with two of six board seats and veto rights, ITI Holdings 14.99%, BAS Engineering 3%, and a 14.99% employee ESOP trust), bought 80% of Raddef for ₹75 crore, slump-sold its thermal weapon sight business (FY26 revenue ₹0.66 crore, net worth ₹21.24 crore) in for ₹50 crore, and had HASPL buy HFCL Defence Systems (ex-Spiral EHL, FY26 turnover ₹166.21 crore) for ₹25 crore plus the Defsys aerostructure business for ₹25 crore. The quantitative prize management attached to it: defence order book rising from ~₹300 crore to ~₹2,230 crore, FY27 defence revenue of ~₹500 crore, and an aspiration of ₹3,000 crore-plus by FY29 and ₹5,000 crore the year after — against a group order book of ₹21,200 crore at FY26 and ₹26,665 crore by Q1 FY27 — in a business management says could eventually be 'nearly comparable in scale to HFCL's current overall business.' The stated objectives are to simplify the group structure, sharpen execution focus, improve capital efficiency and unlock long-term shareholder value, bounded by three principles: long-term shareholder value, operational effectiveness and financial discipline.

**How it evolved:** The idea was put to management by an analyst, not volunteered: on the Oct 17, 2025 call Abhishek Jain (Arihant) asked whether three segments — telecom products, EPC, defence — made a case for value unlocking via demerger, and Nahata replied they had 'not really thought about any such thing at this point of time'; the Feb 3, 2026 call carried no restructuring discussion at all (the capital question there was the ₹550 crore QIP). By the Apr 30, 2026 (Q4 FY26) call the March 25, 2026 Board had already approved consolidating defence under HASPL and a Strategic Restructuring Committee was formed 'today itself,' with Nahata framing it as what to merge and what to demerge, driven by differing capabilities and by strategic-partner offers that cannot enter a mixed entity, while refusing the word 'demerger' for defence ('We are currently trying to consolidate it under one roof'). The June 3, 2026 filings executed the first leg — share subscription and shareholders' agreement for HASPL, 80% of Raddef, the TWS slump sale, and the Defsys aerostructure/HDSPL acquisitions — taking HFCL to 51.02% of the defence platform. On the Jul 22, 2026 call the scope widened and slowed: Ernst & Young was appointed strategic advisor, 'various alternatives' were still under evaluation with no specific outcome commented on, and Nahata clarified the carve-out is partial — ammunition and electronic fuzes 'are still remaining in HFCL.'

**What management expects from it:** For defence/aerospace (HASPL): sharpened execution focus, improved capital efficiency, access to strategic-partner and outside equity impossible inside the mixed parent, ESOP-led talent incentives, order book from ~₹300 to ~₹2,230 crore, ~₹500 crore FY27 revenue scaling to ₹3,000–5,000 crore, margins a couple of points above group. For HFCL: a simpler group, each business realising full growth potential, and unlocked long-term shareholder value.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Oct 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=9f05c17e-2d03-4e56-84c3-6edc036ac0b8.pdf)* — An analyst first raised demerger as a value-unlocking route given three distinct segments (telecom products, EPC, defence); management said it had not considered it. “is there any compelling case for value unlocking via demerger or any other opportunity for us?”
- *[Oct 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=9f05c17e-2d03-4e56-84c3-6edc036ac0b8.pdf)* — Nahata explicitly declined the idea at that stage, promising to revert if it was ever taken up — the baseline against which the later reversal should be read. “We have not really thought about any such thing at this point of time. If we think about it, we'll come back to you.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=3d0dd925-2be0-4b2f-9445-072ed9304615.pdf)* — Opening remarks disclosed the March 25, 2026 Board approval to consolidate complementary defence capabilities under subsidiary HASPL as a dedicated defence and aerospace platform. “The core objective of this proposed transaction is to create a focused and scalable and future ready defence and aer ospace platform by consolidating complementary defence capabilities under our subsidiary, HFCL Advance Systems Private Limited.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=3d0dd925-2be0-4b2f-9445-072ed9304615.pdf)* — Management's stated structural problem: each vertical needs a different skill set and execution model, which is why a Restructuring Committee was constituted to decide what to merge and what to demerge. “Defense requires different capability, different set of people. EPC needs a diff erent set of people, and fiber business needs a different set of people.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=3d0dd925-2be0-4b2f-9445-072ed9304615.pdf)* — The trigger named was inbound strategic-partner interest that cannot be accommodated inside a conglomerate entity mixing defence, EPC, cable and telecom. “Now, any strategic partner cannot come into such a mix of products where defense, EPC and cable and telecom all are mixed up.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=3d0dd925-2be0-4b2f-9445-072ed9304615.pdf)* — Asked how the 1,000-acre Andhra ammunition plant would be funded, Nahata tied the impossibility of an equity partnership directly to the mixed structure — the clearest statement of the capital-raising motive. “There's no plan of any partnership at this point of time because partnership -- equity partnership cannot be done when you are a mix of a telecom, defense and fiber-optic. That's why this restructuring committee.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=3d0dd925-2be0-4b2f-9445-072ed9304615.pdf)* — Management distinguished the defence step (consolidation under one roof) from a demerger, saying the committee formed that day would study whether demerging into specialised entities is more efficient and would enable strategic tie-ups. “But a restructuring committee has been formed precisely to look into such aspects, whether it is efficient to demerge the businesses into the specialized areas so that some strategic tie-up or even if that kind of thing is required, can be done.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=3d0dd925-2be0-4b2f-9445-072ed9304615.pdf)* — The stated benefits of the HASPL structure for the defence vertical were execution focus, capital efficiency and sustainable growth. “We believe that the proposed structure will sharpen execution focus, improve capital efficiency and drive sustainable growth from defence vertical.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=3d0dd925-2be0-4b2f-9445-072ed9304615.pdf)* — The acquired aerospace/aerostructure business brings certifications and a confirmed export order book of ~₹1,930 crore, lifting the defence order book from ~₹300 crore to ~₹2,230 crore. “Importantly, this business comes with established capability base, certifications, long-standing customer relationships and a confirmed export -orien ted order book of approximately INR 1,930 crore, providing immediate revenue visibility.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=3d0dd925-2be0-4b2f-9445-072ed9304615.pdf)* — Buy-versus-build rationale: aerostructure approvals take five to seven years per component, so entering greenfield was not feasible — hence acquisition into a dedicated platform. “If we had tried ourselves, it would not have been possible for next five to seven years with an order book and with certified products and with possibility to get more orders.”
- *[Jul 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=bbc45887-fdfd-4470-8565-f5f5b09fee2d.pdf)* — The mandate was restated as group-wide simplification and value unlocking, and Ernst & Young was appointed strategic advisor, with no specific outcome disclosed. “As communicated earlier, our Board had constituted a Restructuring Committee to evaluate strategic alternat ives aimed at simplifying the Group structure, enhancing operational efficiency and unlocking long -term shareholder value.”
- *[Jul 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=bbc45887-fdfd-4470-8565-f5f5b09fee2d.pdf)* — Three governing principles were set out for any restructuring outcome, with management declining to comment on specifics at that stage. “While it would not be appropriate t o comment on specific outcomes at this stage, I would like to assure our shareholders that every decision will be guided by three fundamental principles creating long -term shareholder value, strengthening operational effectiveness and preserving financial discipline.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No demerger decision, timeline, listing or swap ratio; no valuation of any vertical; no E&Y recommendation; no reason ammunition and fuzes stay in HFCL.

## ICICIBANK — ICICI Bank Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a subsidiary's listing is in motion (DRHP / board approval)) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 3.6/10 · partial spin-off / listing · 4 filing(s) from NSE · first 2025-12-06, latest 2025-12-19

> **Listing:** IPO / listing of the subsidiary in motion since 2025-12-06; date not fixed — Said in the Annual Securities Report filed September 18, 2026: "Effective December 19, 2025, ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Limited is listed on Bombay Stock Exchange and National Stock Exchange."

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company, the group's asset management and portfolio/advisory services subsidiary — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* Bank held 53.0% and PCHL 34.6% at March 31, 2026; Bank bought 2.0% more from PCHL primarily to keep majority shareholding if stock-based compensation is granted
- *What it reveals:* A listed price for a fee business earning Rs 33.0 billion PAT in fiscal 2026 vs Rs 26.5 billion in fiscal 2025, now also holding ICICI Venture's private equity, venture capital and real estate fund management business
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — No shares distributed to Bank shareholders; listing came via PCHL's partial divestment, with the Bank retaining 53.0%
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Slides 33 to 35 of the Q4-FY2026 investor presentation for ICICI AMC's standalone financials versus the Bank's 53.0% stake
- *In their words:* “Effective December 19, 2025, ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Limited is listed on Bombay Stock Exchange and National Stock Exchange.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

There is no separation, demerger or spin-off of a business by ICICI Bank in these texts — the question's premise is not supported by the transcripts or the filing, and the dominant direction of travel is the opposite: consolidation of group entities into the Bank. The nearest things management actually described are four entity-level reorganizations. (1) Pension funds: the Board on July 19, 2025 approved acquiring 100% of ICICI Prudential Pension Funds Management Company Limited from ICICI Prudential Life Insurance, moving it from a step-down subsidiary of ICICI Life to a direct wholly owned subsidiary of the Bank; the share purchase agreement was executed January 12, 2026, and on the Jan 2026 media call Sandeep Batra said the rationale was that 'the synergy with the Bank will be better and the business will be able to expand in a much better fashion,' i.e. 'synergising with the banking set of customers'; ICICI Life booked a Rs. 1.1 billion gain on the sale, which was part of why its FY2026 PAT rose 34.6% to Rs. 16.00 billion (25.0% excluding the sale). (2) ICICI Venture's private equity, venture capital and real estate fund management business was approved in principle on May 8, 2025 for transfer to ICICI Prudential AMC, completed with ICICI Prudential AMC managing the transferred funds effective April 1, 2026; the stated purpose was 'offering of an integrated full range of investment asset classes, including private equity,' while ICICI Venture keeps only 'certain advisory activities' and 'certain residual funds' — ICICI Venture's PAT jumped to Rs. 1.5 billion in FY2026 from Rs. 0.2 billion in FY2025. (3) A small divestment of the Bank's entire stake in the NIIT Institute of Finance and Banking JV (set up around 2006), which Batra on Apr 2025 called 'a very small amount' done to 'rationalise and simplify our own portfolio where we want to remain focused on.' (4) Closure of the Offshore Banking Unit in the SEEPZ, Mumbai, for which RBI gave a no-objection letter in May 2026 (a prior OBU closure had already pushed Rs. 3.40 billion of negative foreign currency translation reserve into the Q4-FY2024 P&L). Against these, the Bank was pulling businesses in, not pushing them out: ICICI Securities was delisted on March 24, 2025 and became wholly owned (56 million ICICI Bank shares issued at a 67:100 swap, which Anindya Banerjee cited as the main reason net worth rose about Rs. 20,000 crore sequentially, 'while it's capital neutral'); the Bank bought ~2% more of ICICI Prudential AMC and ~2% more of ICICI Life, explicitly 'towards maintaining the Bank's majority shareholding' against stock-based compensation dilution; it infused Rs. 5.0 billion (including Rs. 500 crore in Q3-FY2026) into ICICI Home Finance, which Batra justified as meeting 'the regulatory requirement and expansion that is required from their business point of view'; and it acquired the remaining equity of I-Process Services. The only genuine ownership separations described are at the partner/JV level, not the Bank's: ICICI Prudential AMC listed on BSE and NSE effective December 19, 2025 following Prudential Corporation Holdings' February 2025 announcement of a 'potential listing and partial divestment of its stake,' and after PCHL agreed on May 17, 2026 to buy 75% of Bharti Life, ICICI Life applied to IRDAI to reclassify PCHL from 'promoter' to 'investor' and to rename itself 'ICICI Life Insurance Limited' (IRDAI approved the name change August 7, 2026).

**How it evolved:** No separation idea ever surfaces as such: on Apr 2025 (call of April 19, 2025) the only disposal discussed is the small NIIT Institute JV stake sale, framed as portfolio simplification, in the same quarter ICICI Securities was delisted into the Bank (March 24, 2025). The ICICI Venture PE/VC/real-estate fund management transfer was approved in principle on May 8, 2025 and the pension-fund acquisition on July 19, 2025 — the same day as the Jul 2025 call, where neither was mentioned and no analyst asked. By Jan 2026 (call of January 17, 2026) Batra confirmed the pension step-down subsidiary had been brought under the Bank, noting 'we explained this, I think, about two quarters back when we made the decision,' and the Oct 2025 transcript is unreadable so any interim discussion is unverifiable; the Apr 2026 call (April 18, 2026) contains no mention of any of it, and only the September 18, 2026 Annual Securities Report records the ICICI Venture transfer as effective April 1, 2026 and the PCHL promoter-to-investor reclassification.

**What management expects from it:** Nothing was said about a separation, because none was announced. For the moves that were made: the pension business gains Bank-customer synergies and faster expansion; ICICI Prudential AMC gains a full asset-class platform including private equity; ICICI Venture keeps only advisory and residual funds; ICICI Life booked a Rs. 1.1 billion gain. No margin, capital-release, valuation-unlock or focus claims were offered.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Jan 2026](https://www.icici.bank.in/content/dam/icicibank/india/managed-assets/docs/about-us/2026/transcript-earnings-call-jan2026.pdf)* — Batra confirmed the Bank had taken over the pension fund business from ICICI Life, explaining it was a step-down subsidiary and that the decision had been disclosed about two quarters earlier. “It was a step-down subsidiary. We explained this, I think, about two quarters back when we made the decision.”
- *[Jan 2026](https://www.icici.bank.in/content/dam/icicibank/india/managed-assets/docs/about-us/2026/transcript-earnings-call-jan2026.pdf)* — The stated rationale for moving the pension fund manager under the Bank was synergy with the Bank's customer base and faster expansion, not value unlocking or capital release. “We do believe that the synergy with the Bank will be better and the business will be able to expand in a much better fashion.”
- *[Jan 2026](https://www.icici.bank.in/content/dam/icicibank/india/managed-assets/docs/about-us/2026/transcript-earnings-call-jan2026.pdf)* — Asked directly whether the pension business had been acquired from the subsidiary, Batra confirmed it in one word; no numbers, consideration or targets were given on the call. “Yes, we have.”
- *[Apr 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=1a691340-05c5-4029-a15f-cdd78f457400.pdf)* — The only outright exit discussed on any call — the entire stake in the NIIT Institute of Finance and Banking JV set up around 2006 — was framed as immaterial portfolio simplification, with no consideration disclosed. “And over the period, we are just wanting to rationalise and simplify our own portfolio where we want to remain focused on.”
- *Scheme* — The one real carve-out of a business line in the texts: ICICI Venture's private equity, venture capital and real estate fund management business was approved for transfer to ICICI Prudential AMC on May 8, 2025, with ICICI Prudential AMC managing those funds from April 1, 2026. “On May 8, 2025, ICICI Venture Funds Management Company Limited's Board of Directors and ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Limited's Board of Directors, in their respective meetings, approved, in principle, a proposal to transfer the private equity, venture capital and real estate fund management business of ICICI Venture Funds Management Company Limited to ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Limited.”
- *Scheme* — The purpose of that transfer was to give ICICI Prudential AMC a complete asset-class platform, leaving ICICI Venture with only advisory work and residual funds. “The transaction enabled the offering of an integrated full range of investment asset classes, including private equity, by ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Limited.”
- *Scheme* — The pension transaction was a Board-approved intra-group purchase to convert a step-down subsidiary into a direct wholly owned subsidiary, conditional on RBI and PFRDA approvals; the SPA was executed January 12, 2026. “The Board at its meeting held on July 19, 2025 approved the acquisition of 100% shareholding in ICICI Prudential Pension Funds Management Company Limited from ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company Limited to make ICICI PFM a wholly owned subsidiary of the Bank, subject to the Reserve Bank of India, PFRDA and other necessary approvals.”
- *Scheme* — The seller side quantified it: ICICI Life's FY2026 PAT of Rs. 16.00 billion (up 34.6%) included a Rs. 1.1 billion gain on selling the pension subsidiary; growth was 25.0% excluding it. “The profit after tax of ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company Limited grew by 34.6% year-on-year from Rs. 11.9 billion in fiscal 2025 to Rs. 16.0 billion in fiscal 2026, primarily driven by higher investment income from Shareholders' funds, which includes a gain of Rs. 1.1 billion realized from sale of 100% equity shareholding in ICICI PFM.”
- *[Apr 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=1a691340-05c5-4029-a15f-cdd78f457400.pdf)* — Direction of travel was consolidation, not separation: ICICI Securities was delisted and absorbed as a wholly owned subsidiary on March 24, 2025, with Bank shares issued to its public shareholders at a 67:100 swap. “Pursuant to the Scheme of Arrangement amongst ICICI Bank Limited and ICICI Securities Limited and their respective shareholders, ICICI Securities Limited has been delisted from stock exchanges on March 24, 2025 and became a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Bank.”
- *[Apr 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=1a691340-05c5-4029-a15f-cdd78f457400.pdf)* — Banerjee attributed the ~Rs. 20,000 crore sequential jump in net worth to the shares issued to ICICI Securities' minority holders, describing it as capital neutral rather than value creating. “So, we would have issued shares to the minority shareholders of ISec that would have, while it's capital neutral, it would have increased the net-worth by a substantial amount.”
- *Scheme* — Stake increases in the listed subsidiaries were defensive against stock-compensation dilution, not steps toward separation: ~2% more of ICICI Prudential AMC and ~2% of ICICI Life (taking it to ~52.8%). “This purchase was primarily for the purposes of maintaining the Bank's majority shareholding in ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Limited were it to grant stock-based compensation.”
- *Scheme* — The only partner-level separation: Prudential Corporation Holdings signalled a partial exit from the AMC, which listed on December 19, 2025, and after agreeing to buy 75% of Bharti Life it is being reclassified from promoter to investor in ICICI Life, which is renaming itself. “Consequently, ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company Limited has applied to IRDAI for the reclassification of PCHL from 'promoter' to 'investor', along with a proposal to change the name of the company from 'ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company Limited' to 'ICICI Life Insurance Limited'.”

*Not explained on the calls:* Everything a separation thesis needs: no demerger exists. No consideration for NIIT or ICICI Venture's transfer, no pension AUM/economics, no lender, investor or partner demands, no analyst questions, and Oct 2025's transcript is unreadable.

## PFC — Power Finance Corporation Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a subsidiary's listing is in motion (DRHP / board approval)) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 3.6/10 · partial spin-off / listing · 3 filing(s) from NSE, NSE-BM · first 2026-06-28, latest 2026-11-04

> **Listing:** IPO / listing of the subsidiary in motion since 2026-06-28; date not fixed — No new listing; REC is to be "dissolved without being wound up" and PFC issues Consideration Shares; management said on May 13, 2026 "We are targeting for the merged entity to come into existence by 1st of April 2027"; NSE observation letter dated October 19, 2026 valid six months for filing with NCLT

**The stages, as filed:** announced (2026-06-28) → exchange_noc (2026-10-19)

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Nothing separated; documents describe merger by absorption of REC Limited into Power Finance Corporation Limited — class `regulatory_strategic`.

- *Insiders:* PFC holds 52.63% of REC since 2019; Government of India to retain control and merged entity's "Government Company" status, possibly via capital infusion; GoI stake would fall to 41%-42% on plain swap
- *What it reveals:* Swap of 88 PFC shares per 100 REC shares; consolidated loan book INR 11.64 lakh crore, consolidated PAT INR 33,625 crore, net NPA 0.13%, leverage 7.7x-7.8x; group borrowing exposure limit drops from 25% to 20%
- *Selling pressure:* unclear — Documents state REC dissolves and its shareholders receive PFC shares, but say nothing about index exclusion or shareholder flows
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* The draft Scheme's valuation report and Para 25(1) pre-conditions in the NCLT shareholder notice
- *In their words:* “We are targeting for the merged entity to come into existence by 1st of April 2027.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

These documents describe no separation at all: the only restructuring in them is the opposite — a merger by absorption of REC Limited (a 52.63% PFC subsidiary since the 2019 acquisition) into PFC, announced by the Hon'ble Finance Minister in the Union Budget of 1 February 2026 "to achieve scale and improve efficiency in the Public Sector NBFCs, as a first step", and given in-principle board approval at both companies on 6 February 2026. Management's stated reasoning is that funding the power sector toward "Viksit Bharat 2047" needs one institution rather than two near-identical lenders: CMD Parminder Chopra said a unified institution unlocks "better scale, strong capital efficiency, faster decision-making, deeper sector reach and larger financing capabilities" and will be "a single window financing partner for India's power sector", adding that integration is easy because both have very similar business models, regulatory frameworks, and already-aligned lending, pricing, accounting and operational policies. The scale cited on the May 2026 call: consolidated loan book ~INR 11.64 lakh crore (largest NBFC book in India), renewable book INR 1.65 lakh crore, consolidated PAT INR 33,625 crore, consolidated net NPA ~0.13%; PFC standalone FY26 PAT INR 20,051 crore (+16%), net worth past INR 1 lakh crore, CRAR 23.44% with Tier-1 21.93%, standalone book ~INR 5.8 lakh crore growing only 7% against 10-11% guidance because banks aggressively refinanced commissioned assets — and the 12 February 2026 filing says the merged entity "would be positioned as the largest power sector financer in India" with better balance-sheet strength, capital efficiencies and operational synergies, plus stronger technical capability for green hydrogen, CCUS, small modular nuclear reactors and storage. The problems named: two lean teams duplicating work ("we are just 520 and so is the number for the REC", ~1,000 combined, with two people looking at the same account, to be redeployed into monitoring, relationship management, compliance, GIFT City and REC's regional offices); the hold-co discount and an underpriced stock, raised by an investor in May 2024; and the unfinished "logical conclusion" of the 2019 acquisition. It was asked for by the Government of India as majority shareholder — through the Budget, with cabinet and presidential approval required under PFC's Articles — and earlier pressed by minority investors on valuation grounds; lenders and partners are not cited as requesters. Management openly conceded two costs: bank borrowing capacity shrinks because the exposure cap moves from the 25% group limit (itself down from 20%+20% pre-2019) to a 20% single-entity limit, which they argue is manageable given the top-ten banks' aggregate Tier-1 of ~INR 18 lakh crore and a borrowing mix of ~57% domestic bonds, 25% foreign currency, 18% bank/FI; and a plain share swap takes Government holding to ~41-42%, below the Companies Act 50% line, which the Government has committed to cure — possibly by issuing securities to or infusing capital from the Centre — so the merged entity stays a "Government Company". The only genuine business separations in the record are never discussed on any call: PFC Consulting builds transmission SPVs and sells each to the TBCB-winning bidder (e.g. Jam Khambhaliya REZ at INR 19.22 crore, Kakinada I at INR 20.51 crore, Kurnool IV REZ at INR 20.94 crore), a mandated bid-process-coordinator mechanic, not a strategic de-merger.

**How it evolved:** The idea first surfaced only as an investor complaint at the 15 May 2024 investor meet, where a shareholder asked how the Government could be influenced to consolidate given the hold-co discount, and the CMD replied that the merger had always been the logical conclusion of the 2019 acquisition but was put on the back burner by COVID and other Government priorities, pending the majority shareholder's direction; the Nov 2024, Feb 2025, May 2025 and Nov 2025 calls contain no mention of it at all. It became policy with the Finance Minister's Budget announcement of 1 February 2026, a BSE/NSE clarification on 3 February, in-principle board approvals on 6 February and a detailed synergy/exposure note on 12 February 2026. By the 13 May 2026 call the plan had hardened into a merger (not some other restructuring) with legal, transaction, merchant-banking and valuation advisers appointed, a target vesting date of 1 April 2027, and open questions on valuation, the draft scheme, Government-company status and manpower. Execution then proceeded step by step: the Board reserved the proposal for the President on 16 May 2026, presidential approval came 10 June 2026, the Board approved the scheme and the 88:100 PFC:REC share-exchange ratio on 28 June 2026, RBI's no-objection arrived 15 October 2026 and the BSE/NSE observation letters on 19 October 2026, SEBI's clearance being conditional on the RBI approval and settlement of outstanding dues.

**What management expects from it:** No separation is expected; the merger is expected to produce one lender with ~INR 11.64 lakh crore book and INR 33,625 crore PAT, the largest power financier, with better scale, capital efficiency, faster decisions, operational synergies, deeper reach for emerging technologies, redeployed manpower, dividends on merged profit, and (per investors) removal of the hold-co discount. Borrowing cap narrows 25%-to-20%.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The restructuring originates in the Union Budget of 1 February 2026 (para 43), where the Finance Minister framed it as a scale-and-efficiency measure for public sector NBFCs, and PFC's board took it on record and gave in-principle approval to a merger on 6 February 2026. “In order to achieve scale and improve efficiency in the Public Sector NBFCs, as a first step, it is proposed to restructure the Power Finance Corporation and Rural Electrification Corporation.”
- *CALL May 2026* — Chopra's core rationale: one institution rather than two for the power sector's capital needs on the road to Viksit Bharat 2047, built on PFC's existing 52.63% REC stake from 2019. “A unified institution will help unlock better scale, strong capital efficiency, faster decision-making, deeper sector reach and larger financing capabilities.”
- *CALL May 2026* — The positioning objective for the combined lender is to be the sector's one-stop financier. “The combined entity will be positioned as a single window financing partner for India's power sector.”
- *CALL May 2026* — Integration risk is downplayed because the two businesses are already near-identical in model, regulation and policy, so the merger is presented as a formality over an existing alignment. “Over the last few years, we have aligned many of our policies across lending, pricing, accounting and operational processes.”
- *CALL May 2026* — Timeline and approval set: vesting targeted for 1 April 2027 subject to MCA, RBI, SEBI, cabinet and presidential approval, with legal, transaction, merchant-banking and valuation advisers already appointed. “We are targeting for the merged entity to come into existence by 1st of April 2027.”
- *CALL May 2026* — Asked by Nomura's Shreya about 600-700 overlapping employees on each side, Chopra said no portfolio-level plan existed yet, and that the ~1,000 combined staff would be redeployed into monitoring, relationship management, compliance, GIFT City and REC's regional offices rather than cut. “So, we are just 1000 employees and looking at the portfolio.”
- *CALL May 2026* — Piran Engineer (CLSA) pressed on the Government-company test: a plain swap takes Government holding to ~41-42%, below the Companies Act 50% line. “But the Government has committed that they are going to maintain the status of the merged entity as the government Company.”
- *CALL May 2026* — The acknowledged cost of merging is a tighter borrowing cap — from a 25% group limit (itself reduced from 20%+20% before the 2019 acquisition) down to a 20% single-entity limit — which Chopra argued is absorbable given rising bank net worth and limited current utilisation. “And now if from the two entities the merged entity comes into picture, the borrowing limit is going to reduce from 25% to 20%.”
- *CALL May 2026* — Scale credentials cited alongside the restructuring: largest NBFC loan book and highest NBFC profit, with very low NPAs after resolving Sinnar Thermal (INR 3,001 crore, 42% principal recovered, ~INR 670 crore write-back) and TRN Energy (INR 1,139 crore, ~INR 160 crore reversal). “With this size, balance sheet strength and sector experience, we believe that PFC and REC restructuring will create a financial institution of significant scale and strategic relevance.”
- *CALL May 2026* — On dividends post-merger, Chopra noted the present leakage — REC's dividend enters PFC's profit and only 30% of that flows out, so investors effectively get ~9% of it — and said the merged entity will declare 30% of merged profit under the DIPAM policy, subject to RBI's NBFC dividend norms. “And once the merged entity is there profitability of both the companies are there.”
- *CALL May 2024* — Shareholder Manoj Chandani asked the Government nominee director to influence the majority shareholder toward consolidation, arguing the largest NBFC was undervalued at ~7x PE and low price-to-book because of cross-holding between two companies. “On the consolidation front, yes, there is an issue of hold co discount and how you are seeing that the stock is underpriced.”
- *CALL May 2024* — Chopra answered on the nominee director's behalf that merger was always the intended end-state of the 2019 REC acquisition, shelved by COVID and other Government priorities, and that PFC was awaiting the majority shareholder's direction — two years before the Budget announcement delivered exactly that. “You know, at that time of acquisition, the intent, the logical conclusion for the acquisition was the merger of the two companies.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No separation was ever proposed, so no separation rationale exists. Unexplained: valuation basis for 88:100, how Government stake returns above 50%, cost-synergy or ROE quantification, employee restructuring.

## TATATECH — Tata Technologies Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a scheme of arrangement whose nature the documents on file do not settle) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 3.6/10 · scheme (nature unclear) · 1 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-01-16, latest 2026-01-16

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; indicated timeline: Scheme "approved by the Hon'ble National Company Law Tribunal, Mumbai Bench, effective October 1, 2025", resulting in two separate listed companies for CV and PV (stated in results filed January 16, 2026)

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Holding company Tata Motors' Commercial Vehicle business undertaking, demerged into TML Commercial Vehicles Limited — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* not stated
- *What it reveals:* Tata Technologies did the enterprise-application work enabling both companies to stand alone; management calls the split "accretive and positive," expecting accelerated new-product investment at both PV and CV (CV reinforced by the impending Iveco acquisition)
- *Selling pressure:* unclear — Documents give no deal size, shareholding, index or shareholder-reaction detail for either resulting company
- *Parent or spin:* unclear · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Tata Motors / TML Commercial Vehicles scheme and listing filings; Tata Tech's anchor-account share of services revenue (48.9% in Q1 FY27)
- *In their words:* “Pursuant to the Composite Scheme of Arrangement approved by the Hon'ble National Company Law Tribunal, Mumbai Bench, effective October 1, 2025, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicle Limited (formerly Tata Motors Limited) is the Holding Company of Tata Technologies Ltd.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

On these texts alone, Tata Technologies Ltd. is not separating any business of its own — no demerger, spin-off, slump sale, carve-out or segment separation of TATATECH is proposed, discussed or filed in the three years of calls or in the filing. The only separation documented is at its parent: the filing of 2026-01-16 records that Tata Motors Limited (now Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited), 'the Holding Company of Tata Technologies Ltd', approved at its board meeting of August 1, 2024 a Composite Scheme of Arrangement demerging its Commercial Vehicle business undertaking into TML Commercial Vehicles Limited and merging erstwhile Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited into the listed TML, 'thereby resulting in two separate listed companies for the CV and Passenger Vehicle businesses'; the NCLT Mumbai Bench approved it and it took effect October 1, 2025, after which Tata Motors Passenger Vehicle Limited became TATATECH's holding company. Management's only commentary on it came on the Jan 2026 call in answer to an investor (Venkata Siva Ram) who asked 'how Tata Tech is seeing demerger of Tata Motors?' — Warren Harris said TATATECH was 'very instrumental in enabling the 2 organizations to separate', having been 'responsible at Tata Motors for a lot of their enterprise applications' and having done 'much of the work to enable both companies to stand alone and manage their operations independently'. So TATATECH is the vendor to the separation, not its subject: the rationale, problems solved and requesting parties for the CV/PV split are never explained in these texts, only the fact of it, its effective date and its effect on TATATECH's demand. Harris framed the outcome commercially — prospects for both CV and PV 'are strong', CV 'reinforced by the impending acquisition of Iveco', and 'the impact for us, we expect to be accretive and positive'. Everything TATATECH itself did over these 36 months runs the other way — adding businesses, not separating them: acquiring ES-TEC (€51.4m fixed plus up to €14.6m variable, ~300+ engineers, VW access), scaling the BMW TechWorks JV past 2,000 engineers, and explicitly refusing to diversify or restructure its own Services / Technology Solutions mix ('we're not looking to diversify into other industry verticals', May 2026).

**How it evolved:** Nothing on any TATATECH separation appears in Feb 2025, Apr 2025, Jul 2025 or Oct 2025. The parent's scheme, board-approved August 1, 2024, surfaces in these materials only via the Jan 2026 filing (NCLT-approved, effective October 1, 2025, changing TATATECH's holding company) and, the same day, on the Jan 2026 call, where it is raised by a retail investor rather than by management and answered as a delivery credential plus a demand tailwind (Iveco integration, accretive impact). It is not mentioned again in May 2026 or Jul 2026, where the strategic narrative is the opposite — ES-TEC integration, BMW JV scaling, full-vehicle and Tenneco wins, and an explicit decision to stay in Automotive/IHM/Aerospace.

**What management expects from it:** Only for the parent's split: two separately listed CV and PV companies able to 'stand alone and manage their operations independently'. For TATATECH itself, management expects demand, not structure — growth with both Tata Motors CV and PV, CV reinforced by the Iveco acquisition and integration/synergy work, and an effect that is 'accretive and positive'. No margin, capital, valuation or focus claims were made for either entity.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The only separation in the record is the parent's: Tata Motors' board approved on August 1, 2024 a Composite Scheme demerging the Commercial Vehicle undertaking into TML Commercial Vehicles Limited and merging erstwhile TMPV into listed TML, creating two separate listed companies for CV and PV. No rationale is given in the filing. “Tata Motors Limited ("presently known as Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited) ("TML"), the Holding Company of Tata Technologies Ltd, at its Board of Directors meeting held on August 1, 2024, approved a Composite Scheme of Arrangement involving the demerger of its Commercial Vehicle ("CV") business undertaking into TML Commercial Vehicles Limited and the merger of erstwhile Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited with the existing listed company TML thereby resulting in two separate listed companies for the CV and Passenger Vehicle businesses.”
- *Scheme* — The scheme was approved by the NCLT Mumbai Bench and became effective October 1, 2025, changing TATATECH's own holding company to Tata Motors Passenger Vehicle Limited — the only direct structural consequence for TATATECH disclosed anywhere in these texts. “Pursuant to the Composite Scheme of Arrangement approved by the Hon'ble National Company Law Tribunal, Mumbai Bench, effective October 1, 2025, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicle Limited (formerly Tata Motors Limited) is the Holding Company of Tata Technologies Ltd.”
- *[Jan 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=c279cb4f-e386-4a6e-9057-b385f4793186.pdf)* — Asked by an investor how Tata Tech sees the Tata Motors demerger, Harris positioned TATATECH as the enabler of the split rather than a party to it, citing its ownership of much of Tata Motors' enterprise application estate. “So as far as the CV and PV split is concerned, you'll not be surprised to hear that we were very instrumental in enabling the 2 organizations to separate.”
- *[Jan 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=c279cb4f-e386-4a6e-9057-b385f4793186.pdf)* — He specified the work content: separating the enterprise systems so each of CV and PV could operate as an independent, standalone company — a systems-decoupling mandate, with no stated problem the split solves for either parent business. “We've been responsible at Tata Motors for a lot of their enterprise applications. And we did much of the work to enable both companies to stand alone and manage their operations independently.”
- *[Jan 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=c279cb4f-e386-4a6e-9057-b385f4793186.pdf)* — The only 'expected effect' management quantified was commercial and for itself: growth from both post-split entities, with CV demand reinforced by Tata Motors CV's pending Iveco acquisition and the integration/synergy work that follows. “I think on the CV side of things, that will be reinforced by the impending acquisition of Iveco.”
- *[Jan 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=c279cb4f-e386-4a6e-9057-b385f4793186.pdf)* — Net effect on TATATECH from the parent's separation was characterised in one line, with no revenue, margin or concentration numbers attached. “So, the impact for us, we expect to be accretive and positive.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=dc5682bc-d973-4cc7-97fc-4984cf9dfadb.pdf)* — Directly contrary to any TATATECH separation thesis: asked about standing up new verticals, management said it is deliberately NOT splitting or diversifying its own portfolio, arguing concentration on Automotive, IHM and Aerospace makes it more relevant and faster-growing. “And so, in the short -term, we are going to stay very focused, laser -sharp in terms of our focus upon those industry verticals.”
- *[Jul 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=6d7a6276-2a56-41b9-866c-871b440938df.pdf)* — The structural actions TATATECH describes are additive, not separative — Es-Tec integration and cross-selling into VW and BMW, plus a $100m Tenneco transformation deal; the Services (~78%) and Technology Solutions (~22%) segments are managed together, with mix effects (Services gross margin +120bps vs Technology Solutions -250bps) discussed as internal mix, never as a case for separation. “Services remains the core engine of our business, representing approximately 78% of total revenue.”

*Not explained on the calls:* Everything: no TATATECH separation exists here. The parent's split lacks any stated rationale, problem solved, requesting party, financials, valuation, capital or lender/partner involvement.
