> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** not stated — no demerger or separation of any business is described in these documents — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* ESOP 2026: 25,918,613 options, 6.25% of fully diluted capital, floor price INR 325; Umang Vohra appointed Chairman and Group CEO for 5 years from 1 May 2026.
- *What it reveals:* No separation disclosed. Documents instead reveal FY26 revenue INR22.68 billion down ~13%, adjusted EBITDA margin 21% vs standalone 24.6%, destocking impact INR260 crore, and a full leadership change.
- *Selling pressure:* unclear — not stated — no demerger, record date, share entitlement or index change is mentioned in the documents
- *Parent or spin:* neither · *option pricing date:* 27 April 2026 (average market price over the last 21 trading days prior to Board approval of ESOP 2026 on 27 April 2026)
- *Read next:* The postal ballot notice for ESOP 2026 and Mr. Vohra's appointment terms, plus the ESOP 2023 outstanding-grant cap.
- *In their words:* “The exercise price per option shall be decided by the Board/ Nomination and Remuneration Committee at its sole discretion as on the date of grant but shall not be less than INR 325 per share (which is a 2.5% discount to the average market price of the shares of the Company over the last 21 (twenty- one) trading days prior to the approval of ESOP 2026 by the Board on 27 April 2026).”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

On the evidence of these texts alone, Cohance Lifesciences is NOT separating a business: across the nine supplied transcripts (Dec 2024 through May 2026) and the one supplied filing (Board outcome, 27 April 2026) there is no demerger, spin-off, slump sale, scheme of arrangement, carve-out or divestiture of any segment — the corporate action running through this period is the opposite, consolidation. The company merged Cohance into Suven Pharmaceuticals (shareholder approval 99.99%, NCLT hearing 18 Feb 2025, 38.11 crore shares outstanding post-merger, rebranded Cohance in May 2025) and bought capability rather than shedding it: Sapala Organics (oligonucleotides, consolidated from 11 July 2024) and NJ Bio of Princeton NJ (ADCs — 56% stake, ~US$100m pre-money equity value, US$64.4m outlay of which US$49.4m secondary and US$15m primary, on US$32m revenue growing at ~70% CAGR, with call/put on the balance after 5 years), with Himanshu Agarwal stating 'inorganic growth is a core part of our thesis' and Vivek Sharma saying 'our hope is that we don't end at six. We keep adding more.' The only 'separation' management actually describes is organisational, not legal: three distinct business verticals — Pharma CDMO (Yann D'Herve), API+ (Gunjan Singh) and Specialty Chemicals (Amrit Singh) — each given full operational ownership and P&L accountability reporting directly to the Executive Chairman, approved by the Board alongside MD Dr Prasada Raju's resignation and disclosed on the 28 October 2025 update call. The problems that restructuring was said to solve were internal, not structural: a 'multi-business portfolio and expanding global footprint', six formerly family-owned businesses welded into one needing 'greater agility, faster execution, and deeper accountability', and getting to the US$1bn/2030 vision faster; Vivek Sharma explicitly denied there had been any overlap problem at the top ('There was no such thought process that there was an overlap of responsibility'). It was board- and management-driven — no investor, lender or partner is recorded as asking for it; the only investor pressure on record is Varun Bang of Bandhan Life attacking Advent's stewardship ('execution discipline seems to have collapsed') and Chirag Shah of White Pine asking for governance and selective-information-flow fixes, neither of which asked for a separation. The numbers an investor might build a separation case from are disclosed but never framed that way by management: consolidated FY26 EBITDA margin of 21% versus 24.6% standalone (9M FY26: 21% vs 24%; Q3 FY26: 15.5% vs ~19%), i.e. a 4–5% drag Himanshu attributes to first-year NJ Bio consolidation and subsidiary losses in the biotech funding winter, plus INR260 crore of destocking in two large commercial molecules and INR55 crore (INR610 million FY26) lost at the Nacharam formulation site after its OAI and warning letter — and management's answer to all of it is remediation and recovery, with Yann saying NJ Bio needs 'a little bit more than two years to get back to this level', not a sale or demerger.

**How it evolved:** The idea never surfaces: no call in the supplied window raises separating, demerging or selling a segment. The structural idea that does evolve is the opposite — segmentation into three reporting engines (Pharma CDMO, Specialty Chemicals, API+) described as 'engines of growth' from the Feb 2025 and Jun 2025 calls, hardened on 28 October 2025 (filed 1 Nov 2025) into three business-unit CEOs with full P&L authority reporting to Executive Chairman Vivek Sharma plus a platform COO, restated on the 12 November 2025 and 12 February 2026 calls, and then carried into a leadership handover rather than a split: the 27 April 2026 filing records Sharma's resignation effective 30 April 2026 (staying nine months as Special Advisor) and Umang Vohra's appointment as Chairman and Group CEO, who on his first call (12 May 2026) promised only 'a strategic blueprint for growth and sustainable value creation' by fiscal year end — explicitly declining to say whether tough decisions were coming ('I do not know if we are at a point where we will make tough decisions at this stage'). If a separation exists, it is in the six older calls omitted for length or in filings not supplied here.

**What management expects from it:** Nothing — no separation benefits are claimed anywhere in these texts. For the three-vertical reorganisation they claimed only agility, faster execution, deeper accountability, full P&L ownership per CEO, and faster progress toward US$1bn revenue by 2030 with mid-30s EBITDA margins. Margin recovery is pledged via volume, mix and operating leverage within the single consolidated platform, not via separation.

- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=af10d29e-7173-4207-9ccf-86a033601f6e.pdf)* — The stated purpose of that restructuring was speed and accountability inside one company, with the three business-unit leaders given full P&L ownership reporting to the Executive Chairman. “This new structure is designed to bring greater agility, faster execution, and deeper accountability across our businesses.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=af10d29e-7173-4207-9ccf-86a033601f6e.pdf)* — Operational ownership was pushed down to the three vertical CEOs — Yann D'Herve (Pharma CDMO), Gunjan Singh (API+), Amrit Singh (Specialty Chemicals) — with CFO Himanshu Agarwal joining the Board; no entity was carved out. “These business unit leaders have full operational ownership and accountability will henceforth report directly to me.”

## ENDURANCE — Endurance Technologies Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a scheme of arrangement whose nature the documents on file do not settle) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 3.3/10 · scheme (nature unclear) · 1 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-06-24, latest 2026-06-24

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**Stated in the filings:** size hint: 0.48% of net worth.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Veicoli Srl, Italy — fleet-management software platform business, sold 100% for cash to a third party — class `unrelated`.

- *Insiders:* Not stated for promoters/management; documents state buyer Banyan Software UK Limited "does not belong to the promoter / promoter group / group companies of the Company" and transaction is not a related party transaction.
- *What it reveals:* Tiny, non-core unit: income Rs 32.58 crore (0.22% of consolidated income), net worth Rs 3.15 crore (0.48%). Fixed consideration of EUR 2.5 million plus earn-out capped at EUR 5.0 million is a large multiple of that book net worth.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — Outright cash share sale to a third party; no shares distributed to Endurance shareholders, no new listed entity, immaterial size.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Q1 FY27 consolidated results for the gain on sale, deconsolidation of Veicoli and earn-out accounting.
- *In their words:* “Veicoli is a step-down wholly-owned subsidiary of EOSpA and is engaged in the business of providing software platforms to companies operating in fleet management sector.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The business being separated is not a manufacturing division but a non-core software unit: on 23 June 2026 Endurance Overseas SpA, Italy (a wholly-owned subsidiary) signed a Share Purchase Agreement to sell 100% of Veicoli Srl, Italy — a step-down wholly-owned subsidiary 'engaged in the business of providing software platforms to companies operating in fleet management sector' — to Banyan Software UK Limited, an unrelated buyer, with completion expected 1 July 2026. The single reason management put on record is portfolio/resource focus: the decision was taken 'considering the Endurance Group's strategic focus on allocating resources towards the continued growth and development of its core auto components business.' The unit is immaterial to the group: FY2025-26 total income of Rs 32.58 crore, 0.22% of consolidated total income (consolidated FY26 total income was Rs 14,720 crore), and net worth of Rs 3.15 crore at 31 March 2026, 0.48% of consolidated net worth. Consideration is an upfront fixed €2.2 million, deferred fixed €0.3 million, and an earn-out linked to the first three years' financial results capped at €5.0 million, subject to cash and debt adjustments; the filing states the disposal is outside any scheme of arrangement and that 'there is no corporate restructuring or any other event where a scheme of arrangement needs to be filed.' The competing claim on resources is visible in the calls: India capex of roughly Rs 800 crores in FY26 versus Rs 600 crores in FY25 with FY27 'similar', four greenfield plants (AURIC Shendra castings, AURIC Bidkin alloy wheels, the Talegaon battery-pack plant, the Chennai brakes plant), a 12 lakh-unit ABS line addition on top of 6.4 lakh, a fifth aluminium forging press, plus €38 million paid for 60% of Stöferle and about €38 million of Europe capex in FY26. Management's own stated capital rule on 13 February 2026 was that M&A would be 'mainly in our existing areas' and that 'our investments will be in profitable growth products, mainly' — a fleet-management software platform fits neither. The direction of travel in Europe over the same period was consolidation of the auto entities rather than diversification: Endurance Engineering Srl and Endurance SpA were merged into Endurance Castings SpA effective 1 January 2026 (appointed date 1 April 2025), with the surviving company renamed Endurance SpA. No problem, lender, partner or investor request was named anywhere — no analyst asked about Veicoli in any of the seven transcripts, and the only problem the separation is said to solve is where the group's resources go.

**How it evolved:** The separation never surfaced on any earnings call in the window — Nov 2024 through 15 May 2026 transcripts contain no mention of Veicoli, fleet-management software, or any divestment. The only visible precursor is the European entity simplification intimated 31 July 2025 and completed effective 1 January 2026 (Endurance Engineering Srl and Endurance SpA merged into Endurance Castings SpA), alongside the 13 February 2026 call where Jain framed all M&A as 'mainly in our existing areas' and capex as going to 'profitable growth products'. The 15 May 2026 call, five weeks before signing, gave no hint; the SPA was signed 23 June 2026 and disclosed 24 June 2026 as a Regulation 30 sale, expressly outside a scheme of arrangement.

**What management expects from it:** Stated only as resource reallocation: proceeds and management attention move to the core auto components business. Endurance receives €2.2m upfront, €0.3m deferred and up to €5m earn-out. Veicoli ceases to be a subsidiary from completion. No margin, capital-employed, ROCE, focus or valuation benefit is quantified or even claimed for either entity.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The divested entity is identified as a fleet-management software business held two levels down under Endurance Overseas SpA, Italy — i.e. outside the auto-component product range described in every call. “Veicoli is a step-down wholly-owned subsidiary of EOSpA and is engaged in the business of providing software platforms to companies operating in fleet management sector.”
- *Scheme* — The stated rationale is entirely resource allocation toward the core auto components business; no operational problem, loss, dispute or third-party demand is cited. “Considering the Endurance Group's strategic focus on allocating resources towards the continued growth and development of its core auto components business, it has been decided to divest the Group's investment in Veicoli.”
- *Scheme* — Materiality disclosed is tiny — 0.22% of consolidated total income and 0.48% of consolidated net worth — against FY26 consolidated total income of Rs 14,720 crores reported on the May 2026 call. “Total income of Veicoli Srl for the financial year 2025-26 is Rs. 32.58 crore, which is 0.22% of consolidated total income of the Company.”
- *Scheme* — Price is mostly contingent: €2.2 million upfront, €0.3 million deferred, and up to €5.0 million of earn-out over three post-completion years, subject to cash and debt adjustments; buyer is Banyan Software UK Limited, not a related party. “Earn out consideration linked to financial results for the first three years after completion, subject to a cap of € 5.0 million.”
- *Scheme* — The company expressly denies this is a corporate restructuring — it is a straight share sale, not a demerger or court-approved scheme, and not a slump sale. “Yes. There is no corporate restructuring or any other event where a scheme of arrangement needs to be filed.”
- *Scheme* — In parallel the Italian auto entities were being consolidated, not diversified: two step-down subsidiaries merged into one, renamed Endurance SpA, with retrospective appointed date. “Effective Date of the merger is 1st January, 2026 with appointed date being 1st April, 2025.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=7527d629-9f2b-485b-b785-822b5cc98150.pdf)* — Jain defined the group's M&A and capital-deployment boundary as existing product areas with higher margins and a clear target market — the implicit test Veicoli fails. “See, firstly the M&A strategy will be mainly in our existing areas - like we have done, for example in the solar business.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=7527d629-9f2b-485b-b785-822b5cc98150.pdf)* — On the FY27 capex plan Jain said investment would be steered to profitable growth products, citing that over two-thirds of the Rs 930 crores order win was 4W castings and solar dampers at 'much higher margin'. “Our investments will be in profitable growth products, mainly.”

## GESHIP — Great Eastern Shipping Co. Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a scheme of arrangement whose nature the documents on file do not settle) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 3.3/10 · scheme (nature unclear) · 1 filing(s) from NSE · first 2025-12-22, latest 2025-12-22

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** No demerger; only voluntary liquidation and dissolution of Greatship Oilfield Services Limited, a dormant second-tier wholly owned subsidiary — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* No new entity; promoter and promoter group hold 4,29,36,248 shares (30.07%), rising to 31.37% post-buyback, and are barred from participating in the buyback
- *What it reveals:* Nothing unlocked: GOSL had Nil revenue and net worth of Rs 17.73 lakhs. Parent is net cash over $500 million, standalone NAV INR 1,422 per share, trading at 0.8x consolidated NAV
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — No new shares or listed entity created; GOSL had Nil revenue and ceased to exist on dissolution
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Greatship (India) Limited's offshore segment accounts and the INR 392 crore inter-company loan plus INR 272 crore preference shares
- *In their words:* “We now wish to inform you that National Company Law Tribunal has passed an order for the dissolution of GOSL.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

These texts describe no separation, demerger, spin-off, slump sale or scheme of arrangement of any GESHIP business — the premise is not supported by the record supplied. The only corporate actions disclosed are (a) a ₹900 crore open-market buyback of up to an indicative 58,82,352 equity shares (4.12% of paid-up capital) at a maximum ₹1,530/share, approved by the Board on August 27, 2026, opened September 4, 2026, with 20,63,954 shares repurchased by October 7, 2026, and (b) the December 22, 2025 NCLT dissolution of Greatship Oilfield Services Limited, a dormant wholly-owned subsidiary of Greatship (India) Limited with nil revenue and net worth of ₹17.73 lakhs — a shell clean-up, not a business separation. The buyback public announcement affirmatively states there are no pending schemes of amalgamation, compromise or arrangement involving the Company, and that the buyback 'will not result in a change in control or otherwise affect the existing management structure.' The stated reasons for the buyback are capital-allocation, not structural: effectively utilizing available cash (net cash of about $500 million standalone / ₹7,000 crore consolidated, versus ship prices management repeatedly called too high to buy), lifting EPS, book value per share and return on equity by shrinking the equity base, and giving non-promoter shareholders a cash exit option while promoters (30.07%) are barred from participating. Throughout the calls the two businesses — shipping (40 vessels, 3.24 mn dwt) and offshore oilfield services through Greatship (India) Limited (19 vessels, 4 jack-up rigs) — are discussed as continuing parts of one group, with the parent still funding GIL (₹425 crore and ₹65 crore loans, ₹392 crore outstanding at March 31, 2026, plus ₹272 crore of parent-subscribed preference shares being redeemed over four years). Investors on the calls pressed on the 25%-40% discount to NAV and on unlocking value, but management's answer was dividends, buybacks and patience on asset prices — never a separation; it also said it was 'not currently looking to buy any companies and diversify.'

**How it evolved:** No separation idea surfaced in any call. What did evolve is the buyback: Jan 28, 2025 — 'we always evaluate whether we should go for ships or do a buyback... in the immediate future we have no plan'; May 12 and Aug 1, 2025 — 'no discussion around buyback at the board level'; Nov 10, 2025 and Jan 30, 2026 — dividends preferred because they reach every shareholder and buyback tax treatment was 'somewhat unviable'; May 15, 2026 — 'one of the biggest impediments has been removed,' now 'a function of the price'; then the Aug 24/27, 2026 board intimation and approval, Sept 3-4, 2026 commencement, and daily buyback reports through Oct 7, 2026. Separately, the only entity removed from the group was the dormant GOSL (approved April 30, 2025; NCLT dissolution reported December 22, 2025).

**What management expects from it:** Nothing is said about a separated entity, because none is proposed. For the buyback they expect fewer shares outstanding, higher EPS and book value per share, improved return on equity, effective use of surplus cash, long-term shareholder value, no material loss of growth capacity, unchanged control, and public float staying above 25%.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The buyback public announcement (Aug 29, 2026) expressly confirms no scheme of arrangement, amalgamation or compromise involving the Company is pending — i.e. no separation is underway. “there are no pending schemes of amalgamation or compromise or arrangement pursuant to the Companies Act (“Scheme”) involving the Company, and no public announcement of the Buyback shall be made during pendency of any such Scheme;”
- *Scheme* — The same announcement states the transaction leaves the group's structure and control untouched, ruling out a structural separation rationale. “The Buyback of Equity Shares will not result in a change in control or otherwise affect the existing management structure of the Company.”
- *Scheme* — The stated necessity is cash deployment and per-share metrics: ₹900 crore maximum size (7.19% standalone / 6.34% consolidated of paid-up capital plus free reserves), at up to ₹1,530 per share, promoters excluded, minimum ₹675 crore to be deployed. “The Buyback would help to effectively utilize available cash;”
- *Scheme* — The only entity actually exited was Greatship Oilfield Services Limited, a dormant GIL subsidiary with nil revenue and ₹17.73 lakhs net worth, dissolved by NCLT order reported December 22, 2025 — no consideration, no buyer, not a slump sale. “We now wish to inform you that National Company Law Tribunal has passed an order for the dissolution of GOSL.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ceb8c526-89cd-4ec0-b3a2-00258e7fb63b.pdf)* — Asked why not buy back now that buyback taxation had changed, the CFO confirmed the tax impediment was gone but made it purely a price/capital-allocation call, with no mention of any separation. “So, you're right that one of the biggest impediments has been removed.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=4c510083-090a-4e67-a696-b662c6921a10.pdf)* — With ₹7,000 crore consolidated net cash and the stock at a 25-30% discount to NAV, management's chosen value response was dividends, and it framed buyback as a capital-allocation substitute for buying ships — not a structural move. “So, we have chosen dividends because this is something that goes to every shareholder.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=476e1829-179a-4594-a289-3e21c2609667.pdf)* — Asked directly about unlocking value given the discount to NAV, management said no buyback had even been discussed at board level and disclaimed any view on narrowing the valuation gap. “Yes. No, there has been no discussion around buyback at the board level and when we do that there will be all appropriate disclosures.”
- *[Jan 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ce03fee4-ddd3-465d-afe2-3cb1cdf2cbd0.pdf)* — Asked whether the cash pile would be used to acquire companies and diversify, management ruled out corporate-level restructuring and reaffirmed a single-business shipping focus; it also declined bidding for Shipping Corporation of India. “No, we are not currently looking to buy any companies and diversify.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ceb8c526-89cd-4ec0-b3a2-00258e7fb63b.pdf)* — The offshore arm Greatship (India) Limited remained integrated and parent-funded — ₹392 crore of loans outstanding at March 31, 2026 plus ₹272 crore of parent-subscribed preference shares — the opposite of a separation being prepared. “There were 2 loans. One was INR 65 crores and one was INR425 crores.”

*Not explained on the calls:* The calls and filings never mention any separation, demerger, spin-off or listing of the shipping or offshore businesses, so no rationale, numbers, requesters or plan changes exist.

## GODREJIND — Godrej Industries Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a scheme of arrangement whose nature the documents on file do not settle) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 3.3/10 · scheme (nature unclear) · 2 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-01-28, latest 2026-01-28

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**Stated in the filings:** size hint: 7.9% of net worth.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Financial services arm: entire equity stake in Godrej Capital Limited moved under new wholly owned subsidiary Godrej Investment Limited — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* Godrej Investment Limited is a wholly owned subsidiary of GIL; transaction is related-party at arm's length. Promoter stake or incentives in the new entity not stated.
- *What it reveals:* Godrej Capital contributed ₹1,553.80 crore income (7.90%) and ₹3,321.07 crore net worth (32.71%) in FY2025, yet transferred for ₹3,862.69 crore cash — financial services carried above book. GCPL stake (23.23%) is 35.69% of net worth.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — No shares distributed to shareholders and no separate listing stated; GCL merely becomes a step-down subsidiary of GIL.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Board Meeting outcome dated August 13, 2025 and Postal Ballot voting results dated September 29, 2025, for the restructuring rationale.
- *In their words:* “Godrej Investment Limited will carry on the business of financial services.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

On the record available here, GODREJIND's "separation" is the carve-out of its financial services arm, Godrej Capital Limited (GCL) — an NBFC-Core Investment Company (exempt from registration), incorporated September 6, 2019 — out from under the listed company and beneath a newly created, wholly owned intermediate holding company, Godrej Investment Limited (GINVL), incorporated January 5, 2026. GIL transferred its entire 91.11% equity stake in GCL to GINVL on January 28, 2026 for cash consideration of ₹3,862,69,28,016 (≈₹3,862.69 crore), funding GINVL by fully subscribing a rights issue of 3,89,775 equity shares of ₹10 each; GINVL "will carry on the business of financial services" as GCL's holding company. The effect stated in the filings is purely structural: GCL "ceased to be a direct subsidiary (Material Unlisted Subsidiary)" and became a step-down subsidiary, with GINVL as immediate holding company. The scale being ring-fenced is material — in FY25 GCL contributed ₹1,553.80 crore, or 7.90%, of consolidated turnover/revenue/income and ₹3,321.07 crore, or 32.71%, of consolidated net worth. The filings explicitly state the transfer was done outside any scheme: "The transaction is not in accordance with any Scheme of Arrangement. Thus, compliance with Regulation 37A is not applicable," and that it is a related-party transaction on an arm's-length basis with approvals obtained — shareholder approval having been taken by postal ballot (results September 29, 2025) following board approval on August 13, 2025. Separately, GIL continues to monetise its GCPL holding, selling 0.50% in the open market on September 24, 2026 for ₹450.12 crore and retaining 23.23% of an associate that contributes nil consolidated turnover but 35.69% (₹3,989.08 crore) of consolidated net worth. Critically, no management reasoning is present in these documents: no transcripts were supplied ("no transcripts on file"), and the three filings are Regulation 30 intimations that disclose mechanics, dates and amounts only — they state no strategic purpose, no problem being solved, no investor, lender or partner request, and no demerger or listing of the financial services business.

**How it evolved:** The only visible sequence is procedural and comes from cross-references inside the January 28, 2026 filings: the GIL board approved the step on August 13, 2025; shareholders approved it by postal ballot with results declared September 29, 2025; the vehicle GINVL was incorporated January 5, 2026 and intimated to the exchanges on January 6, 2026; and the stake transfer plus the ₹3,862.69 crore rights-issue funding completed on January 28, 2026. The later filing of September 24, 2026 is not a change to that plan but a parallel treasury action — a 0.50% GCPL open-market sale for ₹450.12 crore, taking GIL to 23.23%. Because no earnings call transcripts were provided, there is no call-by-call record of how the idea surfaced, was questioned or was revised; nothing in the supplied texts shows the plan changing from its August 2025 board approval.

**What management expects from it:** Nothing is stated. Across the three filings management gives no expectation for either entity — no commentary on margins, return on capital, debt or fundraising at the NBFC, value unlocking, holding-company discount, management focus, or any future listing of the financial services business. The only articulated outcomes are legal: GINVL becomes GCL's holding company, and GCL becomes a step-down rather than direct subsidiary.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — Filing of January 28, 2026: GIL transferred its entire equity stake in Godrej Capital to newly formed wholly owned subsidiary Godrej Investment Limited, completing the carve-out of the financial services business one level down. “the Company has completed the divestment and transfer of its entire Equity Stake held in Godrej Capital Limited, Subsidiary Company ("GCL"), to Godrej Investment Limited on January 28, 2026.”
- *Scheme* — The stated consequence is structural reclassification only: GCL stops being a direct material unlisted subsidiary of the listed company and becomes a step-down subsidiary under GINVL. “Consequent to the aforesaid transactions, with effect from January 28, 2026, Godrej Capital Limited ceased to be a direct subsidiary (Material Unlisted Subsidiary) of the Company and has become a step-down subsidiary of the Company with Godrej Investment Limited, being the immediate holding Company of GCL.”
- *Scheme* — The only purpose language given for the new entity is that it is a financial services holding company for GCL — the filing's 'objects and impact of acquisition' field offers no further rationale. “Godrej Investment Limited will carry on the business of financial services.  Godrej Investment Limited is the holding Company of Godrej Capital Limited.”
- *Scheme* — Materiality of the business being separated, FY25: GCL contributed 7.90% of consolidated revenue and nearly a third of consolidated net worth. “Turnover/ Revenue/ Income  1,553.80  7.90%  Net Worth  3,321.07  32.71%”
- *Scheme* — Consideration and funding: GIL received ₹3,862.69 crore for the GCL stake and capitalised GINVL by fully subscribing its rights issue — a cash round-trip inside the group. “GIL has further acquired 3,89,775 (Three Lakh Eighty-Nine Thousand Seven Hundred and Seventy-Five) fully paid-up Equity Shares of face value of ₹10/- (Rupees Ten Only) each by way of rights issue done by Godrej Investment Limited and GIL has fully subscribed to it.”
- *Scheme* — It was executed as an arm's-length related-party transfer with approvals, expressly NOT under a scheme of arrangement — so no NCLT-approved demerger or share entitlement to GIL shareholders is disclosed. “The transaction is not in accordance with any Scheme of Arrangement. Thus, compliance with Regulation 37A is not applicable.”
- *Scheme* — Approval trail: board decision August 13, 2025, shareholder postal ballot results September 29, 2025, GINVL incorporation intimated January 6, 2026 — the plan's only visible timeline. “Ref: Outcome of the Board Meeting dated August 13, 2025, Postal Ballot Voting Results dated September 29, 2025, and Intimation dated January 6, 2026”
- *Scheme* — Filing of September 24, 2026: a separate, continuing monetisation of the GCPL associate stake — 0.50% sold in the open market for ₹450.12 crore, leaving 23.23%. “the Company has sold 0.50% of its equity stake in Godrej Consumer Products Limited ("GCPL"), an associate company of the Company, through an open market sale today i.e. on September 24, 2026.”
- *Scheme* — The GCPL holding is pure balance-sheet value, not earnings: nil contribution to consolidated turnover but 35.69% (₹3,989.08 crore) of consolidated net worth as at March 31, 2026. “Contribution in consolidated Net Worth as on March 31, 2026   Percentage - 35.69%   Amount - ₹3989.08 Crore”

*Not explained on the calls:* No transcripts supplied, so no stated 'why': no strategic purpose, capital-raising or regulatory driver, investor/lender/partner demand, valuation or listing intent, timeline, or post-separation financial targets.

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

These texts do not contain any separation, demerger, spin-off or scheme of arrangement by HCL Technologies — the word 'carve-out' appears only on the buy side, where HCLTech is the acquirer of businesses other companies are separating. The two filings provided (both dated 12 January 2026) are the Q3 FY26 un-audited results and the dividend record-date intimation; their only structural notes are Note 4, a definitive agreement signed 18 December 2025 to 'carve-out and acquire' HPE's Telco Solutions Business for ₹1,438 crores ($160 million), including a ₹135 crore ($15 million) performance incentive, to gain IP, product engineering and R&D talent and CSP relationships; and Note 5, a definitive agreement signed 22 December 2025 to carve-out and acquire Jaspersoft from Cloud Software Group for ₹2,157 crores ($240 million) for an embedded analytics/pixel-perfect reporting platform and its developer community. Management framed both as additive — Telco Solutions building on the 2024 HPE CTG acquisition ('which is now growing nicely') to deepen telecom IP, and Jaspersoft/Wobby/Zeenea completing the Actian data-intelligence stack with the missing 'visualize layer' (Jaspersoft closed in early July 2026, guided at $10–15 million revenue per quarter). The only separations discussed as HCLTech's own doing are internal restructuring (a people-and-non-people program costing ~40–50 bps of FY26 margin, 62 bps in Q1 FY27, intended to give 'structural agility' in the AI era), the creation of new subsidiaries rather than divestments (HCLTech Public Sector Solutions in the US, April 2025), discontinuation of some HCL Software products, and walking away from deals worth '$1 billion more' of TCV. Separation appears as a demand theme, not a corporate action: in Oct 2025 CVK cited 'carveout related separation work' at Retail/CPG clients as a revenue pocket. HCLSoftware is described as structurally distinct — 'a dedicated products and platform organization that operates largely independent of the Services business with its own GTM and R&D investments', reported as its own segment with its own ROIC (21.6% in Q1 FY27) and ARR ($1.063 billion) — but no call or filing proposes separating it, and no lender, partner or investor is recorded asking for any separation. The nearest new-entity decision is the July 2026 AI datacenter business: up to ₹3,500 crores, scaling toward 50 MW, possibly funded with partners, equity and debt — but it is described as a new growth vector inside HCLTech, not a carve-out.

**How it evolved:** Jan 2025 (Q3 FY25) is the first structural note: HPE's CTG assets closed 2 December 2024 and HCLSoftware is described as operating 'largely independent' of Services, with no separation proposed. Apr 2025 adds a new subsidiary (HCLTech Public Sector Solutions) and Jul 2025 announces a restructuring program, while Oct 2025 cites clients' own 'carveout related separation work' as a demand pocket. Jan 2026 and the 12 January 2026 filing record HCLTech as the buyer of two carve-outs (HPE Telco Solutions, $160M; Jaspersoft, $240M), Apr 2026 flags both as delayed by US government approvals, and Jul 2026 confirms Jaspersoft closed and CTG-follow-on still pending — never once a separation of HCLTech's own business.

**What management expects from it:** Not applicable — no separation is proposed. For the inbound carve-outs management expects telecom IP, R&D talent and CSP access (HPE Telco Solutions) and a completed data-intelligence stack (Jaspersoft, ~$10–15m revenue/quarter). Restructuring is expected to restore margins toward 17.5–18.5% and give structural agility; software stays a separate segment at ~21.6% ROIC.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — No scheme of arrangement, demerger or separation document is present; both supplied filings dated 12 January 2026 are the Q3 FY26 results and the dividend record-date intimation, whose only structural notes are inbound acquisitions. “On 18 December 2025, the Group has signed a definitive agreement to carve-out and acquire Telco Solutions Business from HPE for ₹ 1,438 crores ($160 million), including ₹ 135 crores ($15 million) incentive payable based on performance.”
- *Scheme* — The second carve-out in the filing is also an acquisition — Jaspersoft from Cloud Software Group for ₹2,157 crores ($240 million) — bought for a BI/reporting platform and its global developer community. “On 22 December 2025, the Group has signed a definitive agreement to carve-out and acquire Jaspersoft, a business unit of CSG providing a leading embedded analytics and pixel-perfect reporting platform, for ₹ 2,157 crores ($240 million).”
- *[Apr 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=48f5d6fd-b499-45da-bc6d-2e0439495ec2.pdf)* — Management explicitly labels both carve-outs as acquisitions excluded from guidance, delayed by the US government shutdown of the approving departments — confirming HCLTech is the buyer, not the seller. “This guidance does not include the two acquisitions, the Telecom Solutions Group from HPE that we announced to carve -out and Jaspersoft.”
- *[Jan 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=08d64f75-ab38-4158-8b8a-0d933bc007d3.pdf)* — CVK positions the HPE Telco Solutions purchase as doubling down on telecom IP, building on the 2024 CTG acquisition, to gain nonlinear growth and new CSP relationships. “This strategic move builds on the momentum from our successful integration of HPE's Communications Technology Group (CTG) , acquired in 2024, which is now growing nicely.”
- *[Oct 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=172ac7e9-7ce4-4c53-9e40-8b70187da3f9.pdf)* — The only 'separation' HCLTech discusses is its clients' — carve-out separation work is named as a pocket of Retail/CPG demand, i.e. a revenue opportunity rather than a corporate action by HCLTech. “A couple of areas where we see this include integration work in M&A , a carveout related separation work , and in large scale SDLC transformation work supported by Generative AI, especially our AI Force platform.”
- *[Jan 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=62047a72-1071-449c-8e13-47d3054a4c7e.pdf)* — HCLSoftware is described as already structurally distinct from Services with its own GTM and R&D, yet no separation of it is proposed on any call; it stays a reported segment with its own ROIC and ARR. “We a s the only Indian service provider are uniquely positioned for the medium to long term with a dedicated products and platform organization that operates largely independent of the Services business with its own GTM and R&D investments.”
- *[Jul 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=70e8e2f8-36ca-4816-9bce-5587cead0c23.pdf)* — The structural action HCLTech did announce is an internal restructuring program across people and facilities for AI-era agility — not a business separation; it cost ~40–50 bps of FY26 margin and 62 bps in Q1 FY27. “We plan to execute a restructuring program , both on people and non -people side during the rest of this fiscal year.”
- *[Apr 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=d64686fb-2ee7-40fc-a0ae-93ecd0dcc725.pdf)* — Corporate structuring in the period created new entities rather than separating existing ones — a dedicated US public-sector subsidiary was established to address government spend. “Further to capitalize on the large spend of public sector , and in line with the strategy to expand our market participation, we recently established HCLTech Public Sector Solutions, a subsidiary dedicated to serving state and local government , and education organizations , as well as federal, civilian and defense agencies in the United States.”
- *[Jul 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=11be9fba-0308-4756-a474-e4f2903fdaac.pdf)* — The newest structural decision is entering the AI datacenter business with up to ₹3,500 crores toward a long-term 50 MW plan, possibly part-funded by partners, equity and debt — a new vector inside HCLTech, explicitly not at the expense of the payout policy. “In this regard, we will make a strategic investment of up to INR3,500 crores and with the potential to scale to 50 megawatts of capacity.”

*Not explained on the calls:* Everything: the texts contain no HCLTech separation — no scheme, rationale, perimeter, ratio, listing plan, timeline, requesting party or entity-level financials exists to reconstruct.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** No demerger in documents; only voluntary strike-off and dissolution of a wholly owned subsidiary — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* not stated
- *What it reveals:* Nothing revealed: the struck-off subsidiary contributed Nil turnover, revenue, income and net worth in the last financial year, with no consideration received and no material impact on Hindalco's operations or financials
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — No shares issued or listed; a nil-revenue subsidiary was dissolved, not demerged to shareholders
- *Parent or spin:* neither · *option pricing date:* not stated

- *In their words:* “Accordingly, East Coast has ceased to be the Company's wholly owned subsidiary, effective June 22, 2026.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

On the evidence of these texts there is no separation, demerger, spin-off or scheme of arrangement at Hindalco to explain: across the five earnings calls (May 2025 through May 2026) management never proposes separating Novelis, the India aluminium, downstream, specialty alumina or copper businesses, and the single filing supplied is not a scheme but a voluntary strike-off of a dormant shell. That filing records that East Coast Bauxite Mining Company Private Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary, was struck off by the Registrar of Companies, Cuttack under Section 248 of the Companies Act, 2013 on its own application, effective June 22, 2026, with turnover/income and net worth contribution stated as 'Nil' and the sale-consideration, buyer, related-party and Regulation 37A/scheme fields all marked 'Not Applicable' precisely because it is a dissolution rather than a disposal; the company states it has no material impact on operations or financial position. The only other separations discussed are operational, not corporate: Novelis idling one of two cast lines in China (management citing smaller low-aluminium-content Chinese vehicles softening long-term auto demand growth to 3%-5%), exiting two North America specialty facilities 'to consolidate capacity and drive higher asset utilisation', a non-binding letter of intent received in early April 2025 to sell the Fairmont property after Novelis had announced closure in late March, and the return/surrender of coal blocks (Kathautia, with a Rs 160 crore impairment of mining rights; Radhikapur East already surrendered; three of four original blocks gone, only IV/4 still run). The nearest thing to an inter-company separation is the opposite direction — an acquisition: Hindalco buying the Essel Mining subsidiary holding Bandha at cost (Rs 48 lakh share capital plus Rs 1,000 crore of debt, c. Rs 2,000 crore paid in FY26, a further c. Rs 4,000 crore capex over a 45-year mine life, 18.5-20 km from Mahan), where Satish Pai said Essel is 'quite happy that we take over the CAPEX' and will stay on only as MDO operator, i.e. ownership of capital separated from mining services. Far from separating Novelis, management repeatedly asserts the group is managed as one pool of capital: AV Minerals raised $800 million at SOFR+105 bps (upsized by $200 million on 10 February 2026) with $750 million injected as equity into Novelis in December 2025, justified by Hindalco's cheaper cost of debt, not wanting Novelis's net debt/EBITDA 'to go too high', worry about 'bond owners' and Novelis's ratings, and the value of 'showing parental support'; on fungibility Pai said 'we look at it as one consolidated. That's how the shareholder will look at it,' and the governing commitment is consolidated net debt/EBITDA at or below 2x (1.02x June 2025, 1.23x September 2025, 1.73x December 2025, 1.83x March 2026) against a $10 billion FY26-FY29 capex plan. The only 'separation' management promises is in disclosure, not legal structure: Pai said specialty alumina would be carved out as a separately reported segment 'sometime next year, just like we have done downstream alumina.' Stated strategy through the May 2026 call is integration and scale — doubling upstream aluminium and copper, a fourfold rise in India downstream EBITDA by FY30, Novelis's '3 by 30' and the $5 billion, 600 KT Bay Minette plant — not disaggregation.

**How it evolved:** No separation idea surfaces at any point: the May 2025 call introduces footprint exits (two North America specialty plants, a China auto finishing line) and the Fairmont letter of intent, plus the inbound Bandha/Essel transfer; the August 2025 call adds the Kathautia coal-block return and its Rs 160 crore write-off. The November 2025 Novelis call reframes the China line idling as strategic (3%-5% auto growth) and introduces the $750 million parent equity infusion, which the November 2025 Hindalco call and the February 2026 call then execute via AV Minerals ($800 million, upsized $200 million on 10 February 2026) while explicitly defending a single consolidated balance sheet. The February 2026 call's only 'separation' is reporting — specialty alumina to be split out, as downstream already was. By the May 2026 call the direction is purely expansionary, and the June 22, 2026 filing is a dormant-subsidiary strike-off, not a scheme of arrangement.

**What management expects from it:** Nothing is claimed for a separation, because none is proposed. For the struck-off subsidiary: no material impact, Nil revenue and net worth. For footprint exits: consolidated capacity and higher asset utilisation at Novelis, supporting the $350-400 million cost programme and $600/t goal. For the group: one consolidated balance sheet at or below 2x net debt/EBITDA funding $10 billion of capex.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The only corporate separation on the record is the voluntary strike-off and dissolution of a dormant wholly owned subsidiary, East Coast Bauxite Mining Company Private Limited, by the RoC Cuttack under Section 248, effective June 22, 2026 — not a demerger of any operating business. “East Coast has ceased to be the Company's wholly owned subsidiary, effective June 22, 2026.”
- *Scheme* — The filing itself rules out a scheme of arrangement, sale, buyer, consideration or related-party angle, answering each field as not applicable because the entity was merely dissolved, and reports its revenue and net worth contribution as Nil. “Not Applicable, since this is the case of voluntary strike-off and consequent dissolution, effective June 22, 2026.”
- *Scheme* — Hindalco states the strike-off changes nothing financially, which is the company's entire stated rationale — there is no value-unlock, focus or valuation argument offered. “These aforesaid action will have no material impact on the operations or financial position of the Company.”
- *CALL May 2025* — The closest thing to a business separation at Novelis is footprint rationalisation: exiting two North America specialty facilities and idling a China auto finishing line, framed as consolidating capacity and lifting asset utilisation, not as separating a business unit. “And exiting two North America specialty facilities to consolidate capacity and drive higher asset utilisation.”
- *CALL May 2025* — Steve Fisher explained Fairmont as a closure that turned into a possible property sale after an unsolicited approach in early April 2025, with closure to proceed over the following months if no agreement was reached. “So, on Fairmont, after announcing that we were moving towards closing the facility in late March, we were approached in early April, we have entered into a non -binding letter of intent to see if we can sell the property.”
- *CALL May 2025* — The Bandha transaction runs the other way — Hindalco takes the Essel Mining subsidiary (Rs 48 lakh share capital plus Rs 1,000 crore debt, c. Rs 4,000 crore further capex, 45-year life, 18.5 km from Mahan) at cost, with Essel separating out of ownership and staying only as mine operator because of the capex burden. “I think for Essel Mining, because of the CAPEX spend and all required, I think that they are quite happy that we take over the CAPEX. And they will continue to be the MDO operator of mine.”
- *CALL Aug 2025* — Asset exits in India are coal-block surrenders rather than business separations: Kathautia is being returned, forcing a Rs 160 crore impairment of mining rights, leaving only IV/4 operating out of the original four blocks. “Kathautia. We are in the process of returning Kathautia. So for that, we had to write off some of the mining rights, et cetera.”
- *CALL Nov 2025* — Steve Fisher gave a demand rationale for idling one of two China cast lines — smaller, lower-priced Chinese vehicles with less aluminium content cutting long-term auto demand growth to 3%-5% — a capacity decision, not a separation. “We estimate this will soften the longer -term aluminum demand growth rate to a range of 3% to 5% and is the strategic rationale behind our decision earlier this year to idle one of two cash lines in China.”
- *CALL Nov 2025* — Pai argued for keeping the group financially integrated — raising debt at AV Minerals and injecting it as equity into Novelis to protect Novelis's leverage, bondholders and ratings and to show parental support — the opposite of separating Novelis. “We have bond owners that we are worried about. We don't want the ratings of Novelis to get negatively impacted.”
- *CALL Nov 2025* — Asked directly whether Hindalco and Novelis are two standalone businesses, Pai confirmed cash is treated as fungible and the group is run and judged on one consolidated net debt/EBITDA (below 2x). “we look at it as one consolidated. That's how the shareholder will look at it.”
- *CALL Nov 2025* — The only 'separation' management commits to is in segment disclosure — specialty alumina (c. 500 KT from Muri and Belgaum, part index-linked, part value-added) to be reported separately from metal-grade Utkal alumina, as downstream already is. “We will start to separate that out sometime next year, just like we have done downstream alumina.”
- *CALL Feb 2026* — The financing step that an investor might mistake for a separation is an intra-group equity injection: AV Minerals, a wholly owned Hindalco subsidiary, raised $800 million at SOFR+105 bps, $750 million of it infused as Novelis equity in December 2025, upsized by $200 million on 10 February 2026 and five years in tenor. “During the quarter, Hindalco's wholly-owned subsidiary, AV Minerals, raised $800 million at SOFR plus 105 basis points.”

*Not explained on the calls:* Everything a separation thesis needs: no demerger, no scheme, no entity split, no listed-entity rationale, no valuation, capital-structure, lender, partner or investor demand for one.

## INDHOTEL — Indian Hotels Co. Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a scheme of arrangement whose nature the documents on file do not settle) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 3.3/10 · scheme (nature unclear) · 4 filing(s) from NSE · first 2025-12-19, latest 2026-08-24

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**Stated in the filings:** size hint: 0.3% of net worth.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** No demerger: IHCL sold its entire 25.52% stake in Taj GVK Hotels & Resorts Limited; Taj name licence terminated — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* No new entity; buyer Ms. Shalini Bhupal is a TajGVK promoter, not IHCL promoter group. IHCL nominee directors stepped down; IHCL holds no shares post-sale.
- *What it reveals:* Separation reveals IHCL keeps the fee stream — ₹25.32 crores FY24-25 management fee, 0.30% of revenue, continuing under Hotel Operating Agreements — while giving up ₹29.09 crores JV profit share; ₹592 crores cash added to a debt-free balance sheet.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — Cash inter-se transfer to a TajGVK promoter; no shares distributed to IHCL shareholders; divested unit was 0.30% of IHCL revenue.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* The Scheme of Arrangement and August 23, 2026 valuation report on IHCL's website; and use of the ₹592 crores TajGVK sale cash
- *In their words:* “The Company would continue to operate the existing portfolio of hotels of the Target Company in accordance with the provisions contained in the respective Hotel Operating Agreements already executed between the Target Company and IHCL.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The premise needs one correction before the reasoning: in these texts IHCL is not separating a business out — it is absorbing one. The only business actually being let go is Taj GVK Hotels & Resorts, where IHCL sold its entire 25.52% (1,60,00,400 shares) at ₹370/share on December 30, 2025, terminated the 2011 Restated Shareholders' Agreement and the 2007 Name & Trademark Licence Agreement, pulled its nominee directors off the board and required Taj GVK to drop 'Taj' from its corporate name — while keeping the Hotel Operating Agreements, so the ₹25.32 crore of annual management fee survives; management framed that as 'recycling capital from ownership into higher return capital light growth' and said it generated ₹592 crore of cash. The structural event of August 24, 2026 is the opposite direction: a Scheme of Arrangement under Sections 230–232 amalgamating Oriental Hotels Limited (OHL, already a 37.05% associate, 7 hotels / 825 rooms, FY26 standalone revenue ₹500.7 crore and net worth ₹480.5 crore) into IHCL (FY26 standalone revenue ₹5,640.16 crore, net worth ₹12,766.95 crore). The stated reasons are: complementary portfolios (OHL is concentrated in Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Karnataka, taking post-merger south-India keys to 2,104 — TN 821, Karnataka 1,002, Kerala 281); giving OHL's business access to IHCL's financial resources and management expertise to fund asset management (added villas and MICE venues at Taj Fisherman's Cove, F&B and Chambers upgrade at Gateway Madurai, full renovation at Vivanta Coimbatore, future expansion at Taj Coromandel); and explicitly 'to reduce the number of operating entities under its holding', eliminating duplication, simplifying the management structure and cutting the cost of maintaining separate entities. The holding-structure cleanup is quantified: IHCL's direct stakes rise to Taj Madurai 52% (26%+26%) and Taj Karnataka 55% (45%+10%) — both becoming operating subsidiaries — plus Taj Kerala 32%, TAL Hotels 49%, St. James Court 88%, Lanka Island Resorts 48% and OHL International (HK) at 100%. The performance gap is the implicit case: FY23–26 CAGR of 19% revenue / 21% EBITDA / 23% PAT(BEI) at IHCL versus 7% / 5% / 8% at OHL. Consideration is all-stock at 25 IHCL shares for every 117 OHL shares (swap 1:4.68), ~2.32 crore net new shares or ~1.6% dilution (net of ~8 lakh IHCL shares held by OHL, which are extinguished), promoter stake moving 38.12% → 37.50%, Appointed Date April 1, 2027 and completion targeted in H2 FY2028, with the deal called EPS accretive from year 1.

**How it evolved:** The OHL merger never surfaced on any of the eight earnings calls in the window — the only precursor is portfolio pruning: on the Feb 12, 2026 call (Q3 FY26) management disclosed the Taj GVK exit for ₹592 crore while retaining the management contracts and described it as 'sharpening the portfolio while strengthening our operating platform', having earlier on the Aug 12, 2025 investor call listed OHL alongside Taj GVK, Banaras Hotels and PM Hotels as listed entities it governs through a 'proper governance structure'. The May 11, 2026 call (Q4 FY26) set up the capacity and the framing — gross liquidity over ₹4,300 crore, zero debt, 68% of the operating portfolio capital-light, and a promise to announce a new Capital Market Day with updated guidance — but named no target. The July 21, 2026 call (Q1 FY27) was silent on structure beyond ₹4,400 crore of gross cash and 'disciplined' capital deployment. The merger appears for the first time in the August 24, 2026 board approval, press release and investor update, where it is positioned under 'Accelerate 2030' as group simplification rather than as anything discussed with analysts beforehand.

**What management expects from it:** For OHL: EBITDA margin from 26.8% to 30%+ on ₹494 crore revenue via IHCL-funded renovations, added villas, MICE and room expansion, plus cost and synergy benefits. For IHCL: 7 hotels and 825 rooms into standalone, 2,104 south-India keys, ~1.6% dilution yet EPS accretive from year one, two new operating subsidiaries, simpler governance, lower overheads, full accounting consolidation.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The scheme's own rationale ties the amalgamation to cutting the number of operating entities IHCL holds, with duplication, management structure and administrative cost as the named problems. “The Scheme is in consonance with the strategy of the Transferee Company to reduce the number of operating entities under its holding, which in turn will lead to elimination of duplication, simpler management structure, better administration, rationalisation of administrative expenses, etc, consequently reducing costs of maintaining separate entities;”
- *Scheme* — Geographic complementarity is the first listed benefit: OHL's seven hotels are concentrated in Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Karnataka, lifting IHCL's south-India operating keys to 2,104. “The Companies are engaged in similar businesses and have complementary portfolios, as the Transferor Company has a significant presence in the states of Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Karnataka.”
- *Scheme* — OHL's constraint is framed as capital and capability, solved by folding it into the larger balance sheet — explicitly including asset management opportunities. “The Scheme shall enable the business of the Transferor Company, by virtue of becoming part of a larger entity, to have access to the financial resources, management experience and expertise of the Transferee Company.”
- *Scheme* — Chhatwal places the merger under Accelerate 2030 and names the three iconic OHL assets whose potential is to be unlocked. “In line with our Accelerate 2030 strategy of creating value, simplifying the group's holding structure and unlocking the full potential of OHL portfolio including iconic assets like Taj Coromandel, Chennai, Taj Fisherman's Cove Resort & Spa, Chennai and Taj Malabar Resort & Spa, Cochin, the Boards of IHCL and OHL have today approved this merger.”
- *Scheme* — The capital argument is that IHCL's balance sheet can fund room additions and product upgrades that OHL on its own could not — the presentation lists added villas and MICE venues at Fisherman's Cove, F&B/Chambers at Gateway Madurai, renovation at Vivanta Coimbatore and expansion at Taj Coromandel. “The merger will drive long-term value creation by leveraging IHCL's strong balance sheet to support strategic investments, including inventory expansion and product enhancements further strengthening the premium positioning of the portfolio.”
- *Scheme* — Dalwani gives the mechanics: an all-stock 25:117 swap (1:4.68), Appointed Date April 1, 2027, completion targeted H2 FY2028; ~2.32 crore net shares issued, about 1.6% dilution, with promoter holding falling 38.12% to 37.50%. “The Scheme of Arrangement proposes a share exchange ratio of 25 IHCL shares for every 117 OHL shares and is an all-stock transaction, with completion targeted in the second half of FY2028 and Appointed Date of April 1, 2027.”
- *Scheme* — The second-order prize is the cross-holding cleanup: IHCL's direct stakes rise to Taj Madurai 52% (26%+26%) and Taj Karnataka 55% (45%+10%), both becoming operating subsidiaries, plus Taj Kerala 32%, TAL Hotels 49%, St. James Court 88%, Lanka Island 48% and OHL International (HK) at 100%. “The merger will further simplify the group's holding structure by increasing IHCL's direct ownership across several entities, resulting in two new operating subsidiaries. This will streamline governance, optimise overheads, enhance operational efficiency, and support our Accelerate 2030 objectives.”
- *Scheme* — OHL minorities (31.48% public; promoter group 68.52%) are offered direct participation in IHCL instead of a stake in a slower-growing associate — OHL's FY23-26 CAGR was 7% revenue / 5% EBITDA / 8% PAT versus IHCL's 19% / 21% / 23%. “The Scheme/ Amalgamation will provide the public shareholders of the Transferor Company with an opportunity to participate directly in the consolidated hospitality business of the Transferee Company through the Consideration Shares proposed to be issued pursuant to the Scheme and they would continue to play a part in the growth of one of India's leading hospitality companies, i.e., the Transferee Company.”
- *Scheme* — OHL's MD frames the ask as coming from the OHL side — its shareholders gaining exposure to IHCL's 17-quarter record run. “The merger of OHL with IHCL will create significant value for OHL shareholders, enabling them to now participate directly in IHCL's growth journey.”
- *Scheme* — The investor update sets the economics: OHL operating revenue ₹440 crore (FY25) to ₹494 crore (FY26), EBITDA ₹110 crore to ₹132 crore, margin 25.0% to 26.8%, targeted post-merger above 30%, with ARR up from ₹10,200 to ₹11,600 and occupancy 71% to 75%. “EPS accretive transaction from year 1”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=685b29d3-5355-4b0c-b42d-b7674636c342.pdf)* — The only actual separation in the window — the Taj GVK exit — was presented as capital recycling out of minority ownership while keeping the fee stream, and a new 250+ room GVK contract in Yelahanka was signed alongside it. “Also, very important is that we have divested our stake in TAJGVK generating INR 592 crores in cash while retaining management contracts for all GVK hotels.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=685b29d3-5355-4b0c-b42d-b7674636c342.pdf)* — Management's own label for the exercise was sharpening ownership while keeping the operating platform — the same logic later used to justify absorbing OHL. “All this reflects disciplined capital allocation, recycling capital from ownership into higher return capital light growth opportunities. In a sense, we are sharpening the portfolio while strengthening our operating platform.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No earnings call ever discussed it; no rupee synergy or capex figure, no basis for the 117:25 ratio, no minority-vote, tax or Taj Kerala treatment detail.

## ITC — ITC Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a filing's text names a demerger; no scheme filing names it yet) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 3.3/10 · spin-off · 5 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-01-29, latest 2026-05-21

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**Stated in the filings:** record date 2026-02-04; appointed date 2025-04-01.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** ITC's Hotels business, distributed to shareholders under a Scheme of Demerger into separately listed ITC Hotels Limited — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* Documents state ITC Limited has no promoter/promoter group; post-demerger ITC Hotels Limited appears among ITC's associates, i.e. a retained equity-method stake. No management shareholding or incentives in the new entity stated.
- *What it reveals:* Separation revealed hotel assets carried far below fair value: FY2025 exceptional items of ₹15,179.43 crores (standalone discontinued operations) and a ₹15,617.37 crores gain on fair valuation of net assets distributed, against only ₹572.52 crores pre-exceptional PBT from hotels; parent retains cash-generative cigarettes.
- *Selling pressure:* likely — Hotels sits outside ITC's three stated business groups (FMCG, Paperboards/Paper & Packaging, Agri); documents disclose no index or shareholder-base detail.
- *Parent or spin:* unclear · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* The Scheme of Demerger of Hotels business, plus ITC Hotels Limited's own results behind ITC's ₹5,288.24 crores equity-method investment.
- *In their words:* “The Company is currently focused on three business groups : FMCG, Paperboards, Paper & Packaging and Agri Business.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

On the documents supplied, the business being separated is ITC's IT services arm, ITC Infotech India Limited (ITCI), a wholly owned subsidiary that is to be carved out of the unlisted group structure and listed on BSE and NSE through a strategic combination with listed Happiest Minds Technologies Limited (31 Aug 2026 filing). The mechanics are two-step: ITCI buys 3,36,61,700 shares (22.106% fully diluted) from promoters Ashok Soota and Ashok Soota Medical Research LLP for ~Rs 1,330 crores cash in two tranches (11.00% at Rs 390/share, 11.106% at Rs 400/share), funded by a Rights Issue of Rs 1,330 crores, after which Happiest Minds amalgamates into ITCI at 25 ITCI shares per 81 Happiest Minds shares (1:3.24) — implying Rs 405/share or Rs 6,167 crores for Happiest Minds and Rs 1,312/share or Rs 11,920 crores for ITCI pre-rights — leaving ITC with ~73.4% and Happiest Minds holders ~26.6%, and ITCI listed. The stated problem it solves is sub-scale: management says '> $1Bn revenue puts provider on the vendor management office radar' and gives the 'Right to Hunt' and 'Right to Win' large deals, so the combination targets US$1 billion revenue by FY28 on a pro-forma basis versus ITCI's FY26 IT services revenue of Rs 4,718 crores (PAT Rs 510 crores adjusted, 18.5% adj. EBITDA margin, 13,000+ employees, 5-yr CAGR 14%) and Happiest Minds' FY26 Rs 2,315.11 crores (FY25 Rs 2,060.84 crores, FY24 Rs 1,624.66 crores, 6,500+ employees, 5-yr CAGR 25%). It also fixes portfolio gaps: Americas mix rises from 27% to 38%, BFSI from 12% to 20%, Build:Run moves to 50:50, and Hi-Tech, EdTech and Healthcare verticals plus 800+ clients and 19,000+ professionals are added, against an industry backdrop of a ~$400 Bn AI-driven TAM by 2030, compression of ~$350 Bn of legacy services, cost-takeout deals at 30-40% savings and vendor consolidation. For ITC shareholders the explicitly stated benefit of separation itself is that it 'Creates a listed IT services platform, enabling independent value discovery and strategic flexibility', alongside ~10% revenue synergies, ~100 bps margin expansion and EPS accretion in the first full year. Nobody is recorded as having demanded it: ITCI's board moved under its own 'Orbit Next' strategy, ITC's board merely 'endorsed' it, and the only external party is the counterparty-seller Ashok Soota, who frames it as Happiest Minds finding 'a welcoming new home'; approvals needed are CCI/anti-trust, stock exchanges/SEBI, shareholders, creditors and NCLT, over ~15 months.

**How it evolved:** No earnings-call transcripts were provided, so the idea is traceable only through filings: ITC had already demerged its Hotels business (visible as discontinued operations with Rs 15,163.06 crores of exceptional items in FY2024-25 and ITC Hotels Limited now an associate), establishing the separation template. The IT separation surfaces fully formed on 31 August 2026, when ITCI's board approved both the 22.106% promoter-stake purchase and the Happiest Minds amalgamation that will list ITCI, endorsed the same day by ITC's board. Housekeeping then followed in the opposite, consolidating direction: on 1 September 2026 step-down subsidiaries Blazeclan Technologies and Cloudlytics were dissolved into ITC Infotech (appointed date 1 October 2024), tidying the entity to be listed, while on 2 November 2026 ITC moved the other way at the parent by absorbing wholly owned Sproutlife Foods (Yoga Bar) to 'reduce the number of operating entities'. The plan's indicative sequencing was set at board approval in Aug'26, Tranche 1 and exchange/SEBI no-objection around Q3FY27-early Q4FY27, shareholder/creditor meetings Mar-Apr'27 and ITCI listing in Q2-Q3 FY28.

**What management expects from it:** ITC Infotech: step change to ~US$1bn revenue by FY28 (from Rs 4,718 crores FY26), Americas mix 27%→38%, BFSI 12%→20%, Build:Run 50:50, ~10% revenue synergies, ~100 bps margin expansion, EPS accretive in year one, 19,000+ people, 800+ clients. ITC: a separately listed IT platform giving independent value discovery and strategic flexibility, while retaining ~73.4%.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The separation vehicle is disclosed in the 31 August 2026 filing: ITC Infotech acquires 22.106% of Happiest Minds for cash and then amalgamates it, with ITCI's own shares to be listed on both Indian exchanges. “The shares of ITC Infotech are proposed to be listed on BSE Limited and the National Stock Exchange of India Limited.”
- *Scheme* — Transaction summary states the listing is the consequence of the merger, not an IPO or a demerger to ITC shareholders; ITC retains ~73.4% and Happiest Minds holders get ~26.6%. “Thereafter, Happiest Minds to merge with ITC Infotech pursuant to which ITC Infotech will be listed”
- *Scheme* — The value-creation case for ITC shareholders names independent price discovery as a benefit of having the IT business separately listed. “Creates a listed IT services platform, enabling independent value discovery and strategic flexibility”
- *Scheme* — Regulation 30 disclosure frames the deal as the execution of ITCI's existing standalone expansion strategy, aimed at a step change in revenue scale and competitiveness. “ITC Infotech's 'Orbit Next' strategy envisages rapid global expansion through capability led strategic partnerships.”
- *Scheme* — The industry slide gives the explicit scale threshold problem the separation-and-combination is meant to clear — being below US$1bn keeps ITCI off large buyers' vendor lists. “> $1Bn revenue puts provider on the vendor management  office radar”
- *Scheme* — Media statement sets the quantified target for the combined, listed entity: US$1 billion revenue by FY28 on a pro-forma basis, AI-first, with 19,000+ professionals. “ITC Infotech (ITCI), a wholly owned subsidiary of ITC Limited and a leading global technology services player, today announced the proposed strategic combination with Happiest Minds Technologies Limited (Happiest Minds) to create a scaled, future-ready, AI-first global technology services enterprise.”
- *Scheme* — Synergy slide quantifies what the combination is expected to deliver financially: roughly 10% revenue synergies, about 100 bps of margin expansion, and EPS accretion in year one. “Expected to be EPS accretive in first full year of combined entity operations”
- *Scheme* — ITC's Chairman Sanjiv Puri justifies it on complementarity of capability and culture rather than on any investor, lender or partner demand. “The coming together of our complementary strengths, deep domain expertise and future-ready capabilities will further enhance our ability to deliver cutting-edge solutions across geographies.”
- *Scheme* — The only external party pressing for a change of ownership is the Happiest Minds promoter selling the 22.106% stake, who wanted a larger home for his company. “We believe that ITC Infotech is the best partner for Happiest Minds to fulfil its destiny and we are pleased that our team will have a welcoming new home .”
- *Scheme* — ITCI's CEO Manas Chakraborty positions the rationale as capability completeness — full-stack AI-led transformation — rather than financial engineering. “Integrating Happiest Minds' Digital Engineering, Data, AI, and Cybersecurity capabilities with our deep domain expertise, cloud and engineering capabilities will enable us to serve as a full stack AI-led transformation partner.”
- *Scheme* — At the parent level ITC is simultaneously simplifying in the opposite direction, absorbing wholly owned Sproutlife Foods (Yoga Bar; FY26 turnover Rs 451.71 crores, total assets Rs 150.07 crores) on 2 November 2026. “Result in reduction of the number of operating entities to simplify the corporate holding structure.”
- *Scheme* — The 1 September 2026 filing shows pre-listing entity cleanup: step-down subsidiaries Blazeclan and Cloudlytics were merged into ITC Infotech with appointed date 1 October 2024. “Accordingly, with effect from 1st September , 2026, BTPL and CTPL stand  dissolved without winding up and have cease d to be subsidiaries of the Company.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No earnings-call transcripts supplied; filings never explain ITC's intent for its 73.4% stake, any ITC-shareholder entitlement, carve-out/dis-synergy costs, valuation basis, or the earlier hotels demerger's rationale.

**PROBABLE** (a scheme of arrangement whose nature the documents on file do not settle) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 3.3/10 · scheme (nature unclear) · 1 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-08-27, latest 2026-08-27
