**The stages, as filed:** nclt_sanction (2026-08-27)

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** not stated — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* not stated; documents only note LIC as promoter/parent of LICHFL, with top management derived from LIC under the articles of association
- *What it reveals:* not stated — no separation in the documents; they instead disclose an admitted claim against a personal guarantor versus a token repayment-plan payout, with security interests retained
- *Selling pressure:* unclear — not stated; no demerged entity, index change or shareholder allotment described in the documents
- *Parent or spin:* neither · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* NCLT Delhi order approving Dr. Subhash Chandra's repayment plan, and corporate Stage-3 exposure of INR2,837 crores
- *In their words:* “We clarify that the recent NCLT order pertains to the Insolvency Resolution Process against the Personal Guarantor Dr. Subhash Chandra, under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, and does not in any manner adjudicate, discharge, dilute or impact the corporate liabilities of the principal borrower entities in anyway.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

These texts do not describe LIC Housing Finance separating, demerging, spinning off or hiving down any business, and management never gives a rationale for one, because no such transaction is discussed anywhere in the four readable transcripts (Aug 2025, Nov 2025, Feb 2026, May 2026) or in the single filing supplied. The only filing in the pack is a 27 August 2026 clarification that LICHFL's INR 1,322.39 crore admitted claim against personal guarantor Dr. Subhash Chandra is being repaid only INR 38.09 lakh under an NCLT-approved personal-insolvency repayment plan, while LICHFL retains its security interest and all recovery rights against the principal borrower entities — a recovery matter, not a corporate separation. What the calls do contain are internal separations of function, not of entity: on May 2026 Adhikari said the Board had decided to create a stand-alone affordable-housing vertical modelled on PNB Housing's 'Roshni', staffed entirely by outside hires, with its own sourcing, credit appraisal, recovery and collections, because in 36-37 years LICHFL had 'never done affordable' and was culturally attuned only to prime salaried individual home loans (84-85% of a INR 3,20,707 crore book, IHL Stage 3 just 1.03%, cumulative IHL yield 9.03% versus 10.05% non-housing individual and 10.56% corporate/project); and a separate 'business retention department' to stop roughly INR 12,778 crore of annual BT-out (about INR 1,000 crore a month). The driver management cited for all of this is margin, not structure: spreads compressed 12 bps to 1.94%, FY26 NIM 2.68% versus 2.73%, because 82-85% IHL puts them head-to-head with banks that reprice instantly off repo ('we are competing with our lenders'), so they are shifting mix toward LAP/LRD (15% from 12%, targeting 25%, 150-200 bps extra margin) and project finance (yields ~11-12%). Investors and analysts (Nischint Chawathe, Renish, Abhijit Tibrewal, Nishit Shah, Mahrukh Adajania) repeatedly pressed on stagnant single-digit growth and asked directly about structural change, a strategic investor and an IDBI Bank merger; management answered that the Board had commissioned a management consultant (Big Four/IIM-type) for a 3-4 month review of structure, verticals, compensation and technology, that top management comes from LIC under the articles of association, that a strategic investor is 'not in the discussion horizon' with CAR at 24%, and that an LIC-IDBI merger is a regulator and parent matter, not theirs. No separation of a business was proposed, approved or explained.

**How it evolved:** Aug 2025 (Q1 FY26): no separation of any kind; only a slow-built affordable-housing push (INR 458 crore FY25, ~INR 1,000 crore target) and margin-over-growth framing. Nov 2025 call (Q2 FY26, held 30 Oct 2025): the Board asks for a 'comprehensive relook at the entire structuring of the company' — offices, locations, distribution channels — and a consultant is being onboarded; co-lending/direct-assignment policy also floated. Feb 2026 (Q3 FY26): consultant onboarding in February, work from March, report by end-April/May, scope widened to verticals, compensation and technology, but management explicitly rules out management-structure change, a strategic investor and an IDBI merger. May 2026 (Q4 FY26): the outcome is internal — a stand-alone affordable vertical with outside hires, a new business-retention department, 200 marketing hires, co-lending/DA policy ready — and still no separation, demerger or scheme.

**What management expects from it:** Nothing is claimed for a separation, because none is proposed. For the ring-fenced affordable vertical they set no targets at all ('the baby has not yet been born'), expecting only eventual access to a higher-margin segment over two to three years. The retention department should cut ~INR 1,000 crore monthly BT-out; LAP/LRD mix shifting 15%-to-25% carries 150-200 bps more margin.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[May 2026](https://cdn.lichousing.com/2026/05/Concall-Transcript_Q4_FY2026.pdf)* — The only 'separate' entity-like structure announced is an internal affordable-housing vertical, created because LICHFL has never run affordable lending and its own staff are not attuned to it; it will be built entirely with external hires. “So this year, a decision has been taken that we need to set up a separate affordable vertical, something like what PNB has done, the Roshni vertical of PNB, we'll be setting up a similar vertical.”
- *[May 2026](https://cdn.lichousing.com/2026/05/Concall-Transcript_Q4_FY2026.pdf)* — That vertical is ring-fenced functionally end-to-end — sourcing, credit appraisal, recovery and collections — but it stays inside LIC Housing Finance; no demerger, subsidiary carve-out or scheme is mentioned. “It will be a complete separate vertical wherein the entire sourcing, the entire credit appraisal, the entire recovery, the entire collection machinery will be handled by people who are attuned with, who are experienced in doing affordable business.”
- *[May 2026](https://cdn.lichousing.com/2026/05/Concall-Transcript_Q4_FY2026.pdf)* — A second internal unit was carved out to attack balance-transfer attrition of roughly INR 12,778 crore in FY26 (about INR 1,000 crore a month of runoff), with authority over every exit case. “So this is one area which we need to focus. We have set up a separate, I would say, department, which we are calling business retention department.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=de178698-2fe2-4e1a-a887-f2fca05e3be2.pdf)* — The Board ordered a structural review of the company and a consultant was being onboarded — the closest thing in these texts to a reorganisation mandate, aimed at offices, locations and distribution, not at separating a business. “And towards that, the Board has guided us or the Board has asked us to go in for a comprehensive relook at the entire structuring of the company in terms of offices, the locations, also in terms of the distribution channels and what we need to do.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://cdn.lichousing.com/2026/02/Concall_Transcript_Q3_FY2026.pdf)* — Asked point-blank how far the company would go — management change, business mix, corporate structure, or a PNB-style strategic investor — management ruled out a strategic investor and said capital is not needed for 2-3 years at 24% CAR. “And, as far as onboarding a new stakeholder or shareholder is concerned, probability , our CAR is 24%, which is, I think, good enough right now.”
- *[May 2026](https://cdn.lichousing.com/2026/05/Concall-Transcript_Q4_FY2026.pdf)* — The only corporate-combination question raised (an LIC-IDBI Bank merger to fix LICHFL's cost-of-funds disadvantage versus banks) was deflected as a parent-company and regulatory matter outside LICHFL's hands. “The regulator is not permitting, neither RBI nor IRD A.”
- *Scheme* — No scheme of arrangement, demerger, slump sale or spin-off document is present in the pack; the sole filing is a 27 Aug 2026 clarification on the Subhash Chandra personal-guarantor insolvency order, where LICHFL's INR 1,322.39 crore admitted claim is allotted INR 38.09 lakh. “We clarify that the recent NCLT order pertains to the Insolvency Resolution Process against the Personal Guarantor Dr. Subhash Chandra, under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, and does not in any manner adjudicate, discharge, dilute or impact the corporate liabilities of the principal borrower entities in anyway.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No scheme, demerger or separation is mentioned anywhere; seven of eleven transcripts (Nov 2023-May 2025) were unreadable scans, and the only filing concerns Subhash Chandra's insolvency.

## MEESHO — Meesho Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a filing's text names a demerger; no scheme filing names it yet) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 3.3/10 · spin-off · 4 filing(s) from NSE · first 2025-12-10, latest 2026-01-30

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'meetings' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**The stages, as filed:** meetings (2026-01-13)

**Stated in the filings:** entitlement **2509 for every 1**.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Grocery and e-commerce (marketplace) undertakings carved out to wholly owned subsidiaries; parent retained Valmo logistics — class `regulatory_strategic`.

- *Insiders:* Promoters/Founders Vidit Aatrey and Sanjeev Kumar; proposed Article 122 keeps their board seats while they hold 3% or 75,62,14,937 shares; both direct MPPL; ESOP 2024 options vest/exercise (44,605,655 shares allotted Q1FY27)
- *What it reveals:* Demerger consideration marks MTPL at Rs 258,623.89mn and MGPL at Rs 7,313.55mn against net assets of only Rs 1,147.24mn, booking a Rs 264,790.20mn "Gain on demerger"; parent's retained Valmo logistics earned Rs 3,537.70mn standalone profit while consolidated stayed loss-making
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — No shares went to public shareholders; MTPL/MGPL remain 100% subsidiaries. The 47.2509-for-1 ratio was a bonus issue, not a demerger entitlement
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* The Composite Scheme of Arrangement and NCLT order of May 27, 2025, plus the CCPS fair-value basis for MTPL
- *In their words:* “As a consideration of the demerger, MTPL and MGPL issued equity shares and Compulsorily convertible preference shares ('CCPS') to the Company.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The separation is a Composite Scheme of Arrangement under Sections 230-232, approved by the boards of Meesho Limited, Meesho Grocery Private Limited (MGPL), Meesho Technologies Private Limited (MTPL) and Meesho Inc. (the erstwhile US holding company), filed with NCLT Bengaluru on April 25, 2024, sanctioned by NCLT on May 27, 2025 and given effect from June 1, 2025: the Grocery undertaking went to MGPL, the Marketplace (e-commerce) undertaking went to MTPL, and Meesho Inc. was amalgamated into Meesho Limited by pooling-of-interests, i.e. the US-to-India 'reverse flip' that made an Indian listing possible — the IPO followed on December 10, 2025 (fresh issue Rs 42,500 million plus Rs 11,712.04 million offer for sale at Rs 111/share). Mechanically, net assets of only Rs 1,147.24 million (MTPL Rs 586.83m, MGPL Rs 560.41m) moved out against consideration of Rs 265,937.44 million in equity and CCPS (MTPL Rs 258,623.89m, MGPL Rs 7,313.55m), producing an exceptional 'gain on demerger' of Rs 264,790.20 million in the standalone accounts, plus Rs 7,607.24 million of interest income on the CCPS — with no consolidated effect, and the flip itself cost real cash: Rs 24,868.42 million of 'tax payable on account of business combination' (GILTI, business combination and passive income) in FY25 and a further Rs 698.26 million in FY26, Rs 7,338.16 million of perquisite tax, Rs 4,824.80 million of incremental ESOP charge on plan modification, Rs 620.55 million of accelerated vesting charge and Rs 1,410.91 million of business-combination expenses. The effect is that the listed parent kept only the Valmo logistics channel, and from June 1, 2025 'generated revenue from providing logistics services through its delivery channel - Valmo - exclusively to MTPL', while the marketplace, grocery, payments (MPPL, a Lending Service Provider) and new initiatives sit in separate wholly owned subsidiaries, and IPO proceeds are pushed down by rights issue (Rs 28,900 million into MTPL on December 10, 2025; Rs 75 crore into MGPL in July/August 2026; Rs 100 crore in May 2026 and up to Rs 400 crore in October/November 2026 into MPPL). A second, narrower separation followed: the board on March 31, 2026 approved an internal reorganisation moving functions, employees and contracts into Valmo Transportation Private Limited (VTPL, incorporated January 28, 2026), stated reasons being 'to enhance administrative efficiency, enable functional specialization, and allow more focused management of the logistics business' — with mid-mile and last-mile in VTPL (which holds a Goods and Transport Agency licence under GST), while first-mile and sort-centre operations stay in Meesho Limited and the parent now bills sellers directly. Management's own framing on the calls is transparency and tax/GST classification rather than value unlocking: Dhiresh Bansal said in January 2026 the logistics subsidiary was set up 'primarily to explore how should we kind of structure the Valmo financials, so that they are more clearly visible for people to understand. There is no plan of opening this up to other third parties', and in July 2026 that consolidated numbers do not change materially, only standalone flows between Meesho Limited, MTPL and VTPL. The problems the structure is said to solve are therefore: an offshore holdco incompatible with an Indian IPO, a logistics business whose economics (a fulfilment spread management keeps at roughly 2%-2.5% of NMV, with 145 bps of one-time FY26 disruption cost and contribution margin recovering from 2.3% in Q3 FY26 to a ~4% Q4 exit) were invisible inside a blended marketplace P&L, a grocery/perishables supply chain Vidit Aatrey says needs 'a fundamentally different logistics network' from Valmo's national network, and loss-making adjacencies (new initiatives capped at about Rs 200 crore annual EBITDA burn; Rs 39 crore loss in Q1 FY27) ring-fenced from the core. No investor, lender or partner is named as having demanded the separation; a proxy advisory firm did question the VTPL/GTA model to SEBI, and management replied it had law-firm and accounting opinions, that no tax or regulatory authority had queried it, and that it had received no communication from SEBI.

**How it evolved:** The Scheme predates the calls (NCLT filing April 25, 2024; order May 27, 2025; effective June 1, 2025) and surfaced publicly only in the first post-listing call on January 30, 2026 (Feb 2026 transcript), where Sachin Salgaonkar asked about 'a new subsidiary on logistics' and Dhiresh Bansal said it existed to structure Valmo's financials for visibility, with no intent to open the network to third parties. By the March 31, 2026 board meeting the plan had hardened into an executed internal reorganisation into VTPL, which the May 6, 2026 call never addressed — that call instead split economics into ads margin versus fulfilment margin and talked about restoring the fulfilment spread after the 145 bps one-time hit. On the July 23, 2026 call the structure was explained in operating detail for the first time: VTPL houses mid-mile and last-mile under a GTA licence, first-mile and sort centres stay in Meesho Limited, VTPL's annual financials will not be a clean read of Valmo volumes, and a proxy advisory firm's GST question had gone to SEBI. Separation then continued by filing rather than by call — Kirana Club/Retail Pulse Labs bought for Rs 2,020.85 million (SPA June 12, 2026) and a new wholly owned lending subsidiary approved on October 28, 2026.

**What management expects from it:** Clearer, separately visible Valmo logistics financials; administrative efficiency, functional specialisation and focused management of logistics; an India-domiciled listed parent able to IPO and push IPO cash into each subsidiary; ring-fenced grocery, payments and new-initiative losses under a ~Rs 200 crore cap; fulfilment spread held at 2%-2.5% of NMV with margin growth from ads; in-house lending capturing full margins.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The Composite Scheme has three legs: grocery to MGPL, marketplace to MTPL, and amalgamation of the US holding company Meesho Inc. into Meesho Limited — the reverse flip that enabled the Indian IPO. “a) transfer of Grocery business of the Company to MGPL; b) transfer of Marketplace business of the Company to MTPL; and c) amalgamation by way of transfer of assets and liabilities of the Transferor Company with the Company.”
- *Scheme* — Net assets of only Rs 1,147.24 million left the parent against Rs 265,937.44 million of equity and CCPS consideration, creating a Rs 264,790.20 million exceptional standalone gain with no consolidated effect. “The surplus/deficit which had arisen after taking effect of consideration over the carrying value of net assets of MTPL and MGPL was recognised as an "exceptional item" in the standalone financial results for the quarter ended June 30, 2025 and the year ended March 31, 2026 respectively.”
- *Scheme* — Post-demerger the listed parent is effectively the Valmo logistics entity, selling delivery services exclusively to the marketplace subsidiary MTPL. “Consequently, from June 01, 2025, the Company generated revenue from providing logistics services through its delivery channel -Valmo -exclusively to MTPL.”
- *Scheme* — The March 31, 2026 board approved a second, logistics-only reorganisation into VTPL for administrative efficiency, functional specialisation and focused management; it makes standalone Q1 FY27 non-comparable. “Pursuant to this reorganization, the Company and its subsidiaries (collectively, the "Group") are reorganising the logistics business across different Group entities to enhance administrative efficiency, enable functional specialization, and allow more focused management of the logistics business.”
- *Scheme* — The flip carried a large cash tax and compensation cost: Rs 24,868.42 million of business-combination tax in FY25 plus Rs 698.26 million in FY26, Rs 7,338.16 million perquisite tax, and Rs 5,445.35 million of ESOP modification/acceleration charges. “During the year ended March 31, 2025, the Company had provided for taxes towards Global Intangible Low-Taxed Income, business combination and passive income collectively referred to as "Tax payable on account of business combination" arising on account of the aforesaid business combination.”
- *Scheme* — IPO money is routed down into the separated entities by rights issue — Rs 28,900 million into MTPL on listing day, Rs 75 crore into MGPL, Rs 100 crore then up to Rs 400 crore into MPPL. “This investment is a part of utilization of the proceeds as specified in Prospectus dated December 05, 2025.”
- *Scheme* — Grocery sits in MGPL as a local-logistics-for-essentials entity, still sub-scale and loss-making: FY26 turnover Rs 112.10 lakhs against a net loss of Rs 6,899.30 lakhs. “Line of Business: Local logistics network for daily essentials and groceries.”
- *Scheme* — A further new wholly owned subsidiary was approved on October 28, 2026 to move lending in-house and capture the full margin instead of acting only as a Lending Service Provider through MPPL. “The incorporation of Wholly Owned Subsidiary will enable the group to build in-house underwriting, control product design, directly own borrower relationships, and capture full lending margins while gaining access to institutional funding.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=bab657a9-3907-420f-86fb-7070154a073e.pdf)* — Management's stated reason for the logistics subsidiary was investor visibility into Valmo's financials, explicitly not opening the network to third-party shippers. “I think we are setting up that subsidiary primarily to explore how should we kind of structure the Valmo financials, so that they are more clearly visible for people to understand.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=bab657a9-3907-420f-86fb-7070154a073e.pdf)* — Logistics is run as a separate economic unit with a deliberately capped spread, with all further efficiency passed back, so margin growth must come from ads and other services. “we keep the logistics margin in a certain trajectory, which is about 2% - 2.5% of NMB from a contribution perspective.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=bab657a9-3907-420f-86fb-7070154a073e.pdf)* — By contrast, Meesho Mall was explicitly kept inside the marketplace rather than carved out, so the separation lines are entity/function-based, not product-based. “So, Meesho Mall is part of the core marketplace , all of the numbers are captured within the marketplace financials.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=bab657a9-3907-420f-86fb-7070154a073e.pdf)* — The asset-light philosophy explains why logistics can be housed in a thin aggregator entity: investment goes into technology, not warehouses or fleet capex. “So, even today in Valmo, the entire software stack end -to-end is our own.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No valuation basis for the Rs 265,937m CCPS consideration, no Valmo standalone P&L or disclosure timetable, no GST-saving quantum, no value-unlock or future listing rationale.

**Stated in the filings:** size hint: 0% of net worth.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** 10% equity stake in Bharat Innovations Global Private Limited, a recently incorporated subsidiary whose business the filing does not describe — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* Buyer is NSDC International Limited, which "does not belong to the promoter or promoter group/group companies"; not a related party transaction. Promoter stake in buyer not stated.
- *What it reveals:* Nothing revealed: turnover INR 30,018 (0%) and negative net worth INR (20,591) (0%); incorporated about a year ago, core operations recently commenced; PWL keeps 90% and consideration was non-cash brand name and goodwill.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — No shares distributed to PWL shareholders; the entity contributes 0% of turnover and net worth and stays a 90% subsidiary.
- *Parent or spin:* neither · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* The December 04, 2024 sale agreement with NSDC International Limited — what brand name and goodwill PWL received.
- *In their words:* “The Company continues to hold 90% of the equity share capital in Bharat Innovations Global Private Limited and accordingly, it shall continue to remain a subsidiary of the Company.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

On these texts alone, Physicswallah is not demerging or spinning off a business under any scheme of arrangement — the 06-Mar-2026 filing expressly answers "Not applicable" to whether the disposal is outside a Scheme of Arrangement, and neither earnings call mentions a demerger, listing of a subsidiary, or value unlock. What the documents do show are three narrow, separate acts of legal carve-out, each explained in operational rather than capital-markets terms. First, PWL sold 10% of Bharat Innovations Global Private Limited (BIGPL), so it ceased to be a wholly-owned subsidiary while PWL retained 90% and consolidation continues; the buyer is NSDC International Limited (not promoter/promoter group, not a related-party transaction), the agreement for sale is dated 04-Dec-2024, completion 19-Feb-2026, with "an inadvertent delay in intimating", and crucially the consideration was received other than in cash, "in exchange for the brand name and goodwill of the acquirer" — i.e. a brand/partnership swap, not a cash divestment; BIGPL is immaterial (FY25 turnover INR 30,018 and net worth of negative INR 20,591, each 0% of the group, incorporated about a year earlier and having "recently commenced its core business operations"). Second, on the Feb-2026 call management said a newly incorporated hostel-services entity exists to pull the fragmented hostel operations of subsidiary Xylem in Trivandrum, plus scattered student-housing pockets (Patna, Trivandrum), out of the operating businesses into "an independent entity" — a business that is "less than a percent" of revenue and which they explicitly do not intend to grow aggressively, framed purely as facilitating student/parent needs. Third, the K-12/schools push is being ring-fenced in a separate legal and reporting vehicle: INR 400 crores has been invested "in our wholly owned company" (the school-management company running Indore, Gurgaon and Varanasi, plus management control of Tender Heart, Ranchi, with 8 more schools — 4 brownfield, 4 greenfield on nine-year build-to-suit leases), and schools will sit in "others", not in the offline segment, once online/offline segmental EBITDA reporting starts on 1 April 2026. The stated problems these solve are fragmentation (hostels run piecemeal inside Xylem), reporting cleanliness (schools and housing, each under 1% of revenue, not muddying offline economics the market is being asked to judge), and acquiring a partner's brand and goodwill without cash (BIGPL/NSDC International). No investor, lender or partner is named anywhere as having asked for any of it; the only external-party driver disclosed is the NSDC International counterparty itself, and the only shareholder action in the filings is ESOP ratification/extension to group, subsidiary and associate companies plus deletion of Part B of the AoA after the shareholders' agreements lapsed on listing.

**How it evolved:** Dec-2025 (Q2 FY26, the maiden post-listing call) contains no separation at all — only the promise to report online and offline EBITDA separately from 1 April 2026, and an M&A template of taking 25–50% first-stage equity with three-to-four-year earnouts rather than one-shot majority. By Feb-2026 (Q3 FY26) two carve-outs surface in the same call: the newly incorporated hostel-services entity consolidating Xylem's Trivandrum hostels and scattered student housing, and the INR 400 crore wholly-owned school-management company, with the clarification that schools go into "others" and not offline. The 06-Mar-2026 filing then discloses the third and only actual stake disposal — 10% of Bharat Innovations Global to NSDC International — on an agreement dated 04-Dec-2024 that completed on 19-Feb-2026 and was intimated late, i.e. a transaction agreed almost a year before listing and surfacing publicly only after it had closed.

**What management expects from it:** Hostels: one integrated entity for fragmented Xylem/Trivandrum housing, deliberately not scaled, under 1% of revenue. K-12 WOS: INR 400 crores deployed, schools at 20–40% (steady state 25–35%) margins, "noticeable significant EBITDA by FY '29-'30", test-prep integration synergy. BIGPL: brand and goodwill of NSDC International acquired without cash. Reporting: online 35–45% versus offline 13–15% EBITDA shown separately.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *FILING 2026-03-06* — PWL sold 10% of wholly-owned Bharat Innovations Global Private Limited; it ceases to be a WOS but stays a 90%-held subsidiary, so this is a dilution/partnering step, not a business exit. “The Company continues to hold 90% of the equity share capital in Bharat Innovations Global Private Limited and accordingly, it shall continue to remain a subsidiary of the Company.”
- *FILING 2026-03-06* — No cash changed hands: the consideration was the acquirer's brand name and goodwill, with buyer NSDC International Limited, outside the promoter group and not a related-party transaction. “The buyer is NSDC Interna Ɵonal Limited, a company registered under Companies Act, 2013.”
- *FILING 2026-03-06* — The disposed entity is financially immaterial — FY25 turnover of INR 30,018 and net worth of negative INR 20,591, each 0% of group — because it had only just started operating. “Note: Bharat Innovations Global Private Limited was incorporated approximately a year ago and has recently commenced its core business operations.”
- *FILING 2026-03-06* — The filing explicitly rules out any scheme-of-arrangement framing (and any slump-sale disclosure), i.e. there is no demerger on record; the sale agreement dates to 04-Dec-2024 with completion on 19-Feb-2026 and late intimation. “There has been an inadvertent delay in intimating the aforesaid sale of stake.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=f33bc430-09e6-471b-8069-0b30cf381910.pdf)* — A new hostel-services entity was incorporated to pull Xylem's fragmented Trivandrum hostel operations and scattered student housing out of the operating businesses. “So about the hostel entity this is designed to integrate a hostel business of our subsidiary Xylem which was fragmentedly run in in Trivandrum as well as we have a very small student housing opportunity at various parts of the country.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=f33bc430-09e6-471b-8069-0b30cf381910.pdf)* — The housing business — under 1% of revenue — is being put into a standalone vehicle with no aggressive growth intent, purely to serve student and parent needs in pockets like Patna and Trivandrum. “So that's why we thought that we will integrate the entire housing business which is very small which is again less than a percent at this point of time into an independent entity.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=f33bc430-09e6-471b-8069-0b30cf381910.pdf)* — K-12/schools is ring-fenced in a separate wholly-owned company funded with INR 400 crores as the vehicle for the school-management build-out. “As of now we've invested INR400 crores in our wholly owned company to drive some of that K-12 platform investments that we will do.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=f33bc430-09e6-471b-8069-0b30cf381910.pdf)* — Schools are also separated for reporting: they will sit in "others", deliberately kept out of the offline segment whose economics the market is being asked to judge from 1 April 2026. “school will not be a part of our offline business, it will be a part of our others business at this point of time.”

- *[Dec 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=c7a95009-a76d-4bec-bddb-a988436b93ad.pdf)* — The group's stated approach to new businesses is partial stakes and staged integration rather than full separation or one-shot control — 40% of Sarrthi IAS now, rising to 85% by FY28. “And we have taken 40% stake in Sarrthi IAS.”

Second, the disinvestment of its entire stake in MYTRIDENT.COM LIMITED, a non-material wholly owned subsidiary with NIL turnover acquired only during the current financial year, sold for INR 1,00,000 (10,000 equity shares at face value of INR 10 each) to Trident Global Corp Limited, an associate and promoter-group entity — a related party transaction the company says was 'made at fair value on arm's length basis.' The filing expressly answers 'Not Applicable' to whether the disposal sits outside a Scheme of Arrangement and to the Regulation 37A compliance question, and 'Not Applicable' to slump-sale disclosures, which means the company itself disclaims any scheme-based separation. **What management expects from it:** Nothing was stated for either entity — no margin, capital, valuation or focus expectation appears. The only forward-looking claim is for the new subsidiary TGIL: enhanced brand presence, brand-building, selling and marketing of Trident products in overseas markets, especially the U.S. For MYTRIDENT.COM LIMITED, a NIL-turnover non-material shell sold at face value, no expected benefit is articulated at all.

- *Insiders:* Not stated for the sold entity; buyer BIIF Infrastructure II "does not belong to the promoter/ promoter group". In parent, Welspun Group Master Trust held 49.33% and took 71,23,809 warrants at Rs. 525.
- *What it reveals:* Rs. ~1,000 crore enterprise value for a subsidiary contributing only Rs. 196.77 crore income (5.44%) and Rs. 55.49 crore net worth (1.90%); ~Rs. 800 crore debt expected to move off balance sheet; management expects better than 1.5x equity invested.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — Cash sale to a SEBI-registered fund; no shares distributed to shareholders, no new listing, no index exclusion event
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* December 01, 2025 — allotment of 1,90,47,619 convertible warrants at Rs. 525 per share (promoter and non-promoter)
- *Read next:* Completion intimation for WASPPL — NHAI/lender approvals and final EV adjustments for carry interest, net current assets, pass-through receivables
- *In their words:* “The proposed divestment reflects our asset -light strategy of developing high- quality infrastructure and monetising them at an appropriate stage.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Nothing in these texts is a demerger, spin-off or scheme of arrangement — twice asked, management refused to split the company. The only "separations" they explained are (a) serial monetisation of completed road concession SPVs under an explicitly asset-light model, and (b) housing the SmartOps wastewater technology JV in its own company under Welspun Michigan (WMEL 50%, WEL effective ~30%) because it is a technology-driven, distributed, O&M-heavy business needing different skills and its own CEO. On roads the logic is timing-driven: NHAI rules force a >51% hold until COD+6 months, and the first annuity "establishes every valuation metrics for the HAM project", so WEL sells only after PCOD/first annuity — Aunta-Simaria's first ₹72 crore annuity came in Q3 FY26, and the July 2026 SSPA sells the entire stake in Welspun Aunta-Simaria Project Pvt Ltd to BIIF Infrastructure II (Build India Infrastructure Fund, manager Alpha Alternatives) at ~₹1,000 crore enterprise value, subject to NHAI and lender approvals; that SPV contributed ₹196.77 crore (5.44%) of FY26 consolidated income and ₹55.49 crore (1.90%) of net worth. In November 2026 the balance 51% of NXT Infra MCP Highways went to NXT-Infra Trust for ~₹339.38 crore under the June 2022 Actis SSPA, cutting the holding to nil (proportionate net worth ₹27.94 crore). The problems solved, as stated: ~₹800 crore of SPV debt moves off the balance sheet, equity turns quickly (₹160 crore invested in Aunta-Simaria, targeted 2x versus 1.5x on the earlier Actis deal, equity IRR hurdle 18%+), ROCE rises above 15% and "significantly higher" with monetisation gains, and net worth is freed because NHAI's new PPP test uses "adjusted net worth" — net worth minus a percentage of existing commitments — the same constraint behind the ₹1,000 crore warrant issue at ₹525 (₹250 crore received, ₹750 crore callable over 18 months). The cited precedent is 2022, when six completed road assets were monetised at over ₹9,000 crore EV and the proceeds funded the pivot into water, wastewater and tunnelling. Asset sales, not a separation of verticals, are therefore the mechanism: management said transport "shall remain as a part of the company" and that oil & gas is "the only noncore asset that we have right now."

**How it evolved:** May 2025 (Q4 FY25) set the frame — monetise MCP's balance 51% to Actis and Aunta-Simaria in FY26 against ~₹300 crore book value — and when asked about WEL/WMEL both sitting in water, Garg handed the vertical to Saurin Patel but said corporate structure changes would be disclosed "at an appropriate time"; in Aug 2025 SmartOps was "institutionalized as a separate company" under WMEL and a direct question on demerging transport was declined. Nov 2025 added the bidding rationale (NHAI adjusted net worth, ₹1,000 crore warrants) and a second refusal to hive off verticals despite two vertical CEOs, while flagging oil & gas as the only non-core asset to divest. Feb 2026 made it concrete — first ₹72 crore annuity received, monetisation targeted Q1–Q2 FY27, ~₹800 crore of debt to leave the balance sheet — and May 2026 put Aunta-Simaria in "advanced stages" with SNRP to follow after its first annuity (possibly FY28). The filings then executed it: SSPA for Aunta-Simaria at ~₹1,000 crore EV on 29 July 2026, and the final NXT Infra MCP tranche of ~₹339.38 crore on 5 November 2026.

**What management expects from it:** For WEL: ~₹800 crore SPV debt off balance sheet, equity recycled at ~2x book (vs 1.5x earlier) at 18%+ equity IRR, ROCE above 15% and higher with gains, net worth freed for adjusted-net-worth PPP bidding, and capital redeployed into transport, water, wastewater and tunnelling at 18%+ EBITDA margins. For the sold SPVs: institutional long-term owners (BIIF, NXT-Infra Trust). SmartOps: own company, CEO and skill set.

**The stages, as filed:** nclt_sanction (2026-07-02) → effective (2026-02-10)

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Madura Fashion & Lifestyle Business, transferred as a going concern to wholly owned subsidiary Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands Limited — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* Not stated for the resulting company; documents disclose only ABFRL's own ESOP Scheme 2026 (3,12,95,000 options, 2.50% of fully diluted capital), which excludes promoters and promoter-group persons.
- *What it reveals:* MFL was the profitable half: FY25 discontinued operations showed revenue ₹7,636 Cr and PAT ₹176.5 Cr, while the retained ABFRL reported FY26 PAT loss of ₹830 Cr, ~₹600 Cr net cash and subsidiary-level debt.
- *Selling pressure:* likely — 1,22,02,94,773 shares issued 1:1 to every ABFRL holder on record date May 22, 2025; listed June 23, 2025.

- *Read next:* Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands Limited's own standalone results — the demerged MFL profit and debt are absent from these filings.
- *In their words:* “The Equity Shares of the Resulting Company listed on BSE Limited and the National Stock Exchange of India Limited on June 23, 2025.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The separation management explains across these texts is the demerger of the Madura Fashion & Lifestyle ("MFL") western-wear brands business — the Lifestyle Brands portfolio plus Reebok, American Eagle, Van Heusen Innerwear and the exited Forever 21 — into Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands Limited (ABLBL), leaving ABFRL with Pantaloons/Style Up-OWND, the ethnic portfolio (designer brands Sabyasachi, Tarun Tahiliani, House of Masaba, Shantnu & Nikhil, plus Tasva, Jaypore and TCNS), luxury retail (The Collective, Galeries Lafayette) and the digital-first TMRW platform. The problem stated is internal competition for capital and attention: the combined ABFRL "had multiple growth opportunities, and we realized at some point of time, that we'll have to capitalize it and structure it differently to pursue independent growth opportunities more aggressively", with Innerwear cited as a business that "will get the attention which it would not have got when we had 5 or 6 such growth opportunities in front of us" (May 2025). The cash-generative, high-margin brands business (FY25 normalised revenue INR7,830 crores, 16.2% EBITDA margin, 19.3% for Brands, 3,200+ stores) was described as "underleveraged in the combined entity", and Ashish Dikshit said "one of the strategic rationale for the demerger was to leave that cash for allowing that business to soar" — funding a historic 300-plus net store rollout in FY26 that franchisees could not drive in a downturn (Feb 2025). On the other side, a USD 490 million QIP plus preferential issue (promoters paying a premium) was raised to make demerged ABFRL debt-free with INR2,350 crores consolidated cash (vs an earlier INR1,300 crores estimate) to fund the TCNS turnaround, Tasva, Style Up, Galeries Lafayette and TMRW "until they become self-sustainable", with a plan to be free-cash-flow positive in about three years; ABLBL started with INR781 crores net debt (INR700 crores planned opening), repayable in 2–3 years, and was to be "a dividend-distributing company at the earliest appropriate opportunity". Management repeatedly framed the purpose as unlocking value through "2 independent entities" / "two focused fashion power houses", each on its own "distinct value-creation journey", with ABLBL guided to double in scale and expand margins over five years and demerged ABFRL to 3x revenue and 2x margin — the latter mostly from turning currently loss-making TCNS, Tasva and TMRW positive rather than from the already-profitable parts. Mechanics: the demerger was Board-approved 19 April 2024, books separated from 1 April 2024, 1:1 share exchange ratio (1,22,02,94,773 shares), NCLT sanction 27 March 2025, effective 1 May 2025, ABLBL listed 23 June 2025, accounted as a common-control transaction at book values with MFL shown as discontinued operations and a one-time INR97 crores gain from discontinuing inter-division elimination (Pantaloons inventory written up to purchase price). The same "separate and separately capitalise" logic continues one level down at TMRW, created as a standalone company in 2021, funded first by ABFRL (INR770–1,000 crores), then by ServiceNow Ventures (INR437 crores for ~11%, round completed at INR450 crores in Q2 FY26), then INR500 crores of NCDs (INR800 crores cash), explicitly aimed at "its own public market journey as we go forward from private to public". The only separation-type item in the newest filings runs the other way: the Scheme amalgamating wholly-owned Jaypore E-Commerce and TG Apparel & Decor back into ABFRL (Board 5 Feb 2026, NCLT 2 July 2026, effective 1 August 2026, appointed date 1 April 2026) for "simplification of legal & operating structure" and lower administrative cost, with no consideration as the shares are simply cancelled.

**How it evolved:** By the Feb 2025 call (17 Feb 2025, Q3 FY25) the demerger was already Board-approved (19 April 2024) and in execution — "progressing well and set for completion within the next 2, 3 months" with the NCLT hearing in the third week of March 2025 — and that call paired it with the USD 490 million fundraise, disclosing the split balance sheets (ABLBL ~INR700 crores opening debt; demerged ABFRL ~INR1,300 crores cash) and the clearest motive statement, that Lifestyle Brands' expansion had been "underleveraged in the combined entity". The May 2025 call (26 May 2025, Q4 FY25) reported completion, restated the rationale as two focused, independently capitalised platforms with explicit five-year targets (ABLBL double scale; ABFRL 3x revenue, 2x margin), and added the Innerwear example of a business that had not got management attention when five or six opportunities competed. The Aug 2025 call (14 Aug 2025) closed the process (ABLBL listed 23 June 2025) and extended the same capital-allocation philosophy to TMRW's external fundraise; by Nov 2025, Feb 2026 and May 2026 the demerger survives only as base-effect accounting (the INR97 crores gain), separate ABLBL/ABFRL earnings calls, leverage guidance "around 2 to 3" for each fashion company, and subsidiaries told to "fund their own growth" — while the newest Scheme filings (5 Feb 2026 to 1 Aug 2026) consolidate two wholly-owned subsidiaries back in.

**What management expects from it:** ABLBL: its own cash flows and 300+ net FY26 stores, doubling scale, meaningful margin expansion, INR781 crores net debt repaid in 2–3 years, early dividends. ABFRL: a debt-free start with INR2,350 crores cash to fund the TCNS turnaround, Tasva, OWND, Galeries Lafayette and TMRW; 3x revenue and 2x margin in five years, mainly by turning loss-makers profitable.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=86aee500-e77b-4d18-9566-af83384f5a37.pdf)* — The demerger of the western-wear brands business into ABLBL was in final regulatory execution, with the NCLT hearing set for the third week of March 2025 and completion expected within 2–3 months. “First, the demerger of western wear brands business into a separate entity, that is Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands Limited, or ABLBL, is progressing well and set for completion within the next 2, 3 months.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=86aee500-e77b-4d18-9566-af83384f5a37.pdf)* — The USD 490 million QIP plus preferential issue was explicitly sized to leave the demerged ABFRL debt-free with enough cash to carry its loss-making growth businesses until they stand on their own. “The fundraise within demerged ABFRL will strengthen its balance sheet by making it debt-free and leaving enough cash in the books to take care of the growth needs of its businesses until they become self-sustainable.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=86aee500-e77b-4d18-9566-af83384f5a37.pdf)* — Management quantified the split balance sheets: ABLBL to open FY26 with INR700 crores of debt, demerged ABFRL with roughly INR1,300 crores of cash (consolidated net debt was ~INR1,800 crores in January 2025 after INR1,860 crores of QIP money). “We expect ABLBL to start the next year with opening debt of INR700 crores, whereas demerged ABFRL will have a likely cash balance of approximately INR1,300 crores.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=86aee500-e77b-4d18-9566-af83384f5a37.pdf)* — The clearest stated motive: the Lifestyle Brands store-expansion opportunity had been starved inside the combined company, and the demerger was designed to leave that business its own cash flows to expand (300-plus stores planned, vs a consolidation year in FY25). “We think that's a large opportunity, which was sort of underleveraged in the combined entity. And one of the strategic rationale for the demerger was to leave that cash for allowing that business to soar.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=86aee500-e77b-4d18-9566-af83384f5a37.pdf)* — Asked why capital was raised at the pre-demerger consolidated level and why ABLBL kept INR700 crores of debt, Dikshit said the simultaneous TCNS merger stretched the demerger to 12–15 months, so raising in the combined entity was simply the fastest route; the books of the two companies were separated with effect from 1 April 2024. “And that's when we decided to do the fundraise in the combined entity, because that is the fastest way of raising capital at that point of time.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=86aee500-e77b-4d18-9566-af83384f5a37.pdf)* — The purpose was framed as value unlock through two independently viable listed companies, each with its own growth runway and balance sheet. “The completion of these steps in the next 2, 3 months will enable us to unlock value through 2 independent entities, both with attractive growth potential and a strong balance sheet through a resilient growth-oriented business model sharpened over time.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=29b83308-dd71-4b41-9802-e328e83350ee.pdf)* — Completion was announced as the creation of two focused entities on separate high-growth trajectories; ABLBL shares were allotted to ABFRL shareholders on the record date and listing was targeted by end-June. “We successfully completed the demerger, creating two focused fashion power houses, Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands Limited, ABLBL; and Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limited, ABFRL, both now set on independent high-growth trajectories.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=29b83308-dd71-4b41-9802-e328e83350ee.pdf)* — The sharpest statement of the capital-and-attention problem the split solves, given in answer to a question on why Innerwear had stagnated at about INR500 crores since 2016–17: ABFRL had five or six competing growth opportunities, so Innerwear never got management focus; inside a cash-generating ABLBL it would. “ABFRL, the combined ABFRL business had multiple growth opportunities, and we realized at some point of time, that we'll have to capitalize it and structure it differently to pursue independent growth opportunities more aggressively.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=29b83308-dd71-4b41-9802-e328e83350ee.pdf)* — Post-demerger targets were given per entity: ABLBL to double in scale and expand margins over five years off 3,200-plus stores and its own free cash flow (FY25 normalised revenue INR7,830 crores, 16.2% EBITDA margin; net debt INR781 crores to be repaid in 2–3 years; dividends "at the earliest appropriate opportunity"). “ABLBL, backed by a robust portfolio over 3,200 stores and healthy free cash flows, is positioned to double in scale and expand margins meaningfully over the next 5 years with 300-plus stores already in the pipeline for FY '26.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=29b83308-dd71-4b41-9802-e328e83350ee.pdf)* — For demerged ABFRL (FY25 revenue INR7,355 crores) the target was 3x revenue and 2x margin over five years on INR2,350 crores of gross cash, with Dikshit saying the bulk of the margin expansion comes from turning TCNS, Tasva and TMRW from loss-making to profitable rather than from the already-profitable units. “ABFRL with a sharpened brand portfolio, a comprehensive diversified play across high-growth segments and a gross cash balance of INR2,350 crores is set to unlock the next phase of growth, targeting a 3x revenue scale up and 2x margin expansion over the next 5 years.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=29b83308-dd71-4b41-9802-e328e83350ee.pdf)* — A mechanical consequence of separation: inter-division eliminations between Madura and Pantaloons stopped, producing a one-time INR97 crores EBITDA gain (inventory written up to Pantaloons' purchase price) that recurs as a base-effect drag in later quarters; ABLBL's INR148 crores of depreciation on discontinued operations was also not charged in consolidated financials. “Reported EBITDA includes gain of INR97 crores on account of discontinuation of interdivision elimination post demerger as company's financials get reset to report on independent and stand-alone basis going forward.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=605235b0-2e2b-4b89-9dcf-9a88f5115fa7.pdf)* — The process closed with ABLBL listed on 23 June 2025, and from Q1 FY26 ABFRL reported only the retained portfolio, with newer businesses already 44% of revenue versus 37% a year earlier. “On demerger, as previously communicated, all requisite processes have been successfully completed, culminating in the creation of Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands Limited. The company was listed on the stock exchange on 23rd June 2025.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No one is named as having asked for it; no valuation or SOTP math, debt-allocation or share-ratio rationale, tax treatment, stranded costs, or brand/shared-service arrangements between the two entities.

## ADANIPOWER — Adani Power Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a subsidiary's listing is in motion (DRHP / board approval)) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 2.9/10 · partial spin-off / listing · 2 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-02-24, latest 2026-08-27

> **Listing:** IPO / listing of the subsidiary in motion since 2026-02-24; date not fixed

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Chandenvalle Infra Park Limited — pre-revenue land-holding subsidiary with land parcels in Chandenvalley Industrial Park, Telangana; sold, not listed — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* Buyer AdaniConneX Private Limited is a 50:50 joint venture between Adani Enterprises Limited and EdgeConneX; "The promoters of AEL and the Company are same." Declared arm's length related-party transaction.
- *What it reveals:* A non-core, pre-commercial land bank inside a thermal power company fetched Rs. 535.69 crore cash from a group data-centre JV; CIPL "is yet to commence commercial activities" yet holds sizeable approved land parcels.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — No shares distributed to shareholders; entire stake sold for cash to a related party, so no new security hits the market.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* CIPL's carrying value and net worth in APL's FY27 accounts, to test the Rs. 535.69 crore related-party price
- *In their words:* “Post completion of the transaction , CIPL shall cease to be a subsidiary of the Company .”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

On the evidence of these twelve transcripts and ten filings, Adani Power is not separating an operating business and management never explained one — the corporate action running through this period is the opposite: an amalgamation of ten wholly owned subsidiaries INTO Adani Power Limited (Adani Power Dahej, Kutchh Power Generation, Resurgent Fuel Management, Mahan Fuel Management, Orissa Thermal Energy, Korba Power, Anuppur Thermal Energy (MP), Mirzapur Thermal Energy (UP), Emberiza Infra Park and Vidarbha Industries Power), approved by the boards on 30 October 2025 with an Appointed Date of 1 April 2025. The stated rationale, as recorded in the sanctioned Scheme, is to 'achieve size, scalability, integration, greater financial strength and flexibility', specifically: enhanced scale and controls, optimisation of overheads, improved creditworthiness with an optimised capital structure, 'improvement in credit profile which will lead to reduction in borrowing costs', enhanced leveraging capability, and simplification of the corporate structure by cutting the multiplicity of legal and regulatory compliances. No shares are issued — every transferor's equity held by APL (and APDL's holding in KPGL) 'shall stand cancelled and extinguished', so this is purely structural, not value-splitting. Management's own calls supply the empirical case for pulling subsidiaries in rather than pushing them out: the Adani Power (Jharkhand) amalgamation completed 25 April 2025 took Godda's 1,600 MW into the standalone entity and lifted its rating from BBB to AA, which the CFO said reduced finance costs, and in the Feb 2026 call he repeated that the merged Jharkhand asset's PFC-REC funding 'is also rated AA and its interest cost has also got reduced significantly'; earlier they amalgamated six subsidiaries (a Rs 4,325 crore provision reversal in Q4 FY23), folded Stratatech/Dhirauli into Mahan Energen, and merged Moxie Power into Coastal Energen. The only genuine separation anywhere in this record is the sale, not a demerger, of Chandenvalle Infra Park Limited — a pre-revenue wholly owned subsidiary that 'is yet to commence commercial activities' but 'holds sizeable land parcels in and around Chandenvalley Industrial Park in Telangana with certain essential land approvals' — sold on 27 August 2026 for Rs 535.69 crore, subject to closing adjustments, to AdaniConneX Private Limited, the 50:50 Adani Enterprises–EdgeConneX data-centre JV, disclosed as a related-party transaction on an arm's-length basis and closed the same day it was signed; APL gave no strategic explanation for it beyond the tabular disclosure, and it is nowhere discussed on any call. Capital context for a special-situation reader: capex of over Rs 2 lakh crore to FY31-32, FFO around Rs 20,000 crore a year, an interim gap of roughly Rs 60,000 crore to be bridged from debt, net debt/EBITDA guided to stay between 2x and 3x, and a Rs 15,000 crore enabling QIP approved at the 14 August 2026 EGM alongside a borrowing limit raised from Rs 75,000 crore to Rs 1,00,000 crore — all of which fits a company consolidating and monetising non-core land, not carving out a business.

**How it evolved:** Across all twelve calls (Nov 2023 through the 23 July 2026 Q1 FY27 call) no analyst asked about and no executive mentioned a separation, demerger or spin-off; the restructuring thread is inbound consolidation — six subsidiaries merged pre-FY24 (discussed 2 May 2024), Stratatech folded into Mahan Energen (30 January 2025), Adani Power (Jharkhand) merged on 25 April 2025 with the BBB-to-AA rating benefit flagged on 1 May 2025, 1 August 2025 and again 29 January 2026. The ten-subsidiary Scheme was board-approved on 30 October 2025 and filed in December 2025/February 2026, then sanctioned in two tranches: NCLT Ahmedabad cleared nine entities on 4 August 2026 while Vidarbha Industries Power stayed sub-judice in Mumbai — the plan's only real slippage — until NCLT Mumbai sanctioned it on 24 September 2026, with the whole Scheme effective 25 September 2026. The lone divestment, the Chandenvalle Infra Park sale to AdaniConneX, was signed and closed on 27 August 2026, i.e. after the last call in this set and before any subsequent one, so it has never been put to analysts.

**What management expects from it:** For the amalgamation: one larger entity with greater scale, tighter controls, lower overheads, pooled cash flows, a stronger credit profile that cuts borrowing costs, more leveraging headroom and fewer duplicated compliances — with no shares issued, so no dilution. For the CIPL sale: Rs 535.69 crore of cash and exit from a pre-revenue, non-core Telangana land bank into the group's data-centre JV. Nothing was said about margins or valuation.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The 27 August 2026 filing is the only separation in the record: APL sold its entire stake in wholly owned subsidiary Chandenvalle Infra Park Limited, which then ceased to be a subsidiary, for Rs 535.69 crore subject to closing adjustments; the agreement was signed and the transaction closed the same day. “Post completion of the transaction , CIPL shall cease to be a subsidiary of the Company .”
- *Scheme* — What was separated is not an operating business but a pre-revenue land bank: CIPL had not begun commercial activity and held land parcels around Chandenvalley Industrial Park in Telangana with essential land approvals — assets suited to a data-centre developer rather than a thermal generator. “CIPL is yet to commence commercial activities , however, it holds sizeable land parcels  in and around Chandenvalley  Industrial Park  in Telangana with certain essential land approvals.”
- *Scheme* — The buyer is inside the Adani group — AdaniConneX, the 50:50 Adani Enterprises/EdgeConneX data-centre JV sharing APL's promoters — so the filing declares it a related-party transaction done at arm's length; no independent valuation, process or use-of-proceeds was disclosed. “Buyer: AdaniConnex Private Limited  ("ACX") . ACX is a 50:50 joint venture between Adani Enterprises Limited (AEL) and EdgeConneX.”
- *Scheme* — The dominant corporate action is the reverse of a separation: ten wholly owned subsidiaries, including Korba Power, Mirzapur Thermal Energy (UP), Anuppur Thermal Energy (MP) and Vidarbha Industries Power, were amalgamated into APL and dissolved without winding up, effective 25 September 2026 with Appointed Date 1 April 2025. “Accordingly, the Scheme has become effective today, i.e., September 25 , 2026 ("Effective Date" ) and consequently, the above mentioned ten wholly owned subsidiaries stand amalgamated with A dani Power Limited and dissolved without being wound up.”
- *Scheme* — The Scheme's stated purpose is scale and structural efficiency — enhanced operations, optimised overheads, pooled financial resources and an improved credit profile — rather than any separation of businesses or unlocking of segment value. “The proposed amalgamation envisaged under this Scheme is intended to achieve size, scalability, integration, greater financial strength and flexibility thereby building a more resilient and robust organization that can address dynamic business situatio ns and volatility in various economic factors in a focused manner, in order to achieve improved long -term financial returns.”
- *Scheme* — Two benefits named in the Scheme are directly financial and consistent with what the CFO said about the earlier Jharkhand merger: a better credit profile cutting borrowing costs, and more leveraging headroom for the combined entity. “(c) Improvement in credit profile which will lead to reduction in borrowing costs;”
- *Scheme* — A second stated benefit is compliance simplification — collapsing ten separate legal entities removes duplicated filings and regulatory obligations across Gujarat, Maharashtra and multiple state regimes. “(e) Simplification of corporate structure by reducing the multiplicity of legal and regulatory compliances”
- *Scheme* — No consideration shares are issued: all transferor equity held by APL (and APDL's holding in KPGL) is cancelled and extinguished, so there is no dilution and no value transfer to any outside party — an intra-group tidy-up, not a transaction with external economics. “all the equity shares issued by the First Transferor Company, the Third Transferor Company, the Fourth Transferor Company, the Fifth Tra nsferor Company, the Sixth Transferor Company, the Seventh Transferor Company, the Eighth Transferor Company, the Ninth Transferor Company and the Tenth Transferor Company , respectively, and held by the Transferee Company and/or its nominees shall stand cancelled and extinguished and in lieu thereof, there shall be no allotment of equity shares in the Transferee Company.”
- *Scheme* — Because only wholly owned subsidiaries are being merged, Regulation 37 of SEBI LODR did not apply and no stock-exchange no-objection was needed — the Scheme was filed only for disclosure, which is why minority shareholders were never asked to vote on it. “Since Regulation 37 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 ("SEBI LODR") does not apply to amalgamation of a wholly owned subsidiary into its holding company, the Transferee Company was not required to obtain a 'no -objection letter' from the Stock Exchange s.”
- *Scheme* — The Vidarbha leg carried the Scheme's only real baggage: a negative net worth and an auditor Emphasis of Matter tied to its CIRP, which APL answered by pointing to its own positive net worth and the clean-slate IBC acquisition; VIPL's Rs 1,471.76 crore securities premium was reduced to nil in FY2025-26. “Further, pursuant to the approved resolution plan, the securities premium reserve of the Tenth Transferor Company amounting to Rs.1,471.76 crore has been reduced to Nil during FY 2025 -26 by way of capital reduction as per resolution plan approved by the Hon'ble NCLT.”
- *CALL Aug 2025* — The CFO gave the clearest management-voiced logic for pulling subsidiaries into the parent rather than separating them: the Jharkhand amalgamation moved Godda's 1,600 MW into the standalone entity and produced a rating upgrade to AA Stable with lower finance costs. “Another key development during the quarter was the amalgamation of Adani Power (Jharkhand ) Limited . This brings the 1,600 MW God da plant into APL's standalone entity. This has led to an implicit credit rating upgrade of God da to AA Stable , reducing finance costs.”
- *CALL May 2025* — On the 1 May 2025 call the CFO quantified the rating arbitrage of merging a subsidiary up: the standalone Jharkhand entity was rated BBB, and post-amalgamation the combined APL facilities are rated AA. “Adani Power (Jharkhand) was rated as BBB level. However, after this amalgamation, the combined facilities of Adani Power and Adani (Jharkhand) within the standalone entity of APL are now rated as AA level.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No call or filing explains the CIPL sale's rationale, valuation basis, or use of proceeds; no demerger/spin-off was ever proposed, discussed, or requested by investors, lenders or partners.

**PROBABLE** (a filing's text names a demerger; no scheme filing names it yet) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 2.9/10 · spin-off · 1 filing(s) from NSE-deep · first 2026-03-16, latest 2026-03-16

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** The EPC business (EPC vertical), demerged into a separately listed entity; described as already completed, not newly announced — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* not stated for the new entity; in the parent, Shekhar Bajaj (promoter) holds 18,14,639 shares (1.57%), Pooja Anant Bajaj (promoter group) 15,41,875 shares (1.34%)
- *What it reveals:* Separation left a two-segment parent: Consumer Products (FY26 revenue ₹3,343 crore, negative EBIT) versus Lighting Solutions (₹1,120 crore, record 8.5% EBIT margin); parent debt-free, ₹934 crore cash, negative working capital
- *Selling pressure:* unclear — not stated; documents mention the demerger only in passing, with no size, index or shareholder-distribution detail
- *Parent or spin:* unclear · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* The demerger scheme and the demerged EPC entity's own filings and financials — absent from this document set
- *In their words:* “During his tenure with the Company, he has played a key role in several strategic and transformational initiatives, including the successful execution of a ₹350 crore rights issue, the demerger of the EPC business into a separately listed entity, the institutionalization of key financial and governance policies, and the evaluation of strategic investments and brand acquisitions.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Across these texts the only business separation management actually explains is the carve-out of the Nirlep brand/business, announced as an in-principle board approval on the Q1FY26 call (Aug 7, 2025), where MD & CEO Sanjay Sachdeva said the Nirlep business "currently has a drag on our financial results." CFO E.C. Prasad gave three specific reasons: Nirlep runs a "totally different GTM" / go-to-market with "no synergy" to the core Bajaj business, its factories were making losses, and the company had concluded that "instead of focusing too much on different spaces, it is better to concentrate on our core" — i.e. the separation is a focus-and-loss-elimination move, not a value-unlocking demerger. Management was explicit on scope: the cooker/cookware category continues under the Bajaj brand, and only the Nirlep brand is being put up for "alternatives" (Vishal Chadha, Aug 2025); by Nov 2025 Chadha confirmed Nirlep had declined at brand level while Bajaj grew. The initiative was management/board-driven — Prasad's "we have realized" — with no lender, investor or licensing partner named as requesting it. The cited precedent is the already-completed separation of the EPC business: BEL carried "over 2,000 crores in debt" and "numerous pending EPC orders" five years earlier, became debt-free by March 2022, and demerged EPC into Bajel Projects Limited in September 2023, which Shekhar Bajaj said means "BEL is now purely a consumer Company" and called "a great success both in terms of data [distinct] identity and focus for the 2 distinct businesses and has resulted in fact, on market capitalization"; the post-demerger split of the 1981 employee welfare trust was done 67:33, "the net worth ratio of the Bajel and BEL at that point in time" (May 2025). Investors reinforced the logic retrospectively rather than requesting it: Anuj Sehgal (Manas) noted that when "the EPC business was part of the company... the allocation of costs was an issue," while still complaining the consumer margins stayed in low single digits. Notably, the opposite move was made on brands the company wanted to keep: in Oct/Nov 2025 the board principally approved acquiring the Morphy Richards brand after 18 years of licensing with 12–13 years left, because, per Shekhar Bajaj, if BEL built it to "a level of INR 1,000 crores" the licensor could "suddenly... say we don't want to deal with you" and "all our effort to create the brand... goes down the drain." The Consumer Products and Lighting Solutions verticals are run and reported separately (Lighting "crafted a separate vertical in 2022," carved out under the departing CFO) and Lighting is being expanded in-house into switchgear, solar and wires — but no legal separation of those two is proposed anywhere in these texts.

**How it evolved:** The idea surfaced on the Q1FY26 call (Aug 7, 2025) as an in-principle approval to restructure Nirlep described as a drag on results, with the no-synergy / different-GTM / loss-making-factories rationale given only in Q&A, and the scope narrowed in the same call to the Nirlep brand with cookers staying under Bajaj. On the Q2FY26 call (Oct 31, 2025), asked to quantify the one-time impact, Prasad said "we don't see any major impact," that the company was "still evaluating the various possibilities," and would update "as and when we are closer to the deal" — the last substantive update; Nirlep's decline at brand level was disclosed on the same call. The Q3FY26 (Feb 9, 2026) and Q4FY26 (May 20, 2026) calls do not mention Nirlep or any separation at all, and the Oct 5, 2026 postal-ballot filing's list of corrective steps omits it. The EPC demerger is referenced only retrospectively — at the management-change call (Jul 22, 2024), the Q1FY25 call (Aug 6, 2024), the trust-bifurcation answer (May 12, 2025) and the CFO's farewell (Oct 31, 2025).

**What management expects from it:** For BEL: removal of a drag on results, focus on core ('concentrate on our core'), cookers retained under the Bajaj brand; no quantified margin, capital or valuation benefit given. From the earlier EPC demerger: debt-free balance sheet, distinct identity and focus for two businesses, and a gain in market capitalisation.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=3fff447f-627d-4ada-9556-ebf63c2a0783.pdf)* — First disclosure of the separation: an in-principle board approval to restructure Nirlep, framed purely as removing a loss-making drag, mentioned alongside the switchgear entry in the CEO's opening remarks. “We have taken an in-principle approval of restructuring our Nirlep business, which currently has a drag on our financial results.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=3fff447f-627d-4ada-9556-ebf63c2a0783.pdf)* — The stated reasons, given by CFO E.C. Prasad in Q&A: a completely different go-to-market, no synergy with the core, and loss-making Nirlep factories — hence 'look at alternatives and concentrate on the core.' “So, Nirlep is a totally different GTM. And we have realized that instead of focusing too much on different spaces, it is better to concentrate on our core, because Nirlep is a totally different go-to-market. There is no synergy, and the factories of Nirlep were making losses. So, that is the reason we thought it is best to look at alternatives and concentrate on the core.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=3fff447f-627d-4ada-9556-ebf63c2a0783.pdf)* — Scope was limited explicitly: the cookware/cooker category is retained under the Bajaj brand; only the Nirlep brand is being separated. “We will continue with the cooker under the Bajaj brand. What we are saying is that we will be looking at alternatives for the Nirlep brand.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=b9d87e6a-b11a-4d7f-9b1d-4c8842ae228f.pdf)* — Asked directly to quantify the one-time financial impact and the post-restructuring effect, management declined — no deal, no structure and no numbers, only 'various possibilities' under evaluation. “So as of now, where we stand, we don't see any major impact. We are still evaluating the various possibilities. And as and when we are closer to the deal, we'll let you know.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=b9d87e6a-b11a-4d7f-9b1d-4c8842ae228f.pdf)* — Supporting evidence for the separation inside kitchen appliances: while Bajaj-branded kitchen grew across mixers, induction and kettles, Nirlep declined at brand level. “At a brand level, Nirlep has seen a decline, and Bajaj has seen growth.”
- *[Jul 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=f33035e6-57df-47aa-9eeb-8c2493fbdc94.pdf)* — The precedent separation, recounted at the MD-exit call: over ₹2,000 crore of debt and pending EPC orders led to debt-free status by March 2022 and the September 2023 demerger of EPC into Bajel Projects, leaving BEL a pure consumer company. “Additionally in September '23, we successfully demerged our EPC business creating Bajel Projects Limited, which means BEL is now purely a consumer Company.”
- *[Aug 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=82bfb72f-77fc-4e64-8503-08d91cea48e0.pdf)* — Chairman Shekhar Bajaj's stated outcome of the EPC demerger — separate identity, focus for two distinct businesses, and a market-capitalisation benefit. “The recent demerger of EPC Projects business, as you will appreciate, has been a great success both in terms of data identity and focus for the 2 distinct businesses and has resulted in fact, on market capitalization.”

Now, of course, that also has been demerged.”

Prasad's resignation, the Chairman listed the structural separations as his legacy — the EPC demerger, the debt-free balance sheet and the internal carve-out of Lighting Solutions as a separate vertical (created 2022). “Under his leadership, he led the demerger of the EPC vertical, transformed BEL into a debt-free company, carved out a Lighting Solution vertical, and streamlined our overall business model.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=838af522-ba54-43ad-9f3d-ebcd1c2087d7.pdf)* — Residual post-demerger housekeeping quantifies the relative size of the separated entities: the 1981 employee welfare trust (and its trustees) was split 67:33 on the Bajel/BEL net-worth ratio at demerger, which also explains a new joint-venture line on the balance sheet. “But now after that thing has settled down, we have decided that the trust would also be bifurcated in the ratio of 67 % to 33%, which was the net worth ratio of the Bajel and BEL at that point in time.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=b9d87e6a-b11a-4d7f-9b1d-4c8842ae228f.pdf)* — The mirror-image transaction: rather than separating Morphy Richards, the board principally approved buying the brand after 18 years of licensing (12–13 years left), to remove licensor termination risk and save a royalty the company refused to quantify as competitively sensitive; Prasad said it is 'value accretive from day one.' “The issue is that by then, we hope that, suppose after so many years, our brand becomes very popular, and we do -- we reach a level of INR 1,000 crores. And then suddenly, they say we don't want to deal with you.”
- *Scheme* — No scheme of arrangement, demerger scheme or separation filing is present in the material supplied: the Oct 5, 2026 filing is a postal ballot on the PSOP-2023 option pool (5,75,510 to 30,02,559 options) and on revised remuneration for Shekhar Bajaj, Sanjay Sachdeva and Pooja Bajaj, and the Mar 16, 2026 filing is the appointment of Suketu Shah as interim CFO. The postal ballot's own 'Steps taken or proposed to be taken for improvement' lists channel-inventory normalisation (channel days down ~30%), 2–5% price increases from Feb 1, 2026, cost rationalisation, distribution optimisation, portfolio expansion into switchgear/solar/wires and brand investment — and no business separation. “Portfolio expansion: Entry into adjacent categories within the Lighting Solutions vertical, including Switchgear (Q2 FY 2025-26), Solar Solutions (Q3 FY 2025-26) and Wires (February 2026), to build an integrated portfolio leveraging the Company's brand strength and distribution reach for long-term sustainable growth.”
