## CAPILLARY — Capillary Technologies India Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a subsidiary's listing is in motion (DRHP / board approval)) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 2.9/10 · partial spin-off / listing · 1 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-02-10, latest 2026-02-10

> **Listing:** IPO / listing of the subsidiary in motion since 2026-02-10; date not fixed

**The stages, as filed:** meetings (2026-02-10)

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Nothing is spun off; a non-operative China subsidiary was deregistered and ceased being a step-down subsidiary — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* not stated
- *What it reveals:* Nothing: revenue Nil and net worth 0.50 million for FY ended March 31, 2026; not a material subsidiary; no impact on business operations, revenue or financial position of the Company or group
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — No shares are being distributed or listed; an empty non-operative shell was deregistered, not separated to shareholders
- *Parent or spin:* neither · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Red Herring Prospectus dated November 18, 2025, for the disclosed closure of China operations
- *In their words:* “Capillary Shanghai is not a material subsidiary of the Company, and its cessation does not have any impact on the business operations, revenue, or financial position of the Company or its group.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

On the texts supplied, Capillary is not separating, demerging or spinning off any business, and no scheme of arrangement, slump sale or business-transfer document is present — so no management rationale for one exists to reconstruct. The only corporate separation of any kind disclosed is the November 2, 2026 intimation that Capillary Technologies (Shanghai) Co., Ltd., a non-operative step-down wholly-owned subsidiary, has completed voluntary deregistration in China; the company's stated reasons are simply that it 'was not carrying on any business operations', that its proposed closure had already been flagged in the RHP dated November 18, 2025, and that it is not a material subsidiary. The quantified impact given is nil: FY26 revenue 'Nil' and net worth of INR 0.50 million, with the Annexure A disclosure marking consideration, buyer, agreement date and 'outside Scheme of Arrangement' all as 'NA' — i.e. no sale, no consideration, no counterparty. Both earnings calls (February 6, 2026 for Q3 FY26 and May 6, 2026 for Q4/FY26) run in the opposite direction: management describes consolidating businesses in, not out — four completed acquisitions (Persuade, Brierley, Rewards, Kognitiv in May 2025) plus the $35 million SessionM merchant-loyalty business bought from Mastercard at ~0.5x revenue, announced February 24 and closed May 1, 2026, taking the group toward $115 million ARR, and 'a couple of other letters of intent' outstanding. The only 'separations' management discusses are platform sunsets inside the group — one of Brierley's two platforms 'fully sunset' in Q3 FY26 — done to lift gross margin from ~30% on acquired stacks to 65–70% on Capillary, not to separate a business from the listed entity. Management does segment the P&L for investors (loyalty stack ~90% of revenue, Engage and Rewards each ~5–7%, aiRA a few million dollars, ~INR 80–100 crores of the INR 735 crores being low-margin acquisition revenue, organic NRR 114–115% vs inorganic 94–96%), and Aneesh Reddy said 'We'll probably change the slides hopefully next time' to show core and inorganic margins separately — but that is disclosure presentation, not a legal or structural separation. No investor, lender or partner on either call asked for a separation; the questions were on margins, ACV-to-ARR bridge, AI disruption, US healthcare payer exposure and cost leverage. Treating the China deregistration as a 'business separation' would misread it: it is housekeeping on a dormant shell already disclosed pre-IPO.

**How it evolved:** The idea never surfaced as a separation: on the February 6, 2026 Q3 FY26 call management framed the group as a roll-up ('let's go buy some of these competitors at 0.5x to 1.5x revenue'), with two LOIs live and Brierley's second platform sunset. On the May 6, 2026 Q4/FY26 call the direction was reinforced — SessionM acquired from Mastercard and closed May 1, 2026, FY27 revenue guided to INR 1,000–1,050 crores — with only a promise to split core versus acquired margins in future slides. The November 2, 2026 filing then completed the one separation in the record: deregistration of the dormant Capillary Shanghai, a step already disclosed in the RHP dated November 18, 2025, so the plan did not evolve, it simply closed out.

**What management expects from it:** Nothing is claimed for a business separation, because none is proposed. For the China deregistration the company states zero effect: no impact on operations, revenue or financial position, nil FY26 revenue, INR 0.50 million net worth, no consideration. Margin, capital and valuation benefits management does cite come from acquiring and migrating customers onto one platform — 30% to 65–70% gross margin, 45% contribution margin, four-to-five-year cash payback.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *FILING 2026-11-02 · Closure of operations* — The only separation disclosed is the completed voluntary deregistration of Capillary Technologies (Shanghai) Co., Ltd., justified solely on the basis that the entity had no operations and the closure was pre-flagged in the RHP dated November 18, 2025. “Capillary Shanghai was not carrying on any business operations, and its proposed closure was disclosed in the RHP.”
- *FILING 2026-11-02 · Closure of operations* — Materiality is expressly denied — no revenue, earnings or balance-sheet consequence for the company or group, and Annexure A shows FY26 revenue 'Nil' and net worth of INR 0.50 million, with sale agreement, consideration, buyer and scheme-of-arrangement fields all 'NA'. “Capillary Shanghai is not a material subsidiary of the Company, and its cessation does not have any impact on the business operations, revenue, or financial position of the Company or its group.”
- *CALL May 2026* — Strategy on the latest call is acquisition and consolidation, not separation: the SessionM merchant-loyalty business was bought from Mastercard (announced Feb 24, closed May 1, 2026) at about 0.5x revenue, $35 million of revenue, 40+ logos, five Fortune 500 customers, pushing the group toward $115 million ARR. “We closed that transaction on May 1st. So it's a sizeable $35 million business, 40 plus logos, including five Fortune 500 companies.”
- *CALL May 2026* — Management's framing of the two 'parts' of the business is a margin-reporting distinction, not a structural one — core Capillary revenue carries essentially all EBITDA while roughly INR 80–100 crores of FY26's INR 735 crores is acquisition-linked low-margin revenue, and the only action promised is a change to the slides. “For the organic platform side, you will continue to see this 2%, 3% more margin growth and probably that's a better way to show it.”
- *CALL Feb 2026* — The stated purpose of the M&A machine is to absorb competitors and migrate their customers onto one platform, moving gross margin from ~30% on acquired stacks to 69–70% on Capillary and paying back purchase price in four to five years — the economics of combining, not separating. “So what we've done is we say let's go buy some of these competitors at 0.5x to 1.5x revenue and migrate those customers over ourselves.”
- *CALL Feb 2026* — The only businesses being 'separated out' are acquired legacy platforms being shut down inside the group, with Brierley (bought 2023) having one of its two platforms fully sunset in Q3 FY26 to release gross margin and below-the-line technology cost. “Like for example, the last quarter we got done with the Brierley, which was one of the companies that we bought in 2023 had two platforms, so one of those platfo rms is fully sunset now.”
- *CALL Feb 2026* — No investor, analyst, lender or partner on either call asked about a demerger, spin-off or carve-out; questions covered AI disruption risk, US healthcare payer exposure, cost leverage, the ACV-to-ARR bridge and aiRA monetisation, and management added that it intends to stay confined to loyalty rather than hive anything off. “No, we will obviously monetize this actively, but we'll stay in the loyalty space only.”

*Not explained on the calls:* Everything a separation rationale would need: no scheme, no business identified for separation, no entity structure, record date, valuation, consideration, lender or investor demand, or Scheme document.

## GAIL — GAIL (India) Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a subsidiary's listing is in motion (DRHP / board approval)) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 2.9/10 · partial spin-off / listing · 2 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-07-31, latest 2026-10-30

> **Listing:** IPO / listing of the subsidiary in motion since 2026-07-31; date not fixed

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** GAIL Gas Limited, GAIL's wholly owned city gas distribution subsidiary, listed via IPO diluting up to 25% — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* GGL is a wholly owned subsidiary of GAIL; GAIL dilutes equity in GGL upto 25%, retaining at least 75%. No management incentives stated.
- *What it reveals:* GGL Q3 FY26 turnover Rs.3,292 crore, PBT Rs.143 crore, PAT Rs.106 crore, 7.8 MMSCMD volume, 12,46,000 DPNG connections, 674 CNG stations; plus six GAs (0.55 MMSCMD, 215 CNG stations) transferred in by slump sale effective 01.01.2027.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — IPO route sells shares to willing subscribers; no distribution to GAIL shareholders, no index exclusion stated.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* GGL's final IPO proposal to GAIL Board on valuation, price band, extent of dilution and modality
- *In their words:* “This is to inform that GAIL Board in its meeting held today i.e. 30.10.2026 accorded in-principle approval for Listing of shares of GAIL Gas Limited, (a wholly owned subsidiary of GAIL) (GGL) on the Indian stock exchanges through Initial Public Offering (IPO) route by diluting GAIL's equity in GGL upto 25%.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The business being separated is GAIL's own directly-authorised city gas distribution (CGD) retail business — the six geographical areas Varanasi, Patna, Ranchi, East Singhbhum (Jamshedpur), Cuttack and Khordha (Bhubaneswar) — which the Board resolved to hive down into its 100% subsidiary GAIL Gas Limited as a slump sale on a going-concern basis, effective 01.01.2027, with the subsidiary then to be listed via IPO diluting up to 25% of GAIL's equity. Management's stated reason was structural, not financial distress: CMD Sandeep Kumar Gupta said it was 'in order to have a single entity for development of GAIL's CGD business and for bringing business synergy, efficiency and retail focused business approach' — i.e. GAIL group CGD was split across GAIL's own balance sheet (six GAs, 0.36–0.55 MMSCMD, 195→215 CNG stations and 3.53→4.64 lakh DPNG connections over FY25–Q3FY26, volumes up ~25% in FY25 but 'currently in their early stages of development'), GAIL Gas (16 GAs plus 9 JVs, 7.0→7.8 MMSCMD, 12.46 lakh DPNG connections, 674 CNG stations, FY25 turnover Rs 12,231 crore, PBT Rs 615 crore up 42%, PAT Rs 451 crore up 40%) and 72 group GAs in all. A pipeline-and-marketing parent was also an awkward owner of a retail business: management said 'we are constantly reviewing these CGDs to optimize costs and enhance efficiencies', and segment reporting of the CGD/marketing split was itself confusing analysts (the Rs 400 crore standalone-to-consolidated regrouping queried in Jul 2025). The upside case cited was CGD demand: a PNGRB projection of consumption rising '2.5 times to 3.5 times by 2030 and 6 times to 7 times by 2040 from the baseline of approximately 37 MMSCMD in FY 24' (~15% CAGR), PNGRB capping CNG/domestic-PNG tariffs at Zone 1 and expected GST inclusion lowering CGD input costs. For the IPO, the argument was scale and timing — 'GAIL Gas is one of the biggest company in the country in terms of city gas distribution... now is high time that we started the process of listing GAIL Gas' — with a consultant already selected and a roughly one-year timeline. The impetus came largely from sell-side investors (Citi's Saurabh Handa on restructuring CGD investments in Nov 2024; Alliance Services' Balaji Das on the IPO consultant in Oct 2025); the only external consent management named was CCEA, 'since these six GAs were authorized to GAIL by CCEA' — no lender or JV-partner demand was cited. Running in the opposite direction, GAIL simultaneously pulled Konkan LNG Limited in: it bought out MSEB Holding's 7,40,55,220 shares via a NCLT-approved capital reduction (paid 06.07.2026, GAIL to 100%) and then merged KLL (FY26 turnover Rs 741 crore, versus GAIL's Rs 1,41,483 crore) into GAIL to 'create a larger and stronger vertically integrated entity, simplify and rationalize group structure'.

**How it evolved:** The idea first surfaced only as an unprompted analyst question on the Nov 06, 2024 Q2 FY25 call, where R.K. Jain said no call had been taken on restructuring GAIL Gas — 'this is in our mind, but nothing concrete' — while adding that GAIL was 'looking for listing one or two JVs'; the Jan 30, 2025 call did not touch it. It became concrete at the May 14, 2025 annual analyst meet, where the CMD disclosed the Board's recommendation (passed 13.05.2025) to transfer the six GAs to GAIL Gas for a 'single entity... retail focused business approach', subject to CCEA. On Oct 31, 2025 the second leg appeared: GAIL confirmed it had started the GAIL Gas listing process, had selected a consultant, and expected 'a one year time line or so'; the Feb 02, 2026 Q3 FY26 call was silent on both. The filings then executed it: 31.07.2026 KLL merger into GAIL, and 30.10.2026 Board approval of the six-GA slump sale effective 01.01.2027 plus in-principle approval of a GAIL Gas IPO diluting up to 25%.

**What management expects from it:** One consolidated, retail-focused CGD entity with business synergy and efficiency; the six early-stage GAs (0.55 MMSCMD) folded into GAIL Gas's 7.8 MMSCMD platform (674 CNG stations, 12.46 lakh DPNG) to capture CGD demand rising 2.5–3.5x by 2030, aided by Zone-1 tariff capping and expected GST; price discovery and capital via an IPO of up to 25%. Parent keeps transmission/marketing; Konkan LNG's merger simplifies the group and adds its cargo-driven profit.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Nov 2024](https://gailonline.com/pdf/InvestorsZone/GAIL_Earnings_Call_Q2_FY25_11112024.pdf)* — Citi's Saurabh Handa raised the split of CGD investments between GAIL standalone and GAIL Gas and asked whether GAIL would restructure them — the first time the idea appears in the record. “On your City Gas investments, whether they are at the standalone entity or in GAIL Gas? Is there any thought process to look at restructuring these streamline these investments?”
- *[Nov 2024](https://gailonline.com/pdf/InvestorsZone/GAIL_Earnings_Call_Q2_FY25_11112024.pdf)* — Director (Finance) R.K. Jain confirmed restructuring was under internal consideration but that no decision existed, while separately flagging that GAIL was working on listing one or two JVs with an update promised in Q3. “As a company about GAIL Gas has not yet taken any call for restructuring of GAIL Gas. This is in our mind, but nothing concrete I can share with you right now.”
- *[Nov 2024](https://gailonline.com/pdf/InvestorsZone/GAIL_Earnings_Call_Q2_FY25_11112024.pdf)* — Alongside CGD restructuring, Jain said listing of group entities was already in progress and at 'a good stage', promising an update in Q3 FY25. “So also, we are looking for listing one or two JVs, which we are in the process and once we move forward and we take a call, we'll come back to you, but that we are certainly working and we are in a good stage.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.gailonline.com/pdf/InvestorsZone/GAIL%20Analysts%20Meet%20Q4%20FY25%2014.05.2025.pdf)* — CMD Sandeep Kumar Gupta disclosed the Board's 13.05.2025 recommendation to transfer GAIL's six directly-held CGD geographical areas to wholly-owned GAIL Gas Limited — the core rationale being one single, synergistic, retail-focused CGD entity. “In order to have a single entity for development of GAIL's CGD business and for bringing business synergy, efficiency and retail focused business approach, the Board has recommended to transfer six geographical areas of GAIL to its wholly owned subsidiary, GAIL Gas Limited.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.gailonline.com/pdf/InvestorsZone/GAIL%20Analysts%20Meet%20Q4%20FY25%2014.05.2025.pdf)* — The only approval condition management named was CCEA, because the six GAs (Varanasi, Patna, Ranchi, Jamshedpur, Bhubaneswar, Cuttack) had been awarded to GAIL by CCEA rather than won by GAIL Gas. “This is subject to approval of CCEA since these six GAs were authorized to GAIL by CCEA.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.gailonline.com/pdf/InvestorsZone/GAIL%20Analysts%20Meet%20Q4%20FY25%2014.05.2025.pdf)* — The six GAs were described as early-stage but fast-growing (volumes up ~25% in FY25, then ~0.4–0.45 MMSCMD) and under continuous cost review — the sub-scale retail assets being pushed into the dedicated CGD vehicle. “In the Financial Year 24-25, these six GAs have shown impressive growth with volumes increasing by approximately 25%. We are constantly reviewing these CGDs to optimize costs and enhance efficiencies.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.gailonline.com/pdf/InvestorsZone/GAIL%20Analysts%20Meet%20Q4%20FY25%2014.05.2025.pdf)* — The growth case for a standalone CGD entity rested on PNGRB's demand projection, supplemented by PNGRB's proposal to cap CNG/domestic-PNG tariffs at Zone 1 and expected GST inclusion to cut CGD input costs. “the CGD sector is anticipated to be the key driver of growth, with consumption expected to increase 2.5 times to 3.5 times by 2030 and 6 times to 7 times by 2040 from the baseline of approximately 37 MMSCMD in FY '24”
- *[May 2025](https://www.gailonline.com/pdf/InvestorsZone/GAIL%20Analysts%20Meet%20Q4%20FY25%2014.05.2025.pdf)* — GAIL Gas's own FY25 numbers framed the receiving entity as a scaled, improving business: turnover Rs 12,231 crore, PBT Rs 615 crore (+42%), PAT Rs 451 crore (+40%), 16 GAs owned plus 9 JVs. “During the current financial year, that is FY '25, GAIL Gas Limited's turnover stood at Rs. 12,231 crores as against Rs. 10,944 crores in FY '24. PBT increased by 42% and stood at Rs. 615 crores as against Rs. 434 crores in FY '24.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.gailonline.com/pdf/InvestorsZone/GAIL%20Analysts%20Meet%20Q4%20FY25%2014.05.2025.pdf)* — On the other entity later consolidated in, management said Konkan LNG (Dabhol) would swing to profit once the all-weather breakwater let it run 34–36 cargoes versus 21, worth roughly Rs 300 crore. “So this year certainly we were not in positive because of the breakwater issue. But going forward, we will have positive bottom line from KLL.”
- *Oct 2025* — An investor (Balaji Das) pressed on the GAIL Gas IPO and the consultant being hired for listing analysis, confirming the second leg of the plan was investor-driven. “And the second question is on, we had like on the listing of the GAIL Gas IPO actually. So, any further progress on consultant and when are the future plans actually for GAIL Gas actually, because we heard that we are hiring consultants for analysis of listing.”
- *Oct 2025* — Jain confirmed the listing process had begun — consultant selected, order imminent — and justified it on GAIL Gas's scale: 7.72 MMSCMD of volume and more GAs than any peer, with Bangalore alone at 1 MMSCMD. “And we in GAIL believe that now is high time that we started the process of listing GAIL Gas, in that regard we have already started the process of hiring of consultant.”
- *Oct 2025* — He put a roughly one-year timeline on the listing, contingent on the consultant's study — the only timing guidance given on the IPO. “So, we are on a path to study about listing of GAIL Gas and after conclusion of that study, certainly that study is very important for us, we expect a one year time line or so should be good enough.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No valuation, slump-sale consideration, IPO size or use of proceeds, standalone margin/ROCE or capex targets, CCEA timing, or why 25%; calls after Oct 2025 went silent.

## IEX — Indian Energy Exchange Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a subsidiary's listing is in motion (DRHP / board approval)) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 2.9/10 · partial spin-off / listing · 1 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-07-15, latest 2026-07-15

> **Listing:** IPO / listing of the subsidiary in motion since 2026-07-15; date not fixed — DRHP dated July 14, 2026 filed with SEBI and BSE on July 14, 2026 (filing July 15, 2026); 'they filed the DRHP in this month and hopefully (would be) getting listed soon' (July 24, 2026); PNGRB extension to bring holding to 25% runs to December 31, 2026 (stated April 24, 2026).

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Indian Gas Exchange (IGX), IEX's 47.3%-held natural gas spot exchange associate, partly sold via IPO — class `regulatory_strategic`.

- *Insiders:* IEX holds 47.3% of IGX and offers for sale up to 16,710,000 shares (22.3%), retaining 25%; management refused any IEX-shareholder reservation, calling it an independent IPO. Other incentives not stated.
- *What it reveals:* IGX is India's only natural gas exchange: FY26 volume 76.8 million MMBtu, PAT Rs 42 crore (up 28-35%), ~3% of India's gas consumption and 20% of the spot market, 40%+ volume CAGR, embedded inside IEX's Rs 492-493 crore consolidated profit.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — Listing is an IPO offer for sale by IEX, not a distribution of IGX shares to IEX shareholders; buyers self-select.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* IGX's DRHP dated July 14, 2026 — offer size, IGX standalone financials and post-offer shareholding.
- *In their words:* “As you may be aware that we have already filed a DRHP (Draft Red Herring Prospectus) for IPO of IGX as we today hold 47.3% in IGX.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The separation here is not a demerger of IEX's own operations but the carve-out of its gas arm, Indian Gas Exchange (IGX), via an offer-for-sale IPO, driven purely by PNGRB's exchange ownership rules, which cap any single shareholder at 25% and any trading member at 5%. IEX held 47.3%-47.5% of IGX and had to cut that to 25% within five years; that five-year window expired in December 2025, so IEX took a one-year extension from PNGRB, now running to 31 December 2026. Management said the original slippage was commercial, not strategic: 'there were huge challenges in the gas market and gas exchange' and the 'business ramp-up has not happened at the rate at which we were expecting it' (Nov 2025). With IGX now scaled - FY26 volume 76.8 million MMBtu (+28% YoY, over 40% CAGR), PAT Rs 41.9-42 crore (+35%), roughly 3% of India's gas consumption and 20% of the spot market, 23 delivery points versus 4 in FY22 and 10 contract types versus 6 - IEX chose the IPO over other divestment options and formally asked IGX to proceed. The DRHP was filed on 14 July 2026 with SEBI and BSE as a pure offer for sale of up to 16,710,000 shares by IEX, i.e. the 22.3% it must shed; no fresh issue, proceeds or valuation was discussed. The same ownership-cap logic makes IEX house each new commodity in its own company: Indian Coal Exchange Ltd was incorporated in June 2026 with board approval, a mineral exchange company is planned, and its shareholding rules are 'similar to what has been notified for the power exchange and the gas exchange.' The only parties asking for the separation were regulators (PNGRB; the Ministry of Coal rules for the coal exchange) - not investors, lenders or partners; investors asked only about timing and for a proportionate reservation in the IGX IPO, which Goel refused because it is 'an independent IPO'. Separately, management rejected the analyst suggestion that the exchange's clearing and settlement function must be hived into its own entity, saying the PSS Act requires registration, not separation, with no financial impact.

**How it evolved:** The idea surfaced on the Nov 2025 call (31 Oct 2025), where Goel disclosed the 25% PNGRB deadline of December 2025, blamed the slow gas-market ramp-up for the delay, said the regulator had assured an extension (IEX asked for eighteen months), and that IEX was 'considering different options for divestment'. By the Feb 2026 call (30 Jan 2026) the option had narrowed to an IPO: IEX had asked IGX to proceed, targeting completion within the year subject to SEBI clearance. On the Apr 2026 call (24 Apr 2026) the extension was confirmed to 31 December 2026 and the process was 'progressing well'. The DRHP followed on 14 July 2026, and at the Jul 2026 analyst meet (24 Jul 2026) Goel sized it as a 22.3% sell-down while also disclosing that Indian Coal Exchange Ltd had been incorporated in June 2026 as a separate company.

**What management expects from it:** Compliance first: IEX falls to 25% of IGX, keeping an associate stake in a business they expect to grow volumes 25-30% annually as gas prices fall; IGX gets its own listing and price. Each new commodity (coal, minerals) sits in its own company under the same 25%/5% ownership caps. No margin, capital or valuation benefit for IEX was claimed.

## NIACL — The New India Assurance Company Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a subsidiary's listing is in motion (DRHP / board approval)) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 2.9/10 · partial spin-off / listing · 1 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-09-09, latest 2026-09-09

> **Listing:** IPO / listing of the subsidiary in motion since 2026-09-09; date not fixed — Filing of 9 September 2026: shares transferred to the "Escrow Account" on 08th September 2026; "The expected date of completion of sale/disposal: End of September 2026 (As indicated by NSE)"

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** No business is separated; NIACL sells 1,05,00,000 equity shares of National Stock Exchange of India Ltd via offer for sale — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* not stated
- *What it reveals:* NIACL's NSEIL holding paid Rs 123,20,00,000 dividend in FY2025-26; the IPO puts a market price on the stake, of which only 29.83% is tendered, leaving roughly 70% held and still unpriced on NIACL's books.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — No shares distributed to NIACL holders; stake monetised for cash through an offer for sale in NSE's IPO
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* NSE IPO prospectus/price band, to value the 70% NSEIL stake NIACL retains
- *In their words:* “Pursuant to Regulation 30 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, we wish to inform you that The New India Assurance Co. Ltd. proposes to divest 1,05,00,000 equity shares of the National Stock Exchange of India Ltd. (NSEIL).”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

These documents do not describe NIACL separating, demerging, spinning off or hiving down any business, and no scheme of arrangement is included — the only separation event in the texts is a financial stake sale. In the 09-Sep-2026 Regulation 30 filing, NIACL disclosed that it 'proposes to divest 1,05,00,000 equity shares of the National Stock Exchange of India Ltd. (NSEIL)', representing 29.83% of the total shares it then held in NSEIL, to be executed as an Offer for Sale through NSE's IPO, subject to regulatory approvals. The filing's own annexure forecloses the 'business separation' reading: it answers 'No' to whether the disposal is outside a Scheme of Arrangement (Reg 37A), 'No' to related-party status, and marks slump-sale disclosures 'Not Applicable'; the only financial magnitude disclosed is the FY2025-26 dividend from NSEIL of Rs 123,20,00,000, i.e. an investment-income metric, not a divisional P&L. Mechanically, the shares were already moved to an Escrow Account on 08 September 2026, completion was expected 'End of September 2026 (As indicated by NSE)', and consideration was to be received only after the OFS concluded — the pattern of a selling shareholder in an IPO, not of a demerger with share entitlement ratios, record dates or a resulting entity. The only call-level trace is the Feb-2026 Q&A, where an analyst noted 'one of your portfolio companies wherein you have a significant holding has just gotten SEBI approval for IPO' and asked about participation; management gave no rationale, replying 'That is in the future, so we will look into it when it comes up.' The nearest thing management did explain at length is not a separation but portfolio exits — walking away from loss-making group mediclaim accounts ('more than nine hundred such accounts we have left in the last year'), roughly Rs 800 crore of business foregone in FY23 and Rs 500 crore in FY24 on price correction, and exits from loss-making motor dealer/CV accounts — all framed as 'growth with profitability' and risk-weighted underwriting, with capital staying inside the same legal entity. Separately, the texts give a plausible monetisation motive for selling holdings generally: of Rs 4,236 crore of profit on sale booked up to Q3FY26, 'Rs. 2,000 crore is pertaining specifically to the wage revision provision', with management stating they 'monetized our investments to help in the provision that we made for the wage revision' (total wage revision ~Rs 2,500 crore, plus Rs 700-800 crore of family pension still to be provided) — but management never linked that motive to the NSEIL sale. No investor, lender or partner is recorded in these texts as having asked for any separation.

**How it evolved:** Nothing resembling a separation appears in the Feb-2024, May-2024, Aug-2024, Nov-2024, Jan-2025, May-2025 or Aug-2025 calls; in Jan-2025 management in fact ruled out structural expansion, saying under a composite licence they have no plans to enter life insurance, and in Nov-2024 said any government-stake dilution awaits Finance Ministry/DFS instructions. The idea first surfaces only obliquely on the Feb-2026 call (02-Feb-2026), as an analyst's question about a portfolio company that had just received SEBI IPO approval, which management declined to address. It crystallises only in the 09-Sep-2026 filing, which converts it into a concrete 1,05,00,000-share (29.83% of holding) Offer for Sale in NSEIL's IPO, with shares already in escrow as of 08-Sep-2026 and completion expected end-September 2026. So the plan did not evolve as a separation thesis at all — it went from an unanswered analyst question to an executed investment divestment, with no stated rationale in between.

**What management expects from it:** Nothing is stated. The filing gives no expected effect on margins, capital, solvency, valuation or focus for NIACL or NSEIL, and no consideration figure — only that proceeds arrive after the OFS completes and that FY26 dividends from the holding were Rs 123.20 crore. On the calls, management declined to discuss the IPO at all.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The only 'separation' in the record is a minority stake sale: 1,05,00,000 NSEIL shares, equal to 29.83% of NIACL's holding, tendered into NSE's IPO as an Offer for Sale, subject to regulatory approvals. “Pursuant to Regulation 30 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, we wish to inform you that The New India Assurance Co. Ltd. proposes to divest 1,05,00,000 equity shares of the National Stock Exchange of India Ltd. (NSEIL).”
- *Scheme* — The filing explicitly states the disposal is NOT outside a Scheme of Arrangement and is not a related-party transaction, and marks slump-sale disclosures not applicable — i.e. there is no demerger, hive-down or business transfer. “Whether the sale, lease or disposal of the undertaking is outside Scheme of Arrangement? If yes, details of the same including compliance with regulation 37A of LODR Regulations No”
- *Scheme* — The only quantification offered is investment income from the holding — the FY2025-26 dividend — rather than any revenue, turnover or net worth of a separated undertaking, confirming this is a portfolio asset, not a business unit. “Total Dividend received from NSEIL inFY 2025-26 was Rs. 123,20,00,000”
- *Scheme* — Execution mechanics are those of an IPO selling shareholder: shares already in escrow on 08-Sep-2026, completion expected end-September 2026 per NSE, consideration only after the OFS completes. “As part of the Offer for Sale process the equity shares have been transferred to the "Escrow Account" on 08th September 2026.”
- *Feb 2026* — The only call-level reference is an analyst's question about a significant portfolio holding that had just cleared SEBI for its IPO; management offered no strategy, intent or rationale. “Madam, one of your portfolio companies wherein you have a significant holding has just gotten SEBI approval for IPO. Do we have a plan to participate in the IPO for that?”
- *Feb 2026* — Management did give a general reason for monetising holdings: funding the wage-revision provision. Of Rs 4,236 crore profit on sale up to Q3FY26, Rs 2,000 crore was attributed specifically to that provision — but this was never tied to the NSEIL sale. “So, the profit on sale that we have realized is around Rs. 4,236 crore. And of this, Rs. 2,000 crore is pertaining specifically to the wage revision provision.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=429f4f78-7367-4477-b1ca-c72efaf5f875.pdf)* — What management does explain as 'exiting businesses' is underwriting portfolio pruning inside the same entity — shedding 900-plus group mediclaim accounts where pricing was inadequate — not a corporate separation. “So, more than nine hundred such accounts we have left in the last year simply to see that we are more profitable on the business that we do.”
- *Feb 2026* — Similarly in motor: deliberate exits from loss-making dealer/OEM and >40,000 GVW commercial-vehicle accounts, accepted as a drag on growth (motor premium -1.18% for 9MFY26) in exchange for ICR repair. “So, the growth on Motor is a little dented because of very strategic and very well-thought-out solutions for these loss-making accounts that we have been suffering from in Motor.”
- *[Jan 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=53cf9d6c-41fc-46d3-ba39-a9706845bba0.pdf)* — Management ruled out the structural expansion that might have implied a separate entity, citing capital needs and long break-even in life insurance. “On the composite license, as of right now, we do not have any plans to foray into life insurance.”

*Not explained on the calls:* Everything: no separation exists in these texts. No rationale, pricing, use of proceeds, solvency or ROE impact, residual 70.17% stake plan, or any management commentary on the NSEIL divestment.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** NLCIL's renewable energy business — 1,430 MW of RE assets transferred to subsidiary NIRL, now to be IPO'd — class `regulatory_strategic`.

- *Insiders:* NIRL is NLCIL's wholly owned subsidiary; NLCIL (a 'Navratna' Government of India Enterprise) offers up to 10 crore shares; its NIRL investment is Rs 5,119.75 crore. Post-IPO stake not stated.
- *What it reveals:* Renewables carries Rs 10,881.76 crore segment assets on only Rs 462.27 crore H1 revenue and Rs 237.08 crore segment result; parent injected Rs 2,000 crore on 12.10.2026; consolidated debt/equity 1.20 vs standalone 0.44.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — IPO with Offer for Sale by the parent, not a distribution of shares to NLCIL holders, so no forced index-driven selling.

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The business being separated is NLC India Limited's renewable energy (solar/wind, plus a 4 MW green hydrogen project) portfolio, which is being hived off out of the lignite-mining-and-thermal parent (NLCIL) into its wholly owned subsidiary NLC India Renewables Limited (NIRL), and then part-sold to the public. The only reason given anywhere in these documents is policy-driven, not strategic-narrative: the financial-result notes say the transfer is being done "In line with the National Monetization Pipeline and in consultation with the Ministry of Coal," under a Business Transfer Agreement with NIRL executed on 31st October 2025 covering 1,430 MW of renewable assets. The mechanics are a slump-sale-style hive-off at book value between holding company and wholly owned subsidiary, explicitly not a scheme of arrangement — the 03.09.2026 filing states "No amalgamation/ merger is envisaged" and that Regulation 37A is therefore inapplicable, with consideration "paid by NIRL in cash /acknowledgement of debt." The size disclosures show why this is about future capital rather than current earnings: the RE assets transferred in Phase II contributed revenue of only Rs. 41.16 crore in FY2025-26, i.e. 0.24% of consolidated revenue of Rs. 17,489.53 crore, while their net worth of Rs. 925.08 crore was 4.30% of the company's Rs. 21,524.76 crore net worth. The separation is being funded and scaled aggressively at the subsidiary level: NLCIL injected Rs. 2,000 crore of fresh equity into NIRL on 12th October 2026 (taking total investment to Rs. 5,119.75 crore), NIRL raised a maiden green loan from Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation of JPY 15.464 billion (USD 100 million) under the ECB framework, and NIRL has spun up its own JV layer — PTC India (2,000 MW, 74:26), OREDA (51:49), NCRTC, SJVNL, MAHAPREIT (DIPAM-approved), Assam and Rajasthan step-down subsidiaries. The end-state is a separate listing: the Board gave in-principle approval for listing NIRL on 12.01.2026 and on 04.11.2026 approved an Offer for Sale of up to 10,00,00,000 equity shares of Rs. 10 each held by NLCIL in NIRL as part of a proposed IPO. The problems this implicitly solves — a renewables segment that is capital-hungry (renewables segment assets grew from Rs. 5,470.15 crore at 30.09.2025 to Rs. 10,881.76 crore at 30.09.2026 while contributing only Rs. 726.06 crore of FY26 segment revenue) sitting inside a regulated, CERC-tariff-bound, lignite-and-coal parent — are nowhere stated in management's own words in these texts.

**How it evolved:** Nothing can be reconstructed call by call: of the seven transcripts supplied, six (Aug 2025, May 2025, Feb 2025, Nov 2024, Aug 2024, Feb 2024) contain no extractable text, and the Feb 2026 item is only the covering letter forwarding the 10.02.2026 transcript link, with no Q&A, so no investor, lender or analyst was recorded asking for the separation and no management explanation of it appears. From the filings alone the sequence is: BTA signed 31.10.2025 for 1,430 MW; Phase I of 7 RE assets transferred with effect from 01.01.2026 (intimated 01.01.2026); Board in-principle approval for listing NIRL on 12.01.2026; the 10.02.2026 press release showing NIRL already borrowing (SMBC green loan) and forming JVs (PTC, OREDA, MAHAPREIT); a second BTA addendum on 03.09.2026 for a further 708.96 MW including a 4 MW green hydrogen plant for Rs. 853.97 crore; Rs. 2,000 crore equity infusion into NIRL on 12.10.2026; and on 04.11.2026 Board approval of an OFS of up to 10 crore NIRL shares as part of NIRL's proposed IPO. The plan therefore widened from an internal asset transfer into a two-phase hive-off plus a third-party-funded, JV-heavy platform headed for its own IPO.

**What management expects from it:** Not stated. No text here gives management's expectations for margins, capital allocation, valuation re-rating or focus for either entity. The filings assert only policy alignment (National Monetization Pipeline, Ministry of Coal), a book-value transfer, and an eventual NIRL IPO/OFS. Observable intent: ring-fenced green debt, JV partners and external equity at NIRL; parent retains mining and thermal.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The stated driver of the hive-off is government asset-monetisation policy, agreed with the administrative ministry, covering 1,430 MW of renewable capacity moved from NLCIL to NIRL under a BTA dated 31 October 2025. “In line with the National Monetization Pipeline and in consultation with the Ministry of Coal, NLCIL executed a Business Transfer Agreement (BT A) with NLC India Renewables Limited on 31st October 2025 for transferring 1,430 MW of renewable energy assets.”
- *Scheme* — Phase I moved seven operating renewable assets to the wholly owned subsidiary with effect from 1 January 2026. “In term of the Regulation 30 and 51 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, we write to inform that the Company has transferred its 7 Renewable Energy Assets ("RE Assets") to NLC India Renewables Limited ("NIRL"), a wholly owned subsidiary of NLC India Limited.”
- *Scheme* — Phase II, agreed by addendum on 3 September 2026, added 708.96 MW still under construction or in operation plus a 4 MW green hydrogen project, for Rs. 853.97 crore based on assets and liabilities as of 1 September 2026. “Addendum to the Business Transfer Agreement with NIRL is signed on 03rd September, 2026 for proposed hiving o ff 708.96 MW of Renewable Energy Assets including a 4 MW Green Hydrogen Project which are at various stages of construction/ operation.”
- *Scheme* — The separated business is tiny in revenue but material in capital: the RE assets transferred earned Rs. 41.16 crore in FY2025-26 (0.24% of consolidated revenue) while carrying net worth of Rs. 925.08 crore (4.30% of group net worth). “Revenue from operational Renewable Energy assets proposed to be transferred was Rs. 41.16 Crore for FY 2025-26, which is 0.24 % of the Company’s revenue of  Rs. 17,489.53 Crore (on consolidated basis) based on Audited Financial Statements of 31st March, 2026.”
- *Scheme* — It is a related-party hive-off done at book value, with consideration in cash or acknowledgement of debt, and deliberately not structured as a court-approved scheme of arrangement, so minority shareholders get no direct shares in NIRL. “No amalgamation/ merger is envisaged. Hence compliance w.r.t. Regulation 37A of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015, is not applicable as the transaction is being entered between the Company and its Wholly Owned Subsidiary i.e. NIRL.”
- *Scheme* — The endgame disclosed is a separate listing of NIRL: in-principle Board approval on 12.01.2026, followed on 04.11.2026 by approval of an Offer for Sale of up to 10 crore NIRL shares held by NLCIL as part of NIRL's proposed IPO. “The Board had earlier, at its meeting held on 12.01.2026, accorded in-principle approval for the listing of NIRL, which was duly intimated.”
- *Scheme* — The parent is pre-funding the subsidiary ahead of that listing, putting Rs. 2,000 crore of fresh equity into NIRL on 12 October 2026 and taking its total investment to Rs. 5,119.75 crore. “The company invested 200,00,00,000 equity shares in NLC India Renewables Limited (NIRL ), wholly owned subsidiary of the company at Rs. IO per share aggregating to Rs. 2,000 crore on 12th October 2026.”
- *Scheme* — NIRL is raising its own third-party, ring-fenced debt — a maiden offshore green loan from SMBC — rather than funding renewables off the parent's balance sheet. “Signed its maiden Green Loan agreement with Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation (SMBC) under the ECB framework , amounting to JPY 15.464 billion (USO 100 million), to fund renewable energy projects through its subsidiary NIRL.”
- *Scheme* — The separate vehicle is being used to take in partners NLCIL could not easily host itself — PTC India for 2,000 MW, plus OREDA, NCRTC, SJVNL, MAHAPREIT (DIPAM-approved) and Assam/Rajasthan step-down subsidiaries. “NIRL signed a JV agreement with PTC India Ltd, for development of 2000 MW of green energy capacity and formation of JV company is in progress.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/corporate/NLCINDIA_16022026185558_Transcripts10022026Signed.pdf)* — No management commentary on the separation is recoverable from this call — the filing supplied is only the covering letter forwarding the transcript link, and the other six transcripts in the window contain no extractable text. “Sub: Regulation 30–Transcript of Investors Conference Call held on 10.02.2026.”

*Not explained on the calls:* Everything about motive: no management words on why, no valuation, margin, debt-shifting or focus argument, no investor/lender/partner demand, no IPO size, timing or use of proceeds.

## OSWALPUMPS — Oswal Pumps Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a subsidiary's listing is in motion (DRHP / board approval)) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 2.9/10 · partial spin-off / listing · 2 filing(s) from NSE · first 2025-11-13, latest 2026-02-07

> **Listing:** IPO / listing of the subsidiary in motion since 2025-11-13; date not fixed

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** not stated — no demerger or separation of any business is disclosed in these documents — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* Promoter Group member Mr Narinder Nath Goela holds 4.30% of Walso Solar post-acquisition; ESOPs of ₹3 millions market value granted to COO Mr Avadesh K. Singh on November 13, 2025; solar module land leased from promoter.
- *What it reveals:* No separation disclosed; instead consolidation — Walso Solar (FY26 turnover INR1,702.65 million) moved from associate to 51% subsidiary, and INR1,598.50 million of IPO proceeds redirected into a captive 1.2 GW solar cell plant (total cost INR4,558.50 million).
- *Selling pressure:* unclear — No demerged or separately listed entity is disclosed, so no index exclusion, size or industry-mismatch flows can be assessed.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* November 13, 2025
- *Read next:* The postal ballot notice on varying IPO objects toward the 1.2 GW Karnal solar cell plant.
- *In their words:* “Consequently, Walso Solar Solution Private Limited has become subsidiary of the Company, effective today.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

There is no business separation in these texts: across all four calls (Aug 2025, Nov 2025, Feb 2026, May 2026) and all four filings, Oswal Pumps never announces a demerger, spin-off, slump sale, scheme of arrangement, or listing of any division — the only entity being separated from the group is a dormant shell, wholly owned subsidiary Oswal Green Private/Industries Private Limited, which the board resolved to strike off because 'it has no significant business operations', with a written-off investment of just INR 0.10 million. Every other structural move runs the opposite way — toward consolidation and deeper backward integration of the same solar-pumping value chain. On 08 June 2026 the company bought an additional 13,07,000 shares of associate Walso Solar Solution Pvt Ltd (mounting structures, BOS, turnkey solar pumping components) at Rs 28/share for Rs 3.66 crore via rights issue, taking it from 38.5% (plus 4.5% on 08 April 2026 and 8% in June) to 51% and converting it from associate into subsidiary, on the stated logic that vertical integration lets the group 'design and develop new products, optimize our operational costs and improve our margins'; Walso's FY26 turnover was INR 1,702.65 million versus INR 720.54 million in FY25. On 10 October 2026 the board approved a greenfield 1.2 GW solar cell plant at Karnal under WOS Oswal Solar Energy Pvt Ltd (formerly Oswal Solar Structure), total project cost INR 4,558.50 million, funded partly by re-directing INR 1,598.50 million of unutilised IPO proceeds away from the Aluminium Frame Facility, the remaining 300 MW EVA encapsulant line and the remaining 500 MW of module capacity, because DCR cells — not frames — are 'the binding constraint', with domestic cell makers offering long-term contracts 'only at elevated prices' and demanding 'very large deposits'; the captive plant is to cover ~75% of cell requirement. Earlier, the December 2025 postal-ballot 'First Variation' merely relocated the module plant to a larger adjacent Karnal parcel (28,000 sq m vs 13,983 sq m, 15-year lease from 25 June 2024) to share workforce, R&D, admin infrastructure and an existing electricity feeder. The one genuinely new legal vehicle is additive, not a carve-out: Oswal Solar Energy incorporated SPV Oswal Doon Baran Bundi Solar Projects Limited with Doon Infrapower Projects Pvt Ltd, holding 60%, to execute HAM rooftop PV on Rajasthan state government buildings. Management's answer to its real problem — single-scheme dependency on PM-KUSUM, whose 2.0 rollout slipped from 'before the end of this fiscal' to June 2026+ — is diversification inside the existing group (rooftop/PM Surya Ghar, utility, C&I, ~300 MW pipeline, exports, private network, in-house inverters), explicitly kept as backward integration and never 'a revenue model', not separation.

**How it evolved:** No separation idea ever surfaces. Aug 2025 describes a fully integrated group (pumps/motors/controllers in-house, modules via Oswal Solar, structures/BOS via 38.5% associate Walso) and a backup plan of exports and private-market pumps if KUSUM 2.0 slips; Nov 2025 adds the module-plant land shift and the Oswal Green strike-off. Feb 2026, after receivable days hit 157 and Maharashtra's Magel Tyala payments stalled, management says the KUSUM 2.0 delay 'brought a point of diversification to our mind' — new verticals, EPC for large rooftops, invoice discounting — all housed internally. May 2026 formalises that with the first PM Surya Ghar order and the 60% Rajasthan HAM SPV, and the October 2026 cell-plant variation pulls capital further into the group rather than out of it.

**What management expects from it:** Nothing is said about a separation. For the moves actually made: absorbing Walso at 51% is to cut operational cost and improve margins; the captive 1.2 GW cell plant is to secure DCR supply, escape elevated contract prices and large deposits, deepen value addition, and strengthen group cost structure, competitive positioning in government programmes and consolidated profitability; the relocated module plant is cost-saving and value-accretive to all stakeholders.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The only entity exiting the group is a dormant wholly owned subsidiary being struck off — not a business separation but the wind-up of a shell with no operations (investment of INR 0.10 million written off). “The Board of our wholly-owned subsidiary Oswal Green Private Limited has resolved to initiate strike-off, as the company has no major business activity.”
- *Scheme* — The June 2026 filing moves in the opposite direction to a separation: Walso Solar Solution (structures, BOS, turnkey pumping components; FY26 turnover INR 1,702.65 million) is taken from associate to 51%-owned subsidiary for Rs 3,65,96,000 at Rs 28/share. “Consequently, Walso Solar Solution Private Limited has become subsidiary of the Company, effective today.”
- *Scheme* — Stated rationale for absorbing Walso is tighter vertical integration of the same value chain — cost and margin control — rather than any separation of businesses. “This approach provides us several advantages including the ability to design and develop new products, optimize our operational costs and improve our margins.”
- *Scheme* — The October 2026 variation redirects INR 1,598.50 million of unutilised IPO money from the Aluminium Frame Facility, 300 MW EVA and 500 MW of module capacity into a 1.2 GW captive solar cell plant (project cost INR 4,558.50 million), because DCR cell supply, not frames, is the choke point. “The binding constraint for Oswal Solar's module business is the solar cell, not the frame.”
- *Scheme* — The cell plant is explicitly captive — sized to internal need, not to be run as a separable merchant business. “At a capacity of 1.2 GW, it will meet approximately 75% of the Company's overall cell requirement, with the balance continuing to be sourced externally in the near term.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=35484296-ce12-474b-8dfb-b74336a69d21.pdf)* — The only 'shift' management flagged in a call was physical, not corporate: moving the module expansion to a larger adjacent Karnal parcel (28,000 sq m vs 13,983 sq m) to share workforce, R&D, admin and an existing electricity feeder; approved by postal ballot on 17 December 2025. “Separately, we proposed shifting the solar module expansion project to a land parcel located adjacent to our existing plant.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=936460b6-a7a4-4d4d-8d8a-37bdc739ee76.pdf)* — Asked what happens if PM-KUSUM 2.0 slips, management's answer is new verticals built inside the existing company and subsidiaries — PM Surya Ghar, exports, private/domestic network, EPC for large rooftops — not a separation of the solar or pump business. “because of the delay, a point of diversification has also come to our mind and we have thought internally that the company should now be diversified even more in different verticals in the coming time, so that in the coming future, if any government scheme is delayed, then a very big impact should not come on our total revenue.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=1b5eda43-41e3-40ee-a1ad-9520e0d5ef7c.pdf)* — The one new vehicle created is an additive project SPV under the solar subsidiary, with a 60% stake alongside a partner, for Rajasthan HAM rooftop projects — a project structure, not a carve-out of existing operations. “Our wholly owned subsidiary, Oswal Solar Energy Private Limited, has also incorporated a special purpose vehicle, Oswal Doon Baran Bundi Solar Projects Limited, in partnership with Doon Infrapower Projects Private Limited, holding a 60% stake to execute rooftop solar photovoltaic power projects on state government buildings in Rajasthan under the Hybrid Annuity Model (HAM).”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=1b5eda43-41e3-40ee-a1ad-9520e0d5ef7c.pdf)* — Even the newest product line, inverters, is deliberately kept inside as captive backward integration rather than set up as a standalone sellable business — the group's consistent stance against separating components. “So, we are not taking the inverter as a solo sale model.”
- *Aug 2025* — The baseline structure described at listing is a single integrated platform across parent, subsidiaries and associate — management treats this integration as the source of industry-leading margins. “Our deep integration helps us ensure consistent product quality, reduce dependency on external vendors, manage cost and delivery timelines more effectively, and consequently achieve industry-leading margins.”

*Not explained on the calls:* Everything about a separation: no demerger, scheme, record date, entity-level financials, swap ratio, rationale, or any investor, lender or partner request for one is mentioned anywhere.

**PROBABLE** (a scheme of arrangement whose nature the documents on file do not settle) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 2.9/10 · scheme (nature unclear) · 1 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-08-21, latest 2026-08-21

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; indicated timeline: No listing date stated; the August 21, 2026 filing says the demerger was "effective from the close of business hours on March 31, 2025" under the NCLT Mumbai order dated February 14, 2025, and that STL Networks Limited "has filed a requisite disclosure ... on BSE Limited and National Stock Exchange of India Limited on August 20, 2026"

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** STL's Global Services Business (system integration / services arm), demerged out of Sterlite Technologies into a separate company — class `unrelated`.

- *Insiders:* Not stated for STL Networks. In the parent, promoter Twin Star Overseas Limited held 42.90%, rising to 47.75% fully diluted on exercise of 4,53,00,000 warrants at Rs.110; ultimate beneficial owner Mr. Anil Agarwal
- *What it reveals:* Leaves a pure-play optical parent: Q2 FY27 record revenue INR 2,529 Cr, EBITDA INR 846 Cr, PAT INR 517 Cr, order book INR 35,274 Cr, net debt-free, CRISIL AA/Stable. Any Kakinada writ contingent gain now belongs to STL Networks, not STL
- *Selling pressure:* unclear — Documents give no size, shareholding, index or float details for STL Networks Limited
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* STL Networks Limited's own August 20, 2026 exchange disclosure and its standalone financials
- *In their words:* “Please note that pursuant to the Scheme of Arrangement approved by the Hon'ble National Company Law Tribunal, Mumbai, vide order dated February 14, 2025, STL's Global Services Business has been demerged into STL Networks Limited, effective from the close of business hours on March 31, 2025.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The business being separated is STL's Global Services (system integration / network-deployment) business, demerged out of Sterlite Technologies Limited (STLTECH) into a separate listed entity, STL Networks Limited, rebranded 'Invenia', leaving STL as a pure optical business (optical fibre, fibre cable, specialty cable, optical connectivity) plus the small STL Digital IT-services arm. Management's stated reason was portfolio simplification and focus: Ankit Agarwal said on the May 2025 call that the demerger 'aligns with our goal of portfolio simplification and sets the stage for focused growth in each of the businesses,' and in Jul 2026 placed it in a multi-year clean-up in which STL exited, sold or shut down wireless solutions, OSS/BSS, active components and other businesses to be 'very, very focused on the optical fiber cable connectivity side.' The second reason was capital and working-capital drag: the services business was a project business with large net fund involvement, and on the Jan 2025 call management's stated priority for it was 'select projects intake to improve the profitability and optimize the net fund involvement,' with Tushar Shroff conceding receivables and contract assets in state-government projects like T-Fiber and MahaNet were liquidating slower than planned because they depended on state budgetary allocation. The scale difference management cited: Global Services did INR 289 crores of revenue in Q3 FY25 at only INR 20 crores EBITDA (6.8% margin), versus the optical business at INR 924 crores and INR 119 crores (12.9%); consolidated net debt was INR 2,195 crores at Q3 FY25 and the retained (post-demerger) business reported net debt of about INR 1,350 crores at Q4 FY25, with a stated target of taking net debt/EBITDA from ~3x to 2x. Structurally, management wanted a clean break rather than a carve-out on paper: in Nov 2025 Ajay Jhanjhari said 'the entire thought process of doing demerger is that there should not be any intercompany guarantees because that is a separate company,' and 'No relationship between STL and STL networks from that perspective.' The INR 2,600 crore BharatNet Phase III Jammu & Kashmir package (3-year build plus 10-year maintenance) went with the demerged entity, and STL now supplies cable to it on an arm's-length basis — in Jan 2026 described as 'our group company, Invenia has secured Jammu Kashmir package, where we will be supplying the cable on arm's length basis.' Each entity also got its own leadership and identity: Pankaj Malik as CEO of STL Networks under the Invenia brand, with shareholders receiving a 1:1 share entitlement on holdings as of April 24, 2025. Across the calls, no investor, lender or partner is named as having demanded the separation; the only shareholder pressure visible is generic complaints about poor equity returns and past cash burn (Q4 FY25 and Q1 FY26 calls), which management answered by pointing to the business exits, the ~INR 1,000 crore QIP of April 2024, and the demerger as portfolio simplification.

**How it evolved:** The idea is already in execution by the Jan 23, 2025 call, where it appears as a standing FY26 priority ('work towards completing the demerger of the services business') with the NCLT timeline laid out — scheme approved by shareholders and creditors July 10, 2024, petition admitted October 2024, final hearing January 30, 2025, listing targeted by Q1 FY26. On the May 16, 2025 call Ankit Agarwal declared it done, effective March 31, 2025, named the new entity STL Networks, the new brand Invenia, Pankaj Malik as CEO and the 1:1 share entitlement, and reported the retained business separately at INR 1,350 crores net debt. By Jul 25, 2025 the plan had slipped only on listing (NCLT approval received Feb 2025, shares expected to list 'by the end of August'), and by Nov 6, 2025 the emphasis shifted to completing the operational separation — no intercompany guarantees, a roughly year-long transition to transfer everything. Thereafter it is treated as finished history: Jan 23, 2026 references Invenia only as a BharatNet customer served at arm's length, and Jul 24, 2026 cites 'we've also demerged our system integration business into a separate entity' purely as evidence of focus.

**What management expects from it:** Focused growth in each entity: STL becomes a pure optical manufacturer chasing global top-3, 70-80% utilisation and 20% EBITDA versus ~13-14%, with net debt/EBITDA cut from ~3x to 2x (net debt INR 1,350 crores post-demerger versus INR 2,195 crores consolidated), no intercompany guarantees, and less capital tied up in project/working-capital-heavy services. Invenia gets its own brand, CEO and large-project mandate.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Jan 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=98f6b077-32ee-41f8-b96d-a36366cf2a48.pdf)* — Completing the demerger of the services business was listed as a formal FY26 strategic priority alongside building value-added services and cutting fund involvement in that business. “Concurrently we will work towards completing the demerger of the services business.”
- *[Jan 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=98f6b077-32ee-41f8-b96d-a36366cf2a48.pdf)* — CFO Tushar Shroff gave the regulatory timeline — scheme approved by shareholders and creditors on July 10, 2024, petition admitted with NCLT in October 2024, final hearing January 30, 2025 — with listing of the resulting company to follow, and a target of completing the demerger by Q1 FY26. “The final approval is expected in Q4 FY25 after which resulting company is anticipated to be listed on a stock exchanges.”
- *[Jan 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=98f6b077-32ee-41f8-b96d-a36366cf2a48.pdf)* — The services business was explicitly managed for lower capital absorption, not scale: Q3 FY25 revenue of INR 289 crores produced only INR 20 crores EBITDA (6.8%), and receivables/contract assets in state projects (T-Fiber, MahaNet) were stuck pending state budgetary allocation. “We will continue to build our capability towards value added services and system integration to improve our margins and reduce the fund involvement going forward.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=3a33a16d-778d-4047-8e61-79e95df6983b.pdf)* — Ankit Agarwal announced completion effective March 31, 2025, with the demerged Global Services business operating as STL Networks under the new Invenia brand, Pankaj Malik as CEO, and a 1:1 share entitlement to STL shareholders based on holdings as of April 24, 2025. “This move aligns with our goal of portfolio simplification and sets the stage for focused growth in each of the businesses.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=3a33a16d-778d-4047-8e61-79e95df6983b.pdf)* — The separation was framed as the last step of a multi-year pruning of the portfolio, after exiting wireless solutions and OSS/BSS, and alongside a ~INR 1,000 crore QIP to repair the balance sheet; the INR 2,600 crore BharatNet J&K package (deployment plus 10 years' maintenance) sat in the demerged entity, not in STL's reported order book. “This is part of the services business, which is now demerged.”
- *[Jul 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=8111472f-4f00-4159-9e5a-70f93bf1b0d8.pdf)* — CFO confirmed NCLT final approval was received in February 2025 and that STL Networks was a separate legal entity from March 31, 2025, with share listing still pending regulatory approvals and expected by end-August 2025 (versus the earlier Q1 FY26 / June target). “As of March 31, 2025, STL Networks Limited is now a separate legal entity.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=6103688c-1b5b-4922-b304-d2d348f60fea.pdf)* — Asked about intercompany loans, advances or guarantees with STL Networks, management said the purpose of the demerger was precisely to have none, while conceding the operational transfer takes about a year to complete. “So, STL networks, the entire thought process of doing demerger is that there should not be any intercompany guarantees because that is a separate company.”
- *[Jan 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=e0a51053-117e-457b-90f3-4487eed18370.pdf)* — The post-separation relationship is purely commercial: STL supplies optical fibre cable to Invenia's BharatNet Phase III Jammu & Kashmir package on an arm's-length basis, and also holds Manufacturing Authorization Forms with other BharatNet bidders. “And as you know, our group company, Invenia has secured Jammu Kashmir package, where we will be supplying the cable on arm's length basis.”
- *[Jul 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=8a08fac5-bc05-4f79-acee-f6a5076525cd.pdf)* — A year later Ankit cited the demerger, alongside exits from active components and other businesses, as proof of a deliberate narrowing to glass-fibre-cable-connectivity, and ruled out adjacent areas like transceivers and semiconductors. “We've consciously chosen to exit, sell off or shut down many businesses. So -- and we've also demerged our system integration business into a separate entity.”
- *Scheme* — The Aug 2026 filing records the legal mechanics: the Scheme of Arrangement was approved by NCLT Mumbai by order dated February 14, 2025, and the Global Services Business demerged into STL Networks Limited from the close of business hours on March 31, 2025, with litigation outcomes of that business (e.g. the Kakinada Smart City writ petition) now accruing to STL Networks. “Please note that pursuant to the Scheme of Arrangement approved by the Hon'ble National Company Law Tribunal, Mumbai, vide order dated February 14, 2025, STL's Global Services Business has been demerged into STL Networks Limited, effective from the close of business hours on March 31, 2025.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No standalone Invenia financials, valuation, debt split, separation costs, or capital allocation given; no investor, lender or partner named as requesting it; listing-date slippage unexplained.
