## SUDARSCHEM — Sudarshan Chemical Industries Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a filing's text names a demerger; no scheme filing names it yet) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 2.9/10 · spin-off · 3 filing(s) from CALLS, NSE · first 2025-12-30, latest 2026-09-01

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** VP4 Frankfurt GmbH, an intermediates tolling operation — sold for cash to Celanese, not demerged or listed — class `unrelated`.

- *Insiders:* No new entity for insiders to hold; buyer Celanese does not belong to promoter group. Promoter group holds 9.32% of parent after Rajesh Rathi's ~Rs 100 crore warrant conversion at a premium
- *What it reveals:* VP4 contributed EUR 15,722,521 revenue (6.71% standalone, 1.64% consolidated) and EUR 5,670,674 net worth, yet fetched EUR 75.8 million cash — roughly 13x net worth, useful against the ballooning acquisition-finance repayment schedule
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — No shares distributed to shareholders; it is an all-cash sale to a third party, so no new listed stock for index or legacy holders to dump
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* 13th December, 2024 — 9,80,000 warrants allotted to Mr. Rajesh Balkrishna Rathi at Rs 1,019.75 each, converted to equity on 10th June, 2026
- *Read next:* The omitted filings from 2025-12-30 onward: no demerger scheme, shareholder/NCLT approval, share-entitlement ratio or record date appears anywhere in these documents
- *In their words:* “The sale of VP4 Frankfurt further sharpens the Company's focus on its core pigment business.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The separation that actually happened is the carve-out and sale of VP4 Frankfurt GmbH, a German step-down wholly-owned subsidiary held under Sudarshan Germany Horizons GmbH, and the stated reason is portfolio focus, not distress: the 1 Sep 2026 filing says VP4 Frankfurt is primarily engaged in manufacturing certain intermediates, primarily as a tolling operator, with only a small share of output meant for captive consumption of Sudarshan Germany Horizons, and that its sale further sharpens the Company's focus on its core pigment business. In other words, the unit is an intermediates tolling plant inherited with the March 2025 Heubach/Clariant asset deal (the German insolvency assets were booked into separable special-purpose entities such as Sudarshan Germany Horizons, Inventories Frankfurt, VP4 Frankfurt, Inventories Langelsheim, Sudarshan Langelsheim PLT/RE, which is what made a clean 100% share sale possible), and it sits outside the pigments segment that is the group's reporting core. The scale given is small relative to the group but material in cash: FY26 revenue EUR 15,722,521, being 6.71% of standalone revenue and only 1.64% of consolidated revenue, net worth contribution EUR 5,670,674, against consideration of EUR 76,500,000 agreed in the SPA signed 31 Aug 2026, with EUR 75.8 million received on completion to Celanese US Holdings LLC on 2 Nov 2026 — a very high price versus the contributed net worth and revenue, i.e. a cash-raising, focus-sharpening disposal of a non-pigment asset. It lands alongside the group's wider German cost surgery: the Q2 FY27 results carry ₹82.9 crore of exceptional expense, of which ₹74.5 crore is termination benefits for an employee restructuring programme agreed with the employee representative organisation at a German subsidiary and ₹8.4 crore is expenses on this disposal group (held-for-sale assets ₹88.8 crore, associated liabilities ₹48.2 crore, including ₹50.9 crore of cash). The same quarter shows the group buying in the opposite direction for core products — Sudarshan Switzerland SLO AG signing on 24 Aug 2026 to acquire Clariant Additives (Switzerland) AG's aluminium dyes and chemicals plant at Muttenz for CHF 7.0 million plus inventory at book value — and simplifying the holding chain by moving Sudarshan Colorants India Limited shares (15.89% for ₹150.8 crore, in-principle approval for all 70.26%) into direct ownership by the listed parent. Context from the calls is that Europe was always designated specialty-only because of high cost (commodity/Azo lines were moved from Frankfurt to the Indian Heubach site at Roha, and Frankfurt rightsizing had already been done by the insolvency administrator before closing), the acquired group's manufacturing fixed cost is structurally high versus variable cost so volume dips hit EBITDA hard, and net debt was INR 755 crore at March 2026 with a ballooning acquisition-finance repayment schedule starting FY27 while management guides to EUR 35 million acquired-group EBITDA in FY27 and EUR 90–100 million in 3–4 years. No investor, lender or partner is named as having asked for it; the only outside pressure visible is analysts repeatedly asking about hiving off RIECO and about disposing of non-core/less-strategic assets.

**How it evolved:** Separation was first floated by analysts, not management: on the Oct 2024 deal call Rathi said no plant closures were envisioned and Germany would be turned into a specialty site, and on the Nov 2024 call the board explicitly rejected selling the engineering (RIECO) business, saying it had decided to transform and build it, which Feb 2025 framed as an 18–24 month turnaround. Through Aug 2025 (no plan to optimize or close any facility; RIECO divestment again refused, Frankfurt rightsizing already completed by the administrator) and Feb 2026 (asked point-blank about merging, hiving off or divesting Heubach operations, Rathi replied the footprint changes were already brought in, Frankfurt rightsized, with only tactical changes left) the stance stayed no-disposal. The first crack came on the Jun 2026 call (held 27 May 2026), where Rathi conceded to Avinash Nahata that non-core assets were being explored, that the thought process was very initial, and that there was definitely an opportunity, while RIECO itself was kept because its transformation was not over (FY26 revenue INR 268 crore, EBITDA back to +INR 10 crore from −INR 17 crore). Execution then came entirely outside the call record: SPA signed 31 Aug 2026 (disclosed 1 Sep 2026) and completion on 2 Nov 2026 at EUR 75.8 million, disclosed in the 6 Nov 2026 results.

**What management expects from it:** Only one stated expectation: sharper focus on the core pigment business, since VP4 Frankfurt is a tolling intermediates plant with minimal captive use and just 1.64% of consolidated revenue. EUR 75.8 million cash comes in against EUR 5.67 million of contributed net worth. No margin, capital-allocation, de-leveraging or valuation benefit is quantified anywhere; Frankfurt remains the specialty site.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Oct 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=16e1eab5-708f-4f0a-a023-637546070399.pdf)* — At the acquisition announcement Rathi ruled out closing or exiting any of the 17 acquired sites, saying the global footprint itself was the advantage; Germany (~30% of manufacturing) was to be converted into a specialty site rather than separated. “We don't envision, sir, any closure of any plants.”
- *[Nov 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=dd4b802a-a627-476e-9e4b-fb2838823f66.pdf)* — Asked whether the engineering business (RIECO) would be hived off or the EPC business sold to help fund the Heubach deal, the CFO said the board had instead decided to transform and build it, with no monetization plan and no spare land to sell. “Second is, as Mr. Rajesh Rathi mentioned in the opening question, as management, we have taken the decision to transform the Rieco business and build this business.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=658eb24c-720e-4cc0-afe6-47478e422af1.pdf)* — Instead of separating RIECO, management committed to a transformation project with benefits over 18–24 months; Q3 FY25 RIECO revenue was INR 65 crore with EBITDA at breakeven versus negative INR 7 crore a year earlier. “We have initiated the transformation project to turn around Rieco business into sustainable profitable business and we expect this turnaround will be visible and will benefit of the same is expected over next 18 months to 24 months.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=8d2568bc-d538-4c8a-8f53-f6d708e0970f.pdf)* — On the first post-closing results call Rathi explicitly denied any plan to rationalise or shut plants, noting the Frankfurt rightsizing had already been initiated by the insolvency administrator before the acquisition. “I think from a manufacturing footprint, we don't plan to optimize any manufacturing or close any facility.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=8d2568bc-d538-4c8a-8f53-f6d708e0970f.pdf)* — Bharat Sheth of Quest asked directly about RIECO divestment; Rathi again answered with investment and turnaround rather than separation, with EUR 35 million acquired-group EBITDA guided for FY26 after EUR 10 million of integration cost. “Third thing is, as we explained in RIECO, we are investing to build that business.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=8d2568bc-d538-4c8a-8f53-f6d708e0970f.pdf)* — The cost logic that later makes a non-specialty German intermediates plant separable was stated here: European manufacturing is admittedly high-cost, so Europe is to make only specialty products while gross margins are high but fixed costs are heavy. “And that's the reason our strategy has been to make only specialty products.”
- *[Oct 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=346e9b35-bf98-4f10-a94d-cd5a867b02c6.pdf)* — Cash preservation was named a core operating principle for the acquired group alongside in-sourcing of previously outsourced products and benchmarking of each site's cost — the frame in which a cash-raising disposal later fits. “Cash is king we are investing for the long term, but how do we ensure that short term, we preserve cash and be prudent is also as important.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=8f7b2ae6-8d97-422a-b6c2-b52affb57c00.pdf)* — Footprint changes at this stage were tactical and tariff-driven (shifting some output to Europe and Mexico), not disposals; of 17 acquired sites five were already in India and the Germany-to-India product transfer was finishing. “In fact, given the tariff situation, we are moving some of the products actually to Europe and to Mexico”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ba3a3f1c-a143-4a16-88eb-41f658953e4d.pdf)* — Chetan Cholera of Pragya Equities asked whether any Heubach operations would be merged, hived off or divested; Rathi said footprint changes were already complete, Frankfurt had been rightsized with production moved to India, and only tactical changes remained. “Is there any plan to merge or hive off some of the operation or divest some of the operation?”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ba3a3f1c-a143-4a16-88eb-41f658953e4d.pdf)* — Rathi confirmed the structural problem in the acquired group: manufacturing fixed cost is very high relative to variable cost (unlike legacy Sudarshan), so any volume dip hits EBITDA hard — Q3 FY26 acquired-group EBITDA was negative INR 38 crore. “So, one of the challenges, and that's where I think we are focusing on fixed cost reduction, the acquired group, the manufacturing cost -- fixed cost is very high compared to the variable cost, and if you look at legacy Sudarshan, the variable cost is high, the fixed cost is low.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ba3a3f1c-a143-4a16-88eb-41f658953e4d.pdf)* — Rathi stated that Frankfurt's rightsizing was already executed and its commodity production shifted to India, leaving Frankfurt as a specialty site — the step that left non-specialty intermediates capacity there as strategically loose. “Frankfurt was to be rightsized, which has been done.”
- *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=4eda5956-37b3-40ab-9bef-88d1ab802c84.pdf)* — First admission of a disposal pipeline: asked by Avinash Nahata (Parami Financials) about assets more strategic to someone else, Rathi said non-core assets were being explored, the thinking was very initial, and there was definitely an opportunity — three months before the VP4 Frankfurt SPA. “Right now, the thought process is very initial and I think we will come back to you at the right time when we could look at this.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No call ever discussed the VP4 sale (last call predates signing). Unexplained: use of EUR 75.8m proceeds, post-sale intermediates supply/tolling arrangement, EBITDA and gain impact, valuation basis, and RIECO's eventual fate.

*Calls read (36 months):* [Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ba3a3f1c-a143-4a16-88eb-41f658953e4d.pdf), [Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=4eda5956-37b3-40ab-9bef-88d1ab802c84.pdf)

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Netria Property Holdings Limited, a wholly owned property-holding subsidiary whose premises Trent occupies; 100% sold to an SM REIT — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* Documents state the buyers do not belong to the promoter/promoter group/group companies and the transaction is not a related party transaction; no promoter or management stake in the Trust stated.
- *What it reveals:* Consideration Rs 11.25 per equity share plus repayment of loans aggregating approximately Rs 171.91 crore and accrued interest; Netria, incorporated 4th September 2025, contributed no prior-year turnover or net worth; Trent keeps occupancy via lease arrangements with the Trust.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — Documents describe a cash sale of Netria's shares into a Trust IPO, not a share distribution to Trent shareholders.

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

On these documents alone, TRENT has not announced or explained a separation (demerger/spin-off) of any business, and no earnings-call transcripts are on file, so there is no management rationale to reconstruct. The only separation-like actions disclosed are: (1) a 22nd October 2026 binding term sheet under which wholly owned subsidiary Nahar Retail Trading Services Limited will divest 100% of Netria Property Holdings Limited to TreBits Investment Trust, a SEBI-registered Small and Medium REIT, conditional on definitive documents and completion of the IPO of the Trust's proposed first scheme, with Trent continuing to occupy the same premises under lease arrangements with the Trust — i.e. a property monetisation/sale-and-leaseback of real estate held in a subsidiary incorporated only on 4th September 2025, for Rs 11.25 per equity share plus repayment of loans of approximately ₹171.91 crore and accrued interest, with net-working-capital closing adjustments; (2) the 21st November 2025 participation in the Inditex Trent Retail India Private Limited (ITRIPL) buyback, tendering 94,900 shares at Rs 15,421.85 each for Rs 146.35 crore and cutting Trent's stake in the Zara associate to 20% (ITRIPL contributed Rs 992.12 crore of total income, 5.72% of consolidated income, and Rs 230.44 crore net worth, 4.22%, in FY25); and (3) two intra-group amalgamations that move in the opposite direction — Fiora Hypermarket Limited (FY25 turnover Rs 22,886.84 lakh, net worth Rs 6,395.44 lakh) into Fiora Online Limited (turnover Rs 11,014.46 lakh, negative net worth of Rs 1,245.72 lakh) effective 1st December 2025 with 3,044,744 shares of Rs 10 issued, and THPL Support Services Limited (turnover Rs 4,208.09 lakh) into Booker India Limited (turnover Rs 16,445.35 lakh) effective 1st February 2026. The stated reasons for those schemes are consolidation and group-structure simplification, not separation; both results statements continue to say retailing/trading is the single business with "no separate reportable segments." No investor, lender or partner is named anywhere as having asked for a separation, and no demerger scheme, record date, entitlement ratio or listing of a resulting entity appears in these filings. The capital actions in the 22nd April 2026 board meeting — 1:2 bonus, Rs 6 dividend, ESOP 2026 of 8,88,700 options at Rs 3,978, authorised-capital reclassification to all-equity ₹85.55 crore, and enabling approval for up to ₹2,500 crore of equity/rights issuance — are disclosed as shareholder-reward, retention and funding measures, with no separation rationale attached.

**How it evolved:** Nothing in the record shows a separation idea surfacing: the 21st November 2025 ITRIPL buyback reduced the associate stake to 20%; the 1st December 2025 and 1st February 2026 filings record intra-group mergers justified as consolidation and simplification; the 22nd April 2026 board meeting added bonus, ESOP, capital reclassification and a ₹2,500 crore enabling fund-raise approval. The first and only asset-separation step appears on 23rd October 2026, when Nahar signs a binding term sheet to sell Netria Property Holdings to the TreBits SM REIT, with Trent leasing the premises back. The 29th October 2026 Q2 FY27 results make no reference to it and still report a single reportable segment.

**What management expects from it:** Nothing is stated. The filings give no expected effect on margins, capital, valuation or focus for any entity. For Netria, only mechanics appear: cash of Rs 11.25 per share plus repayment of about ₹171.91 crore of loans, Netria ceasing to be a subsidiary, and Trent continuing to occupy the premises under lease from the REIT. The merger filings claim only group-structure simplification and operational efficiencies.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Filing 2026-10-23 · Sale or disposal* — The only announced separation is a property-holding subsidiary, not an operating business: Nahar will sell 100% of Netria Property Holdings Limited to TreBits Investment Trust, a SEBI-registered Small and Medium REIT, conditional on definitive documents and the IPO of the Trust's first scheme. “Nahar Retail Trading Services Limited ("Nahar"), a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company, has entered into a binding term sheet dated 22nd October 2026 with TreBits Investment Trust, a Small and Medium Real Estate Investment Trust registered with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (the "Trust"), in relation to the proposed divestment of its entire shareholding (100%) in its wholly owned subsidiary, Netria Property Holdings Limited.”
- *Filing 2026-10-23 · Sale or disposal* — The structure is effectively a sale-and-leaseback: Trent keeps using the same stores/premises under lease from the REIT, so operations are unaffected while the real estate leaves the group. “The Company proposes to continue to occupy the premises owned by Netria pursuant to appropriate lease arrangements with the Trust acting on behalf of the proposed first scheme.”
- *Filing 2026-10-23 · Sale or disposal* — Consideration is stated per share plus loan repayment, with no synergy, margin or valuation rationale given; Netria has no prior-year revenue or net worth to disclose because it was incorporated only on 4th September 2025. “The total consideration to be received upon completion will be Rs 11.25 per equity share (based on unaudited financials as of September 30, 2026), subject to closing adjustments for net working capital as on the closing date, together with repayment of outstanding loans aggregating approximately ₹171.91 crore and accrued interest up to the closing date.”
- *Scheme* — The 1st December 2025 NCLT-sanctioned amalgamation of Fiora Hypermarket (Star/Zudio formats) into Fiora Online (starquik.com) is justified as consolidation and simplification — the opposite of separating a business. “The rationale of the Scheme is to consolidate the retail businesses and rationalize and simplify the group structure.”
- *Scheme* — The 1st February 2026 amalgamation of THPL Support Services (warehousing) into Booker India (Booker Wholesale cash-and-carry) is likewise framed as structure rationalisation, with no consideration since it was a wholly owned subsidiary. “The rationale of the Scheme is to rationalize and simplify the group structure for organizational, financial and operational efficiencies.”
- *Filing 2025-11-21 · General Updates* — Trent reduced its interest in the Inditex JV associate ITRIPL (Zara) to 20% via that company's buyback for Rs 146.35 crore — a partner-level stake reduction, though the filing gives no reason for it. “Pursuant to the said Buyback Offer and in terms of the Board approval, the Company had tendered 94,900 Equity Shares held by the Company in ITRIPL at a price of Rs 15,421.85 per Equity Share.”
- *Filing 2026-10-29 · Outcome of Board Meeting* — As of the latest results Trent still reports itself as one business, which is inconsistent with a pending separation of an operating division; Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue was Rs 5,873.14 crore with PBT of Rs 619.06 crore. “Main business of the Group entities is retailing / trading of merchandise. All other operating activities of the Group are incidental to its main business. Accordingly, there are no separate reportable segments.”
- *Filing 2026-04-22 · Outcome of Board Meeting* — Capital-structure actions were taken for shareholder reward, employee retention and future funding (1:2 bonus, Rs 6 dividend, 8,88,700 ESOPs at Rs 3,978, all-equity authorised capital), plus an enabling fund-raise — none tied to any separation. “Granted enabling approval for raising additional funds not exceeding ₹2,500 Crore, by way of issuance of equity shares, through a rights issue and/or any other permissible mode(s), singly or in combination, in one or more tranches, subject to requisite approvals.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No earnings-call transcripts supplied; no demerger scheme, entitlement ratio, segment financials, asset list, proceeds use, or any investor, lender or partner request for a separation.

## ANANDRATHI — Anand Rathi Wealth Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a scheme of arrangement whose nature the documents on file do not settle) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 2.5/10 · scheme (nature unclear) · 1 filing(s) from NSE · first 2025-12-18, latest 2025-12-18

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** No demerger or spin-off; a non-material subsidiary, Freedom Wealth Solutions Private Limited, sold outright for cash — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* Buyer Aqua Proof Wall Plast Private Limited is part of the Promoter Group; related party transaction stated to be done on arm's length basis
- *What it reveals:* Subsidiary was immaterial: total income Rs 40.63 lakhs, 0.04% of income, net worth Rs 588.14 lakhs, sold for Rs 5.37 crores — roughly net worth, no value unlocking disclosed
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — No shares distributed to shareholders and no new listing; outright cash sale of a 0.04%-of-income subsidiary
- *Parent or spin:* neither · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Letter No. 67/2025-26 dated 13th October 2025, referenced but not included, on the Freedom Wealth sale
- *In their words:* “The sale of shares of Freedom Wealth Solutions Private Limited is outside the Scheme of Arrangement.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

On the evidence of these texts, Anand Rathi Wealth Ltd. is not separating any business for a stated strategic reason, and management never explains one: across all seven earnings calls (Jan 2025 through Jul 2026) there is no mention of a demerger, spin-off, slump sale, scheme of arrangement, or carve-out of any business line, and no filing in this set is a Scheme. The only separation-type event in the record is a small divestment disclosed on 18 December 2025: the Company executed a Share Purchase Agreement selling 23,71,625 equity shares of Rs. 10 each of Freedom Wealth Solutions Private Limited, described as 'a Non-Material Subsidiary Company', to Aqua Proof Wall Plast Private Limited for Rs. 5.37 crores, with the sale expected to complete the same day, 18 December 2025. The disclosure gives only materiality facts and no rationale: the subsidiary's total income was Rs. 40.63 lakhs, contributing 0.04% of consolidated income, with net worth of Rs. 588.14 lakhs; it expressly states the sale is 'outside the Scheme of Arrangement' and that Freedom Wealth Solutions does not meet the Section 180(1)(a) threshold, so Regulation 37A of SEBI LODR did not apply. The buyer is not a third party, a lender or a partner — Aqua Proof Wall Plast Private Limited 'is the part of Promoter Group of the Company', making this a related-party transaction the Company says was done on an arm's length basis, exempt from the usual approvals by virtue of the subsidiary's size; no investor, lender or partner is recorded anywhere as having asked for it. Nothing in the calls connects to it: the Digital Wealth (B2B2C) business kept being reported and growing after the sale (INR 2,218 crores AUM in Apr 2026, INR 2,526 crores and 7,320 clients in Jul 2026), as did the OFA SaaS platform (6,890 subscribers, INR 1.66 lakh crores platform assets), so the texts never even identify what business Freedom Wealth Solutions ran. The structural activity management does discuss runs the other way — adding entities, not shedding them: a UK subsidiary (incorporated Feb 2025, licence applied for, operations 'started' by Jul 2026), GIFT City (first stage done, second in process), Bahrain rep office, Anand Rathi FME (IFSC) Private Limited incorporated 16 February 2026 with in-principle IFSCA Fund Management Entity (Non-Retail) approval and a further Rs. 5.49 crore rights-issue infusion on 2 September 2026 to run AIF fund management, and Board consent in Jul 2026 to apply for an AMC licence, framed as 'backward integration' and 'arming ourselves'. The one business genuinely held outside the listed company — Anand Rathi Global Finance Ltd. (ARGFL), the structured-product issuer in which ARWL holds only about 8% — was not separated during this period; if anything ARWL moved closer to it, subscribing INR 40 crores of its INR 512 crore rights issue at INR 500 per share in FY26 and booking fair-value gains on the stake (INR 54.6 crores in FY26, INR 96 crores of the INR 110 crores other income in Q1 FY27).

**How it evolved:** The idea never surfaces on a call: Jan 2025 through Jul 2026 contain no demerger/spin-off/scheme discussion, and the nearest structural questions run the opposite way — Oct 2025 (Sunil Shah) and Jan 2026 (Jaiprakash) press on concentration in and exposure to group NBFC ARGFL, and management answers that ARGFL is only 8%-held, 'not a subsidiary', with no guarantees given and no intention to raise the stake. The divestment appears only in filings: an intimation of 13 October 2025 (letter 67/2025-26, not included here), then the 18 December 2025 Share Purchase Agreement selling Freedom Wealth Solutions Private Limited to promoter-group entity Aqua Proof Wall Plast Private Limited for Rs. 5.37 crores; the Jan 2026 and Apr 2026 calls, held after it, never mention it. The only later structural filing (2 September 2026) is the opposite — a Rs. 5.49 crore rights-issue infusion into new wholly owned subsidiary Anand Rathi FME (IFSC) Private Limited for AIF fund management, matching the Jul 2026 call's AMC-licence and GIFT City build-out.

**What management expects from it:** Nothing stated. No margin, capital-release, valuation or focus benefit is claimed for any separation; the Freedom Wealth Solutions filing gives only size and related-party facts. For the new entities management expects optionality, not re-rating: an AMC licence as 'armory' and backward integration, a GIFT City FME for AIF fund management, and a UK subsidiary built 'brick-by-brick' with deliberately no value attached to subsidiaries.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — Filing 18 Dec 2025: the only separation in the record is a share sale of non-material subsidiary Freedom Wealth Solutions Private Limited for Rs. 5.37 crores, with no business rationale given anywhere in the disclosure. “In continuation of our letter No. 67/2025-26 dated 13th October 2025, we hereby inform about execution of Share Purchase Agreement entered into and executed by and between the Company and Aqua Proof Wall Plast Private Limited for sale of 23,71,625 Equity Shares of the face value of Rs. 10/- each, fully paid-up, of Freedom Wealth Solutions Private Limited (a Non-Material Subsidiary Company), by the Company to Aqua Proof Wall Plast Private Limited at a consideration aggregating to Rs. 5.37 crs.”
- *Scheme* — Filing 18 Dec 2025: the buyer is a promoter-group company, so the exit is a related-party transaction the Company asserts was at arm's length — not a sale to an outside investor, lender or partner. “Aqua Proof Wall Plast Private Limited is the part of Promoter Group of the Company.”
- *Scheme* — Filing 18 Dec 2025: the entity sold was financially trivial to ARWL — Rs. 40.63 lakhs total income, 0.04% of income, Rs. 588.14 lakhs net worth — which is the only justification-like content offered, and it is a materiality statement, not a reason. “% of Income contributed by subsidiary : 0.04%.”
- *Scheme* — Filing 18 Dec 2025: the Company expressly states this was not done through a scheme of arrangement and that Regulation 37A / Section 180(1)(a) thresholds were not triggered, confirming there is no scheme document to explain the separation. “The sale of shares of Freedom Wealth Solutions Private Limited is outside the Scheme of Arrangement.”
- *Scheme* — Filing 2 Sep 2026: the later structural move is the reverse of a separation — Rs. 5.49 crore rights-issue subscription into newly incorporated wholly owned subsidiary Anand Rathi FME (IFSC) Private Limited (incorporated 16 Feb 2026, in-principle IFSCA Fund Management Entity (Non-Retail) approval) to run AIF fund management. “Anand Rathi FME (IFSC) Private Limited shall set up a fund management entity to undertake Fund Management activities through Alternate Investment Fund (AIF).”
- *[Jul 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=5305fb5f-10d4-4698-8963-61940f23e4a2.pdf)* — Management frames its structural agenda as adding manufacturing capability inside the group (AMC licence, GIFT City, UK), explicitly as backward integration after ~20 years of distribution — the opposite of hiving a business off — and declines to disclose the full reasoning. “So in that, you would see point number three, wealth management is a business of backward integration, not forward integration or simultaneous integration.”
- *[Jul 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=5305fb5f-10d4-4698-8963-61940f23e4a2.pdf)* — Asked directly why it is setting up its own AMC, management says the reasons are deliberately undisclosed, which is as close as any call comes to withholding a structural rationale. “We really have some reasons, but we don't want that to be completely disclosed today.”
- *[Jan 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=e5b0b1af-fdb7-4020-a9b8-9de84187eb15.pdf)* — The one business that sits structurally outside the listed company, structured-product issuer ARGFL, is explained as an 8% holding that is not a subsidiary, with no guarantees and no plan to increase the stake — a pre-existing separation, not a new one. “No, not at all. Crystal clear, the answer is no. And it's not a subsidiary though, with 8%, surely not.”
- *[Oct 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=3f5cf54e-7b9c-4b35-a322-b075772401ff.pdf)* — Investor Sunil Shah pressed on concentration in ARGFL and suggested diversifying issuers (Bajaj Finance, Tata Capital, Muthoot, Shriram, HDB; Citi/HSBC/JPMorgan; Motilal, Edelweiss, IIFL, Kotak, Nuvama); management agreed to diversify issuers but proposed no separation of any ARWL business. “But in terms of the structured products, our concentration risk is high in terms of the Anand Rathi Global Finance, just highlighting .”
- *[Apr 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=f26fafbc-54ac-43e9-a450-b717a3932b3a.pdf)* — Rather than disentangling from the group NBFC, ARWL subscribed INR 40 crores of ARGFL's INR 512 crore rights issue at INR 500 per share to hold its ~8% stake, and books fair-value gains on it (INR 54.6 crores in FY26; INR 96 crores of Q1 FY27 other income). “So the total issue size, which was INR 512 crores, about 8% of that, that was about INR 40 crores that has been subscribed by Anand Rathi Wealth Limited just to continue to hold its holding in the NBFC at a price of INR 500 (per share).”
- *[Jul 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=5305fb5f-10d4-4698-8963-61940f23e4a2.pdf)* — The businesses an investor might expect to be carved out — Digital Wealth (B2B2C) and the OFA SaaS platform — are still reported as growing parts of the consolidated group after the Dec 2025 sale, and management says it deliberately attaches no separate value to them. “Digital wealth business, which is B2B2C business, registered AUM growth of 23% year-on-year to INR2,526 crores and number of clients increased by 16 % to 7,320.”

*Not explained on the calls:* Everything: no rationale, no reason for a promoter-group buyer, no valuation basis for Rs. 5.37 crores, no description of Freedom Wealth Solutions' business, and no mention on any call.

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

These documents do not disclose any separation, demerger, spin-off or business transfer by Ashapura Minechem Ltd.; on the evidence here there is no separation rationale to reconstruct, and the premise of the question is not supported by the texts. Across all four calls (Sep 2025, Nov 2025, Feb 2026, Jun 2026) management consistently describes a single consolidated company run as two halves — the Guinea resource business (bauxite from the HUDA, BOFFA and FAKO concessions, >700 million tons of bauxite reserves, >300 million tons of iron ore, three in-house ports of 16 million tons capacity going to 27 million tons, 370 km of road) and the India value-added minerals business organised into four/three verticals: Bentonite & Allied Minerals and White Performance Minerals, Specialty Adsorbent Solutions through the 50% JV Ashapura Perfoclay, and Advanced Ceramic Materials through the stake in Orient Ceratech. Far from separating them, management argues for keeping them together: Manan Shah says on 11 Feb 2026 that 'Ashapura Group has seen lot of volatility in the bauxite business' but 'our Indian business has always been a source of strength and consolidation for us,' i.e. India is presented as the stabiliser for a cyclical Guinea. The only time separation is raised at all is by an investor, not management: on 4 Sep 2025 Nalin Shah of NVS Brokerage asks whether any value-unlocking strategy, acquisition or 'de-merger' is 'on the card,' and management replies that the company is 'open to all opportunities of acquisitions or any other kind of strategic activities' but that 'our management focus is on the growth of both Guinea and India business as they stand for the time being' — an explicit deferral, with no plan, structure, timeline, swap ratio, record date or appointed-date disclosed then or in any later call. The only filing supplied (postal ballot dispatched 27 March 2026) contains no scheme of arrangement: its items are the Ashapura Minechem Limited – Employee Stock Option Plan 2026 for up to 20,00,000 equity shares of Rs. 2 face value, extension of that ESOP to holding/subsidiary/group/associate company employees, re-appointment of Shri Hemul Shah as Executive Director & CEO for two years from 16 February 2026 at up to Rs. 1,00,90,000 p.a., and regularisation of Shri Jagdish Shetty and Shri Wilson Mathais as Independent Directors from 5 February 2026. Words such as 'merger, demerger, sale of division' appear in that notice only as standard anti-dilution boilerplate for adjusting option entitlements on corporate actions, not as any announced transaction. The nearest things to structural change actually disclosed are capital and partnership moves inside the existing entity: the China Railway tie-up for mining, logistics and port operations in Guinea (a partner, explicitly 'not the end customer'), a possible build-operate-transfer model so beneficiation capex sits with vendors/partners rather than Ashapura's balance sheet (4 Jun 2026), roughly INR 150 crores of India capex across divisions, and a holding chain India → UAE → Guinea that management defended on 11 Feb 2026 when asked about related-party loans and investments.

**How it evolved:** The idea never surfaced from management: it was raised once by an investor, Nalin Shah of NVS Brokerage, on the maiden call of 4 Sep 2025, bundled with questions on acquisitions and inorganic growth, and management set it aside in favour of growing Guinea and India 'as they stand for the time being.' It was not mentioned again on 21 Nov 2025, 11 Feb 2026 or 4 Jun 2026 by any analyst or by management; instead the integrated story hardened, with Guinea framed as the growth engine (8 million tons exported in FY26, INR 4,200 crores revenue, INR 561 crores EBITDA) and India as the stabilising, value-added pillar (INR 998 crores revenue, INR 112 crores EBITDA). The 27 March 2026 postal ballot, the only filing provided, moved in the opposite direction by proposing a single group-wide ESOP extended across holding, subsidiary, group and associate companies, which presumes the group stays together. As of the last call on 4 Jun 2026 the forward agenda was port expansion to 20-27 million tons, a 20,000 tpd bauxite washing plant, iron ore beneficiation and a 100% dividend — no separation.

**What management expects from it:** Nothing, because no separation was proposed. Management's stated expectations are for the combined entity: Guinea volumes of 10-12 million tons in FY27 and 15 million tons by FY27-28 with EBITDA improving off Q4's $5.9/ton after Guinea's quota system, at least $700 million Guinea turnover; India growing via value-added products, seven new bentonite leases and INR 150 crores capex, with no debt addition and a 100% dividend.

On the evidence of these four transcripts and all 28 filings, Aster is not separating a business at all — management never describes a demerger, spin-off, slump sale or carve-out, and no such scheme exists in the documents. The corporate action they explain at length is the opposite: the amalgamation of Blackstone-backed Quality Care India Limited (CARE Hospitals, KIMSHEALTH, Evercare, plus Bangladesh via Evercare/STS Holdings) into Aster DM Healthcare under Sections 230-232, at 977 Aster shares per 1,000 QCIL shares, effective 1 July 2026 and renaming the listed entity Aster DM Quality Care Limited. The stated reasons are scale and resilience (top-3 Indian hospital chain; FY26 proforma revenue INR 9,273 crore, operating EBITDA INR 2,013 crore at 21.7%, three-year revenue CAGR 14.5% and EBITDA CAGR ~20%), diversification across 9 states and 25-28 cities with low micro-market overlap, and synergies guided at a 10-15% EBITDA upside — procurement (Aster's INR 1,000 crore plus QCIL's INR 1,000 crore negotiated as INR 2,000 crore), integrated doctor model, revenue/MVT and insurance coverage, and lower corporate overheads; QCIL had already banked INR 85 crore of its own pre-merger procurement synergies, and Sunil and Varun both stressed Aster-QCIL synergies only begin post-merger. The only businesses management actually says it has stepped out of are small and defensive: the loss-making supply-to-retail unit of wholesale pharmacy, outsourced/exited in FY25 because logistics, reverse logistics and fill rates did not work, removing an INR 1-2 crore monthly drag and taking the segment from negative margins to +1.7% in Q1 FY26, 2.2% in Q3 FY26 and positive ROCE for the first time, with margins structurally capped at 3-3.5%; the de-empanelment of a low-yield state scheme at Aster Aadhar, Kolhapur, where scheme ARPOB was under 50% of cash rates and the 210-bed hospital was already at ~75% occupancy, costing ~1,500-1,600 patients a quarter and 8-9% of K&M inpatient volume but lifting ARPP IP by 17-21%; and, on 6 November 2026, termination by mutual consent of the 4 March 2016 Operation & Management Services Agreement and the 1 April 2026 Medical Services Agreement with promoter-linked DM Education and Research Foundation, worth 0.40% of group revenue, explicitly to eliminate an ongoing stream of related-party transactions. Nobody is said to have demanded a separation: shareholders approved the merger with 96.68% of votes cast (and 94.13% of public shareholders), unsecured trade creditors approved with 100% of votes polled, CCI cleared it on 15 April 2025, NSE and BSE issued no-objection letters on 6 October 2025, and NCLT Hyderabad sanctioned it on 19 June 2026. The only outside pressure visible is governance pressure from stakeholders ahead of the 10 March 2026 vote, which made Aster Promoters and Blackstone commit to waive committee nomination rights and let their three-director nomination rights fall away at 10% shareholding. Adjacent restructurings all run toward consolidation, not separation: MIMS minorities bought up from 79.75% toward 100% at INR 202 a share, Aster Aadhar to 99%, Ramesh Hospitals past 70%, an INR 102.46 crore loan converted to equity in Sri Sainatha, and two hospitality step-downs (KEL into Spiceretreat) merged to simplify the group structure.

**How it evolved:** Aug 2025 call (31 July 2025) is where the only real business exit appears, already done: Sunil reports Aster exited a loss-making wholesale pharmacy unit, lifting that segment to +1.7%, while Alisha explicitly rules out separating or scaling diagnostics into a pan-India play. The Nov 2025 call (7 November 2025) is purely combination mechanics — the 5% QCIL stake acquired via a 3.6% preferential allotment, BSE/NSE no-objections, and the registered office moved from Bangalore to Hyderabad so the NCLT application could go from one state. By the Feb 2026 call (2 February 2026) the pharmacy decision is reframed as sustaining rather than strategic (2.2% margin, positive ROCE for the first time, retail left as a 49%-owned, 203-store brand-licensing vehicle), and by the Jun 2026 call (1 May 2026) the only exit discussed is de-empanelment of the low-yield Aadhar scheme. The separation-shaped disclosure comes only after the merger closes, in the 6 November 2026 board filing terminating the two DMERF agreements to end the related-party stream.

**What management expects from it:** No separated entity is described. Exiting wholesale pharmacy removed an INR 1-2 crore monthly drag, taking margins from negative to 2.2% and ROCE positive for the first time, capped at 3-3.5%. Ending the DMERF agreements forgoes 0.40% of group revenue but eliminates the RPT stream. Aadhar de-empanelment freed beds for cash/TPA patients and lifted ARPP IP 17-21%.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The scheme's own stated rationale is consolidation of the two companies' business interests into one listed vehicle, not any separation of an Aster business. “With a view to consolidate the business interests of the Parties (as defined below), the Parties have decided that the Transferor Company with all its business interests, be amalgamated with and into the Transferee Company.”
- *Scheme* — The 6 November 2026 board filing terminates the 2016 O&M Services Agreement and the 1 April 2026 Medical Services Agreement with promoter-linked DM Education and Research Foundation, a business contributing 0.40% of group revenue, purely to kill a recurring related-party transaction stream. “In line with its corporate governance priorities, efforts are being made to reduce related party transactions within the Group. The closure of both agreements will eliminate the ongoing stream of RPTs with DMERF.”
- *Scheme* — That exit is a negotiated unwind rather than a sale: no consideration is received and the parties simply settle dues. “The termination is proposed to be effected by mutual consent of the parties, subject to execution of necessary termination/closure documents and settlement of the respective rights, obligations and outstanding dues between the parties.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=6e334a7a-3e9d-49d5-b7cd-27bbdb00b570.pdf)* — Sunil frames the wholesale pharmacy exit as the one deliberate business withdrawal, done to remove a drag on consolidated performance; the segment moved to a positive 1.7% margin in Q1 FY26. “As part of a focused strategic shift, we exited loss-making unit within the wholesale pharmacy business, effectively eliminating a key drag on overall performance.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=caa879ae-8f7c-4280-8e22-e09387565d78.pdf)* — Sunil restates it as an outsourcing of the loss-making part, accepting lower reported revenue for better profitability - 1.8% margin for 9M FY26, 2.2% in Q3, and positive ROCE for the first time. “On the wholesale pharmacy front, we took a strategic call last year to outsource the loss-making part of this segment. While this decision led to a reduction in reported revenues, it has materially improved profitability.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=caa879ae-8f7c-4280-8e22-e09387565d78.pdf)* — The operational reason given is that the second business unit built to supply retail pharmacies failed on logistics and fill rates, so Aster retreated to the originally acquired Bengaluru wholesale asset; retail stays a 49%-held, 203-store brand-licensing arrangement expected to break even in a year or two. “And in addition to that, we added the second business unit to supply to a retail pharmacy, which didn't work out really well due to logistics and reverse logistics and the fill rates and a lot of other things.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=caa879ae-8f7c-4280-8e22-e09387565d78.pdf)* — Asked to quantify the removed drag, Sunil puts it at INR 1-2 crore a month, and says the business is deliberately not being grown because distribution margins cap out near 3-3.5%. “Here what we are talking about is that on a monthly basis around INR 1-2 crores every month, that's a number which we have removed.”
- *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=199c44ba-0dff-413b-84de-872f67a011a0.pdf)* — The other exit is revenue-mix pruning, not structural: Aster walked away from a low-yield government scheme at Aster Aadhar, Kolhapur, where realisation was under half the cash rate and the hospital was already capacity-constrained at ~75% occupancy, costing 8-9% of K&M inpatient volume. “The ARPOB compared to a cash market, it is less than 50%. That's how it's been and good thing is that we exited that.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=6e334a7a-3e9d-49d5-b7cd-27bbdb00b570.pdf)* — Alisha explicitly declines to turn diagnostics into a standalone pan-India business, keeping Aster Labs as an ecosystem extension inside the clusters - the opposite of carving it out, even as its margins went from -7.6% in FY24 to 12.8% in FY26 on 27% ROCE. “So, at this point in time, we're not talking about becoming a pan India player.”
- *Nov 2025* — The structural work in this period is all combination: a share swap giving Aster 5% of QCIL for a 3.6% preferential allotment, and a registered-office move from Bangalore to Hyderabad so the NCLT filing would come from a single state. “We completed a strategic share swap, acquiring a 5% stake in QCIL in exchange for a 3.6% preferential allotment in Aster.”
- *Scheme* — Facing stakeholder governance questions before the 10 March 2026 vote, both promoter groups agreed to waive committee nomination rights and let their three-director rights lapse at 10% shareholding - the clearest instance of investors shaping the deal. “Aster Promoters and Blackstone are committed to waive and have their relevant rights (including the right to nominate 3 directors each to the board of directors) as stipulated in the proposed articles of association to fall away at 10% shareholding for both Aster Promoters and Blackstone.”
- *Scheme* — Even the non-core hospitality step-downs are being merged together rather than separated out, for group simplification and cash-management efficiency. “The proposed amalgamation is intended to simplify the group structure, enable better operational and administrative efficiencies, optimise utilisation of resources, facilitate efficient cash management, eliminate duplication of regulatory and compliance requirements and strengthen the business operations of the merged entity.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No spin-off or demerger is proposed in these texts; no rationale for the earlier GCC separation (the Rs.118 special dividend), no DMERF settlement amount, no retail-pharmacy 49% endgame.

## BOSCHLTD — Bosch Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a filing's text names a demerger; no scheme filing names it yet) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 2.5/10 · spin-off · 1 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-02-17, latest 2026-02-17

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** No demerger stated; documents describe sale of the "Video solutions, Access and Intrusions and Communication systems" business — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* Not stated for the transferred business; purchaser Keenfinity is not described as a related party. Promoter Robert Bosch GmbH holds 70.54% of Bosch Limited (pre- and post-preferential issue).
- *What it reveals:* Consideration of Mio INR 5,950 produced a Mio INR 5,560 exceptional gain, implying near-zero carrying value. It "did not qualify as a separate major line of business" under Ind AS 105, so it was immaterial beside the automotive core.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — Cash sale to a third-party purchaser; no shares distributed to Bosch Limited shareholders, so no new listed security can face forced selling.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* FY2025-26 annual report note on the Keenfinity Business Transfer Agreement, including the purchase price adjustment excluded from the Mio INR 5,950 consideration.
- *In their words:* “The transfer of business was completed on May 01, 2025 and accordingly, the Company has recognised a total gain on sale of the said Specified Business in the financial results amounting to Mio INR 5,560 and the same has been disclosed as "exceptional item" in these unaudited standalone financial results.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

A caveat on the premise: across these three years of calls and filings, Bosch Ltd.'s dominant structural move is consolidation, not separation — on April 8, 2026 the Board approved buying 100% of Bosch Chassis Systems India Pvt. Ltd. (RBIC, the Vehicle Motion / safety-and-braking business: ABS, ESP, occupant safety, new braking systems, conventional actuation) for not more than INR 9,068.68 crore (10.6x FY25 EV/EBITDA), ~INR 9,060 crore in cash plus a token 2,460 shares at INR 35,200 so former holders Robert Bosch Investment Nederland B.V. and Robert Bosch LLC keep 'skin in the game', closed July 1, 2026; management's reasons were complementarity with Power Solutions 'without any overlap', powertrain-agnostic demand, day-one margin accretion (FY25 pro forma revenue INR 18,087cr → 22,022cr, EBITDA margin 12.8% → 13.9%, ~5% EPS accretion), and RBIC's own record (FY23–25 revenue CAGR 17% to INR 4,000cr, EBITDA margin 12.8% → 19.3%, net margin 8.1% → 13.9%, one-third two-wheeler). What Bosch Ltd. actually *separated* was the Building Technologies product lines — Video Solutions, Access & Intrusion and Communication Systems — sold under a Business Transfer Agreement approved January 28, 2025 to Keenfinity India Private Limited for Mio INR 5,950 (ex purchase-price adjustment), completed May 1, 2025, booking an exceptional gain of Mio INR 5,560 that drove FY26 PAT to INR 27,702mn (+37.6%). Management framed that exit three ways: it was a sub-scale 'product business' of roughly INR 400–450 crore revenue at about 6% EBIT margin ('not a major impact on our business operations in any way'); it needed 'significant additional investment, a lot of IP and a lot of change dynamics' to reach Bosch's rule of being top-3 in every segment, which 'was not in our focus'; and it was the India leg of a Bosch Group global carve-out of Building Technologies to private-equity owner Triton — routed to a subsidiary of the parent who 'will then take it back to Triton'. The same decluttering logic explains earlier exits (OE/OES Diagnostics, gain INR 485mn in Q2 FY25; Project House Mobility Solutions, gain INR 7,850mn in FY24, 'taken out of the listco... because of the very heavy investments required... heavily negative') and the deliberate decision to leave Bosch Automotive Electronics (RBAI) outside the listed company as a low-margin, capex-heavy captive contract manufacturer with 'no real logic' to buy in. So the driver is portfolio curation by the parent and board, not deleveraging — the company is nearly debt-free with ~INR 10,000 crore of investments at cost — and minority investors were the ones pushing the other way, repeatedly asking for group entities to be folded *into* the listco; management said the discussions were 'going on in the RBIN and Board with the promoter' and that the parent 'has always supported when it makes logical sense... when they want a fair value for whatever has been invested'. Separation also took a third form: new product lines were put into 50:50 JVs rather than built inside the listco — eAxles with Tata AutoComp (volumes too small, 'One Bosch e-axle line produces 150,000 e-axles. The volumes are not there') and, announced May 2026, electronically controlled air compression/processing/suspension/parking-brake modules with Brakes India and Wheels India, an area where 'Bosch is not a player at all'.

**How it evolved:** On the Aug 2024 and Nov 2024 (Nov 12) calls management would only say portfolio moves were 'sensitive' and under discussion 'in the RBIN and Board with the promoter'; the Jan 28, 2025 board meeting then approved the Business Transfer Agreement, and the Feb 2025 call (Jan 28, 2025) explained the Video/Access/Communications exit as the India leg of the global Building Technologies carve-out to Triton, alongside a INR 471mn Mobility restructuring provision. The Jun 2025 (May 29) and Aug 2025 (Aug 5) calls generalised it into doctrine — 'top 3 in every segment', hive off what needs IP and investment we won't fund — with the sale completed May 1, 2025 and the gain flowing through the Nov 2025, Feb 2026 and May 2026 results. From the two Apr 13, 2026 calls the direction inverted: RBIC was bought in as 'the next logical step', RBAI and the loss-making mobility-solutions business were explicitly left with the parent, and by May 2026 management described a permanent two-way process of 'portfolio expansion, portfolio decluttering and enhancement', plus a second JV with Brakes India and Wheels India.

**What management expects from it:** For Bosch Limited: exit of a sub-scale ~INR 400-450 crore, ~6% EBIT product business needing heavy IP and capex, no material hit to operations, a one-time INR 5,560 million gain lifting FY26 PAT 37.6%, and capital plus focus freed for mobility. For the divested unit: funding and ownership under Triton globally.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *CALL Nov 2024* — Asked about restructuring the many unlisted Bosch auto entities in India, management confirmed talks were live with the promoter but refused detail, framing portfolio moves as a standing board-level discussion. “These are discussions that are going on in the RBIN and Board with the promoter.”
- *CALL Feb 2025* — Karin Gilges gave the core separation test for the Building Technologies video/access/communications exit: it is a product business judged against what is core to Bosch Ltd.'s strategy. “This is a product business, and therefore we all the time also have to look at our portfolio and we have to manage our portfolio. And we have to see what is our core and what is our strategy.”
- *CALL Feb 2025* — Guruprasad Mudlapur said the India divestment was not a local decision but the India leg of the Bosch Group's global sale of Building Technologies to private-equity firm Triton, routed first to a parent subsidiary. “And you may have seen that the building technologies division globally has been sold to venture capitalist Triton, and this is an ongoing part of that sequence and in India, we are doing it to subsidiary of our parent who will then take it back to Triton.”
- *CALL Feb 2025* — Management sized the business being separated at roughly INR 450 crore of revenue and about 6% EBIT margin, i.e. immaterial to the listed company's operations. “It's a very small business. About the revenue that goes out is about Rs. 450 crores.”
- *CALL Feb 2025* — Alongside the divestment, the quarter carried a INR 471 million exceptional provision for restructuring Mobility operations to stay cost-competitive as the product mix shifts to common rail and NOx sensors. “During the quarter, the Company has made a provision of 471 million INR towards restructuring its operations to be competitive in the Mobility business .”
- *CALL Aug 2025* — Asked for the criteria that decide what to retain, grow, divest or merge, Mudlapur gave the group's top-3 rule and said Video Solutions/Access/Communications failed it because the IP and investment needed were not a Bosch Ltd. focus. “We want to be in the top 3 in every segment we operate.”
- *CALL Aug 2025* — He made the hive-off reasoning explicit: becoming a top performer in that portfolio would have required investment, IP and change dynamics the listed company did not want to commit. “So based on this, certain portfolio actions are taken and one of them was the building technologies area of Video Solutions, Access and Communication systems, where we realized that significant additional investment, a lot of IP and a lot of change dynamics are required to make this into a top performer, which we believed at that point of time was not in our focus.”
- *CALL Apr 2026* — At the group meeting management cited the earlier separation precedent — the mobility solutions business removed from the listco for heavy investment needs, a market outside India and sustained losses now funded by the parent. “Yeah , see, we had one mobility solutions business which we actually took out of the listco a couple of years ago because of the very heavy investments required.”
- *CALL Apr 2026* — The same logic kept Bosch Automotive Electronics (RBAI) outside the listed entity: a captive, low-margin, capex-intensive contract manufacturer whose consolidation would add no turnover and little profit. “So, at this point of time, we did not find a good commercial logic to bring this business in when it does not add turnover, doesn't contribute much to the margins, and there is very heavy intensity on investments.”
- *CALL Apr 2026* — The counter-move was consolidation: RBIC was bought because its safety and braking portfolio is powertrain-agnostic, complementary with no overlap, and margin-accretive from day one — structured as a fast all-cash close rather than a Maharashtra-Karnataka scheme. “And therefore, all cash deal, even after the close of the ballot and the approval, we would really try to make a fast close, and the target would be a 100% subsidiary under the Bosch Limited.”
- *CALL Apr 2026* — Gilges said the cash structure was deliberately chosen so the Bosch Group would not rise to 75% and dilute minorities, since a share deal would have signalled a later offload. “And what we don't want to somehow do is or send a signal, yeah, that we do a deal, we offload afterwards and then the Bosch Group very clearly said we don't want to dilute the minority shareholders .”
- *CALL May 2026* — Asked about further JVs or carve-outs, Mudlapur described separation and addition as one continuous process rather than a one-off event, with the Brakes India/Wheels India air-systems JV as the latest instance. “As we've informed multiple times in our calls, we are always working on portfolio expansion, portfolio decluttering and enhancement.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No stranded-cost, headcount or asset detail; no purchase-price adjustment, post-exit margin or overhead guidance; no stated reason Triton was buyer; residual Building Technologies plans unexplained.

## CASTROLIND — Castrol India Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a scheme of arrangement whose nature the documents on file do not settle) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 2.5/10 · scheme (nature unclear) · 1 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-06-29, latest 2026-06-29

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; indicated timeline: No new listing; Castrol India's shares remain listed on BSE (500870) and NSE (CASTROLIND). On 4 February 2026 management said "we expect the transaction at some point to close toward the end of the year", subject to regulatory approvals.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** BP's global Castrol lubricants business, held via Castrol Group Holdings Limited, sold to a Stonepeak-led JV — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* Promoter Castrol Limited holds 51% of Castrol India; after the deal BP (via BPMH) keeps 35% non-controlling in the Acquirer, Stonepeak 65% with sole control, CPPIB non-controlling.
- *What it reveals:* A high-quality cash compounder: 12 straight quarters of growth, FY25 revenue INR5,722 crores, EBITDA INR1,348 crores (24% margin), PAT INR950 crores, ~90% dividend payout, debt-free balance sheet, market-leading automotive share in early 20s.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — No new entity is distributed; existing listing continues, and the acquirer is buying up to 77%, risking a shortfall in minimum public shareholding.
- *Parent or spin:* spin · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* The detailed public statement (DPS), due within 5 working days of completion, for the enhanced Offer Price under Regulation 8(12).
- *In their words:* “From Castrol India standpoint, there's no change in our structure, strategy or operating model.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Nothing in these texts describes Castrol India Ltd. separating one of its own businesses — there is no scheme of demerger, no segment carve-out of lubricants, Auto Care, industrial or the Castrol Auto Service network; the separation being reconstructed is at the parent, where BP p.l.c. is detaching the entire Castrol lubricants business (including its 51% promoter stake in the listed Indian entity, held via Castrol Limited and Castrol Group Holdings Limited) from BP's oil and gas group. Management said BP announced a global strategic review of Castrol around February 2025 'with the intention of accelerating Castrol's next phase of value delivery,' and Kedar Lele twice framed the driver as BP's own balance sheet: 'BP's decision to carve out Castrol is driven by the global compulsion that a large oil and gas major faces... the global CEO of BP has said this that they would want to retire the debt and they see in Castrol a good asset that can be monetized' (Aug 2025), repeated in Nov 2025 as 'BP retires some of its debt by giving the value of the assets called Castrol.' The second stated reason is strategic mismatch: Castrol's growth agenda — core mobility, industrial lubricants (12–14% of volume, growing double digit versus high single digit automotive), mobility services (750+ Castrol Auto Service centres, the ~INR 400–500 crore ki Mobility stake, the VinFast aftersales MoU), Auto Care and data-centre immersion/direct-to-chip coolant fluids at roughly $1/litre gross margin — are 'different from the oil and gas business,' so separate ownership brings 'a focus on value creation for Castrol' and lets it be 'a more effective and innovative business partner to our customers.' India was positioned as a reason the asset is attractive rather than a problem being solved: 'a little over 10% of the volume of global Castrol and a little better than that in terms of profitability,' because its mix skews to 2-wheelers and cars. The buyer side was run by BP, not by Castrol India: data was supplied 'into a data room for potential investors... run from our central team bound by the NDA and administered by BP's global M&A team directly,' with the local MD saying 'I do not participate in any of that transaction.' The outcome, announced December 2025, is a joint venture — Motion JVCo Limited (Stonepeak-controlled, with CPP Investment Board taking a non-controlling interest) buying 100% of Castrol Group Holdings Limited under an SPA dated 23 December 2025, with BP Motion Holdings retaining 35% of the acquirer and Stonepeak 65% in sole control; that indirect change of control over the 51% promoter block (50,44,52,416 shares) triggered a mandatory 26% open offer for 25,71,71,820 shares at INR 194.04 per share, up to INR 4,990.16 crore, conditional on roughly two dozen antitrust clearances (including CCI) and a dozen foreign-investment/national-security approvals plus an EU FSR review. For the listed Indian company management insisted the consequence is deliberately nil: no change in structure, strategy or operating model, and specifically that the year-end global base-oil volume rebates that lift Q4 margins to ~26% 'will not get affected by any strategic sales.'

**How it evolved:** It surfaced only as a parent-level item: the Oct 2024 and Feb 2025 calls carry no mention, and the first discussion is the 29 Apr 2025 call (May 2025), where Kedar Lele answers Abinash S. that BP has announced a global strategic review of Castrol to 'unlock value' and accelerate growth in industrial, mobility services and data-centre fluids. By the 6 Aug 2025 call it is named a 'carve out' with an explicit motive — BP retiring debt by monetising Castrol — plus the first sizing of India at ~10% of global Castrol volume and better-than-average profitability; the 6 Nov 2025 call adds process detail (data room, NDA, BP global M&A running it, MD excluded) and reassurance that global base-oil rebates survive any sale. The 4 Feb 2026 call reports the December 2025 outcome — a JV with an investor at 65% and BP retaining 35%, subject to worldwide regulatory approval, expected to close 'toward the end of the year' — consistent with the 24 Dec 2025 open-offer announcement, and by the 29 Apr 2026 call (May 2026) the new interim CEO reduces it to 'no change in our structure, strategy or operating model' pending approvals.

**What management expects from it:** For BP: cash to retire debt and monetise a good asset. For Castrol: dedicated owners focused on value creation, accelerating core mobility, industrial lubricants, mobility services and data-centre fluids, and making it a more effective, innovative partner. For Castrol India: explicitly nothing changes — same structure, strategy, operating model, 21–24% EBITDA band, retained global base-oil rebates and R&D access. Minorities get a 26% exit at INR 194.04.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=2011432e-3fea-44f0-9517-23b34d69d234.pdf)* — First mention: BP's global strategic review of Castrol, framed as unlocking value and accelerating Castrol's growth in core mobility, industrial lubricants, mobility services and data-centre fluids. “So BP announced the strategic review of its Castrol business globally with the intention of accelerating Castrol's next phase of value delivery.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=38016e7c-eaef-4ce9-aa5c-2151888cb1c8.pdf)* — The stated driver is BP's own debt, not any problem inside Castrol: a large oil and gas major monetising a good asset. “Now BP's decision to carve out Castrol is driven by the global compulsion that a large oil and gas major faces. And it is, the global CEO of BP has said this that they would want to retire the debt and they see in Castrol a good asset that can be monetized.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=38016e7c-eaef-4ce9-aa5c-2151888cb1c8.pdf)* — Strategic-fit argument for separation: Castrol's growth lines (mobility, industrial lubricants, mobility services, data-centre fluids) sit outside oil and gas. “All of these businesses are different from the oil and gas business. And with this, there will be a focus on value creation for Castrol.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=38016e7c-eaef-4ce9-aa5c-2151888cb1c8.pdf)* — Sizing of the Indian piece inside the asset being sold — above-average profitability because of the 2-wheeler and car mix. “at an overall level, we do about a little over 10% of the volume of global Castrol and a little better than that in terms of profitability because our business is structured around 2-wheelers and cars, which is really more profitable part of the business versus the average trucks and the average profitability that you see in the segment.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=6f33d826-204e-4df1-8310-f9a4c716f3d9.pdf)* — Process disclosure in answer to Kirtan Mehta (Baroda BNP Paribas): bidders were being served data by BP's M&A team, with the Indian MD walled off. “We have been supplying data into a data room for potential investors, and that gets run from our central team bound by the NDA and administered by BP's global M&A team directly. And I do not participate in any of that transaction.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=6f33d826-204e-4df1-8310-f9a4c716f3d9.pdf)* — Restates the dual purpose — accelerate Castrol's value delivery while BP pays down debt — and dates the review to roughly February 2025. “And the intention was very simple that they accelerate Castrol's next phase of value delivery while BP retires some of its debt by giving the value of the assets called Castrol.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=6f33d826-204e-4df1-8310-f9a4c716f3d9.pdf)* — Answering Harsh on the Q4 margin uplift, management ring-fenced the global base-oil volume rebates (which take Q4 EBITDA to ~26% versus ~24% full year) from the sale. “So none of these discounts that we see in the Q4 will get affected by any strategic sales.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=40456ee7-02fc-47c0-ad1d-c6e0f24b6062.pdf)* — Outcome disclosed to Lokesh (Aionion Capital): a JV where BP keeps 35% and the incoming investor takes 65%, pending approvals, with closure expected toward end of the year. “So at the parent level, BP has signaled that they will form a joint venture with an investor, where BP will remain a 35% shareholder and the investor will take 65%.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=40456ee7-02fc-47c0-ad1d-c6e0f24b6062.pdf)* — No India-level consequence asserted; any disclosures to follow will come from the new shareholders. “To your question on what may or may not impact, very early, it's business as usual for us over here.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=b2502bf8-680b-48ed-a5f0-5409b7938365.pdf)* — Interim CEO Saugata Basuray reduces 'shareholder development at parent level' to a non-event for the listed company while global approvals are pending. “From Castrol India standpoint, there's no change in our structure, strategy or operating model.”
- *Scheme* — The 24 Dec 2025 public announcement shows the mechanism: an SPA dated 23 Dec 2025 under which Motion JVCo Limited buys 100% of Castrol Group Holdings Limited from BP p.l.c., indirectly acquiring the 51% (50,44,52,416-share) promoter block in Castrol India held by Castrol Limited. “The Acquirer has entered into an agreement for sale and purchase with BP p.l.c. ("Seller") dated December 23, 2025 ("SPA"), pursuant to which the Seller has agreed to sell and transfer to the Acquirer, and the Acquirer has agreed to acquire from the Seller, 100% (one hundred percent) of the equity share capital of Castrol Group Holdings Limited ("CGHL").”
- *Scheme* — Consideration structure confirms the 65/35 split: BP Motion Holdings is allotted 35% of the acquirer, Stonepeak Motion Holdco retains 65% and sole control, with CPP Investment Board Private Holdings (6) Inc. a non-controlling co-investor. “Following this, PAC 1 (which presently holds the entire equity share capital of the Acquirer) will hold 65% (sixty five percent) of the equity share capital of the Acquirer and remain in sole control of the Acquirer. BPMH will hold a non-controlling interest in the Acquirer.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No stated post-close terms for brand licensing, BP R&D/technology access, or global base-oil contract scale; no India P&L, dividend-policy or delisting implications; no closing date.
