**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** not stated — the filings concern an employee stock option plan, not a business separation — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* Eligible: employees and directors of the Company and subsidiaries/associates; excluded are promoters, promoter group, independent directors, and directors holding over 10% of issued shares
- *What it reveals:* not stated; the filings only reveal potential dilution of up to 17,73,031 equity shares of Rs. 10 each, with exercise price left entirely to the Compensation Committee
- *Selling pressure:* unclear — No separation or index event in the documents; only option dilution, with grants pending NSE/BSE in-principle approval
- *Parent or spin:* neither · *option pricing date:* not stated — exercise price is 'as determined by the Compensation Committee and communicated to the eligible employee vide the letter of grant'
- *Read next:* The in-principle approvals from NSE and BSE, then the first grant letter disclosing the actual exercise price
- *In their words:* “The total number of Options to be granted under the Plan shall not exceed 17,73,031 (Seventeen Lakh Seventy Three Thousand Thirty One) Stock Options.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

What EIEL is "separating" is not a demerger of a listed business but the carve-out of its new renewable energy business out of the parent EPC company into a dedicated subsidiary chain — EIE Renewables with step-down Sunaxis Renewable, later joined by the acquired wind-EPC company Suyog Urja — while water and wastewater stays entirely in Enviro Infra Engineers Limited. Management's stated reason is a "clear demarcation in the business lines": water/wastewater (STPs, CETPs, ZLD, water supply, HAM) remains in the parent, and every renewable asset, PPA and EPC order sits in the subsidiary, the same logic they already use for HAM projects where an SPV is formed "so that the financials of that particular SPV can be separated and clearly visible." The second driver is capital-allocation risk: the water business is B2G and working-capital intensive (debtors/UBR from JJM in MP, then AMRUT funds stuck across Chhattisgarh, MP, Rajasthan, Haryana and Punjab pushing the cycle to 166 days with 195 UBR days against a 90-day target), whereas renewables are capex- and debt-heavy IPP/BESS assets; ring-fencing lets each carry its own term loans and "separate working capital lines," with consolidated debt-to-equity never crossing 1:1 (Rs 422 crore debt, 0.34 at FY26). Third, the parent's equity exposure is explicitly capped — Rs 50 crore earmarked in the IPO objects, a hard ceiling of Rs 75 crore from Enviro to EIE Renewables and "there will not be any further investment" — with a further ~Rs 40 crore infused directly by Manish Jain, Sanjay Jain and some shareholders, plus project debt (~Rs 100 crore visible for FY27). Fourth, the margin profiles differ and management did not want them blended: water/wastewater guides 22–24% EBITDA (delivered 25–27.6%), while renewables were pegged at 18–20% EBITDA and later 10–12% PAT (BESS EPC ~10%), and in Q4 FY26 roughly Rs 100–120 crore of near-zero-margin renewable IPP revenue visibly dragged reported margins — hence the promise to "give the segmental revenues separately, so the segmental profitability would be clearly visible to everyone." Fifth, separate entities keep the growth stories additive rather than substitutive: the 35–40% water CAGR guidance was always quoted ex-renewables ("it will be double growth"), with renewables scaling from ~Rs 200 crore FY26 to Rs 400–500 crore FY27 and a Rs 2,051 crore renewable execution order book plus Rs 1,079 crore renewable O&M/IPP inside a Rs 6,814 crore total. Finally, the subsidiary is the vehicle for capability and counterparty de-risking: its own 250+ person renewable team under dedicated business heads, a COO hired for the vertical, NTPC B2B BESS orders (930 MWh, ~Rs 1,070 crore) and Suyog's A-to-AAA private wind clients offset government receivable risk, and assets parked in the subsidiary can be monetized/offloaded if leverage rises. Analysts (Dheeraj Ram, Peter and Nikhil Rungta of LIC MF, Meet Shah) pushed hardest on why a separate entity was needed and on the capital crunch; lenders feature only as project financiers (PTC substitution on the Balangir asset, HDFC for Saharanpur, Kotak for Mathura), and JV partners are contemplated only for desalination — no lender or investor is said to have demanded the separation.

**How it evolved:** The idea surfaced on the Feb 2025 (Q3 FY25) call as an item already flagged in the DRHP/RHP: a new subsidiary for solar, 24x7 renewables, hydro and green hydrogen, with a COO to be appointed, framed as "double growth" on top of water. By the Jun 2025 (Q4 FY25) call the structure existed and was questioned as a related-party transaction — EIE Renewables bought for Rs 10 lakh and Sunaxis for Rs 1 lakh, 100% subsidiaries, justified as "clear demarcation" with the HAM-SPV precedent and a Rs 75 crore funding cap; Aug 2025 (Q1 FY26) confirmed the two solar assets sat in EIE Renewables and were excluded from the parent's Rs 1,178 crore order book, and Nov 2025 (Q2 FY26) separated the guidance itself (renewable revenue and 18–20% margins quoted apart from water's 22–24%). Feb 2026 (Q3 FY26) hardened it into financial independence — "both the segments will move independently," separate funding and working-capital lines, no further equity from Enviro, Rs 40 crore from promoters/shareholders instead — against an investor challenge that one arm is working-capital heavy and the other capex heavy. By Jun 2026 (Q4 FY26) it was a three-company group (Enviro, Renewable, Suyog Urja for wind EPC), with dedicated divisional heads, a 250+ renewable team, and a commitment to report renewable revenue, order book and profitability as a separate company/segment.

**What management expects from it:** Parent stays a pure water/wastewater EPC at 22–24% guided EBITDA (25–27% delivered) with its own working-capital lines; renewables carry their own project debt, capped equity (Rs 75 crore from Enviro plus ~Rs 40 crore promoter/shareholder money) and lower 18–20% EBITDA / 10–12% PAT; separate entities and segmental reporting make each one's profitability visible, keep consolidated debt-to-equity under 1:1, and make renewable growth additive — "double growth."

## ELGIEQUIP — Elgi Equipments Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a scheme of arrangement whose nature the documents on file do not settle) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 2.5/10 · scheme (nature unclear) · 2 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-07-11, latest 2026-09-04

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** No demerger; wholly owned subsidiary ELGI Compressors USA divested its equity stakes in two US joint ventures — class `regulatory_strategic`.

- *Insiders:* No new entity, so no promoter stake stated. Buyers were JV partners James Gery Naico and Jeffery Brandon Todd; neither belongs to promoter/promoter group; not related-party transactions
- *What it reveals:* Both JVs were immaterial — 0.09% and 0.02% of consolidated PAT, 0.23% and 0.06% of equity — yet paying with its entire stake to regain exclusivity in California and Texas counties implies direct distribution access is worth more than the JV earnings
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — No shares issued or listed; stakes divested contributed 0.09% and 0.02% of consolidated PAT, so no index or industry shift
- *Parent or spin:* neither · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Next quarterly call commentary on US distribution operations and go-to-market, which management said needs a different strategy
- *In their words:* “Elgi Compressors USA Inc. has secured release of exclusivity in certain counties of Texas, USA and towards that it has relinquished its entire equity stake.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

On these texts alone, Elgi is not separating a business in the demerger/spin-off sense — there is no scheme of arrangement, no appointed date, no entity carve-out, and the earnings calls never once discuss a separation. What the filings actually record are two small disposals by the wholly owned subsidiary ELGI Compressors USA Inc. of its equity in US distribution joint ventures, each sold back to the existing JV partner, and in each case the stated purpose is identical: to buy back territorial exclusivity. On 10 July 2026 Elgi divested PLA Holding Company, LLC together with its subsidiary Pattons of California, LLC to JV partner Jeffery Brandon Todd, receiving USD 100,000 'apart from release of exclusivity by the joint venture partner for oil flooded rotary screw air compressors in certain important counties of California'; the JV had contributed share of profit of USD 41,982 in FY2025-26 (0.09% of consolidated PAT) and share of net worth of USD 532,595 (0.23% of consolidated equity), with turnover not disclosed because the JV was equity-accounted. On 4 September 2026 it relinquished its entire stake in Gentex Air Solutions LLC to JV partner James Gery Naico purely 'for the purpose of release of exclusivity, in certain counties of Texas, USA' — no cash consideration is stated — against share of profit of USD 7,735 (0.02% of consolidated PAT) and share of net worth of USD 138,972 (0.06% of equity). Both filings state the buyers are not promoter/promoter-group, the transactions are not related-party, and that disposal outside a scheme of arrangement is 'Not Applicable'/'Not applicable' — i.e. no Regulation 37A scheme at all. The only rationale that can be reconstructed is the go-to-market problem management described repeatedly on the calls: Elgi's distributor-led US model has plateaued because distributors tied to large brands will not switch, so the stated priority is to 'get in front of the customer more often' through a hybrid direct-plus-distributor model, which exclusivity grants in a county directly block; management also said outright that the earlier route of taking equity to incubate a distributor is 'not our intent now' and that 'a manufacturing company cannot run a distribution company.' Nobody in these texts is said to have asked for it — no investor, lender or partner demand is recorded, and the counterparties are the JV partners themselves.

**How it evolved:** The idea surfaces as strategy, not as a transaction: on the Nov 2025 (Q2 FY26) call management disowned the equity-in-distributor route ('that was an equity investment by us... That's not our intent now') and floated a hybrid model of own direct salespeople partnering distributors for service, in both the US and Europe. On the Feb 2026 (Q3) call Jairam explicitly separated the owned distributors (Pattons, Michigan Air) from 'our JVs' when discussing the distribution-operations shortfall, and framed the hybrid strategy as being about equipment sales rather than aftermarket. At the Mar 2026 annual investor meet the post-mortem became explicit — distribution acquisition was 'strategically the right thing' but 'we are a manufacturing company. We are not a distribution company' — and the channel strategy was declared to be plateauing because a slice of distributors is exclusive to the large brands. The Jun 2026 (Q4 FY26) call promised a 'very measured intervention in very specific areas' on US go-to-market; the actual exits were then filed on 11 July 2026 (California) and 4 September 2026 (Texas), neither of which had ever been pre-announced on a call.

**What management expects from it:** The filings state no expected benefit beyond release of exclusivity for oil-flooded rotary screw compressors in named California and Texas counties. The calls set the expectation only generally: direct/hybrid access putting Elgi in front of customers, where it wins two of three times; growth in installed base feeding aftermarket (12-15% of overseas revenue towards 20%, versus 28% in India); overheads shifted to India to fund revenue-facing roles.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The 11 July 2026 filing records the divestment of PLA Holding Company, LLC and its subsidiary Pattons of California, LLC to JV partner Jeffery Brandon Todd, with the consideration being USD 100,000 plus the release of product-specific exclusivity in named California counties — the clearest statement of purpose anywhere in these texts. “Receipt of USD 100,000 apart from release of exclusivity by the joint venture partner for oil flooded rotary screw air compressors in certain important counties of California, US.”
- *Scheme* — The 4 September 2026 filing shows the entire Gentex Air Solutions LLC stake surrendered to JV partner James Gery Naico with no cash consideration stated at all; exclusivity release in Texas counties is itself the consideration. “Elgi Compressors USA Inc. has secured release of exclusivity in certain counties of Texas, USA and towards that it has relinquished its entire equity stake.”
- *Scheme* — Both disposals are financially immaterial on the company's own numbers — FY2025-26 shares of profit of USD 41,982 (0.09% of consolidated PAT) and USD 7,735 (0.02%), and net worth shares of USD 532,595 (0.23% of equity) and USD 138,972 (0.06%) — and each was signed and completed on the same day. “USD 7,735 As a % of Consolidated PAT = 0.02% USD 1,38,972 As a % of Equity = 0.06%”
- *Scheme* — Neither filing involves a scheme of arrangement, a slump sale or a related party; the Regulation 37A and amalgamation/merger disclosure rows are answered 'Not Applicable', so there is no demerger document to read a rationale out of. “whether the sale, lease or disposal of the undertaking is outside Scheme of Arrangement? If yes, details of the same including compliance with regulation 37A of LODR Regulations. Not Applicable”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=89d7fd72-a7b1-403b-b426-385d1e1e4d33.pdf)* — Asked whether the new Europe/US route meant taking control of distributorships, Jairam ruled out both acquisition and the earlier practice of taking equity to incubate a distributor, describing instead own salespeople partnered with distributors who keep the aftermarket. “No, no, that was an equity investment by us. We incubated a new distributor. That's not our intent now.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=89d7fd72-a7b1-403b-b426-385d1e1e4d33.pdf)* — He defined the core US problem as three layers of distributor inertia — breaking in, fighting for share of a multi-brand distributor's wallet, and a pool that will not leave incumbent OEMs — which is why channel alone cannot deliver the required growth rate. “Now through all this inertia, if our goal is to be in front of the customer more often, then the existing channel-based approach alone is not going to give us that additional goal.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=0390c9c7-8cf2-4685-a930-2eb2613d6053.pdf)* — When the distribution shortfall was raised, Jairam drew a line between the owned distributors and the joint ventures, and said the JVs were not the issue — the only place in the calls where the JV structure is addressed at all. “No, this is nothing to do with our JVs Salil. This is what I mean by distribution operations is Pattons and Michigan Air, which is 2 distributors that we own.”
- *[Mar 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=76ca8e77-b84d-4199-884f-f3a876a32968.pdf)* — Answering a question about the US distribution acquisitions having gone badly, Jairam conceded the capability mismatch directly — the right strategic call, wrong operator — which is the nearest thing in these texts to a reason for stepping back from owned/JV distribution equity. “So the distribution acquisition strategically is the right thing. But what was wrong is we are a manufacturing company. We are not a distribution company.”
- *[Mar 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=76ca8e77-b84d-4199-884f-f3a876a32968.pdf)* — He said the distributor-recruitment strategy is plateauing because exclusivity-bound distributors will never switch — 70-80% of their profit being aftermarket — leaving only multi-brand distributors to fight over, and that 'what got us here is not going to take us there.' “One, out of the universe of distributors that are available, a certain percentage of distributors are exclusive to the large brands. Those distributors are not going to switch.”
- *[Mar 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=76ca8e77-b84d-4199-884f-f3a876a32968.pdf)* — The strategic prize he named for direct access is the win rate when Elgi reaches the end customer, repeated as roughly two in three — the economic logic that makes paying equity for exclusivity release coherent. “We just need to find a way to get in front of the customer because the minute we get in front of the customer, two out of three times we win.”
- *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=feeac222-9b4b-433b-a5a5-b4e3480e77f5.pdf)* — On the last call before the first exit filing, Jairam said India go-to-market investment was done and the next, deliberately narrow, go-to-market intervention would be in the US — but gave no timing, value or mechanism. “We will do a very measured intervention in very specific areas to be able to do that.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=538e96c0-a5c6-4fe8-9a27-68fe53ae6c6a.pdf)* — The only earlier mention of reorganising Elgi's geographic footprint was framed entirely as a contingency against a 50% US tariff, not as a distribution restructuring, and management never linked it to the later JV exits. “The next 25%, the solution is not going to look like the solution that we have had for the first 25%, right? So that's why I said the second 25 will involve certain structural changes in the way we are organized, our geographical presence and all that, yeah it will demand a much more fundamental change.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No stated valuation basis, no cash for Gentex, no initiator, no revenue from either JV, no margin/capital/valuation effect, and not a word about any of it on any call.

## GMDCLTD — Gujarat Mineral Development Corporation Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a scheme of arrangement whose nature the documents on file do not settle) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 2.5/10 · scheme (nature unclear) · 1 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-07-31, latest 2026-07-31

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**Stated in the filings:** record date 2026-05-12.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** The gas transmission undertaking demerged out of Gujarat Energy Limited into GSPL Transmission Limited; GMDC is only a shareholder — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* not stated; filings only note GMDC is a Government of Gujarat Enterprise and a shareholder receiving GEL and GTL shares
- *What it reveals:* GMDC's extinguished unlisted GSPC investment converts into GEL shares (10 per 305 GSPC) plus GTL shares (1 per 3 GEL); documents give no value, only Unallocated segment assets of Rs 4,000.24 crore
- *Selling pressure:* unclear — Documents state only the share-exchange ratios; no size, index or industry information is given
- *Parent or spin:* neither · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* The Composite Scheme of Amalgamation and Arrangement and GMDC's carrying value of the former GSPC investment
- *In their words:* “Pursuant to the Composite Scheme of Amalgamation and Arrangement sanctioned by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs on 8th April 2026 (effective from filing with RoC, Ahmedabad on 1st May 2026), the Company's investment in Gujarat State Petroleum Corporation Limited (GSPC) stood extinguished.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

On these texts alone, there is no evidence that GMDC is separating, demerging or spinning off any business of its own, and management never once discusses doing so — so no rationale can be reconstructed for a GMDC separation. The only corporate separation anywhere in this record is in someone else's capital structure: Note 2 of the Q1 FY27 standalone results (filing dated 31 July 2026) records that under a Composite Scheme of Amalgamation and Arrangement sanctioned by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs on 8 April 2026 and effective on filing with the RoC, Ahmedabad on 1 May 2026, GMDC's investment in Gujarat State Petroleum Corporation Limited (GSPC) stood extinguished, and on the record date of 12 May 2026 GMDC received 10 equity shares of ₹2 each of Gujarat Energy Limited (GEL) for every 305 GSPC shares held; separately, pursuant to the demerger of the gas transmission undertaking, GMDC is to receive 1 equity share of ₹10 each of GSPL Transmission Limited (GTL) for every 3 GEL shares. GMDC is a passive minority shareholder being handed replacement scrip there, not the separating company, and the filing gives only the mechanics — sanction date, effective date, record date, exchange ratios — with no stated purpose, no valuation, no accounting impact quantified and no management commentary. The nearest thing to a separation debate in the calls is the opposite: management defends keeping the 250 MW Akrimota Thermal Power Station (ATPS) rather than exiting it, arguing on 30 July 2024 that "this plant has a plant base and a PPA life of 1.5 decades left" and that a revised PPA plus allowed capex would turn "this bleeding asset" into an income generator — even though the power segment lost ₹79.61 crore at segment level in FY26 on ₹215.72 crore of revenue and ₹6.00 crore in Q1 FY27 on ₹111.25 crore, and on 23 May 2025 an analyst put the run rate at "Rs. 25 crore revenue with Rs. 11 crore loss." The only asset-level disposal idea raised by anyone is an investor's suggestion on 30 July 2024 that GMDC divest its cross-holdings in other Gujarat PSUs to help fund the ₹13,000 crore 2030 capex plan, to which the MD replied only "We would be open to all ideas." Everything else in these three calls is the opposite of separation — Project Shikhar's 4x growth plan, six new lignite mines, three Odisha coal blocks (Baitarani West, Burapahar, Kudanali-Lubri; 26 MTPA combined), the Ambaji copper project and Ambadongar rare earths — all held inside one listed entity, plus two MoUs (GNFC for coal-to-chemicals/UCG and IREL (India) Limited for rare earths) that are collaborations, not carve-outs.

**How it evolved:** The idea never surfaces in the calls: on 30 July 2024 (the Q1 FY25 call, supplied twice — tagged Jul 2024 and Aug 2024, identical transcripts) the discussion is diversification and ₹3,030/₹3,424 crore annual capex, with separation raised only as an investor's unanswered prompt to divest cross-holdings in other Gujarat PSUs. On 23 May 2025 management again treats every business — four lignite mines, Odisha coal, copper, rare earths, ATPS — as one portfolio, and reaffirms holding ATPS after a ₹300–400 crore refurbishment capex it expects to recover as a PPA pass-through with a ~30 paisa higher tariff. The only separation on record appears without warning in the 31 July 2026 filing, as a note on the GSPC Composite Scheme and the GSPL gas-transmission demerger that changed what GMDC holds, not what GMDC does. So the plan did not evolve across the calls — it belongs to GSPC/GEL, and arrived at GMDC as a share-exchange entry.

**What management expects from it:** Nothing is stated, because management never discusses separating a GMDC business. For the GSPC scheme and gas-transmission demerger — which are GSPC's, not GMDC's — the filing gives only exchange ratios and dates, with no expected effect on margins, capital, valuation or focus for GEL, GTL or GMDC. On its own businesses management expects the opposite of separation: everything retained under Project Shikhar's integrated 4x-by-2030 plan.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The only separation documented: GSPC's Composite Scheme of Amalgamation and Arrangement, MCA-sanctioned 8 April 2026, effective on RoC Ahmedabad filing 1 May 2026, extinguished GMDC's GSPC investment; on record date 12 May 2026 GMDC got 10 GEL shares of ₹2 each per 305 GSPC shares. No reason for the scheme is given. “Pursuant to the Composite Scheme of Amalgamation and Arrangement sanctioned by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs on 8th April 2026 (effective from filing with RoC, Ahmedabad on 1st May 2026), the Company's investment in Gujarat State Petroleum Corporation Limited (GSPC) stood extinguished.”
- *Scheme* — A second, separate step: the demerger of the gas transmission undertaking, under which GMDC is to receive GSPL Transmission Limited (GTL) shares at 1 share of ₹10 each for every 3 GEL shares — again stated purely as a ratio, with no rationale, timing or value. “Further, pursuant to demerger of gas transmission undertaking, the Company shall receive 1 equity share of R10/- each of GPL Transmission Limited (GTL) for every 3 shares held in GEL.”
- *[Aug 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=30a137cd-db70-4bbe-9bc7-45666320abea.pdf)* — The closest anyone comes to asking GMDC to separate anything: an investor asks whether GMDC would divest its cross-holdings in other Gujarat PSUs given the funding need; management neither accepts nor rejects it, and it is never raised again. “We would be open to all ideas.”
- *[Aug 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=30a137cd-db70-4bbe-9bc7-45666320abea.pdf)* — Management explicitly argues for retaining the loss-making 250 MW ATPS power business rather than separating or exiting it, citing a revised PPA, allowed capex and a tier-one O&M contractor. “But in the next year, this bleeding asset should turn out to be an income-generating asset for the corporation.”
- *[Aug 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=30a137cd-db70-4bbe-9bc7-45666320abea.pdf)* — The retention case rests on residual plant and PPA life of about fifteen years, which management says GMDC has failed to monetise for a decade and a half. “The entire logic of pursuing with this plant is this plant has a plant base and a PPA life of 1.5 decades left.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=321a0949-9368-49ec-ae47-13bc5527aa97.pdf)* — A year later ATPS is still in the red and still being kept, with ₹300–400 crore of refurbishment capex expected back as a regulated pass-through and power priced ~30 paisa higher; the FY26 power segment result was a ₹79.61 crore loss and Q1 FY27 a ₹6.00 crore loss. “Yes, it is one division which runs in the red, but hopefully after overhaul, we would look at a better future in this year.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=321a0949-9368-49ec-ae47-13bc5527aa97.pdf)* — Partnering, not separating: for Burapahar GMDC sought outside partners for underground coal gasification via a live EOI, keeping the asset in-house — the same logic behind the 31 July 2026 GNFC MoU on coal-to-chemicals/UCG and the IREL (India) Limited MoU on rare earths. “We are looking for partners for underground coal gasification.”
- *[Jul 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=30a137cd-db70-4bbe-9bc7-45666320abea.pdf)* — This transcript is the same 30 July 2024 Q1 FY25 call as the Aug 2024 item, supplied twice; it contains no mention of any demerger, spin-off, carve-out, subsidiarisation or slump sale of a GMDC business. “So GMDC is going to keep on focusing on its core which is lignite and which contributes in excess of 90% of our revenues currently.”

*Not explained on the calls:* Why the GSPC/GSPL scheme happened, its value, accounting or dividend impact on GMDC, whether GEL/GTL shares will be held or sold, and the ₹522.65 crore FY26 exceptional item.

## INTELLECT — Intellect Design Arena Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a filing's text names a demerger; no scheme filing names it yet) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 2.5/10 · spin-off · 1 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-06-08, latest 2026-06-08

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Purple Fabric, its Open Business Impact AI / Enterprise Intelligence Operating System platform business, into an independent Line of Business — class `unrelated`.

- *Insiders:* Deepak Dastrala named CEO and Business Head of Purple Fabric, reporting to Arun Jain, who continues mentoring; Dastrala joins the Intellect Management Council as Senior Management Personnel. No equity stake in the LoB stated.
- *What it reveals:* Purple Fabric is the fourth growth engine: 45+ clients live, 550 domain-aware agents, 18-layer architecture, 95%+ accuracy SLA; ~Rs 200 Crore FY26 revenue target, AI revenue Rs 160 Crore, AI order book over $50 million, TAM Rs 1,000-5,000 Crore, benchmarked against Palantir.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — Carve-out is into an internal Line of Business; documents mention no share distribution, separate listed entity or index change.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Q1 FY27 results: segmented Purple Fabric revenue and its investment/margin split, versus the Rs 200 Crore target guided on calls.
- *In their words:* “As the market approaches an inflection point, moving rapidly from AI experimentation to scaled, enterprise-wide deployment, Intellect has determined that it is the optimal time to give Purple Fabric its independent identity.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The separation is the June 8, 2026 carve-out of Purple Fabric (purplefabric.ai), Intellect's Open Business Impact AI platform, out of the consolidated product organisation into an independent Line of Business under a new CEO, Deepak Dastrala, reporting directly to Arun Jain, who stays as mentor; Dastrala also joins the Intellect Management Council as Senior Management Personnel. Management's stated reason is DNA, not portfolio pruning: Intellect curated two parallel architectural disruptions over two years — eMACH.ai (the composable banking foundation, 700 microservices, ~₹1,667 Cr license-linked revenue, Wholesale ₹1,500 Cr+, Consumer ₹1,000 Cr+, Wealth/Insurance ₹500 Cr+) and Purple Fabric (the cognitive/AI layer) — and concluded 'the intrinsic DNA of eMACH.ai and Purple Fabric are completely different,' so sharing one structure was holding Purple Fabric back. The timing argument is a market inflection from AI experimentation to scaled enterprise-wide deployment, which management says makes this 'the optimal time' to give Purple Fabric an independent identity with dedicated resources, freedom and agility to 'curate its own destiny.' Purple Fabric's own traction justifies standalone status: 45+ clients live, a 95%+ accuracy SLA, an 18-layer architecture, 550 domain-aware agents, ~₹160 Cr FY26 AI revenue off ₹92 Cr of FY26 investment (against a ₹130 Cr plan), a $50mn+ AI order book booked in FY26, and two large enterprise-AI platform deals in India plus three-four outside. The problems it solves are structural: a licence/implementation banking business and a consumption-priced AI platform have opposite economics (Purple Fabric deals start at a quarter-to-half-million dollars and scale in years 2-3 toward a $3-5mn platform target, versus $5-7mn banking licences), opposite operating cadence (Jain's answer to the pricing question was the Salesforce-to-Bajaj analogy), and opposite talent model — the LoB is designed as an organisation 'in flow' with a networked 'Leadership Circle,' micro-teams and people wearing multiple hats instead of hierarchy. Nobody external forced it: Intellect is zero-debt with ₹1,257 Cr cash, so there are no lenders in the story; the pressure came from management's own AI thesis and from SI/partner demand (one large global system integrator plus 14 value-discovery partners signed, a target of ~100 partners), while investors had been pushing for separate Purple Fabric numbers and ROI visibility for four straight calls and were repeatedly refused.

**How it evolved:** Purple Fabric was first framed to investors as a ₹1,000-5,000 Cr opportunity in the December 19, 2024 session and the Feb 2025 call, where Jain said adoption, not revenue, was the objective and declined to split it out of the ₹10,000 Cr funnel. At the Jun 2025 (FY25) call he explicitly ruled separation out — 'We are not separating the company, but we will keep the costs separate' — while committing ₹100-130 Cr of non-capitalisable P&L spend; by Aug 2025 it had its own Business Head (John Turner), by Nov 2025 its own ₹25 Cr/quarter investment line (costing 3-3.25% of EBITDA), its own AI Labs in the new 7.25 lakh sq ft Siruseri facility, and Jain was rebuking the 'cannibalisation' question with 'It's a completely different line of business.' In Feb 2026 it was formally relabelled the 'fourth growth engine,' and the same call exposed the reporting problem — an investor computed only ~₹19 Cr of segmented Purple Fabric revenue against the ₹200 Cr claim, answered with 'Purple Fabric is embedded across the businesses.' After the May 2026 FY26 call disclosed ₹160 Cr AI revenue, a $50mn order book and product-wise Purple Fabric go-to-market (Trade, Lending, Wealth, Risk & Governance, Onboarding), the June 8, 2026 release completed the reversal and granted independent LoB status.

**What management expects from it:** Purple Fabric: dedicated resources, freedom, agility and micro-team speed to accelerate growth and 'curate its own destiny' in Business Impact AI; scale a platform/consumption model from $0.25-0.5mn entry deals toward $3-5mn, against a ₹1,000-5,000 Cr TAM. eMACH.ai remains the foundational architecture. Jain calls it 'a massive long-term opportunity for value creation.' No per-entity margin, capital or valuation target was given.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The core stated rationale is that the two platforms have fundamentally different natures, so independent LoB status buys Purple Fabric freedom and dedicated resources rather than divesting anything. “However, because their intrinsic DNAs are entirely unique, granting Purple Fabric independent LoB status gives it the freedom and dedicated resources to accelerate its growth.”
- *Scheme* — Timing is justified by the market shifting from AI pilots to scaled enterprise deployment, making this the moment for a separate identity to capture it. “As the market approaches an inflection point, moving rapidly from AI experimentation to scaled, enterprise-wide deployment, Intellect has determined that it is the optimal time to give Purple Fabric its independent identity.”
- *Scheme* — The division of labour is explicit: eMACH.ai remains the foundational architecture while Purple Fabric supplies the cognitive intelligence layer; the LoB is built on a networked 'Leadership Circle' with micro-team DNA, backed by 45+ live clients, a 95%+ accuracy SLA, 18-layer architecture and 550 domain-aware agents. “If eMACH.ai forms our foundational architecture, Purple Fabric provides the critical cognitive intelligence enterprises need to operationalize AI with complete confidence.”
- *[Jun 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=424bcfe1-e3bb-489b-840e-b9f01abf7073.pdf)* — In May 2025 Arun Jain explicitly rejected separating the business, committing only to ring-fencing the ₹100-130 Cr Purple Fabric cost inside the consolidated P&L — the position the June 2026 carve-out reverses. “We are not separating the company, but we will keep the costs separate.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=8c771ad3-8296-44be-a89f-e50350f010de.pdf)* — From the start Purple Fabric was run on a different scorecard from the banking products — platform adoption rather than revenue or margin — foreshadowing the DNA argument. “Revenue number is not an objective for Purple Fabric but adoption is.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=8f6dd7f2-9c10-44b8-bcc7-58769be8eb6b.pdf)* — Asked whether Purple Fabric was a top-up or cannibalised existing products, Jain rejected the framing outright and insisted it was a distinct line of business — the same logic later used for the carve-out; the quarter carried ₹25 Cr of Purple Fabric spend, costing 3-3.25% of EBITDA margin. “It's a completely different line of business.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=772d93cd-fcb8-4958-9c4a-b82710ef17bb.pdf)* — Purple Fabric was formally reclassified as a standalone fourth growth engine alongside Wholesale (₹1,400 Cr), Consumer (₹1,000 Cr) and IntellectAI (₹500 Cr), a structural step before the LoB carve-out. “From 2024 onwards, we have begun building a fourth growth engine Purple Fabric, our Open Business Impact AI Platform.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=772d93cd-fcb8-4958-9c4a-b82710ef17bb.pdf)* — Investors pressed on the disclosure problem — only ~₹19 Cr of segmented Purple Fabric revenue was visible against the ₹200 Cr full-year claim — because the platform was buried inside wealth, insurance and the other businesses. “Am I correct in understanding that Purple Fabric in the last 12 months has contributed only ₹19 Crs.”
- *May 2026* — By FY26 Purple Fabric had its own commercial engine — ₹160 Cr revenue, a $50mn+ AI order book off ₹92 Cr invested, platform revenue up 141% to ₹580 Cr, and a product-by-product go-to-market (Trade, Lending, Wealth, Risk & Governance, Onboarding) — plus two India and three-four overseas platform deals. “We have signed two large enterprise AI platform deals in India and three or four platform deals outside India, and our pipeline is growing well.”
- *May 2026* — The technical moat behind the 95%+ accuracy SLA is Jain's accuracy-multiplication argument (85% x 95% x 95% = 76.7%, unusable for core banking processes), solved with ~15 patents filed in six months out of 125 filed overall — research management treats as a distinct discipline from banking product engineering. “For a financial institution's core processes, we need at least 95% as a benchmark to make it usable for production-grade AI, which I call production-grade AI or enterprise AI.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=58254b29-0ea2-4a38-8e51-2b3f066334d7.pdf)* — Purple Fabric's economics were incompatible with the banking P&L from launch — the entire ₹130 Cr was non-capitalisable expense — and Jain positioned it in a different competitive set (Palantir, C3.ai) with its own revenue model (pilot, implementation, transaction/outcome, core-based platform licence). “All of it will be in the P&L. In the market, we cannot capitalise on any of this investment.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=8f6dd7f2-9c10-44b8-bcc7-58769be8eb6b.pdf)* — The go-to-market also diverged: Purple Fabric is sold through system integrators and value-discovery partners (target ~100 globally, 14 signed by Q3, plus one large global SI) rather than Intellect's direct banking salesforce, and separate AI Labs were funded in the new 7.25 lakh sq ft Siruseri campus. “So, we are one of the three options available to SI to take to the market.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No legal structure, demerger, separate entity, shareholding or external funding; no standalone P&L, margin, capital or headcount disclosure; no asset/IP transfer terms; no timeline; no eMACH.ai impact.

## IXIGO — Le Travenues Technology Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a scheme of arrangement whose nature the documents on file do not settle) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 2.5/10 · scheme (nature unclear) · 1 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-08-13, latest 2026-08-13

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**Stated in the filings:** size hint: 0.96% of net worth.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Sale of 17.39% stake (46,264 CCPS) in associate Freshbus Private Limited; it ceases to be an associate — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* Company has no identifiable promoter or promoter group; buyer Twelve Stone LLP's designated partners are Sudhakar Reddy Chirra, Freshbus Founder/MD, and Sasya Chirra
- *What it reveals:* Exit priced at ₹7,911/share versus ₹2,344 paid in October 2022, for ₹36.6 crore cash on an ₹18.87 crore carrying value (0.96% of net worth), removing an associate that cost ₹11.22 crore of FY26 losses
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — Cash sale to the founder's LLP; no new listed share issued; stake was 0.96% of net worth
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* FY27 interim consolidated results — gain on disposal and the removed 'share of loss of an associate' line
- *In their words:* “Upon completion of the transaction, the Company's shareholding in Freshbus Private Limited shall stand reduced from 25.66% to 8.27% of its paid up share capital, resulting in Freshbus Private Limited ceasing to be an associate company of Le Travenues Technology Limited.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

On the documents supplied, ixigo (Le Travenues Technology Ltd.) is not separating, demerging or spinning off any business of its own — there is no scheme of arrangement in the filings, and the one filing tagged 'Diversification/Disinvestment' (August 13, 2026) is expressly marked 'Not applicable' against the question of whether the disposal sits outside a Scheme of Arrangement or needs Regulation 37A compliance. The only actual separation disclosed is the unwinding of ixigo's minority holding in Freshbus Private Limited, the electric intercity bus operator it first backed under an Investment and Shareholders' Agreement dated October 28, 2022 (68,258 CCPS plus 1 equity share at ₹2,344 per share). Under a Share Purchase Agreement dated August 13, 2026 with Twelve Stone LLP and Freshbus, ixigo sells 46,264 CCPS at ₹7,911 per share for cash of ₹365,994,504 (~₹36.6 crore), being 17.39% of Freshbus' paid-up capital, cutting its stake from 25.66% to 8.27% and ending Freshbus' status as an associate company; completion is set for on or before August 30, 2026. The buyer is Twelve Stone LLP, whose designated partners are Sudhakar Reddy Chirra, Freshbus' Founder and Managing Director, and Sasya Chirra — i.e. a founder-side vehicle buying ixigo out — and the filing states it is not a related-party transaction and that ixigo has no identifiable promoter group with an interest in it. The economics ixigo discloses are the only 'problem' the documents attach to the holding: Freshbus was a persistent drag on consolidated profit, with share of associate losses of ₹11.22 crore in FY26, ₹9.1 crore in FY25 versus ₹5.9 crore in FY24, and quarterly call-outs of ₹2.0 crore (Q1 FY25), ₹1.93 crore (Q2 FY25), ₹1.9 crore (Q3 FY25), ₹3.29 crore (Q4 FY25), ₹2.34 crore (Q1 FY26), ₹1.47 crore (Q2 FY26), ₹2.9 crore (Q3 FY26) and ₹45.59 million (Q4 FY26), against a carrying value of just ₹18.87 crore, or 0.96% of consolidated net worth. The exit price of ₹7,911 versus a ₹2,344 entry is roughly 3.4x, so the disclosed facts support a profitable exit from a loss-making, immaterial, non-core associate rather than a structural separation. Management never discusses the sale on any call — the latest call (May 21, 2026) predates the SPA — and in the same period the group is moving the other way, consolidating rather than separating: a ₹1,296 crore Prosus preferential issue (46,270,092 shares at ₹280, allotted November 12, 2025), a new wholly owned Singapore subsidiary IXIGO PTE. LTD., and a 60% upfront acquisition of Spain's Online Travel Solutions S.L. ('Trenes') for €11.70 million through that subsidiary. The only 'separation' management itself describes is organisational, not legal: the 'NewCo inside the old co' AI team built inside ixigo, which has no separate entity, capital or shareholding attached to it.

**How it evolved:** Freshbus enters the story as a deconsolidation, not a separation: on the Aug 2024 call (Q1 FY25, August 1, 2024) management explains it was a subsidiary until September 13, 2023 and became an associate after a primary round diluted ixigo, so its losses moved below EBITDA. Through May 2025 (May 14, 2025), Jul 2025 (July 16, 2025), Nov 2025 (October 29, 2025), Jan 2026 (January 22, 2026) and May 2026 (May 21, 2026) it appears only as a recurring one-off call-out of rising associate losses, never as a candidate for exit, and no analyst asks about it. Separately, on Nov 2025 Rajnish Kumar introduces the 'new co inside the old co' idea for AI self-disruption, which by May 2026 has become 'NewCo inside ixigo' and ixigo NEXT — an internal team, explicitly not a carve-out. The actual disposal surfaces only in the August 13, 2026 filing, after the last transcript, with no management narrative attached.

**What management expects from it:** Nothing is stated. No call or filing sets out expected effects on margins, capital, valuation or focus from the Freshbus exit; the filing gives only cash of ₹365,994,504, cessation of associate accounting (removing ₹11.22 crore of FY26 share-of-loss), and a retained 8.27%. For ixigo overall, management frames Prosus capital, the Singapore vehicle and Trenes as TAM expansion, not separation.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The August 13, 2026 filing is a straight share sale of a minority stake, not a demerger: ixigo sells 46,264 CCPS of Freshbus to Twelve Stone LLP at ₹7,911 per share (17.39% of paid-up capital), and the filing marks the Scheme-of-Arrangement / Regulation 37A question 'Not applicable'. “Pursuant to the said agreement, the Company has agreed to sell 46,264 Compulsorily Convertible Preference Shares of Freshbus Private Limited to Twelve Stone LLP at a price of ₹7,911 per share, constituting 17.39% stake of the paid up share capital in Freshbus Private Limited.”
- *Scheme* — The consequence is loss of associate status: the holding drops from 25.66% to 8.27%, so Freshbus stops being equity-accounted, but ixigo keeps a residual 8.27% rather than exiting fully. “Upon completion of the transaction, the Company's shareholding in Freshbus Private Limited shall stand reduced from 25.66% to 8.27% of its paid up share capital, resulting in Freshbus Private Limited ceasing to be an associate company of Le Travenues Technology Limited.”
- *Scheme* — The only quantified case in the filing is that the holding was loss-making and immaterial: ₹11.22 crore of associate losses in FY26 against a ₹18.87 crore carrying value, under 1% of consolidated net worth. “Net worth: It contributes ₹18.87 crore as investment in associate accounted for in consolidated financial statements constituting 0.96% of the net worth as per the audited consolidated financial statements as on March 31, 2026 .”
- *Scheme* — The buyer is a founder-side vehicle — Twelve Stone LLP, whose designated partners are Freshbus' own Founder and Managing Director and Sasya Chirra — and the exit price of ₹7,911 compares with a ₹2,344 entry price under the October 28, 2022 Investment and Shareholders' Agreement, roughly 3.4x. “The Company had invested in Freshbus Private Limited pursuant to an Investment and Shareholders' Agreement dated October 28, 2022, under which it acquired 68,258 Compulsorily Convertible Preference Shares and 1 Equity Share at a price of ₹2,344 per share.”
- *[Aug 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=89316b41-46c0-4bf6-b6d9-82aaeff5895b.pdf)* — Freshbus had already been separated once — by dilution, not by design: it was consolidated as a subsidiary until September 13, 2023, after which a primary round reduced ixigo's ownership and pushed its losses below the EBITDA line. “Last year, our investment company FreshBus was a subsidiary until 13 September 2023, and therefore in Q1 FY'24 a loss of Rs.1.46 crores was incorporated in our EBITDA.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=a0464314-b6a2-4c2b-b3ca-3496bdae2e11.pdf)* — Full-year disclosure shows the drag widening — associate losses up over 50% year on year — while the earlier revaluation gains shrank from ₹29.7 crore to ₹5.8 crore. “Share of loss of Fresh Bus increased from INR 5.9 crores in FY '24 to INR 9.1 crores in FY '25.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=0d1926e6-c564-489e-bacb-fa72890f5c4f.pdf)* — In the last call before the SPA, Freshbus appears only as a quarterly one-off call-out of ₹45.59 million of associate losses, with no mention of a sale, review or strategic rethink of the stake. “The call-outs for Q4 FY '26 include share of loss from Fresh Bus and associate company of INR45.59 million, tax benefits amounting to INR82.5 million”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=84c79cf0-7cb9-4faa-ba6f-e184bce1a707.pdf)* — The only 'separation' management itself articulates is organisational self-disruption — a 'new co' inside the existing company that uses the parent's data and resources, with no separate entity, capital or shareholders. “We call this building a new co inside the old co.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=0d1926e6-c564-489e-bacb-fa72890f5c4f.pdf)* — By the latest call that NewCo has become ixigo NEXT, described as an internal AI-native rebuild of the organisation and product, reinforcing that it is a team and operating layer rather than a business being carved out. “So over the past year, we created what we internally called NewCo inside ixigo.”
- *[Jan 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=2f27fe6e-df33-4ab5-a4cc-bbf5c9efd8f8.pdf)* — Over the same period the group is consolidating, not separating: ₹1,296 crore raised from Prosus with 25% earmarked for inorganic growth, an investment committee constituted, and a Singapore subsidiary set up as the channel for overseas investment — later used to buy 60% of Spain's Trenes for €11.70 million. “On the AI investments Rajnish talked about, I want to reiterate that when we raised the preferential issue last quarter, we had earmarked 25% of the proceeds for inorganic growth opportunities and 25% for organic growth initiatives.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No stated reason for exiting Freshbus, no buyer-selection or valuation rationale, no mention on any call, no lender, partner or investor request, and no demerger of any ixigo business.

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The supplied record does not contain any statement of why JPPOWER is separating a business, because it contains no earnings call transcripts at all ("no transcripts on file") and no scheme of arrangement, demerger, slump sale or composite scheme document. The only two filings provided are distress/insolvency disclosures, neither of which mentions a separation, a resulting company, a share entitlement ratio, or any business being carved out. The 27th February 2026 filing discloses that National Asset Reconstruction Company Limited, as Trustee of NARCL Trust, acting through its power of attorney holder India Debt Resolution Company Limited, filed a Section 7 IBC application before the NCLT Allahabad Bench at Prayagraj against JPPOWER itself, alleging default of Rs. 511,72,82,207 plus interest and charges, arising from a corporate guarantee JPPOWER extended for Jaiprakash Associates Limited (under IBC); the same dispute was already before the Hon'ble DRT-III, Delhi (disclosed 27th October 2025). The 17th March 2026 filing discloses the NCLT Allahabad Bench's oral order under Section 31 IBC approving Adani Enterprises Limited's resolution plan dated 14th October 2025 (with email clarifications of 5th November 2025) for promoter Jaiprakash Associates Limited, under which JAL's securities will be delisted, shareholders receive NIL consideration because the liquidation value is insufficient to satisfy even secured creditors in full, and all pre-CIRP share capital, convertible instruments, warrants and rights will be entirely cancelled and extinguished for zero consideration on an Effective Date no later than 90 days from NCLT approval. These documents describe a change of control at the promoter level and a creditor-initiated insolvency threat at JPPOWER on a guarantee obligation — not a voluntary business separation. No management named any businesses to be separated (e.g. thermal power, hydro, cement grinding), cited no segment numbers, identified no investor, lender or partner who asked for it, and set out no problems a separation would solve. Any rationale would therefore have to be supplied from outside these texts, which the instructions forbid.

**How it evolved:** The idea does not surface anywhere in the provided record: there are zero earnings calls on file, so there is no call-by-call progression to trace. The only datable developments are the JAL insolvency track — resolution plan filed with NCLT per JAL's 27th November 2025 disclosure, NCLT approval of Adani Enterprises Limited's plan orally pronounced 17th March 2026 (JPPOWER's related disclosure chain beginning 3rd June 2024) — and the guarantee default track, moving from the DRT-III Delhi dispute disclosed 27th October 2025 to NARCL's Section 7 CIRP application against JPPOWER disclosed 27th February 2026. Neither track is presented as, or linked to, a separation of a business.

**What management expects from it:** Not stated. The record contains no management commentary on a separation and therefore no expectations for margins, capital structure, valuation re-rating, or business focus at any entity. The only forward-looking content is JAL's delisting, NIL exit price for its shareholders, and extinguishment of its pre-CIRP share capital within 90 days of NCLT approval.

*Not explained on the calls:* Everything: no transcripts supplied, no scheme document, no businesses named, no segment financials, no demerger rationale, ratio, timeline, or requesting stakeholder.

## JUBLFOOD — Jubilant Foodworks Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a scheme of arrangement whose nature the documents on file do not settle) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 2.5/10 · scheme (nature unclear) · 1 filing(s) from NSE · first 2025-12-29, latest 2025-12-29

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** The Company's entire 31.66% associate stake in Hashtag Loyalty Private Limited, whose business operations were discontinued — class `bad_business`.

- *Insiders:* Buyer is Mr. Karan Chechani, one of the founders of Hashtag, not part of Promoter, Promoter Group or Group Companies; not a related party transaction.
- *What it reveals:* Nothing of value: Hashtag contributed Nil to consolidated income and net worth (FY24-25 total income Rs. 27.47 million, net worth Rs. 1.22 million), already fully impaired, sold for Rs. 6,415.94 total.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — No new shares or listed entity created; a cash sale of an immaterial, fully impaired associate stake.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* FY26 annual report / results note confirming completion of the Hashtag stake sale and any exceptional item
- *In their words:* “Post completion of the transaction, Hashtag will cease to be an associate of the Company.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

On the evidence of these texts, Jubilant FoodWorks is not separating a business in any demerger, spin-off or scheme sense — none of the seven earnings calls contains a single word about separating, demerging, hiving off or listing any business, and no scheme of arrangement is filed. The only separation document present is the Regulation 30 intimation dated December 29, 2025, under which the Company executed a Share Purchase Agreement with Mr. Karan Chechani, one of the founders of Hashtag Loyalty Private Limited, to sell its entire 31.66% stake, after which Hashtag ceases to be an associate; the filing itself answers 'Not Applicable' to whether the disposal sits outside a Scheme of Arrangement. The stated reason is prior discontinuance of Hashtag's business operations, and the numbers management disclosed make the exit economically trivial: Hashtag's FY2024-25 total income was Rs. 27.47 million and its net worth as on March 31, 2025 was Rs. 1.22 million, each contributing 'Nil' to JFL's consolidated financials, the investment was already fully impaired during FY2024-25, and total consideration is Rs. 6,415.94 — a token sum returning the stake to a founder who is explicitly not part of the promoter or promoter group, in a transaction that is not a related-party transaction, with completion expected on or before February 12, 2026. The nearest thing to a portfolio-separation narrative on the calls is pruning, not separation: management repeatedly described curtailing or stopping expansion of Dunkin' and Hong's to concentrate on Domino's and Popeyes, quantifying the emerging-brands EBITDA drag at roughly 200 bps (FY24 base, Nov 2025) and 230-250 bps (Feb 2026), and targeting at least halving it within 12-18 months as part of the 200 bps margin-improvement commitment to FY28. Separately, the Turkey (DP Eurasia) acquisition debt of about EUR 110 million sitting in the Netherlands entity was de-linked from India cash flows — serviced entirely from Turkish internal cash flows and dividends for three quarters by Feb 2026 — but management framed this as refinancing and self-funding, never as a separation of the entity. No investor, lender, brand partner (Domino's International, RBI, Inspire Brands) or aggregator is recorded anywhere in these texts as asking for a business to be separated. The only shareholder-driven structural question was Vivek M.'s May 2025 query about the group's HCCB transaction, which Hari Bhartia answered by reaffirming that focus stays at Jubilant FoodWorks and that funding was already arranged.

**How it evolved:** The idea never surfaces as a separation on any call: Nov 2024 through May 2026 contain only portfolio pruning — Nov 13, 2024 (no expansion for Hong's and Dunkin' until store economics work), May 14, 2025 (expansion in both formally curtailed mid-year to focus on Popeyes; drag to halve), Aug 13, 2025 (expansion 'down to a trickle or stopped', drag halving in 12-18 months), Nov 13, 2025 and Feb 10, 2026 (drag quantified at ~200 bps on FY24 and 230-250 bps, to halve), and May 20, 2026 (drag reduction 'ahead of the plan'). Hashtag Loyalty is never mentioned on any of the seven calls; it appears only in the December 29, 2025 filing, which itself refers back to 'various disclosures made' earlier about discontinuance of Hashtag's operations — disclosures not included in this pack. The plan therefore did not visibly evolve in these texts; a dormant, fully impaired 31.66% associate stake was simply sold back to a founder for Rs. 6,415.94, with completion due on or before February 12, 2026.

**What management expects from it:** Nothing on separation economics is stated. For the retained portfolio they expect the Popeyes/Dunkin'/Hong's drag of roughly 230-250 bps to halve, EBITDA margin up at least 200 bps over FY24 by FY28, Domino's India about 15% revenue growth and about 15% pre-Ind AS margin, and Turkey to self-fund its EUR 110 million acquisition debt.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The only separation/disposal document in the pack: a Share Purchase Agreement dated December 29, 2025 selling JFL's entire 31.66% stake in Hashtag Loyalty Private Limited to founder Karan Chechani, who is not part of the promoter group. “it is hereby informed that the Company has executed a Share Purchase Agreement dated December 29, 2025 inter-alia with Mr. Karan Chechani, one of the founder of Hashtag for sale of its entire stake (31.66%) in Hashtag.”
- *Scheme* — The stated trigger is that Hashtag's business operations had already been discontinued and the investment was written off a year earlier, so the exit carries no P&L consequence; the filing also marks the Scheme of Arrangement question 'Not Applicable'. “During the previous financial year 2024-25, the Company had fully impaired its investment in Hashtag.”
- *Scheme* — Immateriality is the explicit justification: Hashtag's FY25 total income of Rs. 27.47 million and net worth of Rs. 1.22 million each contribute 'Nil' to JFL consolidated, and the entire stake fetches Rs. 6,415.94, with Hashtag ceasing to be an associate on completion by February 12, 2026. “Post completion of the transaction, Hashtag will cease to be an associate of the Company.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=2bf18a77-90a0-45b6-8df0-dfc618e6627f.pdf)* — The closest the calls come to separating businesses is pruning the emerging brands: Khetarpal said JFL had decided mid-year to stop expanding Dunkin' and Hong's and concentrate on Popeyes, expecting the drag between Domino's 14.5% margin and the 11.8% standalone quarterly margin to halve. “And as you would see, we have already taken the stance of curtailing any or not doing any expansion in Dunkin' and Hong's.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=bcbac4b0-896c-451a-9a5a-3fc30dedb9f1.pdf)* — Hegde confirmed expansion of Dunkin' and Hong's had effectively ceased and that the ~200 bps FY25 drag from emerging formats would be at least halved in 12 to 18 months by fixing unit economics rather than by any corporate separation. “Expansion, as you can well see in the numbers we have come out with, have almost come down to a trickle or stopped, right?”
- *Feb 2026* — Hegde quantified the emerging-brands drag at roughly 230-250 bps as disclosed, to be halved on the path to the 200 bps EBITDA improvement over FY24 by FY28 — framed as margin repair inside the listed entity, not as carving anything out. “And the reduction of the drag on the EBUs, at the point in time that we had disclosed our numbers, the drag was of Popeyes, Dunkin and Hong's was approximately about 230 bps, 250 bps.”
- *Feb 2026* — The only de-linking management described was financial, not structural: the roughly EUR 110 million Netherlands-held acquisition debt for DP Eurasia is now serviced wholly from Turkish cash flows and dividends, with no remittance from India for three quarters. “We are pleased to share that Turkey is now servicing its acquisition-related debt entirely through internal cash flows.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=4aedd4df-2e77-498d-bda4-fced35a2ae39.pdf)* — In the most recent call the emerging brands are still described as a drag being managed inside JFL and running ahead of plan — confirming no separation of Popeyes, Hong's or Dunkin' is contemplated in these texts. “Just to remind you, there is a drag of new businesses like Popeyes, Hong's and Dunkin.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=2bf18a77-90a0-45b6-8df0-dfc618e6627f.pdf)* — The one structural question from an investor concerned the promoter group's HCCB transaction and whether JFL resources would be used; Hari Bhartia said focus stays with JFL and funding was already arranged, and nobody asked for a business to be separated. “So about focus, yes, focus will remain at Jubilant FoodWorks.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No demerger, spin-off or scheme is mentioned anywhere; Hashtag's discontinuation, valuation and buyer rationale are never discussed on any call.

- *Insiders:* No new entity described; promoter Abhay Soi holds 23.7% of MHIL as on September 30, 2026; members approved PRSU Scheme 2026 of up to 73,50,000 units (~0.76% of paid-up equity).
- *What it reveals:* not stated
- *Selling pressure:* unclear — Documents describe no demerger, share entitlement ratio, record date or index change; only amalgamations, acquisitions and voluntary liquidations of subsidiaries.
- *Parent or spin:* unclear · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Postal ballot notice and explanatory statement dated August 13, 2026 (PRSU exercise price; altered Main Objects Clause).
- *In their words:* “Healthcare undertaking of Radiant Life Care Private Limited ("Radiant") and residual business of erstwhile Max India Limited merged into Max Healthcare Institute Limited ("MHIL" or "the Company") through an NCLT approved Composite Scheme of Amalgamation and Arrangement on June 1, 2020.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

These texts describe no spin-off, demerger or separation of a business by Max Healthcare Institute Ltd. (MAXHEALTH) — the direction of travel across all eleven disclosures is the opposite: consolidation of subsidiaries into fewer entities, acquisitions (Jaypee Healthcare/Max Noida, Kalinga Hospital Bhubaneswar at ~INR 298 crore for 58.28% rising to 66.34%, Yerawada Properties Pvt. Ltd.) and brownfield/greenfield bed addition (~20% brownfield capacity commissioned in FY26, 500-bed Gurgaon Sector-56, 700-712 beds at Shaheed Path Lucknow for ~INR 1,400 crore). The only business genuinely separated out is small: the Chitta and Anoopshahr hospitals, divested for INR 40 crore under a binding term sheet announced on the Aug 2025 (Q1 FY26) call and completed in September 2025. Management's stated reason was strategic fit and sub-scale economics, not value unlocking: the two came in as part of the Jaypee Healthcare acquisition and 'had limited strategic alignment' with a strategy 'to focus on super-specialty care in selected geographies'; only Chitta was operational, at ~INR 5 crore revenue and an INR 1 crore EBITDA loss in Q1 FY26, running 26% occupancy on 100 of 200 capacity beds, with no plan to spend on opening the balance 100 beds. On the Nov 2024 call Abhay Soi said of Anoopshahr/Bulandshahr that they were 'not meaningful enough', that no value had been attributed to them in the Jaypee price, and that the choice was between spending CSR time and money on them or wrapping them up. The second, larger strand is internal simplification rather than separation: merger of wholly-owned subsidiaries Alps Hospital Limited with Max Hospitals & Allied Services Limited, and of Crosslay Remedies Limited (CRL) with Jaypee Healthcare Limited (JHL), which management said would 'simplify the holding structure, improve governance and optimize cash flows' and 'reduce our outflow on the acquisition by INR 200-225 crore'; the CRL-JHL amalgamation (NCLT Chandigarh, appointed date October 5, 2024, effective December 15, 2025) produced a one-time tax gain of INR 149 crore in Q2 FY26 (~INR 142 crore net after a ~INR 7 crore Q4 FY26 reversal) against a INR 14 crore stamp-duty provision inside the INR 55 crore of Q3 FY26 exceptional items. Alongside this, step-down subsidiary ET Planners Private Limited was voluntarily liquidated with its entire undertaking transferred to Alps Hospital Limited on a going-concern basis (dissolved March 25, 2026), and MHC Global Healthcare (Nigeria) Ltd — nil revenue, negative net worth of INR 70.89 lakh, -0.0076% of consolidated net worth — was put into voluntary liquidation from January 29, 2026. No investor, lender or partner is recorded in these texts as asking for a separation; no scheme of arrangement for a demerger appears in the filings (the only MOA change put to shareholders, approved October 19, 2026, widens the objects clause to add medical colleges, pharmaceuticals/cyclotron radiopharmaceuticals and food & beverage services — an expansion of scope, not a carve-out). The one business repeatedly discussed as structurally separate — the Partner Healthcare Facility societies (Balaji, Devki Devi, GM Modi, Nirogi, Vikrant) — is being drawn closer, not separated: cash is moved between societies or upstreamed into MHIL via revised medical service fees (e.g. ~INR 25 crore a year at Balaji) because, as Yogesh Sareen explained, 'there is no dividend that can be declared for any society' and upstreaming costs ~25% tax.

**How it evolved:** The idea surfaced on the Nov 7, 2024 call, where Abhay Soi called the Bulandshahr/Anoopshahr units 'not meaningful enough', said no value was attributed to them in the INR 1,660 crore Jaypee enterprise value, and was weighing whether to keep them or 'wrap it up'; on the May 21, 2025 (Q4 FY25) call the same assets were disclosed as sub-scale (Chitta 26% occupancy, only 100 of 200 beds opened, no plan to open the rest) while a parallel 'simplify the holding structure' programme was announced — Alps/MHASL merger concluded and a CRL-JHL merger filed with NCLT to cut acquisition outflow by INR 200-225 crore. It hardened into a transaction on the Aug 14, 2025 (Q1 FY26) call with a binding term sheet to divest Chitta and Anoopshahr for INR 40 crore, and was reported complete on the Nov 17, 2025 (Q2 FY26) call under the heading of streamlining the corporate structure, together with NCLT approval of the subsidiary merger and its INR 149 crore one-time benefit. Thereafter the thread is only tidying-up — stamp duty inside Q3 FY26's INR 55 crore exceptional items (Feb 6, 2026 call), liquidation of MHC Nigeria (Jan 29, 2026) and ET Planners (dissolved March 25, 2026) — and by the May 22, 2026 and later disclosures the narrative is entirely acquisition and capacity addition (Kalinga/Bhubaneswar, Pune, Lucknow Shaheed Path), with no separation plan of any kind.

**What management expects from it:** No separation economics were given, because no separation was announced. For the divested Chitta/Anoopshahr units: INR 40 crore proceeds and exit of a strategically misaligned, loss-making asset (INR 1 crore EBITDA loss). For MHIL: a simpler holding structure, better governance, optimized cash flows, INR 200-225 crore lower Jaypee outflow and a ~INR 142 crore net one-time tax gain, against INR 14 crore stamp duty.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *CALL Nov 2024* — First signal: asked whether the Bulandshahr/Anoopshahr units attached to the Jaypee deal mattered, Soi said no value had been ascribed to them and the company was deciding between supporting them or exiting. “No, they're not meaningful enough. And we did not even attribute any value to it. We are trying to determine whether we should focus and spend CSR time and money on this or just wrap it up.”
- *CALL May 2025* — Simplification of the group structure — not separation — is framed as the corporate-action agenda, tied to governance (IiAS 'Next Leaders' recognition) and cash flows; Alps/MHASL merger done, CRL-JHL merger filed with NCLT. “On that note, we would like to highlight that we continue to undertake corporate actions to simplify the holding structure, improve governance and optimize cash flows.”
- *CALL May 2025* — The cash rationale for the CRL-JHL merger is quantified: it reduces the cash outflow on the Jaypee acquisition by INR 200-225 crore. “We have also filed an application with the NCLT for merger of Crosslay Remedies Limited and Jaypee Healthcare Limited, which will, in effect, reduce our outflow on the acquisition by INR 200-225 crore.”
- *CALL May 2025* — Chitta is shown as sub-scale and capital-starved — 100 of 200 beds opened, 26% occupancy on those, and no intention to spend on the rest — the operating backdrop to the divestment decision. “Similarly, Chitta Hospital is a 200-bed hospital, but only 100 beds have been opened. And on those 100 beds, we have only 26% occupancy. So, there is no plan to open the balance 100 beds because that will also require some spend.”
- *CALL Aug 2025* — The only actual business separation: a binding term sheet to divest Chitta and Anoopshahr for INR 40 crore, justified by strategic focus on super-specialty care in selected geographies, with only Chitta operational at ~INR 5 crore revenue and INR 1 crore EBITDA loss in Q1 FY26. “As part of our strategy to focus on super-specialty care in selected geographies, we have executed a binding term sheet to divest Chitta and Anoopshahr hospitals for Rs. 40 crores, with completion expected by September '25.”
- *CALL Aug 2025* — The problem the divestment solves is stated as fit, not funding or valuation: the assets arrived with the Jaypee Healthcare acquisition and did not fit the network strategy. “These assets were part of the overall Jaypee Healthcare acquisition and had limited strategic alignment.”
- *CALL Nov 2025* — Completion is reported under the banner of corporate streamlining, together with NCLT Chandigarh approval of the two-subsidiary merger (appointed date October 5, 2024) and its INR 149 crore one-time benefit. “Alongside our expansion efforts, we also streamlined our corporate structure. Divestment of hospitals in Chitta and Anoopshahr was completed in September 2025.”
- *CALL Feb 2026* — The cost side of the restructuring: Q3 FY26 carried INR 55 crore of exceptional items, part of it stamp duty on the subsidiary merger (INR 14 crore per the FY26 earnings update, with INR 41 crore for the Code on Wages). “During the quarter, there were exceptional items aggregating to INR 55 crore relating to impact of the Code on Wages, 2019 and provision for stamp duty on the merger of two of our subsidiaries.”
- *CALL Feb 2025* — The structurally separate Partner Healthcare Facility societies are explicitly being kept inside the network and their cash upstreamed or moved between societies rather than separated, because societies cannot pay dividends and upstreaming costs ~25% tax; Balaji's fee revision alone adds ~INR 25 crore a year to MHIL. “No, there is no dividend that can be declared for any society.”
- *Scheme* — Filing of May 21, 2026 (FY26 earnings update): the subsidiary amalgamation was completed, with the merged entity retaining the Crosslay Remedies name — a consolidation of two legal entities into one, the opposite of a carve-out. “Post approval of Scheme of Amalgamation, two WoS i.e., CRL and JHL, have amalgamated effective December 15, 2025 and the name of amalgamated entity has been changed to Crosslay Remedies Limited”
- *Scheme* — NCLT order of March 25, 2026 dissolving step-down wholly-owned subsidiary ET Planners Private Limited: its whole undertaking was moved up to parent Alps Hospital Limited on a going-concern basis, removing a legal entity rather than separating a business. “The entire business undertaking of the company which comprises of all assets, all liabilities, customers and suppliers contracts, service agreements, lease and licenses, employees etc. on a going concern basis will be distributed to its shareholder i.e. Alps Hospital Limited.”
- *Scheme* — Filing of January 29, 2026: voluntary liquidation of MHC Global Healthcare (Nigeria) Ltd, a non-material subsidiary with nil revenue and negative net worth of INR 70.89 lakh (-0.0076% of consolidated net worth), explicitly with no business or financial consequence. “The voluntary liquidation of MHC Nigeria will neither affect any business nor impact materially the consolidated financials of the Company.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No demerger, spin-off, listed-entity separation, buyer identity, Anoopshahr financials, or any investor, lender or partner request for a separation is explained anywhere in these texts.
