## MINDACORP — Minda Corporation Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a scheme of arrangement whose nature the documents on file do not settle) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 2.5/10 · scheme (nature unclear) · 4 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-09-24, latest 2026-09-24

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** A 29.5% associate stake in EVQ Point Solutions Private Limited, an EV charging-related step-down associate; no demerger scheme is on file — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* not stated; buyer identity and whether buyers belong to promoter/promoter group "Will be intimated once finalised". Promoters named elsewhere: Ashok Minda, Sarika Minda, Akash Minda, Minda Capital, Whiteline Barter.
- *What it reveals:* Reveals almost nothing: the stake contributed only Rs 3,95,197 of share of profit in FY2025-26 consolidated accounts, and the Feb 2026 call said "EVQ did not contribute". Parent grew revenue 22.3% to Rs 6,185 crores.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — No new listed entity or share distribution; it is a cash sale of a minority associate stake, consideration not yet disclosed.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* The execution intimation: sale agreement date, consideration, and buyer identity, all "to be intimated at the time of execution".
- *In their words:* “The Board has approved the sale of investment held in EVQ Point Solutions Private Limited through Spark Minda Green Mobility Systems Private Limited (Wholly Owned Subsidiary of the Company).”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

These texts do not contain a business separation by Minda Corporation — no demerger, no spin-off, no slump sale of a division, and no Scheme of Arrangement document is present. Across the eight calls (Aug 2024 to May 2026) management describes the opposite direction: buying 49% of Flash Electronics for INR 1,372 crore cash on a INR 3,100 crore valuation (completed Jan 2025), a 60:40 switches JV with Toyodenso of Japan (~INR 150 crore, SOP Q4 FY27), a 50:50 sunroof/power-tailgate JV with HCMF of Taiwan (~INR 80-100 crore, INR 350 crore lifetime order), a TLA with Sanco of China for high-voltage connectors, a Turntide (UK) EV-powertrain JV formed in March 2026, and — announced on the May 22, 2026 call — consolidating associate Minda VAST (~INR 500 crore revenue, ~7% EBITDA margin, >90% passenger vehicle) into Minda Corporation from FY27 to lift PV mix from 14% toward the 25% Vision-2030 target. The single separation event anywhere in the record is a one-line board approval of September 24, 2026 to sell the investment in EVQ Point Solutions Private Limited, a step-down associate in which wholly-owned subsidiary Spark Minda Green Mobility Systems Private Limited holds a 29.5% equity stake. The filing gives no reason at all: buyer 'Will be intimated once finalised', consideration 'shall be intimated at the time of execution', completion date 'Will be intimated in due course of time', not a related-party transaction, and the Regulation 37A / Scheme of Arrangement row is marked 'Not Applicable'. The only quantification attached to it is the FY2025-26 consolidated share of profit of Rs. 3,95,197 — and on the May 2026 call the CFO's associate-profit breakdown (Flash ~INR 70 crore, Furukawa ~INR 8 crore, Minda VAST ~INR 5 crore) records that 'EVQ did not contribute', i.e. an immaterial, non-earning minority stake rather than a business being carved out. No investor, lender, OEM or JV partner is recorded in any call or filing as having asked for a separation; the only balance-sheet asks management responds to are deleveraging (gross debt ~INR 1,100 crore, INR 70 crore repaid in 9M FY26, INR 104-105 crore of promoter warrant money applied to debt repayment, stated intent to move 0.5x debt/equity to 0.2x) and ROCE discipline (22% to 25% by 2030) — funded by promoter warrants and a same-day board approval for up to INR 500 crore of NCDs, not by divesting an operating business.

**How it evolved:** EVQ is never named as a separation candidate in any of the eight calls; it surfaces only once, in Ajay Agarwal's associate-profit breakdown on the May 22, 2026 Q4 FY26 call, where he notes it contributed nothing to PAT. The decision then appears without warning as item 3 of the Board Meeting outcome filed September 24, 2026, alongside unrelated items (INR 500 crore NCD enabling approval, a new wholly-owned subsidiary in China, two senior appointments). Nothing between those two dates — including the Feb 5, 2026 and May 22, 2026 calls, which both discuss capital allocation, debt and Vision 2030 at length — flags it, and the plan has not changed since because no terms have yet been disclosed. Over the same 36 months the only structural change management actually explained was in the other direction: bringing Minda VAST on-balance-sheet from FY27 after a shareholder-agreement change with the JV partner.

**What management expects from it:** Nothing is stated. The filing attaches no expected benefit to the EVQ exit — no margin, capital-release, valuation or focus argument, and no indication of what either Minda Corporation or EVQ Point Solutions gains. The only entity-level expectations management gives anywhere concern additions: Minda VAST lifting PV mix from 14% to 25%, Flash sustaining 16-17% EBITDA, group revenue INR 17,500 crore at 12.5% margin by FY30.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The only separation approved in the record: the Sept 24, 2026 board approved selling the 29.5% stake in EVQ Point Solutions, held via wholly-owned subsidiary Spark Minda Green Mobility Systems, with no rationale stated. “The Board has approved the sale of investment held in EVQ Point Solutions Private Limited  through Spark Minda Green Mobility Systems Private Limited (Wholly Owned Subsidiary of the Company).”
- *Scheme* — The filing explicitly confirms this is not a Scheme of Arrangement or Regulation 37A undertaking disposal — i.e. not a demerger or spin-off. “Whether the sale, lease or disposal of the undertaking is outside Scheme of Arrangement? If yes, details of the same including compliance with regulation 37A of LODR Regulations.  Not Applicable”
- *Scheme* — No buyer, price or timetable was disclosed; the only financial fact given is the FY26 share of profit of Rs. 3,95,197 from the entity. “Consideration for the proposed sale of investment shall be intimated at the time of execution .”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=7488c2e7-7497-4931-b75d-bb7e573d6a8f.pdf)* — Management's own associate breakdown shows EVQ earned nothing for Minda Corporation in FY26, against Flash ~INR 70 crore, Furukawa ~INR 8 crore and Minda VAST ~INR 5 crore. “EVQ did not contribute and Minda VAST contributed about INR 5 crores.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=7488c2e7-7497-4931-b75d-bb7e573d6a8f.pdf)* — The structural move management did explain is the opposite of a separation: pulling associate Minda VAST into the listed entity from FY27 after renegotiating the JV shareholder agreement. “Building on our strategic growth initiatives, Minda Corporation will now consolidate our associate company, Minda VAST, into the Minda Corporation from this fiscal year after the change in our shareholder agreement with our joint venture partner.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=7488c2e7-7497-4931-b75d-bb7e573d6a8f.pdf)* — Minda VAST is being consolidated specifically to raise passenger-vehicle mix from 14% toward the 25% Vision 2030 goal — growth by addition, not by separation. “With the consolidation of Minda VAST business with Minda Corporation from FY 27 onwards, it will certainly accelerate our vision to achieve 25% revenue from Passenger Vehicle segment, which currently stands at about 14%.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=b0c43573-e6d2-43a2-8e12-ecf8d3420967.pdf)* — The capital-structure problem management actually addresses is leverage, solved with promoter warrant money and repayment — not by separating a business. “So our gross debt is about INR 1,100 -odd crores and we have paid abou t INR 70- odd crores debt during the first nine-month period.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=b0c43573-e6d2-43a2-8e12-ecf8d3420967.pdf)* — Capital-allocation discipline is framed as lifting ROCE from 22% to 25% by 2030 through investment in high-margin connected businesses, with no mention of exiting or hiving off anything. “And I think what we have promised the market to deliver by 2030 is improvement from 22% to 25%.”
- *[Nov 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=4703c56f-4910-4b9e-a10e-135636dec066.pdf)* — The only 'what we will not do' discipline management articulates is an M&A screen (no large overseas operations, engine-agnostic products only, ROCE above 20%), i.e. acquisition criteria rather than divestment criteria. “Absolutely. Parag ji, we have very strong financial footings metrics internally approved by Board of Directors on capital allocation, and any kind of inorganic or capital allocation cannot dilute our ROCE.”

*Not explained on the calls:* Everything: why EVQ is being sold, buyer, price, timing, use of proceeds, strategic fit, and why it was never mentioned on any earnings call.

## NSLNISP — NMDC Steel Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a filing's text names a demerger; no scheme filing names it yet) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 2.5/10 · spin-off · 3 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-02-03, latest 2026-08-15

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** NISP — NMDC Ltd's Nagarnar iron and steel plant unit, demerged into a separate listed steel company — class `regulatory_strategic`.

- *Insiders:* GoI to divest its 50.79% shareholding in NSL with management control to a strategic buyer; GoI shall offer 10% of NSL to NMDC Limited after the buyer is identified. Management incentives not stated.
- *What it reveals:* A standalone, leveraged single-plant steel business: borrowings Rs 5,056.15 Cr, net worth Rs 13,228.35 Cr, rating cut AAA to BBB+/A- post-demerger, FY25 loss Rs 2,373.78 Cr turning to Rs 50.51 Cr profit in Q1 FY27 as interest resets 12.45% to 8.40%.
- *Selling pressure:* unclear — Documents state only that GoI will divest 50.79% to a strategic buyer; no index, distribution or float detail given.
- *Parent or spin:* spin · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* The Preliminary Information Memorandum / Request for Expression of Interest for GoI's 50.79% strategic sale.
- *In their words:* “As per the Preliminary Information Memorandum and Request for Expression of Interest invited, GOI had decided to divest its 50.79% shareholding in Resulting Company ("NMDC Steel Limited" or "NSL") along with management control to strategic buyer.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

On the record supplied, the "separation" is not a new divestiture announced by NMDC Steel Limited (NSL, scrip NSLNISP / BSE 543768 / CSE 74920) — it is the already-completed demerger of the NISP business (NMDC Iron & Steel Plant, Nagarnar, Dist. Bastar, Chhattisgarh, a 3 MTPA-class greenfield integrated plant) out of NMDC Ltd., the iron-ore mining parent, into NSL as the "Resulting Company" (CIN L27310CT2015GOI001618). The stated reason is entirely a Government of India privatisation mechanic, not an operating or synergy argument: the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs gave in-principle approval on 27 October 2016 for strategic disinvestment of several CPSEs including the NISP unit of NMDC Ltd., and then on 14 October 2020 approved the demerger of NISP from NMDC together with strategic disinvestment of the resulting entity by selling the entire GoI stake. In other words, the carve-out exists so that the steel plant could be made a separately listed, separately saleable entity, leaving NMDC Ltd. as a pure mining company; the asker is the sovereign owner through CCEA, not investors, lenders or a JV partner. The transaction terms set out in the Preliminary Information Memorandum and the Request for Expression of Interest are that GoI divests 50.79% of NSL along with management control to a strategic buyer, and will additionally offer 10% of NSL to NMDC Ltd. once the strategic buyer has been identified through the bidding process. The scheme also allocated legacy exposure to the parent: the Rs 111.19 Cr GST input-credit dispute for July 2017–March 2021 (Rs 8.45 Cr paid, Rs 45.90 Cr dropped, Rs 56.40 Cr in abeyance before the Bilaspur High Court, Rs 0.35 Cr under appeal) is pre-demerger, so NMDC Ltd. files the appeals "as per the demerger scheme." Nothing in the filings claims the separation improves margins, capital allocation or valuation; the only measurable consequence disclosed is that standing alone cost NSL its parent's credit umbrella — rating fell from AAA to A- on demerger (NCD coupon 7.30% to 8.80% from 16.02.2023), then to BBB+ (9.05% from 5 June 2024), with the Rs 523.80 Cr NCDs rated "ICRA BBB+ Rating Watch with Developing Implications" and Ind A-/Negative until redemption on 28.08.2025, and the SBI rupee term loan of Rs 4,476.20 Cr (drawn Rs 4,475.81 Cr) repricing off external rating from 7.1% to 12.45% w.e.f. 01.03.2025 before being repositioned at NSL's request to 8.70% (12.04.2025), 8.45% (12.10.2025) and 8.40% (12.01.2026). Financially the standalone entity moved from a FY25 loss before tax of Rs 3,321.72 Cr on revenue of Rs 8,503.05 Cr (PAT Rs -2,373.78 Cr, EPS -8.10) to FY26 revenue of Rs 13,641.81 Cr with PBT Rs 75.78 Cr and PAT Rs 58.72 Cr, and Q1 FY27 (quarter ended 30.06.2026) revenue Rs 3,661.84 Cr with PBT Rs 73.95 Cr, PAT Rs 50.51 Cr, borrowings Rs 5,056.15 Cr and net worth Rs 13,228.35 Cr — i.e. the asset was handed to the market loss-making and has only just crossed into profit as the sale process remains open.

**How it evolved:** There are no earnings-call transcripts on file, so the only visible evolution is the repetition of the same two-step CCEA history — 27 October 2016 (in-principle strategic disinvestment of the NISP unit) and 14 October 2020 (demerger of NISP from NMDC plus sale of the entire GoI stake in the resulting entity) — carried verbatim as a note in each of the three filings dated 3 February 2026, 29 May 2026 and 14/15 August 2026, with the PIM/EoI terms (50.79% plus control to a strategic buyer, 10% offered to NMDC Ltd. afterwards) unchanged throughout. What changes across the three is the aftermath rather than the plan: by the 3 February 2026 filing the Rs 523.80 Cr NCDs had been redeemed on 28.08.2025 (principal plus Rs 42.98 Cr interest, net of Rs 4.42 Cr TDS), ending the "Rating Watch with Developing Implications" overhang, and the SBI term loan had been stepped down from the 12.45% post-DCCO reset to 8.45%. By the 14 August 2026 filing the rate is 8.40% (from 12.01.2026), term-loan outstanding is Rs 3,177.27 Cr after Rs 1,298.54 Cr repaid, and the entity is profitable (Q1 FY27 PAT Rs 50.51 Cr) — but no filing records any new stage of the sale, bidder shortlist or revised structure. No fresh separation is announced by NSL in this window; the company reports a single segment and no subsidiaries, JVs or associates.

**What management expects from it:** The filings state no expected benefit — no margin, capital, valuation or focus claim. Stated outcomes are only structural: GoI exits 50.79% of NSL with management control to a strategic buyer; NMDC Ltd. may take 10% post-bidding; NMDC retains pre-demerger tax appeals. The measured effect was dilutive to credit: AAA to A- to BBB+, and costlier debt.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — Filings of 03.02.2026, 29.05.2026 and 14.08.2026 all trace the separation to CCEA's 27 October 2016 in-principle approval for strategic disinvestment of CPSEs including the NISP unit of NMDC Ltd. — i.e. the sale decision predates the carve-out. “Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs ("CCEA"), in its meeting dated October 27, 2016, gave in-principle approval for strategic disinvestment ("Strategic Disinvestment") of several CPSEs including the NISP unit of NMDC Ltd.”
- *Scheme* — The demerger itself was approved on 14 October 2020 expressly as the vehicle for selling the Government's entire holding in the resulting entity — separation as a privatisation enabler, not an operating restructuring. “Subsequently, on October 14, 2020, CCEA gave its 'in­principle' approval to the demerger of NISP from NMDC and strategic disinvestment of the resulting entity by selling entire stake of Government of India ("Gol").”
- *Scheme* — The disclosed transaction is a 50.79% block in NSL sold together with management control to a strategic buyer, per the Preliminary Information Memorandum and Request for Expression of Interest. “As per the Preliminary Information Memorandum and Request for Expression of Interest invited, GOI had decided to divest its 50.79% shareholding in Resulting Company ("NMDC Steel Limited" or "NSL") along with management control to strategic buyer.”
- *Scheme* — A 10% residual stake is reserved for the former parent NMDC Ltd., but only after the bidding process identifies the strategic buyer — the parent keeps an option on the demerged steel business rather than a clean exit. “Additionally, Gol shall offer 10% stake in Resulting Company to NMDC Limited after the strategic buyer has been identified through the bidding process.”
- *Scheme* — The demerger scheme allocates legacy liabilities: the Rs 111.19 Cr GST input-credit dispute for July 2017–March 2021 is pre-demerger, so NMDC Ltd. and not NSL litigates it (Rs 56.40 Cr in abeyance before the Bilaspur High Court). “As the matter pertains to the pre-demerger period, NMDC Ltd, is filing the appeals as per the demerger scheme.”
- *Scheme* — Cost of separation disclosed: losing NMDC's balance sheet cut NSL's rating from AAA to A- and repriced the Rs 523.80 Cr NCDs upward, with a further cut to BBB+ in June 2024. “Subsequent to demerger and revision in the Rating from 'AAA' to 'A-', the coupon rate was revised to 8.80% w.e.f. 16.02.2023.”
- *Scheme* — The pending sale kept the credit on watch until the NCDs were redeemed on 28.08.2025 (Rs 523.80 Cr principal plus Rs 42.98 Cr accrued interest, net of Rs 4.42 Cr TDS). “The ratings till redemption i.e. 28.08.2025 were "ICRA BBB+ Rating Watch with Developing Implications" and Ind A-/Negative by Credit Rating Agencies, ICRA and India Ratings & Research respectively.”
- *Scheme* — Rating-linked grid pricing on the Rs 4,476.20 Cr SBI term loan spiked the standalone entity's cost of debt to 12.45% from 01.03.2025 before NSL negotiated it back down (8.70%, then 8.45%, then 8.40% from 12.01.2026; outstanding Rs 3,177.27 Cr at 30.06.2026). “Accordingly, the interest rate was reset to 12.45% p.a. w.e.f. 01.03.2025. Based on the request of NSL towards repositioning of the interest rate, SBI has revised the interest rate to 8.70% p.a. linked to 3 months MCLR from 12.04.2025.”
- *Scheme* — Post-separation NSL is a single-business, single-plant entity with nothing further to split — one reportable segment and no subsidiaries, JVs or associates as at 30.06.2026. “The Company is engaged in the manufacturing of Iron and Steel Products and generates revenue primarily from Iron and Steel Products which is the only reportable segment of the Company.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No calls or scheme document on file: no management rationale, synergies, margin/valuation case, bidder identity, timeline, or lender/investor demands. May-2026 filing attaches Dec-2025 review report.

## PAYTM — One 97 Communications Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a scheme of arrangement whose nature the documents on file do not settle) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 2.5/10 · scheme (nature unclear) · 1 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-04-25, latest 2026-04-25

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Paytm Payments Bank Limited, an associate company, separating from the Company via voluntary winding up — class `regulatory_strategic`.

- *Insiders:* Not stated for any new entity; filings state One 97 Communications Limited 'is a professionally managed company and does not have any identified promoter.'
- *What it reveals:* PPBL contributed Nil turnover, revenue, income and net worth last financial year, and the Company has no exposure or material business arrangements with it — so the separation removes a regulatory overhang without giving up earnings; all Paytm services continue uninterrupted.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — No shares distributed or listed — PPBL is being wound up and contributed nil revenue and net worth; no index exclusion arises.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* The winding-up order of the appropriate court or authority, which determines any consideration receivable by the Company.
- *In their words:* “The Company wishes to assure its shareholders and investors that the winding-up of PPBL and the consequential cessation of the associate relationship are not expected to have any material impact on the business, operations, or financial condition of the Company.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The business being separated is One 97 Communications' (OCL) Offline Merchant Payments business — the device-led acquiring franchise (soundbox, card soundbox/EDC card machines, QR) — which has been carved out of the listed parent and transferred as a going concern, on a slump-sale basis, to Paytm Payments Services Limited (PPSL), OCL's wholly owned subsidiary that holds the online payment-aggregator licence. The stated reason in the Business Transfer Agreement filing is regulatory: "The transfer is being undertaken to take steps to comply with the Reserve Bank of India's Master Directions on Regulation of Payment Aggregators dated September 15, 2025"; the filing additionally characterises it as "an internal restructuring intended to consolidate the related business within a dedicated wholly owned subsidiary, in alignment with applicable regulatory requirements and to achieve operational efficiency." Mechanics and numbers: shareholder approval on November 23, 2025, BTA executed November 28, 2025, effective from midnight of November 30, 2025, for a lump-sum cash consideration equal to the book value of the transferred undertaking at the effective date, with approximately INR 960 crore cited as the March 31, 2025 reference book value; Mr. Ripunjai Gaur (COO – Offline Payments) and Mr. Deependra Singh Rathore (CTO – Payments) transferred to PPSL and ceased as OCL Senior Management Personnel. Because it is a parent-to-wholly-owned-subsidiary transfer at book value, the filing stresses "there is no change in the ultimate beneficial ownership or control, and the entire economic interest in the Transferred Undertaking will continue to vest with the holding company." On the calls, the problem management says this solves is legal-entity fragmentation: online and offline acquiring sat in separate legal entities, so omnichannel merchants "could have not onboarded" — and online merchant onboarding had been paused/under embargo since 2021-22. With licences and entities combined, Vijay Shekhar Sharma says Paytm can "formally" do omni-channel, give a merchant a single dashboard, and layer value-added services — spend analytics, settlement, payout — so "per payment, we make more bps"; he also took over as CEO of PPSL (disclosed on the Jan 30, 2026 call) and called online "literally a new line of business" that will be "materially sizable," carrying platform fees plus EMI and card initiatives and feeding payment processing margin (guided above 4 bps, with net payment margin ~9 bps in Q4 FY26). Who asked for it: the RBI, via the September 15, 2025 Payment Aggregator Master Directions, with OCL shareholders approving the slump sale on November 23, 2025 — no investor, lender or commercial partner demand is cited anywhere in these texts. Critically for a special-situation investor, this is not a demerger to shareholders: there is no scheme of arrangement (the filing marks the Regulation 37A/scheme questions "Not Applicable"), no separate listing and no value-unlock event — the separation is purely intra-group consolidation into the licensed entity.

**How it evolved:** On the July 22, 2025 call there is no mention of any carve-out at all — payments is discussed as one full-stack business ("We own the machine, we own the customer") operating at breakeven. The plan surfaces in the Oct 15 and Nov 24, 2025 disclosures referenced by the BTA filing, and on the November 5, 2025 call Vijay Shekhar Sharma confirms the rationale for the first time — the regulator "made both licenses and one license together," so "now formally, we can do omni-channel," plus new VAS revenue per payment; the BTA is then executed November 28, 2025, effective November 30, 2025. By the January 30, 2026 call the framing has shifted from compliance to offence: VSS discloses he has become CEO of PPSL, says "now we can acquire both in the same entity," and calls online a new, materially sizable line of business paused since 2021. On May 7, 2026 Madhur Deora describes online as a tailwind that "obviously has a full license now" and "a very meaningful double digits" of GMV, and by July 21, 2026 the subject disappears into broad-based growth commentary (GMV +31%, embargo described as past).

**What management expects from it:** One licensed entity for all merchant acquiring: formal omnichannel, a single merchant dashboard, VAS (spend analytics, settlement, payout) and more bps per payment; online — higher-MDR, platform-fee, EMI/card-led — becomes a materially sizable new revenue line lifting payment processing margin past 4 bps. OCL receives book-value cash; no change in beneficial ownership or economic interest.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The BTA filing of November 28, 2025 states the sole purpose of transferring the Offline Merchant Payments business to wholly owned subsidiary PPSL is compliance with the RBI's September 15, 2025 Payment Aggregator Master Directions. “The transfer is being undertaken to take steps to comply with the Reserve Bank of India's Master Directions on Regulation of Payment Aggregators dated September 15, 2025.”
- *Scheme* — The company frames it as intra-group consolidation at book value — not a value-unlock demerger — with the related-party/arm's-length answer spelling out the consolidation and efficiency logic. “Yes, the transfer is proposed to be carried out at book value, given that it forms part of an internal restructuring intended to consolidate the related business within a dedicated wholly owned subsidiary, in alignment with applicable regulatory requirements and to achieve operational efficiency.”
- *Scheme* — Consideration is lump-sum cash based on book value at the November 30, 2025 effective date; the only number given is the prior-year reference book value of the transferred undertaking. “For reference, the book value of the Transferred Undertaking as on March 31, 2025 is approximately INR 960 Crores (Indian Rupees Nine Hundred Sixty Crores).”
- *Scheme* — Because it is a parent-to-WOS slump sale, OCL argues there is no economic change for shareholders — no scheme of arrangement, no listing, no dilution. “As the transaction is between the holding company and its wholly owned subsidiary, there is no change in the ultimate beneficial ownership or control, and the entire economic interest in the Transferred Undertaking will continue to vest with the holding company.”
- *Scheme* — Two Senior Management Personnel — Ripunjai Gaur, COO Offline Payments, and Deependra Singh Rathore, CTO Payments — moved with the undertaking and ceased to be OCL SMPs from midnight of November 30, 2025, after shareholder approval on November 23, 2025. “Further Mr. Ripunjai Gaur, COO - Offline Payments and Mr. Deependra Singh Rathore, CTO - Payments, both designated as Senior Management Personnel (SMPs) of the Company, will also be transferred to PPSL w.e.f. midnight of November 30, 2025 and upon such transfer they will cease as SMPs of the Company.”
- *[Jul 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=0380fc7f-f4b4-4828-a3fe-9c5d05201db9.pdf)* — Baseline before the carve-out: payments is presented as a single full-stack, breakeven business with no mention of any entity transfer, and VSS insists Paytm owns both the device and the merchant relationship (the assets that later move to PPSL). “We own the machine, we own the customer. We are in that business.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=86dfa175-b19a-424b-a170-5341345487b7.pdf)* — First call-level rationale, three weeks before the BTA: VSS says the regulator collapsed the two licences into one, which finally lets Paytm serve a merchant omnichannel from one entity with a single dashboard. “And now formally, we can do omni-channel. I mean, you can imagine that a single company will be able to see their single dashboard, et cetera, et cetera. So we are very happy about it. The regulator has also made both licenses and one license together.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=86dfa175-b19a-424b-a170-5341345487b7.pdf)* — Asked directly by Vijit Jain (Citi) whether combining online and offline payment aggregation is what enables omnichannel, VSS names the constraint explicitly — the offline business sitting in a different legal entity blocked onboarding of omnichannel merchants. “So all these businesses, we couldn't have onboarded and just because there's an offline entity was a different company, a legal entity could have not onboarded.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=86dfa175-b19a-424b-a170-5341345487b7.pdf)* — The commercial payoff claimed is incremental bps per payment from value-added services that only a combined entity can sell. “Yes, not just this element, but there are other VAS elements like spend analytics, like settlement, like payout. All those things start to show up as new value-add items. So per payment, we make more bps or more money than we will make standalone and offline or standalone and online.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=86dfa175-b19a-424b-a170-5341345487b7.pdf)* — Management links the restructuring to margin mix: newly onboardable online merchants carry higher MDR and net margin, supporting the payment processing margin improvement reported that quarter. “Sachin, another thing that we now have is the privilege of onboarding online merchants. Online merchants eventually are high MDR plus high net margin.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=4720712e-95e6-432a-ae09-64d5fb6ff426.pdf)* — Post-transfer, VSS discloses he has personally taken over as CEO of PPSL, the entity now holding both online and offline merchant payments. “You may have noticed that I've become the CEO of the PPSL company. So online business will start generating more upside in payments and financial services.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=4720712e-95e6-432a-ae09-64d5fb6ff426.pdf)* — He reframes the carve-out as creating a new revenue line — online acquiring, effectively paused since 2021 — boosted by both the licence permission and the new entity structure, with enterprise sales hiring behind it. “I mean, it's an important thing to note that the payment business will get boosted because of permission and the structure that we are doing.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No final consideration, no PPSL standalone financials or online/offline revenue split, no tax, capex or capital-structure impact, no reason for slump sale over demerger, no shareholder value event.

## PFOCUS — Prime Focus Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a scheme of arrangement whose nature the documents on file do not settle) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 2.5/10 · scheme (nature unclear) · 4 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-04-01, latest 2026-05-12

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'nclt_sanction' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**The stages, as filed:** nclt_sanction (2026-05-08)

**Stated in the filings:** size hint: 0.06% of net worth.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** The AI / Technology business consolidated under the Company's "Brahma" vertical — Brahma India, PFT US, proprietary software — class `regulatory_strategic`.

- *Insiders:* Namit Malhotra, a promoter, redesignated Non-Executive to Whole-time Director from August 7, 2026 (3 years). Documents state no benefit accrues to promoter/promoter group from the restructuring; no promoter stake in Brahma entities stated.
- *What it reveals:* Intra-group prices mark the AI assets: Brahma India at USD 90.09 million versus INR 278.63 crore net worth (10.95% of consolidated); PFT US at ~USD 21 million on INR 1.04 crore net worth. Parent carries INR 483,094 lakh current borrowings and a stayed Section 7 admission.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — No shares distributed to shareholders; transfers are between step-down subsidiaries and remain within the group; no separate listing stated.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* NCLAT order in Comp. App. (AT) (Ins.) No. 850 of 2026, listed for hearing July 9, 2026.
- *In their words:* “The said software assignment forms a part of internal restructuring and consolidation of the AI / Technology business under the Company's vertical "Brahma".”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

There are no earnings-call transcripts on file, so the only stated reasoning is in the Regulation 30 filings, where management frames the separation as an internal group restructuring that splits the AI/technology business from the VFX/post-production services business. The entity being separated is Prime Focus Technologies Limited — renamed Brahma AI Services India Limited — together with the Metaphysic assets (Metaphysic Limited renamed Brahma AI Services UK Limited, DAX Cloud ULC renamed Brahma AI Canada Inc., DNEG Creative Private Limited renamed Brahma AI India Technologies Private Limited); the stated purpose of the March 30, 2026 steps is "internal restructuring and consolidation of the AI / Technology business under the Company's vertical 'Brahma'", which the company says "is expected to leverage the brand value and provide additional revenue streams", and the April 1, 2026 steps are to "streamline the business operations". Mechanically the separation runs both ways: pure software/IP moves up into Brahma (proprietary software assigned from Brahma India to Brahma AI ME Ltd for INR 75.2 Crores, and from Prime Focus Technologies Inc. for USD 3.44 Million), while the people-and-services tails move back into DNEG — the TCS business and Restoration business sold as a going concern by slump sale to DNEG India Media Services Limited for INR 26.5 Crores (FY25 turnover INR 102.62 Crores, 2.85% of consolidated turnover; net worth INR 23.86 Crores, 2.38%), and all of Prime Focus Technologies Inc. (the US services arm, revenue sliding from USD 13,459,863 in FY23 to USD 10,589,160 in FY25) sold by Brahma India to DNEG S.a.r.l. for about USD 21 Million. The holding structure is then re-pointed: DNEG S.a.r.l. sells 100% of Brahma India (its own 92.23% plus the residual 7.77% from other holders) to Brahma AI Holdings Limited, Jersey, for USD 90.09 Million, so the AI business sits under a separate Jersey holdco that is 90.20% held by Double Negative Holdings Limited — i.e. roughly 9.8% outside equity already sits at the Brahma level, which is the only structural hint at third-party participation. Management stresses this is not a divestment and not a court scheme: "the sale is outside the scheme of arrangement. Regulation 37A is not applicable", and "PFT US and Brahma India will continue to be part of the group and will continue to be step-down subsidiaries of the Company". It is also explicitly cashless at the parent: the conversion of Brahma India's inter-company loan and optionally convertible redeemable preference shares in PFT US into equity "does not involve any fresh infusion of capital by the Company or Brahma India". By the time shareholders ratified both transfers as material related-party transactions at the September 30, 2026 AGM, the same notice also carried an increase in authorised capital from 85 Crore to 100 Crore shares and an enabling resolution to raise up to Rs 3,000 Crore via QIP/ADR-GDR/preferential/rights issue — the clearest signal of what the cleaned-up structure is meant to be used for. No filing names any investor, lender or partner as having asked for the separation.

**How it evolved:** The groundwork predates the Brahma language: in the June 2024 quarter Prime Focus Limited sold its entire shareholding in Prime Focus Technologies to step-down subsidiary DNEG S.a.r.l. for Rs 69,302.55 Lakhs, booking an exceptional gain of Rs 21,621.18 Lakhs (shareholder approval June 6, 2024), and on February 14, 2025 the group acquired Metaphysic Inc. for USD 130 Million settled in subsidiary shares (goodwill Rs 96,942.67 Lakhs, later topped up by Rs 6,399.09 Lakhs), while FY25 also carried Rs 38,017.71 Lakhs of exceptional impairments including Rs 17,574.77 Lakhs of decommissioned intangibles. The July 3, 2025 preferential issue of 46,26,69,444 shares at Rs 120 (Rs 5,55,203.33 Lakhs, mostly a 2,561-for-100 swap of DNEG shares, allotted September 17 and 23, 2025) pulled DNEG up into the listed entity and cut non-controlling interest from Rs 1,28,432.26 Lakhs to Rs 45,713.96 Lakhs — a precondition for cleanly re-sorting the subsidiaries. The split itself then arrives in two board/audit-committee steps: March 30, 2026 (software assignments to Brahma AI ME Ltd plus the TCS and Restoration slump sale to DNEG India) and April 1, 2026 (PFT US to DNEG S.a.r.l.; Brahma India to Brahma AI Holdings Limited, Jersey), with the Prime Focus Technologies → Brahma AI Services India renaming confirmed in the May 28, 2026 results. Approval was completed at the September 30, 2026 AGM (resolutions 4 and 5), alongside the capital increase, the Rs 3,000 Crore fund-raise enabling resolution, and Namit Malhotra's move from Non-Executive Director to Whole-time Director effective August 7, 2026.

**What management expects from it:** Only two stated effects: consolidating all AI/technology under the Brahma vertical to "leverage the brand value and provide additional revenue streams", and streamlined operations. Structurally, Brahma AI Holdings (Jersey, 90.20% held) gathers the platform and Metaphysic IP; DNEG takes back PFT US, TCS and Restoration services. No margin, capital-allocation or valuation claim is made anywhere in the filings.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — Filing of March 30, 2026: the stated reason for assigning proprietary software out of Brahma India and PFT USA into Brahma AI ME Ltd (INR 75.2 Crores and USD 3.44 Million respectively) is consolidation of the AI/technology business under the 'Brahma' vertical, justified on brand value and new revenue streams. “The said software assignment forms a part of internal restructuring and consolidation of the AI / Technology business under the Company's vertical "Brahma". This is expected to leverage the brand value and provide additional revenue streams.”
- *Scheme* — Same filing: the TCS business and Restoration business are sold as a going concern by slump sale from Brahma India to DNEG India Media Services Limited for INR 26.5 Crores, on the identical Brahma-consolidation rationale — i.e. services work is deliberately moved out of the AI entity and into the VFX entity. “The said slump sale by Brahma India to DNEG India forms a part of internal restructuring and consolidation of the AI / Technology business under vertical "Brahma". This is expected to leverage the brand value and provide additional revenue streams.”
- *Scheme* — The March 30, 2026 filing draws the dividing line between the two businesses explicitly: Brahma India is the cloud software platform, DNEG India is the post-production services operation. “Brahma India: Provides a cloud-based technology platform for content, workflow, supply chain, and production management for the media and entertainment industry.”
- *Scheme* — Filing of April 1, 2026: the two share transfers — 100% of PFT US from Brahma India to DNEG S.a.r.l. (about USD 21 Million) and 100% of Brahma India from DNEG S.a.r.l. to Brahma AI Holdings Limited, Jersey (USD 90.09 Million) — are presented only as streamlining of operations, with no financial target attached. “the following mentioned subsidiaries of Prime Focus Limited (the "Company" or "PFL") have proposed to undertake certain steps for internal restructuring within the group to streamline the business operations”
- *Scheme* — Management is emphatic that nothing leaves the group and that this is not a demerger or court-sanctioned scheme requiring Regulation 37A compliance. “Upon completion of the aforementioned transfers, PFT US and Brahma India will continue to be part of the group and will continue to be step‑down subsidiaries of the Company.”
- *Scheme* — The restructuring is funded by converting existing intra-group exposure, not new money: Brahma India's inter-company loan and optionally convertible redeemable preference shares in PFT US convert to equity before PFT US is handed to DNEG. “It is important to note that the issuance of additional equity shares does not involve any fresh infusion of capital by the Company or Brahma India.”
- *Scheme* — AGM of September 30, 2026 (Annexure A): the separated AI entity is sized for shareholders — Brahma India FY2025-26 consolidated turnover INR 328.72 Crores (7.03% of group) and net worth INR 278.63 Crores (10.95% of group), versus PFT US turnover INR 99.74 Crores (2.13%) and net worth of just INR 1.04 Crores (0.04%). “Consolidated Turnover of Brahma India for FY 2025 -26: INR 328.72 Crores”
- *Scheme* — The same AGM that ratified both transfers as material related-party transactions also raised authorised capital from 85 Crore to 100 Crore shares and approved an enabling resolution for up to Rs 3,000 Crore of fresh capital, linking the clean-up to a funding event rather than to any disposal. “To consider, evaluate and approve the proposal to raise funds of an amount not exceeding Rs.3,000 Crore (Rupees Three Thousand Crore Only) or its equivalent in any other currency through one or more permissible mechanism as may be deemed appropriate by the Board of Directors of the Company ("Board"), by way of issuance of equity shares and/ or debt securities or non -convertible securities and/or other securities including share warrants and/ or any other equity linked securities.”
- *Scheme* — Audited results of May 28, 2026 undercut any claim that the two businesses are already reported separately — despite the Brahma/DNEG split the group still reports a single operating segment and still describes itself as one integrated setup. “The Group is mainly engaged in operating as integrated post-production setup.”
- *Scheme* — Context for the timing: the FY26 results carry an emphasis of matter on the admitted-then-stayed Section 7 insolvency petition by Raspalfa (formerly Reliance Alpha) for Rs 35,379.75 Lakhs, with the full amount deposited with the Registrar, NCLAT; the underlying Bombay High Court suit was recorded as settled and withdrawn on August 4, 2026, and the group refinanced USD 500 Million of foreign-subsidiary debt to June 2029. “Subsequent to year end, the Group has refinanced its debt facilities of USD 500 Mn in its foreign subsidiary tills June 2029”

*Not explained on the calls:* No earnings-call transcripts on file. Filings give no margin, valuation or synergy numbers, no listing/demerger plan for Brahma, no segment financials, and name no investor, lender or partner as requesting it.

- *Insiders:* Promoter/promoter group/group companies have no interest in Buildnext; buyer JSW One is not promoter group. Consideration is JSW One shares to PVPL; "our shareholding will be insignificant in JSW One."
- *What it reveals:* Buildnext is sub-scale: FY25 revenue Rs 18.38 cr (0.04% of consolidated), PAT Rs (9.11) cr, net worth Rs (1.87) cr. Pidilite instead takes unlisted JSW One stock; Finemake similarly exited. Parent cash ~Rs 3,000 crores.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — No scheme of arrangement, no shares distributed to Pidilite shareholders, nothing listed; transferred business was 0.04% of consolidated revenue.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* The Share Swap Agreement's agreed valuation and PVPL's resulting percentage stake in JSW One — withheld "for confidentiality reasons."
- *In their words:* “And we felt that the business is best served with an owner like JSW who can provide its scale and profitability.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

No demerger or spin-off of a Pidilite operating segment appears anywhere in these texts; the only business separation disclosed is the exit of its venture-stage investments, chiefly BuildNext Construction Solutions Private Limited, a home design and project management services company held as an associate through wholly owned subsidiary Pidilite Ventures Pvt. Ltd. (PVPL). Per the 29 April 2026 Reg. 30 filing, PVPL signed a Share Swap Agreement dated 28 April 2026 with JSW One Platforms Limited and BuildNext to transfer its entire BuildNext shareholding to JSW One, consideration being JSW One shares at a 'mutually agreed valuation' withheld for confidentiality, expected to complete 10 August 2026; as part of the same transaction PVPL agreed to inject up to Rs. 22 crore into BuildNext via CCPS, which on full subscription would have given PVPL majority shareholding on a fully diluted basis. The economics management disclosed are small and loss-making: BuildNext FY25 revenue Rs. 18.38 crore (0.04% of consolidated revenue, versus Rs. 13.87 crore FY24 and Rs. 10.14 crore FY23), PAT of Rs. (9.11) crore and negative net worth of Rs. (1.87) crore. On the 8 May 2026 call Sudhanshu Vats said the reason was 'strategic synergies' and that BuildNext 'has a good home in JSW One', adding that after investing and watching it 'for some time' Pidilite concluded JSW One is 'the right home' to take BuildNext further; Sandeep Batra was blunter — BuildNext was strategic for both sides and 'the business is best served with an owner like JSW who can provide its scale and profitability', so Pidilite was 'very happy to swap' its shareholding, and its resulting JSW One stake will be 'quite insignificant'. Vats framed the residual JSW One shares as, at this moment, a financial investment, consistent with Pidilite's stated habit of taking small stakes in new platforms to look at them more closely, and separately said marketplaces like JSW One and Birla Pivot will go well beyond their own products, so Pidilite will keep evaluating when it is right to sell on one or many of them. The same pattern of pruning sub-scale, loss-making non-core holdings continued after the swap: on 29 September 2026 PVPL agreed to sell its entire stake in associate Finemake Technologies (FY26 revenue Rs. 24.36 crore, 0.06% of consolidated revenue; PAT Rs. (7.82) crore; net worth Rs. (6.18) crore) back to founders Nallu Rajashekar and Sambasiva Rao Chowdary Chana, completion expected 15 October 2026, and on 19 August 2026 step-down subsidiary Nina Percept (Bangladesh) was voluntarily liquidated because it had been 'inoperative since incorporation due to lack of business opportunities'. No investor, lender or partner is said to have asked for any of this — the only external parties named are the counterparties themselves (JSW One, the Finemake founders), and the filings state the deals are not related-party transactions and the buyers are not promoter group.

**How it evolved:** Through Aug 2024, Feb 2025, May 2025, Aug 2025, Nov 2025 and Feb 2026 calls there is no mention of separating any business — only portfolio-level housekeeping: the FY24 Pulvitec Brazil divestment and Pidilite USA wind-down in the base (May 2025), a Rs. 20 crore standalone / Rs. 25 crore consolidated exceptional impairment of a loan and investment in an associate (May 2025), and Batra's Oct 31, 2025 remark that Pidilite Ventures 'continuously is evaluating' new investments or raising stakes, with roughly Rs. 3,000 crore of cash on hand. The plan surfaces only in the 29 April 2026 Reg. 30 filing of the Share Swap Agreement and is then explained for the first and only time on the 8 May 2026 Q4 FY26 call, in response to Abneesh Roy's opening question. It then widens into a broader clean-up without further call commentary: Nina Percept (Bangladesh) liquidated effective 19 August 2026 (filed 3 September 2026) and the Finemake stake sold back to its founders (filed 29 September 2026, completion 15 October 2026). The only shift in framing within the May 2026 call is from Vats's 'strategic synergies' to Batra's narrower position that Pidilite's JSW One stake will be insignificant and that scale and profitability belong with JSW.

**What management expects from it:** For BuildNext: an owner able to give it scale and profitability, taking it further than Pidilite could. For Pidilite: an exit of a loss-making 0.04%-of-revenue adjacency, replaced by an admittedly insignificant JSW One shareholding treated as a financial investment, plus optional future access to JSW One's marketplace. No margin, capital-release, valuation or focus benefit was quantified on the call.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The 29 Apr 2026 filing discloses PVPL's Share Swap Agreement (dated 28 Apr 2026) with JSW One Platforms and BuildNext: PVPL's entire BuildNext stake goes to JSW One for JSW One shares at an undisclosed valuation, completion expected 10 Aug 2026. “The transfer of shares of PVPL in Buildnext to JSW One is proposed to be effected in consideration of issuance of shares of JSW One to PVPL at a mutually agreed valuation, the details of which have not been disclosed herein for confidentiality reasons.”
- *May 2026* — Asked why Pidilite would transfer BuildNext, Vats gave the rationale as strategic synergies and a better owner, not a financial exit. “So Abneesh, I think the reason is that we found strategic synergies in doing this transaction. I think BuildNext basically has a good home in JSW One.”
- *May 2026* — Batra said the separation solves an ownership/scale problem: BuildNext was strategic to both sides, but JSW can supply the scale and profitability Pidilite could not, so Pidilite swapped out willingly. “And we felt that the business is best served with an owner like JSW who can provide its scale and profitability.”
- *May 2026* — Vats explained the decision followed a period of ownership and observation after Pidilite's own investment in BuildNext. “Now having seen that for some time, we think JSW One is the right home for BuildNext to take BuildNext further as we go forward.”
- *May 2026* — Batra pre-empted any read-through that this creates a meaningful JSW One holding or paints tie-up, capping the retained stake as immaterial. “Our shareholding in JSW will be quite insignificant.”
- *May 2026* — Vats characterised the retained JSW One shares as, for now, a financial investment arising from the swap rather than a strategic stake. “So see, it is at this moment through the transfer of BuildNext financial investment.”
- *May 2026* — Pressed on competing with JSW in paints (they bid against each other for Akzo), Vats would only say the marketplace relationship is a future option Pidilite will evaluate. “So what our point of view is that we will keep evaluating it in a manner of speaking and see when it is right for us to be on one or many of these marketplaces.”
- *Scheme* — The filing's only stated object for the holding being separated is 'Investment in adjacency business', with BuildNext's business described as home design and project management services, incorporated 16 Oct 2015. “Investment in adjacency business.”
- *Scheme* — BuildNext's disclosed numbers show why it was immaterial to Pidilite: FY25 revenue Rs. 18.38 crore, just 0.04% of consolidated revenue, with a Rs. 9.11 crore loss and negative net worth of Rs. 1.87 crore. “The revenue of Buildnext for the financial year ended 31st March 2025 was Rs. 18.38 crores as per the financial statements of Buildnext, which contributed 0.04% to the consolidated revenue of the Company for the same period.”
- *Scheme* — Unexplained in the calls: as part of the same exit transaction PVPL agreed to put up to Rs. 22 crore of fresh money into BuildNext via CCPS, which on full subscription would have made PVPL the majority shareholder on a fully diluted basis. “As a part of the aforesaid transaction, PVPL has agreed to make additional investment in Buildnext of an amount not exceeding Rs. 22 crore, by subscribing to Compulsorily Convertible Preference Shares (CCPS) of Buildnext.”
- *Scheme* — The same pruning extended to Finemake Technologies on 29 Sep 2026: PVPL's entire associate stake sold back to founders Nallu Rajashekar and Sambasiva Rao Chowdary Chana at an undisclosed valuation, completion expected 15 Oct 2026, with FY26 revenue of Rs. 24.36 crore (0.06% of consolidated revenue), PAT of Rs. (7.82) crore and net worth of Rs. (6.18) crore. “Pidilite Ventures Pvt. Ltd. ("PVPL") has agreed to transfer its entire shareholding in Finemake Technologies Private Limited ("Finemake"), an associate company of PVPL, to the founders of Finemake at a mutually agreed valuation, the details of which have not been disclosed herein for confidentiality reasons.”
- *Scheme* — A third, purely administrative separation: step-down subsidiary Nina Percept (Bangladesh) Pvt. Ltd. was voluntarily liquidated effective 19 Aug 2026, with nil turnover, a BDT 7,01,654 loss and BDT 30,13,824 net worth. “NPBPL has been inoperative since incorporation due to lack of business opportunities.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No valuation, swap ratio or stake percentage; no reason for the Rs. 22 crore CCPS top-up before exiting; no P&L impact; no Finemake rationale; no investor, lender or partner asked.

## SHILPAMED — Shilpa Medicare Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a scheme of arrangement whose nature the documents on file do not settle) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 2.5/10 · scheme (nature unclear) · 1 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-01-15, latest 2026-01-15

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**Stated in the filings:** size hint: 0.03% of net worth.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Koanna Healthcare Canada Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary, sold outright to an individual buyer in Canada — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* Buyer Steve N. Slilaty, individual residing at Quebec, "doesn't belong to promoter/promoter group/group companies"; no promoter or management stake in the entity stated.
- *What it reveals:* Reveals an immaterial unit: income Rs 34.33 lakhs (0.03%) and net worth Rs 46.09 lakhs (0.02%), sold for CAD 2000; investment already provided for, so no financial impact.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — No shares distributed to shareholders; sold to one individual; not a material subsidiary under Regulation 16.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* FY26 consolidated accounts: the provision already made against the Koanna investment, and remaining Koanna group entities.
- *In their words:* “Consequent to the above transaction, Koanna Healthcare Canada Inc. has ceased to be a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company with effect from 14 January 2026.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Nothing in these texts describes Shilpa Medicare separating a business: there is no demerger, spin-off, slump sale of a division or separate listing of a vertical anywhere in the eight transcripts (Jul 2024 to May 2026) or the three filings, and no analyst, lender or partner on any call asks for one. The corporate actions on record run the other way, toward consolidation into the listed parent: the NCLT Bengaluru order of 27 Feb 2026 (certified copy received 16 Mar 2026) sanctions the amalgamation of Shilpa Therapeutics Private Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary with revenue of only Rs 2.31 cr (FY23) and Rs 3.07 cr (FY24), into Shilpa Medicare, with no shares issued since the transferor is a WOS, its shares cancelled, authorised capital clubbed, staff absorbed under Clause 7.1 and the appointed date pushed from 01.04.2023 to 01.04.2025 at the Regional Director's insistence; the Regional Director flagged that the loss-making transferor merging into a profit-making transferee means there may be a negative outflow of income tax, and the same tax logic was stated explicitly for the earlier inward merger of INM Technologies (NCLT approval 18 Jun 2025), where Alpesh Dalal said unabsorbed INM losses would lower FY25 tax outflow, taking the Q1 FY26 effective tax rate down to 5.5%. The only genuine separations disclosed are two small exits, neither explained strategically: Koanna Healthcare Canada Inc. ceased to be a wholly owned subsidiary on 14 Jan 2026 when 2,84,21,020 shares were allotted to an individual, Steve N. Slilaty of Quebec, for CAD 2,000 total, a non-material subsidiary contributing Rs 34.33 lakh of income (0.03%) and Rs 46.09 lakh of net worth (0.02%) in FY25, already provided for, so no impact on financials; and in Q4 FY26 the sale of a 31% stake in JV Sravathi Advance, retaining 34%, booking an exceptional gain of INR 30 crores and reclassifying it from joint venture to associate. Management's stated strategic direction is the opposite of separation: Shilpa is described as an integrated one-stop solution across API, formulations, biologics and CDMO, with API deliberately feeding captive formulations because, in Dalal's words, you get end-to-end margins there, which lifted FY26 group gross margin to 70% and EBITDA margin to 29%. The nearest thing to a requested carve-out is presentational, not legal: investors repeatedly pressed for CDMO, captive-API and biologics revenue to be reported separately (CDMO was INR 158 cr in FY25; about INR 110 cr of API CDMO in FY26), and management said it was considering showing CDMO separately, while already publishing an adjusted ROCE that excludes biologics, NBE and albumin investments (4% in FY23 to 17.4% in FY26). The schemes' own rationale clauses are not reproduced in the filings, so no managerial reasoning for any structural change is available in this corpus beyond the tax and capital-clubbing mechanics recorded by the regulators.

**How it evolved:** The idea that surfaces is consolidation, not separation: on the Aug 2025 (Q1 FY26) call Alpesh Dalal disclosed NCLT Bangalore approval for amalgamating INM Technologies into Shilpa Medicare and said its unabsorbed losses would cut prior-year tax, cutting the quarter's ETR to 5.5%. The first actual separation appears only in the 15 Jan 2026 filing, when Koanna Healthcare Canada Inc. stopped being a wholly owned subsidiary for CAD 2,000, never mentioned on the Feb 2026 or May 2026 calls. The second scheme was sanctioned on 27 Feb 2026 (intimated 5 and 17 Mar 2026), merging Shilpa Therapeutics Private Limited inward with the appointed date moved to 01.04.2025. Only on the May 2026 (Q4 FY26) call did a divestment get narrated, as the 31% Sravathi Advance stake sale yielding an INR 30 crore exceptional gain and reclassification to associate, prompted by an analyst question rather than by management strategy.

**What management expects from it:** No separation benefits were stated, because no business separation was announced. For the inward mergers management cited only tax relief from unabsorbed subsidiary losses (Q1 FY26 ETR 5.5%), clubbed authorised capital, absorbed employees and no dilution. Koanna Canada's exit was called financially immaterial; Sravathi's 31% sale yielded a INR 30 crore gain and associate reclassification. Margin and ROCE gains were attributed to integration, not separation.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The 27 Feb 2026 NCLT order amalgamates a wholly owned subsidiary, Shilpa Therapeutics Private Limited, into the listed parent with no consideration and no dilution, the transferor's shares simply cancelled. “Since the Transferor Company is a wholly owned subsidiary of the Transferee Company, upon the Scheme coming into effect, in connection of the amalgamation of the Transferor Company with the Transferee Company in the terms of the Scheme, no shares will be issued/allotted under the Scheme by the Transferee Company to any person.”
- *Scheme* — The Regional Director's report frames the merger's economic consequence purely in tax terms: a loss-making transferor folding into a profit-making transferee, with an undertaking sought on tax implications. “Hence, there may be a negative outflow of income tax once the Scheme is sanctioned.”
- *Scheme* — The appointed date was not a strategic choice but a regulator-driven correction, shifted from 01.04.2023 to 01.04.2025 because the original date was too old relative to filed annual returns. “It is submitted that the Petitioner Companies herein do not have an objection for change of the Appointed Date to 01.04.2025 in accordance with the directions of this Tribunal.”
- *Scheme* — The 15 Jan 2026 filing records the only outright separation of an entity: Koanna Healthcare Canada Inc. exits via allotment of 2,84,21,020 shares to an individual in Quebec for CAD 2,000, with no rationale given. “Consequent to the above transaction, Koanna Healthcare Canada Inc. has ceased to be a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company with effect from 14 January 2026.”
- *Scheme* — Koanna Canada was immaterial on both metrics disclosed for FY25 and fully provided for, so the exit is presented as financially inconsequential rather than value-unlocking. “The company has already provided for the above investment in the subsidiary. Hence, there is no impact on the Company's current financials.”
- *CALL Aug 2025* — The earlier inward merger, INM Technologies into Shilpa Medicare, was explained to investors solely as a tax benefit, which drove the quarter's effective tax rate down to 5.5%. “And the tax impact of unabsorbed losses of INM is likely to result in lower tax outflow for the previous financial year, and the effect for the same has been captured in the current quarter.”
- *CALL May 2026* — The only partial separation discussed on a call: 31% of JV Sravathi Advance sold for an INR 30 crore exceptional gain, with 34% retained and the entity deconsolidated to associate status; no strategic reasoning offered. “During the quarter, we also had an exceptional gain amounting to INR30 crores on account of stake sale in one of our JV company, Sravathi Advance, where we have sold 31% stake and now hold 34% stake.”
- *CALL Nov 2025* — Management's framing is integration across verticals, the opposite of separating a business, positioning API, formulations and biologics as a single platform with high entry barriers. “We are operating in some of the most advanced, complex and high entry barrier segments, namely API, Formulations, Biologics, as an integrated one-stop solution.”
- *CALL Feb 2026* — Dalal defends captive API supply to the formulation vertical as a deliberate strategic call for end-to-end margins, rebutting an analyst who wanted non-captive API judged separately. “The API business is also supporting the Formulation business with the supplies. And that's a strategic call that we have taken because you get end-to-end margins there.”
- *CALL May 2026* — The nearest thing to a carve-out is presentational: a reported ROCE that strips out biologics, albumin and NBE investments to show the rest of the group's returns. “Our adjusted ROCE, excluding investments made in high-growth potential businesses like biologics and albumin, has seen a significant improvement from 4% in FY23 to 17.4% in FY26.”
- *CALL May 2025* — Investors asked for CDMO (INR 158 crores in FY25, 20-plus programs) to be disclosed as its own line rather than buried inside API, formulations and biologics; management said it was considering separate reporting, not separate ownership. “And what we are trying to do, is that in the years to come or in the next financial year, segregate CDMO revenues.”
- *CALL Feb 2025* — The only other separation in the record is at shareholder level, not business level: inactive promoter-family members sought reclassification to public category, explained as compliance relief. “So, it was just more of a compliance-related requirement that was coming up, which they wanted to avoid, nothing more than that.”

*Not explained on the calls:* The schemes' rationale clauses are never reproduced, only considered at first motion. No strategic, valuation or capital-allocation reason is given for the Koanna or Sravathi exits, and neither was discussed on any call.

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The premise cannot be supported: nothing in these ten transcripts or the single filing announces, proposes, or explains a separation, demerger, spin-off, slump sale or hive-off of any Solar Industries business. The only time separation is raised at all is an analyst question in the Q3 FY25 call (Feb 6, 2025), where Rakesh Roy of Boring AMC asks whether the defence business could be spun off in 2-3 years; Aanchal Kewlani answers that defence sits in the group alongside the explosives business and 'that will continue' — a refusal, with no rationale, structure, record date or ratio offered. Management's repeated stance across the whole period is the opposite of separation: 'we treat business as one unit' (May 21, 2025), 'we run business as a whole' (May 15, 2026), 'Like we always say that for us, our business is one' when refusing to split FY27 capex of INR2,050 crores between defence and non-defence, and refusals to disclose segment-level EBITDA margins ('we as a business as a whole, we are achieving around 27% EBITDA margin'). The group is in fact consolidating and integrating rather than separating: defence is run through subsidiary Solar Defence (noted in May 2026 as 'a subsidiary of Solar Industries'), with capex of INR2,700 crores over two years, a INR12,700 crore 10-year MoU with the Government of Maharashtra, nine-plus overseas manufacturing subsidiaries, the Problast (South Africa) acquisition, and a stated intent to move up the value chain into complete 155 mm rounds rather than only supply energetics ('our intention is to make a complete round of 155'). The closest thing to separation language is descriptive, not structural: on May 15, 2026 Manish Nuwal said 'the defense vertical is steadily maturing into a powerful stand-alone platform' — immediately after reporting defence revenue of INR2,634 crores for FY26 (up 94%, 27% of the INR9,838 crore group) and an INR18,000 crore defence order book inside a INR21,300 crore total, i.e. scale and focus, not a legal split. The lone filing (April 24, 2026) is not a scheme at all: it is newspaper clippings of an IEPF unclaimed-share transfer notice; the scheme-of-arrangement text on those same newspaper pages belongs to unrelated companies (Swan Defence and Heavy Industries / Triumph Offshore, plus Tata Chemicals' IEPF notice and BGR Energy's insolvency notice) and must not be read as Solar's. No investor, lender or partner in these texts asks for a separation, and no problem is said to be solved by one.

**How it evolved:** Feb 6, 2025: the only separation question in three years is asked by an analyst and declined — defence 'will continue' inside the group. May 21, 2025 through Feb 4, 2026: management repeatedly reaffirms one-business management (single EBITDA guidance ~27%, undivided capex, no segment margins), while defence is scaled up inside subsidiary Solar Defence under the INR12,700 crore Maharashtra MoU. May 15, 2026: defence is called 'a powerful stand-alone platform' and FY27 capex of INR2,050 crores is again explicitly refused a defence/non-defence split ('for us, our business is one'), so the only trajectory visible is integration, not separation. The April 24, 2026 filing adds nothing: it is an IEPF share-transfer newspaper notice, with the only demerger/amalgamation text on the page belonging to other issuers.

**What management expects from it:** Nothing is stated, because no separation is proposed. For the consolidated company management expects FY27 revenue of INR14,000 crores (defence over INR4,500 crores) on a INR21,300 crore order book, EBITDA margins held near 27-28%, INR2,050 crores of undivided capex, and working capital normalising to ~90 days within two quarters.

So, that will continue.”

- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=d441b5e0-98fc-4d6a-828b-877d1758a99a.pdf)* — Asked specifically for defence EBITDA margin, management refuses segment-level disclosure and restates a single consolidated ~27% margin, so no standalone defence economics exist in the record on which a separation case could rest. “You can ask such things, but we will answer only one thing, that we as a business as a whole, we are achieving around 27% EBITDA margin, and we should be able to continue with the similar margins.”
