## SONACOMS — Sona BLW Precision Forgings Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a scheme of arrangement whose nature the documents on file do not settle) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 2.5/10 · scheme (nature unclear) · 1 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-07-22, latest 2026-07-22

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** The Electric Vehicle Business: air-cooled traction motors, generators, traction inverters, eAxles for 2 and 3-wheelers — class `regulatory_strategic`.

- *Insiders:* Promoters not interested except via their shareholding in the Company; Mr. Vikram Verma Vadapalli (WTD/KMP) holds 1 nominee share and is Non-Executive Director of Sona eDrive; Mr. Sat Mohan Gupta also a director
- *What it reveals:* EV Business carve-out financials revealed: FY26 turnover INR 3,855mn, net worth INR 3,471mn, EBITDA INR 405mn; Deloitte valued it INR 8,694–9,180mn (mid INR 8,932mn), while DENSO subscribes 49% at enterprise value INR 17,500mn
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — No shares distributed to shareholders; Sona eDrive stays a 51% subsidiary and remains consolidated, parent listing unchanged
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Deloitte India Valuation LLP valuation report linked in the postal ballot notice, and the October 6, 2026 e-voting result
- *In their words:* “The management assessed the Proposed Transaction to be in the larger interest of the Company and is expected to facilitate strategic business objectives, unlock significant value and support long term growth of the EV Business.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Management presented the separation not as a fix for a broken business but as the vehicle for closing its biggest admitted portfolio gap and executing its 'Look East' growth engine. On the 23 July 2026 call Vivek Vikram Singh said Sona had built 'one of India's broadest portfolio of electric powertrain products' but 'did not participate at all in high voltage electric as well as hybrid powertrain systems for passenger and commercial vehicles' — a market S&P Global Mobility puts at over 2.3 million Indian hybrid/EV cars and commercial vehicles, about Rs 24,000 crore in 2030 and 'maybe 3 times that' by 2035 — and that DENSO (world's second largest mobility technology company, with electrification revenue above $8 billion a year, and 100:1 better known than Sona) fills it. The mechanics: Sona carved its existing 2W/3W EV business (air-cooled traction motors and generators, traction inverters, eAxles) out of the listed company by slump sale on a going-concern basis into wholly owned Sona Comstar eDrive for INR 8,932 million (INR 8,575 million cash plus roughly INR 357 million in eDrive shares; Deloitte India Valuation LLP range INR 8,694–9,180 million), then sold DENSO 49% of eDrive at an enterprise value of INR 17,500 million while keeping 51%, majority directors and a 7-year transfer lock; separately a new JV2 for liquid-cooled high-voltage 4W+ motors, generators and inverters (excluding eAxles and gears) is 51% DENSO / 49% Sona out of a INR 535 million subscription, Sona putting in INR 262.15 million, with DENSO contributing the technology, IP and management. The stated problems solved: zero participation in high-voltage and hybrid 4W+ systems; a 2/3W business stuck at about 25% India share that Vivek wants above 50% and which is the group's lowest-margin line (FY26 revenue INR 3,855 million, EBITDA INR 405 million, roughly 10.5%, repeatedly cited as dragging consolidated margin); a customer base 'that is in a way not that open to us right now'; and exports 'to other markets where Denso is far more dominant'. Royalties are reciprocal — each partner is paid by its own majority-owned JV — which Vivek called the 'ultimate validation' of Sona's technology and possibly the first royalty income by an Indian auto company from a global mobility technology company. The filings add the corporate-speak version: technology collaboration, long-term product development capability, enhanced market access, 'operational focus' for the EV Business and to 'unlock significant value'. Nothing in the calls or filings attributes the move to any investor, lender or customer demand — Vivek framed DENSO as having chosen Sona ('why Sona Comstar?'), analyst Sonal Gupta instead challenged 'the motivation for putting that in the JV', and Sona's suspension motor and all other non-traction motor businesses were explicitly kept outside the transaction.

**How it evolved:** On the May 2025 and Aug 2025 calls the 4W/high-voltage piece was purely an in-house project ('we are developing high voltage traction motors') and the eastward route ran through a China driveline JV with JNT, which was then 'put in abeyance' on the Oct 2025 call for geopolitical reasons and 'the need to prioritize other active capital allocation decisions'. The Jan 2026 call carried the first real foreshadowing: the 'big boy piece, which is the four-wheeler bit' was being worked on, 'closer than one expected', with a 'meaningful update' promised in 6-7 months and an explicit fallback that 'if we are not able to do it ourselves, we'll... collaborate, partner, do something'; as late as the May 2026 call M&A was still 'nothing that has reached a stage which is worth sharing or reportable'. Definitive agreements were signed 22 July 2026 and unveiled on the 23 July 2026 call, where Vivek revealed the strategy had been worked on 'more than 2 years ago' but deliberately not discussed until there was something tangible. A postal ballot notice dated 31 August 2026 (voting 4 September – 3 October 2026) then put the slump sale, the eDrive share issue and a 29-year Chennai land sublease to shareholders as a material related-party transaction of about INR 8,934.05 million, with closing targeted on or before 31 March 2027.

**What management expects from it:** eDrive (2/3W): more customers, leadership extended 'to one of dominance' beyond 25% share, DENSO-enabled exports, royalty income, Sona 51% control and continued consolidation, plus INR 8,575 million cash and eDrive shares to the parent. JV2 (high-voltage 4W+): DENSO technology, IP and management, a Rs 24,000 crore 2030 market, capital-light returns. Group: 49% becomes non-controlling interest.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Jul 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ba4be72b-164f-4dd9-b6ae-ff475176e5bc.pdf)* — Management named the gap the JVs are meant to close: no participation at all in high-voltage electric and hybrid powertrain systems for passenger and commercial vehicles. “We did not participate at all in high voltage electric as well as hybrid powertrain systems for passenger and commercial vehicles.”
- *[Jul 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ba4be72b-164f-4dd9-b6ae-ff475176e5bc.pdf)* — The high-voltage prize was sized from S&P Global Mobility data, and Vivek later said the 2035 number could be roughly three times the 2030 figure. “If we go by S&P Global mobility, Indian hybrid and EV cars and the commercial vehicle market alone represents an addressable market of over 2.3 million vehicles, which would roughly amount to about a 24,000 crore opportunity in 2030 itself.”
- *[Jul 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ba4be72b-164f-4dd9-b6ae-ff475176e5bc.pdf)* — In the 4W+ high-voltage JV Sona is the minority partner and DENSO brings technology, IP and management control. “In this JV, Denso will hold the majority stake, contribute the relevant technology and intellectual property, and lead the business from a management perspective.”
- *[Jul 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ba4be72b-164f-4dd9-b6ae-ff475176e5bc.pdf)* — In the 2W/3W JV — the business being carved out of the listed company — Sona keeps majority ownership and control and licenses in its own technology. “Here we will retain majority ownership and management control while licensing our own technology into the joint venture.”
- *[Jul 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ba4be72b-164f-4dd9-b6ae-ff475176e5bc.pdf)* — The stated commercial aim for the carved-out 2/3W entity is more customers and a shift from leadership to dominance; Vivek said 25% India share 'is also not enough. Why not more than 50%?' “Today, we have a leadership position in 2 and 3 wheelers in India, and through this partnership, we should hopefully add more customers to the 2 and 3-wheeler JV and extend our leadership position to one of dominance.”
- *[Jul 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ba4be72b-164f-4dd9-b6ae-ff475176e5bc.pdf)* — Answering Sonal Gupta's challenge on why a business already doing well should go into a JV, Vivek cited a customer base 'not that open to us right now' plus exports. “Third, the export opportunity opens up for us to other markets where Denso is far more dominant.”
- *[Jul 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ba4be72b-164f-4dd9-b6ae-ff475176e5bc.pdf)* — Royalties run both ways, each JV paying the partner whose technology it licenses; Vivek called this the validation that Sona's technology has value. “JV2 will pay royalties to Denso for its high voltage technologies, while JV1 will pay royalties to Sona Comstar for our 2 and 3 wheeler technologies.”
- *[Jul 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ba4be72b-164f-4dd9-b6ae-ff475176e5bc.pdf)* — The business being separated is the group's lowest-margin product line, which management repeatedly blamed for consolidated margin dilution in the same quarter. “There was also a product mix impact as traction motor sales grew quite rapidly, and as is well known to you, that product category has the lowest margins relative to our average company margin, so that also dragged it down a little bit.”
- *[Jul 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ba4be72b-164f-4dd9-b6ae-ff475176e5bc.pdf)* — Scope was explicitly fenced: only traction motors/controllers for 2W and 3W move; suspension motors and other non-traction motor businesses stay in the listed company. “Let me also clarify because we got some calls that our suspension motor business, together with all our other non-traction motor businesses remain completely outside the scope of this transaction.”
- *[Jul 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ba4be72b-164f-4dd9-b6ae-ff475176e5bc.pdf)* — Management argued motor and controller businesses are capital-light, with Sat Mohan Gupta putting high-voltage revenue at 11-12 rupees per rupee of capex versus 8-9 in two-wheelers. “Sure, capex intensity of motor business and control system businesses is actually low.”
- *[Jan 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=a597eb28-0b1a-4389-b416-e8dcf2e65db3.pdf)* — Six months before the announcement, the four-wheeler traction motor move was flagged as live and nearer than expected, with an update promised in 6-7 months. “And obviously, the big boy piece, which is the four-wheeler bit, is something that we are working on, and hopefully, we can share something in the times to come.”
- *[Jan 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=a597eb28-0b1a-4389-b416-e8dcf2e65db3.pdf)* — The same call pre-committed to a partnership route if Sona could not crack the four-wheeler segment alone. “If we are not able to do it ourselves, we'll, of course, figure out a way to collaborate, partner, do something, but it is a segment that we will come to in the end,”

*Not explained on the calls:* SOP timelines withheld; no margin, return or revenue guidance for either JV; nothing on royalty rates, use of the INR 8,575 million cash, or why 51/49; call's JV1/JV2 labels inconsistent.

## TATACAP — Tata Capital Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a filing's text names a demerger; no scheme filing names it yet) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 2.5/10 · spin-off · 1 filing(s) from NSE · first 2025-12-22, latest 2025-12-22

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**Stated in the filings:** demerged undertaking: ) of Tata Motors Limited had been demerged, transferred and vested into TML Commercial Vehicles Limited.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** The Commercial Vehicles Business of Tata Motors Limited, demerged and vested into TML Commercial Vehicles Limited on a going concern basis — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited ceased to be a member of Tata Capital's Promoter Group, its 43,26,651 TCL shares (0.10%) passing to TML Commercial Vehicles Limited (now Tata Motors Limited).
- *What it reveals:* Only that the Commercial Vehicles entity now holds Tata Capital's 43,26,651 equity shares (0.10% of paid-up capital); the documents disclose nothing about the demerged business's economics or value.
- *Selling pressure:* unclear — not stated
- *Parent or spin:* unclear · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* The Composite Scheme of Arrangement and NCLT Sanction Orders dated August 25, 2025 and September 10, 2025
- *In their words:* “Pursuant to the said Scheme, the Commercial Vehicles Business ("Demerged undertaking") of Tata Motors Limited had been demerged, transferred and vested into TML Commercial Vehicles Limited on a going concern basis.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The premise cannot be supported from these texts: in the three transcripts (Oct 28, 2025; Jan 19, 2026; Apr 23, 2026) and the three filings (Dec 22, 2025; Dec 23, 2025; Jun 17, 2026), Tata Capital Ltd. never announces, proposes or discusses separating, demerging, spinning off, hiving down or divesting any business of its own. The only corporate restructuring involving Tata Capital runs the opposite way — consolidation: the scheme of arrangement sanctioned by NCLT Mumbai on May 1, 2025 amalgamated Tata Motors Finance Ltd. (TMFL) INTO Tata Capital with effect from May 8, 2025 (appointed date April 1, 2024), and management spent all three calls explaining the integration of that Motor Finance book, not its separation: repricing legacy TMFL borrowings (60 bps cost saving, ~95% done in FY26), pivoting from a captive to a multi-OEM model (non-Tata OEM share of new CV disbursements 0% in Q4 FY25 → 13% in Q2 FY26 → 19% in Q3 → 26% in Q4 FY26), shifting mix from heavy CVs to used and small/mid CVs, rationalising 90+ branches, merging IT systems, and taking the book from INR26,694 crores (Mar '25) down to INR23,698 crores (Sep '25) and INR25,390 crores (Mar '26) under a 'fitness-first' approach, with break-even in Q3 FY26, PAT of INR43 crores in Q4 FY26 and a target ROA of 2% by FY28. The one genuine demerger in the documents belongs to a different company: the Composite Scheme of Arrangement among Tata Motors Ltd., TML Commercial Vehicles Ltd. and Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Ltd. (NCLT Mumbai, Aug 25 / Sep 10, 2025), which demerged Tata Motors' Commercial Vehicles business and, as a side effect, moved a 43,26,651-share (0.10%) stake in Tata Capital from Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles to TML Commercial Vehicles (renamed Tata Motors Ltd.) effective Oct 1, 2025 — a promoter-group shareholding transfer disclosed under PIT Regulation 7(2), not a separation by or of Tata Capital. Far from separating businesses, management repeatedly defended keeping overlapping ones together: asked by PhillipCapital on Apr 23, 2026 why Tata Capital runs two LAP books (~INR38,000 crores in the NBFC versus ~INR17,000–18,000 crores in Tata Capital Housing Finance) with 'two separate sales team and two separate credit teams', Rajiv Sabharwal said both entities should continue, and Sarosh Amaria argued the shared housing sales team improves field productivity. The stated strategy is explicit diversification across 25+ products — 'We don't consider any business to be the most important' — with retail and SME at 86–88% of AUM, housing growing ~29–30%, and no business flagged for exit. No investor, lender or partner in any of the three calls asks for a separation; the only pull-back ever described is tactical de-growth and tighter underwriting in unsecured retail and Motor Finance, not structural separation. The only other corporate action in the filings is the Board's Jun 17, 2026 approval to raise up to Rs. 36,000 crore of NCDs on private placement, and a SEBI settlement (Rs. 32,00,000) for erstwhile TMFL's 2019/2020/2022 NCD issuances deemed public issues.

**How it evolved:** There is no separation idea to trace: across Oct 28, 2025, Jan 19, 2026 and Apr 23, 2026 the restructuring narrative is consistently the integration of the acquired Tata Motors Finance book into Tata Capital, which completed on May 8, 2025. On Oct 28, 2025 management framed it as transformation in progress (book down INR2,996 crores to INR23,698 crores, break-even guided for Q4 FY26, 2% ROA by FY28); on Jan 19, 2026 it reported break-even achieved a quarter early in Q3 with AUM down 6% and disbursements up 17% QoQ; on Apr 23, 2026 it reported Q4 PAT of INR43 crores, non-Tata OEM share at 26%, negative net slippages, and growth resuming in H1 FY27. The only demerger in the record appears in the Dec 22, 2025 filing and belongs to Tata Motors, touching Tata Capital only as a 0.10% promoter-group share transfer effective Oct 1, 2025.

**What management expects from it:** Nothing, because no separation is proposed. Their stated expectations concern the reverse — absorbing Tata Motors Finance: 2%+ ROA by FY28, NIM plus fee up ~50 bps, credit cost down 60-70 bps, cost-to-average-assets down 30-40 bps, 60 bps funding saving from Tata Capital's AAA, growth resuming H1 FY27; group-wide 23-25% AUM growth, 2.5-2.7% ROA, 33-34% cost-to-income by FY28.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The scheme of arrangement involving Tata Capital is an amalgamation INTO it — Tata Motors Finance Ltd. merged into Tata Capital per NCLT Mumbai's May 1, 2025 order, effective May 8, 2025, appointed date April 1, 2024 — not a separation of any business out of it. “Kindly note that pursuant to a scheme of arrangement amongst the Company , TMFL  and their respective shareholders, sanctioned by the National Company Law Tribunal, Mumbai vide its order dated May 1, 2025, TMFL has amalgamated with the Company with effect from May 8, 2025 , with the appointed date being April 1, 2024.”
- *Scheme* — The only demerger in the documents is Tata Motors' own Composite Scheme (NCLT Mumbai, Aug 25 / Sep 10, 2025) separating its Commercial Vehicles business; its sole effect on Tata Capital was moving a 43,26,651-share, 0.10% stake between promoter-group entities, disclosed under PIT Regulation 7(2). “Consequently, the shareholding of Tata Capital Limited (“TCL”) previously held by the Company, comprising 43,26,651 equity shares (representing 0.10% of the TCL’s paid-up share capital), has been transferred to TML Commercial Vehicles Limited (now Tata Motors Limited) in accordance with the Scheme.”
- *CALL Nov 2025* — Management presents Motor Finance as an acquisition being absorbed, reported separately only for comparability, and calls its presence essential to growth — the opposite of a candidate for separation; the net loan book fell INR2,996 crores to INR23,698 crores by Sep '25 as a transitional integration effect. “As a business, we believe that our presence in the Motor Finance business is crucial to our growth , and we are confident of transforming this business into a 2% plus RoA business by FY'2 8.”
- *CALL Nov 2025* — The stated strategy is deliberate breadth — 25+ lending products used as switchable growth engines (SME/Corporate during COVID, secured retail/housing/SME while unsecured was stressed) — with no business identified for exit or hive-off. “A very well diversified suite of 25 + lending products that help us manage growth and quality better.”
- *CALL Jan 2026* — Asked about the shrinking Motor Finance book, management describes portfolio reorientation and a lower future weight (12–13% of AUM at merger, ~9.5% in Q3 FY26, drifting to 7–8% by FY28) through slower growth — a mix shift, never a separation. “Talking now a little more about the Motor Finance business, our primary focus in the Motor Finance business is on reorienting the portfolio rather than pursuing near -term growth.”
- *CALL Jan 2026* — Management explicitly rejects ranking or subordinating any business line, stating each segment is run to be best-in-class — a direct statement against separating or deprioritising a unit. “We don't consider any business to be the most important and others around it to serve as the next in line business.”
- *CALL Apr 2026* — PhillipCapital pressed on the duplicated LAP books (~INR38,000 crores in the NBFC vs ~INR17,000–18,000 crores in the HFC) with separate sales, credit and operations teams; management defended keeping both rather than consolidating or separating either. “We feel it's a large market and in terms of portfolio quality, both the portfolios have done very well and we do believe that both these entities have an opportunity to do so.”
- *CALL Apr 2026* — The housing MD reinforced keeping the overlapping business inside one team for productivity — a cross-sell and field-efficiency argument against separating home loans from LAP. “So from that perspective also and what Rajiv added, it makes a lot of sense for the same team which sources the home loans to also look at LAP because it improves the productivity on the field.”
- *CALL Apr 2026* — On the merged Motor Finance business, management reports integration benefits realised — approvals in Q1 FY26, break-even in Q3, INR43 crores PAT in Q4, non-Tata OEM share 26%, ~95% of legacy borrowings repriced — framing the entity as retained and improving, with growth resuming in H1 FY27. “So I would say the overall strategy which we had put in place where we wanted to make this business extremely profitable for us over the next three years, that's very well in motion.”

*Not explained on the calls:* Everything about a separation: no such transaction, business, rationale, timeline, investor/lender/partner demand, valuation or capital argument appears anywhere in these calls or filings.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Solutions Infini Technologies (India) Private Limited's Non-licensed Business undertaking, demerged into fellow wholly-owned subsidiary Novamesh Limited — class `regulatory_strategic`.

- *Insiders:* Not stated beyond: 'Details of benefit, if any, to the promoter / promoter group / group companies from such proposed restructuring — Not Applicable'; all three entities remain wholly-owned subsidiaries
- *What it reveals:* Nothing reaches listed shareholders — ownership and beneficial economic interest are unchanged. It reveals only that the CPaaS/messaging stack (Solutions Infini, Novamesh, Kaleyra) is being consolidated; no asset values or segment numbers for the Non-licensed Business are given

- *Parent or spin:* neither · *option pricing date:* not stated

- *In their words:* “All the three entities involved in the Scheme are wholly-owned subsidiaries of Tata Communications Limited.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

On the texts supplied, the only 'separation' Tata Communications has actually filed is intra-group, not a shareholder-level spin-off: a composite scheme of arrangement (intimated 22 January 2026) demerging the Non-licensed Business undertaking of Solutions Infini Technologies (India) Private Limited into Novamesh Limited, after which Solutions Infini is amalgamated into Tata Communications Collaboration Services Private Limited and ceases to exist, with an Appointed Date of 1 April 2025. All three entities are wholly-owned subsidiaries of TATACOMM, so the stated rationale is structural rather than strategic: operational synergies, centralisation, simplification and streamlining, 'reduction of administrative costs and productivity gains by pooling of financial, managerial and technical resources', 'enhanced potential for higher revenues and profits' for the transferee and surviving companies via rationalisation of the management and administrative structure, and removal of 'the multiplicity of legal and other regulatory compliances' plus the running costs and overheads of operating in separate entities. The split line is drawn on licence status — only the Non-licensed Business undertaking is carved into Novamesh — but the filing never explains that choice. The same simplification programme runs through the Kaleyra structure acquired in 2023: TATACOMM transferred 100% of Kaleyra, Inc. to Tata Communications (Netherlands) B.V. and merged Kaleyra, Inc. into Kaleyra US Inc. on 31 October 2026, 'aimed at simplifying and consolidating the ownership structure of the Tata Communications’ Group' with no change in ultimate beneficial ownership or economic interest; BUC Mobile, Inc. (FY25 turnover ₹766.70 crore, 3.32%; net worth ₹790.15 crore, 12.87%, contracts moved to Kaleyra US Inc. by Asset Transfer Agreement effective 1 February 2025) was dissolved 16 February 2026, Campaign Registry, Inc. on 14 January 2026 and Kaleyra Africa (Pty) Limited on 4 September 2026. The earnings calls never discuss this scheme; what they do explain is the adjacent portfolio clean-up — exiting non-core assets that were 'tying our balance sheet and management time' (TCPSL/ATM business, Netfoundry, land parcels, TCTS turnaround), creating UK and Netherlands subsidiaries as tax-efficient acquisition vehicles, redomiciling the subsea cable entity from Bermuda to Switzerland to preserve roughly $400 million of NOLs, and the ₪900 crore FY25 digital-portfolio loss management wants converted into ₹2,300 crore of EBITDA. No investor, lender or partner is recorded anywhere as asking for the separation.

**How it evolved:** The idea is visible only as a general 'strategic review of all our assets' theme: Apr 2025 (Q4 FY25 call) framed FY25 as a year of interventions — TCPSL disposal, land monetisation, action on Netfoundry, TCTS profitability — to shift away from non-core businesses; Jun 2025 (Investor Day) extended it to entity architecture, with UK/Netherlands acquisition vehicles, the Bermuda-to-Switzerland subsea redomicile, and a promise that under-performing units would keep being reviewed and funding pulled. Aug 2025 (Q2 FY26 call, held 15 Oct 2025) added rightsizing of 'two of our businesses internally within Tata Comm and for our one of our subsidiaries as well'. The Solutions Infini demerger then appears abruptly in the 22 January 2026 filing, one day after the Jan 2026 call whose transcript here is only a cover letter, and the Kaleyra legal-entity consolidation follows through 2026 (Feb, Sep, 31 Oct 2026) — so the plan never changed on a call, it only surfaced in filings.

**What management expects from it:** Scheme only: Novamesh and Tata Communications Collaboration Services gain pooled resources, a rationalised management structure, 'enhanced potential for higher revenues and profits', and lower compliance, running and administrative costs; Solutions Infini ceases to exist. All stay wholly-owned, so TATACOMM's economic interest is unchanged and no margin, capital-release or valuation effect is quantified. Calls separately target digital breakeven and ₹2,300 crore EBITDA.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The transaction is a two-step composite scheme: Solutions Infini's Non-licensed Business undertaking demerges into Novamesh Limited, then Solutions Infini amalgamates into Tata Communications Collaboration Services Private Limited, Appointed Date 1 April 2025, to be filed with the Mumbai NCLT. “Tata Communications Limited has been informed that a composite scheme of arrangement for the demerger of Solutions Infini Technologies (India) Private Limited's (‘Transferor Company’) Non-licensed Business undertaking into Novamesh Limited (‘Transferee Company’) and the subsequent amalgamation of the Transferor Company into Tata Communications Collaboration Services Private Limited (‘Surviving Company’) (‘Scheme’) has been approved by the respective board of directors of all the entities involved in the Scheme.”
- *Scheme* — The stated benefit is cost and administrative: pooling resources across the entities to cut administrative cost and gain productivity. “operational synergies, centralisation, simplification, streamlining and facilitation of efficient administration and reduction of administrative costs and productivity gains by pooling of financial, managerial and technical resources, personnel capabilities, skills, expertise and technologies of the entities;”
- *Scheme* — The problem named is duplicated compliance and the overhead of running the same businesses through separate legal entities. “the Scheme would remove the multiplicity of legal and other regulatory compliances, required to be carried out by the Transferor Company, Transferee Company, and the Surviving Company separately and significantly reduce the various running costs and overheads involved in running the businesses in separate entities;”
- *Scheme* — Because all three companies are wholly-owned, there is no change in TATACOMM's ownership: the transferee and surviving companies stay wholly-owned and Solutions Infini disappears. “All the three entities involved in the Scheme are wholly-owned subsidiaries of Tata Communications Limited.”
- *Scheme* — The Kaleyra leg (Oct 2026 filing) is explicitly ownership-structure simplification with no economic effect: Kaleyra, Inc. moved under Tata Communications (Netherlands) B.V. and merged into Kaleyra US Inc. “The aforesaid transactions form part of an intra-group restructuring aimed at simplifying and consolidating the ownership structure of the Tata Communications’ Group and does not result in any change in the ultimate beneficial ownership and beneficial economic interest of the Company in Kaleyra Group entities.”
- *Scheme* — The only sized entity in the whole programme is BUC Mobile, Inc., dissolved 16 February 2026 after its contracts were transferred to Kaleyra US Inc. effective 1 February 2025. “Turnover (FY25): ₹ 766.70 crore (3.32%) Net worth (FY25): ₹ 790.15 crore (12.87%)”
- *[Apr 2025](https://gamma.tatacommunications.com/assets/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/q4-fy2025-earning-call-transcript.pdf)* — Kabir Shakir framed FY25's disposals (TCPSL, land, Netfoundry, TCTS) around one theme — releasing balance sheet and management bandwidth from non-core units into the data business. “At the heart of these interventions is one underlying theme shifting focus away from non-core businesses that was tying our balance sheet and management time.”
- *[Jun 2025](https://gamma.tatacommunications.com/assets/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/institutional-investors-and-analysts-meet-2025-transcript.pdf)* — At the Investor Day, Shakir described the entity-level engineering behind the restructuring: UK and Netherlands step-down subsidiaries converted into direct, tax-efficient acquisition vehicles — the Netherlands entity that later received Kaleyra, Inc. “We made them direct subsidiaries with the intent of them becoming acquisition vehicles.”
- *[Jun 2025](https://gamma.tatacommunications.com/assets/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/institutional-investors-and-analysts-meet-2025-transcript.pdf)* — The same call showed tax as a driver of intra-group moves, citing roughly $400 million of NOLs preserved by redomiciling the subsea cable entity out of Bermuda ahead of BEPS 2.0. “close to $400 million is what we have preserved by moving, you know, that entity from Bermuda to Switzerland.”
- *[Jun 2025](https://gamma.tatacommunications.com/assets/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/institutional-investors-and-analysts-meet-2025-transcript.pdf)* — Shakir distinguished units to be exited outright from the digital portfolio being kept and fixed, and quantified the digital drag for the first time: a ~₹900 crore FY25 loss to be turned into ₹2,300 crore of EBITDA. “It is not a Netfoundry. It is not a ATM business where we are saying we want they are not making money. We want to get rid of them.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.tatacommunications.com/hubfs/Quarterly%20report/q2-fy2026-earning-call-transcript.pdf)* — Rightsizing was extended to subsidiaries, with an exceptional item in PAT for reshaping operating models — the operational counterpart to the later legal-entity consolidation. “There is an exceptional item that we have in PAT, and one of the reasons why that PAT dropped as well, that is to right size some of our businesses, including our subsidiary as well from an operating model perspective.”
- *[Apr 2026](https://www.tatacommunications.com/hubfs/Quarterly%20report/q4-fy2026-earning-call-transcript.pdf)* — The one separation investors did ask about was the 26% STT Telemedia stake; Shakir said rights were secured and an IPO is the lead monetisation route, pending deal closure — unrelated to the Scheme. “We have engaged with STT and we have engaged with the new buyer and secured our rights on the monetisation of which IPO is the lead option.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No call ever mentions the demerger: no size of Solutions Infini or Novamesh, no licensed-versus-non-licensed logic, no timeline, NCLT status, cost saving, or requesting party; Jan 2026 transcript missing.

*Calls read (36 months):* [Oct 2024](https://gamma.tatacommunications.com/assets/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/q2-fy2025-earning-call-transcript.pdf)

## THYROCARE — Thyrocare Technologies Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a scheme of arrangement whose nature the documents on file do not settle) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 2.5/10 · scheme (nature unclear) · 3 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-09-21, latest 2026-09-21

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**Stated in the filings:** size hint: 5.38% of turnover.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Nueclear Healthcare Limited's radiology and diagnostic imaging business, sold 100% to Trovera Healthcare Private Limited — class `bad_business`.

- *Insiders:* Trovera does not belong to the promoter/promoter group; promoter group has no interest in it. Thyrocare itself retains 42,500 CCPS, ~4.5% of Trovera fully diluted. Promoter Docon/API holds 51.02% of Thyrocare, now fully unpledged.
- *What it reveals:* NHL is 14.27% of consolidated net worth but only 5.38% of turnover, PAT margin 10.9% vs 19.2% standalone; sold for Rs 141.4 crore vs net worth Rs 83.55 crore, leaving a higher-return pathology parent plus a 4.5% IPO-linked CCPS stake.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — No shares are distributed to shareholders; consideration is cash plus unlisted Trovera CCPS retained by the Company itself.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* The share purchase agreement intimation when executed, plus the Regulation 37A special-resolution notice with the NHL valuation report.
- *In their words:* “This will enable the Company to focus its capital and management attention on its core pathology business.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The business being separated is the radiology / diagnostic-imaging arm held in wholly-owned subsidiary Nueclear Healthcare Limited (NHL) — PET-CT and CT imaging centres, nuclear-medicine diagnostics and radiopharmaceuticals made in medical cyclotron facilities — leaving Thyrocare a pure pathology company. Management's core reason is return on capital: Guha said the nuclear business 'has not been growing' and that Thyrocare had deliberately not invested in it, 'being fairly conservative looking at the return on capital profile of that business versus our pathology business' — a new PET-CT centre costs about INR10 crores (Apr 2025), the carrying investment is about INR140 crores, and it delivered only INR1.72 crores PAT in Q1 FY27 with 'INR6 crores PAT... for the year, not more', against a pathology business whose ROCE rose from 15% in FY23 to 34% in FY26 and EBITDA from 23% to 32%. The filings quantify the mismatch: FY26 NHL turnover of Rs 44.62 crore was only 5.38% of consolidated turnover yet its net worth of Rs 83.55 crore was 14.27% of consolidated net worth, and NHL's PAT margin was 10.9% versus 19.2% standalone. The Scheme rationale is that radiology 'requires continued investment in diagnostic equipment, technology, maintenance and infrastructure', and exiting 'will enable the Company to focus its capital and management attention on its core pathology business' — the same logic behind earlier steps of closing a loss-making centre, 'foregoing unprofitable growth' and consolidating centres, which cut radiology revenue 6% in FY26 and 4% YoY in Q1 FY27 while improving its bottom line, and had pulled consolidated growth to 18% in Q3 FY26 versus 20% for pathology. Rather than keep funding it, Guha wanted 'a partner who is ready to invest into the nuclear business and grow it and give us better dividends than how it is right now'. The agreed structure keeps a sliver of that upside: Rs 141.40 crore total — Rs 81.90 crore cash (working-capital adjusted) plus 42,500 CCPS of Trovera Healthcare Pvt Ltd at Rs 14,000 each (Rs 59.50 crore, ~4.5% fully diluted, 1:1 convertible on an IPO filing or after 20 years) — valued by V. B. Desai Financial Services and Raj Pradip Shroff, with Thyrocare separately buying its own Gurugram and Hyderabad lab premises out of NHL for Rs 20.59 crore so the pathology labs it currently rents from NHL stay with it. No lender or partner is shown demanding the exit; the only external push on record is an InCred analyst congratulating the board because 'the segment has been dilutive to the consolidated return ratios', while at the parent level API was separately 'selling nonstrategic assets' to cut debt from INR1,700 crores to INR1,050 crores — a link management never drew to NHL.

**How it evolved:** Through Oct 2024 radiology was still a growth line (+21% YoY) with mid-teen guidance, and in Apr 2025 management reversed an INR11.2 crore deferred-tax provision originally created against an NHL impairment precisely because 'NHL business is doing good', while refusing to add INR10-crore centres. The tone turned in Oct 2025 ('the Radiology business last year was loss making... a drag on our overall bottom line'), Feb 2026 (radiology pulled consolidated growth to 18% against 20% pathology) and May 2026 ('strategic consolidation of centers', FY26 radiology revenue -6% but better bottom line). On July 23, 2026 the board gave in-principle approval to evaluate a demerger/slump sale of NHL's radiology undertaking outside the group, and on the same day's call Guha said he had 'just took approval', expected roughly 6 months and had 'no definitive... buyer at this point in time'. On September 21, 2026 the board approved the outright sale of 100% of NHL to Trovera Healthcare Pvt Ltd for ~Rs 141.40 crore (cash plus Trovera CCPS), plus the buy-back of the Gurugram and Hyderabad lab properties, targeted for completion by November 30, 2026.

**What management expects from it:** Thyrocare becomes pure-play pathology with capital and management attention on it: no further imaging equipment/technology capex, exit of a segment dilutive to return ratios (standalone PAT margin 19.2% vs NHL 10.9%; ROCE already 15%→34% FY23-FY26), release of ~14% of consolidated net worth for ~5% of revenue, plus Rs 81.9 crore cash and retained ~4.5% Trovera upside; NHL gets an owner willing to invest, grow it and pay better dividends.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Jul 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=c3d826e4-58a3-4476-b5f0-b486f3ada8fc.pdf)* — Guha gave the first public rationale on the same day as board approval: NHL had not been growing and Thyrocare had chosen not to invest because its return-on-capital profile was inferior to pathology. “We have been fairly conservative looking at the return on capital profile of that business versus our pathology business.”
- *[Jul 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=c3d826e4-58a3-4476-b5f0-b486f3ada8fc.pdf)* — He framed the exit as handing the asset to someone willing to fund it, rather than Thyrocare funding growth itself. “So therefore, we felt -- let us see if there is a partner who is ready to invest into the nuclear business and grow it and give us better dividends than how it is right now.”
- *[Jul 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=c3d826e4-58a3-4476-b5f0-b486f3ada8fc.pdf)* — At the time of the in-principle approval there was no counterparty identified and the process was expected to run about six months (it in fact signed two months later). “I anticipate the process will take 6 months, right? But we don't have any definitive what you call buyer at this point in time.”
- *[Jul 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=c3d826e4-58a3-4476-b5f0-b486f3ada8fc.pdf)* — Sizing the drag: about INR140 crores of capital employed in NHL generating INR1.72 crores PAT in Q1 FY27 and an expected INR6 crores for the full year. “See, first quarter, we did about INR 1.72 crores PAT. I think INR 6 crores PAT is what we can expect for the year, not more.”
- *[Jul 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=c3d826e4-58a3-4476-b5f0-b486f3ada8fc.pdf)* — The only external voice on record pushing the idea was an InCred analyst, who congratulated the board for stepping away from a return-dilutive segment. “The segment has been dilutive to the consolidated return ratios.”
- *[Jul 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=c3d826e4-58a3-4476-b5f0-b486f3ada8fc.pdf)* — Radiology revenue fell 4% YoY on centre consolidation even as profitability improved, and reporting was recast to show NHL plus Pulse Hitech together. “On a year -on-year basis, core revenue declined by 4%, primarily due to the consolidation of centers.”
- *[Jul 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=c3d826e4-58a3-4476-b5f0-b486f3ada8fc.pdf)* — Separately, Guha described group-level asset monetisation to cut API's debt from INR1,700 crores to INR1,050 crores ahead of any API IPO — context he never explicitly connected to the NHL sale. “And as you -- if you have been following, we have been, what you call, selling nonstrategic assets, seeing what all options are there to monetize to bring down the right?”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=d3b11bca-8f94-4b5e-aa89-8763849fb974.pdf)* — Radiology was already being shrunk deliberately: centres consolidated during FY26, revenue down 6% for the year, but a stronger bottom line. “In radiology, as covered in earlier calls also, we undertook some strategic consolidation of centers during the year.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=06ece0c5-d914-459e-98fa-9e84c03be7e6.pdf)* — Radiology was openly identified as the reason consolidated growth (18%) lagged pathology (20%). “Our radiology business is what has pulled it down to 18%, right?”
- *[Oct 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=15c309fa-b64b-4370-a22b-af1c58d156c0.pdf)* — Management stated radiology had been loss-making the prior year and a drag, and that it had chosen to forgo unprofitable growth, closing a non-profitable centre and raising realisation per scan. “But the Radiology business last year was loss making, right, and a drag on our overall bottom line.”
- *[Apr 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=fb9de534-ff06-4e6b-801d-72d3f049b8ba.pdf)* — Capital discipline was already explicit: no new imaging centres because each costs about INR10 crores, only price-led margin repair. “At this point, we are not contemplating filling up new centers and Nueclear .”
- *[Apr 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=fb9de534-ff06-4e6b-801d-72d3f049b8ba.pdf)* — An eventual sale of the NHL investment had been contemplated in accounting terms since the 2019-20 impairment; the INR11.2 crore deferred-tax asset was reversed in Q4 FY25 because NHL had turned around. “And whenever we are -- if we are going to sell that investment, the impairment loss -- against the impairment loss, the deferment tax benefits are going to come.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No quantified post-exit ROCE/EPS or margin impact, no use of proceeds, no Trovera background or CCPS liquidity/exit terms, no staff, centre or Pulse Hitech continuity detail.

## TORNTPOWER — Torrent Power Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a scheme of arrangement whose nature the documents on file do not settle) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 2.5/10 · scheme (nature unclear) · 2 filing(s) from NSE · first 2025-11-11, latest 2025-11-11

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** The Renewable Power Undertakings (316.60 MW solar and wind) transferred to wholly owned subsidiary Torrent Green Energy Private Limited — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* Transferee is a wholly owned subsidiary of Torrent Power; Torrent Investments Limited is named Holding Company and Promoter of Torrent Power. No promoter/management stake or incentive in the transferee stated.
- *What it reveals:* Renewables is the highest-margin segment: H1 FY27 segment results ₹754.74 Cr on revenue ₹945.41 Cr, but carries segment assets ₹20,479.72 Cr against liabilities ₹12,845.37 Cr — a capital-intensive, debt-funded growth arm now housed outside the parent's standalone books.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — Transfer to a wholly owned subsidiary by slump sale for cash (₹694.05 Crore consideration); no shares distributed to shareholders, no separate listing stated.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* The Scheme of Arrangement and NCLT orders dated January 27, 2025 / February 18, 2025, plus Renewables segment assets and liabilities.
- *In their words:* “The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) vide its Order dated January 27, 2025, subsequently modified vide order dated February 18, 2025 (received on March 07, 2025), has sanctioned the Scheme of Arrangement ("Scheme") for transfer and vesting of "the Renewable Power Undertakings" (comprises of 316.60 MW of solar and wind power) of the Company to Torrent Green Energy Private Limited (TGEPL), a wholly owned subsidiary (incorporated w.e.f. August 02, 2023) of the Company, on a going concern basis by way of slump sale with effect from the appointed date i.e. April 01, 2024 under sections 230 to 232 and other applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 2013.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

These texts contain no management explanation of the separation. Across the five extractable calls (May 14 2025, Aug 5 2025, Nov 11 2025, Feb 10 2026, May 13 2026) neither Saurabh Mashruwala nor Rishi Shah mentions the demerger and no analyst asks about it; the six earlier calls (Nov 2023–Feb 2025), i.e. exactly the window in which it was conceived and sanctioned, are scanned PDFs with no extractable text. The only description of the separation anywhere in this record is Note 2 to the November 11 2025 results and Price Waterhouse's emphasis paragraph, and both give mechanics, not motive: NCLT (order January 27 2025, modified February 18 2025, received March 7 2025) sanctioned a Scheme of Arrangement under sections 230–232 transferring 'the Renewable Power Undertakings' — 316.60 MW of solar and wind — out of Torrent Power Ltd into Torrent Green Energy Private Limited (TGEPL), a wholly owned subsidiary incorporated August 2 2023, on a going concern basis by way of slump sale, appointed date April 1 2024, effective April 1 2025 on ROC filing, with slump-sale consideration of ₹121.56 cr (H1 FY25), ₹186.07 cr (FY25) and ₹694.05 cr (H1 FY26). No tax, lender, partner, valuation or focus reason is stated, and no investor, lender or partner is named as having asked for it. What the filings do establish — without management ascribing it as the reason — is a subsidiary-housed renewable growth vehicle: Renewables is a separate Ind AS 108 segment (Q2 FY26 revenue ₹326.62 cr, result ₹281.37 cr, assets ₹12,172.51 cr, liabilities ₹7,636.35 cr, rising to assets ₹20,479.72 cr and liabilities ₹12,845.37 cr by Sept 30 2026); all new renewable capacity sits in subsidiaries (dozens of Torrent Urja SPVs under TGEPL; the Nov 2025 call notes a 250 MW FDRE LOA won by 'subsidiary of the company'); and the parent funds them by equity and loans (standalone investments in subsidiaries ₹1,655.07 cr at Mar-25 → ₹5,083.14 cr at Sep-25 → ₹12,864.06 cr at Sep-26), against renewable capex of ₹2,500 cr (FY25), ₹7,000–8,000 cr planned and ₹6,500 cr spent (FY26), a 4 GW/₹28,000 cr pipeline inside a ~₹80,000 cr five-year plan, after a maiden ₹3,500 cr QIP. Two further separations sit in the same window: the Power Cable business left the T&D segment on October 16 2024 (₹77 cr non-recurring gain, flagged in the Feb 2026 call), and on March 30 2026 three pumped-storage SPVs were moved under Torrent Energy Storage Solutions Private Limited while UNM Foundation was sold up to promoter Torrent Investments Limited for ₹5,00,000.

**How it evolved:** The idea never surfaces in any call that is readable here: the extractable transcripts begin with Q4 FY25 (May 14 2025), after the Scheme was already effective (April 1 2025), and the Nov 2023, Feb 2024, May 2024, Jul 2024, Nov 2024 and Feb 2025 calls — spanning TGEPL's incorporation (Aug 2 2023), the April 1 2024 appointed date and the January 27 2025 NCLT order — are image-only PDFs. The first and only trace in this record is retrospective: Note 2 and the auditor's emphasis paragraph in the November 11 2025 filing, which also restate the Sept 30 2024 comparatives. The plan's only visible later movement is structural rather than explanatory: the Feb 10 2026 call books the cable-business exit as a prior-year one-off, and the March 30 2026 filings reorganise the pumped-storage SPVs under one holding subsidiary and push UNM Foundation up to the promoter; by the May 13 2026 call management discusses renewables purely as capex and commissioning, never as a separated entity.

**What management expects from it:** Nothing is stated. In these texts management never describes any expected effect of the separation on margins, capital, valuation or focus for either Torrent Power or Torrent Green Energy. The only disclosed consequences are accounting ones: restated FY25 comparatives (H1 PBT ₹1,942.38 cr to ₹1,869.16 cr) and slump-sale consideration of ₹121.56 cr, ₹186.07 cr and ₹694.05 cr.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The sole substantive description of the separation: NCLT-sanctioned Scheme moving 316.60 MW of solar and wind out of the listed parent into wholly owned TGEPL by slump sale, appointed date April 1 2024, under sections 230–232. “The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) vide its Order dated January 27, 2025, subsequently modified vide order dated February 18, 2025 (received on March 07, 2025), has sanctioned the Scheme of Arrangement ("Scheme") for transfer and vesting of "the Renewable Power Undertakings" (comprises of 316.60 MW of solar and wind power) of the Company to Torrent Green Energy Private Limited (TGEPL), a wholly owned subsidiary (incorporated w.e.f. August 02, 2023) of the Company, on a going concern basis by way of slump sale with effect from the appointed date i.e. April 01, 2024 under sections 230 to 232 and other applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 2013.”
- *Scheme* — The auditor flags the Scheme as an emphasis matter, confirming it is a parent-to-wholly-owned-subsidiary transfer of the renewable power undertaking, not a sale to a third party; conclusion unmodified. “We draw your attention to Note 2 to the Statement which describes that the Scheme of Arrangement (the "Scheme") between the Company and Torrent Green Energy Private Limited (the "Transferee Company") for transfer of the Company's renewable power undertaking to the Transferee Company, which has been approved by the National Company Law Tribunal ("NCLT") vide its order dated January 27, 2025, subsequently modified vide order dated February 18, 2025 (received on March 07, 2025).”
- *Scheme* — Only quantified effect disclosed anywhere: standalone comparatives were restated downward — Q2 FY25 PBT ₹669.32 cr to ₹641.42 cr and H1 FY25 PBT ₹1,942.38 cr to ₹1,869.16 cr — showing roughly ₹73 cr of half-year PBT left the parent. “The reported figures for the comparative quarter and six months ended September 30, 2024 without giving effect of the Scheme and the figures after giving effect of the Scheme are provided below:”
- *Scheme* — The parent received cash consideration for the slump sale in instalments — ₹121.56 cr in H1 FY25, ₹186.07 cr in FY25 and ₹694.05 cr in H1 FY26 — but no basis or purpose for the consideration is explained. “Consideration received on slump sale (Refer note 2) 694.05 121.56 186.07”
- *Scheme* — Renewables is reported as its own segment, and the subsidiary list shows TGEPL as a direct subsidiary sitting above dozens of Torrent Urja / Saurya Urja SPVs, i.e. the carve-out created the apex of an existing SPV stack. “Renewables: Comprises of generation of power from renewable energy sources i.e. wind and solar.”
- *Scheme* — A second, earlier separation is visible only in the segment note: the Power Cable business was removed from Transmission and Distribution with effect from October 16 2024. “Transmission and Distribution: Comprises of transmission and distribution business (licensed and franchisee) and related ancillary services. It also comprises Power Cable business till October 16, 2024.”
- *Feb 2026* — The cable-business exit is quantified only as a prior-year one-off gain of ₹77 crore in Q3 FY25 PBT; management gives no reason for the disposal. “PBT for the corresponding quarter of the last include nonrecurring income of INR77 crores on account of sale of cable business.”
- *Scheme* — Further intra-group reorganisation on March 30 2026: three pumped-storage SPVs (Torrent Energy Storage Solutions 1/2/3), all with negative net worth, were sold for ₹1,00,000 each into Torrent Energy Storage Solutions Private Limited, creating a single storage holding entity for the 3 GW PSP. “the Company has sold Equity shares of various Wholly-owned Subsidiaries as mentioned in Annexure – A to one of its Wholly-owned subsidiary Company viz. Torrent Energy Storage Solutions Private Limited on today i.e. March 30, 2026 at 03:16 pm.”
- *Scheme* — Same day, the Section 8 CSR vehicle UNM Foundation was pushed out of the listed company up to the promoter/holding company Torrent Investments Limited for ₹5,00,000, a related-party transaction stated to be at arm's length. “the Company has sold 50,000 Equity Shares at face value of ₹ 10 each for a total consideration of ₹ 5,00,000/ - of UNM Foundation (Section 8 Company) ("UNM") to Holding Company of the Company viz. Torrent Investments Limited on today i.e. March 30, 2026 at 05:40 pm.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.torrentpower.com/public/pdf/investors/TorrentPower-Earnings-Nov11-2025.pdf)* — Confirms new renewable awards now land in the subsidiary rather than the parent — a 250 MW FDRE LOA from the company's own licensed distribution unit was won by a subsidiary. “During the quarter, in addition to our existing renewable pipeline, subsidiary of the company received LOA of 250 MW of FDRE Renewable Generation from our licensed distribution unit.”
- *Feb 2026* — Scale of the ambition housed in the separated renewable vehicle: a stated aspiration of 10 GW of renewable capacity, against roughly 2 GW installed. “As we have stated earlier also, I think our aspiration is to reach a 10 gigawatts of renewable capacities, which we look at it.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.torrentpower.com/public/pdf/investors//TorrentPower-Earnings-Aug05-2025.pdf)* — Renewable capital intensity flowing into the carved-out structure: ₹7,000–8,000 crore planned for FY26 and more in FY27, financed at 70:30 or 75:25 debt-equity per the Feb 2026 call. “So for '26, it should be around INR7,000 crores to INR8,000 crores for this year and slightly higher number for next year.”

*Not explained on the calls:* Everything about motive: no stated tax, lender, partner, valuation, listing or focus rationale; no requester named; no consideration basis; no per-entity targets. The 2023–Feb 2025 calls are unextractable.

## BLUESTONE — BlueStone Jewellery and Lifestyle Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a subsidiary's listing is in motion (DRHP / board approval)) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 2.1/10 · partial spin-off / listing · 2 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-09-02, latest 2026-09-02

> **Listing:** IPO / listing of the subsidiary in motion since 2026-09-02; date not fixed

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** not stated — no demerger, spin-off or subsidiary listing is described in these documents — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* Only subsidiary mentioned: lab-grown brand Ethereal, BlueStone holds 74%, rest with founders Nitesh and Sharad; no new-entity stakes stated
- *What it reveals:* No separation disclosed. Documents instead show a 74%-owned lab-grown-diamond subsidiary (Ethereal) run founder-led, and ESOPs where ~90% sit with the top six managers
- *Selling pressure:* unclear — No spin-off shares exist; only a 360 ONE staggered open-market sale of 35,13,672 parent shares on September 24, 2026
- *Parent or spin:* unclear · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Ethereal subsidiary disclosures and any Scheme of Arrangement board outcome; none present in these filings
- *In their words:* “So, Ethereal, which is our subsidiary, we have 74% holding in that, but rest of the equity is with the founders, Nitesh and Sharad.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

On the evidence supplied, there is no business separation to reconstruct: across all six transcripts (Sep 2025, Nov 2025, Jan 2026, Apr 2026, Jul 2026) and all four filings (Dec 2025 postal ballot, two Sep 2026 board/CS items, Sep 2026 Reg 29(2) disclosure), BlueStone's management never announces, discusses or is asked about a demerger, spin-off, hive-off, slump sale or scheme of arrangement of any business, and no scheme document, record date, share-entitlement ratio, NCLT filing or Reg 30 intimation of one appears. The word 'Scheme' in the filings refers only to the BlueStone Jewellery and Lifestyle Limited - Employee Stock Option Plan 2014, which the Dec 26, 2025 postal ballot asks shareholders to ratify post-IPO under Regulation 12 of the SEBI SBEB Regulations (pool 1,17,27,642 options, less 15,00,243 already exercised and listed, leaving 1,02,27,399 granted plus ungranted), and the Sep 2, 2026 board outcome merely allots 29,305 ESOP shares (capital to Rs.15,27,78,705) and appoints Mandar Godbole as Company Secretary. The only ownership change disclosed is a financial investor sell-down: 360 ONE Alternates Asset Management's sixteen funds sold 35,13,672 shares in the open market on Sep 24, 2026, taking their stake from 1,05,31,448 shares (6.89%) to 70,17,776 (4.59%) - a stake sale, not a business separation. What management does describe repeatedly is the opposite of separation at the operating level: 95% in-house manufacturing is kept deliberately because 'in a vendor-driven ecosystem... your designs eventually get dissipated', online and stores are 'one continuous journey' with 80%+ of sales originating online, and the stated plan is one integrated company going from INR2,441 crore FY26 revenue to INR12,000 crore in four years at 20% store CAGR and 7.5%-to-15% pre-IndAS EBITDA. The nearest structural unwinding discussed is the franchisee estate - 67 of 340 stores at Mar 2026 - which was only ever 'a capital access or a capital structure tool' / 'mezz financing' at 12-15% minimum guarantee and is being consolidated from FOCO into COCO because it is 'a very expensive capital structure... related to what our cost of capital is', with the drop concentrated in FY27 and FY28 while five-year contracts are honoured. The other separately-held entity mentioned is Ethereal, the lab-grown-diamond subsidiary in which BlueStone holds 74% with founders Nitesh and Sharad holding the rest and running it at arm's length - held separately from inception, with no indication it is being carved out of, or into, anything.

**How it evolved:** No separation idea surfaces or evolves anywhere in these texts. The only structural thread that moves call to call is the franchisee unwind: Sep 5, 2025 - franchises stopped and contracts being exited (75 of 292 stores, settlement costs in franchisee expense); Nov 4, 2025 - no structural discussion at all, only the IPO equity raise; Jan 22, 2026 - FOCO-to-COCO consolidation confirmed as continuing and 'PAT accretive', and Ethereal described as a 74%-held founder-run subsidiary receiving more money; Apr 24, 2026 - 67 franchisee stores, exits not accelerated, FY27-FY28 to see a 'substantial drop', with FOFO floated only hypothetically as a way to push gold inventory onto other balance sheets; Jul 21, 2026 - franchisees not mentioned, and vertical integration defended as strategic and permanent.

**What management expects from it:** Nothing is stated, because no separation is disclosed. For the one structural change they do discuss - converting franchise (FOCO) stores to company-owned (COCO) - Dugar says the franchise structure is expensive against BlueStone's cost of capital and the consolidation is PAT accretive, with the substantial drop in FY27-FY28; franchisees are treated as a capital-structure tool, not an operating segment.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — No scheme of arrangement exists in the filings; the only 'Scheme' is the 2014 ESOP plan, put to a postal ballot (remote e-voting Dec 27, 2025 to Jan 25, 2026) purely for post-IPO ratification under SEBI SBEB Regulation 12 before fresh grants. “Therefore, in terms of Regulation 12 of the SEBI SBEB Regulations, the Scheme is required to be ratified by the Shareholders of the Company prior to making any fresh grants under the Scheme, and accordingly the same is referred to the Shareholders for their ratification.”
- *Scheme* — The only September 2026 ownership event disclosed is a financial investor's open-market sell-down by 360 ONE's sixteen funds, cutting their holding from 6.89% to 4.59% - not any separation of a business. “This is to inform you that the Company has received a disclosure dated September 28, 2026 from 360 One Alternates Asset Management Limited Shareholder of the Company pursuant to Regulation 29 (2) of the SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011 in respect of sale of 35,13,672 Equity Shares of the Company through the open Market on September 24, 2026.”

## CCAVENUE — AvenuesAI Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a subsidiary's listing is in motion (DRHP / board approval)) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 2.1/10 · partial spin-off / listing · 1 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-03-31, latest 2026-03-31

> **Listing:** IPO / listing of the subsidiary in motion since 2026-03-31; date not fixed

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Rediff.com India Limited, the subsidiary holding the e-commerce platform, content and consumer digital business, via IPO — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* Rediff is a subsidiary of AvenuesAI; Vishal Mehta is Chairman and Managing Director of AvenuesAI Limited and Rediff.com. Promoter/management stake and incentives in Rediff: not stated.
- *What it reveals:* A small, high-margin business hidden inside a huge low-margin payments consolidation: H1 FY27 E-Commerce Platform revenue INR 1,112.6mn gave segment profit INR 515.0mn, versus Payment Business INR 54,483.8mn revenue for only INR 821.3mn.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — An IPO, not a demerger: no Rediff shares are distributed to CCAVENUE holders. Offer size and structure not stated.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Rediff's Pre-DRHP for standalone revenue, EBITDA and offer structure; meanwhile the E-Commerce Platform segment result.
- *In their words:* “The filing of the Pre-filed Draft Red Herring Prospectus shall not necessarily mean that Rediff will undertake the initial public offering.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The separation is the carve-out of Infibeam Avenues' e-commerce platform infrastructure business (the GeM-style enterprise commerce software framework licensed to Jio, Saudi Telecom and ~7 other enterprises) out of the listed parent and into its subsidiary Rediff.com India Limited, approved by the Board on August 8, 2025 as a slump sale for INR 800 crores, with Rediff subsequently filing for its own IPO (Pre-DRHP March 31, 2026; confidential DRHP referenced on the Jun 2026 call). Management framed it under the theme of "platform convergence": the platform business, while "extremely strong on its own," would deliver "even greater value when paired with Rediff's enterprise ecosystem," for four stated reasons — (1) framework fit, because Rediff's RediffOne stack (Rediffmail enterprise email, RediffPay, ERP/CRM/HRMS productivity suite) is "purpose-built for productivity, CRM and ERP" and adding e-commerce "completes the entire circle"; (2) go-to-market, because Rediff already has "long-standing relationships with thousands of businesses" (20,000+ enterprise email customers, 100mn+ registered users, 0.5–1bn emails/day) giving "immediate access to trusted distribution channels perfect for bundling, upselling and scaling quickly"; (3) brand, Rediff's two-decade legacy and credibility in India and globally; and (4) retained control, with Infibeam keeping "more than 80% equity control of Rediff" (and "significantly more than 50%" even after Rediff's own fundraise). The investor case was stated as "financial clarity" and "business focus" through "2 powerful independent scalable verticals": Infibeam/AvenuesAI as a pure-play fintech and AI payments company (CCAvenue plus Phronetic.AI), and Rediff as the AI-first consumer/enterprise platform (commerce, content via Rediff TV, RediffPay UPI), which management said made Infibeam "compared apple to apple with any payment company, whether it is a Pine Labs or a Paytm." The consideration was structured half-and-half: INR 400 crores as 28% additional equity in Rediff (Rediff itself fair-valued at INR 300–400 crores, "maybe a factor more than what we had invested in earlier," against the ~INR 100 crore 54% purchase of Sept/Oct 2024) and INR 400 crores in cash expected on Infibeam's balance sheet "within the next 3 months to 9 months," to be funded not from Rediff's existing cash but from a Rediff capital raise — private equity or strategic partner, "it could be a combination thereof" — against "some inbound interest from time-to-time." A second, funding-driven rationale was that Rediff needs capital Infibeam did not want to carry in the payments entity: Rediff was guided to spend "upwards of $75 million to $100 million in the next three years... Rs. 500 crore to Rs. 700 crores" on tech, branding/marketing, developers and petabyte-scale hardware, and "if there is additional capital that will be required, then Rediff will have to raise that capital," a decision "for the Board of Rediff." Management also argued the combination would grow faster inside Rediff — "Rediff is expected to cross INR 300 crores in run rate revenues and we are confident it will exceed INR 1,000 crores in annualized revenue within the next 12 months of closing" — helped by data-localization/sovereignty demand pulling large Indian enterprises (including energy-sector names amid sanctions, plus BFSI clients like HDFC Life) off MNC email platforms. Management was explicit that consolidated reported revenue would be unaffected ("on a consolidated basis, all revenue consolidates... you won't see much of a difference"), so the gain claimed is structural — focus, Rediff's own capital access, and ultimately an SOTP/IPO value unlock, which by FY27 became the stated priority of "unlocking the value of Rediff."

**How it evolved:** The pieces were assembled before any separation was mentioned: on the Feb 2025 call management described acquiring a controlling (54%) stake in Rediff as "a pivot for us to get into consumer payments" and launched RediffOne as an enterprise ERP/CRM/HRMS suite, and on the May 2025 call it actively rejected a shareholder's suggestion to split the company (Deepesh Sancheti asked whether it made sense to "disinvest the company into 2 things... payments... and the AI"), with Vishal Mehta answering that AI "is a horizontal layer. It's not a vertical layer" — so the split that came was platform-into-Rediff, not AI. On Aug 8, 2025 the Board approved the INR 800 crore slump sale of the e-commerce platform business to Rediff, pitched as "platform convergence," with INR 400 crores taken as a 28% Rediff stake, INR 400 crores of cash to follow from a Rediff fundraise in 3–9 months, closing in "3 months to 9 months," and listing already acknowledged as an option for the Rediff board; by the Nov 2025 call the deal was described in the past tense ("platform divestiture to Rediff" in an analyst's own words) and Infibeam declared itself "a pure-play fintech and AI payments company," with INR 87 crores of rights-issue money already injected into Rediff. The Feb 2026 call repositioned Rediff from a divested recipient to the centre of a "closed-loop" flywheel alongside CCAvenue under the new AvenuesAI brand, Rediff filed its Pre-DRHP with SEBI/BSE/NSE on March 31, 2026, and on the Jun 2026 call management confirmed a confidential DRHP while refusing further detail and taking an investor request to disclose Rediff's revenue and EBITDA separately for SOTP purposes; by the Aug 2026 and Nov 2026 results "unlocking the value of Rediff" was priority one of three for FY27, and the parent's standalone accounts showed the platform business as discontinued operations and a single remaining segment (Payment Business).

**What management expects from it:** Infibeam/AvenuesAI: a pure-play fintech-plus-AI payments company, comparable "apple to apple" with Paytm or Pine Labs, with capital, leadership and strategy aligned to CCAvenue and Phronetic. Rediff: platform plus SaaS scale (INR 300cr to INR 1,000cr run rate in 12 months), its own INR 500–700cr investment capacity and own capital raise/IPO, with Infibeam retaining >80% (post-dilution >50%) and consolidated revenue unchanged — focus, clarity and eventual SOTP value unlock.
