## EDELWEISS — Edelweiss Financial Services Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a subsidiary's listing is in motion (DRHP / board approval)) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 2.1/10 · partial spin-off / listing · 5 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-01-20, latest 2026-11-02

> **Listing:** IPO / listing of the subsidiary in motion since 2026-01-20; date not fixed — DRHP filed January 19, 2026 (intimated January 20, 2026); SEBI observation letter April 23, 2026 "enables EAAA to proceed with IPO in next 12 months"; IPO opened October 26 and closed October 28, 2026; allotted October 29, 2026 and "admitted for listing and trading with effect from November 2, 2026"

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** EAAA India Alternatives Limited, the alternative asset management (investment manager to alternate-asset funds) business, part-listed via IPO offer for sale — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* ESIPL, wholly owned subsidiary and "one of the promoters", sold 72,07,207 shares yet still holds 78.43%; EFSL through all subsidiaries holds 83.88%. Management incentives in EAAA not stated.
- *What it reveals:* IPO price Rs 1,665 values EAAA's ~6.47 crore shares near Rs 10,700 crore versus EFSL net worth of Rs 5,866 crore; Alternatives segment earned PBT Rs 241.40 crore on Rs 989.53 crore capital employed; FPAUM Rs 41,920 crore, up 33% YoY.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — No shares distributed to EFSL shareholders; EAAA shares were sold into a book-built IPO at Rs 1,665 to bidding investors.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* EAAA's Red Herring Prospectus dated October 19, 2026 — fee-earning AUM, fee rates and the Rs 963.76 crore FY26 income mix
- *In their words:* “We are pleased to share that we have filed EAAA's DRHP for IPO in January and are on track for the listing, marking the first step towards building EAAA as a standalone institutionalized platform.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

On the documentary record available, Edelweiss is not executing a demerger scheme but a sequence of subsidiary-level separations that convert a holding-company conglomerate into separately capitalised, separately owned businesses — described in its own press release as "seven independent and well-governed businesses" each with "dedicated management teams and strong boards." The clearest stated reason is the Alternative Asset Management arm, EAAA India Alternatives: management said the IPO was "the first step towards building EAAA as a standalone institutionalized platform," i.e. separating the fastest-growing, fee-income business (FPAUM INR 41,920 Cr, +33% YoY; nine-month fund raise INR 7,576 Cr, +67% YoY; total income Rs 963.76 Cr in FY26 versus Rs 584.25 Cr in FY24; net worth Rs 1,075.54 Cr) from the credit-heavy parent so it can be valued and institutionalised on its own. Critically, the EAAA listing was a pure offer for sale by holdco subsidiary ESIPL (originally up to Rs 15,000 mn, cut to Rs 12,000 mn in the RHP, finally Rs 1,200 Cr gross / Rs 1,120.63 Cr net at Rs 1,665 per share) — no primary money went to EAAA, so the cash accrues to the Edelweiss holding structure, which fits the stated priority of "focused reduction in corporate net debt" (down 15% to INR 6,520 Cr over two years, with consolidated net debt INR 11,390 Cr and a 3.46x debt-equity ratio). The second separation is Housing Finance: Nido Home Finance was handed to a strategic majority investor, CA Sardo Investments (The Carlyle Group) with Salisbury Investments (Aditya Puri's family vehicle), investing ~INR 2,100 Cr — Rs 580.68 Cr of secondary for 45% plus Rs 1,446.14 Cr of primary equity and warrants at INR 193 — taking them to 58.26% immediately and 72.70% fully diluted within 18 months, so Nido "ceased to be a subsidiary" and Edelweiss fell to 38.91% (25.46% diluted). Here the separation solves a growth-capital problem Edelweiss itself was not funding: a business contributing only 5.47% of consolidated income (Rs 520.63 Cr) but consuming 13.99% of net worth (Rs 828.2 Cr) was recapitalised with third-party primary money, with Edelweiss retaining upside via a minority stake and "an additional payment based upon returns realized by CA Sardo Investments." The same template was applied to the Mutual Fund arm, where a 15% sale of Edelweiss Asset Management and Edelweiss Trusteeship to WestBridge moved both into joint control, crystallising a Rs 2,440 Cr unrealised and Rs 281 Cr realised gain (and a Rs 389 Cr deferred tax charge) — evidence that the separations are also being used to mark up carrying value and lift reported net worth/PAT (nine-month PAT Rs 549 Cr, +45% YoY). Taken together, the stated logic is: each business reaches scale, then gets its own owner, its own capital and its own valuation, while the parent de-levers.

**How it evolved:** This cannot be traced call by call: all ten earnings-call transcripts supplied (Nov 2023, May/Aug/Oct/Nov 2024, May/Aug/Nov 2025, Feb 2026, Apr 2026) contained no extractable text, so no dated management commentary is available. From the filings, the sequence is: EAAA's DRHP filed 19–20 January 2026 (OFS up to Rs 15,000 mn by ESIPL); on 10 February 2026 the Q3FY26 release framed it as "the first step towards building EAAA as a standalone institutionalized platform" and the same day the Carlyle/Salisbury definitive agreements for a majority of Nido were announced, with WestBridge's Mutual Fund investment consummated in that quarter; SEBI observations came 23 April 2026, the Nido transaction closed 25 September 2026 (versus a 31 July 2026 expectation), and the EAAA IPO was repriced down to Rs 12,000 mn in the RHP of 19 October 2026 before listing on 2 November 2026 at Rs 1,665. So the plan visibly scaled down in size (Rs 1,500 Cr to Rs 1,200 Cr) and slipped in timing, while widening from one business to three.

**What management expects from it:** EAAA becomes a listed, "standalone institutionalized platform" with its own valuation; Nido gets Carlyle/Puri growth capital and majority ownership while Edelweiss keeps 25–39% plus a returns-linked earn-out; Mutual Fund gains a strategic partner and a Rs 2,440 Cr value mark; the parent frees capital (Rs 1,120.63 Cr net OFS proceeds) to push corporate net debt below INR 6,520 Cr.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The EAAA IPO is explicitly positioned as the first step in separating the alternatives business into a self-standing institutional platform, announced alongside the DRHP filing in January 2026. “We are pleased to share that we have filed EAAA’s DRHP for IPO in January and are on track for the listing, marking the first step towards building EAAA as a standalone institutionalized platform.”
- *Scheme* — The structural end-state management describes for the group is a set of separately governed operating companies rather than an integrated financial conglomerate. “Edelweiss is a diversified financial services company with seven independent and well-governed businesses.”
- *Scheme* — The separations sit directly under the stated priority of de-levering the holding company, with corporate net debt the metric management tracks. “Corporate net debt continues to be on path to reduction, with a 15% decline to INR 6,520 Cr over the last two years”
- *Scheme* — Housing Finance was separated by bringing in Carlyle and Aditya Puri's family vehicle as strategic majority owners with roughly INR 2,100 crores of new money. “has entered into definitive agreements (the Agreements) with CA Sardo Investments (an affiliate of The Carlyle Group (NASDAQ: CG)) and Salisbury Investments Private Limited (an investment vehicle of Aditya Puri and his family) (collectively Buyers) for the Buyers to invest approximately INR 2,100 crores to acquire a strategic majority stake in Nido.”
- *Scheme* — The Nido deal is a true deconsolidation, not a minority stake sale — Edelweiss gives up control of the housing finance book. “Consequent to the transaction, Nido will cease to be a subsidiary of the Company.”
- *Scheme* — Nido was absorbing far more of the group's capital than it contributed in income — 13.99% of net worth for 5.47% of income — which the recapitalisation by third parties addresses. “Income 520.63 5.47% Net Worth 828.2 13.99%”
- *Scheme* — Most of the Carlyle money is primary capital into Nido's balance sheet rather than cash out to Edelweiss: Rs 580.68 Cr secondary versus Rs 1,446.14 Cr of fresh equity and warrants. “Further, in accordance with the Agreements, Nido has also issued 2,59,06,736 equity shares and 5,18,13,472 warrants, to the Buyers, for an aggregate amount of INR 14,46,13,99,102.56.”
- *Scheme* — Edelweiss retains economic upside in the separated housing business through a retained minority stake and a contingent payment linked to Carlyle's realised returns. “Pursuant to the Agreements and subject to applicable laws, the Sellers (Edelweiss) may also receive an additional payment based upon returns realized by CA Sardo Investments from its investment in Nido.”
- *Scheme* — Control of Nido passes progressively to the buyers — 58.26% on closing rising to 72.70% fully diluted — while Edelweiss falls to 25.46%. “the Buyers now hold 58.26% shareholding of Nido which would be increased to 72.70% within 18 months, on a fully diluted basis post conversion of the warrants.”
- *Scheme* — The Mutual Fund business was separated on the same template, with a 15% strategic sale converting EAML and ETCL into jointly controlled entities. “Additionally, the WestBridge investment in Mutual Fund received its final approval from the regulators, and the deal has been consummated this quarter.”
- *Scheme* — That Mutual Fund separation crystallised very large accounting gains — Rs 2,440 Cr unrealised plus Rs 281 Cr realised — showing the separations also re-rate carrying values inside the consolidated accounts. “Pursuant to the terms of the SHA, the Group now has joint control for both of these Entities with the new investor, and consequently, in accordance with Ind AS 110 and Ind AS 28, these entities are now classified as jointly controlled entities under Ind AS accounting principles.”
- *Scheme* — The EAAA listing raised no primary capital for EAAA itself; proceeds went to the holding-company subsidiary ESIPL, consistent with using separation to fund parent de-leveraging. “The IPO comprises an offer for sale (“OFS”) for an amount not exceeding Rs. 12,000 million, which is proposed to be undertaken by Edelweiss Securities & Investments Private Limited (“ESIPL”), a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company.”

*Not explained on the calls:* All ten earnings-call transcripts were unextractable, so management's spoken rationale, investor/lender demands, use of proceeds, valuation targets, and any formal demerger scheme are absent.

## BORORENEW — Borosil Renewables Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a filing's text names a demerger; no scheme filing names it yet) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 1.7/10 · spin-off · 1 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-03-04, latest 2026-03-04

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Consumer and scientific & industrial products business, separated from the company by demerger (and later split again) — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* Shreevar Kheruka, Promoter & Vice Chairman of Borosil Renewables, holds 20,04,324 shares (1.43%) after buying 52,577 shares; he is Vice Chairman and MD of Borosil Limited.
- *What it reveals:* The separation leaves Borosil Renewables a single-segment flat glass (solar glass) business: FY26 standalone sales Rs 1,534.83 crores, EBITDA 32% of sales, and 600 TPD expansion raising capacity 60%.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — Both demergers were completed under NCLT-approved schemes in 2020 and 2023; no new share distribution is pending in the documents.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* The Composite Schemes themselves (Scheme 1 and Scheme 2) and their share allotment ratios referenced in the March 04, 2026 filing.
- *In their words:* “In terms of the Composite Sheme of Amagalmation and Arrangement approved by Hon'ble National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT), Mumbai, on January 15, 2020, inter-alia, Gujarat Borosil Limited (producer of solar glass) had been amalgamated with the Company, and the consumer and scientific & industrial product business of the Company had been transferred by way of demerger to Borosil Limited ("Scheme 1").”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

These texts contain no announcement, scheme or rationale for Borosil Renewables separating one of its own businesses into a new entity — the only forward-looking corporate-action question, on reported 'strategic investment' talks (Jul 2026 call), was met with 'I cannot offer any comment on this.' The separation management does explain at length is the severing of the European solar-glass business from the Indian one, executed through insolvency rather than a demerger: the hot end (melting furnace) of step-down subsidiary GMB Glasmanufaktur Brandenburg was cooled on 31 December 2024, GMB filed for insolvency on 4 July 2025, its holding company Geosphere Glassworks filed on 22 December 2025, and the marketing arm Interfloat Corporation was progressively impaired. The cause given was that from June 2023, roughly 6–7 months after the takeover, about 80 GW of Chinese modules were dumped into Europe in a couple of months, destroying local module manufacturing so that GMB's tailor-made customers disappeared and it could not sell beyond 50% of production, while promised EU/German policy support never turned into action. The cost of staying was quantified repeatedly: EBITDA losses of about INR 8 crore per month before shutdown, targeted down to INR 4 crore (employee cost ~INR 2 crore plus ~INR 2 crore other fixed cost), an inventory write-off of ~INR 16 crore, and standing charges of about EUR 900,000 (~INR 9 crore) a month that Geosphere would have had to keep funding. Management's stated purpose was that 'this filing of insolvency of the subsidiary would arrest recurring losses and permit reallocation of capital and managerial focus towards the India operations,' and that the one-time INR 325.91 crore provision against Geosphere/GMB (Rs 32,590.81 lakhs; written off in the FY26 accounts, with a INR 75 crore tax provision written back in Q4 FY26) would remove the continued drag on consolidated results so that 'the ROCE and EPS will substantially improve'; Laxman AG separately impaired INR 33.87 crore of its INR 57.59 crore exposure to Interfloat. The push came from several directions: GMB's own managing director was obliged under the German Insolvency Code to file once no further shareholder funding was available; German state bank ILB demanded repayment of the EUR 4.81 million capital subsidy, which Geosphere could not honour and which triggered its own filing; Borosil had already paid INR 185 crore from the February 2025 preferential issue to settle the SBLC given to GMB's lenders, while roughly INR 120–125 crore of GMB's remaining external liabilities (severance plus the government grant) were said not to travel to Borosil; and investors on the November 2025 call explicitly pressed management to shut Interfloat down as well. The group's only genuine demergers appear incidentally in a share re-lodgement filing — the NCLT-approved composite scheme of 15 January 2020 that amalgamated Gujarat Borosil (solar glass) into Borosil Renewables while demerging the consumer and scientific & industrial businesses to Borosil Limited, and the 2 November 2023 scheme demerging scientific & industrial out of Borosil Limited into Borosil Scientific — producing the 'three listed companies with different products, different businesses' and separate CEOs/teams described on the Jul 2026 call. Notably, the newest business, Borosil-branded rooftop solar kits (module, inverter, battery; ~INR 36–75 crore first-year revenue target, single-digit margins, no capex), is being built as a division inside Borosil Renewables, not separated out.

**How it evolved:** On the Nov 2024 call management was still 'reviewing all our options' for Germany, trying to fill the furnace with orders from the USA and EU; by Feb 2025 it had cooled the GMB furnace on 31 December 2024 pending the German election, and in May 2025 it sounded hopeful about the new Christian Democrat/Social Democrat government and was evaluating a cold-end-only restart using imported annealed glass. The Jul 2025 call reversed that: insolvency had been filed on 4 July 2025, the full INR 325.91 crore exposure was provisioned, and the stated purpose became arresting losses and reallocating capital and managerial focus to India. The Nov 2025 call extended the exit to Interfloat (INR 33.87 crore impaired; a shutdown decision promised 'by next quarter'), Feb 2026 confirmed GMB and Geosphere were fully deconsolidated so that consolidated and standalone results were now nearly identical, and May 2026 recorded the formal write-off after the Cottbus administrator's 1 December 2025 report said creditors would receive nothing; Jul 2026 only cleaned up the associated INR 75 crore tax shield.

**What management expects from it:** India: end of the consolidated loss drag, substantially improved ROCE and EPS, capital and managerial focus redeployed to the Bharuch 600 TPD expansion, and sustained 30–33% EBITDA margins. Europe (GMB/Geosphere/Interfloat): handed to court-appointed administrators, with roughly INR 120–125 crore of liabilities staying there rather than travelling to Borosil, and nothing expected back for shareholders.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Nov 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=575ef6da-948b-4f9c-abae-5d6228eb2c77.pdf)* — Germany's problem was framed as collapsed demand, not cost: with local module makers unprotected and Chinese modules cheap, GMB's local demand fell to about 40% of production, and management said it was still weighing alternatives. “So we are reviewing all our options. We are trying to first get the orders from other geographies so that we can still run at higher capacity, bring down the per unit cost of production and manage to bring both ends together in terms of revenue and cost, failing which we will have to look at more alternatives.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=99cf2f04-c3dd-4bd8-a433-a30c732d359e.pdf)* — First physical step in the separation: the GMB melting furnace was cooled on 31 December 2024 while the German government was in crisis, with EBITDA losses of ~INR 8 crore/month to be halved to ~INR 4 crore and most workers put on state-funded short-time work. “Since no decision could be expected until the formation of a new government, we decided to cool down the furnace on 31st December 2024, thus temporarily pausing the hot-end operations.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=e680b5b1-b8dc-4bc7-8ab9-2e572269b010.pdf)* — Still trying to save it — a cold-end-only restart processing imported annealed glass was being evaluated, an INR 16 crore inventory write-off was taken, and INR 185 crore of fresh Indian equity money was pushed out to settle GMB's lender liability. “INR185 crores from this amount has been utilized to repay the loan liability of our step-down subsidiary, GMB.”
- *[Jul 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=042e3a5b-2755-4eec-940e-4a225dca1dcc.pdf)* — The decisive explanation of the separation: insolvency filed 4 July 2025, INR 325.91 crore provisioned in full, and the stated gain was stopping ~INR 9 crore/month of standing charges and redirecting capital and management attention to India. “For our Company, this filing of insolvency of the subsidiary would arrest recurring losses and permit reallocation of capital and managerial focus towards the India operations where we see a long-term potential and policy support.”
- *[Jul 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=042e3a5b-2755-4eec-940e-4a225dca1dcc.pdf)* — The root cause given for the European exit was the June 2023 dumping of roughly 80 GW of Chinese modules into the EU, which wiped out GMB's customers for tailor-made glass and left it unable to sell beyond 50% of output. “In June '23, just immediately after 6 to 7 months of our takeover of the Company, the imported Chinese modules started to be dumped in European markets, almost 80 gigawatts of modules were dumped in couple of months' time over there, which destroyed the local manufacturing.”
- *[Jul 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=042e3a5b-2755-4eec-940e-4a225dca1dcc.pdf)* — The accounting purpose of taking the hit in one quarter was explicitly to clean up the entity left behind — no further consolidated drag, with better ROCE and EPS. “However, this one-time provision will ensure that there is no continued drag on the consolidated results and performance, and that the ROCE and EPS will substantially improve.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=d3452e3a-5811-40b5-80c7-184c77fc5df8.pdf)* — The separation was extended to the European marketing arm: Interfloat lost its customers after GMB stopped annealed glass on 31 December 2024, and Laxman AG impaired INR 33.87 crore of its INR 57.59 crore exposure, with an investor pressing management to shut it entirely (answer: a decision 'by next quarter'). “Following an independent review by the management of Interfloat, it is assessed that there are no clear indicators of demand recovery in the near term that would support a return to profitable operations.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=c6d3ddb3-d2c9-4920-ac44-620c127de6af.pdf)* — Separation complete in accounting terms — both GMB and its holding company Geosphere were deconsolidated, control lost to the court-appointed administrator, so consolidated results now essentially equal standalone India. “So from the perspective of accounting and losses, we already deconsolidated the balance sheet by deconsolidating GMB, which is an operating step-down subsidiary and now we also deconsolidated Geosphere, which was a holding company of GMB.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=4eeb9028-bca0-4395-be53-a9f841b84ad1.pdf)* — Final step: after the Cottbus administrator's 1 December 2025 report said GMB's assets were insufficient and creditors would get nothing, the INR 325.91 crore exposure was written off, with no additional loss because it was already provided. “In view of this, the company in its books of accounts for the financial year ended 31 March, 2026 has written off the above exposure in Geosphere and GMB.”
- *[Jul 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=c5724e06-b82b-4447-92f4-06f9c155a025.pdf)* — The only governance rationale offered for keeping businesses in separate listed vehicles was management bandwidth: three listed companies, each with its own chairman/MD, CEO and functional teams, with Borosil Renewables' policy-heavy solar business needing P.K. Kheruka's full attention. “So we have three listed companies with different products, different businesses.”
- *[Jul 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=c5724e06-b82b-4447-92f4-06f9c155a025.pdf)* — Asked directly about press reports of a strategic investment, management declined to say anything — no further corporate restructuring was disclosed on any call. “I cannot offer any comment on this.”
- *Scheme* — The group's actual demergers appear only in a 4 March 2026 share re-lodgement filing: the 2020 NCLT composite scheme amalgamated solar-glass maker Gujarat Borosil into Borosil Renewables and demerged the consumer and scientific/industrial businesses out to Borosil Limited (50 shares of each per 100 Gujarat Borosil shares). “In terms of the Composite Sheme of Amagalmation and Arrangement approved by Hon'ble National Company Law Tribunal ( NCLT ), Mumbai, on January 15, 2020, inter-alia, Gujarat Borosil Limited (producer of solar glass) had been amalgamated with the Company, and the consumer and scientific & industrial product business of the Company had been transferred by way of demerger to Borosil Limited ("Scheme 1").”

*Not explained on the calls:* No demerger scheme, swap ratio, record date, valuation, listing plan or shareholder vote is discussed; nor why rooftop solar stays an in-house division.

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Nothing in these eight transcripts or ten filings describes CGCL separating, demerging, spinning off or listing any business — there is no scheme of arrangement, no swap ratio and no record date anywhere in the material, and as late as the Jan 2026 filing the company still states that it 'operates mainly in the business segment of fund based financing activity' with 'no separate reportable segments' under Ind AS 108. The only corporate separations management actually explains are internal: the car-loan distribution (DSA) business was moved out of the listed parent into a newly formed wholly-owned subsidiary, Capri Loans Car Platforms Private Limited, and three further subsidiaries were incorporated in FY26 — Capri Global Capital Markets Private Limited (debt-capital-market investment banking, subsidiary w.e.f. 8 Jul 2025), Capri Global Securities Private Limited (institutional debt placement, online bond platform, exchange trading, w.e.f. 15 Jul 2025) and Capri Global Insurance Brokers Private Limited (w.e.f. 2 Dec 2025), funded with ₹100 mn, ₹600 mn and ₹7.5 mn respectively in Q3 FY26. The logic given for housing these in separate entities is that they are capital-light, pure fee/distribution businesses — 'no capital involved, there's no risk involved' in car loans — that ride on the same supervisory team and 1,800-person field force, so they are 'accretive to the profit' from year one rather than denting the cost-to-income ratio. The only cost management attributed to the car-loan carve-out was transitional: FY25 car-loan profit was guided 'slightly lower than the last year because of various transition from old CGCL to the new company,' with volumes of ₹10,700 cr and ₹96 cr net fee in FY25 rising to ₹11,910 cr origination (up 13%) across 14 partner banks in FY26. No investor, lender or bank partner is cited anywhere as having asked for a separation; the mortgage business already sits in a separate licensed subsidiary (CGHFL) for regulatory reasons, into which the parent injected ₹200 cr via a rights issue allotted 23 Mar 2026 at ₹274/share. On the evidence given, the premise of a business separation is not supported, and I have not inferred one.

**How it evolved:** Aug 2024 (Q1 FY25) is the first mention, reported as already done: the car-loan vertical had been shifted out of CGCL into a newly formed subsidiary, with the softer Q1 fee (₹246 mn vs ₹271 mn) explained by seasonality. Nov 2024 (Q2 FY25) added the only stated cost — transition to the new entity plus the used-car launch would hold FY25 car-loan profit below FY24, with 'all-time high' profit promised the next year. Aug 2025 (Q1 FY26) extended the pattern to two newly incorporated companies for debt-capital-market investment banking and securities/bond distribution, described as capital-light and profit-accretive from year one; the Jan 2026 filing adds Capri Global Insurance Brokers and the funding amounts. By May 2026 the framing had become monetisation of the car-loan entity alone — ₹20 cr profit next year scaling to ₹60–70 cr of fee income over 4–5 years, with used cars, credit cards, personal loans and mortgages added over 3–4 years.

**What management expects from it:** No separation economics are claimed, because no separation is announced. For the subsidiarised fee businesses management expects capital-light, profit-accretive-from-year-one income: car loans ₹20 cr PAT in FY27 scaling to ₹60–70 cr fee income in 4–5 years on 12–15% origination growth; capital markets ₹20–25 cr net fee plus removal of 2–3% treasury negative carry; no change to lender capital or parent valuation is asserted.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Aug 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=520e7947-2e87-43af-89b5-42d8090736c4.pdf)* — First disclosure, after the fact, that the car-loan distribution business had been moved out of the listed parent into a new wholly-owned subsidiary; the Q1 fee dip (₹246 mn vs ₹271 mn) was attributed to seasonality, not the move. “Car loan, we have shifted the business from the Capri Global Capital Limited to the newly formed subsidiary.”
- *[Nov 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=7d546298-8483-41df-abe0-f69510d86595.pdf)* — The only cost management ever attached to the carve-out: FY25 car-loan profitability would fall below FY24 because of the transition out of CGCL into the new company, alongside the used-car product launch. “This year, we will have profitability slightly lower than the last year because of various transition from old CGCL to the new company.”
- *[Nov 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=7d546298-8483-41df-abe0-f69510d86595.pdf)* — Management framed the drag as purely transitional stabilisation cost in the new entity, with volume and profit expected at an all-time high the following year. “This year, it will take some stabilization in the new entity along with the launch of the new product, where we'll see some operational cost offsetting the profit of this vertical.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=3466d074-35e8-43c1-a551-78db98c17ae9.pdf)* — The rationale for keeping car loans as a separate, non-lending vehicle: it is pure origination for 12 partner banks (₹10,700 cr disbursed, ₹96 cr net fee in FY25, 813 locations across 31 states) with no balance-sheet exposure. “So, this is a pure fee vertical where we just originate the lead and share. There's no capital involved, there's no risk involved.”
- *Aug 2025* — Two further subsidiaries incorporated — one for debt-capital-market investment banking, one securities company for institutional debt placement, an online bond platform and exchange trading, staffed by a team of about 10 people. “There are two companies we have incorporated. One is going to carry out the investment banking activities only for the debt capital market.”
- *Aug 2025* — The stated test for putting these businesses in separate entities is that they are capital-light and self-funding, so they add fee income without hurting the cost-to-income guidance for FY26. “Both of these will not consume much capital, and they will be from the year 1 that will be accretive to the profit rather than taking any dent on the cost income side.”

- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=345ec5b5-e595-4428-957a-1b77d5f31a0d.pdf)* — The capital-markets subsidiary's purpose is given as reducing a 2–3% negative carry on an earmarked ₹600–800 cr treasury book plus ₹40–50 cr gross (₹20–25 cr net) fee income once the licence is received, expected by end-June. “So, it will contribute to the fee income as well as also to reducing our negative carry in our treasury income.”
- *Scheme* — No scheme of arrangement, demerger, spin-off or separation of any business appears in any of the ten filings; as of the Q3 FY26 results the company still reports itself as a single-segment lender, and the only equity actions disclosed are fund-raising (₹4,000 cr enabling resolution, USD 30 mn bonds, GMTN programme) and a ₹200 cr rights-issue injection into housing subsidiary CGHFL. “The Company operates mainly in the business segment of fund based financing activity. All other activities revolve around the main business.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No separation, demerger or listing is explained anywhere — no scheme, rationale, valuation, swap ratio, record date, subsidiary-level financials, or any investor, lender or partner request.

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** The Hyderabad property/facility, closed February 2025 and reclassified as an "Asset held for sale" in FY25 — an asset sale, not a demerger — class `regulatory_strategic`.

- *Insiders:* Not stated for any new entity; filing states the buyer does not belong to the promoter/promoter group/group companies and the transaction is not a related party transaction.
- *What it reveals:* INR 54.5 crores cash for a facility the Company says will have no impact on profits or net worth; Karamsad now runs full with a five-to-six-month glass-lined backlog on three shifts, implying the sold capacity was surplus.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — No shares are issued or distributed; a property sale worth 1.6% of consolidated revenue, so no index exclusion or forced selling.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* FY26 cash flow / Q4 FY26 numbers confirming the INR 54.5-55 crores proceeds were received and deployed against debt.
- *In their words:* “Since this facility was closed in February 2025 and its operations were consolidated at Karamsad, Gujarat, this sale will have no impact on the Company's profits or net worth.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

These texts do not describe GMM Pfaudler separating, demerging or spinning off a business: across all six transcripts and the one filing there is no scheme of arrangement, no slump sale of a business, no record date and no entity-separation rationale, so the premise cannot be sourced here. What management actually explains is the opposite — consolidation of one group: closure and merging of glass-lined capacity (UK Leven shut in FY26 Q2; Hyderabad shut February 2025 with its load moved into Karamsad, which then ran three shifts at 80%+), downsizing of Pfaudler GmbH Germany by 30 plus about 5 people, roughly 25-30% of the German wage bill, costing an exceptional INR 44 crores in Q3 FY26 (later raised by INR 9 crores, inside a FY26 exceptional of about INR 65 crores alongside INR 13 crores for the new Indian labour code) and yielding INR 45 crores of annual savings, plus a 51% Poland JV (11 million zloty, about INR 25 crores) that is roughly 30% cheaper than Switzerland/France and feeds MAVAG and MIXEL. The only disposal in the filings is a property, not a business: the already-closed Hyderabad plant, reclassified as an asset held for sale in FY25 and sold for INR 54.5 crores to Topsun Power Private Limited (a Bhagyanagar Properties subsidiary), explicitly flagged as 5.6% of standalone and 1.6% of consolidated FY25 revenue and as having no impact on profits or net worth, with 'Not Applicable' entered against the scheme-of-arrangement question. The only business ever put up for separation was Edlon, the US PTFE/semiconductor unit, which was formally run as an asset-for-sale process when it was a USD 8-10 million business and then deliberately retained — 'we decided to keep that business within the group' — after semiconductor demand took it to USD 25 million at high margin. Management instead keeps aggregating: four mixing units (Mixion India, MIXEL France/China, MixPro Canada and SEMCO Brazil, bought for USD 18.5 million / INR 162 crores) are being pulled 'under one umbrella' with a rebranding, and the India-versus-international split in reporting is being dismantled in favour of global product verticals (technologies, heavy engineering, process, performance, systems) from Q1 FY27. The nearest thing to a 'separation' pressed by outsiders is structural, not operational: investors (Anil Shah, Rushabh Sharedalal) attacked the EBITDA-to-PAT leakage — INR 680 crores of idle cash against INR 120-130 crores of interest — and management conceded an inherited Pfaudler-acquisition structure, an intercompany Germany-Luxembourg loan driving FX and a high tax rate, a Big Four six-month study, fresh Board approvals, financing agreements running to 2028 that must be renegotiated with lenders and tax authorities, and intent to repay about USD 20 million. No business is being carved out of the listed entity in anything provided.

**How it evolved:** Feb 2025 (Q3 FY25) first frames it as footprint rationalisation — Hyderabad consolidated into Karamsad, UK rationalised, Poland agreement executed — and Edlon is cited as a diversification win, not a sale candidate. May 2025 and Aug 2025 confirm Leven's closure, the INR 20 crore India transformation cost and Greg Gelhaus's transformation mandate, while Aug 2025 adds that the India-versus-international reporting split will be replaced by a global view. Nov 2025 and Feb 2026 push the other way — SEMCO and the Poland JV are consolidated in, four mixing units are to be combined under one brand, and Germany is downsized for INR 44 crores; Feb 2026 also reveals Edlon had earlier been 'put as an asset for sale' and was kept. By May 2026 the only separation-like workstream left is the legal/financing/tax restructuring of the Luxembourg entity and the intercompany loan, Board-approved but explicitly unfinished, with the three-year strategy deferred to a capital markets day pushed from August-September 2026 by the Middle East conflict.

**What management expects from it:** No separation, hence no per-entity guidance. For the single group they expect INR 45 crores of annual German savings, about 30% lower cost in Poland versus Western Europe, Karamsad full on three shifts, international EBITDA of roughly INR 264 crores plus that 45, a 15% blended group EBITDA margin medium-term (cut from 16-18%), leverage below 1x, and about USD 20 million of debt repaid once the Luxembourg structure is fixed.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=9c47c8f6-a227-4369-a4ad-5c1974058bea.pdf)* — The first consolidation step was closing the small Hyderabad glass-lined plant acquired from De Dietrich and moving output to the larger Karamsad (Gujarat) factory, purely for fixed-cost absorption; the site was held, not sold, at that stage. “As of right now it just made a lot of sense to consolidate everything into one, so all your cost is in one facility, and your better utilization as well.”
- *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=f1bba782-35f4-4736-a70b-c20229ec3521.pdf)* — Footprint optimisation was presented as ongoing: Hyderabad shut with costs taken in Q3 FY25, Leven UK on track to close in Q2 FY26, and Poland established as the low-cost site — all inside one group, with no entity separation proposed. “Our global manufacturing footprint optimization continues. Our UK facility in Leven is on track for closure in Q2 FY26.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=397d2b79-dc7b-4cf3-9226-bc9a77ca3098.pdf)* — Production is being moved from high-cost Western European entities (MAVAG Switzerland, MIXEL France) into the Poland JV rather than any business being hived off; Tarak quantifies roughly a 30% cost benefit versus Western Europe. “We have now started sending orders from Western Europe, high cost geographies like Switzerland and France to Poland, the quality and the delivery from those sites have been very good.”

There is a rebranding strategy going on.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=abe1b8dc-3b81-47e2-951d-ce2bd0e83f00.pdf)* — Germany is downsized — 30 plus about 5 people, roughly 25-30% of the German wage bill, agreed with the works council, INR 44 crores exceptional in Q3 and INR 13 crores for the Indian labour code — because global glass-lined capacity exceeds demand. “This continues and our glass-lined capacity today, as what we have across the world, needs to be consolidated and the next initiative in this front is to reduce about 30-people in Germany.”
- *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=abe1b8dc-3b81-47e2-951d-ce2bd0e83f00.pdf)* — The only business genuinely put up for separation was Edlon, the US PTFE/semiconductor unit, run as a formal asset-for-sale process at USD 8-9 million of revenue and then retained as it tripled to USD 25 million at high margin. “But I think you would remember, Salil, a few quarters ago when Edlon was not performing that well, we had actually put it as an asset for sale.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=b898ceb5-6fa9-44e1-b612-1fc569d993c6.pdf)* — The restructuring is monetary and legal, not a carve-out: INR 45 crores of annual German savings, UK and Hyderabad shut, Poland live — while reporting shifts from India/international to global product verticals from the next quarter. “In fact, we would like to share that we saved with this initiative INR 45 crores on an annual basis.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=b898ceb5-6fa9-44e1-b612-1fc569d993c6.pdf)* — Investors pressed hardest on the inherited Pfaudler acquisition structure — INR 680 crores of cash against INR 120-130 crores of interest, the Germany-Luxembourg intercompany loan and the Luxembourg tax leakage — and management has Board approval to restructure financing and entities, bounded by agreements running to 2028, tax authorities and other parties. “But do keep in mind that this was inherited because we acquired the Pfaudler business and was structured in a certain way.”
- *Scheme* — The only filed disposal is the already-closed Hyderabad property, sold for INR 54.5 crores to Topsun Power Private Limited (a Bhagyanagar Properties subsidiary), with the scheme-of-arrangement and slump-sale disclosure boxes both marked Not Applicable — confirming no business separation. “Since this facility was closed in February 2025 and its operations were consolidated at Karamsad, Gujarat, this sale will have no impact on the Company's profits or net worth.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The record supplied contains no earnings-call transcripts ("no transcripts on file") and no scheme of arrangement, demerger, spin-off or business-separation filing, so there is no management-stated rationale for separating a business to reconstruct. GMRP&UI's twelve filings cover three unrelated actions: a Rs. 1,200 crore preferential issue, the exit from one real-estate joint venture, and the dissolution of a dormant Singapore coal subsidiary. The only two disposals that resemble a "separation" are explained in narrow, transaction-specific terms. First, the company sold its entire 26% (2,600 equity shares of Rs. 10 each) in Portus Ventures Private Limited — a JV with Shree Naman Developers Private Limited for land development inside Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport, Mumbai, described as "in pre-planning phase and recently entered construction phase" — to Adani Airport City Limited for just Rs. 36,400, stating two reasons: majority shareholder SNDPL decided to exit and GMRP&UI exercised its tag-along right, and the exit aligns with GMR Group's intent to focus on real-estate opportunities already identified inside its existing businesses; PVPL contributed Nil revenue and net worth. Second, GMR Coal Resources Pte. Ltd., a step-down wholly owned Singapore subsidiary with "Nil turnover" and "insignificant" net worth, was voluntarily liquidated effective October 1, 2026 (ACRA confirmation October 16, 2026), with no reason given beyond its dormancy. The capital action the filings do explain in detail is deleveraging, not separation: Rs. 1,200 crore was raised at Rs. 120.88 per share/warrant (Rs. 800 crore equity to Synergy Industrials, Metals and Power Holdings Limited — Rs. 450 crore — and Värde-controlled Credit Solutions India Trust — Rs. 350 crore; Rs. 400 crore of warrants to promoter-group Hyderabad Jabilli Properties Private Limited), to "meet the requirements for Repayment/prepayment of outstanding borrowings and other general corporate purposes." After BSE/NSE observation letters forced a corrigendum, the use of proceeds was itemised as Rs. 550 crore for the parent's borrowings, Rs. 450 crore for borrowings of GMR Generation Assets Limited, GMR Smart Electricity Distribution Private Limited and GMR Highways Limited, Rs. 100 crore for infusions into subsidiaries/JVs and Rs. 100 crore general corporate purposes, monitored by CARE Ratings Limited. No investor, lender or partner is recorded as asking for any separation; the only third-party pressure documented is from the stock exchanges demanding more disclosure, and from a JV partner's exit triggering a tag-along.

**How it evolved:** There are no calls in the record, so the idea cannot be traced call by call. On the filings' own timeline: April 3, 2024 — an earlier intimation on PVPL (referenced, not supplied); December 12, 2025 — board meeting notice to consider raising up to Rs. 1,200 crore; December 17, 2025 — board approval, postal ballot notice, and two superseding re-issues of the outcome (the equity allottee's name corrected to Synergy Industrials, Metals and Power Holdings Limited); January 8, 2026 — corrigendum adding the itemised debt-repayment split after exchange observation letters; January 28, 2026 — allotment of 6,61,81,335 shares and 3,30,90,668 warrants after the January 16, 2026 shareholder approval. Only then do the two disposals follow: the PVPL share purchase agreement on June 8, 2026 (completion expected by June 17, 2026) and GCRPL's dissolution effective October 1, 2026 — each disclosed as a standalone exit, never as part of a staged separation plan.

**What management expects from it:** Nothing is stated for any separated entity, because no separation is disclosed. For the company itself, management expects Rs. 1,200 crore of preferential-issue proceeds to repay or prepay Rs. 550 crore of parent borrowings and Rs. 450 crore at GMR Generation Assets, GMR Smart Electricity Distribution and GMR Highways within 24 months, plus Rs. 100 crore for subsidiary/JV infusions. No margin, valuation or focus benefit is quantified.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Filing 2026-06-08 (Sale or disposal, Portus Ventures)* — The 26% PVPL exit is attributed to the majority shareholder SNDPL's decision to sell and GMRP&UI accepting its tag-along right, not to any separation plan of its own. “SNDPL had decided to sell its entire stake in PVPL to the Buyer and the Company had accepted the tag-along option provided to it, considering the exit of majority shareholder.”
- *Filing 2026-06-08 (Sale or disposal, Portus Ventures)* — The only strategic reason given is a narrowing of real-estate focus to opportunities inside existing businesses; the JV was an airport-land development at CSMIA Mumbai sold to Adani Airport City Limited for Rs. 36,400 with Nil revenue and net worth contribution. “Further, the exit by the Company from PVPL would also align with the GMR Group's strategic intent to focus on real estate opportunities already identified as part of its existing businesses.”
- *Filing 2026-10-17 (General Updates, GCRPL winding up)* — The Singapore coal subsidiary was dissolved with no rationale given beyond immateriality — it is a housekeeping liquidation, not a carve-out of an operating business. “GCRPL recorded Nil turnover and its Net worth contribution was insignificant during the last financial year.”
- *Filing 2025-12-17 (Shareholders meeting, Postal Ballot Notice)* — The stated purpose of the Rs. 1,200 crore preferential issue is deleveraging and general corporate purposes — the filings' explanation for fixing the balance sheet is fresh equity, not a business separation. “The Company intends to raise funds to, inter alia, meet the requirements for Repayment/prepayment of outstanding borrowings and other general corporate purposes.”
- *Filing 2026-01-08 (Corrigendum to Postal Ballot Notice)* — Only after BSE and NSE observation letters did the company name the specific borrowers to be de-levered — the parent (Rs. 550 crore) plus GMR Generation Assets, GMR Smart Electricity Distribution and GMR Highways (Rs. 450 crore), with Rs. 100 crore for infusions and Rs. 100 crore general corporate purposes. “Thereafter, the Company has received observation letters from the Stock Exchanges wherein the Company was required inter alia, to elaborate on the "Utilisation of Issue proceeds" in further more details through a corrigendum to the Notice.”
- *Filing 2026-01-28 (General Updates, allotment)* — Rs. 899.99 crore was actually received on allotment — Rs. 450 crore from Synergy, Rs. 350 crore from Värde's Credit Solutions India Trust and Rs. 100 crore (25%) on promoter-group warrants — lifting share capital to 78,10,17,529 shares and diluting promoters from 50.56% to 48.46% fully diluted, with no reference to any separation. “Consequent to the said Allotment, the paid-up equity share capital of the Company has increased from Rs. 3,57,41,80,970 comprising 71,48,36,194 fully paid-up equity shares of Rs. 5/- each to Rs. 3,90,50,87,645 comprising 78,10,17,529 fully paid-up equity shares of Rs.5/- each.”
- *Filing 2025-12-17 (Outcome of Board Meeting)* — The December 17, 2025 board outcome was issued and then twice superseded the same day, with the equity allottee renamed from "Synergy Industrial and Power Metals Limited" to "Synergy Industrials, Metals and Power Holdings Limited" — the only plan change visible anywhere in the record. “This is in furtherance to outcome of Board Meeting dated December 17, 2025, please find revised outcome of the Board meeting in supersession of the previous one.”

## HCG — Healthcare Global Enterprises Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a scheme of arrangement whose nature the documents on file do not settle) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 1.7/10 · scheme (nature unclear) · 1 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-03-26, latest 2026-03-26

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Milann, the fertility and reproductive healthcare business held in BACC Health Care Private Limited — sold, not demerged — class `unrelated`.

- *Insiders:* Dr. B.S. Ajaikumar, promoter and Non-Executive Chairman, is Sponsor of buyer Inviga Healthcare Fund I and controls it; promoters hold 9.30% (Ajaikumar), Hector 54.27%, Catalyst 0.18% of HCG. No promoter stake in a new entity disclosed.
- *What it reveals:* Not a hidden gem: Milann's centres fell from nine to six, low EBITDA margin, only marginally above post-rent break-even; enterprise value INR 63 crore, equity INR 37.6 crore, with Rs 3,752 lakhs impairment booked. Parent left a pure-play oncology network, net debt 1.4x.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — No shares distributed to shareholders; entire stake sold for cash to a promoter-controlled fund, so no new listing or index exclusion.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated for the divested business; HCG granted 64,46,843 options on 9 September 2026 under HCG ESOS 2026 at exercise price INR 495
- *Read next:* BACC's FY26 revenue of Rs 60.45 crore and Rs 17.53 crore net worth against the INR 63 crore enterprise value.
- *In their words:* “BACC is not a material subsidiary of the Company and is engaged in the business of fertility and reproductive healthcare services, which is not a core business activity of the Company.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Management presents this as an exit from fertility to concentrate capital and management bandwidth on oncology. The business separated is Milann, HCG's fertility/IVF chain held through BACC Health Care Private Limited — a majority stake taken in 2013 and a fully-owned subsidiary from 2020 — sold to Inviga Healthcare Fund I at an enterprise valuation of INR 63 crore, with equity consideration of INR 37.6 crore for 100% including certain transition services support, 75% received upfront at closing and 25% over 18 months (filings specify INR 28.23 crore at closing and INR 9.41 crore deferred, not contingent). The problems cited: Milann's operating footprint had steadily declined, centres falling from 9 to 6; the business ran at a low EBITDA margin and was only marginally above break-even on a post-rent basis; and reviving and scaling it would need significant management bandwidth plus primary capital infusion, both outside HCG's focus on building the core oncology network. Filings add that BACC is not a material subsidiary and that fertility is not a core business activity — FY26 revenue of INR 60.45 crore (4.45% of HCG standalone revenue) and net worth of INR 17.53 crore (1.09%). The root cause of the decline was named earlier: Milann's original founder/partner exited, her non-compete lapsed, and she opened her own centres very close to HCG's, denting revenue at Kumara Park and J.P. Nagar. The buyer was described as better positioned to infuse growth capital, scale the business independently and carry forward the Milann legacy, and was chosen through a comprehensive, competitive sale process focused on maximizing valuation, transaction certainty and a smooth transition for Milann's employees, with Audit Committee and Board approval and an independent third-party valuation. Crucially, the buyer is a related party: Inviga Healthcare Fund I is sponsored and controlled by Dr. B.S. Ajaikumar, HCG's promoter and Non-Executive Chairman. The push came repeatedly from analysts (Avener Capital, ChrysCapital, Sameeksha, Ambit, Pratap Securities) rather than lenders or partners, and the exit was explicitly held back until the incoming majority shareholder arrived — Ajaikumar said HCG was waiting for the new investor and had discussed it with them.

**How it evolved:** The idea surfaced on the Nov 2023 call, where Ajaikumar said post-COVID Milann had been through a tough time, a Delhi centre had been closed, and HCG was looking at divesting with no firm timeline; on the Mar 2025 call (Feb 27, 2025) he named the cause — the founder's non-compete expiring and her new centres next to HCG's — and said the timing of a divestment was still being decided. By May 2025 it hardened into intent: HCG was definitely putting a proposal to divest, hopefully within that fiscal year, having waited for and consulted the new investor (KKR/Hector). At the Dec 4, 2025 investor meet the new CEO Manish Mattoo said operations had been stabilised but the focus would be cancer care, with several strategic options under evaluation and divestment of the vertical named as one; Feb 2026 carried no update though revenue was already reported excluding fertility. It completed on May 19-20, 2026 — SPA signed May 19, board approval and pricing disclosed, closing guided to Q1 FY27 — and filings confirm BACC ceased to be a subsidiary from June 30, 2026.

**What management expects from it:** For HCG: management bandwidth and capital freed for the core oncology network (brownfield/greenfield, 1,000 beds by FY30), sharper single-specialty focus, modest cash (INR 37.6 crore, 75% upfront) on an already de-levered balance sheet (net debt/EBITDA 1.4x after the INR 425 crore rights issue). For Milann: a new owner able to infuse growth capital, scale it independently and carry its legacy forward. No margin or valuation uplift was quantified.

- *[Mar 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=c8b81c48-e01f-48a4-98c4-b270b8711902.pdf)* — Ajaikumar named the competitive cause of Milann's revenue dip — the founder's exit, expiry of her non-compete, and her new centres opening next to HCG's Kumara Park and J.P. So because of that, particularly in Kumara Park and J.P. Nagar, we have seen a dip in the revenue.”

## KSB — KSB Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a scheme of arrangement whose nature the documents on file do not settle) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 1.7/10 · scheme (nature unclear) · 1 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-09-28, latest 2026-09-28

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Pofran Sales and Agency Limited, an inoperative wholly owned subsidiary, being voluntarily struck off — not a business demerger — class `bad_business`.

- *Insiders:* not stated
- *What it reveals:* Nothing revealed: turnover, revenue, income and net worth contribution 'Not applicable' as Pofran has been inoperative since last 7 years; no consideration received
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — No shares distributed or new listing; a dormant subsidiary simply ceases to be a subsidiary on strike-off
- *Parent or spin:* neither · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Nuclear RCP test results after testing began 22 March 2026 and invoicing of two to four pumps
- *In their words:* “Pofran was incorporated on January 7, 2005 and was not operating for past seven years.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The texts do not support the premise: in the three years of calls and the one filing provided, KSB Ltd. announces no demerger, spin-off, slump sale or scheme of arrangement of any operating business, and management never gives a separation rationale. The only separation of any entity is administrative — the 28 Sep 2026 filing says Pofran Sales and Agency Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary incorporated on 7 January 2005, has applied for voluntary strike-off with the Registrar of Companies, Pune, and will cease to be a subsidiary on completion. The stated reason is simply dormancy: Pofran 'was not operating for past seven years' and 'has been inoperative since last 7 years.' The Annexure A disclosure confirms there is no economics to it — turnover/revenue/income and net worth contributed are 'Not applicable,' as are the sale agreement date, consideration, buyer details, related-party and arm's-length questions, and the regulation 37A / scheme-of-arrangement item; the only timeline given is 'according to the prescribed guidelines of voluntary strike off under Companies Act 2013.' No investor, lender or JV partner is said to have asked for it, and no cost, capital, focus or valuation benefit is claimed. The nearest portfolio decisions management does discuss run the other way or are exits, not separations: in Mar 2026 Rajeev Jain says of the BP&CL reciprocating-pump business that 'initially, we thought to sell it off, luckily we did not and we decided to build it ourselves,' and in Mar 2025 he describes having exited cast-iron foundry work (about 1,100 patterns and 3,000 metric tonnes) by handing it to third-party foundries, while FGD business 'suddenly overnight has vanished' because of a change in government regulation. Throughout, the strategy presented is consolidation and range-completion within one listed entity — nuclear (₹1,300 crore order book), solar (₹245 crore CY25 to 300+ crore CY26), valves, SupremeServ at ~15-17% of sales, firefighting, mining, exports at 17% — not separation of any of it.

**How it evolved:** The idea never surfaces in the calls: Mar 2024, Mar 2025, Sep 2025, Nov 2025 and Mar 2026 all discuss capacity additions (Shirwal and Sinnar sheds to be commissioned by March 2026), new segments and the group's willingness to localise more products, with no question or answer about demerging, hiving off or listing any division separately. Over this period the only direction of travel discussed is inward: BP&CL technology (acquired 2023) being built up rather than sold, and openness to further acquisitions ('if such opportunities occur in future, we are definitely exploring it', Sep 2025). The single separation event appears only in the 28 Sep 2026 filing, as the voluntary strike-off of the dormant shell Pofran Sales and Agency Limited. The plan therefore has no evolution to trace — one administrative cessation announced once, with no prior or subsequent discussion in the transcripts supplied.

**What management expects from it:** Nothing is claimed. The filing states only that Pofran ceases to be a subsidiary on completion; it attributes no revenue, income or net worth to it, names no consideration, and asserts no benefit to margins, capital, focus or valuation for KSB or for the struck-off entity. Management's stated goals stay unchanged: double-digit topline growth, 13-14% EBITDA, rising dividend.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The only separation disclosed is a voluntary strike-off application for the wholly owned subsidiary Pofran Sales and Agency Limited, filed with the Registrar of Companies, Pune; on completion Pofran ceases to be a subsidiary. “With reference to the captioned subject, we would like to inform you that Pofran Sales and Agency Limited ("Pofran"), a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company, has made an application for strike-off with the Registrar of Companies, Pune.”
- *Scheme* — The entire stated reason is dormancy — the entity, incorporated 7 January 2005, has not traded for seven years. No strategic, capital or valuation rationale is offered. “Pofran was incorporated on January 7, 2005 and was not operating for past seven years.”
- *Scheme* — Annexure A confirms the separated entity contributed nothing: turnover/revenue/income and net worth contribution are 'Not applicable' because it has been inoperative for seven years. “Pofran has been inoperative since last 7 years.”
- *Scheme* — There is no buyer, no consideration, no sale agreement and no related-party or arm's-length question, and the scheme-of-arrangement / regulation 37A item is 'Not applicable' — i.e. this is a dissolution, not a demerger or slump sale. “whether the sale, lease or disposal of the undertaking is outside Scheme of Arrangement? If yes, details of the same including compliance with regulation 37A of LODR Regulations Not applicable.”
- *Scheme* — The only timeline given is the statutory strike-off process under the Companies Act 2013, not a board-approved scheme with record dates or share entitlement ratios. “Time line according to the prescribed guidelines of voluntary strike off under Companies Act 2013.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Nothing in these three transcripts or the single filing describes MOIL separating, demerging, spinning off or hiving off any business — there is no scheme of arrangement, no record date, no resulting-company structure, no swap ratio, and no mention of investors, lenders or partners asking for a separation. Across all three Investors' and Analysts' Meets (Nov 2023, Aug 2024, Mar 2026) management consistently frames MOIL as one integrated manganese miner that it intends to grow, not divide: 10 mines (7 underground, 3 opencast) in Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh, ~50-52% of Indian manganese ore production, plus two small downstream units — the 12,000 tpa ferromanganese plant at Balaghat and the 1,500 tpa EMD plant at Dongri Buzurg — which are described as segments to be grown, not detached. In Mar 2026, Director Finance Rakesh Tumane explicitly minimises the ferroalloy unit rather than proposing to separate it: capacity 12,000 tons per year, "it's not going to have any impact" and "not something impactful thing here." The only corporate-structure actions discussed are additive and outward: proposed joint ventures (GMDC in Gujarat at 51% MOIL / 49% GMDC on a 9.5 million-ton resource, MP State Mining Corporation for Bhudkum and Selva blocks, CMDC for 218 sq km in Nilkanthpur/Balrampur, Chhattisgarh), DIPAM and NITI Aayog approvals for JV formation, INR275 crore earmarked for overseas acquisition within a INR600 crore FY26 capex target, and a possible third-party beneficiation plant near the mines if MOIL can commit ~3 lakh tons per annum of low-grade ore. The lone filing provided (28.05.2026) is unrelated to any restructuring: it is a request to waive an NSE fine of Rs 5,31,000 for non-compliance with Regulation 17(1) of SEBI LODR because the Ministry of Steel / President of India has not appointed enough Independent Directors. On these texts alone, the premise of a separation cannot be supported, so no rationale, no cited numbers justifying a split, and no requesting stakeholder can be reconstructed.

**How it evolved:** Nov 2023 (17.11.2023): only JV/MoU expansion is raised — GMDC (9.5 mt resource, proposed 51:49), MPSMC, CMDC — alongside buybacks, dividends and capex of INR245-295 crore; no separation. Aug 2024 (23.08.2024): the same JV path advances ("nearing the signing of joint venture with GMDC"), plus EC expansion from 24.88 lakh to 50 lakh tons and the 3.5 million-ton-by-2030 goal; still no separation. Mar 2026 (17.03.2026): DIPAM/NITI Aayog approvals for the GMDC and MP JVCs, a possible third-party beneficiation tie-up and INR275 crore for overseas assets — all additions to MOIL, never a carve-out of an existing business. The 28.05.2026 filing concerns only board-composition non-compliance and an NSE penalty waiver.

**What management expects from it:** Not stated for any separation, because none is described. Management's stated expectations concern MOIL as a single entity: 3.5 million tons of ore and ~32% market share by 2030, EC raised from 36.33 to 50 lakh tons, cost of production falling from ~INR5,500 to ~INR5,300 per ton via mechanisation and long-hole open stoping, and continued high returns on equity.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** No demerger disclosed; Nutraceutical Business and Nestlé Business Services Division were earlier slump-sold per filings — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* not stated
- *What it reveals:* Scheme of Arrangement reclassified Rs. 8,374.3 million from General Reserve to Retained Earnings; Rs. 964.2 million capitalised as 1:1 bonus (Aug 2025) and Rs. 3,856.6 million now paid as Special Dividend 2026, returning reserve cash to shareholders.
- *Selling pressure:* unclear — Documents disclose only a cash dividend record date; no demerged entity, share allotment or index change is mentioned.
- *Parent or spin:* unclear · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* The Scheme of Arrangement at nestle.in/investors/stockandfinancials/scheme-arrangement, and residual reclassified reserve balance
- *In their words:* “Pursuant to the Scheme of Arrangement (“Scheme”) sanctioned by the Hon'ble National Company Law Tribunal, New Delhi Bench, vide its Order dated 15th September 2023, which became effective from 19th October 2023 (“NCLT Order”), an amount of Rs. 8,374.3 million was reclassified from General Reserve to Retained Earnings (“Reclassified Amount under the Scheme”).”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The texts describe two separate things that both fall under 'separation', and neither is a classic demerger of a listed business into a new listed entity. First, Nestlé India carved out businesses by slump sale: the Nutraceutical Business was transferred to Dr. Reddy's and Nestlé Health Science Limited — a 49:51 joint venture (Nestlé India 49%, Dr. Reddy's 51%) that 'came together only in July of last year' (July 2024) — and the Nestlé Business Services Division was transferred to Nestlé Business Services India Private Limited (formerly Purina PetCare India Private Limited), a Nestlé affiliate; the gains on both appear as exceptional items of Rs 2,908.2 million standalone and Rs 1,834.2 million consolidated for the nine months to 31 December 2024 and FY ended 31 March 2025. The only rationale management gave, in the 4 February 2025 analyst meet, was capability complementarity rather than any problem with the parent: Nestlé India is 'a consumer product company with a more limited health care exposure as compared to Dr. Reddy's which is a health care company', so the JV 'combin[es] the synergies of product portfolio and distribution reach' to attack an addressable health-science/nutrition opportunity management sized at 'INR 24,000 Crores', with Nestlé Health Science products to be 'by and large manufactured locally' using Nestlé's R&D base (INR 1.8 billion R&D spend in CY2023, 4,000+ employees, 23 sites). Suresh Narayanan reported the integration as 'successful', the teams 'working well together', 'double digit growth', and new launches on the anvil from both the Nestlé Health Science and Dr. Reddy's portfolios; he sits on the JV board. Second, and legally distinct, a Scheme of Arrangement sanctioned by the NCLT New Delhi Bench on 15 September 2023 and effective 19 October 2023 reclassified Rs 8,374.3 million from General Reserve to Retained Earnings — a balance-sheet/distributable-reserve action, out of which Rs 964.2 million was capitalised for the 1:1 bonus issue in August 2025 and the residual Rs 7,410.1 million funds the Rs 2 per share Special Dividend 2026 (Rs 3,856.6 million). Post-separation, the JV is accounted for as an associate, not consolidated, and Nestlé India's consolidated accounts carry a charge for its share of the associate's result (Rs 164.4 million in Q1 FY2026-27, Rs 423.1 million for 9M FY2025-26 and Rs 455.2 million for FY2025-26), so the carved-out business is currently a drag on consolidated versus standalone earnings. Nowhere in these texts did management cite investor, lender or regulatory pressure as the reason; no analyst on the 4 February 2025 call asked a single question about the slump sales or the Scheme.

**How it evolved:** Only one earnings call falls in the window, and the separation was already largely done by then: the Scheme of Arrangement was sanctioned on 15 September 2023 and became effective 19 October 2023, and the Dr. Reddy's JV 'came together only in July of last year', i.e. July 2024, with the slump-sale gains booked in the nine months to 31 December 2024 and FY ended 31 March 2025. At the 4 February 2025 analyst and institutional investors meet, Narayanan presented the JV twice — once as a 'rising health consciousness' growth platform with an INR 24,000 crore opportunity and once under 'Partnerships' as 'the first of its kind in India for Nestlé' — reporting successful integration and double-digit growth, but gave no rationale for the Scheme itself and no financials for the transferred businesses. In every filing after that (30 January 2026 results, 3 July 2026 dividend intimation, 22 July 2026 Q1 results) the Scheme appears only mechanically, as the source of the reclassified Rs 8,374.3 million used for the August 2025 1:1 bonus and the Rs 2 per share Special Dividend 2026; the only new structural step disclosed is the 30 January 2026 in-principle approval of 26% stakes in two captive renewable SPVs with Adani Green Energy and Radiance Renewables, which is not a business separation.

**What management expects from it:** For the JV: combined portfolio plus Dr. Reddy's healthcare distribution attacking an INR 24,000 crore opportunity, local manufacturing using Nestlé R&D, new launches from both portfolios, and continued double-digit growth. For Nestlé India: focus on its core five-six categories plus premiumisation, with the Scheme's reclassified reserves funding the 1:1 bonus and the Rs 2 special dividend. No margin, capital-release or valuation claims were made.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The slump sales are identified as exceptional items for 9M to 31 December 2024 and FY ended 31 March 2025: the Nutraceutical Business went to the Dr. Reddy's JV and the Nestlé Business Services Division to a Nestlé affiliate (formerly Purina PetCare India Private Limited); gains were Rs 2,908.2 million standalone and Rs 1,834.2 million consolidated. “Exceptional items for the nine months ended 31st December 2024 and financial year ended 31st March 2025 comprise of gain on slump sale of the following businesses: Nutraceutical Business to Dr. Reddy's and Nestlé Health Science Limited. Nestlé Business Services Division to Nestlé Business Services India Private Limited (Formerly known as Purina PetCare India Private Limited ).”
- *Scheme* — The Scheme of Arrangement, separate from the slump sales, was sanctioned by the NCLT New Delhi Bench on 15 September 2023 and effective 19 October 2023, and its only disclosed effect is the reclassification of Rs 8,374.3 million from General Reserve to Retained Earnings. “Pursuant to the Scheme of Arrangement (“Scheme” ) sanctioned by the Hon'ble National Company Law Tribunal, New Delhi Bench, vide its Order dated  15th September 2023, which became effective from 19th October 2023 ( “NCLT Order ”), an amount of Rs. 8,374.3 million was reclassified from General Reserve to Retained Earnings ( “Reclassified Amount under the Scheme” ).”
- *Scheme* — The reclassified reserve has been used for shareholder returns: Rs 964.2 million capitalised for the 1:1 bonus issue in August 2025, leaving Rs 7,410.1 million from which the Rs 2 per share Special Dividend 2026 (Rs 3,856.6 million) is paid on and from 30 July 2026. “Out of the Reclassified Amount  under the Scheme, Rs. 964.2 million was capitalised through the issuance of bonus equity shares in the ratio of 1:1 in August  2025. The aforesaid Special Dividend 2026 shall be paid out of the balance reclassified amount of R s. 7,410.1 million included  in the Total Retained Earnings of the Company as at 31st March 2026.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=cce29c06-5e1f-4c2a-9585-327e6d47710c.pdf)* — The stated rationale for putting the nutraceutical/health-science portfolio into the JV is capability mismatch inside Nestlé India versus Dr. Reddy's healthcare reach, with the two portfolios combined in a 49:51 structure. “We are a consumer product c ompany with a more limited health care 
exposure as compared to Dr. Reddy's which is a health care c ompany .”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=cce29c06-5e1f-4c2a-9585-327e6d47710c.pdf)* — Management framed the separation as a first-of-its-kind partnership for Nestlé in India whose logic is pooling portfolio and distribution reach rather than fixing a problem in the parent. “One is this partnership you would say that we got into it . This is the first of its 
kind in India for Nestlé, a joint venture partnership with Dr. Reddy's. And I 
think it is combining the synergies of product portfolio and distribution reach.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=cce29c06-5e1f-4c2a-9585-327e6d47710c.pdf)* — The size of the prize management cited for the separated health-science business was INR 24,000 crore, explicitly described as a large opportunity rather than a firm forecast. “I talked there about INR 24,000 
Crores, that is just a number. But it is a large opportunity.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=cce29c06-5e1f-4c2a-9585-327e6d47710c.pdf)* — Narayanan reported post-separation execution: integration done from July 2024, teams working together, double-digit growth, and new launches planned from both parents' portfolios, with himself on the JV board. “They came together only in July of last year, but I think the integration has been strong and solid. They have shown double digit growth, which is also encouraging.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=cce29c06-5e1f-4c2a-9585-327e6d47710c.pdf)* — Nestlé India retains a manufacturing and R&D role for the separated products, so the carve-out is of the commercial/portfolio layer rather than a full exit of capability. “The Nestlé Health Science products that will be
part of the Dr. Reddy's portfolio will be by and large manufactured locally, which really means that we will be getting some of the expertise from the R&D facilities to be able to do that as we move forward.”
- *Scheme* — Post-separation the JV is an associate, not consolidated, and Nestlé India's consolidated results carry its share of the associate's result as a deduction — Rs 164.4 million in Q1 FY2026-27, Rs 423.1 million for 9M FY2025-26 and Rs 455.2 million for FY2025-26 — so consolidated EPS (Rs 4.97) trails standalone (Rs 5.06). “The Statement includes the results of the following entities:
Holding Company
a) Nestle India Limited
Associate
a) Dr. Reddy's and Nestle Health Science Limited”

*Not explained on the calls:* No stated rationale for the Scheme itself; no revenue, margin, asset or valuation detail for the carved-out Nutraceutical or Business Services units; no mention of investor, lender or regulatory demand; no analyst questions on it.
