## PNCINFRA — PNC Infratech Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a scheme of arrangement whose nature the documents on file do not settle) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 1.7/10 · scheme (nature unclear) · 1 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-03-27, latest 2026-03-27

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Entire stake in road SPV PNC Challakere (Karnataka) Highways Private Limited — final of twelve identified SPVs sold — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* Buyer does not belong to promoter/promoter group/group companies; no promoter or management stake in Vertis stated. Shareholders approved by special resolution dated 28 September 2024.
- *What it reveals:* Sale is for cash, not a listed spin: Rs 683.84 crore EV on an SPV contributing 1.30% of consolidated revenue and 2.42% of net worth; consolidated cash Rs 2,856 crore, Rs 1,100 crore of it inside PNC Infra Holdings.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — No new listed security or share distribution; assets transferred to an InvIT for cash, parent remains sole listed entity.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Monetisation framework for the remaining 14 HAM assets (5 with PCOD) and PNC Infra Holdings cash deployment.
- *In their words:* “This transaction marked the completion of the final tranche of the strategic divestment of 12 assets announced in January 2024.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

There is no demerger or spin-off scheme in these texts: the 'separation' PNC Infratech describes is a staged, 100% equity divestment of a ring-fenced road-concession portfolio — 12 SPVs comprising 11 National Highway HAM projects plus 1 State Highway BOT-Toll project, spanning about 3,800 lane-km — to KKR-backed Highways Infrastructure Trust (later renamed Vertis Infrastructure Trust), under definitive agreements/SPA dated 15 January 2024, approved by shareholders by special resolution on 28 September 2024 and executed explicitly 'outside Scheme of Arrangement' (Reg 37A), completing on 27 March 2026 with PNC Challakere (Karnataka) Highways. Management's stated purpose was capital recycling and de-leveraging: the 12 SPVs carried Rs 6,480 crore of project debt, and after tranche 1 consolidated debt fell from Rs 9,345 crore to about Rs 4,300 crore, taking net debt/equity from 1.56x to 0.72x (0.76x by FY26). The realization was pitched at roughly 1.67x equity invested at SPA signing — tranche 1 (10 HAM SPVs, closed 22 May 2025) fetched Rs 1,827.6 crore equity consideration against Rs 1,371 crore invested, plus about Rs 200 crore of back-to-back receivables and Rs 624 crore of change-of-scope works (Rs 584 crore received); Bareilly-Nainital BOT-Toll closed 31 July 2025 at Rs 716.2 crore enterprise value (Rs 153.48 crore equity, Rs 239.35 crore unsecured loan, Rs 80 crore further receivables); Challakere closed at Rs 683.84 crore EV (Rs 80.48 crore equity, Rs 134.94 crore unsecured loans) against Rs 114 crore equity invested, having contributed only 1.30% of FY25 consolidated revenue (Rs 164.03 crore) and 2.42% of consolidated net worth. Gains were booked in the holding subsidiary PNC Infra Holdings (about Rs 460 crore pre-tax, Rs 400 crore post-tax), with no gain in standalone, and roughly Rs 2,200 crore net of debt was collected across 11 assets, leaving Rs 1,100–1,300 crore of cash in PNC Infra Holdings. That cash was explicitly 'earmarked' for fund-based project equity — Rs 1,744 crore of HAM equity commitments (Rs 663 crore, later Rs 542 crore, still to be infused) and about Rs 400 crore for the NHPC solar-plus-BESS SPV — and a buyback was explicitly ruled out. Management also tied the lighter balance sheet to bidding power: with cash and investing capacity it could bid large HAM and BOT-Toll projects directly, where competition is 'moderate' versus 'cutthroat' EPC. The counterparty, not investors or lenders, drove the deal; lenders and the authority were only consent-givers (NOCs from 34 lenders across 11 projects, NHAI in-principle change-of-control approvals obtained asset by asset).

**How it evolved:** The programme was announced with the 15 January 2024 definitive agreements and was tracked purely as execution thereafter: by Nov 2024 management split it into 10 assets (equity value Rs 1,490 crore, enterprise value ~Rs 7,690 crore) for FY25 and 2 assets for FY26, and said the MoRTH debarment did not disturb it. Feb 2025 was about consents — 34 lender NOCs for 11 projects and NHAI in-principle approvals for 8 of 11 — with the target raised to 11 assets by March 2025; Jun 2025 reported tranche 1 of 10 HAM SPVs closed 22 May 2025 at Rs 1,827.6 crore (after a negative Rs 378 crore descoping adjustment that explained the slip from the Rs 2,900 crore headline) and consolidated debt down to ~Rs 4,300 crore. Aug 2025 added Bareilly-Nainital (11 of 12 done), Nov 2025 confirmed the last change-of-control approval and Rs 2,200 crore received net of debt, and Feb 2026 showed the proceeds landing in cash (standalone cash jumping to Rs 1,299 crore 'includes the proceeds received from the KKR') while a second-round divestment of the newer HAM assets was only 'evaluating all the options' with investors approaching. The 27 March 2026 filing and the May 2026 call closed the loop: all twelve SPVs transferred, described as the final tranche of the strategic divestment announced in January 2024, with the next monetisation framework still undecided.

**What management expects from it:** For PNC: consolidated debt down (Rs 9,345 crore to ~Rs 4,300 crore, 1.56x to 0.72x), ~Rs 2,200 crore cash net of debt realised at ~1.67x equity invested, held in PNC Infra Holdings and earmarked for Rs 1,744 crore HAM equity plus ~Rs 400 crore solar/BESS equity, no debt-funded equity, no buyback; a balance sheet that supports direct bidding for large HAM/BOT-Toll with less competition. For the buyer-trust: operating concessions transferred with their debt.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The 27 March 2026 filing records the transfer of PNC Challakere (Karnataka) Highways to Vertis Infrastructure Trust at Rs 683.84 crore enterprise value (Rs 80.48 crore equity, Rs 134.94 crore unsecured loans), completing all twelve SPVs under the 15 January 2024 SPA; it is a sale outside any scheme of arrangement, shareholder-approved by special resolution on 28 September 2024, and the asset was only 1.30% of FY25 consolidated revenue and 2.42% of consolidated net worth. “Now, the Company has completed transfer of all the twelve identified Special Purpose Vehicles ("SPVs") pursuant to the Share Purchase Agreement ("SPA') dated January 15,2024 (as amended from time to time).”
- *[Jun 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=399c2ca5-73ea-4207-90b6-9f1363814953.pdf)* — Management described the perimeter of the separation: 12 road assets, 11 NH HAM plus 1 state BOT-Toll, about 3,800 lane-km, sold to KKR-backed Highways Infrastructure Trust in two tranches under January 2024 definitive agreements. “Earlier, in January 2024, the Company had signed definitive agreements with HIT to divest a total of 12 road assets, comprising 11 National Highway HAM projects and 1 State Highway BOT – Toll project spanning approximately 3,800 lane -km, to be transacted in two tranches.”
- *[Jun 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=399c2ca5-73ea-4207-90b6-9f1363814953.pdf)* — The de-leveraging effect was quantified immediately after tranche 1: consolidated debt fell from Rs 9,345 crore to about Rs 4,300 crore and net debt/equity from 1.56x to 0.72x. “After completion of monetization of the 10 assets, as on date the debt got reduced to Rs. 4300.00 crores, which translates net debt to equity of 0.72 times as against 1.56 times.”
- *[Jun 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=399c2ca5-73ea-4207-90b6-9f1363814953.pdf)* — Tranche 1 economics: Rs 1,827.6 crore equity consideration for 10 HAM SPVs against Rs 1,371 crore of equity invested, plus about Rs 200 crore of back-to-back receivables and Rs 624 crore of change-of-scope works executed (Rs 546–584 crore already received). “Tranche 1 comprised of 10 HAM assets concluded for an equity consideration of Rs. 1,827.6 Crore, after adjustments on account of certain items of works descoped in these 10 projects.”
- *[Jun 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=399c2ca5-73ea-4207-90b6-9f1363814953.pdf)* — Asked what they would do with the surplus, management said the proceeds would go into new fund-based PPP mandates in HAM, selectively BOT-Toll, and other central-agency fund-based projects (solar, battery storage, smart metering), judiciously and after due diligence. “Yes, we are pursuing quite a few fund-based projects on a PPP mode l, both in the sectors where we are very much active in roads, highway sector, like HAM projects and very judiciously we will do look at the BOT toll projects also.”
- *[Nov 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=27af90d2-8d19-49d0-a91b-517c2251b3e6.pdf)* — Sizing of the two tranches and the enterprise value being taken off the consolidated balance sheet: 10 assets at Rs 1,490 crore equity value out of Rs 1,739 crore for all 12, against roughly Rs 7,690 crore enterprise value and Rs 6,480 crore of SPV debt. “The 10 assets equity value is INR1,490 crores as against the INR1,739 crores of 12 assets, and enterprise value will be around INR7,690 crores.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=4859bfe9-8716-4753-9774-34f24238d98a.pdf)* — The separation was gated on third-party consents rather than on any investor demand: NOCs from 34 lenders across 11 projects and NHAI in-principle change-of-control approvals (8 of 11 received, 3 pending). “So, there are NOCs required from lenders as well as from the authority and out of the 12 assets, we have already received the NOCs of 11 projects from 34 lenders as of date.”
- *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=4859bfe9-8716-4753-9774-34f24238d98a.pdf)* — The valuation yardstick management had guided to was about 1.67x the equity invested, measured at the time of signing the share purchase agreement. “Earlier we have given in our note, about 1.67 times of the equity invested at the time of signing of the share purchase agreement.”
- *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=d5326993-b516-4f4f-8de0-5ed916d00cb4.pdf)* — Bareilly Nainital, the single BOT-Toll state highway asset, closed on 31 July 2025 at Rs 716.2 crore enterprise value (Rs 153.48 crore equity, Rs 239.35 crore unsecured loan, Rs 80 crore further receivables), taking the count to 11 of 12. “With the successful transfer of PNC Bareilly Nainital Highways Private Limited, the Company has now completed the 100% equity divestment in 11 out of the 12 assets under the definitive agreement executed for the equity sale last year.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=9fff26a5-f259-4fd7-84f8-e4eb1708ee19.pdf)* — Management stated the proceeds are reserved for equity in fund-based projects — Rs 663 crore of HAM equity and about Rs 400 crore for the solar-cum-BESS SPV, funded from PNC Infra Holdings cash plus internal accruals, with no debt funding of equity and a buyback explicitly rejected. “We will be basically, for the fund -based projects, we have earmark ed this money.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=9fff26a5-f259-4fd7-84f8-e4eb1708ee19.pdf)* — Shareholder return was explicitly not the use of proceeds; large-value HAM bids and TBCB transmission/solar/BESS projects were named as the destination instead. “No. As of now, we are not considering the buyback of this thing.”
- *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=9fff26a5-f259-4fd7-84f8-e4eb1708ee19.pdf)* — Final asset economics disclosed: Rs 114 crore equity invested in the last HAM SPV against about Rs 630 crore enterprise value with Rs 394 crore of original debt, and Rs 2,200 crore net of debt already received for the 11 closed assets (Rs 200 crore holdback, Rs 38–42 crore received so far). “For the 11 asset, the net receivable net of debt was Rs. 2,200 crore , which we have received.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No stated hurdle IRR or valuation method, no transaction costs/tax detail, no InvIT-unit or sponsor-stake option, no framework or timing for monetising the remaining 14 assets.

### The business being separated — its own numbers

**Toll & Annuity (BOT projects/OMT/Maintenance of Narela industrial park) — consolidated reportable segment; the documents carry NO separate financials for the divested portfolio itself (12 road assets / SPVs sold to Vertis Infrastructure Trust, formerly Highways Infrastructure Trust)** · unit ₹ Lakhs · Revenue = 'Segment Revenue — Toll Annuity' from consolidated Operating Segment Information; segment revenue includes sales and other income directly identifiable/allocable to the segment including inter-segment revenue, though reported inter-segment revenue is nil, so the figure equals net revenue from operations for the segment. Operating_profit = 'Segment Results' for Toll Annuity, i.e. segment result after directly allocable expenses but before unallocable expenditure (which includes most finance cost), unallocable income and tax — closer to EBIT than EBITDA, and NOT PBT. PAT is not disclosed segment-wise. This is the Group's whole toll/annuity segment, not the carved-out entity: it mixes the divested HAM/toll SPVs with retained assets (Gwalior-Bhind, Rae Bareli-Jaunpur, Narela), and FY2026 figures already reflect part-year ownership of the assets sold during FY2026.

## TEXRAIL — Texmaco Rail & Eng. Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a scheme of arrangement whose nature the documents on file do not settle) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 1.7/10 · scheme (nature unclear) · 1 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-07-24, latest 2026-07-24

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** No demerger; defence business in subsidiary Texmaco Defence Technologies Ltd (TDTL), diluted from 100% to 70% by outside subscription — class `regulatory_strategic`.

- *Insiders:* Company retains 70% of TDTL. "Promoter/ Promoter group/ Group does not have any interest in Calculus." No promoter stake in TDTL stated; parent LTIP 2026 grants up to 24,00,000 options at Re. 1 face value.
- *What it reveals:* TDTL had nil revenue and net worth of Rs. 0.01 crore as on 31st March 2026, yet Calculus subscribes for 30% within a Rs. 200 Crores investment — a pre-revenue defence vehicle being externally valued inside a wagon maker.
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — No shares distributed to shareholders; TDTL remains an unlisted 70% subsidiary, so no index exclusion or industry-mismatch selling.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* The SSSA terms and TDTL's implied valuation from Calculus's Rs. 100 Crores equity subscription for 30%
- *In their words:* “Upon completion of the proposed subscription, Calculus shall hold 30% of the equity share capital of TDTL, and TDTL shall accordingly cease to be a wholly-owned subsidiary and shall become a subsidiary of the Company.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The business being separated is Texmaco's EPC arm — the 'Infra – Rail & Green Energy' segment (the erstwhile Kalindee business plus Hydromechanical & Bridge works) — which the Board decided to transfer as a going concern on a slump-exchange basis into a 100% subsidiary of Texmaco Rail (a participant on the Feb 2025 call called the transferee 'BEL'; Belgharia Engineering Udyog Pvt Ltd appears as a wholly owned subsidiary in the filings). Management's stated reason is that this EPC vertical was the one persistent loss-maker dragging a profitable wagon/foundry company: Q1 FY25 segment EBIT loss of Rs 10.1 crores, FY25 segment revenue of only Rs 438 crores with 'infra business did not make much profit' (versus Freight Car Rs 4,300 crores and Bright Power electrification at Rs 368 crores revenue, 16% EBITDA, Rs 44 crores PBIT), and in FY26 a segment loss of Rs 27.4 crores on Rs 348 crores of revenue — all attributed to a handful of 'legacy contracts' they were trying to complete or short-close, against which large unrealised claims from government customers were pending. The separation was framed as a way to ring-fence those legacy liabilities and claims, give the EPC business its own focused management and revive it, 'unlock value, enhance organizational focus and streamline business operations across key verticals,' while repositioning it away from conventional EPC towards niche rail infra, systems and solutions, signalling, ballastless track, auto-fare collection and safety — where the Union Budget outlay (Rs 2.5 lakh crore in FY26, a record Rs 2.93 lakh crore in FY27) is concentrated. It also sits inside a broader restructuring: wagon assets were consolidated (Texmaco West Rail amalgamated into the parent, effective 1 April 2025), while non-core activities were pushed out or into separate vehicles — a freed 12-acre prime land parcel in Kolkata became a separate Real Estate division because 'the competency requirement for development of land is totally different from making wagons', defence was put into Texmaco Defence Technologies Ltd (Rs 200 crores committed, later diluted to 70% with Calculus/Vagus taking 30%), and the Touax leasing JV stake went from 50% to 34% with TrinityRail joining. Nobody outside demanded the hive-off: investors (UTI Mutual Fund, Nuvama, Dalal & Broacha) repeatedly pressed on the infra drag and the weak consolidated margin versus Titagarh/Jupiter, and the lenders were an obstacle rather than a requester — banks withheld clearances and wanted a counter/corporate guarantee from the parent, which management said 'doesn't make much sense to us'. Management insisted it was not a sale or monetisation: 'We want to continue with this business. We see tremendous future for the EPC business.' By FY27 the segment had turned positive (Q1 FY27 segment result +Rs 0.82 crores) and management said the legacy aberrations would be over, which is the outcome they said the separation was meant to produce.

**How it evolved:** The idea was already live and stalled by the Aug 2024 call (14 Aug 2024): exchange no-objection obtained, but held up by bank clearances, corporate-guarantee demands and the unsettled strategy for the new company, with an NCLT timeline of 9-12 months and shareholders' interest cited as the reason it stayed 'work in progress'. By Oct 2024 (28 Oct 2024) management said approval was received and it was 'committed for the separation of that wing', pushed by an investor calling the segment 'a drag on our profitability'. The structure was fixed at the Feb 2025 call (3 Feb 2025) — a slump-exchange transfer of the EPC group as a going concern into a 100% subsidiary, 12-15 months to complete — and by May 2025 (17 May 2025) the scheme had been filed with the stock exchanges, queries answered, NOCs in progress and final approval expected January 2026, now justified as 'unlocking value' and a repositioning into niche rail infra and signalling. After that the scheme largely drops out: Nov 2025 reports only the opposite-direction Texmaco West amalgamation plus the 12 acres of land freed by 'restructuring', Feb 2026 and May 2026 (13 May 2026) speak only of the legacy contracts winding down, a new Real Estate division, Texmaco 2.0 and defence being carved into a subsidiary.

**What management expects from it:** For the EPC/Infra-Rail & Green Energy entity: focused management, revival from losses, exit from legacy contracts, a shift to niche rail infra, signalling and systems with higher margins. For the parent: a streamlined structure, operational efficiency, value unlocking, margins moving from ~10% toward mid-teens and 'beyond mid-teens', and freed prime land monetised through a separate real estate division.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *CALL Aug 2024* — The demerger was already under way but stuck on lenders: exchanges had given no-objection, while banks had not cleared it and were seeking a counter/corporate guarantee from the parent, which management rejected as illogical; NCLT alone was expected to take 9-12 months. “In the meanwhile, we also have to discuss and finalize the arrangement with the banks because currently we don't have the clearances from them with a counter guarantee, corporate guarantee, which doesn't make much sense to us.”
- *CALL Aug 2024* — CFO quantified the problem being separated — the Infra-Rail & Green Energy segment (Kalindee, Hydromechanical and Bridge) posted an EBIT loss of Rs 10.1 crores in Q1 FY25, driven by a few legacy contracts management wanted to complete or short-close. “They had reported a loss of INR10.1 crores over EBIT. The main reason of it is that yes, there are a few legacy contracts which are being continued, which management has full focus on how do we close this contract, either close and complete or how can we short-close this contract.”
- *CALL Aug 2024* — Vice Chairman added that these same legacy EPC contracts carry large unrealised claims against government customers that take years to recover — the overhang the separation was meant to isolate. “I'd like to add Hemant on to your comments by saying that most of these contracts there are a huge amount of potential claims, which we have not yet got paid.”
- *CALL Oct 2024* — An institutional investor (UTI Mutual Fund) framed the segment as a drag on group profitability and asked for the demerger status; the MD confirmed approval was in hand and the company was committed to separating the wing, declining to promise FY25 completion because of statutory processes. “So Nikhil, we have received the approval, and you know that these things require a kind of a process.”
- *CALL Feb 2025* — The structure was disclosed: the EPC group would be transferred as an ongoing business on a slump-exchange basis into a 100% subsidiary of Texmaco Rail, expected to take 12-15 months, alongside the inward merger of Texmaco West Rail. “Additionally, as part of our business organization, we also decided to transfer the Infra -Rail and Green Energy, which is our EPC group primarily, as an ongoing business on a slump exchange basis into a 100% subsidiary of Texmaco Rail.”
- *CALL Feb 2025* — Asked directly whether the EPC business would be monetised after the slump exchange, management said no — it is being separated to be grown and made profitable like the wagon business, given budget focus on track-laying and signalling. “We want to continue with this business.”
- *CALL Feb 2025* — In closing remarks the Vice Chairman tied the separation to risk control and a careful, blip-free move into new areas (passenger mobility via the Saira interiors acquisition), explicitly naming the demerged business. “That's the reason we have decided to demerge the EPC business, which is the Infra -Rail & Green Energy business.”
- *CALL May 2025* — Opening remarks gave the formal rationale for both restructuring legs — the West Rail merger and the Infra-Rail & Green business transfer — as value unlocking, organisational focus and streamlining. “The proposed merger of Texmaco West Rail Limited, which was erstwhile Jindal Rail Manufacturing Company and business transfer of Infra-Rail and Green are expected to unlock value, enhance organizational focus and streamline business operations across key verticals.”
- *CALL May 2025* — CFO gave the procedural status and the only completion date ever put on record: the scheme had been filed with the stock exchanges, exchange queries answered, NOCs being worked on, with final approval expected in January 2026. “We are working with the NOCs , and we are expecting final approval in January 26.”
- *CALL May 2025* — The MD said the act of taking up the demerger had itself already reduced losses, and that the purpose was a focused approach to revive the business and reposition it from conventional EPC into niche rail infra, systems, solutions and signalling, domestically and on select international projects. “But this was the whole purpose that we have a very focused approach to revive that when we have huge positive traction so far the orders progress in the market and the government push to improve the infrastructure.”
- *CALL May 2025* — The Vice Chairman noted the consolidated FY25 margin of 10.3% was achieved despite the infra segment making almost no profit — the arithmetic case for ring-fencing it (Infra-Rail & Green Energy FY25 revenue Rs 438 crores versus Freight Car Rs 4,300 crores and Bright Power Rs 368 crores at 16% EBITDA, Rs 44 crores PBIT). “This is, I think, in spite of the fact that our infra business did not make much profit.”
- *CALL Nov 2025* — The restructuring of the non-wagon businesses (hydromechanical power station equipment, bridges) freed a 12-acre land parcel in Kolkata, which management decided to develop rather than sell in a distressed sale, adding a land-unlocking motive to the reorganisation. “By restructuring all this, we have seen that we have a land parcel.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No valuation, consideration, debt/guarantee allocation, capital structure or listing plan for the transferee; no quantified value unlock; and no confirmation the scheme actually completed after the January 2026 target.

## TSFINV — TSF Investments Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a scheme of arrangement whose nature the documents on file do not settle) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 1.7/10 · scheme (nature unclear) · 1 filing(s) from BSE-screener · first 2026-09-09, latest 2026-09-09

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'nclt_sanction' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

**The stages, as filed:** nclt_sanction (2026-09-09)

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** not stated; documents describe an amalgamation of Forge 2000 into Axles India, not a separation — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* Not stated for Axles India. Promoter Sundaram Finance not interested; promoter group Srivats Ram (WIL Chairman & MD), Gita Ram, Nivedita Ram subscribe Rs.30 Cr in Wheels India issue
- *What it reveals:* No separation value shown. Reveals TSF deploying Rs.150 Cr internal accruals into 25.007%-held Wheels India (turnover Rs.5124.40 Cr, PAT Rs.138.56 Cr, net worth Rs.974.53 Cr) to cut WIL debt toward peer leverage
- *Selling pressure:* unlikely — Intra-group merger of unlisted subsidiaries; no shares distributed to TSF shareholders and no index change stated
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* NCLT order dated 27 August 2026 for share exchange ratio and Axles India post-merger financials
- *In their words:* “The proposed capital infusion will enable your Associate Company to repay or reduce its Debt thereby enhancing the leverage position, narrowing the gap to the peer averages and ensuring adequate headroom for sustained growth.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

These texts do not describe TSF Investments separating, demerging or spinning off any business — nothing in the six filings proposes a separation, and no earnings-call transcripts are on file, so no management rationale for a separation exists in this record. What the filings actually show is the opposite direction of travel: consolidation of the group's holdings. On 19 August 2026 the Board and Audit Committee approved subscribing to a preferential private-placement issue by associate Wheels India Limited (WIL) — initially 10,57,827 shares at ₹1,418 (premium ₹1,408), aggregating not more than ₹150 Crores — stating the objective as 'To consolidate the shareholdings in Wheels India Ltd (associate company)'; TSF already held 61,09,914 shares, or 25.007%, of WIL. Management's stated reasoning was that TSF, as an Exempted Core Investment Company, was 'looking at better investment opportunities to optimize returns on investments and also consolidating its shareholdings in its Group Companies', and that the capital infusion would let WIL 'repay or reduce its Debt thereby enhancing the leverage position, narrowing the gap to the peer averages and ensuring adequate headroom for sustained growth'; funds at WIL were earmarked for 'Debt Reduction' and TSF's source of funds was 'Internal accruals'. Scale numbers cited: WIL FY2025-26 standalone turnover ₹5,124.40 Cr, PAT ₹138.56 Cr, net worth ₹974.53 Cr (turnover ₹4,424.86 Cr in 2024-25, ₹4,619.03 Cr in 2023-24); TSF's own FY2025-26 consolidated turnover ₹985 Cr, making the materiality threshold ₹98.50 Cr, so the deal (15.23% of TSF turnover, 2.74% of WIL turnover) needed shareholder approval as a material related-party transaction under Reg. 23(4). The second structural item is also a combination, not a separation: the NCLT, Chennai, by order dated 27 August 2026 (uploaded 8 September 2026), sanctioned the amalgamation of wholly-owned subsidiary Forge 2000 Private Limited into subsidiary Axles India Limited; no reasons for that merger are given in these filings. The only parties shown asking for a change were the exchange and the regulator — NSE advised WIL to reprice the issue — not investors, lenders or partners seeking a separation.

**How it evolved:** No separation idea surfaces anywhere in this record, and there are no earnings calls to trace it through. The consolidation plan appears on 19 August 2026 (Board/Audit Committee approval of the ₹150 Cr WIL preferential subscription) and is put to shareholders by Postal Ballot Notice dated 19 August 2026, dispatched 20 August 2026 with e-voting from 22 August to 20 September 2026. It changed once: a corrigendum dated 3 September 2026, after NSE advised WIL to reprice under Chapter V of SEBI ICDR, cut TSF's allotment from 10,57,827 shares at ₹1,418 to 10,26,694 shares at ₹1,461 with the ₹150 Cr total unchanged; the resolution passed with 99.29% of votes in favour on 21 September 2026, while separately the NCLT sanctioned the Forge 2000 into Axles India merger on 27 August 2026.

**What management expects from it:** Nothing about a separation is stated. For Wheels India: ₹150 Cr equity to repay or reduce debt, better leverage, a narrower gap to peer averages, headroom for sustained growth and support for its sustainability and growth plans. For TSF: optimised returns on investments and a consolidated 25.007%-plus stake in its associate, funded from internal accruals with no new borrowing.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The only scheme in the record is a merger, not a separation: Forge 2000 Private Limited (wholly-owned subsidiary) was amalgamated into Axles India Limited (subsidiary), sanctioned by NCLT Chennai on 27 August 2026 and uploaded to the NCLT portal on 8 September 2026. No rationale for it is stated anywhere in the filings. “We wish to inform you that the National Company Law Tribunal, Division Bench Court – II, Chennai, has, vide Order dated 27th August 2026 has sanctioned the scheme of amalgamation between Forge 2000 Private Limited (wholly-owned subsidiary) ('Transferor Company') and Axles India Limited (Subsidiary) ('Transferee Company') and uploaded the order in NCLT portal on 08th September 2026.”
- *Filing 2026-08-19 (Acquisition disclosure)* — The Board's stated object for the ₹150 Cr WIL subscription is consolidation of group shareholdings — the opposite of a separation. TSF proposed 10,57,827 shares at ₹1,418 (premium ₹1,408), to complete on or before 30 September 2026 subject to shareholder approval. “To consolidate the shareholdings in Wheels India Ltd (associate company)”
- *Filing 2026-08-20 (Postal Ballot Notice)* — Management framed the investment as part of TSF's role as an Exempted Core Investment Company optimising returns and consolidating group stakes, with TSF already holding 61,09,914 shares (25.007%) of WIL. “Your Company being an Exempted Core Investment Company has been looking at better investment opportunities to optimize returns on investments and also consolidating its shareholdings in its Group Companies.”
- *Filing 2026-08-20 (Postal Ballot Notice)* — The purpose at the investee level was deleveraging: WIL would use the money for debt reduction, closing its leverage gap to peer averages; TSF funded it from internal accruals with no borrowing. “The proposed capital infusion will enable your Associate Company to repay or reduce its Debt thereby enhancing the leverage position, narrowing the gap to the peer averages and ensuring adequate headroom for sustained growth.”
- *Filing 2026-08-20 (Postal Ballot Notice)* — Materiality was driven by TSF's own small revenue base: FY2025-26 consolidated turnover of ₹985 Cr set a ₹98.50 Cr threshold, so the ₹150 Cr deal (15.23% of turnover) required prior shareholder approval by ordinary resolution under Reg. 23(4). “The annual consolidated turnover of the Company for the year ended 31st March 2026 was ₹985 Crores and therefore any transaction in excess of ₹98.50 Crores (i.e. 10% of the annual consolidated turnover of the Company) with a related party will be deemed to be a material related party transaction and shall require prior approval of the shareholders of the Company by way of an Ordinary Resolution.”
- *Filing 2026-08-20 (Postal Ballot Notice)* — Promoter-group members subscribed alongside TSF — Srivats Ram (WIL's Chairman & Managing Director) ₹15.00 Cr / 1,05,782 shares, Gita Ram ₹7.50 Cr, Nivedita Ram ₹7.50 Cr — and related parties were barred from voting. “Mr. Srivats Ram, Ms Gita Ram and Ms. Nivedita Ram are also participating in the preferential issue of WIL.”
- *Filing 2026-09-03 (Corrigendum)* — The plan changed on exchange instruction, not investor pressure: NSE told WIL to reprice under Chapter V of SEBI ICDR, raising the price to ₹1,461 and cutting TSF's allotment to 10,26,694 shares with the ₹150 Cr aggregate unchanged. “Wheels India Limited ("Wheels India") was advised by National Stock Exchange of India Limited ("NSE") to revise the price of the equity shares being offered on preferential basis by applying an appropriate pricing methodology as per Chapter V of the SEBI (ICDR) Regulations.”
- *Filing 2026-09-21 (Postal ballot result)* — Shareholders approved the consolidation overwhelmingly: of 36,661,411 votes cast by 386 holders (16.506% of paid-up capital), 36,399,641 shares were in favour and 261,770 against. “% of E-Votes in favour 99.29%”

*Not explained on the calls:* No separation, demerger or spin-off is mentioned at all; no transcripts exist. Filings give no reason for the Forge 2000–Axles India merger, and no post-issue stake, valuation or margin figures.

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The texts provided do not describe any separation, demerger, spin-off or hive-off of a Vikram Solar business — no such transaction, business, rationale or scheme is mentioned anywhere in the four earnings calls or the two filings, so no separation rationale can be reconstructed from these documents alone. What management actually describes is the opposite of separation: a consolidation of the whole PV value chain inside one listed entity through backward integration, staged as "modules first, then cell, then wafer and ingot" (May 8, 2026), taking the company from 9.5 GW of modules to 15.5 GW, to a 9 GW TOPCon cell plant (first cell December 2026, ~70% backward integration) plus 3 GW in FY28, and a 12 GW wafer-ingot plant whose first 6 GW phase (~INR 3,700 crores, commissioning FY29) was board-approved the day before that call. The explicit logic given is integration, not disaggregation: the 6 GW wafer-ingot addition "turns Gangaikondan into a single integrated solar manufacturing campus - ingot to module with zero transport cost between fabs, zero transit damages, and nil inventory buffers," and the cell/wafer mandates (ALMM List-II from June 2026, draft ALMM List-III from June 1, 2028) are cited as a "coherent industrial framework" rewarding integrated players. The second new business, battery energy storage (target 15 GWh by FY30; 5 GWh cell-to-pack by March 2027, INR ~150 crores assembly, 7.5 GWh cell phase FY29 and second phase FY30; capex quoted at INR 4,300 crores on 65:35 debt:equity in the Jan 20, 2026 call), is also described as being built inside Vikram Solar — "This completes our energy platform and it takes us from a product company to a complete energy solution provider" — not carved out. Asked directly about structural moves on May 8, 2026, the CEO said the company is "not thinking anything beyond" backward integration and BESS. The only things scaled back or dropped were capacity plans, not legal entities: the 2 GW Falta module expansion was held back (17.5 GW guidance cut to 15.5 GW) and the 3 GW US module plan was shelved because of US traceability-to-quartz requirements and skilled-manpower constraints. The two filings on record are insolvency matters, not a scheme of arrangement: an NCLT Kolkata order of June 12, 2026 admitting an Isitva Steels Section 9 petition (claim INR 9,44,12,332 incl. 14% interest; principal held at INR 5,22,25,343), set aside by NCLAT on June 29, 2026 because the admitted dues of INR 91,98,556 were below the INR 1 crore threshold.

**How it evolved:** No separation idea surfaces in any of the four calls — Sep 10, 2025, Oct 17, 2025, Jan 20, 2026 or May 8, 2026 — so there is nothing to trace. What does evolve is integration and diversification within the single entity: on Sep 10, 2025 management framed 17.5 GW of modules plus a 12 GW captive cell line by FY27 and a 1-5 GWh BESS plan; on Oct 17, 2025 it added a 186-acre Gangaikondan campus (6 GW module, 12 GW cell, INR 6,100-6,200 crores) and said wafer capex was only being "actively evaluated" pending ALMM-III; on Jan 20, 2026 module guidance was trimmed to 15.5 GW (Falta 2 GW deferred), 9.5 GW of modules were commissioned and BESS was sized at INR 4,300 crores; and on May 8, 2026 the board approved the first 6 GW of wafer-ingot (INR 3,700 crores) to make Gangaikondan an ingot-to-module campus, with the US module plan dropped. The June 19 and June 30, 2026 filings are IBC proceedings, unrelated to any restructuring of businesses.

**What management expects from it:** Nothing is said about a separation. For the integrated company management expects margin gains: non-DCR EBITDA of INR 1.75-2/Wp in FY27 rising to about INR 5/Wp in FY28 post cell integration, FY27 EBITDA of INR 1,500-1,600 crores (up ~74%), module utilisation 65-70% and cell 70-75%, with net-debt/equity held below 1.5 and coverage above 2.5x at peak drawdown.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=2de81c90-b6f7-480c-9126-341d76cac383.pdf)* — Asked directly whether the company would pursue further vertical or horizontal moves like peers, the CEO ruled out anything beyond backward integration and BESS — no structural separation was contemplated. “At this point of time, we are completely focused on backward integration on the module and expanding into BESS. At this point of time, we are not thinking anything beyond.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=2de81c90-b6f7-480c-9126-341d76cac383.pdf)* — The stated strategic logic is to pull the value chain into one site and one entity (6 GW wafer-ingot approved at ~INR 3,700 crores, commissioning FY29), explicitly for cost and quality gains from co-location — the opposite of separating a business. “This addition turns Gangaikondan into a single integrated solar manufacturing campus - ingot to module with zero transport cost between fabs, zero transit damages, and nil inventory buffers between stages of the value chain.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=2de81c90-b6f7-480c-9126-341d76cac383.pdf)* — BESS (target 15 GWh by FY30) is positioned as completing Vikram Solar's own platform rather than as a separable unit. “This completes our energy platform and it takes us from a product company to a complete energy solution provider, delivering solar plus storage as dispatchable power .”
- *Jan 2026* — The only capacity 'removed' was the 2 GW Falta module expansion — deferred, not divested, pending ALMM-II cell mandates; module guidance was cut from 17.5 GW to 15.5 GW. “No, we have not cancelled that. So, we have retained it at 15.5 for the time being to ensure 75% backward integration with the 12 GW capacities planned.”
- *[Sep 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=26740374-0093-470f-ab7c-d09fcfafcc3f.pdf)* — Cells were always framed as captive inputs for Vikram Solar's own modules (1:1 cell-to-module ratio against 12 GW cell vs 17.5 GW modules), not as a standalone cell business. “So, we would be looking at captively consuming the solar cells for our modules.”
- *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=2de81c90-b6f7-480c-9126-341d76cac383.pdf)* — The US module capacity (3 GW) was abandoned on operating grounds — traceability and manpower — with capital and management bandwidth redirected to India, again with no entity separation involved. “Which is why we are focusing all of the capital as well as management bandwidth on scaling our existing business in India and backward integrating.”
- *Scheme* — No scheme of arrangement is on record. The two filings are an NCLT Kolkata order of June 12, 2026 admitting an Isitva Steels Section 9 IBC petition and an NCLAT order of June 29, 2026 setting it aside because the admitted dues were below the INR 1 crore threshold. “since it is admitted case that the due amount was less than Rs. 1 crore ; the admission order dated 12.06.2026,  stands  set aside.”

*Not explained on the calls:* Everything about a separation: there is no demerger, no entity to be separated, no stated rationale, no requester, no valuation or capital logic, and no scheme document.

## Rights and preferential offerings — who is buying

A rights issue hands the paper to existing holders; a preferential issue of equity or warrants hands it to named buyers at a fixed price. The notes' question is the same for both: are the insiders putting money in? Promoters taking warrants (25% upfront, 18 months to convert) is insiders betting on the stock; paper placed with outsiders is dilution. Each row names the buyers the filings name.

## How this was built

- **Filings:** NSE's corporate-announcements feed read month by month for the 2025-10-14 → 2026-11-07 window and filtered to the 750 official NiftyTotalMarket constituents; BSE via its daily RSS (accumulating) and the BSE-sourced per-company lists on screener.in. Each filing is classified by category and headline, its attachment reduced to text and re-classified from the text. Stored in `IndividualStockAnalysis/India/Announcements/NiftyTotalMarket/`.
- **Confidence:** confirmed = a Demerger / Scheme filing or a scheme text that demerges is on the exchange record; probable = a subsidiary listing in motion or a scheme whose nature the documents do not settle; indicated = news verification, denial or calls alone.
- **Listing:** from the record date and listing filings; where neither exists, what the filings and calls say about timing, or that nothing is stated. The 4–10 week note is the typical gap between record date and listing seen in these filings, not a forecast.
- **Rationale:** every passage in the last 36 months of the stored calls where the separation was discussed, plus the scheme's rationale section, read by the judge; each point links to its transcript. Transcripts and presentations are indexed in `InvestorPresentations/NiftyTotalMarket/_concall_links.csv`.
- **Parent numbers:** the stored consolidated P&L and cash-flow statements (screener.in); growth and margins computed here. P/E from the live Nifty 500 market file, else latest stored close ÷ latest fiscal-year EPS. Charts are Mermaid xychart blocks (render on GitHub).
- **Segment numbers:** the last three annual reports and twelve quarterly presentations (`AnnualReports/`, `InvestorPresentations/`, page-marked text), their segment-reporting pages read by the judge with document and page per number; growth and margins computed here. Where the pages do not carry the figures, the report says so.
- **Judge:** claude-opus-5 read the schemes, three years of calls and the segment pages; reads only the documents shown to it, must quote, cached per document hash and model.
- **Score:** share of checklist items answered yes (1) or partly (½), on 10 — visibility of the pattern in the documents, not stock quality.
- **Coverage:** `_coverage.csv` lists, per highlighted company, which of the above was found and which was not.
